title: Redo and front/back answer to the chords graphic editors use
detail: Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ are what a designer already has in their fingers. The redo audit found the opposite: Ctrl+Shift+Z would have undone.
check: pressed the documented chords with a selection made, and read the object order before and after each

title: An undo crossing an image no longer deletes it
detail: The image's persisted src was an object URL revoked at decode, so Fabric could not enliven it on restore and dropped the object — one undo deleted the asset. Revocation moved to session end. NOTE: the user later corrected the framing — the underlying complaint was that transformations never entered history, and this fixed the restore path rather than that. See vg-030.
check: imported an image, moved it, undid, and confirmed the image was still on the canvas

title: Entering a group makes only that group's objects selectable
detail: "You are inside a group" lived in grouping-manager's context array and only the layer panel read it, so the artboard contradicted the list. Worse, editor-shell routed every double-click into enterGroup, so double-clicking a text box to edit it recorded a group context.
check: entered a group and counted selectable objects: 1 of 51, where before it was 51 of 51

title: The trends chart is no longer the only aliased one
detail: MAX_BACKING_PIXELS clamped the largest chart to 1.53x while every smaller one got 2x, so the only aliased graph was the one a reader looks at longest.
check: compared rendered pixels per chart at equal scale; every chart now samples at the same multiple

title: An inserted object is named, and the name round-trips
detail: Without this, every object an author created was a uuid in the layer list, permanently.
check: inserted a shape, named it, saved the package, and read the name back out of the zip

title: The glass control renders on every object and says why where it cannot apply
detail: The user's own test found the first version incomplete: "The checkbox is unselectable but the tooltip only show when tabbed, not mouse hovering." aria-disabled rather than disabled, because a disabled control leaves the tab order and the reason would reach a mouse and nobody else. **MOVED 2026-10-14, and this row is no longer the current answer.** The user, testing the editor, asked for the glass section to be hidden on a subject that cannot be frosted (item 8), and Task 13.4 landed it. **`vg-465` owns what is decided now**, and this row stays `verified` as the record of what was decided before it and why — that withholding the control "left nothing anywhere saying so", which is the cost the reverse ruling accepted. `vg-008` (verified) still owns which shapes accept glass.
check: selected a Line, tabbed to the glass control, and read what a screen reader announces: the control, and the reason it is unselectable

title: A bounded number field clamps onto its bound and carries a native slider

check: typed 60 into the glass blur field and read the field, the object and the new slider: 48, blurRadius 48, range min 0 max 48

title: Glass works on Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon
detail: Ruled by the user. Polyline, Path and Line are excluded — an open path has no interior to sample. A prior attempt to read this as "clamping proven nearby" is why the check names the shapes.

title: The player's failure screen names the cause, not a JavaScript parse error
detail: It printed V8's SyntaxError verbatim on a wall display, which is both meaningless to a reader and misleading — it says the theme file is corrupt when the likeliest cause is that nothing is serving.
check: pointed the player at a missing theme and read the screen: "The host did not answer with a theme — it may not be running."

title: A POSIX root volume joins its own drive
detail: library-devices stripped a trailing slash, turning / into "", and compared fs against mount. On Windows the path is C: and the strip is a no-op, so the suite was green and the whole platform was broken.
check: a test with a volume at / on a device that also holds /data; before, disk.total was undefined

title: A theme is a folder; a ZIP is only what an author exports
detail: Ruled twice by the user. The list() call was decompressing every package in the library to print N lines, and a 33 MB asset saved successfully and then 404'd. The window between two renames could also make a theme look deleted.
check: saved a theme from the real editor and read the folder: theme.json, assets/, thumbnail.png beside it

title: A saved theme can be read back by id
detail: Before, the editor could not open a saved theme at all: rename, save, reload /editor/, and the edit was gone. A save is a write-only surface with no way back to it.
check: renamed a theme, saved it, opened /editor/?theme=<id> in a fresh document, and read the saved name; a dead id falls back to the default

check: three writes through the real API: current base 200, no base 200, stale base 409, and the stored theme unchanged after the 409

detail: documentKey boxed one JS number per asset byte and stringified it — 1,614 ms and 86 MB retained, on every open, new and save. The key now holds the envelope and each declared digest.

detail: Ruled by the user: the menu was redundant with the toolbar, not a drift to be synced. An agent was dispatched to make the menu offer all eight before the ruling arrived; it was killed with nothing committed. **MOVED 2026-10-14, and only one half of it.** The user asked for the eight arrange actions to leave the canvas dock and appear at the top of the inspector when two or more elements are selected (item 6), and Task 13.4 landed it. **This row's own decision stands: the Arrange *menu* is gone and does not come back.** What moved is *where the toolbar keeps the eight*, which this row's rationale leaned on when it ruled the menu redundant — so read **`vg-463`** for the current answer and this row for why the menu went.

title: A crop control is reachable for a selected image

detail: All four ordering actions left the child in BOTH collections — same reference — so Fabric painted it twice and the scene serialised it twice. The binding is Ctrl+Shift+], not Ctrl+].
check: pressed Ctrl+Shift+] three times on a grouped object, then serialised: 51 top-level objects and the child once, not twice

title: The starter theme's charts render in the player, gauges included
detail: Fixed in 7904424 on 2026-09-28; what was missing was the evidence — the stack had never been kept. ECharts 6.1.0's _renderPointer reads _progressEls inside a data-diff callback assigned only after a render that drew an arc. Player-only: it renders before telemetry arrives and flips progress.show under a datum already present.
check: counted distinct colours in each chart own ECharts canvas on a real host: ram-gauge 6 to 57, vram-gauge 6 to 45, track ink flat

title: Double-clicking outside an entered group does not exit it; only Escape does
detail: "double clicking outside a group didn't exit it, only the Esc key does." editor-shell.ts binds mouse:dblclick to enterGroupOnDoubleClick — enter only. Nothing on screen says Escape is the way out. Neither fixed nor recorded until the user tested for it.
check: Fix reverted: 2 of 6 dblclick tests fail. Live: entered a group by double-click (3 rows in context, 50 dimmed), then double-clicked empty canvas and the group context cleared - q1-group-entered.png vs q1-group-exited.png.

title: Locked and unlocked icons are hard to tell apart; locked should be a filled lock
detail: "Locked and unlocked icons in the layer panel is visually hard to distinguished. Locked should use a filled lock icon, not an outline icon like unlocked." The layer panel already has a KIND_ICONS pattern to follow. Small.

title: A locked object should stay selectable on the canvas, just not movable
detail: "Locked icon should still be selectable in the canvas, it just can't be transformed, moved. Otherwise user will have to go hunt for it in the layer panel." selectable: false is currently how a locked object is prevented from being transformed, and the same flag is what makes it unselectable — the same split the group fix made once.
check: Reverted fix: 5 of 7 lock tests fail. Live on a locked object: hasControls false and every lock* flag set, a 120px drag moved it 0px, 8 arrange actions disabled, and a shift-click alongside an unlocked object left it out of the selection - q1-locked-selected.png.

title: The drag-select marquee vanishes when the mouse pauses rather than releases
detail: THE ROWS HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG and the real cause is worse. Not bound to pointerup: the marquee is drawn straight onto the canvas context by Fabric, is not part of the scene, and every full repaint erases it. The editor repaints the whole scene 30 times a second (editor-main starts startChartRefresh at rate 30), so the marquee survived about 33ms — one frame — and was then gone until the pointer moved again. That is exactly the reported symptom: flashing during a drag, gone when the pointer stops. The editor now holds the refresh for the duration of a pointer gesture. Live readings are not worth showing mid-drag anyway, and the first frame after mouse:up brings them current.
check: Reverted fix: the browser test fails with the upper canvas reading 0, i.e. no marquee at all after a 600ms pause. With the fix the same read is non-zero. Live by hand on a rebuilt bundle: held the pointer still mid-drag for 1.8s and the marquee is still drawn (vg-027-fixed-held.png), where before the pause it was absent (vg-027-held.png); CPU readings resumed after release, 26% then 41% then 46%.

title: The crop notice contradicts the geometry it describes
detail: WITHDRAWN — the notice was right and the report was my instrument error. Fabric anchors .left/.top, it does not read them as a box: a theme that omits originX/originY revives at originX center, so the object box runs -60.5 to 140.5 while the glyph run is at -60.5 to -38.5, genuinely off a 1920 artboard. The real defect found alongside it — a revived display had no artboard boundary at all, so objects painted over the letterbox bars while the notice said they were not shown — is fixed in 299c0bf, which added artboard-clip and artboard-crop coverage and the persist.ts boundary. Kept rather than deleted because the mistake is the reusable part: a notice that disagrees with the geometry is usually the reader, and the way to tell is to check which one Fabric actually honours.

title: Every unmatched host path serves the player
detail: CAUSE ESTABLISHED, and it was not the fallthrough itself but serveStatic: an extension-less path was treated as a client route and fell back to the bundle index.html, so /play and /display resolved to the dashboard. A file with an extension never took that branch, which is why /theme.json had always 404d while /nope returned 200 with a live display. The editor needs its fallback — it is a client-routed app under /editor — and the player does not: it is one document, so only "/" may fall back. serveStatic now takes that as a parameter, true at the editor mount and false everywhere else. ADR-0018 already claimed this path, so the 404 that answers now says Not found. rather than a build hint that is not true.
check: Reverted fix: the new test fails on expected 200 to be 404 for /play. Live against a rebuilt host: /?data=live and /favicon.svg serve 200, while /play, /display, /nope and /theme.json all answer 404 Not found. 43 host tests pass.

title: A text object's Height field shows a stale measurement before the author has authored a height
detail: REFUTED as stated, and the search beside it found something worse. The Height field is NOT stale: on a freshly inserted Text it read 79 for a measured 78.83, and after a longer run wrapped inside a 64-unit box it read 463 for a measured 462.85 — it tracks the measurement exactly. The real defect is one field away and is vg-057. The original claim is kept above because the refutation is the useful part: a field that follows a measurement is not reporting a stale one.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: the Height field read 79 against a measured 78.83, then 463 against 462.85 after the run wrapped. Reverted against the half-box it did not produce: see vg-057.

title: A palette token's key and the name an author sees are different strings, and that is by design
detail: MEASURED on the built editor, three colours added in a row. Keys: colour, colour-2, colour-3. Names: New colour, New colour, New colour — and renaming the second to "CPU brand" left its key at colour-2 and the list showing "CPU brand · 0". So the reported shape is real and the defect it was filed as is not: the key is an internal id that §75 already rules is never renamed, and it NEVER REACHES THE AUTHOR. document.body.innerText contains neither colour-2 nor colour-3; they appear only as select value attributes in the HTML. The layer list shows the name, which is the string a person typed. The one residue worth keeping: every added colour carries the identical default name New colour, so three of them are indistinguishable until the author renames each.
check: Live in the built editor: after three adds the token select reads colour, colour-2, colour-3 while the visible labels read New colour, CPU brand, New colour, and a body-text scan for colour-2 and colour-3 returns nothing. Renaming moved the label and left the key alone, which is the id contract rather than a defect.

title: A text run could not be told not to print its unit, so the author got the unit twice
detail: REFUTED AS WRITTEN, and the real gap is narrower and now closed. The mechanism always existed: formatValueSegment reads run.unitDisplay ?? binding.unitDisplay, and the reference theme uses it — measured on the shipped Starter, cpu-card-value is a value run on cpu.load with unitDisplay none plus a literal % at the caption size, and its canvas text reads 47%, one percent sign. What did not exist was a control. unitDisplay was on the CHART bindings panel and absent from the TEXT RUN panel, so an author who wanted the reference pattern had no way to author it: set a reading and the unit printed itself, add a literal % beside it and the unit printed twice. REPRODUCED BY HAND on the rebuilt editor: set the run to Short and cpu-card-value renders 69%%, set it back to None and it renders 64%. The run panel now carries the same four options the chart panel has, Default/None/Short/Long. It writes the RUN rather than the binding, because a run own unitDisplay takes precedence — writing the binding is silently shadowed by exactly the theme this control exists to reproduce, which the first version did.
check: Red without the control: the new test fails with TypeError reading a null select. With it, 26 run-panel tests pass, and live in a rebuilt editor the run reads 47% at None, 69%% at Short and 64% back at None — the doubled unit, produced and then prevented by the control.

title: The background media is declared as an asset and has no layer
detail: WITHDRAWN as a duplicate — this is vg-030 for one kind of asset, and the row said so itself. MEASURED to confirm it is still true: the Starter declares starter-backdrop as its background media and paints it full-bleed, the layer list has 52 rows and NOT ONE of them is the backdrop, and the canvas holds 52 objects of which zero are images. The media is declared, rendered and unaddressable, which is the same defect vg-030 carries for assets generally. Tracked once, in vg-030. The GitHub issue is closed with this row named.
check: Live in the built editor: 52 layer rows and 0 of them match backdrop/media/background/image; 52 canvas objects and 0 are images, while the theme settings declare starter-backdrop as Background media. Confirms the duplicate rather than the closure — the underlying defect stays open in vg-030.

title: Delete cannot remove an object that lives inside a group
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry. FIXED in 82eef78 — see vg-018. Kept here so the issue and the registry agree; close the issue against vg-018.

title: The Ctrl+N discard prompt times out waiting for a Discard button
detail: THE ROW WAS RIGHT AND IT WAS A TEST DEFECT, in three places rather than one. REPRODUCED: reference-theme.spec.ts times out on waiting for a Discard button inside a dialog that is already visible — because the dialog it found was the artboard SIZE CHOOSER, which has Cancel and Create. Measured by hand on the running editor: Ctrl+N on a changed document opens Choose an artboard size; the question about the changes, Save changes before opening another theme?, arrives only after Create is pressed. The test looked for Discard one step too early. The second failure was also stale: it asserted the scene still held the reference composition after New, but New is a blank theme of the chosen size and the reference is the separate New from starter command — measured, the canvas holds 0 objects after Create and Discard. The third was the status copy, New Fabric theme against the products New theme. All three call sites now go through one answerDialogIfShown helper that WAITS for the dialog rather than asking is it up right now, which is what an async dirty guard made unanswerable.
check: Red before, green after. The test was waiting on the Discard button inside a dialog that was already visible, because the dialog it found was the artboard size chooser with Cancel and Create; pressing Ctrl+N twice is what reaches the discard prompt. With the helper it passes in 15.5s, the two dialog tests in editor.spec.ts still pass, and npm run lint is clean with no isVisible().catch races left in tests/e2e.

title: The crop frame is drawn a whole image up and to the left of the image it frames
detail: A Rect is anchored at its centre but getBoundingRect() reports a corner, so the frame begin() built sat at twice the offset: its top-left was the image top-left, putting the frame up and to the left by one full image width and height. Three of its four edges, and the crop handles on them, fell off the canvas, so the session read as a frame that could be grown but never cropped. Owner: crop-manager/index.ts begin().
check: Reverted fix: the crop-frame test fails on origin left/top. The frame bounding rect now equals the image bounding rect left, top and size.

title: The display tells a reader it has 30 sensors when it reads 19
detail: MEASURED on the Starter served by a live host: the stream was requested with 30 key entries covering 19 distinct sensors (cpu.load three times, gpu.load three, ram.used.percent three, and six more twice), and the availability strip read "2 of 30 sensors have no reading". startHostedTheme built its key list with a flat map and no Set, while the two other call sites that answer the same question — the editor private semanticKeys in editor-main.ts and requiredSemanticKeys for a ThemeDocument — both dedupe. The hosted path is the one a real deployed display takes, so the count a wall reader sees is inflated by how many objects happen to bind the same reading. The repeat request is the same defect: the display asks for the same sensor three times a second and nothing new comes back.
check: Reverted fix: 2 of 3 bound-keys tests fail. Live on the served Starter after a player rebuild: the stream requests 19 distinct keys with no repeats, and the strip reads 2 of 19 sensors where it read 2 of 30 - vg-053-sensor-count.png.

title: A missing file is reported as a bundle that was never built
detail: serveStatic sent one message for every file it failed to read, so "The player bundle is not built. Run: npx vite build packages/player" answered requests for a theme.json, a package zip and a stale chunk alike. MEASURED against a host with both bundles built: /theme.json, /assets/theme.zip, /assets/nope.js, /editor/assets/nope.js and /editor/nope.html all returned 404 with that text. The message is the one AGENTS.md itself sends people chasing, so following it rebuilds a bundle that is already there and returns the identical answer — the failure mode is a loop, not a delay. The message now says Not found. once the bundle entry exists, and the build hint is reserved for the case it is true of. ADR-0018 records why no static server upstream solves this shape.
check: Reverted fix: the built-bundle test fails on "expected the player bundle is not built not to contain is not built". Live against a rebuilt host with both bundles present: /theme.json, /assets/nope.js and /editor/assets/nope.js all answer 404 Not found., while / and /editor/ still serve.

title: A pasted image and a new group are listed by their uuid instead of a name
detail: MEASURED in the built editor: pasting a PNG added a row reading image-d8032a9b-438c-4a46-8d1e-b469d3fdad16, and grouping two cards added group-<uuid>, while an inserted Rectangle read Rectangle. object-name.ts states the contract plainly — absence of a name means fall back to the id — and the id of a freshly minted object is a uuid, so the two creators that set no name are the two the fallback cannot help. image-manager and grouping-manager were the only creators not going through newObjectName, whose own comment already named this failure. Both now call it; the words Image and Group live in ui-copy beside text and panel, where newObjectName already reads them.
check: Reverted fix: both tests fail on expected undefined to be Image and undefined to be Group. Live in a rebuilt editor: a pasted image row reads Image and a group built from a canvas shift-click multi-select reads Group, where both previously printed a 42-character id.

title: Filling in one Size field left half an authored box, and the text object lost its width
detail: MEASURED, and it destroys the object. A text inserted by the editor has no authored box — its width is Fabric measurement until an author types one. Typing 120 into Height wrote yunariText.box as { height: 120 } with no width; the merge in selection-inspector was correct, the box it merged into did not exist. The next text change made authoredBox multiply an undefined width by the scale, and the object ended with width null and getBoundingRect() returning nulls — unrenderable, unselectable by geometry, and no longer savable. Fixed by seeding both dimensions from the object own measured edge, so the first Size field an author fills in produces a whole box.
check: Reverted fix: the new test fails on expected undefined to be 126.21875, the measured width. Live on a rebuilt editor, the same sequence that ended at width null now reads width 63.8 and a bounding rect of 100x379, with yunariText.box holding both dimensions - vg-042-box-width.png.

title: Entering a group did not dim the layer list until something else re-rendered it
detail: MEASURED on the built editor: group two cards, double-click into the group, and 0 of 53 rows carry data-context. Click any row and 3 light up while 50 drop to opacity 0.45. CAUSE ESTABLISHED and it is not Fabric forgetting: entering a group does not move the selection. The group is already the active object, so setActiveObject is a no-op and MEASURED: zero of the four canvas events the bridge republishes on fire at all. The layer panel therefore never learns the context changed and keeps whatever projection it had. The manager now announces the context on the editor:group-context-changed canvas event — the custom editor: convention the other managers already use — and the bridge listens to it alongside its four.
check: Reverted fix: the announcement test fails on expected [] to have a length of 1. Live on a rebuilt bundle with real gestures: entering the group gives 3 rows in context and 50 dimmed, and double-clicking empty canvas returns to 0 and 0. 139 tests across the grouping and shell suites pass.

title: A chart's series colours and its bindings are coupled by index, so removing a middle binding shifts the colours
detail: MEASURED ON THE REFERENCE THEME, then fixed. The per-series paint is a positional array sitting beside the bindings, and removing a binding filtered the bindings without touching the paint. Measured on trends-chart: palette [cpu, gpu, ram] with bindings [trends-cpu, trends-gpu, trends-ram]; remove the MIDDLE one and the palette became [cpu, gpu] while the bindings became [trends-cpu, trends-ram] — so the RAM series painted with the GPU green. Nothing on screen looked wrong; the chart simply told a different story. seriesPaintFor already reconciled the arrays lengths and its truncation is right for the LAST binding, which is why the case nobody tries passes. The manager now carries each surviving series own paint through the removal before the length fix runs, so a middle removal keeps cpu and ram. Adding is unchanged: a new series repeats the last colour, which is what extending a chart means.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: trends-chart reads [palette.cpu, palette.gpu, palette.ram] before and [palette.cpu, palette.ram] after removing gpu.load, where it read [palette.cpu, palette.gpu] before the fix and painted RAM green. Two unit tests: carriedPaintFor pins the middle, the last and the unchanged case, and the panel test pins that the three Remove buttons name their reading and remove only their own. NOT PINNED: the one-line call from #writeBindings into carriedPaintFor — the manager-level test needs a panel harness this file does not have, and I did not build one. That wiring rests on the live measurement above, not on a test.

title: The palette colour field accepts anything, and persists it
detail: FIXED AT THE SOURCE, and the validator was not the gap. Measured first: the palette colour field accepted rebeccapurple, not-a-colour, #GGG and rgb(1,2,3) with no alert and checkValidity() reporting the field valid — and the published validator is no tighter, because validateGlobals checks the entry id, the name, that a value exists and that there are no unknown keys, and never looks at a colour. So the file the editor wrote passed its own schema because the schema has no rule. The field now asks the browser, which already holds the answer: CSS.supports("color", value) is the same engine that will paint it, so there is no second hand-written list of colour names to keep in step. A value the engine rejects is refused with the browsers own validity message naming it, and not committed — which matters because ctx.fillStyle keeps the PREVIOUS colour for an unparseable one, so accepting it meant the edit silently did nothing while the document carried the nonsense. STILL OPEN, deliberately: whether a CSS keyword such as rebeccapurple belongs in the vocabulary is a decision about which words the product accepts, not about correctness, and nothing here settles it. Upstream of vg-031 stays true — a picker does not fix a write path that does not check.
check: Red without the guard: the browser test fails on validity.valid expected false received true. Live in the built editor: #123456 commits, not-a-colour leaves the field invalid with a message naming it, and after the panel redraws from the palette the field reads #123456 again — the refused value was never committed. jsdom has no CSS object, so this can only be pinned in a browser; the unit suite cannot cover the predicate.

title: A selected Line shows a diagonal bounding box instead of two end handles and a rotate handle
detail: BUILT, after the search in ADR-0020 and a correction to it. A Line now carries two endpoint controls and the rotation handle — endpointA, endpointB, mtr — and no bounding box at all: hiding the six handles it does not need would have left the box, which is the defect. Each endpoint reads its own corner from x1/x2 and y1/y2 rather than assuming top-left and bottom-right, because width and height are absolute: measured on a line drawn right-to-left, the same two numbers are the other pair of corners. Moving an end writes that end and leaves the other where it was. Shift holds the line at a multiple of 15 degrees, on a modifier that branches in exactly one unrelated place. THREE THINGS THE ROW AND THE NOTE GOT WRONG, all found by measuring rather than reading. ONE: this projects Line is x1, y1, x2, y2 — four scalars, no points, no pathOffset, no setDimensions — so Fabric polyline controls and the anchor technique that go with them do not apply to it; nothing in snap-manager reads either representation, so snapping was never going to understand an endpoint for free. TWO: writing x2 makes Line re-derive left/top, so reading the objects own matrix back on every mousemove mapped each step through a frame the previous step had already moved — measured, the handle landed about 1.6x where it was dropped and a purely horizontal drag raised the far end by 188 units. The gesture frame is now taken once at mouse-down. THREE, and it is the one that would have shipped: Line.ownDefaults resolves up the prototype chain to the object every Fabric object shares, so assigning controls onto it took the handles off rectangles and text boxes too. Caught by an existing handle-size test, and assigned as a new defaults object now.
check: Red without the controls: all three new tests fail, the first on the control names. Live in a rebuilt editor: a selected Line reads endpointA, endpointB, mtr; a textbox, a rect and a chart each still read all nine with mtr. Dragging the far end 100 canvas px at 0.374 zoom moved x2 by 266.7 against 267.1 expected — 0.06 percent — with x1 and y1 unchanged, and with Shift held the line settled at 15.0 degrees. Editor suite 1041 across 84 files.

title: The Performance Trends panel does plot; the empty reading was a five-second-old source
detail: REFUTED, and the row own hypothesis was the right one. Measured against a live host rather than the preview source, after 18 seconds: history() over a 60-second window returns 42 points for each of cpu.load, gpu.load and ram.used.percent, every one status ok, and the panel draws all three lines - vg050-trends-live.png. The earlier reading of zero keys came from the PREVIEW source after 5 batches and 7 seconds, which is exactly the explanation the row offered when it filed itself as a measurement rather than a finding: chartPlaybackDelayMs exists on the source, so playback simply had not filled the window yet. The pass repeated mistake is closing here: two sessions read an empty source as a broken chart, and the thing that separated them was waiting longer and reading a real telemetry source, which is what this row said to do.
check: Live on a host streaming real telemetry: 42 points in the 60s window for each of the three series, latest 39.2, 30 and 83.6 percent, all status ok, and the panel draws three lines. The strip beside it reads 2 of 19 sensors have no reading, which is the LibreHardwareMonitor gap and not this.

title: The Starter was reported as edited the moment it opened
detail: FIXED, and the cause was not what two earlier readings of this row guessed. isDirty compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and the document differed from itself. THE INSTRUMENT THAT SETTLED IT, built in jsdom because a browser probe could not reach it: mount the Starter, snapshot, run one live pass, snapshot, and report the differing JSON paths. THE ANSWER IS styles. One pass rewrites .scene.objects.N.styles[M] on 18 of the Starter 52 objects — exactly its binding count — with nothing touched. styles is Fabric per-character formatting; the authored truth for a bound text object is yunariText.runs, and the renderer resolves runs into styles and text. documentKey now compares the document with those two renderings removed, on the objects whose runs are the authored truth; an object without runs owns its text and styles and keeps them. The asset half was fixed separately and is in the same commit — it enumerated the loaded byte map, so the key depended on how much had loaded rather than on what the document declares. NOT text, as I first assumed: stripping text alone changed nothing, and I reverted that rather than ship a key transform on an unproven hypothesis that could hide a real edit.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: Ctrl+N then Create on an UNTOUCHED Starter no longer asks to save. It still asks after inserting a Rectangle, and still asks after editing a text run by hand. Red without the fix: the shell test fails on isDirty expected false received true. 20 tests across the shell and persistence suites.

title: An asset in use cannot be removed — and that is told to the author, not swallowed
detail: THE FOUR DEFECTS MEASURED, AND THREE OF THEM ARE NOT DEFECTS. (1) Replace allocates a new path per import: REFUTED. With a PNG selected, replacing it with a different PNG left the list at two entries and kept the same key, so it replaces in place and the key an author sees does not move. (2) and (3) the layer list being inconsistent and some assets showing while some do not: REAL, and one thing, which is vg-047 folded in here as its duplicate — measured, the Starter declares starter-backdrop, the artboard uses it as its background media, and the canvas document mentions NEITHER asset while the layer list has 53 rows and names no asset at all. (4) some assets cannot be removed: REFUTED, and the opposite of swallowed. Pressing Remove on the one asset the artboard is using leaves it in place and says That asset is in use and cannot be removed — the panel guards on a reference check and reports it. I first read this as a silent no-op because I was reading the editor status footer instead of the panels own alert line; the button is enabled, the click does something, and the something says why. NOTHING WAS FIXED HERE because there was nothing to fix: what survives is the layer-list gap, which is the row that was already carrying vg-047.
check: Live on the Starter: Remove on starter-backdrop leaves the list at one and reports That asset is in use and cannot be removed. Replace on a selected PNG keeps the list at two and the same key. backgroundMedia is starter-backdrop while the layer list names no asset and the canvas document mentions neither.

title: The palette colour field has a picker that keeps alpha
detail: BUILT on shadcn, per the ruling that this fields ecosystem is shadcn/ui rather than Base UI; that ruling supersedes the plans 2026-09-29 search, which reached the opposite conclusion, and the plan is annotated so the question is not re-litigated. WHAT IT IS: a popover with four tracks — saturation, brightness, hue and alpha — over a checkerboard so a translucent token reads as translucent, a hex field for exact entry, and a swatch trigger beside the existing text field, which stays because a value can be typed exactly and a picker cannot always be dragged to it. Everything is 8-digit hex, which is what the envelope stores. WHY NOT A NATIVE INPUT, which is the requirement that rules the obvious answer out: input type=color has no alpha channel and the themes paints carry it — panel is 85 percent and frost is 30 percent — so accepting one would be a way to lose the value. THE COST, STATED ONCE: shadcn components are Radix-based, so this adds a second headless library beside Base UI, plus clsx, tailwind-merge and cva. The user ruled with that cost in view. The maths is a pure module with its own tests, away from the DOM: it caught two of my own bugs — alpha scaled as if it were a 0-255 channel, turning 85 percent into 1/255, and a regex capture passed where the parsed alpha belonged, producing NaN in the hex.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor, dragging each track in turn: hue on white leaves it white (correct — hue cannot move a colour with no saturation), saturation gives #26ff3c, brightness gives #137f1e, and alpha gives #137f1e66 with the field and the hex readout agreeing. The token name survives a colour change. 5 maths tests, and the editor suite is 1049 across 85 files.

title: A gradient is edited on a track, with the colour picker on every stop
detail: BUILT on the pickers parts, which is what the row asked for: one picker per stop rather than a second colour vocabulary. A gradient was angle plus an offset and a colour per stop, as three number fields and a free-text box, with nothing to look at while editing it. There is now a preview of the gradient it produces, a track whose handles are its stops, and the shared shadcn picker on each. The number fields stay because a drag cannot land on 0.37 exactly and an author who wants exact entry still can. THE STOP COUNT IS NOT CAPPED AT TWO, which is what ruled out the Cladd ColorEditor in the plans search — the track is driven by the stop array and the panel adds stops itself. WHAT THE BUILD LEARNED: the pickers were first behind a click that opened the chosen stop picker, and it never worked, because the palette panel rebuilds its own DOM on every redraw and React state naming this stop is open was destroyed by the next commit — the popover would have closed on the very pick that applied it. They are inline per stop instead, which needs no state and is the better behaviour anyway. As with vg-031 the surface is shadcn on Radix, per the ruling, and the cost of that ruling is the same second headless library. VERIFIED BY HAND AFTER THE FACT, so the record carries the measurement and not just the claim. On the rebuilt bundle: select a palette token, set Paint to Linear gradient, and the panel gives Angle, Stop 1 position, Stop 1 colour, Stop 2 position, Stop 2 colour and Add stop, with the stops addressable as buttons labelled Gradient stop 1 and Gradient stop 2. IT ENDS TO END: a gradient set on Frosted panel saved as {"kind":"gradient","angle":0,"stops":[...]} in the document's globals.palette and rendered in the player across all eight objects that use the token - I set a white-to-black sweep and watched every card in the player go with it. THE ALPHA TRAP THIS ROW WAS ABOUT IS NOT A TRAP: typing 8-digit hex into a stop's colour field is accepted and persisted, Stop 1 taking #0815234d and saving as exactly that, so a translucent token carries its translucency into a gradient. The reuse answer the row reached for - that the colour picker's swatch and hex field already are the gradient editor - is what got built on top. One cosmetic note for whoever reads this next, since it is the only thing I would raise: switching a Solid token to Linear gradient seeds #ffffff and #000000 and discards the token's existing colour with no way back but undo, and both defaults are fully opaque, so a 30% frosted token became a solid sweep across eight objects from one dropdown choice. The token row does say Frosted panel · 8, so the author has the count.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: a token switched to Linear gradient shows the preview, two draggable stop handles and two pickers. Dragging stop two from 1.0 to 0.75 moved the handle and the numeric field with it; picking on stop one committed #33c2ff into that stops colour. Editor suite 1049 across 85 files.

title: A binding no longer outlives its object, so deleting a readout does not disarm saving
detail: FIXED AT THE SERIALISER, not at the delete. A binding is keyed by its object id, so deleting the object left a key naming something the scene no longer had; serialiseThemeEnvelope then produced a document the validator refuses and every later save in that session threw with nothing in the UI saying so. The Starter binds 25 of its 52 objects, so deleting one sensor readout disarmed saving for the rest of the session while the row simply looked like it had vanished. snapshot now drops bindings whose key is not an object in the scene. WHY THERE AND NOT AT EACH DELETE: the keyboard, the layer list, the context menu, undo and any path added later all arrive at snapshot, so this cannot be the one that was forgotten, and it is a trust boundary — the serialiser no longer names an object that is not there, whatever removed it. A binding is meaningless without its object, so nothing is lost that the document could still use, and an author who re-adds an object with that id gets its reading back. THE ROWS OTHER TWO QUESTIONS ARE NOT ANSWERED and are still decisions: whether a save that throws should report itself rather than vanish, and whether a failed save leaves the document marked dirty so the author is warned on the way out. Both are separable from this and neither is fixed here.
check: Against a live host, the rows exact sequence: delete network-up, then File > Save to library. The host document now reads 51 objects with network-up absent, bindings 25 to 24, and no binding naming a missing object — and no pageerror. Red without the fix: the test fails with Invalid Fabric theme: Fabric object network-up is not in this scene, the exact error the row reported. Editor suite 1050 across 85 files.

title: A deleted object now disappears from the layer list, the canvas and the inspector together
detail: FIXED, and it was two subscriptions rather than one. A deletion fires no selection event — the active object is discarded first — so neither the bridge nor the selection inspector was told, and the row survived. Measured on the row own sequence: after Edit > Delete on network-up the canvas reported 51 objects and the host document agreed, but the layer list still showed 52 rows including network-up, and the inspector still read its name and geometry. So the three surfaces disagreed about what the document contained, and the row is right that this is one defect seen three ways. Both now subscribe to object:removed and object:added: the bridge, which republishes the layer projection, and the selection inspector, which re-binds its fields. After the same keystroke all three agree — 51 rows, no network-up, and the inspector empty. THE STUB WAS ALSO LYING, which is worth recording: bridge.dom.test.ts canvas stub answered getObjects but had no add or remove, so a test that deleted an object was still projecting from an array that still held it. A test written against that stub would have passed for the wrong reason — mine did, on the first attempt. The stub now has Fabric own add and remove, and the tests pin the republish rather than the projection, because layers() reads live and so was never the thing that was stale.
check: Live: Edit > Delete on network-up takes the layer list 52 to 51 with network-up gone, the canvas to 51 objects, and the inspector back to empty. Red without the subscription: both bridge tests fail. Editor suite 1052 across 85 files.

title: Insert > Text takes the caret, so the first keystroke lands
detail: FIXED, and the obvious fix was not the one that worked. insertNewText now enters editing and selects the new text, which is what every editor this product is measured against does when you ask for a text box. Calling it SYNCHRONOUSLY put the caret in and then lost it: the menu the insert came from takes focus back for itself as it closes, so a keystroke after Insert still went nowhere and document.activeElement was BODY. The call is deferred a frame, and guarded on the new object still being the active one so a late frame does not steal focus from whatever the author has moved on to. EditorInteraction.textManager.addText was widened to FabricObject although the manager has always returned a Textbox and its own interface said so; narrowing it there is what lets a caller enter editing at all. TWO TEST-STUB FIXES were needed and are worth naming because both would have passed for the wrong reason: the panel stub returned undefined from getActiveObject, so the guard could never pass; and addText was typed to return undefined, which is not what it returns.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor: after Insert > Text the focused element is a TEXTAREA (Fabric hidden textarea) with isEditing true, and typing Hello leaves the object reading Hello — where it previously stayed New text. Red without the call: the new test fails. Editor suite 1054 across 85 files.

title: Release package and Open package both work; automation could not see either
detail: REFUTED IN FULL, and it is the most expensive instrument error on the pass: it would have had two working features fixed, and vg-034s rename applied to buttons that already do their job. Both commands are wired and both complete. Release package asks window.prompt for major/minor/patch and then downloads; answering it produces yunari-demo-dashboard.yunari-theme. Open package calls picker.click() and a native file chooser opens. THE ROUND TRIP THEY EXIST FOR WAS RUN END TO END: Release exported a package, that file was fed back through Open package, and the editor came back with 52 objects and 52 layer rows. WHY IT LOOKED INERT, twice over, and neither is the product. Release uses window.prompt, and automation DISMISSES it without being asked — the handler takes the null and returns early, so there is no download, no toast and no page error, which is precisely the signature filed as a dead command. Open package opens a native file chooser, which a script cannot observe at all. I hit this myself earlier in the same session: I triggered Release, could not answer the dialog, and recorded that the download never fired. The sibling Save package works because it has neither a prompt nor a chooser, which is why the comparison made the other two look broken. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is worth more than the row: a native prompt or a native chooser is invisible to automation and an auto-dismissed prompt is indistinguishable from an absent one. Any future finding of the form a command does nothing at all must first be checked for a dialog or a chooser in the way.
check: Live: Release prompts for a bump and downloads yunari-demo-dashboard.yunari-theme once answered; Open opens a native file chooser; that exported file fed back through Open restores 52 objects and 52 rows.

title: Each rail pane keeps the scroll offset you left it at
detail: FIXED IN THE LAYOUT, which is where the swap happens. The rail is single-panel, so opening Assets takes the layer list down and builds it again — and everything else survived that swap while the scroll did not, which is what made it worth separating: the selection stayed, the inspector kept its geometry, the canvas kept its handles. choosePane now reads the outgoing panels scroll offset off the DOM and restores the incoming ones a frame later, after the new content is laid out, or the offset would land on whatever height it has at that instant. Read off the DOM rather than kept in state on purpose: the panel is torn down by the swap, so anything held in state is gone by the time the next panes turn runs.
check: Live: scroll the layer list to 499, click Assets (reads 0), click Layers and it is back at 499. Red without the restore: the new test fails. Editor suite 1055 across 86 files.

title: A rename changes the name and leaves the id, so it cannot orphan a binding
detail: REFUTED, and it is the same reading error as the other name-versus-id ones: the rows evidence searched the saved document for the new name and found the old id gone. MEASURED, on the rows own sequence — click network-down, Enter, type RENAMED-BOUND, Enter, File > Save to library. The saved object reads id network-down, name RENAMED-BOUND, and its binding is still keyed network-down still holding network.download; 52 objects, 25 bindings, and nothing dangling. A rename moves the DISPLAY NAME and leaves the id alone, which is the documented contract: the id is the stable key bindings, the schema path and the envelope carry. So there is no route by which renaming an object can orphan its binding, and the asymmetry the row describes — delete throws while rename saves a dangling document — cannot arise from this. Note what IS true and now covered either way: vg-059s serialiser drop would catch a rename that did re-key, because it drops any binding whose key is not an object in the scene. So this row was unreachable before the fix and harmless after it, which is why the earlier claim that the two paths end differently no longer holds either.
check: Live: rename network-down to RENAMED-BOUND and save. The host document reads id network-down, name RENAMED-BOUND, binding still keyed network-down with semanticKey network.download, 52 objects and 25 bindings, and no key naming a missing object.

title: Collapsing or restoring a rail panel refits the theme to the space it freed
detail: FIXED, and the timing was the whole problem. Collapsing a panel hands the canvas 288px and the theme kept its zoom, so at a 1024-wide window the canvas grew from 370 to 658 and stayed at 22 percent — the freed space bought nothing. The viewport deliberately keeps its zoom across a resize, because a window nudge should not re-frame the theme, so the refit belongs on the panel toggle and not on the observer. It is done there by waiting on the viewport own change event, which is the signal that it has already resized. TWO WRONG VERSIONS FIRST, both worth recording because the second looked like a fix: one rAF fitted before the aside re-rendered, which fixed the collapse and left the restore at the collapsed zoom; two frames fitted before the viewports own ResizeObserver ran and did the same thing. Only the event is late enough to measure the new box. MEASURED at 1024 wide, the rows own case: 370 at 0.221, collapsed 658 at 0.394, restored 370 at 0.221. NOT PINNED BY A TEST, and the row should say so: the scroll half of this same commit is unit-tested and bites, but a refit test has to drive a whole React shell layout and the harness fought me for it, so I removed it rather than ship one that did not hold. The behaviour is verified in a browser, not by a unit test. HALF OF IT IS STILL OPEN AFTER THE FIX, re-measured by hand against cde9aa6 (collapsing a panel refits the theme to the space it freed) rather than taken from the agent's report. The panel half works: at 1024 the zoom badge reads 22%, hiding the layer panel takes the canvas 370 to 658 and the badge to 39%, which uses the freed width. THE WINDOW-RESIZE HALF DOES NOT - that is vg-072, filed from the same sitting. Closing this row for the panel case is right; the resize case was folded into it and did not come with it.
check: Collapsing or restoring the rail refits the theme to the space it freed: live at 1024x720, canvas 370px at zoom 0.221, collapsed 658px at 0.394, restored 370px at 0.221. Editor suite 1055 across 86 files.

title: The layer list answers the keys it declares by being a tree
detail: FIXED. The rows said the panel declares role=treeitem and answers to none of a trees keys, and that was right about the symptom and wrong about the cause: the code deliberately declined arrow keys, with a comment saying the window-level nudge handler owns them. THAT COMMENT WAS TRUE AND THE CONSEQUENCE WAS HIDDEN. The nudge defers only for a TEXT ENTRY — isTextEntryTarget — and a layer row is a div, so an unmodified arrow key was not blocked by the row, reached the nudge, and MOVED THE SELECTED OBJECT while the list did nothing at all. So the row was not merely missing keys, it was passing them somewhere worse. The row now takes ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End and ArrowRight/ArrowLeft, and stops propagation and prevents default, which is what lets the list be a list: navigation while focus is inside it, nudging while it is not. ArrowRight expands a collapsed group or steps into an expanded ones first child; ArrowLeft collapses or steps out to the parent, found by aria-level. MEASURED live with a real selection: from network-down, ArrowDown twice reaches network-card-icon, ArrowUp goes back, End reaches wordmark, Home reaches network-chart — and network-down is still at left 1355 top 702, where it was before any key was pressed.
check: Live: all four navigation keys move focus between rows, and the selected object does not move (left 1355, top 702 unchanged). Red without the handler: the new test fails on ArrowDown leaving focus where it was. Editor suite 1056 across 86 files.

title: A hidden layer is dimmed in the list, not only admitted by a tooltip
detail: FIXED, and it reuses a rule the stylesheet already had. The row measured a hidden row as identical to one that had never been touched — opacity 1 in both, same colour, nothing changed — with the eye buttons title the only tell. That is a mouse affordance for a state an author sets once and then forgets, and the list is the thing that should say what the canvas is doing. Rows now carry data-hidden, and the row dims on it with the SAME 0.45 an unreachable row uses for an entered group, because the two mean the same thing to an author: this is here but not available. MEASURED live: hiding cpu-card-icon through its own eye button takes the row to opacity 0.45 while gpu-card-icon beside it stays at 1. The rule deliberately does not stack with data-context=false, so a hidden row inside an entered group does not become 0.2 and unreadable. The test pins the ATTRIBUTE rather than a computed style, because jsdom applies no CSS and a computed opacity here would be a green test that proves nothing — the same trap as the marquee upper canvas and the bridge remove stub, both earlier today.
check: Live: hiding cpu-card-icon takes its row to opacity 0.45 with gpu-card-icon at 1. Red without the attribute: the new test fails on data-hidden being null. Editor suite 1057 across 86 files.

title: A focused layer row can be selected with the keyboard, so the list needs no mouse
detail: FIXED, and it is the residual of vg-067 rather than a separate problem: the rows own note says navigation works and no key SELECTS a row, which is true and is the other half of the same contract. A treeitem you can walk to but not pick is half a tree. Space selects the focused row, and Enter is deliberately left to rename, which already had it — so the two keys do not fight. MEASURED live end to end, which is the whole loop the row said was missing: click network-chart to start, ArrowDown twice to walk focus to network-down, and the selection is still network-chart; press Space and the selection becomes network-down; and the canvas follows, with getActiveObject returning network-down. So an author can navigate the list and pick from it without touching a pointer, and the object they pick is the one the canvas shows.
check: Live: navigate twice then Space selects the focused row, and the canvas active object becomes it. Red without the handler, the new test fails on selectLayer never called. Editor suite 1058 across 86 files.

title: A paired phone is served its own scripts, which it cannot carry a token for
detail: FIXED, AND IT IS THE PLAN FRAME BROKEN END TO END: a phone is the main display type, and a phone opening the hosts own pairing link got a blank page. REPRODUCED AND ISOLATED TO THE INTERFACE, not the phone: over LOOPBACK the same link renders the dashboard — 1 canvas, zero console errors, every asset 200 — while over the hosts LAN address the document is served and then everything it references is REFUSED. index-DKPxU5E6.js 403, echarts 403, favicon 403. THE CAUSE: the LAN guard sits before the static bundle routes, and a session token rides in the query string because fetch and EventSource carry one and script src cannot. So the guard was refusing the very request whose credential could never arrive. It was right about what it protects and placed too early. The bundle is not dashboard content — it is the same bytes any loopback visitor already has, with no reading, theme or device in it — so /assets/* and the favicon are now served ahead of the guard. Everything the guard exists for stays behind it: measured on an UNPAIRED device over the LAN, /api/themes/.../document 403, /api/display 403, /editor/ 403, /api/health 200, and the bundle 200. ADR-0019 records the search, including why the conventional answer — a cookie — is not this design, which pairs by a printed link with an expiring token.
check: Live: a paired phone at 390x844 over the LAN address renders the dashboard with 1 canvas and 0 console errors, where before the bundle and favicon were 403 and the page was blank. An unpaired device still gets 403 on the theme document, /api/display and /editor. Red without the exemption the test fails on the bundle being 403. Host suite 371 across 28 files.

title: The two Lines in the Insert menu no longer share a React key; their labels still do
detail: PARTLY FIXED, and the parts are worth separating. THE ROWS VISIBLE HALF IS WEAKER THAN FILED: the Insert menu DOES render group headings — Shape and Chart — so the chart Line is not unlabelled context, it sits under a Chart heading three items after Gauge. Measured live: thirteen items, Text then Shape then Chart, two entries reading Line. THE REAL DEFECT WAS UNDERNEATH IT, in the DOM rather than on screen: the item key was object.label, so a shape Line and a chart Line were two SIBLINGS WITH THE SAME REACT KEY, which is a reconciliation hazard rather than a cosmetic one. The key now carries what makes them different — shape:line and chart:line — so no two items in the menu can collide whatever they are called. STILL OPEN, and it is a copy decision rather than a bug: whether the chart family should read Line chart. That string is chartFamilies.line, shared with the Add pane and the inspector, so renaming it is a vocabulary change across three surfaces rather than a fix here, and it belongs to whoever owns that word. The group headings already do most of the disambiguating work; this fixes what was actually wrong under them.
check: Live on a rebuilt editor: the menu still lists all thirteen items with both Shape and Chart headings after the change, and the first Line still creates a line object named Line, so nothing was damaged. The key change is a one-line correctness fix with no surface to assert from — a unit test would have to re-derive the key expression and test its own arithmetic, so the claim rests on the code and the live check above rather than on a test that proves nothing.

title: A negative Size lands on the bound by ruling, and a test says why
detail: CONFIRMED AS FILED, THEN FOUND TO BE A RULING AND LEFT ALONE. The measurement holds: select storage-card-title, type -50 into Width, and the field and the object both read 1. But that is not an oversight — the repo decided it, wrote the decision down, and pinned it with a test whose comment names this exact case. refuses a value that would make the object invalid asserts that -5 lands on 1 and says why: it was restored to 40 with nothing recorded, and the floor is 1, so reverting is what made the bound undiscoverable. number-field.ts carries the same reasoning in code: Landing on the bound teaches it; reverting to the old value hides it. So the rows reading of AGENTS.md — refuse invalid numeric input rather than coercing — is about INVALID input, and the field does refuse it: X, 1e999, an empty string and 12.5.6 all leave the value untouched, exactly as the row itself measured. A negative size is a RANGE question the repo answered on purpose, not an invalid-input one, and reversing a considered ruling on the strength of a row that had not read the test would be wrong. I built the opt-in refusal, saw the existing test fail with expected 1 to be 240, and reverted. WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING: the field is silent about the change. An author who types -50 and watches a 240-wide object become 1 wide gets no message, and whether that should be said is a smaller and better question than whether the value should be taken.
check: A negative size lands on the bound by ruling, and the test says why: live, -50 and 0 both set field and object to 1 with no alert, while 300 applies normally; `refuses a value that would make the object invalid` pins the 1 and explains it. The suite is 1058 across 86 files after the revert.

title: One Import asset click declares the file once
detail: FIXED, AND I CAUSED IT. The row found a real defect and it was mine, introduced by the vg-070 work earlier today: I moved the pane two-step place into AssetManager.placeImage so the assets pane and a pasted image would share one path, and forgot that the pane already did the import itself. placeImage imported again, so one Import click declared the file twice — the row measured three options from one import of one file, with one Image object on the canvas, which is the signature of a declaration made twice and a placement made once. MEASURED BEFORE, on the select options rather than a closed select innerText, which is the correction the row itself asked for: BEFORE one option, starter-backdrop; after ONE Import click, THREE options — starter-backdrop, the name, and the name with a -2 suffix. AFTER the fix, one click gives two options and one object, and a SECOND import of the same file is correctly its own asset at -2 rather than a phantom. The fix is that placeImage takes the declaration the caller already made, so a caller that imports first and then places cannot be given a second one; a caller with no declaration still gets one, which the second test pins. The lesson is the one this pass keeps recording in a new shape: moving a two-step into its owner is not the same as removing the callers step, and nothing failed until someone did the most ordinary thing in the product — import a file.
check: Live: one Import click gives [starter-backdrop, name] and one image object, where it gave three options before; a second import of the same file gives name-2. Red without the fix the new test fails with two declarations. Editor suite 1060 across 86 files.

title: The editor says how much of the scene its artboard now holds
detail: FIXED, and the panel own comment is why it took this long. It said the scene was not its to read, so it stated a rule true at every size and therefore said nothing — measured, shrink the artboard to 700x400 with 44 of 52 objects outside and the sentence was byte-identical to its own before the change. The counting moved out of the player into scene-fabric, because WHICH objects an artboard does not contain is a fact about the scene and both surfaces now read one number rather than one of them guessing; the player keeps only what a display says about it. The panel takes the scene and measures on render. THE FAULT WAS MINE AND IT TOOK THE EDITOR DOWN AT BOOT: sceneNote() ran before let current: Artboard was assigned, so the filter read artboard.width off undefined and nothing mounted. Caught by loading the page rather than by any test, and confirmed by stashing the work and watching the editor boot clean — which is the check I should have reached for first, since the error was in a filter I had just written.
check: Live: at the Starter size the note is the rule; after resizing to 700x400 it reads 45 of 53 objects are now outside the artboard and will not be shown on a display. Editor suite 1371 across 117 files.

title: Circle and Triangle are gone; a new Ellipse arrives round
detail: RULED BY THE USER and built. The premise was checked first and holds: nothing in the editor kept a Circle round. Fabric keeps its radius in step with scaleX and scaleY, so one dragged corner makes it an ellipse, and the selection inspector already said so — a circle, an ellipse and a triangle own NO shape-specific field, each is fully described by the width and height the general fields carry. So a Circle protected nothing an author cannot undo with one number, and a 3-sided Polygon already reached a Triangle with MIN_POLYGON_SIDES at 3 and a side-count field. The Insert menu now reads Text, Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Polyline, Line, Path and a new Ellipse arrives at rx 180 and ry 180 — a circle, so the common case (a dot, a ring, a chip) is still the default and stretching it is one edit away. What was lost: two layer icons and one menu item each. What was gained: one entry per behaviour, and no shape whose name promises a constraint the product does not keep.
check: Live: the Insert menu lists seven shapes with no Circle and no Triangle, and inserting an Ellipse gives rx 180 and ry 180. The shape-kind test pins the list. Editor suite 1371 across 117 files.

title: Nothing anywhere says the document has unsaved changes
detail: MEASURED BY HUNTING FOR A SIGNAL THAT IS NOT THERE, which is the only way to measure an absence. There is a dedicated status element for it - footer.editor-shell-status, reading Fabric editor ready - so the affordance exists and is wired to something. It never changes. Select an object: still Fabric editor ready. Save to library: still Fabric editor ready. Type into the theme Name field and leave it unsaved, giving the document a real difference from what is on disk: still Fabric editor ready. Alongside it, the document title is Yunari — editor with no asterisk and no suffix, no element carries a class matching /dirty|unsaved|modified/i anywhere in the tree, and the body text contains no unsaved marker. So an author who has just renamed their theme and typed a rectangle has no visible signal that anything is pending. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC COMPLAINT IS THE COMBINATION WITH vg-060, and the two together are worse than either alone. vg-060 is that reopening the editor loads the Starter rather than the saved theme, so saved work disappears from view on reload. This is that nothing tells the author work is pending before they reload. An author renames a theme, adds a card, sees no dirty marker, closes the tab, reopens, and is looking at the Starter - with two independent signals that should have prevented it and neither present. There is a dirty key in the editor already: vg-026's own description records that isDirty is a string comparison against a key captured in the PersistenceManager constructor, and the Ctrl+N prompt consults it at editor-session.ts. So the state exists and is read in one place; it is simply never surfaced. The cheapest version of this fix is the status line the editor already has. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, because the fix does not work and the reason is worth the row. The obvious signal is save() in editor-shell, which is what every OBJECT manager calls, so I plumbed a document-change callback from it to the status bar and rendered Unsaved changes over the last message. Live, the status did not move: a nudge still read Fabric editor ready, and renaming the theme in the Name field still read Fabric editor ready, while Save to library correctly read Saved to library. So save() is NOT the funnel the rows hunt-by-hunting-for-a-signal assumed. There are at least THREE edit paths — object managers through save(), the nudge through the shortcut manager into canvas-nudge, and the theme and palette fields through their own panels commits — and only the first goes through it. The reason it matters: PersistenceManager.isDirty(current, assets) already answers this exactly, and the session already calls it, but only on the way to a replacement prompt. Wiring every edit path would duplicate a comparison that already exists; asking the session for the answer instead is the design question, not a patch. Reverted rather than shipped: a status bar that says Fabric editor ready while dirty would be worse than the current one, which at least says nothing false.
owner: editor/src/editor-session.ts; the footer mark is editor-shell/save-state.tsx
check: Live at 1280, in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8791. Untouched Starter: the footer reads nothing and session.isDirty() is false. Insert > Rectangle: 52 layers to 53 and the footer reads 'Unsaved changes' — and it STAYS that way, which is the half the reverted attempt failed. ArrowRight after a Save to library: the mark clears to empty, the object moves 361 to 362, the mark returns. Renaming the theme Name field to SENTINEL-9931, which the row names as a path that never reaches save(): the mark turns on with no Fabric event involved. Save to library: the footer reads 'Saved to library' with no mark, and isDirty() is still false 2.5 s later, so a save does not re-dirty itself. Editor suite 1037 across 87 files.

title: The browser will refresh or close with unsaved work and warn nobody
detail: RAISED BY THE USER, and confirmed by hand including a control that proves the measurement is sound rather than an automation blind spot. Select a palette token, click Import asset, choose one file - a real, unsaved change - then refresh. The page goes, 53 rows become 52, and nothing is said: no dialog, no status message, no prompt. Same on navigating away to another page. The obvious worry is that Chromium suppresses beforeunload dialogs under automation, which would make this unmeasurable here rather than absent. It is not: with a beforeunload handler installed by hand on the same page and the same harness, the reload DOES produce a dialog of type beforeunload and the harness records it. So the instrument can see exactly what the app is not producing, and the app produces none. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OBVIOUS: vg-060 already established that reopening the editor loads the Starter rather than the saved theme, and vg-071 that nothing anywhere signals unsaved work. This is the third leg of the same shape, and it is the one that is nearly free to fix - a beforeunload listener reading the isDirty key the editor already computes. Note the browser owns that dialog's wording and gives no room to customise it, so if the product wants to say what would be lost rather than just ask, that is a deliberate design call rather than something beforeunload can do. Related: vg-071 and vg-060.
owner: editor/src/editor-main.ts (the listener); the answer is editor/src/editor-session.ts
check: Live, with a dialog listener on the page, which is the control the row used to prove the instrument is not blind. A fresh load of the untouched Starter leaves with NO dialog, isDirty() false, 52 layers. Insert > Rectangle, then reload: the page raises a dialog of type beforeunload with an empty message — the browser owns that wording, so the app can only ask. Red without the fix: no dialog at all on either load, which is what the row measured.

title: Reopening the editor discards saved work and shows the Starter instead
detail: MEASURED THREE WAYS, and it is the second half of vg-059's damage. Rename the theme through the theme-settings Name field from System dashboard to SENTINEL-9931 - the field reads SENTINEL-9931 and the host's document reads {"name":"SENTINEL-9931"}. Then reload the editor page. The Name field reads System dashboard again and the layer list is the Starter's 52 rows. The saved work is still on the host - it is the editor that does not open it. So the author's round trip is: edit, see it saved, close the tab, reopen, and be holding the Starter with no prompt and no warning that what they were working on is still there. NOT THE SAME AS vg-026: that row is the discard prompt appearing when it should not, and this is a document that never being loaded in the first place, so even discarding everything correctly would not help. THE ACTIVE THEME IS UNSET, which is where I would look first but have not established: /api/themes/active returns {"active":null} alongside the theme list, so nothing designates yunari-demo-dashboard as what the editor should open, and Save to library evidently does not set it. Save to library, Release package and Open package are three different verbs in the File menu and only one of them is the one an author means by save. Worth noting for whoever picks this up: the editor does reach the library through File > Open library, so the path exists - what is missing is that the default open is the Starter rather than the author's own theme, and that Open library first raises the same spurious Save changes before opening another theme prompt that vg-026 is about. RE-CONFIRMED AT ITS STRONGEST, with the editor rebuilt and on the current mainline, and this time the work is a real object rather than a name. Rename the theme to MY-REAL-WORK, insert a Rectangle, File > Save to library: the host's document reads MY-REAL-WORK with 53 objects - the Starter's 52 plus the rectangle. Then reload the editor, which is what closing and reopening the tab does. The Name field reads System dashboard and the layer list shows 52 rows. The author's name is gone, their rectangle is gone, and nothing was said. This is the shape an author actually loses work in, and it is the same shape vg-071 makes invisible: there is no dirty marker to warn them before the reload (vg-071) and the reload itself discards the theme they were working on (this row). Together they are a session's work vanishing with no signal at either end. NOT THE DISCARD PROMPT and not the Starter's dirty-on-open state that vg-026 is about - I re-checked that guard this pass and it is correct, Ctrl+N on an untouched document goes straight to the size dialog and the prompt appears only after a real edit. The defect here is narrower and worse: the default document the editor opens is the template, not the author's own saved theme, and no part of the product says so.
owner: editor/src/boot-theme.ts; the host already carried the mtime this needs
check: Live, on a rebuilt editor against a host on 8791 with one saved theme. The row's own sequence, unchanged: rename to SENTINEL-9931, Insert > Rectangle (52 to 53 layers), File > Save to library — the host holds yunari-demo-dashboard named SENTINEL-9931. A bare /editor/ with no query string then opens 53 layers named SENTINEL-9931 with the footer reading 'Opened SENTINEL-9931', where it opened 52 Starter rows before. Two negatives hold: a dead ?theme=deleted-long-ago opens the same 53, and a second host on 8792 with an empty library opens 52 Starter rows. The unsaved marker reads empty in all three, so the reopened document is not falsely edited — the guard vg-026 established survives the new boot path. Red without the fix: 52 layers and System dashboard on every load. boot-theme suite 10 tests.

title: The colour picker jumps to the top-left of the window the moment it is clicked
detail: RAISED BY THE USER and reproduced exactly, with the coordinates. Open the palette, select Frosted panel, click Pick a colour. The picker opens where it should: 208 by 296 at (1773, 455), anchored beside the swatch that opened it in the right-hand panel. Click once anywhere inside it - the saturation square, which is the control an author reaches for first - and the picker's bounding box is (0, 6). Top-left corner of the window, full 2048 pixels away from where it was and roughly 1773 from the control that owns it. It stays there through subsequent clicks on hue and alpha. THE CONSEQUENCE IS WORSE THAN THE MOVEMENT. The panel now sits over the layer list on the far side of the window, so the controls and the colour they are editing are in different parts of the screen, and the swatch that opened it is off in the inspector with nothing pointing back to the panel that is now editing it. The screenshot at the moment of the jump shows the picker floating over the left rail while the Colour field it is driving reads #0a16234d on the far right. A picker that relocates on its first interaction is not merely misplaced - the author loses the link between what they are dragging and what it is changing, and on a laptop at a smaller window the jump can also push it partly off screen. Nothing here about where it should go is arguable: anchored, and not moving, is what every other colour control does.
check: Live at 1600x900 against host 8792, measuring the same four numbers the row did. Red: picker 208x296 at (1325, 480) beside its trigger at (1325, 444); one click in the saturation square and it reads (0, 6), with the trigger node tagged beforehand now absent from the document. Green, after the fix: the picker reads (1325, 480) at open, after a saturation drag, after a hue click and after a close-and-reopen, and the tagged trigger is still connected at all four. The popover hex and the panel's Colour field agree at every step (#1519234d), and the frosted cards on the canvas take the committed colour. The panel test pins the surviving node and is red with the rebuild guard forced on. Editor suite 1044 across 87 files.

title: The gradient control is confusing to use, and it discards the colour it replaces
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - the gradient control is very confusing to use - which is a judgement I am recording rather than contradicting, and which one measurement sharpens rather than settles. WHAT I COULD MEASURE is what the control does to an author's existing work. Select the Frosted panel token, which is a 30% alpha #0815234d used by eight objects, and switch Paint from Solid to Linear gradient. The panel gives Angle, Stop 1 position, Stop 1 colour, Stop 2 position, Stop 2 colour and Add stop, and it is usable - I typed 8-digit hex into a stop and it saved and rendered exactly - so this is not a report of a broken control. What it does is replace the token's colour with #ffffff and #000000, both fully opaque, and both defaults are unlike the colour they are replacing: a 30% frosted panel becomes an opaque black-to-white sweep across eight objects, from one dropdown choice, with the previous colour gone and only undo to get it back. The token row does say Frosted panel · 8, so the author has the count, and the defaults are a defensible starting point. But a gradient seeded with white and black is a colour nobody would have chosen for a frosted panel, and the control offers no starting-from-current behaviour, which is the one thing that would make it feel predictable. THE COMFUSION THE USER DESCRIBED MAY BE EXACTLY THIS and is worth naming rather than assuming: the first thing the control does to a colour is overwrite it with two unrelated colours. That is a design answer, not a defect, and it is the user's call - but the measurement is what an author meets first, and seeding from the current value costs nothing.
check: Live on the row's own token, Frosted panel with its 8 uses, against host 8791 on a rebuilt editor. Red: Paint Solid #0815234d, switch to Linear gradient, and the stops read #ffffff and #000000 - the colour replaced is gone and both are opaque. Green: stops read #0815234d and #0815234d, and switching back to Solid reads #0815234d again, so a round trip loses nothing in either direction. The screenshot at the gradient state shows the panel's stop swatches still translucent and the frosted cards on the canvas still glass. The palette tests pin the seed in both directions and are red against the old white-to-black default. Editor suite 1045 across 87 files.

title: A pasted image is saved as a blob: URL and never becomes an asset, so it is gone everywhere else
detail: MEASURED END TO END, AND IT IS SILENT DATA LOSS. Put a PNG on the clipboard, click the canvas, press Ctrl+V. The image appears on the canvas at 0,0, is named Image, and the inspector shows it with a Crop button - the paste path itself works. Then File > Save to library. The saved document does contain an object named Image, and its src reads blob:http://127.0.0.1:5311/081c983e-cebf-4fd8-b75a-8d9a3e45bfc8. A blob URL is a handle into one browser session's memory; it means nothing in any other tab, any other browser, on a phone, or on a second visit.  HALF FIXED, AND THE REAL BLOCKER IS NOW NAMED. A pasted image took the HALF-ONLY PATH: the clipboard called imageManager.importImage and stopped, so the object kept the blob URL it was decoded from and nothing ever declared the bytes. The assets pane did both halves and the paste did not, which is why an asset import survives and a paste does not. AssetManager now owns both — placeImage declares the file AND puts it on the canvas — and the assets pane and a paste both go through it, so neither can take the half-only path again. The clipboard manager takes its importer from the session, which owns the asset manager; the shell builds it before that exists, so the importer is installed rather than injected.
