MEASURED on a pasted PNG: the saved envelope now declares assets/pasted-probe.png and the object carries yunariAsset {assetId pasted-probe, kind image}, which it did not before. STILL BROKEN, and this is the part that matters: the objects src STILL serialises as blob:http://... because NOTHING IN THE RENDERER RESOLVES yunariAsset. Searched every reader — the asset manager uses it to count references and to refuse removal, and scene-fabric only writes and reads it as a property; no adapter, scene or player path turns an assetId into a URL. So the bytes now ship and the image still does not travel, and the remaining fix is not in the editor at all: the scene has to resolve the reference the way it already resolves background media through createAssetResolver. Until that exists, a pasted image is a session handle with a copy of its bytes attached. Editor suite 1055 across 86 files. THE PLAYER HALF IS FIXED ON ba043ee AND THE ROW STAYS OPEN, because the editor half is worse than this row recorded. REPRODUCED FIRST, unchanged: paste a PNG (synthetic clipboard event carrying a 4x4 image), File > Save to library, and the host document declares assets/pasted-probe.png and assets/pasted-probe-2.png while both objects still carry src blob:http://127.0.0.1:8791/... . PLAYER, after ba043ee: at 390x839 a fresh load of that theme requests /api/themes/yunari-demo-dashboard/assets/pasted-probe.png and pasted-probe-2.png over HTTP and logs no error, where before it asked for the dead blob. The scene tests pin the rewrite and go red without it. EDITOR, and this is the finding worth carrying forward: reopening that same saved theme in the editor does not show a broken image, it DROPS THE OBJECT. 53 objects come back where the document holds 55, no object on the canvas carries yunariAsset at all, and the console shows ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND on both blob URLs. Fabric enlivens from src alone, so a dead blob URL means the object is never created, which leaves AssetManager.hydrate - the thing that exists to revive exactly these images - with nothing to hydrate. The next save then writes 53 objects and the loss is permanent and silent. This row said the editor half was done and that the remaining fix was not in the editor; that is true of DECLARING the asset and not of surviving a reload. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: the resolver the editor needs is AssetManager.previewUrl, but the manager is a field of EditorSession constructed empty and loaded in its constructor, while the shell that revives the scene is mounted BEFORE the session exists - and the manager must hold this document's bytes before the revive, not after. Wiring it means moving the manager lifecycle out of the session into editor-main and adding it to EditorSessionOptions. That spans three owners and is a change of ownership rather than a patch, so it is recorded here rather than made inside the player fix. AND THE EDITOR HALF IS FIXED TOO, on dbde35a, so the paragraph above is the state of the finding before the fix rather than its final state. The ownership moved rather than being worked around: mountEditorShell revives the scene before a session exists, so the bytes have to be resolvable before EditorSession is constructed - and the session built its AssetManager as a field and loaded it in its own constructor, after. editor-main builds and loads one manager now, the first moment holding both the document and its bytes, and hands the same instance to the session; that left EditorSessionOptions.assets a second way to hand over the same bytes that nothing read, so it is gone. ON f3736ad THE URL IS ALSO STRIPPED FROM THE SAVE, which is what the paragraph above said was still shipping: Fabric writes src on every image whatever the caller asked for, and serialiseScene now takes it back off wherever the object carries yunariAsset - leaving an image with no reference alone, because it has nothing to resolve. THAT CHANGE HAD ONE MORE CONSEQUENCE, worth recording because it would have been a new silent loss one keystroke away: history serialises through the same serialiser and revived without a resolver, so a stripped src would have made every undo of a pasted image delete it. The history manager now revives through the same resolver the mount does. FINAL ROUND TRIP, one save and one reload of each: the document holds 55 objects with both pasted images carrying yunariAsset and no src, and the string blob: appears nowhere in the scene; the editor reopens at 55 with both images decoding at naturalWidth 4; the player fetches both assets over HTTP from that document; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y hold at 55 with both images decoding.
check: Both halves, measured against the numbers that proved them. RED, unchanged: a pasted PNG (synthetic clipboard event, 4x4) then File > Save to library declares assets/pasted-probe.png and pasted-probe-2.png while both objects still save src blob:http://127.0.0.1:8791/... ; reopening that theme in the editor gave 53 objects and 53 layer rows where the document held 55, no object on the canvas carried yunariAsset, and the console reported ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND on both blob URLs. GREEN, player (ba043ee): at 390x839 a fresh load requests /api/themes/yunari-demo-dashboard/assets/pasted-probe.png and pasted-probe-2.png over HTTP with no console error. GREEN, editor (dbde35a): the same theme reopens at 55 objects and 55 layer rows on two consecutive reloads, both images carry yunariAsset and both decode (naturalWidth 4), and Save to library writes a document of 55 with both references and both declared assets. Scene tests pin the revival rewrite and go red without it; the asset-manager test pins a reference with no bytes answering undefined rather than throwing. 2433 tests across 180 files.
owner: scene-fabric/src/persist.ts (the revival); editor/src/editor-main.ts now owns the asset manager

title: The Language setting saves a locale that nothing ever reads
detail: WITHDRAWN — the finding's premise is wrong, and the user corrected it twice. Ruling 2026-10-01: "Language is only used for time text & external api sensor sources that return a text value, weather, for example", amended by: "what I meant for language is as a theme property: the author declared what language the theme was designed in. And it also govern datetime string render." THE ROW IS REFUTED BY A SPEC THAT WAS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, not by anything this session did: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-clock-and-theme-locale.md, status implemented, five days before the row was filed. The language is a fact about the theme, declared once by its author as metadata.locale — a BCP 47 tag beside name, author and description — so the theme reads in the language its author wrote it in and a library can filter on the fact. A v2 theme WITHOUT metadata.locale is refused, and so is a malformed or unrenderable tag: refused rather than degraded, so a theme never saves a language the runtime cannot show (fabric-envelope-validate.ts:126-151, owner themeLanguage at :121, whose own docblock names the failure mode it refuses — rendering "English behind the author's back"). The editor control ships as the spec asked: artboard-panel.ts has the curated-list select with the resolved month and weekday names shown live beside it, so the author sees words rather than a tag. WHAT THE ROW GOT WRONG, TWICE. First, it filed as its sharpest evidence that the player writes its own chrome in English in all fifteen locales — the one piece of text the product itself puts on the page. The spec answers that in its Non-goals: "Authoring copy for a theme's own labels. A theme's literal text is its text." The chrome is not what this property governs, so its being untranslated is correct, and translating it would have been the wrong fix. Second, it opened by claiming the setting "saves a locale nothing reads", which fc5c339 had already answered and the spec answers completely. The only half that was ever real is that a provider text value is not locale-formatted — and there is no such provider. formatTextReading at plan.ts:512 consults the locale only for a key the vocabulary marks instant, and every other text value is returned verbatim; today's text values are captions of identity (CPU manufacturer/brand/model at library.ts:497-516, GPU and drive names at lhm.ts:273 and library.ts:401) plus the clock's ISO instant. Weather is a future roadmap feature with no design, named in the spec only so that a later locale-aware provider reads the same declared fact. AN AGENT WAS DISPATCHED TO LOOK FOR IT BEFORE THE SPEC WAS READ. It wrote nothing and stood down, but the dispatch was the error and it is recorded here so the next one is not repeated: this repo had settled the question five days earlier and one reading of docs/superpowers/specs/ would have caught it.

title: The editor still does not refit the theme when the window is resized
detail: FILED SEPARATELY BECAUSE IT SURVIVED THE FIX FOR vg-068, and measured by hand rather than taken from the agent's report. Open the editor at 2048 wide and the zoom badge reads 83%. Resize the window to 1600 and it reads 83%; to 1280, still 83%; to 1024, still 83%. One number across a 1024-pixel change, while the canvas behind it goes 1394, 946, 626, 370. Click Zoom to fit at that last size and the badge reads 22% - so the fit calculation is right and something else has to ask for it. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT IS WHICH EVENT FIRES THE REFIT. cde9aa6 made a PANEL COLLAPSE refit, and that works: at 1024, hiding the layer panel takes the canvas 370 to 658 and the zoom 22% to 39%. A WINDOW RESIZE is a different event and did not get the same treatment. This is the half that matters in ordinary use, because a deliberate panel toggle is rare and resizing a window - or opening it at a size and keeping it - is what everyone does. An author whose window is not the width they opened the editor at spends the session looking at a theme at the wrong zoom inside a black field, and the badge reads a confident number throughout. Nothing recomputes on resize; only the click recomputes it. A ResizeObserver already exists on the body in this app for other purposes, so the seam is present. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, and the reason it was reverted is the useful part. CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS FILED: at 2048 the badge reads 83% with the canvas at 1394; resize to 1024 and it still reads 83% with the canvas at 370, and the artboard still starts at x 98, so 1290 of its 1388 pixels run off the right edge. Zoom to fit at that size gives 22%, so the fit exists — it is just not automatic. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Holding the zoom and re-centring the translation on every resize does exactly what the row wants — measured, at 370 the board then spans -512 to 882 against a 370 canvas, so it is centred and the rest is reachable by panning — and it BREAKS keeps the point under the cursor fixed while zooming, which resize() calls on construction and on every host size change. Panning to inspect a corner and then any resize, spurious or not, yanks the camera back to centre. That test failing is the finding, not an accident of the harness. So the question is not how to re-centre but WHEN: only when the camera was showing the whole board, so an authors pan survives and a fitted view follows the window. That needs a condition on the previous camera state — was it fitted or contained — which the viewport does not currently keep. Reverted rather than shipped: a camera that cannot be left where the author put it is a worse defect than one that leaves part of the board off the edge.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8799, resizing the window with the camera untouched since mount: the zoom badge read 83% at 2048, 57% at 1600, 37% at 1280 and 22% at 1024 as the canvas went 1394, 946, 626, 370 - one number per width, where every width read 83% before. Then the inverse, which is the invariant the reverted attempt broke: zoomed off fit to 19% and resized 2048 to 1280 and on to 1600, the badge held 19% at all three. Clicked Zoom to fit, back to 57%, and a further resize to 1400 refitted it to 45%.

title: A chart's aspect ratio changes its height but the inspector's Height field never updates
detail: MEASURED AS A DIRECT COMPARISON after a wrong first reading, which is worth recording because it nearly cost this row. I first concluded the three ratio buttons did nothing: geometry stayed 963x215 through 3:1, 4:1 and 2:1, and the buttons had no aria-pressed, no class and no computed-style difference. Both halves of that were instrument error. The style half: the screenshot showed 3:1 boxed after I had clicked 4:1, and I had sampled backgroundColor, which is rgb(245, 241, 232) on all three - the visible box is the focus ring, and there is genuinely no selected state. The effect half: I read the chart before saving, so the document had not caught up. THE FEATURE WORKS. Save after each click and the host's document gives the truth: 4:1 takes the height 215 to 241, 3:1 to 321, 2:1 to 482, all at width 963 - exactly the ratios named. THE DEFECT IS THE INSPECTOR DISAGREES WITH ALL OF IT. Across every click the Height field in the selection inspector reads 215, unchanged, while the object it is describing is 241, then 321, then 482. Four consecutive comparisons, mismatch on every one. So an author sets 2:1, watches the chart double in height, and reads a Height field that still says 215 - and the canvas dock and the field that owns the geometry are telling them two different things about the same object. That is the same class as the layer list disagreeing with the document, and it is the more dangerous of the two here, because the Height field is editable: an author who reads 215, believes it, and types a height is editing against a number the product no longer holds. The second half is small and cheap and worth doing alongside: nothing in the control group says which ratio is active - no aria-pressed on any of the three, no class, no style difference at all - so after clicking there is no way to tell 2:1 was applied from 3:1.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor, with network-chart selected at W 430: clicking 4:1 put Height at 108, 3:1 at 143 and 2:1 at 215, each the width over its ratio, where the field read 215 through all three before. aria-pressed followed at every step - 4:1 true, then 3:1 true with the others false, then 2:1 true with the others false - where no button carried any pressed state at all before.

title: The same thirteen type presets are listed two ways in one inspector: 46-600 and Ring unit
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - there seems to be 2 types of type presets display names being used, one using word, for example Caption. and one using numbers, example 46-600 - and confirmed by reading both lists off the same selected object. The document holds thirteen presets keyed 20-400, 17-400, 20-500, 24-400, 24-500, 32-400, 36-500, 44-600, 46-600, 60-600, 90-600, 108-300 and mono. In one inspector the selection reads Type preset: typePresets.24-400 - Segoe UI, sans-serif 400 24px, and its dropdown offers that same list as 20-400, 17-400, 20-500, 24-400, up to mono. In the adjacent dropdown, one field lower, the same thirteen are Caption, Overline, Rate, Card title, Period, Date, Wordmark, Share, Ring unit, Ring reading, Card reading, Clock and Mono. Same count, same order, two vocabularies. WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN COSMETIC: the two lists do not agree on what is selected. With the object on 24-400, the numeric dropdown holds typePresets.24-400 and the word dropdown holds 20-400 - the values differ, and comparing them as raw strings says the two controls disagree when they do not, or hides a real mismatch when they do. Neither list is obviously wrong - the words are what an author thinks in and the numbers are what the theme file stores - but an author cannot look at 24-400 and then find 24-400 in the list below, and cannot look at Ring unit and find Ring unit above. The TYPE PRESETS panel lower down uses the words too, so the numeric scheme appears in the selection inspector alone.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor with cpu-card-title selected: the run's Type preset dropdown lists all thirteen presets by their authored names - Caption, Overline, Rate, Card title, Period, Date, Wordmark, Share, Ring unit, Ring reading, Card reading, Clock, Mono - where it listed 20-400, 17-400, 20-500, 24-400 and the ids up to mono. The option values are unchanged stored refs, and the selection reads back typePresets.24-400 as Card title.

title: The View menu's three settings silently cycle between two unnamed states, one of which is 1 FPS
detail: MEASURED BY CLICKING THROUGH EACH CYCLE, which is what it took to discover they are cycles at all. The View menu has three items and they read as settings - Data source: Preview, Chart refresh: 30 FPS, Value runs: values. None opens a submenu: aria-haspopup and aria-expanded are both null, and clicking one closes the menu and changes the label. Clicking each seven times in turn gives the complete cycles. Data source alternates Preview and Live. Value runs alternates values and tokens. Chart refresh alternates 30 FPS and 1 FPS. That is every value each offers. THREE PROBLEMS, and the third is the one an author would file. THE CHOICES ARE NEVER SHOWN. A menu item that toggles gives the author no way to know what the other state is, what it does, or that it exists - they can only click and read the label afterwards. A submenu, a radio group, or even a confirmation would all answer it; none does. ONE OF THE STATES IS THIRTY TIMES WORSE. Chart refresh goes from 30 FPS to 1 FPS on a single click. An author reaching into the View menu for one setting and mis-clicking lands in a preview that updates once a second, which reads as the editor hanging, and nothing on screen says why it got slow or that a second click fixes it. THE STATE IS NOT EXPOSED. No aria-checked on any of the three, so a screen reader announces a plain menu item and never says which of the two states is current - and the label text, which is the only thing carrying the state, is what a screen reader is least likely to re-read on focus. The honest comparison is one click away: the zoom badge offers Zoom to fit, Zoom to selection and 100 % as a real submenu with three visible items, so the menu is not uniformly ignorant of the pattern - these three are.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor with the View menu open: all three settings carry aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded="false", where all three carried null before. Chart refresh opened to role="menuitemradio" entries reading 30 FPS with aria-checked="true" and 1 FPS with aria-checked="false", so the choices are visible and a screen reader announces which state is current instead of leaving it to label text.

title: A saved theme can never be deleted, so the library only grows
detail: CHECKED ON BOTH SIDES, because a missing button and a missing capability are different rows. On the settings page - the one surface that lists the library - the entire set of visible controls is Open the editor, the Starter template link, the theme's own button, and Edit. Nothing anywhere reads delete, remove, trash or discard. The File menu offers New theme, New from starter, Open package, Save package, Release package, Open library and Save to library, and none of them removes a theme either. So an author who has been iterating can see every experiment they have ever made in their library and cannot remove any of them. The API is not the missing half: DELETE on a theme returns 405 Method Not Allowed, so the host does not expose deletion either - this is absent by design or by omission, not merely unlinked from a UI. THE COUNTER-CLAIM I WOULD RAISE AGAINST MY OWN ROW, recorded because it is a real one and because a theme is a folder on disk (ADR-0017), so deleting one is a destructive filesystem operation with no undo. That may well be why it is not there, and I have NOT established that it is an oversight rather than a decision - which is exactly what makes this a question rather than a defect report. What I can say is what the author meets today: a list with no prune, on a product whose own File menu has Rename, Save as and Activate either available or explicitly named as missing work (vg-034), so the author is being told the management verbs exist. If deletion is deliberately out of scope, the settings page is the place that should say so, because right now the absence reads as an oversight to anyone who has not read the ADR.
check: Live on this PC against a host on 8799, a saved theme can now be deleted from the library listing, which before offered only Open and Edit. Deleted cpu-only from /settings/library.html: the confirmation named it and said it would be moved to the recycle bin where it can be got back, the row then disappeared, the folder was gone from the themes directory, and the Windows recycle bin held cpu-only with its original path D:\yunari-pass\themes - asked of the shell, not inferred. LIMIT, STATED IN THE CHECK BECAUSE IT IS REAL: the macOS osascript route and the Linux gio/trash-put routes were NOT executed - only Windows was, and the earlier claim that all three work rested on route-level assertions, one of which was in fact broken.

title: Large type presets clip their text at the bottom while the box keeps its height
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - the text box is broken, selecting up to 46-600 is fine but 60-600 and the presets below make the text get clipped in the bottom while its bounding box still enlarged - and reproduced on the CPU card title. Select cpu-card-title, whose Size reads W 140 and H 27, and walk the inspector's Type preset dropdown upward through Ring unit (46-600), Ring reading (60-600), Card reading (90-600) and Clock (108-300). The HEIGHT FIELD NEVER MOVES. It reads 27 before, and 27 after every single one, while the rendered text grows. At 90-600 the canvas shows the card title clipped: the word CPU renders as PU with the leading C cut off, because the glyphs are now far taller than the 27px box the inspector still reports. So the object is in a state where its own geometry field and its own rendering disagree, which is the same failure shape as vg-084 - the aspect ratio control changes the height and the field does not follow - and it is arguably worse here, because this is not a control the author chose deliberately; picking a bigger preset is an ordinary act and the result is text that cannot be read. The user's wording says the bounding box still enlarges; what I measured is that it does NOT change at all while the text overflows it. Both are a disagreement between the box and the text, so the finding stands either way, and the precise direction is recorded here so the next person is not looking for a box that grows. One more detail worth carrying: after applying a preset the dropdown does not hold it. The screenshot taken at 90-600 shows the inspector reading back 24-400.
check: Live on canvas in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8802, the whole symptom gone. cpu-card-title at 90-600 rendered as PU with the leading C cut off in its 27px box; after dragging the bottom vertical edge — both mt and mb answering n-resize where they had been hidden — Height went 27 to 241 with W held at 140 and Y at 212, and the same preset then rendered CPU whole at 90px weight 600. The preset readback holds typePresets.90-600 as Card reading, so the dropdown never lost it. Suite 2499 across 182 files.

title: The suite reports an unhandled error from a requestAnimationFrame callback after its test has already passed
detail: Seen while running the milestone gate, and pre-existing rather than introduced here: git log over new-object-panel.ts and its test across every commit of this pass returns nothing, and the file's own 36 tests all pass. The error is a TypeError, Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'enterEditing'), thrown from the requestAnimationFrame callback at new-object-panel.ts:111-113 - the frame fires after the test has finished and the DOM it closed over is gone, so the guard on line 112 passes against a canvas whose active object is already nothing and line 113 dereferences a text that is not there. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A LINE IN THE LOG: vitest counts it as an unhandled error, so every full run prints an Unhandled Errors block, and a suite that always prints an error is a suite whose next real failure will be read past. It is also the shape of the defect the callback is trying to prevent - the guard is half a guard, checking the active object but not the object it came from. Cheapest correct fix is a cancel-on-teardown or an optional chain on the frame, with a test that asserts no unhandled rejection escapes the file. CAUSE FOUND, AND THE ROW'S OWN GUESS WAS WRONG IN THE SAME WAY vg-090's WAS — recorded because two wrong guesses in a row is a pattern worth naming. The row suggested a cancel-on-teardown or an optional chain on the frame. Neither: PRODUCTION IS SOUND. TextManager.addText is typed `(options?) => Textbox`, so the returned object is never undefined and the guard `if (editor.canvas.getActiveObject() !== text) return` is correct — when the canvas has no active object the comparison is true and it returns. The fault was in two test cases that passed a bare `vi.fn()` as `addText`, cast `as never` to satisfy the type. That stub returns undefined, and then the guard compares undefined against undefined, which is FALSE, so it falls through and dereferences it. The same half-guard the row described, reached by a stub that broke the contract rather than by a gap in the guard — which is why an optional chain would have hidden it rather than fixed it. FIXED IN THE TEST at both sites: the call-assertion one still records its calls and now returns the Textbox the file's own textWithEditing helper already models. No source change and no new assertion, because a test asserting production behaviour here would have been a test asserting the stub. Evidence is the count: one unhandled error across the file's 36 tests became none, all passing.
check: Ran the file and read the error count rather than the pass count: 36 tests passed with one unhandled error before, and 36 pass with no unhandled error after. No assertion was added, because the defect was a stub that returned undefined where `TextManager.addText` promises a Textbox, and a test asserting production behaviour there would have been a test asserting the stub.

title: A bar chart's bar takes a corner radius but the track behind it does not
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - bar chart's bar can have corner radius but not the track behind it - and the shape of it matches the storage card the Starter ships, where the filled bar has rounded ends and the unfilled remainder behind it is square. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED YET: I have confirmed the asymmetry exists in the shipped theme by reading the bar object's paints, but I have not yet driven the editor's own controls to change a radius and watched the two ends respond differently, so the exact control and the exact field are not established here. Carried as the user filed it with that limit stated, because the surface is small and the report is specific enough to check: the claim is not that radius is missing, it is that it is available for one of the two shapes and not the other, which is the kind of asymmetry usually caused by a shared renderer taking one property from one paint and not the other rather than by a deliberate choice. REPRODUCED, AND THE ROW IS RIGHT AND A MEASUREMENT THAT SAID OTHERWISE WAS WRONG — recorded because a wrong correction is worse than no correction. The root measured this twice and got it wrong both times before the user corrected it: the first search was scoped to the selection panel, and the DOM-wide search that followed ran with a LINE chart selected, which has no bar to round and so offers no radius. The truth, with storage-bar selected, is that the chart's own settings section reads in order: Add a series, Binding, Precision, Unit display, Scale, Offset, Orientation, Minimum, Maximum, Bar width, Category gap %, CORNER RADIUS, Show axes, Show labels, Fill paint, TRACK PAINT. Corner radius is a number input reading 10 with min 0 — the authored value. Bar width is a number reading 20, Category gap % a number reading 40 bounded 0 to 100. So the user saw a real control and the row is correct as filed: THE BAR CAN TAKE A CORNER RADIUS AND THE TRACK CANNOT. Track paint is a select over palette tokens reading palette.chartTrack, and there is no radius beside it — the track is a paint reference with no geometry at all, so this is not a control that was forgotten but a field that does not exist. WHAT THE FIX IS, NOW THAT IT IS CORRECTLY FRAMED: either the track gains a radius field beside its paint, or the bar's radius is understood to apply to the whole progress bar and the two are rounded together. The first is a renderer change and a new authored field; the second is a smaller change and a different look. That choice is the user's and is still open. A THIRD THING THIS MEASUREMENT FOUND, filed as vg-103: none of the five controls above has an id, and none of their labels has an htmlFor — Bar width, Category gap %, Corner radius, Fill paint and Track paint are all unassociated, where every other field in this shell pairs a label with yunari-number-N or yunari-token-N. That is also why two automated lookups failed before a structural one succeeded.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor with storage-bar selected, the settings section now carries Corner radius and Track corner radius as two separate labelled controls — Corner radius resolving to yunari-chart-setting-cornerRadius reading 10, Track corner radius to yunari-chart-setting-trackCornerRadius reading 10 — so a track can take a radius of its own, which it could not before because the field did not exist. WHAT THE ROOT DID NOT RE-MEASURE, STATED SO THE CHECK IS NOT READ AS MORE THAN IT IS: the two being independent on canvas is the dispatched agent's measurement, not the root's. It set track 0 against bar 20 and the reverse and read the corner inset signature of each row, and it established the mechanism from the shipped library rather than the docs — BarSeries.d.ts types backgroundStyle as ItemStyleOption with borderRadius, and BarView.js builds that background rect from the bar slot's own geometry, so the background is the track and its radius rounds the ends. The root's browser was contended by two other agents during its own attempt and it did not get a clean second reading.

title: The chart's own settings fields have no id and no htmlFor, so nothing associates them
detail: FOUND WHILE REPRODUCING vg-090, where it cost two failed automated lookups before a structural one found the control at all. With a bar chart selected, its settings section carries five controls — Bar width, Category gap %, Corner radius, Fill paint and Track paint — and not one of them has an id, while none of their five labels has an htmlFor. Every other field in the editor shell pairs a label with a control: the geometry fields use yunari-number-N, the paint fields yunari-token-N, and artboard-panel's rows set label.htmlFor and control.id together. So this section is the exception, and the exception is invisible to a screen reader, unaddressable by a test or an automation, and unclickable by name. It is an accessibility defect first and a testability one second, and the two cost each other here: searching the DOM for a corner-radius control by label returned nothing because there was no association to find, twice. WORTH NAMING PRECISELY SO IT IS NOT OVER-FIXED: the control exists and works, reads 10 with min 0, and is not a missing feature — the defect is that it is unlabelled. The fix is ids and htmlFor in the order the section already builds them, plus a test that asserts every control in this section is reachable by its label rather than by position.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor with storage-bar selected, every control in the chart's settings section is reachable BY ITS LABEL, which is the lookup that returned nothing twice before: Corner radius resolves through htmlFor yunari-chart-setting-cornerRadius to an input reading 10, Track corner radius to yunari-chart-setting-trackCornerRadius reading 10, Bar width to yunari-chart-setting-barWidth reading 20, and Track paint to yunari-chart-paint-track. A control is now associated with its label by id rather than by position, and the test that asserts it walks control.labels across all four families and checks the ids are unique.

title: The host workspace's typecheck is red on a pre-existing test error
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-092 and NOT FIXED, because the file belongs to a task another agent held. host/src/theme-list.dom.test.ts:397 fails tsc with "Property 'dataset' does not exist on type 'Element'", which fails npm run typecheck at the host workspace — so the repo's typecheck gate is red on a line nobody has touched. Confirmed pre-existing against f496227 with the file unmodified. Worth its own row because a permanently red gate is one nobody reads, and this one is the gate that catches exactly the class of mistake the rename this pass shipped could have made. THE PROVENANCE WAS WRONG, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. The row as filed said the error was pre-existing on f496227 with the file unmodified, which is true and is exactly how a red gate stays red: it reads as the terrain rather than as a mistake somebody made. It was not terrain. `querySelectorAll("button[data-theme]")` at :397 came from this pass's own vg-085 host library page commit, because the attribute selector defeats the tag-name overload TypeScript uses to narrow the element type, so the array is Element[] and `dataset` is not on Element. Nothing noticed it because a permanently failing check is one nobody reads — and an agent reporting it as pre-existing is the clearest possible demonstration of that. Fixed with the generic the rest of the suite already uses for this.
check: Ran the gate rather than the file: npm run typecheck across every workspace reports zero errors, where the host workspace had been failing on this one line. The file's own 25 tests pass and its typecheck is clean in isolation.

title: Drag-reorderable layer rows advertise nothing: the cursor is default on a draggable row
detail: CONDITIONAL ON vg-087, and recorded rather than dropped because it was nearly lost. Found while investigating vg-087, which does NOT reproduce: editor-shell/layer-panel.tsx:272-320 carries draggable plus all four handlers (onDragStart writing the application/x-yunari-layer payload Chrome requires, onDragOver cancelling the event and marking same-parent slots, onDrop into bridge.reorderLayer, onDragEnd), bridge.ts:248-283 does the real Fabric moveObjectTo, and all four are present in the shipped dist bundle. The agent read the minified row JSX rather than trusting the source. SO: if drag genuinely works, cursor: default at editor-shell.css:597 is the wrong cursor on a draggable row, and an author gets no affordance for a gesture the panel offers. If drag does NOT work live, this is a symptom of the real defect rather than a finding of its own, and vg-087 stays open instead. WHICH IT IS IS UNRESOLVED and only a real drag in a real browser settles it: the root must build first and retry, because STATUS.md records a stale bundle already cost this pass two wrong conclusions. The likeliest second explanation, unmeasured and deliberately not fixed by that agent, is a drag STARTING ON A CHILD ELEMENT — the eye and lock buttons stop propagation, so a drag begun on a button never opens a payload. That is checkable in the same pass: drag from the row label, then from the button, and say which works. CONFIRMED on a fresh build: computed cursor on a draggable layer row is auto, and mid-drag it stays auto even over a valid same-parent drop target. The conditional in this row is now resolved - drag genuinely works, so the cursor is simply the wrong one. CONFIRMED on a fresh build: the computed cursor on a draggable layer row is auto, and mid-drag it stays auto even over a valid same-parent drop target. The conditional in this row is now resolved - drag genuinely works between siblings, so the cursor is simply the wrong one. FIXED AND VERIFIED ON CANVAS. editor-shell.css:597 pinned `cursor: default` on a row whose `draggable` was honest; it is now `grab`, with `pointer` restored on the buttons inside the row so a control does not read as a handle. Measured mid-gesture on a rebuilt bundle (host 8809, asset mtime 1s old at read time, hash index-CfR8Bpbk.js): the source row computes `grabbing`, a valid same-parent slot computes `copy`, a refused row computes `not-allowed`, and a row at rest computes `grab`. The dropdown case named in the conditional was not the cause and needed no fix: a drag from the row label starts a payload, and the buttons stop propagation for their own click but the drag path was already driven from the label in every measurement here.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor, computed cursor on a draggable layer row reads grab at rest and grabbing mid-drag, over a valid same-parent drop target it reads copy, and over a cross-parent row it reads not-allowed.

title: A layer row refuses a cross-group drag with no signal at all
detail: MEASURED, and it is the real half of what vg-087 reported as a missing feature. The layer panel's drag reorder refuses to drop a row into a different group - dragover marks only same-parent slots - and the refusal is entirely silent. Mid-gesture across parents: the target row carries the same yunari-layer-row class as before the drag began, the computed cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. Between siblings the same gesture works and reorders, so the panel offers a gesture that sometimes acts and sometimes does nothing, with no way to tell which case you are in until nothing happens. THE ROW'S OWN FRAMING WAS BACKWARDS: vg-087 filed the whole attribute as a lie, an agent then confirmed all four handlers are present and wired in the shipped bundle, and a live drag showed both that the handlers all run and that they refuse by design. So the attribute is honest and the defect is the silence, not the drag. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT AS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A CHOICE: whether same-parent-only is deliberate product intent or an implementation limit nobody wrote down. The gate itself looks right - reordering across groups is a different operation from reordering within one, and Fabric groups make it a real structural change - so this is filed as a question about the refusal being visible, not as a request to allow the drop. Cheapest correct fix is a cursor and a drop indicator on same-parent rows during a drag. FIXED AND VERIFIED ON CANVAS. The refusal now has three answers instead of one silent one, all from a single gesture. layer-panel.tsx:onDragOver writes `data-drop="slot"` or `data-drop="refused"` on the row under the pointer (only ever one, so a refusal cannot linger beside a slot) and `data-dragging` on the tree; editor-shell.css dims every row that is not the slot to 0.4 during a drag, holds a refusal at 0.65 with a strike-through and `not-allowed`, and marks the source row `grabbing`. `preventDefault` is now conditional so the browser adds its own no-drop cursor to the same answer. The rule is also stated in text - uiCopy.panels.reorderRule under the panel heading, reached by a screen reader through the tree's own `aria-describedby` rather than duplicated. NOT the bottom action row and NOT the heading itself: the action row is object commands, so a rule sentence among icon buttons is not read as anything but a label, and the heading names the pane rather than constraining it; one muted line directly above the list is where an author looks before starting a drag. MEASURED ON CANVAS, host 8809, a theme with a real group: over a sibling `kid-1` carries `data-drop=slot`, opacity 1, `copy`, and the drop line is drawn at y=200 against a row top of y=200; over the group's own row `grp` carries `data-drop=refused`, opacity 0.65, `not-allowed`, strike-through `line-through`, and no line. Releasing over the sibling still reorders (kid-1 onto kid-2 flipped grp,kid-2,kid-1 to grp,kid-1,kid-2) and a cross-group drop still leaves the order byte-identical. All marks clear on release. TWO MORE DEFECTS FOUND ON CANVAS IN THE SAME PASS, both in this file and both committed with it. (1) The drop line was left lit while the pointer moved to a refusal: one line serves the whole tree, so it offered the drop the row had just refused. (2) The line had NEVER DRAWN AT ALL - the offsets went into custom properties without units, `top: 48` is an invalid length, the declaration was dropped and the element sized to zero. Measured at width 0px on a real drag where `hidden` was false and the browser agreed; with `px` it is 229px. The pre-existing test asserted the unitless value, so it was pinning the bug rather than catching it.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor with a real group, dragging one child over its sibling marks that row data-drop=slot with the drop line drawn and cursor copy, while the same gesture over the group's own row marks it data-drop=refused with a strike-through, no drop line and cursor not-allowed, and releasing over the sibling still reorders.

title: Chart edits do not serialize cleanly, and one undo reverses several actions
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - chart edits seem to not get serialized properly, one undo press undoes several actions - and it is reported as two symptoms of one cause, which is why they are filed together. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED YET: I have not driven a chart through several edits, saved, and compared the document, nor counted how far one undo travels. What makes this worth taking seriously rather than filing as-is is the neighbouring evidence already on the register: this same pass found the chart aspect-ratio control changing the object's height while the inspector kept reporting the old one (vg-084), and found the inspector's Height field for text objects disagreeing with what is rendered (vg-089). Three separate findings all say the chart and text editing surfaces do not agree with what they have actually changed. That pattern - rather than any one measurement - is the reason to suspect the serialisation or the change-notification path rather than the individual controls. The two symptoms are also the shape a shared cause takes: if several small edits collapse into one history entry, a single undo reverting all of them is the same defect seen from the other side, not a second bug. EVIDENCE ARRIVED FROM THE vg-084 FIX, AND IT POINTS AT THIS ROW FROM AN UNEXPECTED DIRECTION. chart-manager/index.ts #resizeToAspect resized a chart and announced nothing, so the aspect change never reached editor-shell.ts:259 save — meaning a chart aspect change was not undoable at all. The vg-084 fix fires object:modified, so it is now recorded, but INCIDENTALLY rather than by design: nobody decided that an aspect change should be its own history entry, it happened because the event that makes the inspector re-read is the same event that saves. That is the shape this row has been guessing at from the other side. vg-091 reports ONE UNDO REVERSING SEVERAL ACTIONS; this is the same seam read from the other end, where one action recorded NOTHING. Both are the question this row should be answering: which edits are their own history entry, and which are folded into one. Still unreproduced on the undo travel itself — this is the serialisation half, found by a neighbouring fix and not by driving the editor. REPRODUCED, AND WORSE THAN THE ROW GUESSED. Three discrete edits to three separate fields on trends-chart - W 963 to 500, then H 215 to 300, then X 616 to 900 - each applied and read back before the next. ONE Ctrl+Z reverted all three: after re-selecting the object it read W 963, H 215, X 616, the complete original rather than one edit. Undos two, three and four then changed nothing further, so the three acts were one history entry and there was nothing behind them. This is exactly what the user reported, and it is not the serialisation half the row led with - the edits are all in the document. It is the grouping: three deliberate acts on three different fields, each its own moment at the keyboard, collapsed into one entry. The first undo also blanks the selection panel, which is vg-101 and is a separate defect from the grouping - it made reading the undo necessary at all, since the geometry fields come back undefined until the object is re-selected. CLOSED, AND THE GROUPING READING WAS WRONG — recorded because it is the third time this pass that a confident interpretation of a measurement survived longer than it should have. The row led with serialisation and the root reinforced it: the edits were all in the document, so the symptom had to be which entry an undo landed on. It was neither. Restores were not serialised, so overlapping presses read the index before either finished and overlapping saves collapsed several actions into one entry — which presents exactly as grouping from outside. The fix is a queue, not a grouping rule, and a second thing the row never named fell out of it: two presses that both read the index before either restore finished landed on the same entry, so an author who pressed again after seeing nothing happen walked the history backwards in steps that were really steps of two. Three edits, three undos, one entry per press, measured on canvas.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8813, the exact case the row measured and it no longer reproduces. Three edits to three separate fields on trends-chart — W 963 to 500, H 215 to 300, X 616 to 900, each read back before the next — and then three presses of Ctrl+Z, each stepping exactly one entry: 500/300/616, then 500/215/616, then 963/215/616. Before, ONE press reverted all three and undos two through four then did nothing. The cause was not grouping, as the row and the root both assumed: restores were not serialised, so overlapping presses and overlapping saves collapsed several actions into one undo. Queueing them one at a time is the whole fix.

title: Undo on a text object drops the selection instead of restoring it
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-089, reproduced on the pre-existing Size-field path and then measured by the root, who got a DIFFERENT and smaller answer than the agent reported. The agent said Ctrl+Z leaves the object unpainted. MEASURED: it does not. Set cpu-card-title W to 60, pressed Ctrl+Z, and the object still renders — screenshot shows CPU whole at 90px — with the layer row still present. What actually happens is that the undo CLEARS THE SELECTION: no selection outline or handles on the canvas, and the inspector's W, H, X and Y read undefined, so the panel blanks rather than showing the restored geometry. So the finding stands but the shape is different from what was reported, and the correction is the useful part: an author who undoes a width edit loses their place in the editor and has to find and re-select the object to see what the undo did. The undo restored the width — the geometry is right on re-select — so this is about selection surviving history, not about history being wrong. It sits next to vg-091, which is about which edits become their own history entry, and near vg-023, where the same class of problem appeared as a layer list that did not re-project. ALSO HAPPENS ON A CHART, so it is not a text defect. Three edits to trends-chart and the first Ctrl+Z left the selection panel showing W, H and X as absent, exactly as it does for cpu-card-title; re-selecting the row brought the panel back. Whatever drops the selection on undo is not text-specific.
owner: editor/src/history-manager, and whatever drops selection on undo
check: Live in a rebuilt editor, an undo now keeps the selection and the panel stays readable. With cpu-card-title selected at W 140, two edits and two presses of Ctrl+Z read W 80/X 528 then W 140/X 528, and every reading came back as a number — W, H, X and Y were ABSENT after the first undo before, and no reading here is absent. On trends-chart the same held across three edits and three undos. A revive replaces every Fabric object, so the selection is carried across by id rather than by instance.

title: Selecting a colour stutters badly: nine main-thread stalls across one drag
detail: RAISED BY THE USER as visible lag and stuttering when selecting colours, and measured rather than taken on trust - with the honest caveat that it does not reproduce on every run, which is itself part of what makes it hard to pin down. MEASURED, dragging the saturation square at roughly a human cadence - 20 moves with 40 ms between them, 3.05 seconds of dragging: nine long tasks, durations 93, 68, 76, 50, 81, 60, 77, 88 and 59 milliseconds, totalling 652 ms, maximum 93. That is 21% of the drag time with the main thread blocked, and the stalls are spread across the drag rather than bunched, so the author feels every few pixels. It was measured on Frosted panel, which eight objects use, so one colour change re-renders eight frosted surfaces - the likely shape of the cost, though I did NOT establish that: repeating the drag on tokens with 1, 8 and 28 uses produced no long tasks at all in that run, so the scaling is unconfirmed and the cause is not established here. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY: this is the interaction an author repeats most in the palette panel, a deliberate drag rather than a click, so per-move cost is exactly the wrong thing to be expensive. It also composes with vg-080 - the picker is already jumping under the author's cursor, and now the drag stutters as well, so the two together make the colour control feel broken rather than merely awkward. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the same drag measured on a token with few uses against Frosted panel's eight, a few runs each, since one clean run and one clean run that measured nothing is not yet a comparison. REPEATED, AND THE VARIANCE IS PART OF THE FINDING. Re-measured with the preserved probe (docs/product/probes/longtask.mjs, which now exists because this row needed it) after the editor had been rebuilt with more work in the palette: 40% blocked with 19 long tasks peaking at 137ms, then 27% with 12 tasks peaking at 155ms, then 56% with 27 tasks peaking at 123ms. Add the original 21% and the range is 21% to 56% across four runs of the same drag, with individual stalls reaching 155ms. No build was running during the repeats, so machine load does not obviously explain it, though on a shared machine I cannot rule that out from here. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: a single measurement will not settle it and a run that happens to come back clean does not mean the author's report is wrong. The number to beat is the low end of that range, and the useful test is a drag repeated until it is fast, not once. The fact that a first run measured 21% and later runs measured two to nearly three times that is itself consistent with something in the path being intermittent rather than uniformly slow - which is the same shape of problem as vg-028's unreproduced chart slide, and the same reason both rows stay open rather than closing on a clean run. MEASURED AGAIN AFTER vg-080, and IT IS NOT FIXED BY THAT WORK, so it stays open on its own evidence rather than on a guess. Same instrument (PerformanceObserver longtask, the one docs/product/probes/longtask.mjs keeps), same 20 moves at 40 ms, same Frosted panel token with its 8 uses, viewport 2048x962: 38% blocked over 18 tasks, 44% over 24, 48% over 25 - inside the 21% to 56% range above. WHAT DID CHANGE IS THE SHAPE: the peaks the row recorded at 93, 123, 137 and 155 ms are gone and every task now lands between 50 and 57 ms with a few at 66 and 81. A run that used to spend a fifth of a second in one block now spends it in a fifth of a second in many. Two rebuilds of the whole palette field set per commit are no longer in that path, which is the most that change can be credited with; whatever costs 50 ms at a time is something else and this work did not reach it. A TRAP FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP NEXT, which cost this run its second half: installing a PerformanceObserver per run stacks every earlier observer onto the same array, and the counts climb past 100% blocked share within three drags (96, then 192, then 300 tasks over one ~2.8 s drag). Install one observer, clear the array between runs, and distrust any share above 100%. The token comparison this row asks for is still the open question - 1 use against 8 was attempted here and produced no usable comparison, because of that trap, so the scaling is still unconfirmed. CAUSE ESTABLISHED, AND IT WAS NEITHER THE DRAG NOR THE USE COUNT. A 30 fps loop re-measured all 28 textboxes whether or not anyone was dragging: 3.2 s of pure idle did 7084 re-measures and 77 renderAll against a drag's 6844, with zero long tasks at idle. Use count does not predict the cost - frost at 8 uses read 10/11/4%, panel at ZERO uses read 25/4/6% and produced the single worst run at 145 ms peak - so the row's eight-frosted-surfaces shape is REFUTED. And a value-compare guard does not fix it: tested, it recovered 44 ms/s of 750, because bound values carry a live timestamp and genuinely differ every tick. Two causes, not one: the rate was wrong for data that changes once a second, AND each pass measured every object twice, because fabric-text.ts called initDimensions straight after a set whose three keys already make Text re-measure on the way out. FIXED: the redundant initDimensions is gone and the loop runs a 250 ms tick; refresh() still repaints everything at once because every setter calls it, and setGlobals now marks the repaint due rather than doing it, which is what keeps a dragged colour within a frame. The gesture guard was REFUSED with a mechanism rather than a preference - a palette drag reaches the canvas only through this loop, so pausing it would freeze the very preview the drag exists to produce. Cost of that refusal, stated: no gesture-time saving on a colour drag, and readings are now at most 250 ms stale. RESULT: idle 7084 to 506 re-measures, 14x; one drag 6844-7212 to 1554, 4.4x. THE ROOT VERIFIED THE PART THAT IS NOT LOAD-DEPENDENT: three canvas captures 4 and 6 seconds apart all differ, so readings and the clock still update, and 3.2 s of idle produced zero long tasks. The agent reports the drag's blocked-frame share did NOT track the 4.4x drop in work and says so rather than claiming the drag got faster - that is the honest reading and the counts are the finding.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8814: three canvas captures four and six seconds apart all differ (520874, 522141 and 523847 bytes), so the readings and the clock still update, and 3.2 s of idle produced ZERO long tasks. The drag's own share is the dispatched agent's number, not the root's, because blocked-frame share is not load-independent and five agents were building on this machine; it reports 13/19/22/17/31/40% before against 6/8/31/13/13/13% after - overlapping, and NOT tracking the 4.4x drop in work, which the agent states plainly rather than claiming the drag got faster. The load-independent number is the re-measure count: idle 3.2 s went from 7084 to 506, and one drag from 6844-7212 to a constant 1554.

title: Icon fill floods the enclosed spaces instead of covering only the path
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - icon fill colour should not fill the empty spaces inside of an icon, but should overlay the icon paths with the selected paint; maybe fill was the wrong choice of word here - and it is a clear description of the intended behaviour, which makes the useful part the diagnosis the user already offered: the control is named Fill and it does exactly what the word says. The Starter's icons are Paths built from outlines, so a fill floods any region the outline encloses, including the counters - the holes that make a chip, a card or a gauge read as an icon rather than a blob. The author's own framing is the right one and is kept verbatim: overlay the icon paths with the selected paint, not fill them. That is a different rendering operation and a different control name, and the mismatch between the name and the wanted behaviour is why this reads as a defect rather than a preference. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED YET - I have not yet changed an icon's fill in the editor and compared the result against what the path geometry intends, so the exact set of icons affected, and whether any of them already read correctly, is not established here. Filed as the user filed it, with the design question separated from the measurement question so the next person knows which half they are inheriting. REPRODUCED, with the user's own diagnosis confirmed and one thing about the starting state worth recording. The Starter's icons are STROKED, not filled: storage-card-icon reads Fill not set, Stroke palette.cpu, Border width 3, and its Path data carries several M subpaths - which is why they read correctly out of the box and why the defect is invisible until an author touches the control. Setting Fill to palette.text on storage-card-icon floods every counter between the stack lines and the icon renders as a solid grid of squares, against the CPU icon's open stroked outline immediately beside it in the same screenshot. So the user's framing is right on both halves: the control is named Fill and does exactly what the word says, and what is wanted is overlaying the icon paths with the paint rather than filling the region they enclose.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8816. With storage-card-icon selected the paint control now reads INK rather than Fill, the Stroke field is no longer offered beside it, and setting it to palette.text recolours the icon while the counters stay open - the screenshot shows the hard-drive body with its divider and both dots still readable, where the same control set to the same token before this fix rendered it as a solid grid. The icon is recoloured and still reads as a hard-drive.

title: The colour dropdown beside the type preset prints palette ids where every other picker prints names
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-088, in the file that fix touched, and left behind on purpose: the brief owned a disjoint file set and a widening diff is how two agents collide. selection-inspector/runs.ts:676 builds the run's colour dropdown with ref.replace("palette.", "") as the option text, printing the palette token id, while selection-inspector/panel.ts:155 and chart-manager/panel.ts:311 both print entry.name for the same tokens. So vg-088 and this are almost certainly ONE defect with two sites, four lines apart in one file — which is what makes it worth a row rather than a shrug. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED IN THE RUNNING EDITOR: it was established by reading the code path the vg-088 fix was already inside, and the root should see it once on canvas before closing it. Cheap and worth folding into the next change that touches that file.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor with cpu-card-title selected, the run's colour dropdown offers 18 options labelled Background, Letterbox bars, Text, Muted text, Panel, Frosted panel, Panel outline and Rule among them, where it offered the palette ids. The values are unchanged stored references - palette.background, palette.bars, palette.text - so nothing persisted moves.

title: The type preset resolution line prints the stored ref where every other picker prints the name
detail:
FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-089, and it is the third surface of a pair vg-093 already records. vg-088 fixed the two dropdowns, and vg-093 is the colour dropdown in the same file with the same defect; this is the read-only resolution line at selection-inspector/index.ts:503-510, which prints typePresets.24-400 where the preset panel prints Ring unit and the dropdowns now print Card title. Worth recording that it also REFUTES part of vg-089: the rows claim the dropdown read back 24-400 after 90-600 was applied, and on the built editor the dropdown holds typePresets.90-600 as Card reading. What was photographed was this line printing the ref as text — the settled value-is-a-ref, label-is-a-name distinction, arriving through a third surface that never got the treatment. Same for the palette equivalent below it. **SUPERSEDED 2026-10-15, AND THE CHECK ABOVE CAN NO LONGER RUN:** Task 14.2 (the user's item 17) removed the Spends section, and the resolution lines this row's check reads were `resolutionField` in `selection-inspector/appearance.ts`, which went with it — nothing renders a label/value resolution line now, so there is no surface left to read `Type preset: Card title` off. The row's subject was a *third* surface printing a ref where the others print a name, and the defect it recorded was fixed at its date; what is gone is the ability to re-run the check, not the fix. **Its state is the user's call, not a fix round's** — the register has no state for a finding whose subject a later change deleted (`vg-501`).

WITHDRAWN 2026-10-15 by the ruling on `vg-501`: this row's subject was deleted by Task 14.2, so what it verified no longer exists in the product.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor with cpu-card-title selected, the visible text of the whole editor contains ZERO raw references - no typePresets.* and no palette.* anywhere - and the resolution lines read Type preset: Card title and Paint: Text. The stored ref was what that line printed, and it is what the author copies when a token has been deleted and no name is left.

title: Text alignment has no vertical control, and the model already answers where the property belongs
detail: RAISED BY THE USER — should there be a vertical and horizontal alignment property, and would it live at the text layer level rather than per text run. BOTH HALVES ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE MODEL ALREADY AGREES WITH THEM. TextContent in renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts:198-202 already carries align?: "left"|"center"|"right" AND verticalAlign?: "top"|"middle"|"bottom", beside box, wrap and overflow — ON THE CONTENT, NOT ON TextRun. Both are in serialize.ts:58 and validated in validate.ts:119, and placeInBox (scene-fabric/authored-box.ts:144-168) consumes both to position the object inside the box. So there is no model change to make and no per-run question to settle. THE TEXT LAYER IS ALSO THE RIGHT LAYER, and the code already reasons why: a run is a line of text, so aligning one line differently from its siblings is almost never what an author means, and ADR 0003 makes the box the owner — placeInBox positions the OBJECT in the BOX, which is exactly a layer-level property. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS ONE CONTROL. selection-inspector/runs.ts:287 already writes align through a select labelled Align, so the horizontal axis is authorable. NOTHING IN THE EDITOR WRITES verticalAlign ANYWHERE — the Starter ships it hardcoded at new-fabric-theme-cards.ts:301 as { align: "center", verticalAlign: "middle" }, so a shipped theme can carry vertical alignment and an author cannot set one. That asymmetry is the whole finding: the field is authored, serialized, validated and rendered, and unreachable from the UI. ONE TRAP TO KNOW BEFORE WRITING IT, found while answering this and recorded because the words collide: arrange.ts:6-9 declares align-left, align-center-x, align-right, align-top, align-center-y and align-bottom for ARRANGING SELECTED OBJECTS relative to each other on the canvas, and ui-copy.ts:268-273 carries those accessible names. Same words, different concept — one moves objects, the other moves text inside a box. Two concepts sharing a vocabulary in one editor is a hazard for the next reader and for the accessible-name audit, so say which one a new control is in its label and in its code. QUEUED BEHIND vg-089, not dispatched yet: selection-inspector/runs.ts is owned by an agent working on the textbox resize handles, and both touch the same file. A RENAME WAS PROPOSED AND THEN WITHDRAWN, recorded so it is not re-proposed. The user asked whether alignment should be added and where it should live, then asked for the keys to be renamed to text-align-v and text-align-h, then corrected that the keys meant were the persisted theme documents, then DISREGARDED the whole rename request: "Those existing key names are good." So align and verticalAlign STAY, and this row is only ever the missing vertical CONTROL — TextContent already carries both axes on the content rather than the run, and nothing in the editor writes verticalAlign. MY ARGUMENT FOR THE RENAME DID NOT WIN, and it is worth recording why a future agent should not re-raise it: I offered that the pair is asymmetric, since one key says vertical and the other does not. The user read that and kept both names. The asymmetry is accepted here, so treat it as settled rather than as an oversight — the rule that names should be self-explanatory and unambiguous is still the users standing guidance, but these two keys have been judged against it and passed. QUEUED, not dispatched: selection-inspector/runs.ts, which an agent working on the vg-089 resize handles owns right now. WHAT TO CALL THE NEW CONTROL, given no rename: something that says text alignment on a vertical axis, and that does not collide with arrange.ts align-top / align-center-y, which arrange SELECTED OBJECTS. Two concepts in one editor saying align without saying which is the hazard this row exists to avoid, and it is now a naming question about the control only, not about the document. ADDING THE CONTROL EXPOSED A DEFECT THE CONTROL ITSELF WAS HIDING, and it is the reason the row is worth more than the control. runtimeLayout in scene-fabric/src/fabric-text.ts:81 returned the layout CACHED AT CONSTRUCTION and ignored the authored one, so applyAuthoredText placed the object by the value the control had just replaced: the control persisted, displayed, and did nothing. Horizontal alignment escaped it, because line 298 writes textAlign straight from authored.align — which is exactly why only the vertical axis was dead, and why a working control immediately above gave no hint that anything was wrong. Fixed by re-reading the authored alignment scalars while still serving the measured half from the cache, so both measures-once-per-pass guards still hold at 1. The dispatched agent took scene-fabric/ outside its file set and said so: without it the control would ship persisting without painting, which is the same asymmetry this row exists to close. AND IT NOTICED THAT TWO PROBES DISAGREED — the control said Middle while the canvas said top — and settled which was lying by testing the horizontal control as a control rather than believing the first reading. Filed alongside: the new control has no id and no aria-label, so it is unlabelled to a screen reader - the vg-103 defect on a control added after vg-103 was fixed.
check: Live in a rebuilt editor against a host on 8817, with cpu-card-value selected: a vertical control offers Top, Middle and Bottom, and the text visibly moves in its box — a tight crop of the card shows the reading sitting high against the box's top edge under Top and low against the bottom under Bottom. Its dataset name is data-yunari-text-vertical-align and does not collide with arrange's align-top / align-center-y / align-bottom vocabulary, which arranges OBJECTS; a test asserts the two sets stay disjoint. The model was not changed: TextContent, serialize.ts, validate.ts and placeInBox are untouched.

title: new-object-defaults says a path is stroked, and the code fills it
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-092. new-object-defaults.ts:283 states that an open shape is stroked rather than filled, naming a polyline, a line and a path — and case "path" at line 432 takes newShapeSurface and arrives filled. The comment and the code disagree, and the comment is the one carrying the rule the rest of the editor now relies on: vg-092's fix routes a paint on a fill-less Path to its stroke on the strength of that stated intent, so the intent now has a behaviour depending on it. Left alone by that agent because changing it moves the product's default for a newly inserted path, which is a product decision rather than a correction — an author inserting a path today probably wants a filled shape, and an author inserting a polyline gets a stroke. What is cheap and safe is either making the comment say what the code does, or splitting the sentence so path is not claimed.
check: The path default is now pinned by a named case rather than by a sweep: breaking case "path" to the stroked branch fails the pin and the three sweeps, four failures in all, so the disagreement cannot come back quietly. The comment's rule was split rather than rewritten — it still states that an open shape is stroked, and case "path" now says why it is filled.

title: The envelope's allowed metadata keys are hand-maintained twice — in the JSON schema and in validate.ts
detail: FOUND WHILE RENAMING the persisted language key, by checking a registry the brief had not mentioned. renderer-core/src/theme/validate.ts:94 carries a KNOWN_KEYS.metadata entry list which is NOT generated from the published schema/theme-document.schema.json, and that schema sets additionalProperties: false over the same bag. So two registries hand-maintain one set of keys, and a rename that updates only one leaves the validator accepting the OLD key while refusing the NEW — a failure that runs in the OPPOSITE direction from a missed reader, which falls back to en and renders quietly. Both are silent until a theme is opened, so they are the same hazard seen from two sides, and this one is the larger of the two because it fails the SAFE direction. The rename touched both, which is the only reason anyone noticed. WHICH OWNS IT IS A DECISION, not a patch: generate the validator list from the schema, or make the schema the single source and have the validator read it, or drop the runtime list and let validation depend on the schema at the boundary. The ownership map decides which concept these are one instance of, and it has not been consulted on this. CLOSED, AND THE DRIFT WAS LIVE RATHER THAN HYPOTHETICAL, which is the finding that makes the row worth having. The disagreement test builds a real v2 envelope and asks both registries about it: the stale locale key, a pinned timeZone, a stray backgroundMedia.scale, plus set-equality against the schema's own key sets. Before the fix, $defs/binding published SIX keys while the v2 validator accepted EIGHT - and the editor's runs panel authors timeZone and serialize.ts persists it, so THE PUBLISHED SCHEMA REFUSED A THEME YUNARI ITSELF PRODUCES. That is the opposite-direction failure this row predicted, and it was happening. THE OWNER QUESTION WAS ANSWERED BY COVERAGE, NOT BY SPEED, and the answer was not the obvious one. The published schema describes the v2 Fabric envelope; KNOWN_KEYS describes the v1 semantic document, which is still live in the player and fake-source. Of the 23 shapes the code decides, only 7 are published at all - the other 16, including transform, node, textContent and the four chart settings shapes, live inside Fabric JSON that the schema validates as opaque jsonValue, and fabric-envelope-schema-sync.test.ts explicitly forbids publishing the node tree. So 'the validator reads the schema' cannot own the list: it would leave two thirds of it with no owner. The code decides; the schema stays a hand-written contract held to that decision by a test. GIVEN UP, and it should be said: drift is now DETECTED rather than made impossible - a commit that changes both sides can still be individually wrong, and the test has to be run. The rejected alternative was measured first: parsing the 9,862-byte schema 1000 times costs 53.7 ms, or 0.054 ms each, so it was rejected on the two real costs rather than on performance - it cannot cover the 16 unpublished shapes, and a JSON Schema validator cannot express unresolved-asset-ref, unresolved-global-ref, duplicate-id or binding-count, so adopting one would mean deleting those checks or keeping a second validator.
check: Read the two registries against each other rather than trusting either. The published schema now carries timeZone, which it refused before while the v2 validator accepted it - a key the editor's runs panel authors and serialize.ts persists, so the schema was refusing a theme Yunari itself produces. A new disagreement test builds a real v2 envelope and asks both registries about the stale locale key, a pinned timeZone and a stray backgroundMedia.scale, plus set-equality against the schema's own key sets derived from the file; reverting the schema side fails two of the seven cases. 227 tests pass across the twelve theme files, and validate.ts still holds literals at load, so there is no startup cost for the one-owner arrangement.

title: After the resize refit, two redundant refit paths are left behind — one of them now contradicts the code
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-072, both halves left behind on purpose because they sit in files the vg-072 agent did not own. vg-072 made viewport-manager/index.ts refit on a host resize when the camera was fitted, derived from the live transform rather than a remembered flag, because a flag must be cleared by every writer and one missed writer silently eats the author's pan — which is exactly what got the previous attempt reverted. That makes two older mechanisms redundant. (1) editor-shell.ts:406 registers a SECOND ResizeObserver on host calling the same viewport.resize() as index.ts:67 — duplicate work on every resize, one of the two provably redundant. (2) editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:379-396 refitOnViewportChange subscribes to onChange and calls zoomToFit(), so a panel collapse now refits twice; harmless today because a refit is idempotent, but it was written under the explicit assumption that the viewport does NOT refit, and its comment now contradicts index.ts. AGENTS.md asks a changed decision to propagate to contradictory current docs together, so the comment is the part that is not cosmetic — it now describes behaviour that no longer holds. Left alone by that agent because editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx belonged to another agent working at the time, which is the disjoint-ownership rule working as intended rather than a gap in it. CLOSED, AND ONLY HALF OF IT WAS REDUNDANT — the half the row called redundant was load-bearing, and deleting it would have broken the panel collapse vg-072's own verification depended on. Half 1, the duplicate observer: editor-shell.ts registered a second ResizeObserver on host calling the same viewport.resize() that viewport-manager/index.ts already observes. Which one goes is not arbitrary — resize() reads canvas.getWidth()/getHeight() BEFORE setDimensions overwrites them, so the first caller decides from the box the camera was framed in and the second reads the box the first already wrote, concludes still-fitted, and fits again to the same place. The shell's is the later registration and is the one deciding from a frame the camera was never in. It was invisible precisely because the refit is idempotent. Half 2, refitOnViewportChange: KEPT, and its comment rewritten. It is not redundant — resize() deliberately holds a camera the author has zoomed or panned, because re-centring that is what broke the point-under-cursor invariant, while a panel collapse is the author handing the canvas 288px on purpose. That is the one case where their view should still follow. The old comment claimed the viewport keeps its zoom across a resize, which stopped being true when the derived refit landed. A THIRD DEFECT FELL OUT OF VERIFYING IT: a pane swap between two open panes changes which pane shows, not the panel's width, so the host never resizes — but choosePane armed the refit on every swap. It sat until the author's next gesture and then fired and swallowed their zoom: one ctrl-wheel notch after a swap left the badge on 57% instead of 50%. Fixed with a collapsed guard, which keeps the reopen path because that one does hand back 288px. The agent judged that against the on-the-fly bar and fixed rather than filed, which was the right call: cause named, one owner, behaviour specified, test obvious.
check: One host carries one resize observer, and one host notification produces one camera change — asserted directly, with the test recording every observer the shell builds; it read two before the fix. 141 tests pass across the thirteen editor-shell files the root ran. The badge readings are the dispatched agent's, and they reproduce vg-072's numbers the root measured independently earlier — 57% against a canvas of 946 at 1600, 22% against 370 at 1024, and off fit at 50% held across two window resizes and re-framed to 74% on a panel collapse, which is the distinction the kept refit rests on. The root could not re-measure them here because another agent's uncommitted work left the tree failing typecheck, so those figures are named as the agent's rather than claimed.

title: The vertical alignment control ships with a dataset name and no id, so nothing associates it with a label
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING vg-098, whose own fix was otherwise sound and careful about vocabulary. The new select carries data-yunari-text-vertical-align and nothing else: no id, no aria-label, no name, read off the live control. So it is invisible to a screen reader and unaddressable by anything looking for a control by name. That is vg-103's defect — the chart settings section carrying no ids and no htmlFor — reproduced on a control added AFTER vg-103 was fixed, which makes the point sharper than the original: the fix was applied to one section rather than enforced anywhere, so the next control written in the same neighbourhood reproduced it. The row's own naming care is worth recording alongside: the dataset deliberately avoids arrange's align-top vocabulary because those arrange objects, and a test asserts the two sets stay disjoint. The vocabulary is right and the association is missing, which is the exact split vg-103 described. The fix is an id and an htmlFor following the shell's existing scheme, and ideally the assertion vg-103 added generalised from one section to every control in the editor, so this cannot be written a third time. THE ROW'S CENTRAL CLAIM WAS WRONG AND THE REAL DEFECT IS SHARPER, which is why this row is worth more closed than open. The vertical alignment control was never unassociated: runs.ts wraps each control in its label, CONTAINMENT IS AN ASSOCIATION THE PLATFORM HONOURS, and the browser's own accessibility tree announced it combobox "Vertical text align". What was missing was the EXPLICIT association - and that matters because a wrapping label is named by its WHOLE text content. formatField put the format field's live preview span and its token vocabulary paragraph INSIDE the format label, and the browser read a field named "Format 04:38 Tokens: YYYY YY - MMMM MMM MM M - dddd ddd - DD D - HH H hh h - mm ss - A a. Words in [square brackets]." A field whose name was a clock and a whole vocabulary, changing every minute. THE RULE THAT SEPARATES THE TWO CASES, and it is the part worth keeping: a wrapping label contains its control AND NOTHING ELSE. That passes a legend, a group heading and a label wrapping exactly one control, and catches a span hint that counting labelable descendants would have missed. Auditing the whole live editor found ZERO genuinely unassociated labels - the defect was the opposite shape. Twelve controls took an id from one labelled() helper, the preview and hint moved beside the format label, and three assertions now walk every control the editor builds rather than one section.
