title: The well's resting 1px boundary reads at 2.15:1 in graphite and 1.42:1 in light, below the 3:1 bible section 5 asks of a control boundary
detail: FOUND BY THE DESIGN-LANGUAGE PARITY GATE (this plan, task 4) on the gate's first green run, and it is a token rather than a control. MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER, not modelled: `design-language.spec.ts` hides the text, screenshots the page, samples the pixel under each control and composites the computed border colour over it, so the numbers include whatever alpha the token carries and whatever gradient sits beneath. Six control states pass in all six palettes - label, refusal, selected, value, checked and focus; this one does not. The well is `--panel-2` fill plus a 1px `--edge` border, which is bible section 5's vocabulary exactly, so the composite is the token's own: graphite `rgba(221,244,238,0.26)` over `rgb(11,18,22)` = 2.15:1 (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:127`) and light `rgba(38,70,56,0.20)` over `rgb(246,254,250)` = 1.42:1 (`:242`). The other four palettes read 5.5-18.4:1 because their `--shell-edge` is opaque. WHY IT IS NOT JUST A NUMBER: `--edge` is the boundary that says a value is editable (section 5 rule 1), so at 1.42:1 the light palette's control boundaries are effectively invisible, and the same hairline bounds every panel and divider the editor draws. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair is a design decision and not a task: either section 3's fine hairline yields to section 5's 3:1 by raising the alpha to something that is no longer a hairline, or the ratio is accepted for a resting boundary and only the focus boundary is held at 3:1 (which is what section 5.4 already does). Both change every surface, and neither is this plan's to choose. PINNED, NOT WAIVED, in `design-language.spec.ts` as `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary` (graphite 2, light 1.2) so a regression still fails the gate; the floor is deleted and the bible minimum restored when this row is ruled on. SEVERITY: medium - nothing errors, the boundary reads wrong. RE-MEASURED BY PLAN 7 TASK 4 (`a3d2c407`, 2026-10-11), and it is worse than this row records: graphite's well boundary is now **1.20:1**, not 2.15:1, because graphite's `--shell-edge` became the checked drawing's own `--edge` (`current/shell.html:17`, `#242b34`) verbatim - an opaque dark line where the shipped edge had been a 26%-alpha light hairline, and 1.20:1 is that line against `--panel-2` `#171c23` (1.27:1 against `--panel`). `design-language.spec.ts`'s `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary.graphite` moved 2 -> 1.2 to hold the value that ships, which the controller ruled a re-measurement rather than an allowlist widened to pass: the shipped value is mandated by the drawing, no other threshold moved, and this row stays open and owns the ruling. (This row's title says light is 1.42:1 while the pin's light entry reads 1.2 - two different measurements of light, neither corrected here.) THE DECISION IS NOW SHARPER RATHER THAN ANSWERED, and one number settles it: clearing section 5's 3:1 against `--panel-2` needs the edge at relative luminance ~0.134, a near-`#676767` hairline, which is a visibly different shell from the drawing the user ruled is the gold style. The controller's provisional reading, recorded so a later session need not re-derive it: section 5's 3:1 binds the focus boundary (rule 4, already >=3:1 in all six palettes) and a boundary that is a control's ONLY separation, while a well also carries a fill, a hover-raise to `--muted` and a label, so its resting hairline is a divider. That reading would leave this row's graphite half as a deliberate low-contrast style rather than a defect - which is the user's call to make, not an agent's, so the row stays open and the shortfall stays recorded. SECOND REGION IN THE SAME CLASS (filed 2026-10-11 as vg-318, by plan 8 Task 3's review): the settings modal's frame against its scrim reads 1.22:1 before and 1.08:1 after in graphite, 1.07:1 to 1.21:1 in editorial, and no gate reaches it - this row's own chrome-contrast test measures the rail and opens no dialog. It is not merged into this row because its remedy is a reader that does not exist rather than a token change, but this row's floor ruling settles it too, so the two must be read together. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11), asked as one question with three readings. The NARROW reading is the user's answer: bible section 5's 3:1 binds the focus boundary -- which section 5.4 already holds at >=3:1 in all six palettes -- and any boundary that is a control's ONLY separation. A well also carries a fill, a hover-raise to --muted and a label, so its resting hairline is a divider rather than the control's sole marker, and this row's graphite half is deliberate low-contrast style rather than a defect. WHAT CLOSES IT, and it is one change: `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary` is deleted from `design-language.spec.ts` and bible section 5 states the narrower rule in words, so the next reader does not re-file the same shortfall as a regression. This row and `vg-318` then close together, because this ruling is the answer to both. WITHDRAWN BY THE USER (2026-10-11), and nothing is fixed because nothing was a defect: the shortfall is deliberate low-contrast style. The user's ruling, quoted from 12e75d42 verbatim: ‘the NARROW reading of §5's 3:1: it binds the focus boundary and any boundary that is a control's ONLY separation. A well also carries a fill, a hover-raise and a label; a modal frame also carries a fill, a shadow and a radius. Both are dividers, so the shortfalls (graphite 1.20:1, light 1.42:1; the frame 1.08-1.21:1 against its scrim) are deliberate low-contrast style, not defects. They close together when `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary` is deleted and §5 states the narrower rule in words.’ WHAT CLOSED IT, in this commit: PINNED_FLOOR.boundary is deleted from design-language.spec.ts, the well probe is a divider and minimumFor gives a divider no floor, so the ratio is still measured and printed and no minimum is asserted; design-language.md section 5 states the narrow rule in words. No check and no artefacts - a withdrawn row records a decision, not work.

title: The modal frame's own boundary against the scrim reads 1.22:1 in graphite and 1.08:1 in editorial, below the 3:1 section 5 asks, and no gate measures a dialog at all
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 3'S REVIEW (2026-10-11, finding F1, `task-3-review.md`), which rejected the implementer's discharge of its own measured regression. MEASURED RENDERED, not modelled, before and after `51245173`: the frame's `--shell-edge` composited over the pixel behind it, the same arithmetic `vg-200`'s pin uses - graphite 1.22:1 before, 1.08:1 after; editorial 1.07:1 before, 1.21:1 after. The scrim is the page's dimming, so replacing the overlay's `#0009` (60% black) with section 3's `#00000073` (45%) moves every colour behind it; graphite got worse and editorial got better, and both sit far below 3:1 either way. WHY `vg-200` DOES NOT OWN THIS, which is the whole finding: `vg-200` pins the well and chrome hairline over `--panel-2`, read by a chrome-contrast test that measures the RAIL's own surface pixel and opens no dialog (`design-language.spec.ts:1985-2043`, `PINNED_FLOOR` at `:137`), so the modal's frame is measured by no gate and pinned by nothing - and `vg-200` is itself `open`, awaiting the user's ruling on a different region's floor, so citing it as this region's floor cites an open question. Plan 8's Review Focus 4 and Task 3 Step 3 ban a SILENT third cell, not a recorded finding, so the reviewer's remedy was a row rather than a revert. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a modal frame's resting boundary is a control's only separation - section 5's 3:1 binds that - or a frame that also carries a fill, a shadow and a radius, which is `vg-200`'s provisional reading and would make it a divider. The user's ruling on `vg-200` decides this row too, which is why the two are cross-referenced rather than merged. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a gate that measures a dialog's frame against whatever is behind it - the parity table cannot, because the drawing draws no scrim at all (`mockup-values.ts:946-948`) - together with the resolution of `vg-200`'s floor ruling. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): the narrow reading, which is `vg-200`'s ruling and therefore this row's too -- a modal frame carries a fill, a shadow and a radius and is not a control's only separation, so its resting boundary against the scrim is a divider and the 1.08-1.22:1 readings are deliberate low-contrast style rather than defects. WHAT REMAINS, and it is not the contrast: no gate measures a dialog at all, so this row's other half is real and stands -- `design-language.spec.ts`'s chrome-contrast test measures the rail and opens no dialog. SUPERSEDED IN PART: the user has since ruled that Settings should be a PANE rather than a modal (`vg-330`), which retires the scrim this row measures; the reader gap is re-read there rather than closed here. WITHDRAWN BY THE USER (2026-10-11): the shortfall is deliberate style, not a defect. The user's ruling, quoted from 12e75d42 verbatim - the same ruling that closes vg-200: ‘the NARROW reading of §5's 3:1: it binds the focus boundary and any boundary that is a control's ONLY separation. A well also carries a fill, a hover-raise and a label; a modal frame also carries a fill, a shadow and a radius. Both are dividers, so the shortfalls (graphite 1.20:1, light 1.42:1; the frame 1.08-1.21:1 against its scrim) are deliberate low-contrast style, not defects. They close together when `PINNED_FLOOR.boundary` is deleted and §5 states the narrower rule in words.’ WHAT CLOSED IT, and it is not the contrast: the contrast half is settled by that ruling and needs no gate, and the row's own reader-gap half (no gate measures a dialog at all) is re-read by vg-330, which the user parked with the settings surface becoming a pane. No check and no artefacts - a withdrawn row records a decision, not work.

title: The settings drawing's six palette preview bars depict a different token per palette — four a `--shell-surface`, light a backdrop gradient, graphite a gradient `a3d2c407` retired — where the product paints all six from `--shell-backdrop`, and no row reads a bar's colour
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 5 (2026-10-11, as the first `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `411dbe91`). MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:46-83` draws twelve bars inside six cards, and the first bar of each card holds a different role depending on the palette - `#fffdf7` for editorial, and editorial's own `--shell-surface` IS `#fffdf7` while its `--shell-backdrop` is `#f5f1e8` (`editor-shell.css:32-34`), so that bar draws the palette's SURFACE; ember, moss and plum likewise; light's bar is its `--shell-backdrop` gradient; and graphite's bar is `linear-gradient(145deg,#101923,#071116)`, the first two stops of the three-stop graphite backdrop gradient `a3d2c407` REMOVED from the token. The product paints all six bars from `--shell-backdrop` (`editor-shell.css`), which is §4's 'The window behind everything' and the plan's and the measurement's own word for this bar, 'the palette's ground'. WHY IT IS NOT SETTLED HERE: the drawing is gold for treatment and README `:120-123` lists COLOUR among the treatment that is copied from the original and 'never redrawn from the product', so correcting the drawing's six bars to the product's reading is exactly the move that rule forbids; but the drawing contradicts itself across its own six cards, so it cannot be read as one rule either, and the four-of-six majority reading would put `--shell-surface` where §4 puts no ground. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the bar depicts the palette's surface (the drawing's majority) or its backdrop (§4's one ground role). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on which role the ground bar depicts, then either the drawing's six bars corrected or the product's one declaration changed, plus a `PARITY` row that reads a bar's colour - the row that exists reads the bar's HEIGHT (`mockup-values.ts:1050`), so today the instrument cannot see either reading and both pass every gate. HOW IT WOULD SURFACE OTHERWISE: plan 8 Task 10's §13 capture is the only place a person would look at the six cards beside the drawing. RELATED: `vg-320` is the same shape one step further out - a drawing value no gate reads. PLAN 8 TASK 10 READ THIS ROW AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (2026-10-11, b78ee264) and found no predating rule that decides it, so it stays open and blocked on the same question. The six palette cards now render in `docs/design/mockups/current/settings-capture-graphite.png` and `-editorial.png` beside the drawing: twelve bars whose grounds are visibly not the light ground, while the drawing gives a different role per palette (four a shell surface, light a backdrop gradient, graphite the retired a3d2c407 gradient) and the product paints all six grounds from --shell-backdrop and all six accents from --shell-accent (`editor-shell.css:777-784`). Section 7.8 (`design-language.md:412`) requires only that palette choices retain visual swatches and names no role, and section 4's --bg (`:123`) is a definition of a role rather than a requirement that a preview bar depicts it. RULED BY THE USER (2026-10-11): the bar depicts the palette's GROUND, `--shell-backdrop`, which is the product's reading today and section 4's 'the window behind everything'. The drawing's six bars are the stale side: it gives a different role per card rather than stating one rule, which is an internal contradiction and so correcting it is a treatment fix rather than the redraw `README.md:120-123` forbids. WHAT CLOSES IT, and it is two changes: the drawing's six bars are repainted to --shell-backdrop, and a `PARITY` row is added that reads a bar's COLOUR -- today the only row on those bars reads their height (`mockup-values.ts:1050`), so the instrument cannot see either reading and both pass every gate. WITHDRAWN BY THE USER (2026-10-11) as a treatment fix rather than a defect, and done. The user's ruling, quoted from 12e75d42 verbatim: ‘the preview bar depicts the palette's GROUND, `--shell-backdrop`. The drawing's six bars are the stale side, and correcting them is a treatment fix rather than the redraw README forbids, because the drawing contradicts itself rather than stating one rule. A PARITY row must read a bar's colour; today the only row reads its height, so both readings pass every gate.’ WHAT CLOSED IT, in this commit: the drawing's five solid bars are repainted to the palettes' grounds (--shell-backdrop), the height row is re-anchored on the value the drawing now paints, and five PARITY colour rows read a bar's colour, one per solid-ground palette; the light bar's gradient is read by no colour row and is reported as uncovered in task-1-report.md. No check and no artefacts - a withdrawn row records a decision, not work.

title: editor-shell's bare :root base still paints editorial's values while graphite is the named default, so a fresh profile's pre-JS first frame is the old default
detail: FOUND BY the graphite-default task (2026-10-11, task 5), on the brief's own instruction to report rather than change the :root base. WHAT: DEFAULT_SHELL_PALETTE is now graphite (src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/palette.ts:15) and systemShellPalette(false) is light (palette.ts:31), but editor-shell.css:15 still reads 'The editorial palette is the default and is defined on bare :root so a fresh profile renders it before any palette attribute is applied', and the bare :root selector block (editor-shell.css:31-33, shared with [data-shell-palette=editorial] and .editor-shell-palette-swatch) still declares editorial's values - --shell-backdrop #f5f1e8, --shell-surface #fffdf7, --shell-text #14120e and the rest. editor/index.html:19 likewise sets the pre-shell light first frame to background #f5f1e8. EFFECT: for a fresh profile the base paint before React runs applyShellPalette is editorial, not the named default. The end state is still correct - applyShellPalette writes data-shell-palette and the palette blocks override the base by later source order (editor-shell.css:90-93) - so this is a first-frame mismatch, not a wrong render, and the browser test 'a fresh profile with no stored palette renders light' (src/web/tests/e2e/shell-appearance.spec.ts:608) reads the attribute and cannot see it. WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX: the change needs a design decision - whether the bare :root base becomes graphite (which forces editorial, currently sharing the base selector, to gain its own full block) or stays editorial (and the :15 comment stops calling editorial the default). OWNER: editor-shell's shell-palette owner, editor-shell.css. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on which palette the bare base paints, then either repaint the base and give editorial a full block, or correct the :15 comment. NOT A DUPLICATE: vg-350 is the light preview-bar colour row; this is the base block's pre-JS ground. VERIFIED (2026-10-11, artefact cd910a5e, ruled by the user the same day: repaint the base under a prefers-color-scheme media query, with no inline script, because palette.ts owns that rule and a second copy of it would be a second owner). WHAT LANDED: the bare :root in editor-shell.css is now the palette systemShellPalette resolves - light on a light-reporting OS, and a new @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block repainting it as graphite - and editor/index.html:19-30 paints the same two, with the dark branch no longer #0b1419 but graphite own --shell-backdrop #0b0e12 and --shell-text #e8ecf3. Editorial is no longer the base: it keeps its own block, and .editor-shell-palette-swatch stays grouped with it so a preview bar still resolves the palette it names rather than the one in force. The two non-colour tokens (--shell-display, --shell-flat) stay on bare :root because ember, moss, plum and light inherit them from there, and the dark base deliberately omits them and --yunari-control-bg, which would otherwise move those four palettes settled values under a dark-reporting OS; that ceiling is recorded in the stylesheet. THE DIRECTION THE ROW ASKED FOR was a ruling on which palette the bare base paints; the ruling is the user own, and it is systemShellPalette answer rather than either of the two the row offered.
check: Repainted both base paints and red-proved it. src/web/tests/e2e/shell-appearance.spec.ts, "the frame before the palette attribute is the palette the OS resolves", blocks the bundle so nothing writes data-shell-palette, emulates a light then a dark OS, and compares the frame that is actually painted - the body background and :root own --shell-backdrop and --shell-text - against the same stylesheet palette block read through a probe carrying the attribute; on the reverted source it failed with the editorial cream #f5f1e8 against light gradient, pass at cd910a5e, and it cannot see the settled state because it asserts the attribute is absent. editor-shell.tokens.test.ts ties the bare :root base to the light block and the dark @media block to graphite minus the three tokens that would move the other four palettes, and asserts both base rules precede the palette blocks. Every palette computed tokens and all 36 live/named swatch combinations are byte-identical before and after the change, measured in Chromium under both color schemes (the only difference is the document element own pre-shell paint, which is what the fix is).

title: An unresolved palette reference takes the inspector column down and makes the scene snapshot throw, though the product renders that state and carries its copy
detail: FOUND BY the visual stress set (2026-10-12), chasing the one item of DESIGN.md section 13.1 that no test exercised: that a long unresolved reference leave its control and reason reachable. WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED, by forcing the state onto a live object: the scene snapshot throws (Invalid Fabric theme: fill must reference an existing palette token through yunariPaint, renderer-core fabric-envelope-validate.ts) and the editor-shell-inspector count goes 1 to 0, so the column disappears rather than showing the reason. WHAT MAKES THAT A DEFECT RATHER THAN AN IMPOSSIBLE STATE: the product already renders it and already carries its words -- appearance.ts builds the shown value as the reference plus ui-copy.ts inspectorFields.unresolved (no longer resolves), and ui-copy.ts has a whole message The selection is set to that reference, which no longer resolves -- so the surface was built for a state the data path refuses to carry. The envelope validator also refuses an undeclared reference on LOAD, so a saved document holding one does not open with a reason; it does not open. REACHABILITY NOT ESTABLISHED, and this is the part a fixer must settle first: no guard was found preventing the removal of a palette token that an object references -- ui-copy.ts carries assetReferenced, an in-use refusal, for ASSETS only -- but whether the palette editor can actually produce the state was not tested, so it is not claimed here. Two readings, and they want different fixes: if the state is unreachable by construction, record that and make it impossible rather than leaving a surface that can only be reached by force; if it is reachable, the surface must degrade to the copy it already carries instead of throwing. This is why the item is filed rather than fixed on the fly: more than one owner is involved (the envelope validator, the snapshot path and the palette editor) and the correct behaviour needs a design decision, not a patch.
check: the palette editor cannot leave a reference unresolved -- deleting a referenced token reassigns it first, driven in a browser: editor.spec.ts 'reassigns palette references before deleting a token' and three siblings pass 4/4, while editor-session.ts's deletePalette migrates object paint, shadowColor, text runs, chart settings and the artboard before dropping the token

title: The inspector is unreachable by keyboard until something is selected, so one of the shell four body regions has no focus target in the state the shell opens in
detail: FOUND BY Task 1 of the keyboard-only walkthrough plan (2026-10-12), on the real host, while deriving REGIONS from the shell rather than inventing them. WHAT: the census in src/web/tests/e2e/host-walkthrough.spec.ts opens the host editor mount on the pinned fixture theme e2e-hosted and presses Tab until focus returns to an element already seen. It took 30 presses (presses 0-29, the walk closing when press 30 would have revisited File, well inside the bound of 200) and reached three of the four body regions: rail at presses 4-8 (button Composition), pane at presses 9-24 (the Layers treeitems and each row own Rename, Hide and Lock) and stage at presses 25-28 (button Zoom out). It never reached the inspector. EVIDENCE: the inspector holds nothing focusable in this state -- Playwright own aria snapshot of the surface reads complementary > paragraph Select an object to inspect it, with no control under it -- so no press count could have reached it, and the bound is not why the walk stopped. THE CONDITION, INFERRED RATHER THAN DRIVEN -- and the heading here read MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED until the Task 1 review caught the overstatement: the region is not unreachable in general. inspector-sections.spec.ts asserts controlCount(page) > 0 inside .editor-shell-inspector once a selection exists, so the column is full of buttons, inputs and selects as soon as an object is selected; the empty column is the state with no target. WHY IT MATTERS: the editor-redesign spec section 13.1 states without qualification that each region has a reachable focus target, and that sentence is one of the two invariants acceptance item 3 is read from, so a keyboard author with nothing selected cannot put focus in the inspector at all. The walkthrough itself selects through Composition before it needs the column, so this does not block the walkthrough; it makes the census sentence false as written, which is a rule question as much as a code question. CLOSE THIS when either the empty inspector gains a focus target of its own, or section 13.1 is ruled to mean the populated region and the census test is rewritten to say so. OWNER: whoever owns the inspector empty state and the shell focus order; deliberately not the walkthrough plan, which records unreachability rather than repairing it. FIRST RECORDED with an 18-press count taken before the boot document was pinned; the count here is the reproducible one. WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SHOW, added by the Task 1 review (2026-10-12): controlCount() > 0 proves controls EXIST inside the populated column, not that Tab REACHES them. Nobody has driven a keyboard selection into that column and then pressed Tab, so the populated-state reachability is inferred from its DOM rather than measured -- and that is precisely the half that decides what section 13.1 means. The conclusion stands; the label claimed more than the evidence did. RULED BY THE USER on 2026-10-12, which settles the question this row was filed as: section 13.1's "each region has a reachable focus target" means a region that has CONTENT, so an empty inspector legitimately contributes no tab stop, no product change is owed, and the row's second branch is the one taken -- the census test is rewritten to select an object by keyboard first and then walk into the populated column. That rewrite is the walkthrough's amended Task 1 and is NOT yet done, so this row stays open until the amended census passes; it closes on the rewrite, not on the ruling.

title: Layer rows declare draggable but nothing consumes the drop, so reordering by drag does nothing
detail:
MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a row that does not reorder is only a finding if reordering is a thing the panel is offering. It is: every layer row carries draggable="true" in the DOM, which is an explicit promise that an HTML5 drag will be received and acted on. Nothing acts on it. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title changes the list not at all - the first eight rows are byte-identical before and after. That is true for a mouse drag and also for Playwright's dragTo, which is the technique that drives HTML5 drag-and-drop rather than mouse events, so this is not my probe using the wrong gesture. THE OPERATION ITSELF WORKS, which is what makes the dead attribute a real cost rather than an unimplemented feature: select the date text on the canvas, right-click, Bring to front, and the host's document moves date from index 6 to index 51 and every other object shifts down. So an author who wants to reorder can, by finding a context menu; an author who tries to drag, which is what the attribute invites and what every other layer panel in this class of tool invites, silently does nothing and gets no feedback. THE HONEST MITIGATING FACTOR: the row's cursor is default, not grab, so the panel does not visually advertise dragging - the promise is in the markup, not in the pixels. That is why this is filed as a smaller row than it first looks, and why the fix could legitimately be to drop the attribute rather than to implement the drop. What I would not accept is leaving an attribute that says draggable on an element where drag does nothing, because it is a false statement the next agent or the next tool will believe. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But the drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-yunari-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents, the target row carries the same yunari-layer-row class as before, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule. That is the row worth keeping, and it is filed as vg-099. vg-096 is CONFIRMED by the same measurement: cursor is auto on a draggable row. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But that drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-yunari-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents the target row carries the same yunari-layer-row class as before the drag began, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule - and cannot tell which case they are in until nothing happens. Filed as vg-099.

 CROSS-LINK, deliberately NOT withdrawn, for the same reason as vg-056: the drag handler lives in a panel being replaced, but drag-to-reorder is a requirement that has to be carried into the composition panel. The polish spec records it and the redesign's section 3 keeps row-level commands, so the requirement is carried in docs - but this row is the only place the DOM advertises draggable with nothing consuming the drop, and that advertisement has to not survive the rewrite.
check: `bridge.ts` `reorderLayer` consumes `draggable`; `bridge.dom.test.ts` proves sibling reorder. Residual cross-group refusal is `vg-099` (verified)

title: Fabric's coordinate cache goes stale after the authored box is restored, so the selection frame, snapping and arrange work off the pre-pass size
detail: FOUND WHILE REFUTING vg-109, and it is the real artefact under that row's wrong measurement. assertBoxWidth and assertBoxHeight in scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts:130,150 assign width and height DIRECTLY rather than through set, because a set re-enters initDimensions and would widen the object again - that is why they bypass it. But Fabric's aCoords is a separate cache, and bypassing set leaves it describing the PREVIOUS size. getBoundingRect() is makeBoundingBoxFromPoints(this.getCoords()), so everything that reads an object's box through the canvas reads a stale one: the SELECTION FRAME an author drags by, the SNAP positions the guides are computed against, and ARRANGE, which aligns selected objects to each other's edges. Measured: one text object read 172.78 x 102.7 stale, and 141 x 28.12 after a single dirty = true; setCoords(). A direct assignment or a setCoords after the restore would both be guesses until established, so the fix is to find where the pass leaves the object and mark it dirty once there - not to sprinkle setCoords at every reader. Left alone by the agent that found it because scene-fabric/ was held by another agent at the time, which is the disjoint-ownership rule working rather than a gap in it. This is worth its own row and its own dispatch: vg-089 already made a textbox's height a cache of its box, and this is the cost of that arrangement showing up somewhere the previous work did not measure.
check: `authored-box.ts` `markBoxWritten` sets `dirty` and `setCoords` where the pass restores the box

title: group() leaves every member cached box stale, so a bounding rect read right after Ctrl+G is the pre-grouping box
detail:
AMENDED after an independent review measured every consumer, because the row as first filed would have sent a fixer to two safe sites and past the broken one.

grouping-manager/index.ts:185 builds `new Group(members)`, which rewrites each member into group-local coordinates and leaves Fabric's aCoords cache holding the pre-grouping box. setCoords() is the only thing that refreshes it.

MEASURED, ON A 1200x800 ARTBOARD: before group() outside=5 of 30; immediately after, outside=11 of 30, which is what the artboard panel reads; after renderAll() outside=10; only after a forced refresh does it return to 5. An author who groups two objects sees "11 of 30 outside" when 5 are.

TWO OF THE SEVEN CONSUMERS FIRST LISTED ARE NOT AFFECTED. snap-manager/bounds.ts:71 calls setCoords() on the line immediately before getBoundingRect(), so snapping is immune - measured, it returns the correct 421 rather than the stale 983. scene-fabric/src/glass.ts:584 likewise refreshes what it samples. arrange.ts reads getBoundingRect() with no refresh, but its members are no longer canvas roots after grouping, so reaching it needs a gesture the current UI does not offer - weaker than first claimed, not zero.

THE ONE CONSUMER THAT IS BROKEN is the crop count: scene-fabric/artboard-crop.ts:167 walks getObjects() recursively including children, so it reads the stale cache. Note that renderAll() only partially heals it, 11 to 10, because the glass sampler touches the card's frosted Rect but not its other six members - cpu-card-icon, -title, -value, -caption, -sparkline and -freq all stay stale.

ALSO RECORDED because it is incidental and therefore fragile: renderAll() does NOT refresh the cache by design. It appeared to, only because glass.ts:584 - an unrelated frosted-glass sampler - happens to call setCoords() on what it samples. A change to the glass renderer could silently reintroduce this, so nothing may cite "renderAll does not refresh" as a property of Fabric.
check: `member.setCoords()` follows `new Group(members)` on both paths

title: The player fit-mode spec intermittently measures nothing inside fit-contain, in a suite that gates merges
detail: FOUND ON THE FULL GATE WHILE CLOSING vg-119, and it is not this sweep: nothing in b29ccc21..HEAD touches display-fabric.spec.ts, background-media.ts or anything they read. MEASURED: the serial full gate collected 410 and reported 409 passed / 1 failed, the one being tests/e2e/display-fabric.spec.ts draws each fit mode, and every icon, in its own box - "fit-contain drew nothing inside its own box", expected > 0.05, received 0. Re-run on its own, --repeat-each 3, that is 6 collected and 6 passed, so it is an intermittent and not a standing red. The claim is the INK, measured inside the box the fit mode is supposed to fill, and a reading of exactly 0 is what a frame that had not painted yet looks like - the same class as the chart-palette status race vg-131 recorded, where an action arrives before the surface has settled. NOT DIAGNOSED: whether it is the player waiting for a decode, the probe sampling before the first paint, or a genuine intermittent in the fit path is not established, and the one thing established is that 3 samples is not enough to call it fixed either. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: --repeat-each 20 on that spec with the ink reading captured per run, which separates a paint that is late from a fit that is wrong in a way that only sometimes shows. The base was green - STATUS.md at b29ccc21 records 252 passed 0 failed 0 flaky - so this appeared somewhere between there and here, and that is not narrowed to this sweep because this sweep did not touch the surface.

title: colour-picker.tsx reaches past the vendored popover to @radix-ui/react-popover directly, so two wrappers own one primitive and the spec's own "incoherence" survives the plan that was written to end it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 9'S AUTHORING PASS while verifying what §8 left it, and verified here against the source rather than taken from the report. `packages/editor/src/components/ui/colour-picker.tsx:1` and `packages/editor/src/components/ui/popover.tsx:1` both import `* as PopoverPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-popover"`, so the colour picker does not go through the vendored shadcn wrapper that the rest of the editor uses. WHY IT MATTERS: the spec names this as its motivating example -- §8's table row reads `popover | both -- the incoherence` (`:429`), and the paragraph above it says the app has 'two primitive libraries and two popover implementations'. Plan 9 migrates the five Base UI imports to Radix, which ends the two-LIBRARY half of that. It does not end the two-WRAPPER half, and plan 9's author named it Out of scope rather than folding it in. THE COST IS NOT COSMETIC: a change to the shared wrapper -- its accessibility attributes, its positioning, or a `--shell-*` token it should carry -- does not reach the colour picker, and nothing reddens when the two drift apart, because each is correct in isolation. That is the same shape as the two-ScenePlan-builders defect (vg-176) that this session fixed one layer down: duplication is invisible until the copies disagree. NOT A BLOCKER and not part of the redesign's acceptance: this is a pre-release internal duplication the repo may break cleanly, which is why it is a row and not a task inside plan 9. Whoever takes it should decide which wrapper is the owner -- keeping colour-picker's direct use and deleting the vendored one, or routing the picker through the wrapper -- and that is a small design decision rather than a rename.
check: `colour-picker.tsx` imports `@base-ui/react/popover`; no `@radix-ui` import in the editor

title: display-fabric's repaint check times out on every run, so the assertion that the update loop reaches the canvas never executes
detail: FOUND AT PLAN 9 PHASE 1'S BOUNDARY while re-reading a full browser suite that had reported 21 unexpected on a loaded box. THE MEASUREMENT, which separates this from a flake rather than from a hunch: `npx playwright test display-fabric --workers=1 --repeat-each=3` collected 144 and reported 6 unexpected, and all six are the SAME test - `keeps repainting as samples arrive`, two projects by three repeats - every one a `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded`. One run of it alone fails 2 of 2 the same way. So this is a STANDING RED, not an intermittent: different from `vg-140`, which files an intermittent in the same file but a different test (`draws each fit mode, and every icon, in its own box`, an ink reading of exactly 0), and different from the 30 s timeouts that appeared in the same suite under load and vanished when the spec set was re-run alone. **NOT ATTRIBUTED TO THE DIFF IN THE TREE, and that was measured rather than argued:** the same spec was run at `af499716` with the 22 `@radix-ui/*` packages reinstalled and both builds rebuilt, and it fails there identically - 2 collected, 2 unexpected, both 30 s timeouts. WHAT IT COSTS: the test's whole subject is that the player repaints when telemetry samples arrive, and its own comment records that the failure was verified by sabotage - `handle.update(plan())` cut, and it goes red. A test that times out before reaching its assertion cannot play that role, so the coverage this file believes it has for the update loop is currently absent rather than passing. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the shape narrows it to two candidates: the body awaits `openCanvasPlayer(page)`, reads the artboard canvas with `toDataURL()`, then awaits `page.clock.runFor(4000)` - Playwright's FAKE clock, standing in for the player's once-a-second plan rebuild - and reads the canvas again. A 30 s timeout on that sequence is a readiness wait that never resolves, so either the player never reaches the state `openCanvasPlayer` waits for, or the fake clock never advances it because the player schedules its rebuild off something `page.clock` does not drive. THE NEXT STEP is to separate those two and it is cheap: log which await the timeout lands on, and whether the artboard canvas is non-empty at the first read. A row rather than an immediate fix because the owner is not established - `openCanvasPlayer` is a shared helper several specs read, so a change there is not this file's to make alone - and because a fake clock that fails to drive a real timer is a decision about how the player is tested rather than a defect in one assertion.
check: `display-fabric.spec.ts` deleted by `ad94e5ed`; no `page.clock` caller remains. **See §3.3**

But editor-shell.css styles only .editor-shell-dock[data-visible="true"] (editor-shell.css:2350), and a grep for data-visible across that stylesheet returns that single line - there is no rule for the false state. title: The identity chip differs from the mockup in three ways Task 10 must list as deliberate
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 5's task review, comparing the landed chip against the checked reference at docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:178-184. The mockup draws (a) a 1px separator between the theme name and the edited state, (b) the WORD 'edited' in --muted, and (c) the name at font-weight 500. title: The visual-evidence README claims every capture uses `?static=1` and a controlled clock, which is false for the editor's captures
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 9's implementer while doing the parity capture, and REPORTED rather than obeyed: the brief it worked from carried the same sentence forward and told it to use `?static=1` and the controlled clock, and the implementer checked, found the editor has neither, used the harness the two existing editor captures use, and flagged the instruction as stale. MEASURED before filing, because 'the editor has no static mode' is the kind of claim that is easy to make and cheap to check. docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:14-15 states, as a rule for every capture: 'Captures use `?static=1` and a controlled clock.' Neither half holds for the editor. (1) The editor reads exactly ONE query parameter — packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:383 is bootTheme(window.location.search, libraryClient), which is `?theme`. There is no `static` branch anywhere in the editor bundle. (2) Every `?static=1` in the browser suite is against the HOST/PLAYER: tests/e2e/clip-parity.spec.ts:535, display-fabric.spec.ts:757, host-bleed.spec.ts:35 and :64, all `page.goto(`${HOST}/...`)`; and tests/e2e/canvas-probe.ts:201, which appends the parameter for the player probes, is imported by exactly three specs — display-fabric.spec.ts, host-player.spec.ts, player-chrome.spec.ts — none of them an editor spec. (3) No editor capture pins a clock: the shared capture helper tests/e2e/editor-canvas.ts contains no setFixedTime or setSystemTime, and neither editor.spec.ts's captures nor design-language.spec.ts's pin one. WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG: the README is the instructions a capture author follows, and this sentence sent one looking for a static mode and a pinned clock the editor has never had. It cost this task a rebuild-and-check cycle and a paragraph of report, and a less careful implementer would have 'fixed' it by pausing Date in a spec, which would have changed the capture's evidence rather than its accuracy. It is the same failure shape as a vacuous gate: an instruction that reads as authoritative, cannot be satisfied, and is not checked by anything. NOTE THE EDITOR CAPTURES ARE TIME-DEPENDENT BY DESIGN — the starter clock and the live chart values are real — which is why the correct replacement is not 'the editor also gets a fixed clock' but a sentence that says which captures the rule is about. The README ALREADY CONTAINS the narrower truth elsewhere: its `## Settings page` table names `desktop-host` and `publish` projects for the captures that drive the host. NOT FIXED IN TASK 9 because its brief scopes README changes to registering the new action, and because the right replacement sentence is a decision — the blanket claim about 'captures' has to become a claim about the player/host captures — which is the README owner's to make once. OWNER: whoever owns docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md. SEVERITY: low — documentation only; no capture is wrong today, and every editor capture that exists demonstrably works without either mechanism.
check: the README now scopes `?static=1` to player captures and says why the editor cannot

title: The shell's four body regions are inset 8px and rounded at an off-scale 12px radius, where the bible's diagram draws them flush and section 3 has no 12px step
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 10 (difference list row 19), REPORTED to the controller rather than filed, and VERIFIED BY THE CONTROLLER before filing - both halves. Same family as vg-227 (the rail's 34px slot): an off-scale value that no mechanism watches, on a surface whose task is closed. Then whoever owns editor-shell.css. SEVERITY: low - nothing breaks and nothing is unreachable; the finding is that the shell's largest layout fact and five radius values are owned by no document and watched by no gate. CORRECTED 2026-10-09 by plan 2's final whole-branch review, which found this row's line citation off by four: the `gap` is at :761 and the `padding` at :764, both inside the same .editor-shell-body rule, not at :757. The five 12px radii and the --radius-* citations were already exact, and the conclusion is unchanged. UPDATE 2026-10-10, THE USER'S RULING, which closes this row's open question: the mockup is NOT replaced — in the user's words, "Do not replace the mockup. Even the setting panel you just built looks nothing like it. Goddamn it why is it so hard to stay on target when we already have a clear visual mockup?" So the alternative this row left open is settled in favour of the product work: the drawing stays the target and the shipped surface is pulled to it, which makes the 8px inset and the four literal 12px radii a decided defect to fix rather than a difference to adjudicate. Scheduled by the mockup-parity plan this ruling requires, not by this row. CORRECTED (§8.2) 2026-10-12: the citations above are of the pre-fix stylesheet. `42283107` squared the four flush regions, and `f31b000b` removed the body grid's gap and padding, so no cited line holds its value now — `.editor-shell-body` is at :911 carrying neither, no `border-radius: 12px` remains in the file, and the `--radius-*` scale is at :446-449.

title: selection-inspector/index.ts grew from 540 to 822 lines, past the plan's own holds-or-shrinks constraint
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 3'S FINAL WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW (2026-10-09), and invisible to every task review because each saw one branch of one function. MEASURED per commit by the reviewer: 540 -> 527 -> 515 -> 690 -> 718 -> 791 -> 822, the growth starting at 6be5aa4c and never ruled on. THE CONSTRAINT IT BREAKS IS THE PLAN'S OWN: the Global Constraints in docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-the-inspector.md:70 read 'index.ts holds or shrinks (540 ... and the surface moves out of it)', and AGENTS.md names 800 lines as a stop for normal source files. title: The unit display options are four hardcoded English strings while every other list in the editor is Intl-derived
detail: REFUTED, and the refutation was already in the code when this row was filed. TWO claims; neither survives. (1) "ask Intl for these rather than write them". The probe was already run and recorded at ui-copy.ts:386-401, and re-run here independently: Intl.supportedValuesOf("unitDisplay") THROWS RangeError, Intl.DisplayNames.of("unitDisplay") throws RangeError (its six types are language, region, script, currency, calendar, dateTimeField), and Intl.supportedValuesOf("unit") is the 45 sanctioned UNITS OF MEASUREMENT (acre, byte, celsius), not the ways to display one. None of the four labels is a platform string: short and long are the platforms unitDisplay VALUES with no name attached, none is rejected outright (Intl.NumberFormat unitDisplay:"none" throws RangeError), and "Default" is the ABSENCE of the key rather than a word. (2) "every other list in the editor is Intl-derived, so a theme authored in another language meets four English words in the middle of an otherwise translated inspector". Two halves, both wrong. requirements.md §35 states "Multiple locales are not in scope for product UI copy; a theme declares the language its own text is written in" - the inspector is not translated, so there is no otherwise-translated middle for four English words to sit in. And the other lists are not Intl-derived either: ui-copy.ts carries artboardOrientations, artboardResolutions and fitModes as hand-written tables in the same object as the unit options (lines 378-385). THEME_LANGUAGES is the one genuinely Intl-labelled list, and its comment says why the LIST is hand-owned while the LABELS are not. WHAT THE ROW GOT RIGHT, and why it is still not a defect: the options were once written twice, in runs.ts and in the chart panel, so a rename fixed one and missed the other. That is fixed - the four options now live once in ui-copy.ts as unitDisplayOptions and both panels read them. The table is an OWNER, not a localisation debt. NO CODE CHANGED: the fix the row asks for would replace four correct strings with four undefined ones.
check: the unit display options are four hardcoded English strings in `ui-copy.ts`, the one owner both panels read

title: The reuse gate watchlists the repo-root scripts/ as a prefix, so a script directory under src/web/ is never gated
detail: FOUND WHILE LANDING THE FONT CATALOGUE GENERATOR, whose task brief instructed me to write a decision note first because scripts/ is on the gate watchlist and src/web/scripts/ is under it. Measured: it is not. reuse-gate.mjs:53 resolves every candidate path against the repo ROOT, so the watchlist entry scripts/ matches only a path whose repo-relative form begins scripts/ - and src/web/scripts/generate-font-trios.mjs does not. Piping that path into the gate returns 0 (allowed), while scripts/anything.mjs returns 2 (refused). So the second scripts/ directory in the repo is ungated and an agent can add a generator there without ever meeting the seven rungs. I landed the note anyway, because being told to is right and the gap is not mine to close silently, but the gate is not doing what its watchlist reads as saying. The fix is a judgement, not a typo: either add src/web/scripts/ as its own entry, or widen the matching so a bare directory name matches at any depth - which is the same shape as the bare-gitignore-pattern rule the repo already follows and would also catch a scripts/ under packages/. Worth deciding deliberately, because widening it means deciding what else under a path called scripts/ is a mechanism boundary.
check: `matchesDirectory` matches a bare watchlist entry at any depth, so the reuse gate covers a script directory under `src/web/`; probe exits 2

title: Five more tests read the camera as a constant, found by changing the default camera after vg-136 was fixed
detail: FOUND BY THE SABOTAGE RUN AGAINST vg-136, which is why it is filed rather than never noticed: setting DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to `9:19.5` and rebuilding makes five more tests fail, and all five are the SAME defect class vg-136 just fixed - a measurement that reads the camera as a constant - and all five are PRE-EXISTING and outside vg-136's diff. THREE fail inside `assertBlur`. glass-probe.ts:261 builds the sampled band as `bandTop + Math.max(8, Math.floor(height * 0.25))`: the 0.25 term scales with the camera because `height` is the panel's device box, but the 8 is a literal DEVICE-row floor, so the two halves of one expression disagree about which space they are in. glass-authoring.spec.ts:207, :323 and :420 all land there. TWO fail on snapping.spec.ts's GUIDE_ROWS_PRESENT (50) and GUIDE_ROWS_ABSENT (20), which count device rows carrying the guide colour. The file's own comment says 'the artboard is 600 scene px tall, so a real guide covers hundreds of device rows' - hundreds AT THE ZOOM IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. At the artboard's full height in device rows that count is 600 * zoom, so the 50 floor is a floor on the camera in the same way RAW_TOLERANCE was, and reference-theme.spec.ts:1595 fails on the same measurement. THE POINT IS NOT FIVE FAILURES, IT IS THE SHAPE. vg-136 repaired three tests that read the camera as a constant and proved the repair under a changed camera; this row is the remainder of that same audit, and it exists because the audit's instrument - change the default camera and re-run - found more than the row it was run for. The device lens is not the first thing to move that camera: every one of these would break again on the next zoom control, the next lens, or a window resize, and none of them names the camera in its failure message the way the repaired snapping assertions now do. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: it is a different set of files from vg-136's three (glass-probe.ts is a shared helper read by several specs, and the guide-row constants sit among tests vg-136 did not touch), and it is a scope decision rather than a defect on its own. Worth deciding together whether the honest repair is per-constant derivation from liveZoom, or one shared helper that converts a scene measurement into the device pixels a given assertion is about - the second would stop the next row being needed. MEASURED on this Windows box by setting DEFAULT_DISPLAY_LENS to 9:19.5, rebuilding the editor, and running the three specs under playwright.config.ts. Not verified on any other camera: portrait is the one that was measured, and Fit at 0.98 passes these today.
check: the camera's band floor and the guide rows derive from the same measurement; no test reads it as a constant

title: The plus cannot dismiss the chooser it opened, though it announces that it can

NOT FIXED AFTER THE CLOSE because it is a behaviour change to a closed plan, and the register owns it: the fix is to make the handler toggle, and it then needs a browser case proving the second press closes rather than reopening.

title: The authored text box stores the scaled width, which the shared writer's own comment says would grow the box on every pass
detail: FOUND by a read-only architecture survey the user asked for ('does any domain manager need clean-up — same domain spread across a few managers, a domain under another owner that should be its own'), run on 2026-10-09 with docs/architecture/ownership.md as the yardstick. VERIFIED BY ME by reading both writers. authored-box.ts:196-197 documents writeAuthoredBoxDimension as 'The single write every geometry surface shares'. The writers half was fixed on 2026-10-12 by Task 9 candidate rank 4 (commit dd7c3365): all three now call the helper and both inline writers are gone. The units half survives — text-manager/index.ts still passes target.width * scaleX. The three disagree about units, and the source says which is right: authored-box.ts:70-74 'yunariText.box is scene units; Fabric's width is the same box before scaleX', and writeAuthoredBoxDimension seeds with the UNSCALED object.width/object.height under a comment (:216) reading 'Seeding with the scaled value would grow the box on every pass'. text-manager/index.ts:90 does exactly that — width: target.width * scaleX. Because boxFrom (authored-box.ts:42-62) multiplies by scaleX on read, storing the scaled value makes the read-back scaleX squared for a scaled object. (CORRECTED 2026-10-12, measured: the read-back is NOT scaleX squared -- the stored box and the object's own width are one number, because assertBox copies the box onto the width -- and what the scaled write does instead is shrink the object by scaleX on every resize. See the SETTLED paragraph below.) The inline writers also skip the helper's refusals: the value < 1 / non-finite guard (:203) and the sibling-dimension seeding (:209-223) that exists so an object never loses its width. NOT ESTABLISHED: reachability — the survey could not trace whether scaleX can be non-1 when adoptResizedBox runs, since the width guard puts object.width back before object:resizing reports and whether it resets scaleX is untraced. What would settle it: one browser check, scale a text object, drag a side handle, compare yunariText.box.width against width * scaleX. THAT RUN HAS NOW HAPPENED. SETTLED 2026-10-12 (Task 2.1 and its fix round 1, commit 6cec8acf): the check ran and the row's mechanism is right about the defect and wrong about its shape. At scaleX 0.7432 a 240-unit mr drag landed the edge 62.4156816858345 scene units short of the pointer -- 177.584 for 240 asked, the request times scaleX -- while the stored box and the object's own width agreed throughout (the log's boxAfter and fabricWidth are one double), because assertBox copies the stored box onto the width on the next pass. So the read-back is NOT scaleX squared; what a scaled write does is leave the object scaleX times the size the author dragged to, which is the user-visible half. Writing target.width unscaled in adoptResizedBox lands the same drag within 1.31 units and the case passes; restoring target.width * scaleX fails it on the landing arm (Expected: < 2 | Received: 62.4156816858345, C:/tmp/vg21/RUN-RED.json), so the close rests on a case that fails on this defect. The comparison this row asked for -- yunariText.box.width against width * scaleX -- is NOT the discriminator and is not asserted as one: the two are equal under either write, since assertBox makes them the same number. Reachability, the row's other open half, is answered: the resize path does run for a scaled text, with scaleX 0.7432 at the write, reached by a real corner drag. selection-inspector/index.ts is a file another agent is mid-task on, so that writer may be moving. NEAR ROWS: vg-057 (verified, the half-box), vg-109, vg-112 — none names the three writers. OWNER: scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts, which already claims the job and should hold the only writer. SEVERITY: medium if reachable, low if the guard makes it unreachable — hence the one check first.
check: `editor.spec.ts`'s "resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote" measures what the authored box stores when a scaled text is resized: the starter wordmark is scaled to `scaleX` 0.7432 by a real corner drag, its `mr` handle is dragged 240 scene units, and the case asserts the resized edge lands where the pointer asked (within 2 units). With the scaled write in `adoptResizedBox` that arm FAILS -- the 240-unit request lands at 177.58431831416544, so the shortfall is 62.4156816858345 (exactly `asked - landed`). CORRECTED 2026-10-12: this row also called that landing 'the request times `scaleX`', and it is not -- 240 x 0.7431987269831705 is 178.36769447596086, 0.78 units above the recorded landing. The equality that IS exact is on the box, which is the mechanism this row established: the pre-fix `boxAfter` 237.94593984979582 is the post-fix 320.1646224767875 times `scaleX`, and the pre-fix `boxBefore` 26.485265692492487 is the post-fix 35.6368555689039 times `scaleX`, so the scaled write shrank the object by exactly `scaleX` -- and with `target.width` unscaled it passes at 1.31 units; the same run also asserts the saved box is the object's own width, the reopened box is that saved number, and the reopened width is the pre-save width. Red-proved by restoring `target.width * scaleX` in `adoptResizedBox`, where the case fails on the landing arm (C:/tmp/vg21/RUN-RED.json, C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json) (desktop-chromium, --workers=1). WHAT EACH REPORT IS, corrected 2026-10-12 by Task 2.2 of the backlog-drain plan, which this task's re-review filed as a Minor: RUN-RED.json is NOT a run of the committed blob. It ran a pre-commit revision of `editor.spec.ts` (written 16:31:06 +07, committed 16:32:28 +07), whose case declaration sits 15 lines above the committed one -- the report's case at line 4206 against the committed 4221, its failing location at 4317 against the committed assertion block at 4329-4332 -- and its own stdout carries this fix round's log fields. The assertion it fails is the same one, with the same message ('the resized edge lands where the author dragged it') and the same `Expected: < 2 | Received: 62.4156816858345`, so the substance is corroborated rather than assumed; vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json is the run of the committed bytes, reporting the case at line 4221.

title: The editor's rotation gesture on the canvas is performed by no test now that the indicator capture block is deleted

THE READOUT IS NOT UNVERIFIED, and neither is the rotation configuration: src/web/packages/editor/src/indicator-manager/index.dom.test.ts:76 fires object:rotating and asserts .yunari-angle-indicator reads 30 degrees, then hides on object:modified; src/web/packages/editor/src/controls-manager/index.test.ts:11 asserts snapAngle === 1 and :26 asserts the mtr handle's cursor and offset. So the readout and the control configuration are unit-tested and only the canvas gesture is not. Rotation still exists in the product: controls-manager/index.ts binds mtr to ROTATION and renderRotationHandle, and indicator-manager/index.ts draws the readout (showRotationAngle defaults true). WHY IT MATTERS: a regression in the canvas rotation control now has no test that would notice. THIS ROW WAS FIRST WRITTEN TOO BROADLY: it claimed the gesture AND the readout were untested and that no unit test drove the rotation control, and both halves were false; an independent review found the counterexamples above and the row was narrowed in this task's fix round. title: The glass-authoring spec's empty-radius test fails deterministically because its well is read through a div.ml-auto ancestor that never existed

title: The checked drawing declares four values that contradict the bible - two 9px cluster radii, three #0007 cluster shadows and a bordered follow-the-system row - and no mechanism compares the drawing to the bible at all
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-10), adjudicating every region of the two measurements into .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md. MEASURED, each against a bible section that states the value: (1) `editor-shell.html:178` and `:185` put the identity chip and the view cluster at `border-radius:9px`, where `design-language.md:93` gives `--radius-xl` 10px to exactly those clusters (dock, view controls, identity chip) and section 3 declares the radius scale closed; (2) `editor-shell.html:178`, `:185` and `:195` write the cluster shadows as `0 8px 20px #0007` and `0 10px 26px #0007`, where `design-language.md:103` fixes elevation 1 as `0 8px 20px #00000059`; (3) `editor-shell.html:288` wraps the follow-the-system toggle in `border:1px solid #242b34;border-radius:8px;padding:9px 10px`, a bordered container section 5 has no vocabulary for and section 1 forbids in the words "Chrome does not decorate". CONSEQUENCE: spec section 13 says "A mockup that no longer matches the bible is worse than no mockup, because it is believed" and requires the bible, the mockup and the spec to move in one commit - but the drawing is compared only to the PRODUCT (this plan reads it as the acceptance instrument and pulls the product to it), so a value the drawing gets wrong is inherited by the product rather than caught. This is the mirror of vg-291, which records the product diverging from a current drawing; here the drawing itself is off the bible and is the artifact that is stale. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a 9px cluster radius or a #0007 shadow is a deliberate drawing gesture or drift - the drawing has no commit trail of its own and every value is a literal in one file. What would settle it: a ruling on whether section 3's elevation 1 and the 10px cluster radius bind the drawing as tightly as they bind the product, and if they do, the three cited lines corrected in one commit that names this row. NARROWED BY TASK 3 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-11), reviewing `42283107` and `be54cfc5`. THE SHELL DRAWING'S PART IS DONE: the two `9px` cluster radii and the three `#0007` shadows are corrected in the current set, where the lines are `current/shell.html:150`, `:157`, `:170` - this row cited `editor-shell.html`, the frozen original, which stays as it was - and the correction went wider than the four values cited here: twenty-one literals were off section 3's closed scale (eighteen `7px`, three `5px`; seventeen dock buttons, three view-cluster buttons, the follow-the-system track) and each is now its section 3 or section 5 entry. REMAINING: the third case, the bordered follow-the-system row at `current/settings.html:89-93`, is the modal's and is plan 8's (`vg-303` is its `padding:9px`). AND THE INSTRUMENT CLAUSE IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: no parity row reads any of these literals - putting one `7px` back into the drawing at `be54cfc5` leaves `design-language.spec.ts` green (5 passed) - so the correction this row asked for is not one the suite can hold in place. What would settle the clause is a row that reads a drawing's `border-radius` against section 3's scale; Task 6's gate is its natural owner. DISCHARGED IN PART BY PLAN 7 TASK 6 (2026-10-11, artefact 43e24bc5): the radius clause now has its mechanism - `design-language.spec.ts:2397-2436` reads every border-radius the drawing declares (75 declarations) and asserts each is a section 3 scale step (4, 6, 8, 10, 999, transcribed from `design-language.md:86-94`) or one of three named degenerates (1px, 2px, 50%, each carrying its reason in the row), with a positive control so an empty read cannot pass. The check is the row itself: putting one 7px back into `current/shell.html` reddens it naming the file and line, where at `be54cfc5` the same plant left the suite green. STILL OPEN: this row's other two clauses - the three #0007 cluster shadows and the bordered follow-the-system row - are read by no row, so the title's claim that no mechanism compares the drawing to the bible at all is now false of radii and still true of shadows and borders. THE MECHANISM CLAUSE WAS AN OVERCLAIM FOR ONE ROUND, AND IS NOW TRUE (2026-10-11, artefact c64c4c16, the whole-branch review of the shell-parity plan). The paragraph above says the gate reads every border-radius the drawing declares; at artefact 43e24bc5 it read `MOCKUP_PATH` and the shell drawing alone, and the file it named in a failure was a hardcoded constant - so the clause was true of one drawing of the four in `docs/design/mockups/current/`, which is the same failure this row exists to record, one level up. THE CLASS HAD MOVED RATHER THAN GONE, and the review found it where the gate was not looking: `settings.html` still declared twelve `3px` swatch chips and a `26x14` toggle track at `7px`, `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` the identical track, and `settings.html` a `0 10px 26px #0007` shadow - the same off-scale values Task 3 corrected in `shell.html`, in three files no row opened. WHAT LANDED: the gate now reads the directory through `currentDrawings()` (`mockup-values.ts:104`, a sorted directory read, so a fifth drawing is read the moment it lands) and each failure names the file and line it is in, with a per-drawing positive control; the test now sits at `design-language.spec.ts:2445`. Each corrected literal takes its section 3 entry - `--radius-sm` 4 for the swatch, `full` 999 for the track, as `current/shell.html:338` already read - and the settings dialog frame takes section 3 elevation 3, `0 24px 60px #000000b3`, not the elevation 1 the fix brief implied: the element is the modal frame, its product counterpart `.editor-shell-dialog` paints `--elev-3` (`editor-shell.css:1302`, token at `:362`), and section 3 reserves elevation 1 for floating clusters. RED PROVED: a planted `7px` in `controls.html` reddens the gate naming `controls.html:159`. CLOSED 2026-10-12 BY TASK 2.3a OF THE BACKLOG-DRAIN PLAN (2026-10-12, artefact 6f9b3492). BOTH REMAINING CLAUSES NOW HAVE THEIR ARMS, AND EACH ARM'S RED PROOF IS THE RUN'S OWN JSON REPORT. The drawings gate ("every literal the checked drawings declare is on §3's scale or §2's") gains TWO arms beside radius, spacing and type: an ELEVATION arm holding every box-shadow a drawing declares to §3's elevation table (level 1 `0 8px 20px #00000059`, level 2 `0 18px 44px #00000099`, level 3 `0 24px 60px #000000b3`, or no shadow at all, which is level 0) with only §5 rule 4's two marks exempt — the spread-only accent-at-18% halo and an `inset` shadow, both read by shape rather than named in an allow-list — and a BOUNDARY arm holding every `border`/`border-*` to §5's 1px hairline. Both read the whole file through `mockupDeclarations` and both carry a per-arm positive control, because a control drawing legitimately declares no shadow at all, so a class no drawing feeds reddens rather than passing over an empty read. RED PROOF (0 expected / 1 unexpected, read from the run's own JSON report at `%TEMP%/yunari-drain/red-arms.json`): planting `0 18px 50px #0009` at `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:148` and `border: 2px solid var(--edge)` at `:129` reddens BOTH new arms, and each entry names its file and line - `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:148 box-shadow: 0 18px 50px #0009 - ... is not on §3's elevation table (1 ..., 2 ..., 3 ..., or no shadow at all) ...` and `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:129 border: 2px solid var(--edge) - ... is not on §5's boundary vocabulary - a 1px hairline ..., or no boundary ...`. Both plants were reverted and the drawing is `cmp`-clean against `git show HEAD:docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html`. The green run over this arm and the shell/settings parity test is `%TEMP%/yunari-drain/final-green.json`, 2 expected / 0 unexpected / 0 flaky. THE ELEVATION ARM FOUND A LIVE ONE: `current/shell.html:148` drew the stage's artwork at `0 18px 50px #0009` — level 2's offset, level 2's colour, and a 50px blur where §3 prints 44 — so the drawing was the stale side and is corrected with the arm that reads it. WHAT THE BOUNDARY ARM DOES NOT CATCH, and why the row's third clause is a record rather than a gate: a declaration cannot tell a bordered CONTAINER from a bordered control, so the follow-the-system row cannot be refused by declaration — and it does not need to be, because §5 rule 2 positively admits it ("a switch row whose label fills the row inside a panel box ... is not a field row and keeps the shape it is drawn with"), read from §5 itself rather than granted here. §8.15 CORRECTION APPLIED: the row's text reads as though `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html` were missing — the file is present (33.6 KB) and frozen by design, the checked set is `docs/design/mockups/current/`, and every line this row cites (`:178`, `:185`, `:195`, `:288`) is the frozen original's rather than the current set's. §8.2 CORRECTION APPLIED: the two `editor-shell.css` lines this row cites have moved — `.editor-shell-dialog`'s `box-shadow: var(--elev-3)` is at `:1427` (the rule opens at `:1405`), not `:1302`, and the `--elev-3` token is at `:466`, not `:362`. Both old numbers now land on unrelated content (`.editor-shell-inspector [data-yunari-crop-aspect]:hover` and `--shell-primary-text`), which is how the drift was confirmed rather than assumed.

title: The drawings now declare six values `editor-shell.css` contradicts, and no gate reads the product side of a drawing comparison
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 8 (2026-10-11), materialised from the six `Discovered, not fixed:` trailers in the fix commit `f5e6870d`. The implementation commit `80ae353f` carried the same six in prose only and no trailer, which is why they nearly reached the register as nothing at all. MEASURED, each verified at the line by the controller before filing: (1) the Close - `settings.html` draws `margin-top:16px`, `.editor-shell-dialog > button` declares `18px` (`editor-shell.css:1400`); (2) the rail - `shell.html` draws `gap:4px`, `.editor-shell-rail` declares `3px` (`:872`); (3) asset buttons - `controls.html` draws `padding:4px 8px`, the rule declares `4px 7px` (`:1146`); (4) asset-button text - the drawings say `12px`, the rule inherits `13px` (`:1147-1154`, a role disagreement rather than an off-scale value); (5) the Add pane body - `shell.html:62` draws `10px 10px 14px`, `.editor-shell-panel` declares `12px` (`:931`); (6) the nav column - `settings.html` draws `10px 6px`, `.editor-shell-settings-tabs` declares `padding: 0` (`:1460`) because the 150px is a border-box width and a padding there would shorten the content box the parity row reads (`:1438-1441`). WHY THE CORRECTIONS CREATED THEM: Task 8 moved 268 off-scale drawing literals onto section 3's steps and section 2's scale; where the product counterpart lives in `editor-shell.css` - which appears in no `design-tokens.gated.json` entry - the drawing lands on the step while the product keeps the old number. Three of the six are product-off-scale (18px, 3px, 7px), one is a role disagreement, and TWO ARE COMPOSITION DIFFERENCES WHERE BOTH SIDES ARE ON SCALE (the Add pane body and the nav column), so this is not a single remedy. WHY NOBODY OWNS THEM: Task 9 Step 3 explicitly refuses a fix that moves pixels ('a design decision ... belongs to vg-274's own pass - do not fold it in'), so the three off-scale values are not its work either, and plan 8's ten tasks name no product file for any of the six. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a correction should have been withheld where it created a divergence. The controller ruled it should not - the bible wins where the current set disagrees with it (`docs/design/mockups/README.md`) and spec `:481-483` makes a drawing that disagrees with the bible worse than no drawing - so the six are the price of the instrument being right, and the remedy is a product pass rather than a drawing retreat. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the two composition differences disposed of in Task 10's section 13 difference list if a predating citation exists (the nav column's border-box invariant is the strongest candidate, and it must be verified against a rule that predates this plan rather than against the `:1438-1441` comment plan 8 wrote), and the four scale and role differences as a named product pass of their own. IT IS NOT vg-231, which is the shell's four body regions at an off-scale 12px radius - a different set of values in the same file - and it is not vg-274, which counts that file's residuals rather than its disagreements with the drawings. PLAN 8 TASK 10 SUPPLIED THE DISPOSITION THIS ROW ASKED FOR (2026-10-11, b78ee264), and the answer is NOT the candidate the row proposed: the `editor-shell.css:1438-1441` comment is one plan 8 itself wrote (Task 2, 5e8ba2b0), and a comment the plan wrote cannot license the plan's own divergence, so it was refused rather than cited. The nav column's `padding: 0` was disposed instead as the other face of the composition difference the census already records for its rows 4 and 7 - the product places the dialog's inset on the frame at `20px 24px`, which section 3 (`design-language.md:79`, the 20-24 between-regions and dialog-padding row) positively licenses, so its children declare none; a literal fix of the nav column alone would give it a 10px inset IN ADDITION to the frame's 24px, matching neither the drawing nor the product. The Add pane body's inset was disposed the same way, licensed by section 3 (`design-language.md:77`, the 12-14 section-padding and panel-gutter row; a first pass cited `:79`, which is the other row). Both composition differences are therefore dispositioned rather than open, and the four scale values remain a named product pass - capped and counted by name in the ceiling Task 9 landed (`vg-274`): margin-top 18px at `editor-shell.css:1400`, gap 3px at `:872`, and padding 4px 7px at `:1148` and `:1189`. CORRECTED 2026-10-12 (§8.2 stale citations): the `editor-shell.css` lines this row cites have moved — `:1400` is `.editor-shell-dialog > button`'s `margin-top` at `:1503`, `:872` is `.editor-shell-rail`'s `gap` at `:975`, and `:1146`/`:1148`/`:1189` are the two plain-DOM button groups' `padding` at `:1251` and `:1292`.
