title: The built stylesheet emits only the prefixed -webkit-backdrop-filter, so the glass blur applies in no browser that has dropped the alias and the cluster treatment is a gradient and a shadow alone
check: No rule in `editor-shell.css` declares `backdrop-filter` at all: the cluster treatment is the chrome's own 95% fill and §3's `--elev-1` shadow alone, so there is no blur left for the build to prefix away, and `shell-appearance.spec.ts` asserts every floating cluster computes `backdropFilter: none` and paints no gradient. [CLOSED 2026-10-13: this retires the SYMPTOM, not the cause. The editor's `vite.config.ts` still names no `css.lightningcss.targets`, so lightningcss remains free to ship only a prefixed form of any property — that cause is filed as `vg-430`, and this row's own text already called it "a configuration gap rather than a stylesheet one".]
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11) while writing the treatment boundary assertion, which wanted to read a cluster's `backdrop-filter` and found it unreadable under every palette. MEASURED IN THE BUILT BUNDLE: `packages/editor/dist/assets/index-*.css` carries `-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(10px)saturate(135%)` and `-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(6px)` and NO unprefixed `backdrop-filter` declaration at all (a `[;{]backdrop-filter:` sweep returns zero matches), while `editor-shell.css` declares both properties on both rules. MEASURED IN THE BROWSER: in this Chromium (HeadlessChrome/153.0.8010.12) `CSS.supports("backdrop-filter","blur(1px)")` is true and `CSS.supports("-webkit-backdrop-filter","blur(1px)")` is false; `getComputedStyle().backdropFilter` reads `none` on the dock, the view cluster and the identity chip under all six palettes; and a probe that sets the STANDARD property inline computes `blur(10px) saturate(1.35)`, so the property works and the shipped declaration is what does not. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this Chromium has dropped the alias or the packaged build differs from Chrome stable; what is established is that the bundle ships only the prefixed form and this browser does not apply it. The build is Vite 8 (Rolldown) with the editor's `vite.config.ts` setting no `css.lightningcss.targets` and no browserslist, so lightningcss picks the prefix and the standard longhand is dropped - a configuration gap rather than a stylesheet one. NOT FIXED IN TASK 5: the fix is a build target, and Task 5 owns the treatment boundary, not the toolchain. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE: the cluster half of the boundary is asserted as translucency + gradient + elevation shadow and cannot assert the blur as a computed value, which is also why `shell-appearance.spec.ts` had already chosen `box-shadow` rather than `backdrop-filter` as its discriminator. TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the browser half this row owed is taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3. CSS.supports('backdrop-filter','blur(1px)') is true while CSS.supports('-webkit-backdrop-filter','blur(1px)') is false; getComputedStyle().backdropFilter reads 'none' on the dock ([data-yunari-canvas-toolbar]), on the view cluster (.editor-shell-zoom) and on the identity chip (.editor-shell-identity); and the freshly built stylesheet, index-BCKGgSdQ.css, carries THREE -webkit-backdrop-filter declarations and ZERO unprefixed backdrop-filter longhands (a [;{]backdrop-filter: sweep returns nothing against a raw count of FIVE -webkit-backdrop-filter occurrences, FOUR of which carry the colon and three of which are declarations, the two non-declaration sites being the @supports not ((-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(1px)) or (backdrop-filter:blur(1px))) condition, which carries the colon, and a transition-property value list in which -webkit-backdrop-filter and backdrop-filter sit among filter and display, which does not). Both halves of the row now reproduce. STAYS OPEN: the fix is the editor's build target, and which browsers the editor's stylesheet targets is a support-matrix decision that rewrites the whole built stylesheet — the opposite of a line this task may guess at.

title: `npm run gate` calls itself the one command that means green and omits `npm run design:check`, so a red design:check survives every local close until CI
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13 BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE FIXING `vg-319`'S SECOND FACT, WHICH IS NOT THE TASK IT BELONGS TO. MEASURED: on a clean tree at `3be574fe`, `npm run design:check` exits **1**, naming `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1071 right: 7px` -- "holds 1 violation(s) the record does not, above its ceiling of 0 -- re-record the file's residual set". A `git stash` of the working change re-ran it identically, so it was red at HEAD and not red because of the edit in progress. CAUSE, NAMED. `src/web/package.json`'s `gate` is `biome check .. && npm run gates:self-test && npm run test`; `design:check` is `node ../../scripts/design-tokens.mjs && npm run design:md`. **They are different commands and CI runs both, as separate steps** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:56` runs `npm run gate`, `:63` runs `npm run design:check`). So the local recipe and CI differ by exactly one step, and the local one is the one every close in this repo uses. `gate`'s own `//gate` comment in `package.json` reads "The one command that means green (D1's ruling, 2026-10-12 ...)" -- and it does not mean green while a step CI runs is red. `gates:self-test` does include `design-tokens.mjs --self-test`, which is why the gate is green: it runs the instrument's own fixtures and never the instrument over this repo's files. WHAT INTRODUCED IT: Phase 8's rail fix `8b1b9106` set `right: -7px` on `.editor-shell-rail button[aria-pressed="true"]::before` to compensate the 1px a `§5` rule-6 transparent resting border insets the padding box by -- a correct measurement -- and did not record it in `scripts/design-tokens.mjs`'s `CEILINGS`, whose `max` is `0` over that file. WHAT MISSED IT, AND THIS IS THE FINDING: **Phase 8's close and Phase 9's close both ran `npm run gate` and nothing else**, and the drain's ledger rule names that command and its exit code as a close's evidence. Two consecutive closes therefore reported green over a red check, which is the exact failure that rule was written to prevent -- the rule got the exit code right and the command wrong. Had anything been pushed, `ci.yml:63` would have failed on a commit whose close said green. FIXED 2026-10-13, and the fix is the violation rather than the recipe: the missing `CEILINGS` entry was added by name with the reason it is not a step, and `npm run design:check` now exits **0** with `counted: 0` and `dead: 0`. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THE REST: a decision this row does not take -- either `design:check` joins `gate`, which makes the comment true and lengthens every local gate run, or it stays a separate step and `gate`'s own comment stops claiming to be the one command that means green, with the drain's close rule naming both commands and both exit codes. Either way the close recipe in `docs/superpowers/plans/` and `AGENTS.md`'s verification section need to agree with whichever is chosen rather than naming `npm run gate` alone. NEAR ROWS: `vg-434` (no check resolves a reference into the plans directory) -- a different missing instrument, and the same shape: a rule the repo believes is enforced and is not. `vg-327` (a ceiling count sees a rise and not a swap). OWNER: `src/web/package.json`'s scripts together with `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which is the statement of what CI actually runs. SEVERITY: medium -- nothing behaves wrongly in the product, and the cost is not the 1px. It is that a close can report green while a check CI runs is red, which is the one thing a close's evidence rule exists to make impossible. CLOSED 2026-10-13, AND THE OPTION TAKEN IS THE FIRST OF THE TWO THE ROW NAMED. `design:check` joins `gate` rather than the close recipe learning to name two commands, and the measurement is what decided it: the check runs in **1536 ms** on this box, so the "lengthens every local gate run" cost the row weighed is negligible against a close that can report green while a check CI runs is red. **It is also the only option available that does not require editing `AGENTS.md`**, which is user-owned: its verification section names `npm run gate` alone, and that is now complete rather than wrong. The row's other propagation ask is satisfied by the same move -- the close recipe in `docs/superpowers/plans/` names `npm run gate` alone, which is now the whole local gate, so no plan text needed changing. What did need changing was the drain plan's Task-level annotation at `:593`, which had restated CI's step list (`vg-384`'s rot, in the very annotation that warns about it); it now names the command rather than enumerating the steps, and records that the separate CI step went with the change.

title: The `--text-*` line-height companions are declared and consumed at one site of twenty-three, so the settings dialog reads 1.5 where DESIGN.md section 2 states 1.4
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13 while checking whether the settings dialog still matches its drawing after the 2026-10-13 chrome fixes. **MEASURED, in a browser against a bundle built from HEAD.** `.editor-shell-dialog` computes **12px / 18px (1.5)** and `.editor-shell-dialog-lead` **15px / 22.5px (1.5)**, read with `getComputedStyle` off the live sheet. DESIGN.md section 2 states `--text-sm` **1.4** (16.8px) and `--text-lg` **1.3** (19.5px), and the drawing this surface is pulled to, `docs/design/mockups/current/settings-about.html`, declares `font: 12px/1.45 system-ui`. **Three values for one element, and the shipped one is the loosest.** **THE MECHANISM, AND THE COUNT IS THE FINDING.** The six companions are declared in the `@theme static` block (`editor-shell.css:478-489`, `--text-2xs--line-height` through `--text-xl--line-height`), and the note above them says they are "stated, not inherited" -- with the reason that Tailwind computes its own from a size the token no longer has. But the only shape that consumes a companion is Tailwind's own utility: the built CSS carries `.text-sm{font-size:var(--text-sm);line-height:var(--tw-leading,var(--text-sm--line-height))}`, while a rule that writes `font-size: var(--text-sm)` directly takes the size and drops the companion, leaving the element on `html`'s preflight `line-height: 1.5`. **Measured across the shell: 22 `font-size: var(--text-*)` declarations, 3 literal line-heights (`1.2` at `:1266`, `1.35` at `:1932`, `1` at `:2119`), and one Tailwind `text-*` utility in the whole editor-shell -- `settings.tsx:234`'s `text-sm`.** So one site of twenty-three receives the companion section 2 states, and every other shell surface inherits 1.5. The `@theme static` note anticipates declared-and-never-consumed tokens and points at the `design-tokens.gated.json` ratchet, but that file gates *files* against the design language, not token consumption, and it names no `line-height` -- so this is not already-recorded debt. **WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX.** The correct value is a design decision with three candidates already in the repo (section 2's stated companion, the drawing's 1.45, or accepting the inherited 1.5), and the fix is either "state the companion wherever a size is stated" across 22 sites or "set it once on the shell root and retire section 2's companions" as a scale member. Neither is an on-the-fly edit. **NOT ESTABLISHED.** Whether 1.5 was ever chosen: no comment in `editor-shell.css` mentions a line-height outside the `@theme` note and those three literal sites, so the divergence reads as unexamined rather than decided. And only the dialog's two elements were measured -- the other 21 sites are inferred from the rule shape, not from a reading per site. NEAR ROWS: `vg-326` (the same token family from the other side: the drawings' `font` shorthand sets no line-height, so drawn row heights are font-metric-dependent); `vg-317` (the `--text-sm` decision that gave the dialog its size and did not give it a companion); `vg-435` (same class -- a rule the repo behaves as though something enforces). SECOND MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-13 -- THE PROPERTY IS UNREAD ON BOTH SIDES OF THE COMPARISON, AND ITS VALUE IS ALREADY PINNED WHERE A UTILITY IS USED. Three results from looking for the check that should have caught this, and one of them corrects this row's own first reading. **(1) The expected value is already asserted, for the utility.** `shell-appearance.spec.ts:424-429` pins `text-sm` to `{ "font-size": "12px", "line-height": "16.8px" }` and `text-xs` to `14.3px` -- 12 x 1.4 and 11 x 1.3, exactly section 2's companions. So 16.8px is not merely stated in prose, it is a value the repo tests; the dialog computes 18px on the same token. **(2) The drawing side cannot read it either, and says so.** `design-language.spec.ts:3054-3057`, in the row that owns section 2's type scale, reads: "What this row cannot read, and does not claim. `line-height`, `font-weight` and `letter-spacing`" -- with the reason that a drawing's `/1` on a one-line label is a box rather than a reading step. So no instrument reads this property on either side of the parity comparison, which is how it survived a gate that is otherwise thorough. That limit is a dispositioned one, not an oversight, and this row is not re-opening it: what it did not cover is the product's side, where the value is stated and pinned. **(3) The drawing's 1.45 is page furniture, not a competing value -- correcting this row's first reading.** `settings-about.html:10` writes `font: 12px/1.45` inside the file's `<style>` block, which is the page body; the modal inside it declares no line-height and inherits that one. The same comment at `:3058-3065` says the page furniture is read like everything else and passes today only because its values happen to be on the scale. **So this is not a three-way tie between 1.4, 1.45 and 1.5: the drawn surface states no line-height of its own, and section 2's companion is the specified value.** **WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN IS SCOPE, NOT VALUE.** The question is whether section 2's companion binds every direct `font-size: var(--text-*)` in the shell -- 22 sites, all in one stylesheet, each taking its own token's companion -- or only Tailwind's utility. It stays a row rather than becoming a fix for two reasons: the first reading changes rendered line boxes across the whole shell by roughly 7%, and no existing check can see the property, so the change lands green either way and only a browser assertion proves it. **ALSO MEASURED, AND NOT FILED AS ITS OWN ROW BECAUSE IT IS ALREADY DISPOSITIONED.** Of the drawings' 47 declared property kinds, the two readers between them cover 14 -- `ParityRegion`'s eleven plus the declaration-level reader's `border`, `box-shadow` and `margin-top`. The unread remainder is mostly layout scaffolding (`display`, `flex`, `position`, `align-items`, `margin`, `overflow`, `min-height`), and of it only the three properties `design-language.spec.ts:3054` already names are design-language subjects. Colour is not among the gaps: `SHELL_ROLES`' eleven-token table compares the drawings' palette tokens against the product's `--shell-*` values. NO NEW ROW: filing the remainder would re-report a limit the code states in its own words. NEAR ROWS: `vg-326` (the same class from section 3: a drawn rule no gate reads); `vg-317` (the size decision this one is the missing half of). THIRD MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-13 -- WHAT THE DRAWINGS ACTUALLY RENDER, WHICH MAKES THE VALUE CONTESTED THREE WAYS AND CORRECTS THIS ROW'S SECOND READING. Each of the six drawings in `current/` was loaded in Chromium and every element holding its own text was tallied by its resolved `font-size`/`line-height`, so this is the drawings' rendered rhythm rather than the declarations they inherit it from. **THE DRAWINGS' 12px TEXT RENDERS AT 1.45, NOT AT SECTION 2's 1.4.** `settings-about.html` 7 elements at 12px/17.4px; `settings-keyboard.html` 24 at 12px/17.4px; `settings.html` 4 at 12px/17.4px; `shell.html` 7 at 12px/17.4px. Every one is 1.450, and not one element in any drawing renders 12px at 1.4. **THE 11px TEXT DOES THE SAME**, at 15.95px = 1.45: 12 elements in each of `controls.html` and `controls-light.html`, 12 in `shell.html`, 7 in `settings.html`. Section 2's companion for `--text-xs` is 1.3. **So there are three values for the same role, and no instrument compares any of them.** The product computes **1.5** (Tailwind preflight, inherited); DESIGN.md section 2 states **1.4**; every drawing renders **1.45**. The parity gate reads no line-height at all (`design-language.spec.ts:3054`), so the drawing side was never compared and the three coexisted unseen. **THIS CORRECTS THE SECOND MEASUREMENT, WHICH WAS TOO DISMISSIVE.** It read `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` as page furniture and concluded that the drawn surface states no line-height of its own, so section 2's companion was simply the specified value. The furniture reading is right about where the *declaration* lives (`:3058-3065` explains that the furniture is read like everything else and that a furniture value off the scale would redden that row) and wrong about the consequence: the ratio reaches every drawn element, and 1.45 is what the acceptance instrument shows. **The value is therefore contested between the instrument the user ruled is the acceptance instrument and the contract DESIGN.md states, and that is the user's call, not this row's.** **METHOD, AND ONE THING IT DOES NOT MEASURE.** Elements whose computed `line-height` is `normal` were excluded rather than counted: the probe substituted size x 1.2 for them, which is a guess at the font's own metric and not a reading. So the counts above are explicit values only, and the drawings carry more text at `normal` than the tally shows. Repeating this must exclude `normal` or it will report a number nobody set. **WHAT A FIX WOULD BE, FOR WHICHEVER VALUE WINS.** Twenty-two rules declare a size from a token and state no line-height; one more (`.yunari-add-label`, `editor-shell.css:1265-1266`) pairs `var(--text-2xs)` with the literal `1.2`, which is that token's companion written out. All 23 are in one stylesheet, and the three rules that *do* state a line-height (`:1266`, `:1932`, `:2119`) are deliberate and unaffected. A browser assertion and a pairing contract on the stylesheet would hold whichever value is chosen. VALUE RESOLVED AND THE PRODUCT FIX LANDED, 2026-10-13; WHAT REMAINS IS THE DRAWING. The second and third measurements left the value contested between the acceptance instrument and DESIGN.md and gave the choice to the user. It is not contested, on four readings taken 2026-10-13. (1) DESIGN.md section 2's table gives `--text-sm` line-height 1.4 and its own front matter reads `typography: # --text-* with their stated line-height companions`; the same six ratios are declared in `editor-shell.css`'s `@theme static` block, whose note says they are stated rather than inherited. (2) `shell-appearance.spec.ts:424-429` already pins the utility path to 12px/16.8px and 11px/14.3px - those ratios - so 1.4 is a value this repo tests. (3) The file's own shape: `.yunari-add-label` paired `--text-2xs` with its companion, and the scale pin in `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts` already ends 'every size states its own', so one rule doing it is what makes the other 21 omissions rather than choices - no comment in the file mentions a line-height at any of them. (4) The drawings' 1.45 is page furniture, `settings-about.html:10`'s `font: 12px/1.45` on the page body, and the drawings README states the precedence in its own words: 'Where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins and the file is stale.' `design-language.spec.ts:3058-3065` adds that a furniture value off the scale would redden that row, and 1.45 is not one of section 2's six ratios, so the furniture is off-scale by the spec's own rule and unread only because no reader reads the property. **LANDED.** `editor-shell.css` now pairs all 22 sites with `var(--text-N--line-height)` (21 added, 1 literal replaced). `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts` gains the source contract 'pairs every stated size with that token's own line-height', which listed exactly those 22 sites before the change (exit 1) and none after (exit 0). `shell-appearance.spec.ts`'s density test now reads the shell's own rules in a browser: 18px / 16.5px / 15px / 22.5px against the pre-fix bundle (exit 1), and section 2's 16.8px / 14.3px / 12px / 19.5px against the rebuilt one (exit 0). `npm run design:check` exit 0 with `editor-shell.css` at 0 violations under a ceiling of 0; the editor-shell unit suite 26 files / 317 tests green; the six specs holding the changed selectors 46 passed / 0 failed serially. `editor.spec.ts` ran 80 passed / 5 failed in parallel and all five passed serially in 28.3s, which is this suite's recorded load behaviour rather than this change. **WHAT REMAINS, AND WHOSE.** The drawings' furniture still renders 1.45, so the acceptance instrument is now the stale side by its own README's rule - and the correction is not one value: section 2's companions differ per size (1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.3, 1.3, 1.2), so a single page-body ratio cannot express them and each drawn text element would have to state its own. That is the drawing owner's act, filed as `vg-440`. The frames beside those drawings were already stale before this change and nothing re-shoots them (`vg-402`), so this deepens that row rather than creating it.

title: Two hairlines the control-set drawing draws have no counterpart in the product: the read-only rows' dashed dividers and the section headers' trailing rules
detail: FOUND BY RE-MAKING PLAN 1'S PARITY COMPARISON (2026-10-13, read-only; the census is on `vg-390`). WHAT: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` draws each read-only row with `border-bottom:1px dashed var(--edge2)` (`:176` and `:180`) and draws each section header as eyebrow + count + a `flex:1;height:1px;background:var(--edge2)` rule + chevron (`:31`, `:43`, `:119`, `:126`, `:152`, `:171`). The product renders neither: the read-only rows are `flex items-baseline gap-…` carrying no border (`selection-inspector/column.tsx:196-202`), and the section header ends at the chevron's `ml-auto` (`components/ui/inspector-section.tsx:83`), the section's own separation being a top `border-t border-edge` (`:58`). WHY NO GATE SEES IT: the two comparisons that still read this drawing read the label column's width (`tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:913-934`) and the plain-DOM box's padding (`design-language.spec.ts:2540-2552`), and no row reads a divider. WHAT THE RULE SAYS, AND WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN EDIT: §4 *describes* `--edge-2` as 'A boundary, and a fainter one (dividers inside a section)' (`DESIGN.md:100`) — a definition of the role, not a requirement that any element carry it — so neither hairline is backed by a cited rule, and no §5 entry names either. WHAT SETTLES IT: the user's ruling of 2026-10-10 makes the drawing the acceptance instrument, so the default reading is to draw them; but a decoration no rule requires and no instrument reads is the ruling owner's call rather than a fixer's, and the same question is open on the inspector's selected-state headers, which draw the same rule. TWO WAYS IT CLOSES: implement both hairlines from the drawing, or record them as deliberate and give the item's second clause the rule it is missing. NEAR ROWS: `vg-443` (the same header's family, where the drawing and §2 agree against the product), `vg-442` (a drawn value no instrument reaches), `vg-402` (a capture that compares nothing for a region the drawing draws). RESOLVED IN TWO HALVES ON 2026-10-13, AND THE CENSUS THAT FILED THIS ROW MISSED A RULE FOUR LINES ABOVE ITS OWN EVIDENCE. HALF ONE, THE READ-ONLY ROWS' DIVIDER, IS BACKED BY A CITED RULE AND IS NOT A DEFECT: `selection-inspector/column.tsx:191-194` carries the product's own note — 'A read-only row is not a control: no well, no border, because a border means editable (DESIGN.md §5.1)' — which is exactly the clause this row said did not exist, so the drawing's `border-bottom:1px dashed var(--edge2)` (`controls.html:176`, `:180`) is the stale side and the class-4 entry the census gave it on `vg-390` is corrected there. HALF TWO, THE SECTION HEADER'S TRAILING RULE, IS IMPLEMENTED: `components/ui/inspector-section.tsx` now renders the drawn `flex:1;height:1px` line in `--edge-2` between the count and the chevron, carrying `data-yunari-section-rule`, and its docblock records why this half is a difference the drawing wins where half one is a difference a rule wins — nothing in the product or in `DESIGN.md` argued against it, and the docblock's four recorded decisions (the header is the button, a read-only section says so in words, the 24×24 target, the count's place) do not mention it. RED FIRST, on a build from this tree: `toHaveCSS("height", "1px")` failed `Error: element(s) not found` against the pre-fix bundle, and the whole spec passes after the rebuild (12 passed, exit 0). **So this row is closed: implemented for the header, and backed by §5.1 for the divider**, and nothing in the inspector is left of the drawing's hairline question — the neighbouring instrument gaps are `vg-402` (a capture that compares nothing for a region a drawing draws) and `vg-442` (a drawn value no instrument reads).
check: `inspector-sections.spec.ts` "the section header takes the drawing's rule, §2's mono count and §4's faint, and the subject name §2's 600" asserts the trailing rule (`[data-yunari-section-rule]` is 1px, in `--edge-2`) and passes red-then-green on a built bundle; the read-only rows' dashed dividers are the rule-backed half — `selection-inspector/column.tsx:191-194` cites §5.1 — so both hairlines the drawing asked for are settled

title: The case named 'names where to choose from when nothing is selected' pins a literal that names no place, so §7.4 is counted met by a check that cannot fail
detail: FOUND WHILE CHECKING PLAN 2'S DEFERRED ADJUDICATIONS (2026-10-13). WHAT THE RULE REQUIRES: §7.4 — 'With nothing selected the column is empty and says where to choose from' (`DESIGN.md:279`). WHAT THE PRODUCT DOES: it renders `Select an object to inspect it.` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts`'s `inspectorFields.nothingSelected`, drawn by `selection-inspector/inspector.tsx:60-66`), a line that names no place an author can choose from, so the product is off the clause. WHAT THE CHECK DOES: `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts:635` is named 'names where to choose from when nothing is selected', and its assertion (`:647`) pins that same literal — which the jsdom case compares against `uiCopy.inspectorFields.nothingSelected` itself (`:643-646`) — so the case's *name* asserts §7.4 while its *assertion* pins the string: it passes whether or not the line names a place, and it would pass if the copy got worse. THE ARCHIVED LEDGER ALREADY COUNTED IT MET: plan 6's acceptance records the inspector's empty state as naming where to choose from, on this case, which is how a §7.4 gap survived a plan whose subject was copy and whose instruments were its own. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the fix is a string and two authorities disagree about what it should say — the drawing's second line is `Pick something on the canvas` (plan 2's table row 20), which names the canvas rather than the Add pane the author actually inserts from — so which place the line names is a copy decision, and it is also the half of the item that `vg-445` leaves open. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a line that names where to choose from, plus a case that fails against the present string — the two together, since either alone leaves the clause counted met by nothing. RESOLVED 2026-10-13, BOTH HALVES THIS ROW NAMED. THE LINE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts`'s `nothingSelected` now reads 'Select an object on the canvas to inspect it.' The place is the canvas because that is the surface an existing object is chosen on; the Add pane inserts a new one, which is a different act and not what §7.4's 'choose from' names. THE CASE: `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s 'names where to choose from when nothing is selected' now asserts the property the clause states rather than the literal — `toHaveText(/canvas/i)` — so it registers a line that stops naming a place, which the literal pin could not; the string's provenance stays pinned in jsdom, where it is compared against the constant itself. RED FIRST, on a bundle without the fix: the case failed `unexpected value "Select an object to inspect it."`; it passes after the rebuild, and the whole spec file passes 12/12. Gate `npm run gate` exit 0 (255 files, 3,363 tests). **Nothing of §7.4 is left uncounted**: the clause is now asserted by a case that can fail, and the neighbouring row `vg-445` closes on the same commit for the second half of its pair.
check: `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts`’s case "names where to choose from when nothing is selected" asserts the place the line names (`toHaveText(/canvas/i)`) rather than the literal, so it fails when the line stops naming a place; it was red against the pre-fix bundle (`unexpected value "Select an object to inspect it."`) and passes after the rebuild, with `ui-copy.ts`’s `nothingSelected` reading "Select an object on the canvas to inspect it."

title: Two differences plan 2 deferred to later plans were never landed: the Add group headings are still singular, and the inspector's empty state still carries the capture's one-line wording
detail: FOUND BY CHECKING PLAN 2'S TWELVE DEFERRED ADJUDICATIONS AGAINST THE PRODUCT (2026-10-13, read-only; the census is on `vg-390`). Plan 2's parity table (`docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:731-757`) defers twelve of its differences to plans 3, 4 and 5, and the tally at `:768-771` names them; nine landed, and these two did not. ONE, the Add group headings — plan 2's row 9: the drawing writes `CARDS / SHAPES / CHARTS` (`:743`) and the product renders `Card` / `Shape` / `Chart` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy.ts:709-711`). Plan 4's completion report calls these 'plan 4's copy', and the history contradicts the claim: `bd36733d` (2026-10-04, 'a card is insertable as a unit') introduced `cards: "Card"`, four days *before* plan 2's comparison was taken, and no later commit changed them. TWO, the inspector's empty state — plan 2's row 20: the drawing draws two lines (`Nothing selected` over `Pick something on the canvas`, `:754`) and the product renders one, `ui-copy.ts`'s `inspectorFields.nothingSelected` (`selection-inspector/inspector.tsx:60-66`); plan 3 built the surface (`f1a35b82`) and left the wording as the capture had it. WHY THE FIRST MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: a plan recorded a difference as deliberate on the strength of a later plan's ownership, and that plan asserted the same ownership while changing nothing — so the difference has been owned by nobody since 2026-10-08 while two completion reports read as if it were settled. WHY THE SECOND IS NOT PURELY COPY: §7.4 requires the empty column to say where to choose from (`DESIGN.md:279`), which the product's line does not do, and that half is filed as `vg-446`. WHAT SETTLES BOTH: the drawing is the acceptance instrument, so the plural headings and the two-line empty state are the target, and `vg-154` records the neighbouring case where plan 4 declined the mockup's dashed import row on purpose — the difference here is that no record declines these two. NEAR ROWS: `vg-269` (the third unlanded deferral, which plan 4 declined *and* filed, which is the correct handling these two did not get), `vg-154`, `vg-446`. RESOLVED IN TWO HALVES ON 2026-10-13, AND THE FIRST WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN BUILT. HALF ONE, THE ADD GROUP HEADINGS: there is no difference left to land, because the target moved to the product's own words. The current drawings write `Card` / `Shape` / `Chart` / `Asset` — singular strings at `docs/design/mockups/current/shell.html:63`, `:96`, `:116` and `:128`, uppercased by CSS (`text-transform:uppercase`), which is the form plan 2's table transcribed as `CARDS / SHAPES / CHARTS`. The plural belonged to the frozen original `docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:91` ('Cards'), which the drawings README says is 'the record of the first cut, not the target', and the same README requires the current set's copy to be taken string by string from `ui-copy.ts` — so the drawing and the editor cannot disagree about these words by construction. The process half of what this row recorded stands and is worth keeping: a plan called the difference deliberate on the strength of a later plan's ownership, and that plan asserted the same ownership while changing nothing (`bd36733d`, 2026-10-04, introduced `cards: "Card"` four days before plan 2's comparison), so the difference was owned by nobody until the target absorbed it. HALF TWO, THE EMPTY STATE: landed on the same commit as `vg-446`, whose clause is the same clause — `ui-copy.ts`'s `nothingSelected` now names the canvas. **So this row closes**, and the third of plan 2's unlanded deferrals, `vg-269`, remains the one that was handled correctly: plan 4 declined it and filed it.
check: The Add group headings are not a difference against the target: the current drawings write singular `Card` / `Shape` / `Chart` / `Asset` at `current/shell.html:63`, `:96`, `:116` and `:128` (uppercase by CSS), and the drawings README requires the current copy be taken from `ui-copy.ts`, so the plural `CARDS` belongs to the frozen original `editor-shell.html:91`; the empty state’s wording landed on the same commit, where `nothingSelected` names the canvas

title: The Composition row's role word is painted over by the layer-state slot at the rail's normative 246px - it is covered, not clipped, and the row's own proposed check would pass
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 11 (2026-10-10) WHILE CAPTURING THE PANES FOR THE PARITY GATE, NOT BY A FAILING TEST - and that half of it stands: no gate in this repo renders the panes (design-language.spec.ts's spacing gate reads [data-fixture-root] *, carried only by the synthetic control-fixture.tsx), so the only way this was going to be seen is a person looking at a capture. WHAT THE CAPTURES SHOW: in three registered captures - composition-panel-starter, composition-panel-two-hundred and the new pane-composition - the last glyph of every row's role word is not fully rendered at 1x (Networ / Storag / Cloc / Tex), while the name column beside it ellipsises properly. RE-MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-10, built bundle at 788f1448, live editor preview, default Composition pane, all ten rows), AND THE FRAMING CHANGES: the role word is not clipped, it is COVERED. Nothing reports overflow - .yunari-layer-role's glyph extent equals its box on all ten rows (a Range over the text node gives Network 250-291 = 41px against a box of 250-291, and Performance trends 196-291 = 95px against a box of 196-291), the element is overflow: visible with text-overflow: clip, and .yunari-layer-row reports scrollWidth == clientWidth == 220 with its box at 75-295 and the grid column at 62-308. THE CAUSE IS A SLOT THE ROW PAINTS OVER ITSELF: .yunari-layer-state is position: absolute with left: 212.4px, right: 2px and width 6px, so it occupies x 287-293 - inside the row's own 220px box, but 4px across the role's right edge at 291 - and it carries background-color: rgba(239, 249, 242, 0.75). It is empty (, no children, no ::before/::after content), so that fill is all it paints, and a 75%-opaque six-pixel panel-coloured block laid over the role's last glyphs is what reads as a cut glyph at 1x. THIS ALSO CLOSES THE ARITHMETIC THE ROW COULD NOT CLOSE: nothing consumes the missing width, because no width is missing - the 289-293 range the row measured the cut at IS the state slot's own box. The row had the answer in hand and filed it as a width puzzle: it named the state controls as laid over the row edge by position: absolute, then asked only whether they consume width. They do not; they cover. WHAT THIS DOES TO THE ROW'S OWN CLOSURE CHECK: it would pass, so it is not the gate. 'The role element must not report scrollWidth > clientWidth inside the row at 246px' is satisfied today (41 == 41) and will stay satisfied however the overlap is fixed. The check has to be geometric or painted: the role's box must not intersect the state slot's box, or the capture must assert the last glyph's pixels. FILED RATHER THAN FIXED (AGENTS.md): the cause is now established, but more than one owner could fix it and the fix is a design decision - reserve the slot's width in the row's layout so the role stops before it, take the state out of the role's tail, or move it - and no plan owns that yet, so it needs a ruling first. HOW TO CLOSE IT: make one capture-driven geometric check (role.right <= state.left at 246px) and re-capture the three Composition images. READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, default Composition pane, all ten rows): the geometry the row describes measures the same — `aside.editor-shell-panel` is 246px (box 46-292, scrollWidth 245 == clientWidth 245, so the column does not scroll); every `.yunari-layer-role` box ends at right 275 and every `.yunari-layer-state` slot occupies x 271-277 (6px, `position: absolute`, computed `background-color: rgb(18, 22, 28)` - graphite's panel), so the overlap is 4px on all ten rows. That is the same 4px the row measured, at a different absolute x because the column moved (46-292 today against the row's 62-308), and the fill is now opaque rather than the 75%-alpha block the row found. The row's own closure check still passes and is still not the gate: role `scrollWidth == clientWidth` on every row (41/41, 37/37, 95/95, 30/30, 24/24, 21/21, 21/21, 26/26, 19/19, 19/19). Geometry can be stated at this width: role.right 275 against state.left 271 fails today by 4px on all ten. RESOLVED 2026-10-13, AND THE FIX WAS NOT THE ONE THE ROW PROPOSED — WHICH IS WHY THE ROW'S OWN CHECK WOULD HAVE PASSED. What the captures show is real and was still there at HEAD: measured on a built bundle at 1280×720, all ten starter rows lost the last glyphs of their role at rest. But the cause the row settled on was half of it. The slot is `position: absolute; right: 2px` and carried its panel fill and its 6px `padding-left` unconditionally, so an EMPTY slot — and at rest every slot is empty — laid a six-pixel opaque block over the role's tail: 4px of overlap on all ten rows, `slotWidth` 6. THE FIX: the fill and the lead-in belong to the slot's buttons (`.yunari-layer-state:has(button)`), so a slot holding nothing paints nothing and has no width, and the room the buttons need is reserved by the row's own `padding-right` rather than by a margin on the key column — because the column under the slot is the key on some rows and the ROLE on a row whose selection reads nothing, which is the row the row's own reading measured. The four `:has` arms keep the arithmetic they had (`4 + 2 + 6 + 26n + 4(n - 1)`, the same 32px at n=1) and `design-tokens`' ceiling records the four new sites in place of the three old ones. THE CHECK IS THE GEOMETRIC ONE THE ROW ASKED FOR, with one correction: it asserts the state the three captures were taken in — nothing selected, nothing hovered — rather than every state, because the attended row is a second defect with its own cause. RED FIRST: the case read a 4px overlap on all ten rows before the fix and passes after the rebuild; the file's 11 cases pass and `npm run gate` exits 0 (255 files, 3,363 tests). The four Composition captures beside the drawings were re-taken (`composition-panel-starter`, `-two-hundred`, `-document`, `pane-composition`). WHAT THE ROW DID NOT SEE: once the slot holds real controls, a row whose reserved strip is wider than its columns can spare runs the role under the slot — 45.3px at three controls, 53.8px at four — and no column may yield, since the mark, the name's floor and the role are each recorded as never giving way. That is filed as `vg-447`, and it is the reason the row's own proposed closure ('the role element must not report scrollWidth > clientWidth') was never the gate: it is satisfied in both states, as the row itself said. RULED 2026-10-13: **THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A DESIGN CHOICE, so it is fixed and closed rather than carried to the reading the plan reserved for it.** The run dissolved the question instead of pinning it — the slot carried its panel fill and its 6px `padding-left` whether or not it held a control, so at rest, where every slot is empty, a six-pixel opaque block lay over the last glyphs of the role on all ten starter rows (4px of overlap) and nothing was being traded against anything. title: The rail's slot is a 34px icon-only control, outside section 5's 26-30px icon button
detail:
FOUND BY the controller while correcting a stale STATUS claim about who owned the value, and MEASURED before filing. editor-shell.css:789-790 sets the rail slot's width and height to 34px, and rail.tsx:33 documents it as 'a 34px icon-only control whose one word is both its tooltip and ...'. Bible section 5 states its control vocabulary is CLOSED - 'A control is one of these, or it is not a control' - and its icon button is 'a 26-30px square at --radius-md, glyph only'. A 34px glyph-only control is therefore either an icon button outside the range the bible states for it, or a control the closed vocabulary does not contain. NOTHING OWNS THE DECISION, which is the part worth recording: the shell plan never mentions 34; scripts/design-tokens.gated.json's designLanguagePx array is [3, 11, 14, 26, 30, 32, 36, 46, 246, 276, 999, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8] and contains no 34; and the value lives in editor-shell.css, which is deliberately UNGATED - Task 8 records that file's hex count as a before-state for plan 3 rather than adding it to the guard - so the guard never sees it. rail.tsx IS a gated file, but it carries the 34 only inside a comment, which the guard does not read. So the one mechanism that could have caught this is blind to it twice over. Same family as vg-202 (a well's horizontal padding at 6px where section 3's table assigns 4px): a value off the bible's own table that no gate watches. OWNER: whoever owns the rail's control size - either the rail moves into 26-30px, or designLanguagePx gains 34 and section 5 gains the entry the slot needs. SEVERITY: low, and note the direction of the risk: a target larger than the bible's range is safer than one smaller, so this is a conformance gap rather than an accessibility defect.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller on the user's direction that the rail icons be 'a bit bigger than right now', with the code/architecture half judged rather than asked. THE SLOT GOES TO 36PX, SECTION 5 GAINS A RAIL-SLOT ROLE RATHER THAN STRETCHING THE ICON BUTTON RANGE (26-30px is the icon button's and stays), AND designLanguagePx GAINS 36 so the value stops living in a comment the ratchet cannot read. RESOLVED 2026-10-13, ON THE RULING'S OWN RECIPE AND THEN MEASUREMENT. title: The shell ships two competing cluster treatments, and the glass one sits off the elevation ladder in both directions
detail:
FOUND BY the controller while ruling on plan 2 Task 6's cluster surface, and then MEASURED before filing rather than filed from the ruling. The product has two floating-cluster treatments. (1) The identity chip states bible section 7.5 literally: --panel at ~95%, blur(6px), elevation 1. (2) The dock (canvas-dock.tsx:126) and the view cluster (display-switch.tsx:104) carry .editor-glass (editor-shell.css:375-400), whose base is box-shadow: none - section 3's LEVEL 0, flat - and whose five non-editorial palettes override with a gradient background, two inset highlights, 0 18px 40px #0000004a and backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(135%). Against the bible that is off the ladder twice over: 0 18px 40px is section 3's LEVEL 2 (overlay) value, not the LEVEL 1 (0 8px 20px #00000059) that section 3 assigns to floating clusters over the canvas, and blur is 10px where section 3 says clusters blur their backdrop at blur(6px). Section 7.5 independently calls a cluster --panel at ~95% with backdrop blur, 1px --edge, elevation 1. So in five palettes a cluster renders at overlay elevation and in editorial it renders at no elevation at all. Worth recording precisely: the bible contains NO per-palette glass rule - section 4 says only that colour is a runtime palette of six - so 'editorial is flat and the other five are glass' is an IMPLEMENTATION choice pinned by shell-appearance.spec.ts from the earlier authoring work, not an instruction that outranks section 7.5. That matters because the tempting resolution (match the chip) reddens that spec for all six palettes, which is why Task 6 kept the glass and filed this instead. OWNER: first a design-language decision - which of the two treatments is the product's, whether the ladder's level 1 or the glass palette's overlay value wins, and what editorial does about elevation when it is deliberately flat - and then whoever owns the two surfaces. Task 10's difference list inherits it. SEVERITY: medium - nothing fails and nothing is unreachable, but two settled-looking treatments disagree in the same window and the ladder has no answer for editorial. AMENDED BY PLAN 7 TASK 5 (2026-10-11), which moved the treatment boundary: `.editor-glass` is now the CHROME default (`background: var(--panel)`, no shadow, no blur) and the two clusters opt into the glass by name (`.editor-shell-dock.editor-glass`, `.editor-shell-zoom.editor-glass`), so this row's citation of `editor-shell.css` line numbers and of a base that is `box-shadow: none` with five per-palette overrides is a stale landmark rather than a description of the file. THE FINDING IS UNCHANGED and so is the treatment this row measures: the dock and the view cluster still paint a gradient, two inset highlights, `0 18px 40px #0000004a` and `backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(135%)`, and Task 5 gave `editorial`'s two clusters the same treatment, so the off-ladder cluster surface now reaches all six palettes where it reached five. Task 5 did not absorb this row: the elevation-2 shadow and the 10px blur against section 3's elevation 1 and `blur(6px)` are untouched, and the identity chip's competing treatment is untouched too.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE IDENTITY CHIP'S TREATMENT IS THE PRODUCT'S CLUSTER TREATMENT -- elevation 1 with blur(6px). The dock and view clusters come down to the ladder rather than section 3 gaining the level their glass implies, so the off-ladder surface that Task 5 spread to all six palettes is retired rather than documented. CLOSED 2026-10-13 AS VERIFIED, AND THE CLOSE IS ONE MEASUREMENT PLUS ONE LEFTOVER THE RULING COULD NOT SEE. The ladder half: `d0c67844` took the dock and the view cluster to the chrome's own 95% `--panel` and section 3's `--elev-1`, under the user's later ruling on this same surface (asked for Graphite, answered "All six palletes, all flat"), so the `135deg` gradient, the two inset highlights, `0 18px 40px #0000004a` and `blur(10px) saturate(135%)` that Task 5 spread to every palette are gone, and elevation is now the whole difference between chrome and a cluster. The chip half: this row's ruling makes the chip's treatment the product's, and the chip still declared `backdrop-filter: blur(6px)` with its `-webkit-` twin - the last declaration of the glass treatment anywhere in the product, and invisible to every computed read because the build emits the prefixed form alone (`vg-311`, whose cause is `vg-430`) and this Chromium does not apply it. So the stylesheet asked for a blur while the case that reads all six palettes was green over it. `f7f838dc` deleted the two declarations and gave `shell-appearance.spec.ts` the read that catches the state it was in: the treatment-boundary case now also scans the authored text for `backdrop-filter:`, prefixed forms included, red on both lines before the deletion. THE RULING'S BLUR CLAUSE IS THE ONE PART NOT CARRIED, AND THE USER SUPERSEDED IT THE NEXT DAY by ruling the product flat for all six palettes; DESIGN.md section 3 and section 7.5 were propagated with that decision, so `blur(6px)` is no longer a value the language assigns to any cluster rather than a value these two lack. title: At the bible's 246px the Composition row fits its role column by one pixel, and the attended row clips its name and key, and no test can see either
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 1'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST - that is the finding. Plan 4 moved the Composition pane to the bible section 7.3 width of 246px (editor-shell.css:96, grid-template-columns: 46px 246px minmax(0, 1fr) 276px), superseding the 360px plan 2 had measured. At that width the worst name in the starter is group-trends-card, whose uiCopy role reads "Performance trends": it overflowed the row by 11px, so the implementer re-cut the row's mark slot from 40px to 28px (editor-shell.css:145) and it now fits with ONE PIXEL of slack on the one font stack measured. THE ROLE IS flex:none and is the only statement of what a row is on four rows in five, so a font stack or DPI that renders a hair wider clips it mid-word. NOTHING CATCHES IT: tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts:205-206 asserts directions only (the role costs names; the shipped column clips at least as many as the superseded one) and never a pixel, so the case stays green while the role clips. WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the 246px is bible-mandated so the constraint is not negotiable here; the reviewer offered 26px as a one-number fix, but that does not remove a clip, it moves it from the role to the mark - the column the row is designed to give up - and nothing measured which loss is worse, so the correct behaviour needs a design decision. Plan 4 Task 2 RE-CUT AND RE-MEASURED IT (2026-10-10, commit f94f0f7a), and the answer is worse than the one-pixel fit this row was filed on. On the worst row - all four controls (twisty, rename, eye, lock) AND a bound key - the row is 205px wide with 61px of room kept, and BOTH the key column and the layer name are clipped at 246px (annotations four-control-row-width-px=205, four-control-room-kept-px=61, four-control-key-clipped=true, four-control-name-clipped=true; every structural figure identical across two gate runs, only the millisecond figures moved). It is the SELECTED or ATTENDED row that loses its name, not the resting one, and the controls that cost it are the 26px boxes bible section 5 mandates, so the plan is not free to shrink them and bible section 173 wants the name readable - the two constraints meet here. STILL OPEN, AND NOW A DESIGN DECISION RATHER THAN A PATCH: choose between narrowing the mark slot, shortening the role copy, reserving less room when a row carries all four controls, or accepting the clip on the attended row, then pin the choice with a measurement rather than a direction. Not fixed on the fly because the correct behaviour needs that decision (AGENTS.md). Task 10's ratchet and Task 12's register pass are where the choice is expected to surface. PLAN 4 TASK 3 EXTENDS THIS ROW (2026-10-10, commit 96099ba8, found by its task review): the SAME worst string at the SAME 246px width clips in the Add pane too — the card tile draws "Performance trends" as 86px of label into a 41px box in the four-column diagram grid, and the other seven card names fit. Same cause, same width, same string, so it is recorded here rather than filed as a second row. The accessibility half is discharged separately and in this task (the tile now discloses its full name on hover/focus, proved by a case that fails without it); the CLIPPING remains this row's design decision. CONTROLLER MEASUREMENT, 2026-10-10 (built bundle at 788f1448, default Composition pane): the role column does NOT fit by one pixel - .yunari-layer-role's right edge is 291 with the row's clip at 295 and the pane column at 308, so it has 4px to the row and 17px to the column; the element that gives up width is the NAME (.yunari-layer-name is flex: 1 1 auto with min-width 43.3px and ellipsises in nine of the ten starter rows, its glyph run reaching 256 against a box ending at 246). The role's real problem at this width is not its own slack but the 4px the absolutely-positioned .yunari-layer-state overlaps it by - see vg-265, which owns that measurement.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: NARROW THE MARK SLOT FURTHER. The left glyph column gives way rather than the name, the role copy or the reserve, so the selected row keeps its name and its key readable at the design languages 246px. The rows own requirement rides this ruling: the choice is pinned by a MEASUREMENT rather than a direction -- the worst row (all four 26px controls plus a bound key) is re-measured after the change, and the number is recorded on this row, because the current test asserts directions and never a pixel. COST IF WRONG: the mark is the column the row is designed to give up, so the loss moves there; if the narrower mark turns out to be the worse loss, the measurement this ruling requires is what shows it. MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND THE RULING'S LEVER IS DISPROVED BY THE MEASUREMENT IT ASKED FOR. The ruling was implemented on a built bundle at the floor the column's own contents set — 20px, against the 28px it shipped — and re-measured. THE ATTENDED ROW'S OWN NUMBERS ARE IDENTICAL AT BOTH WIDTHS: on the worst row (all four 26px controls plus the bound key, in a 205-row document at the 246px pane) the name is 28px short of readable and the key 41px short at 28px and at 20px alike; the one figure that moves is the role's coverage by the slot, 58px → 50px, which is `vg-447`'s symptom rather than this row's. THE REASON IS ARITHMETIC, NOT TASTE: the row is 206px with 126px reserved and 6px of left padding, so its content box is 74px, while the line's natural width is twisty 20 + mark 20 + name 71 + role 31 + key 41 + four 4px gaps = 199px — and both shrinkable columns are already at their floors (the name at its `6ch` minimum, the key at zero, the role held at full width by `flex: none`), so the freed 8px only shortens how far the line overruns into the reserved strip. NO WIDTH OF THE MARK REACHES THE SHORTFALL: zeroing the whole slot would still leave the line 36px over the content box. WHAT THE NARROWING DOES INSTEAD IS A TRADE, AND IT IS NOW TWO COUNTS TAKEN IN ONE RUN (`composition-panel.spec.ts`, the shipped-column case): of the starter's 60 names 2 unclip (31 → 29) and of its 28 specimens 5 more lose their last letters (7 → 12 clipped), where at 20px the marks read `V…`, `R…`, `G…` — a column whose whole job is to be recognised at a glance and says nothing. The cost lands on rows the ruling is not about and the benefit on the attended row is zero, so THE COLUMN IS HELD AT 28px AND THIS ROW STAYS OPEN: commit `11d8ce0e` lands the instrument and this record rather than a value, the product's appearance is deliberately unchanged, and the captures and the ratchet's residual record are untouched for the same reason. WHAT THE ROW NOW NEEDS IS A LEVER THE ARITHMETIC CAN HONOUR, and the row already names the four: the mark (disproved here), the role copy, the reserve, and accepting the clip on the attended row. Each of the remaining three moves an invariant a ruling has already fixed — the role is `flex: none` by design, the reserve is what this ruling forbade shrinking, and 246px is DESIGN.md §7.3 — so the next move is the user's. `vg-447` is the same arithmetic seen from the other end (the role painted over rather than the name clipped) and should be ruled with this row rather than after it. CLOSED 2026-10-13 AS WITHDRAWN, ON THE USER'S RULING OF THAT DAY: **hold the mark slot at 28px and accept the attended row's clip.** The route to it is the row's own requirement - the choice is pinned by a measurement - and the measurement is what removed the alternative: implementing the 2026-10-12 ruling at the floor the column's contents set (20px against the shipped 28px) leaves the attended four-control row's numbers *identical*, name 28px short and key 41px short at both widths, because the content box is 74px against a 199px line and both shrinkable columns are already at their floors; zeroing the whole slot would still leave the line 36px over. What the narrowing did instead was trade 5 more clipped specimens (12 of 28 against 7) and read `V…`, `R…`, `G…`, on rows the ruling was not about. So the lever is disproved rather than declined, and the user ruled on the numbers. TWO HALVES OF THE FINDING LANDED ANYWAY AND ARE NOT WITHDRAWN WITH IT: the instrument (`11d8ce0e`) is what lets a person see the clip at all - the row's own text says no test could see either - and it prices any future width in one run; and the clip itself is now the language's stated trade rather than a silent one, at DESIGN.md section 7.3 ("a row yields its name and its key before it yields a control"), which is the normative source item 16's clause needs for a difference that stands. Cost if this ruling is wrong: the product keeps a 28px mark and clips two columns on a row carrying every control, and the way back is two declarations (the slot and the new section 7.3 sentence) with both sides already priced by the case. **CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (`e9d5e670`, `vg-492`): the two sentences stating a four-control row's arithmetic — the 206px row with 126px reserved against a 74px content box, and the attended four-control row's numbers at both widths — describe a shape `vg-462` retired at `e572c302`.** The slot holds at most three buttons, so the reserve is at most 96px, and the fourth arm that matched 126px is deleted. The figures stay as the dated record they are; what changes is that the row they measure can no longer be drawn.

title: The opacity slider does not follow the pointer, and its value lands only when the gesture ends
detail: FOUND BY THE USER ON 2026-10-13, REPORTING THE EDITOR AS SLUGGISH — "Slider adjustments take half or close to a second to update slider position" — AND MEASURED IN THE BUILT EDITOR BEFORE ANY CHANGE. WHAT THE GESTURE DOES, with the pointer driven through CDP rather than by synthetic events, so the input path is the real one: press the inspector's Opacity track and drag it 30 px in three steps over about 400 ms, and the well reads the same number at every step while no value is written at all; one write lands on pointerup and the thumb jumps there. `data-dragging` is present on the control for the whole gesture, so the primitive knows it is dragging, and neither `aria-valuenow` nor the range input's `value` moves until the end. A CLICK on the track is correct — one write, at the pointer — so this is the drag path alone. CAUSE, NAMED: `ControlSlider` is a controlled Base UI slider whose preview half is never wired. `components/ui/control-slider.tsx` renders `value={value}` straight from its props and sends the moving value to `onPreview`, and NEITHER CALLER PASSES `onPreview` — `selection-inspector/column.tsx` passes only `onCommit` and `control-fixture.tsx` passes only `onCommit` — so nothing feeds the drag position back into `value`, and a controlled primitive renders the thumb at the last committed number. The control's own doc comment states the split it was built for ("onPreview fires while the gesture is moving and writes nothing, one changed value reaches onCommit when the gesture ends"), so the contract is written down and the wiring is missing. OWNER: `ControlSlider` itself — a drag preview is the control's own state, because its callers' only contract is `onCommit`, the way a number field already keeps its own typing draft. NOT ESTABLISHED, and not to be guessed: whether the primitive renders an uncontrolled drag with no state owner at all, which decides whether the fix is local state in the control or a new preview route in `SelectionEdits`. SEVERITY: high for the author's felt speed, low for the product — nothing is written wrong, the committed value is the one the pointer last reported, and what is missing is every intermediate position.
check: `inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s "follows the pointer while the opacity slider is dragged, and lands the value once" — the real inspector's Opacity slider is dragged with the button held, and the value well is read between moves. Red proof: against `HEAD`'s `control-slider.tsx`, restored byte-identical after (`cmp`), it exits 1 at "the readout did not follow the pointer: 100, 100, 100"; with the control's `dragging` state it reads three descending values and the commit still lands the last one. Exit 0 on `f849c425`, after `npm run build -w @yunari/editor`.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: NOT REPRODUCED in 30 seconds of live playback against a real host, and BOTH of the rows named candidates are ruled out for that window. The row guessed a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change; neither fired: the viewport transform was byte-identical at the start and the end (0.61602870 with the same offset, zero changes in thirty samples), the chart own box never moved (left 616, top 695, 963x215, angle 0, scale 1 and 1), and a ResizeObserver on the body fired once, which is the probe own DOM reads rather than anything the chart did. STILL OPEN, because occasionally is rarer than thirty seconds and closing it on a non-reproduction would be the same mistake as filing it on a screenshot. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD USE, because two attempts here failed for one reason and the reason is worth keeping: counting ink in the chart region cannot see this. The card is opaque and the sampled rect includes the dark part of the backdrop, so every column reads as drawn and every column reads as dark — the first probe reported a constant firstX of 0 and lastX of the full width, and a luminance profile reported the same. Watching the EVENTS is what separates a slide from data changing, because data moves locally and a slide moves everything. BROWSER PASS TAKEN 2026-10-12 (base 9e5d261e, --workers=1): the triage cell command `npx playwright test editor.spec.ts --grep "playback"` collects ZERO tests - editor.spec.ts has no case whose title carries that word - so the cell reproduction does not exist and this run measured nothing. The row is unchanged and still wants the event-watching probe it describes, against a real host, for longer than thirty seconds. MEASURED 2026-10-13, IN THE EDITOR AGAINST THE BUILT BUNDLE, BEFORE ANY CHANGE, AND IT NARROWS THE ROW RATHER THAN CLOSING IT. The editor's line charts redraw at exactly 1 Hz, not at the 30 fps the refresh loop runs at, because `chart-manager`'s `#applyCharts(false)` repaints a chart only when its reading moved and a line's reading is the newest sample of `source.history(...)`, which the preview source quantises to the second (`FakeSampleSource.history` steps in `sampleIntervalMs`); the gauges and the bar moved at 24.9 Hz in the same window, so the loop is not the limit. Recorded over 42 s on `trends-chart`: 42 `setOption` calls, `xAxis.min` and `max` each stepping 999, 1000, 1005, 994, 1000, 1000, 998, 1001, 1014, 1003, 995, 999, 1000, 1000 ms — monotone, uniform and never backwards, with the axes' span a constant 61000 ms (60 s window plus the 1000 ms playback delay), `n` a constant 62 points, the backing canvas a constant 1958x430, and the object's own rect constant. SO A SLIDE OF THE WINDOW IS NOT WHAT THE EDITOR DOES: it steps, ~16 CSS px once a second, and every difference between the drawn and the authored crop is constant rather than intermittent. What the row describes — smooth most of the time, occasionally sliding left to correct a position — needs a surface that redraws every frame, which is the PLAYER (`player/src/main.ts` calls `hydrateCharts` from `startChartRefresh(refresh, 30)` unconditionally), and the two clocks that could produce a correction there are now named: the axis is built from `Date.now()` per frame while the samples' position comes from `presentationTimestamp`, which `createLiveSource` overwrites with the BROWSER's clock at the moment a batch arrives, and `SampleStore.history` windows on `lastNowMs` — the last ingest — rather than on the wall clock. THE PROBE THE ROW ASKS FOR IS UNRUN: it needs a real host and a display, for longer than thirty seconds, watching `xAxis.min`/`max`, the newest point's timestamp and the object's rect per frame. The editor measurement above was taken with the browser driven directly (CDP input and an in-page recorder), not from a test. REPRODUCED 2026-10-13 IN THE PLAYER, AGAINST A REAL HOST AND A DISPLAY, AND THE SLIDE IS THE DISPLAY REFITTING ITSELF WHEN A TRANSIENT CHROME STRIP COMES OR GOES. Setup: the built player served by `node packages/host/bin/yunari.js --no-browser --app-dir <the e2e display library>` (theme `yunari-new-theme`, `?data=live`, seven charts, four of them lines), a headed Chromium at 1920x1080, and an in-page recorder wrapped around each chart's own `setOption` plus a per-frame reader of the artboard's box, the canvas `viewportTransform` and every `[id^="yunari-"]` strip. THE MECHANISM, and it has three owners: the chrome bands are in flow (`packages/player/src/chrome.ts` puts a strip into the band `index.html` declares, and `index.html` is `display:flex; flex-direction:column` with `#artboard { flex: 1 1 auto }`), so a 29px strip takes 29px FROM the artboard; `main.ts`'s ResizeObserver then refits the scene, which recomputes both the scale and the centring offset. Measured boxes and transforms: artboard 1920x1022 with transform scale 0.946296 and offsetX 51.5556 while a strip is up, against 1920x1051 with scale 0.973148 and offsetX 25.7778 when it is not. THE SLIDE IN PIXELS, read off the drawn canvas by sum-of-absolute-differences over a +-48px window at six horizontal slices, so it is the picture moving and not a count of ink: with the ink at y=300 and y=520, the strip ARRIVING moves it +16 and +24 px to the RIGHT, the same strip LEAVING moves it -15 and -25 px to the LEFT, and a control pair captured with no strip change measures 0 px at both. The two directions are the author's complaint and its inverse, and at 1920x1080 the artboard is height-limited, so the whole composition grows 2.8% and every point left of centre jumps left while every point right of centre jumps right. TRIGGERS MEASURED: the connect strip leaving about eight seconds after load; `Lost the host. Values shown are the last received` appearing when the host is killed (`live-source.ts` sets `reconnecting` on an EventSource error); and the availability strip, `2 of 9 sensors have no reading - LibreHardwareMonitor`, both appearing and clearing around a host restart. AT REST NOTHING FLAPS ON ITS OWN: 180 s uninterrupted, 13,222 frames, one layout signature and ZERO changes - so a slide needs a strip event, and what recurs on the author's own box is whatever makes one: an EventSource reconnect after a sleep or a network blip, or on a phone the browser's own chrome changing the viewport height. UNMEASURED and not to be guessed: both of those recurring triggers, and whether the availability strip flaps on a host whose LibreHardwareMonitor readings come and go. THE OTHER CANDIDATE IS NOW RULED OUT, in the same runs: over 45 s and again over 180 s, every line chart's axis span stayed a constant 61000 ms, its `xAxis.min`/`max` stepped 19-88 ms per redraw, NEVER once at or below zero and never above 250 ms, `xAxis.max` minus the newest point's timestamp stayed inside 1..2682 ms, and the backing canvas and the object's own rect did not move. WHAT THE ROW NOW AWAITS IS A RULING, NOT A MEASUREMENT: today a transient message moves the composition 16-25 px, and the alternative `chrome.ts`'s own comment says was measured and rejected is the message COVERING that band of the composition instead (28.8px of a 390px artboard, 14.8%, while it is up). The two are a trade the module made one way on purpose, so reversing it is a decision rather than a fix - the third shape, permanent chrome taking room and a transient notice overlaying, is the one this measurement suggests and neither the code nor a decision names yet. RULED 2026-10-14: a transient notice OVERLAYS the display's edge and the composition never moves; permanent chrome — the crop strip — keeps taking room. LANDED 476d8db7: `putStrip` gained the placement, the transport and availability notices pass `overlay: true`, and `chrome.ts`'s and `index.html`'s comments now state the split. THE CHECK: `host-chrome.spec.ts`'s rewritten case reads the host box as the whole viewport with the availability notice up and the notice at the top edge over the artboard — red against `HEAD`'s `chrome.ts` (the host box 798.4 against 752.8, and the notice not over the artboard) and green with it, so the slides the author reported are gone for the notices that flash. RESIDUAL, and it is not this mechanism: a phone's own browser chrome changing the viewport height still re-fits the display, which is a viewport change rather than a notice, and it stays unmeasured — the two recurring triggers named above (an EventSource reconnect and the mobile viewport) were never driven on the author's own box.
check: `host-chrome.spec.ts`'s "a notice that arrives after the fit does not move the composition", read on a real host: with the availability notice up the host box is the whole viewport and the notice sits at the top edge over the artboard, so the chart display's position no longer moves when a notice flashes. Red proof: with `HEAD`'s `chrome.ts` restored byte-identical (`cmp`) the case exits 1 at the host box 798.4 against 752.8 and at the notice not overlapping the artboard; exit 0 with the fix, on a rebuilt player bundle. Its unit half is `chrome.dom.test.ts`'s "overlays the notices that can flash, and leaves the crop strip in flow".

title: The gated list's dom-test membership is two of fifteen: which of a converted surface's tests the ratchet covers is whichever task happened to add it
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 8's task review as an observation rather than a defect, and deliberately left unfixed there — the right scope for a measurement task, since its union rule is 'each task's additions' and that rule holds. The list has 23 entries of which exactly TWO are dom test files, display-switch.dom.test.tsx and pane.dom.test.tsx, while packages/editor/src/editor-shell/ holds fifteen .dom.test.tsx files. The reviewer's own wording: 'the dom.test membership rule is genuinely inconsistent, but the report declares it inherited and out of scope.' The sharpest case is a single task: Task 2 CREATED pane.dom.test.tsx, which is gated, and MODIFIED layer-panel.dom.test.tsx (65.8 kB), which is not — and Task 8 has since gated layer-panel.tsx itself, so that surface's component is covered while the test beside it is not, and its sibling's test is. Why this is worth a row rather than a shrug: a ratchet's value is that its coverage can be trusted to mean something uniform, and today it means 'the files their own tasks chose to name'. A reader cannot tell from the list whether a missing dom test was a decision or an omission, which is the same failure mode as a vacuous gate. NOT FIXED IN TASK 8 because closing it requires choosing a rule first, and the choice is the guard owner's to make once: either every converted surface's dom test joins (which would add layer-panel.dom.test.tsx, canvas-dock.dom.test.tsx, document-identity.dom.test.tsx, publish-indicator.dom.test.tsx, publish-control.dom.test.tsx, rail.dom.test.tsx, save-state.dom.test.tsx and shell-layout.dom.test.tsx — Task 8's report measures all of them clean, so the additions cannot fail the guard), or none does (which removes the two current members and changes what plan 1's list has meant since it landed). Task 8's brief scopes this out explicitly, so it is a decision rather than an oversight. OWNER: whoever owns scripts/design-tokens.gated.json. SEVERITY: low — no value goes unchecked today; the finding is about what the list guarantees, not about a violation it misses.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D5's membership ruling covering vg-228, vg-267, vg-271, vg-274 and vg-286 together: TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST. A test file that renders the shell is ratchet material, expressed as one rule in the checker rather than judged file by file -- today 11 test files are gated and 35 exist, and the four files carrying violations become checked. D5'S RULED WORK WAS ADOPTED BY NO PHASE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: this row carries D5's ruling and the plan carries no task that lands it. The plan's own closing rule (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:80`) says a ruled row closes only 'when the change the ruling authorises lands, on the work phase that did it', and measured over both documents **none of D5's five -- this row, `vg-267`, `vg-271`, `vg-274`, `vg-286` -- appears in any work phase's list**. W3 is the phase that owns `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` and its row list is `vg-166`, `vg-199`, `vg-323`, `vg-327`, `vg-329`, `vg-332`, `vg-340`, `vg-384`, `vg-385`; the other four rows appear in no phase list at all, and `vg-274`'s only later appearance is the same recording step's §8.9 drift correction. **So the ratchet's membership ruling of 2026-10-12 produced work no task took**, which is why all five are still open. **What the work needs before it can be adopted, which is where the second half of the finding sits**: the criterion. The ruling's membership test, 'a test file that renders the shell', is not one a text scanner can evaluate -- measured at `vg-286`, a literals-keyed rule gates 275 of 289 test files and 732 violations (mostly chart and fixture data in `renderer-core` and `scene-fabric`, the failure mode ADR-0040 names), while an imports-keyed rule finds the two dom tests and misses the six `tests/e2e/` specs that are most of `vg-286`'s own measured violators. One sentence from the ruling's owner pins the reading; then the work is a checker rule plus the files the row already measured. RULED 2026-10-13: THE CRITERION OF THE 2026-10-12 MEMBERSHIP RULING, asked as its own question and answered by the user: **EVERYTHING THAT RENDERS OR DRIVES THE SHELL**. The gated set is derived on every run rather than enumerated - every `*.dom.test.tsx` under `src/web` (a test file that renders the shell) and every Playwright spec that opens the editor preview (a test file that drives it) - so membership is one rule in the checker and the JSON list keeps only its source files. Measured at the answer, on the built tree: the rule selects 58 files of which 36 are `*.dom.test.tsx` (11 already gated) and 22 open the editor; 22 of the 58 carry literals, 146 in all. The other readings were priced and the price is why this one: an imports-keyed rule selects 16 package tests including three that render nothing (`ui-copy.test.ts`, `copy-defects.test.ts`, `view.test.ts`) and misses the browser specs that are most of `vg-286`'s violators, while a literals-keyed rule gates 275 of 289 test files and 732 violations, mostly chart and fixture data - the failure ADR-0040 names. The work this criterion authorises is the drain's Task 11.1-11.3 (Phase 11), because no phase of the plan has ever carried it.
check: `node scripts/design-tokens.mjs`, the checker `npm run gate` runs, and its `--self-test`: the gated list's test half is DERIVED on every run rather than listed — every `*.dom.test.tsx` under `src/web` plus every Playwright spec that opens the editor preview — so which of a converted surface's tests the ratchet covers is the rule's answer and not whichever task happened to name it. Measured, not recalled: at HEAD `node scripts/design-tokens.mjs` exits 0 with `design-tokens: 118 gated file(s) clean`, its own `by rule:` lines name 58 test files (36 `*.dom.test.tsx`, 22 driving specs) beside the 60 source files the JSON holds, `--self-test` exits 0, and at `44b01bb7` — the commit that derived the test half — the same command exits 1 with `116 violation(s) across 118 gated file(s)`, all 13 files under `tests/e2e/`. The self-test is what rules out the matching vacuity — a rule that selects nothing fails rather than passing, and a file the rule did not select is not scanned. Landed `44b01bb7` (the rule) and `1058424f` (the 116 literals it selected, converted).
