title: The ratchet's gated list has no rule for test files, so a hex literal or off-scale px asserted in a browser spec or a test fixture is unchecked
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 5 (its Step 1 coverage census), and sharpened by that task's review, which re-ran the checker over every file the plan touched rather than only the directory the report listed. MEASURED: 9 plan-touched files under src/web/ carry violations and are ungated, 6 of them under tests/e2e/ — editor.spec.ts, shell-appearance.spec.ts, rebuild-composition.ts, design-language.spec.ts, editor-rail.spec.ts, panel-labels.spec.ts. The other three are packages/editor/src/accessible-names.dom.test.ts (6 hexes), ui-copy.test.ts (7 hexes, theme fixtures at lines 114/133/141/142/146/367/368) and editor-shell.css (68), the last being vg-274. The gated list is not production-only by design: it names four test files (control.dom.test.tsx, control-choice-row.dom.test.tsx, display-switch.dom.test.tsx, settings-keyboard.dom.test.tsx, pane.dom.test.tsx and others), so the actual blind spot is that NO RULE decides which test files belong — membership was chosen file by file as each task converted something. CONSEQUENCE: a browser spec that pins a rendered colour or an off-scale spacing is a second owner of that value and no gate reads it; the violations measured today are mostly fixture data and selector strings rather than surfaces drifting, so this is a coverage hole, not nine defects. NOT FIXED HERE: widening the audit is plan 6's (2026-10-08-iconography-and-copy) and the plan's own Tasks 2 and 5 both say not to widen a coverage contract mid-sequence. SAME FAMILY as vg-274 (no .css file is gated) and vg-271 (a replacement control emits its own native input, which no <select> grep counts): each is the acceptance instrument claiming more coverage than it has. What would settle it: decide whether *.dom.test.tsx and tests/e2e are ratchet material and express that as a rule in the checker rather than as a list.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D5's membership ruling covering vg-228, vg-267, vg-271, vg-274 and vg-286 together: TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST. A test file that renders the shell is ratchet material, expressed as one rule in the checker rather than judged file by file -- today 11 test files are gated and 35 exist, and the four files carrying violations become checked. THE RULING IS UNIMPLEMENTED AND NO PHASE OWNS IT, MEASURED 2026-10-13: D5 ruled on 2026-10-12 that TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST, with the operative clause 'the four files carrying violations become checked'. **No phase of the active plan carries that work.** Searched the plan's own text: this row's id appears only in Phase 1's ruling-recording steps (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:275`, `:319`, `:325`, each saying 'record them; do not re-ask'), and nowhere in Phases 2-10, whose row lists are closed out. Phase 4 is the phase that owns `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` and it names `vg-327`, `vg-332` and `vg-340` -- not this row -- so the checker's own membership rule fell between the ruling and the phases. **THE RULING CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED AS WORDED WITHOUT PINNING ITS CRITERION, AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOWS IT.** 'A test file that renders the shell' is the membership test, and the checker cannot evaluate it: a test's rendering is not visible in its text. Tested at HEAD by taking the *derivable* reading instead - every test or spec file carrying a design literal joins the list - which is the reading the ruling's own operative clause invites: `git ls-files` finds **289 test/spec files, 14 gated and 275 ungated, and the 275 carry 732 violations between them**. That set is mostly files the design language has nothing to say about - `renderer-core/src/charts/fill.test.ts` (50), `tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts` (49), `renderer-core/src/charts/gauge.test.ts` (38), `line.test.ts` (35), `scene-fabric/src/text-runs.test.ts` (25) - where a hex literal is chart or fixture data rather than a surface drifting. Gating them would redden the gate over values the ratchet was never meant to read, which is the failure mode ADR-0040 names ('a gate that starts red and stays red is turned off'). **AND THE IMPORT-BASED READING MISSES MOST OF THIS ROW'S OWN VIOLATORS.** The nine files this row measured are six under `tests/e2e/` (editor.spec.ts, shell-appearance.spec.ts, rebuild-composition.ts, design-language.spec.ts, editor-rail.spec.ts, panel-labels.spec.ts) plus `accessible-names.dom.test.ts`, `ui-copy.test.ts` and `editor-shell.css` (that last being `vg-274`). **A browser spec imports no shell module** - it drives a built preview - so a rule keyed on imports finds the two dom tests and none of the six e2e specs, while a rule keyed on literals finds 275 files. The ruling sits between the two readings and does not say which. **WHAT UNBLOCKS IT, WHICH IS ONE SENTENCE FROM THE RULING'S OWNER.** The criterion: whether a browser spec that pins a rendered colour is 'a test file that renders the shell' - this row's own text says a browser spec pinning a rendered colour 'is a second owner of that value and no gate reads it', which reads as yes - and if yes, whether membership is expressed as a path rule (`tests/e2e/**` plus the dom tests that mount a shell component) or as an explicit list the checker requires to be complete. With that pinned, the work is bounded: the ruling's 'four files' is a subset of the nine measured here, and each violation is a fixture value to move onto a role or a step. **Not implemented by this session, and deliberately**: the criterion is a decision about the gate's coverage, not a correction, and a session that guessed it would either gate 275 files or gate the wrong six. D5'S RULED WORK WAS ADOPTED BY NO PHASE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: `vg-228` carries the full measurement. In short: none of D5's five rows appears in any work phase's list, and the plan's closing rule (`2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:80`) lets a ruled row close only on the phase that lands its change, so this row is ruled and unclosable until a task adopts it. The blocker is its criterion rather than its scope -- see `vg-228` for the two readings and their measured costs. RULED 2026-10-13: THE CRITERION OF THE 2026-10-12 MEMBERSHIP RULING, asked as its own question and answered by the user: **EVERYTHING THAT RENDERS OR DRIVES THE SHELL**. This row's own question was whether `*.dom.test.tsx` and `tests/e2e` are ratchet material or out of scope; the answer is both, as one derived rule, and the six `tests/e2e` specs this row measured are inside it. Measured at the answer: 58 files selected, 36 of them `*.dom.test.tsx` and 22 opening the editor; 22 carry 146 literals. The work is the drain's Task 11.1-11.3.

title: The drawing's view cluster draws its three zoom/fit buttons at 22px where section 5's icon button starts at 26px, so the checked drawing shows a glyph control the bible has no vocabulary for
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 3 OF THE SHELL-PARITY PLAN (2026-10-10), reviewing `42283107` at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/task-3-review.md` finding 3. What would settle it: a ruling on whether section 5's 26-30px bound is the floor for every glyph square in the drawing, and if it is, `current/shell.html:158,161,164` drawn at 26px, with whatever the cluster's own layout then needs. No parity row reads this geometry today, so nothing reddens in the meantime.

READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, the stage's top-right cluster): MEASURED ON THE BUILT BUNDLE - the `.editor-shell-view-step` class matched three elements, each 26x26 CSS px at `border-radius: 6px` ("Zoom out", "Zoom in", "Zoom to fit"). title: `controls-light.html` is named for the `light` palette and draws `editorial`'s, and the drawings README states the false claim outright
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13 BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE PLACING THE CONTROL SET'S PARITY CAPTURE -- the acceptance item says the capture sits "beside the matching mockup", so which mockup a drawing is had to be established before the pair could be read as matched. MEASURED, from the files. `docs/design/mockups/current/controls-light.html` declares `--bg:#fffdf7`, `--panel:#fffdf7`, `--panel2:#f5f1e8`, `--well:#f5f1e8`, `--text:#14120e` (lines 10 and 17-18). Those are `editorial`'s values exactly: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:186-195` gives `editorial` `--shell-backdrop:#f5f1e8`, `--shell-surface:#fffdf7`, `--shell-text:#14120e`. `light` is a **different palette and a different colour entirely** -- `editor-shell.css:400-402` gives it `--shell-surface:#eff9f2bf`, `--shell-surface-strong:#f8fffbdf` and `--shell-backdrop: linear-gradient(145deg, #d8ebe4, #afd4d1)`, a mint. `DESIGN.md:86-87` lists them as two of the six (`editorial`, `graphite`, `ember`, `moss`, `plum`, `light`), and `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/palette.ts:16-22` keeps them distinct in `shellPalettes`, with `systemShellPalette` opening a light-reporting OS on `light` -- so the id is live and load-bearing, not vestigial. **THE DRAWING IS NOT A TOKEN SWAP OF EITHER PALETTE.** Its accent is `#0d7a6a`, which is neither `editorial`'s `--shell-accent:#14120e` (ink) nor `light`'s `#1c6b4f`, and its `--knob-edge` is the same `#0d7a6a`. So it is a hand-drawn light-mode variant on editorial's paper, and the token table was not swapped to any settled palette. **THE FALSE CLAIM IS IN A DURABLE DOC.** `docs/design/mockups/README.md:25` describes the file as "The same column in the light palette -- the same file with the token table swapped, so a hard-coded colour cannot hide in it". The second clause is the drawing's whole stated purpose, and the file does not do it. The same words are in the archived plan that created it (`docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-10-shell-parity.md:451`), so the intent was `light` from the start and the drawing never matched it. **THE LOOSE NAME HAS PROPAGATED INTO THE INSTRUMENT AND THE EVIDENCE.** `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:86` calls it "the same column on the light ground"; `:925` labels the parity row `region: "field row -- label column (controls-light drawing)"`; `src/web/tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts:464` calls it "its light twin"; and `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:59` says "the light ground `controls-light.html` draws (its `#fffdf7` paper)" -- a sentence that names the palette wrongly in the same breath as the value that contradicts it. **AND THE FILE'S OWN COMMENT POINTS AT ITSELF.** `controls-light.html:14-16` reads "`controls-light.html` is this file with the token table swapped and nothing else" -- cloned from `controls.html:16`, where the sentence is true, and not adapted, so on this copy it describes the file it is written in. The `<title>` (line 5) says "Yunari inspector column, light" for the same reason. (`:7`'s `color-scheme: light` is correct and unrelated -- that is the CSS light-mode hint, not the palette id, and it is part of why the name reads as obvious.) **WHY THE COST IS NOT ZERO, GIVEN THE PAIR RENDERS FINE TODAY.** The capture that now sits beside it is `controls-capture-editorial.png`, correct because its ground is editorial, and the parity row reads geometry rather than colour -- so nothing is red. The hazard is the next reader: the acceptance item's clause is "its capture beside the **matching** mockup", and matching by name pairs this drawing with the `light` palette, whose capture would be mint. A reader, or a later capture run, that trusts the filename gets a surface the drawing does not show. **WHY THIS IS A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX.** Two readings, and they are different repairs: (a) the file was always meant to be `light` and should be re-drawn against `editor-shell.css:400`'s mint, which changes what the parity instrument checks (the region labels and the geometry both follow); or (b) the file is legitimately an editorial-ground drawing and should be renamed to `controls-editorial.html`, which is a five-site edit across the mockup, `docs/design/mockups/README.md:25`, `mockup-values.ts:106`/`:131`/`:925`, `mockup-values.test.ts:73`/`:398`, `design-language.spec.ts:464` and `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:59`. Which one is a design call about what the control set's second drawing is *for*, and (a) is a redraw of a checked drawing rather than a rename. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT:** the user picks (a) or (b). Under (b) the rename also fixes the README claim and the self-referential comment in one pass; under (a) the drawing is redrawn and the name becomes true. Either way the six-name palette list is the naming authority the file should agree with. NEAR ROWS: `vg-434` (references that resolve to nothing -- the same class, a name that does not mean what it says); `vg-319` (the control-set drawing's own unresolved facts, which this row's outcome changes the venue of, since both readings alter the drawing that row measures against); `vg-296` (a seventh drawing is read the moment it lands, which is how a rename would be picked up). OWNER: `docs/design/mockups/` together with `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts`, which is the instrument that names the drawing in its own regions. SEVERITY: low -- nothing renders wrongly and no gate is red; the cost is a name that means a palette the file does not draw, sitting in the acceptance instrument's own vocabulary. A THIRD READING, MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND WHY OPTION (b) IS NOT THE CLEAN ONE. Option (b) reads the file as 'legitimately an editorial-ground drawing' and renames it, which is true of its paper - `--bg:#fffdf7`, `--panel:#fffdf7`, `--panel2:#f5f1e8` are editorial's exactly - and not true of its accent. `--accent:#0d7a6a` and `--knob-edge:#0d7a6a` appear nowhere in the product, and the six accents are `#1c6b4f` (baseline and light, `editor-shell.css:41` and `:409`), `#72e0c0` (graphite, `:146` and `:265`), `#14120e` (editorial, `:194`), `#8f4208` (ember, `:314`), `#38601a` (moss, `:347`) and `#543484` (plum, `:377`) - so the file matches no palette in either token. Renaming it `controls-editorial.html` would therefore replace a name that is false about the palette with one that is false about the accent. That leaves three repairs rather than two, and the third is the smallest: stop naming a palette at all, in `docs/design/mockups/README.md:25`'s 'the light palette' and in the instrument's labels and the evidence README, and describe the file as what it is - the same column on a light ground with a hand-drawn token table. THE PAIR'S STATED PURPOSE IS MET, MEASURED: the clause says the second file exists so 'a hard-coded colour cannot hide in it', and `controls.html` is graphite (`--bg:#0b0e12`, accent `#72e0c0`, the shell drawing's own palette at `current/shell.html:17-18`) while its twin is a light ground, so two grounds are drawn and the mechanism the clause describes exists. What is wrong is the name and the words that repeat it, not the pair. RULED 2026-10-14: RENAME IT `controls-editorial.html`. The pair's stated purpose is met either way and that is the measurement this rests on — two grounds are drawn, so a hard-coded colour cannot hide — so what is wrong is the name and the words repeating it, not the pair. The six sites that carry the name are corrected together and the drawing's token table stays editorial; nothing is redrawn, because a redraw would change what the parity instrument checks for that row in exchange for fixing a name.
check: The drawings README no longer states the false claim, and the file is renamed: `grep -rn controls-light src/web/tests docs/design docs/evidence` returns 0 lines, `CONTROLS_LIGHT_MOCKUP_PATH` resolves to the renamed `controls-editorial.html`, and the seven live sites (README, the drawing's own title and comment, the screenshots README, `mockup-values.ts`, `mockup-values.test.ts`, `design-language.spec.ts`) name the new file. Sites that survive are records of what was true then: the archived parity plan, the dated design spec, the dated triage note and the register rows themselves.

title: The line chart advances at its data's cadence, so the View menu's refresh rate does nothing between samples
detail: FOUND BY THE USER TESTING ON 2026-10-14: "The line chart currently refreshes at 1fps regardless of 30fps or 1fps refresh mode is selected." THE USER ALSO STATED THE INTENDED DESIGN, which is the specification this row is fixed against rather than a reading of it: "keep data polling at 1 [sample per second]. The chart refresh selection only affect drawing. In 30fps mode, the frames between 2 data points are extrapolated. The line chart render 1s more to the right (invisible) then scroll into view." CAUSE, named and read off the source: `ChartManager.#readingSignature` (`packages/editor/src/chart-manager/index.ts:517`) keys a chart's draw on its newest sample alone — `history(key, windowSeconds + delay).at(-1)` as `status:timestamp:value` — and the draw is skipped when that string is unchanged (`#applyCharts`, `:451`). But the **line** family's drawn picture depends on the clock: `buildLineOption` (`packages/renderer-core/src/charts/line.ts:178-181`) sets `viewportNowMs = nowMs - linePlaybackDelayMs(chartPlaybackDelayMs)` and the axis to `min = viewportNowMs - windowMs`, `max = nowMs`, and `plan.ts:476` passes `context.nowMs` for the line case and **no other family** (gauge, bar and pie read `latest` alone). So between samples the signature is identical, the window does not slide, and the trace steps once a second at 30fps as it does at 1fps. THE DESIGN THE USER DESCRIBES ALREADY EXISTS AND IS UNTOUCHED: the editor's sources declare `chartPlaybackDelayMs: LIVE_SOURCE_CHART_PLAYBACK_DELAY_MS` = 1000 ms (`preview-source.ts:18`, `renderer-core/src/data/live-source.ts:52`, asserted at `preview-source.test.ts:9`), so the viewport lags the render clock by one second and the series is drawn out to `nowMs` (`renderOverscanRightMs: 1000`) — one second past the visible right edge, revealed as the window slides. Only the draw gate defeats it. REGRESSION SOURCE: `97264e6c perf(charts): a chart is drawn when its reading moves, not every frame` (row `vg-107`, 2026-10-13), whose own body disclosed the trade — "a line chart's trailing window is part of what it draws, so it now advances at its data's cadence rather than every frame — the rate is a ceiling, not a floor" — and that disclosure is the defect. VENUE: editor only; the player has no such gate (`packages/player/src/main.ts:194` calls `startChartRefresh(refresh, 30)` and re-plans every frame), so wall displays still sweep. NEAR ROW: `vg-431`, the same mechanism seen from the gate's side — the idle editor's repaint count collapsed, which is why `glass-lifecycle.spec.ts` now fails on its own vacuity guard; this fix returns a repaint floor to any scene carrying a line chart, so that row's options narrow when it is taken.
check: The line chart advances at the draw rate rather than at its data's cadence: measured in the running editor against the real host, the four line charts (trends-chart, network-chart, cpu-card-sparkline, gpu-card-sparkline) draw 25 times a second with the fix and 1.00 times a second with only the clock term disabled, while the two gauges and the bar draw 25 times a second either way. Unit guard: npx vitest run packages/editor/src/chart-manager exit 0, 64 passed, and exit 1 with the term disabled (1 failed, 63 passed, expected "setOption" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times).

title: plan 7 Task 2.4's constraint contradicts itself: three File menu rows satisfy its own rule for a chord, and the reason it excludes them is false in the source
detail: FOUND BY THE ROOT WHILE VERIFYING TASK 2.4 (`f6335fff`), by reading what each row actually dispatches rather than by reading the executor's report. The plan's own rule is right and its enumeration is wrong, because the parenthetical the enumeration rests on is false. THE CONTRACT, `docs/superpowers/plans/archive/2026-10-07-keyboard.md:1471-1475`: "Only the six Edit items have one (`edit.undo`, `edit.redo`, `edit.copy`, `edit.cut`, `edit.duplicate`, `edit.delete`); the File and Insert items do **not**, because `session.savePackage()` has no binding while `file.save` exists, and pairing them by eye is how a menu starts teaching a key that runs something else. Add one only if the id in `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` runs the same call the item runs, and say which in a comment." THE PREMISE IS FALSE IN THE SOURCE, and the file it names is the proof. `session.savePackage()` is not a row with no binding behind it: the bridge method is `savePackage: () => this.#save(options)` (`editor-session.ts:566`) and the shortcut is `this.#shortcuts.register("file.save", () => { void this.#save(options); })` (`:461-463`). Both reach `#save` (`:703`) with the same argument, and `this.#options` is the constructor's own `options` (`:272`), so the receiver and the argument are identical rather than merely equal. The same holds twice more: `file.open` (`:464`) and the row's `openPackage()` (`:567`) both reach `#open`, and `file.new` (`:467`) and `newDocument()` (`:565`) both reach `#new`. SO THE PLAN'S OWN RULE GIVES NINE ROWS, NOT SIX. Applying "add one only if the id in `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` runs the same call the item runs" to the source yields the six Edit rows plus `file.new`, `file.open` and `file.save` on the File menu -- the three rows it excludes are the three that satisfy its rule most plainly. The rows that carry none are right, and for the reason the plan gives: `newFromStarter`, `releasePackage`, `openLibrary` and `saveLibrary` have no binding in `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS`, and no Insert row does either, since the table binds nothing under `insert`. WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE TREE: `f6335fff` ships six chorded rows, matching the plan's enumeration, and a comment at `shell-layout.tsx:265-269` that repeats the false premise verbatim -- "`session.savePackage()` is not `file.save`" -- so the falsehood is in shipped source and not only in the plan, and the commit message's second paragraph says it a third time. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: AGENTS.md's on-the-fly test requires that "the correct behaviour is already specified", and here it is not. The contract states a rule and an enumeration that disagree, and resolving them changes user-visible behaviour. §7 of the spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:401,482`) says only "shortcuts in tooltips; `?`" and is silent on menu rows, so the plan is the sole contract and it contradicts itself. Whether a File row teaches Ctrl+S is a product decision, not a bug fix. TWO SMALLER THINGS THE SAME READING FOUND, not filed separately: the comment's one worked example is the one that is wrong, so any rewrite of the comment pre-judges this row and belongs with the decision; and the plan's file handle is stale for the third time in this phase, citing `item` at `shell-layout.tsx:268-272` where Task 2.3 left it at `:233`. RULED 2026-10-14: TEACH THE CHORDS. The File rows whose `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` id runs the same call the item runs print their key, each carrying the comment the plan's own contract requires naming which call — so the rule is applied as written to the rows its false premise excluded. Where an id does not run the same call the item runs, the row stays chordless and the comment says so, which is the half of the contract that was already right.
check: The three File menu rows teach their chords, and each names the call it shares with its `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` id: `shell-menu-bar.tsx`'s File group passes `file.new`, `file.open` and `file.save` to `item`'s fourth argument, and the Edit group's comment keeps the half of the plan's rule that was true instead of the false premise. Verified: npx vitest run packages/editor/src/editor-shell exit 0, 27 files / 333 passed. Red-proof: with the `file.save` argument removed, shell-layout.dom.test.tsx exits 1 with "Save package: expected undefined to be 'Ctrl+S'" (1 failed / 25 passed); restored and confirmed byte-identical with cmp.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for. RULED 2026-10-14: A REALISTIC CADENCE, AND THE TOTALS HOLD STILL. The fake source reports on a slower, steadier period so the preview reads like real hardware rather than noise, and **the total RAM and VRAM readings stop fluctuating entirely** — a device's total capacity is not a moving quantity, so only the used readings move. Both are the source's own values and both are asserted where the source is written; "realistic" is settled by the cadence a real provider reports rather than by taste, and the two totals are constants the row's own reader can check.
check: The preview data source holds each reading for its tick instead of re-sampling every frame, and a capacity total is a constant: `createPreviewSource().latest` now routes through `setNow` + `latest`, and `CAPACITY_TOTALS` answers `ram.total`/`vram.total`. Verified: npx vitest run packages/fake-source packages/editor/src/preview-source.test.ts exit 0, 2 files / 29 passed, and the implementer's full npx vitest run exit 0 (255 files / 3379 passed). Red-proof re-run by the controller: restoring the raw-instant sampleAt fails the preview case, exit 1 (1 failed / 1 passed, "expected { sensorId: 'cpu.load', ... } to deeply equal { sensorId: 'cpu.load', ... }"), restored byte-identical by cmp. The 1 s tick is the host's own, not a chosen number: DEFAULT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_MS is 1000 at packages/host/src/server.ts:151, and /ws reported distinct instants 1004/1007/1005/1014/1007 ms apart.

title: A text object's Height field reports what it was told, not what is drawn
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING vg-098, and recorded because it has already cost one measurement this pass. With a text object carrying no authored box — which is what the editor inserts — the Size H field reported 220 while the drawn box stayed about 70. The field echoes the number it was given rather than reading what the object measures, so it is not a reliable probe for a box write. That mattered concretely: an agent verifying the vertical alignment control read the Size field and the canvas, the two disagreed, and the field was the one that was wrong — twice, because the control itself turned out to be dead. Two findings had to be told apart before either could be fixed, and a third party reading the same field would draw the same wrong conclusion. Worth noting it is adjacent to vg-057, which seeded both dimensions of the box from the object's own measured edge so a first Size edit produces a whole box; this is the read side of the same seam, and it is pre-existing rather than introduced here. THE ROW DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and the disagreement was the instrument rather than the field. On every text object reachable through the editor's own controls the field and the object's own edge agree - measured cpu-card-title 27 against 27.12, a freshly inserted caption 79 against 78.83 - and readField re-reads the object on every render rather than echoing anything. Fabric's getBoundingRect() is makeBoundingBoxFromPoints(this.getCoords()), and getCoords() reads a cache that assertBoxWidth and assertBoxHeight never invalidate, because they assign width and height directly rather than going through set (a set re-enters initDimensions). One object read 172.78 x 102.7 stale, and 141 x 28.12 after a single dirty = true; setCoords(). The 220-against-70 came from that. THE FIELD MUST KEEP SHOWING THE AUTHORED BOX - write puts the number the author types into yunariText.box, so a Size field reading the measured edge would name a number it is about to overwrite - but the box is stored UNSCALED, so a scaled text object draws a larger box and nothing said so. The field now says which is which where they differ: Size is the box the text was authored in (140 x 27). The object measures 280 x 54. STAYS OPEN because withdrawing is the user's call, alongside vg-087 which is also measured false. What is NOT uncertain is the real artefact underneath, filed as vg-112: the stale coordinate cache is not confined to a probe. RULED 2026-10-14: KEEP IT, AND FIX THE FIELD. The Size field's height reads the object's drawn box rather than echoing the number it was given, so the readout stops reporting a value the canvas does not have — which is what forced two findings to be told apart before either could be fixed, and what would draw the same wrong conclusion for a third reader. The owner is the readout's own source, and the row closes when the field and the drawn box agree; the alternative of a comment warning readers off the field is refused, because a reading that needs a warning is the defect. PATH CHECKED 2026-10-16 (§8.11), and the table's premise does not hold for this row. Its prose cites no path at all, and the two paths it does carry both resolve as written: `owner` is `editor/src/selection-inspector/index.ts`, and the `check`'s `index.dom.test.ts:1501` lands in range inside `selection-inspector/index.dom.test.ts` (1810 lines) on the case that verifies this very readout — `reads a shape's scaled size, which is the same rule`, whose comment says a shape's `width` is the number the canvas draws. Nothing moved, so there was nothing to correct.

title: ui-copy.ts carries a display cap for Escape that nothing can reach, because the module that owns displayable bindings and the one that owns the vocabulary disagree about whether Escape is displayable
detail: FOUND BY TASK 1.3 OF PLAN 7, and noticed independently by Task 1.2s executor one task earlier, which is why it is written down rather than left to be noticed a third time. Two facts, both verified here at the source. `ui-copy.ts:300` has `escape: "Esc"` in `uiCopy.shortcuts.named`, the map `display.ts:48-52` reads to print a named key. And `display.ts:75-84` builds every label from `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` **only**, so `shortcutLabel("view.exit-group")` filters an empty list and returns `""`. `view.exit-group` is bound on `Escape`, but it lives in `CONTEXT_SHORTCUTS` (`index.ts:67-71`), whose own comment says those bindings are never displayed. So the string is unreachable and stays unreachable after Task 3.3, which binds `?` and not Escape. WHY IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN NOTHING: the two modules disagree about one fact. `index.ts` holds that Escape is deliberately undisplayable; `ui-copy.ts` holds a display cap for it. Neither is wrong alone and the pair is incoherent, which is the same shape as vg-179 (`colour-picker.tsx` bypassing the vendored popover) one layer down. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the correct behaviour is not specified, which is the condition AGENTS.md turns on. Keeping the entry is defensible -- `named` is a vocabulary keyed by *key name*, Escape is a key the product binds, and the entry is correct the moment anything renders a context binding -- and deleting it is equally defensible as dead copy. Picking one is a decision about whether that map describes keys or surfaces, not a lookup. No test can catch it either way. Cosmetic in effect: nothing renders wrong, and no author can see the difference. RE-MEASURED BY TASK 1 OF PLAN 6 (2026-10-11), and the title's premise has moved. The first of the two facts is gone: `uiCopy.shortcuts.named` no longer exists -- that block now holds `reference`, `close`, `alternativeSeparator` and `groups` -- so nothing in `ui-copy.ts` claims Escape is displayable and the two-module disagreement the title asserts is no longer in the code. `escape: "Esc"` now lives at `shortcut-manager/display.ts:57` in `NAMED_KEYS`, with `"Escape"` at `:74` in `SPOKEN_NAMED_KEYS`: the vocabulary's own home, seen by nothing else. The residual survives and is narrower than the title says. `CONTEXT_SHORTCUTS` (`shortcut-manager/index.ts:86-90`) binds `{ key: "escape", modifier: false, action: "view.exit-group" }` under a comment saying those bindings are never displayed, so `shortcutLabel("view.exit-group")` filters an empty list and returns `""`. That is now **by design rather than by disagreement**, which collapses the two readings this row posed into one question: whether a context-only binding should be labelable at all. The row stays OPEN with its cause still not established; the title is left as written because it is this row's identity, and retitling it is the closing edit's to make. RULED 2026-10-14: A CONTEXT-ONLY BINDING IS NOT LABELABLE. `escape: "Esc"` leaves `uiCopy.shortcuts.named`, so the vocabulary stops carrying a cap nothing can print, and `CONTEXT_SHORTCUTS` stays undisplayed exactly as its own comment says it is. The point of the row was that two modules disagreed about one fact; this makes them agree on the side the binding's own owner already took, rather than growing the display module a reach no surface currently shows.
check: The Escape display cap is now pinned on both sides, so the unreachable entry cannot return unnoticed. Confirmed by the scoped re-review at `88d1f0ba`: one case catches both halves — re-adding `SPOKEN_NAMED_KEYS.escape` alone reddens `display.test.ts:104` at "expected 'Escape' to be ''", and re-adding `NAMED_KEYS.escape` alone reddens `:93` at "expected true to be false" — and the case's comment and its renamed neighbour now describe what the assertions do. display suite exit 0 (11 passed).

title: The parity gate accepts any reason for a divergence, so a plan can grade its own surface 'deliberate' against a drawing it does not resemble — the rule that the mockup governs where the written rules are silent was absent
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER on 2026-10-10, answering the user's "why is it so hard to stay on target when we already have a clear visual mockup?" — the question was the finding: the process had no instrument that could report drift. MEASURED, by reading what each parity gate actually did rather than what it promised: plans 1-5 built to docs/design/design-language.md (the bible — §3 space/radius/elevation, §4 colour roles, §5 the closed control vocabulary, §7 per-surface rules) plus the spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md), and BOTH ARE PROSE ABOUT A LANGUAGE. A surface can carry every correct token, every control in the vocabulary, no hex literal and the right rhythm, and still look nothing like docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html — which is exactly what shipped: the shell insets its four regions 8px apart at an off-scale 12px radius where the drawing is flush (editor-shell.css:726,729,749,814,1130,1784, filed as vg-231), and the settings modal the just-closed plan built departs from the drawing's settings section in its frame, tab strip and palette cards (evidence: .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/settings-vs-mockup-measurement.md). Spec §13 makes "a capture beside the mockups" a gate item, so every plan did produce one — six images for the settings modal alone — and every plan also produced a WRITTEN LIST of differences, ten of eleven called deliberate at plan 5 Task 6 and 22 at plan 2 Task 10. A written list is an argument; it has no failing state, so the gate could not redden and each plan closed green on accumulating drift. The controller compounded it by ruling those differences legitimate instead of treating the drawing as the acceptance test. CONSEQUENCE: the acceptance instrument claims coverage it does not have, the same family as vg-271 (a replacement control emits its own native input, which no <select> grep counts), vg-274 (no .css file is gated at all) and vg-286 (no rule decides which test files the ratchet covers). ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT DEFECT: vg-291 is the mockup file left stale; this row is the absent comparison, and this one is the cause. NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is a check or a rule — either measure a built surface's treatment and compare it to the drawing's, or make the drawing's own values the source a surface resolves from so the two cannot diverge — and that is the mockup-parity plan the user's 2026-10-10 ruling requires. What would settle it: state which surface-to-mockup comparison is enforced, name the owner, and prove it reddens on the state shipped today. CORRECTED 2026-10-10, BY THE USER, who said the verify step was requested at the outset: "I specifically requested to add a verify step to each of the plan to compare the current state against the mockup." That is true and this row's first version was wrong to say no comparison existed. VERIFIED: the requirement is in the spec — §12's table is followed by "Every plan above ends with a mockup-parity gate (§13) ... a completion condition of each plan", §13 steps 1-4 specify capture, placement beside the drawing, a difference list and an empty-diff finding, and the Acceptance section carries it as an item — and all six plans carry the gate (parity-step hits: gates 4, shell 3, inspector 4, panes 2, settings 4, copy 5). So the step existed, ran in every plan, and produced exactly this. THE REAL DEFECT IS THE ADJUDICATION RULE, at §13 step 3 as it stood: "Every difference is either fixed, or recorded in the commit as deliberate, with the reason." Any reason satisfied it. Plan 5 Task 6 listed eleven differences and recorded ten as deliberate, each citing a section's SILENCE as the warrant — D1 kept a horizontal tab strip because "§7 fixes the three tabs and what each holds, not their axis"; D2 kept two-column radio rows where the drawing has a 3x2 grid of cards; D3 kept the drawing's explanatory line absent; D9 kept the palette's glass where the drawing is opaque — and the aggregate of those locally-reasonable reasons is a modal the user described as looking nothing like the mockup. Plan 2's Task 10 has the same shape at 22 differences. A verdict that cannot be wrong is not a gate, and the missing premise was that silence in the bible is the drawing's jurisdiction rather than a licence. FIXED IN THE SPEC, 2026-10-10: §13 step 3 now requires a deliberate difference to name the bible §N, ADR or spec section that POSITIVELY requires the product's treatment; a new paragraph states that the mockup governs wherever the written rules are silent and quotes this failure as why it exists; the mockup-current paragraph now records the user's ruling that replacing the drawing is not an available disposition, allowing edits only to repair a stale or self-contradictory drawing; and the Acceptance item now reads for what a citation proves. STILL OPEN: the product surfaces are not yet brought to the drawing — that is the mockup-parity plan, scoped from the measurements in .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/. What would settle it: a parity report whose deliberate differences each cite a rule that requires them, or none. SECOND MECHANISM, SAME ROW, FOUND BY THE MEASUREMENT OF 2026-10-10: a plan can license its own divergence. Exactly one of the settings modal's 19 measured regions is backed by a bible section, and that section - §5's "Choice row" - was ADDED TO THE BIBLE BY THE SAME PLAN that then cited it to justify drawing palette choices as radio rows instead of the mockup's cards. Amending the written language is legitimate (the control set is closed and the plan had to name the control it added), but a section written in the same commit is evidence of what was decided, not a rule that required it, and it cannot discharge the gate. The spec's §13 amendment of 2026-10-10 carries this as well as the silence rule: only a licence that predates the divergence counts.
check: The parity gate no longer accepts any reason: a licence names a resolvable rule, quotes a whole unit of it, and dates that quotation. Confirmed by a scoped re-review at `13015088` — the workflow sets `fetch-depth: 0` (`ci.yml:37-44`), `requireFullHistory` refuses a shallow tree loudly (proved on a real `git clone --depth 1`: exit 1, seven failures each naming the checkout), and `ruleCommit` dates the quoted text rather than the section marker, so the §5 row added by `61d7435b` is now caught where the marker arm let it pass. Wrap-awareness is load-bearing: replacing `rawOffsetOf` with `indexOf` reddens two cases. Two LOW findings remain and are filed as vg-476 and vg-477 rather than closed here.

title: A layer row's kind mark is drawn four different ways, and the add pane's shape glyphs are hand-authored rather than drawn from the one icon family
detail: FOUND BY THE USER while testing the editor, in the list they gave on 2026-10-14 (item 2): group and chart icons are right, a text row should be a T in a rounded rectangle outline, a shape row should be its own type's mark as the add panel draws it, one representative icon per kind, and every icon in the GUI should be Lucide. The add pane's shape tiles are hand-authored SVG rather than Lucide, deliberately and with the reason written down: `panes/add/add-pane.tsx:171-182` draws them and `:158-170` records that Lucide has no `wedge` or `arc`, which is the obstacle the user's request has to answer rather than assume away. `editor-shell/icons.ts:47` states it is the only module that reads lucide, and `object-actions.ts:1-23` imports lucide too, so that claim is already false. RULED 2026-10-15, on the scoped review of `a7745cc7` (agent's report at `C:\tmp\yunari-drain\task-13.2-review.md`): **the commit is accepted and this row STAYS OPEN.** The row's own title names two owners — the layer row's mark and the add pane's hand-authored glyphs — and the commit discharges the first alone, so a `verified` check would have to name a word from a half that is untouched. Everything the review could test held: the red-proofs reproduce with the implementer's own messages and restore byte-identical under `cmp`; the five affected files exit 0 at 107/107; `tsc -p packages/editor` exits 0 with zero errors, **so the three errors the implementer's own report carried are live-tree sibling artefacts rather than a defect**; and the four files outside the brief's list are this task's own — the brief was under-scoped, the commit did not over-reach, and each of the four is argued by its diff (the deleted `.yunari-layer-thumb` class, the mark comments and deleted classes in `editor-shell.css`, the `LayerMark` reshape `kind-mark.tsx` consumes, and the specimen half of `clippedNames`). **WHAT IT DID DISCHARGE:** the mark column is one glyph per kind from one family, and the specimen, the paint swatch and the thumbnail are gone. The reviewer probed every Fabric shape class's `type` getter — `rect`, `ellipse`, `polygon`, `polyline`, `line`, `path`, `arc`, `wedge` — and every one takes a mark, so no primitive falls through to a generic glyph. **WHAT IT DID NOT:** the text mark is `Type`, not the `T` in a rounded-rectangle outline the user asked for (`editor-shell/icons.ts:220`), and no such glyph exists in `lucide-react` 1.48.0 — `SquareText` is a rounded square with three rules, and no `square-type` is installed. The add pane's shape tiles are still hand-authored (`panes/add/add-pane.tsx` untouched; `icons.test.tsx:92` still exempts it). And **`wedge` takes `ChartPie` (`icons.ts:172`), the same component the chart family's own `pie` wears (`:137`)**, so a wedge shape row and a pie chart row render the identical class. **THE CONFLICT THE USER'S OWN ITEM CONTAINS, now measured rather than argued:** "a shape row should be its own type's mark AS THE ADD PANEL DRAWS IT" and "every icon in the GUI should be Lucide" cannot both hold while the add panel draws its shape tiles by hand — and it draws them by hand for the reason this row already recorded, that Lucide has no `wedge` or `arc`. The two halves resolve only together: bring the add pane's tiles into the one vocabulary, and the layer row's mark agrees with the add pane's by construction rather than by being copied. **THE FOUR FINDINGS ARE CARRIED AS TASK 13.2b** rather than a fix round on a finished agent, because they are one coherent change — one vocabulary for every icon, the add pane included — and because they need a de-collision decision with two possible owners (`wedge` moves, or the chart family's `pie` does). It runs after 13.4 on a settled tree. Also carried, and one line: the comment at `kind-mark.dom.test.tsx:42-45` claims the expectations are read off the vocabulary "rather than written as a literal", while `:120` and `:125` assert the literals `lucide-gauge` and `lucide-chart-line` — defensible assertions under an untrue comment, in the file that must gain the cross-arm distinctness case `wedge` and `pie` now need. **CLOSED 2026-10-15 as `verified`**, by Task 13.2b's close: the scoped review of `a7745cc7` found the title named two owners and that commit discharged one, so the add pane's half is `ffa23c9c` and both are named in `check`. title: The rule that a bounded number carries a slider is applied to five fields and not to the rest, so corner radius, border, shadow and rotation are typed-only
detail: FOUND BY THE USER while testing the editor, in the list they gave on 2026-10-14 (item 12): "all properties that accept a min & max numerical values should get the slider + input box combo. Currently many doesn't. For example: corner radius, polygon's sides, rotation degree, start angle, end angle, etc." MEASURED AND RENDERED 2026-10-14, by a census over the rendered column's own `data-*` hooks: the controls that ALREADY have a slider are opacity, a polygon's sides (3–32), an arc's start and end angle (0–360) and the glass blur. Those that are TYPED-ONLY are the corner radius, the panel border, the shadow's blur and offset, and rotation — `selection-inspector/panel.ts:200-212`, `:244-263`, `:281-299` and `per-kind-column.ts:312-326`. THIS IS AN EXISTING VERIFIED RULE'S UNFINISHED APPLICATION RATHER THAN A NEW DECISION: `vg-007` (archived, verified, `source: user`) owns the rule in its own words — a bounded number field clamps onto its bound and carries a native slider — so the row that closes this one should cite that rule rather than re-decide it. It is also NOT `vg-254`, which is a different subject. NO SWEEP ROW OWNS THE GAP. The census covered the selection column and not every field in the editor, so the list above is a lower bound rather than the whole set. THE FULL SWEEP, taken 2026-10-15 after the user said their examples were examples: twenty-five fields, and the count of places that decide how a number renders was written down wrong here — the corrected count, with its method, is further down. Across the selection inspector the writable boundary is the `WRITABLE_FIELD_IDS` map in `selection-inspector/view.ts`, which holds 26 ids of which EIGHTEEN are numeric — seventeen `"integer"` and one `"number"` (this is the re-measurement of 2026-10-15; the earlier text said 27 ids and 12 numeric fields and neither reproduces — the method is to count the map's own `[id, kind]` entries by kind, in that one file). The column renders those numbers in two shapes: FIVE are already sliders (`opacity`, `shape-sides`, `shape-angle-startAngle`, `shape-angle-endAngle`, `glass-blur`) and FOUR are bounded and typed only (`angle`, `panel-radius`, `panel-border`, `panel-shadow-blur`). `panel-shadow-offset` is DELIBERATELY unbounded and `panel.ts:289-291` says why (a shadow above a panel is legitimate, and a floor of zero would display a value the field then refuses), so it is not a candidate; neither are left/top/width/height or a line's four endpoints. THE LARGEST PART OF THE SWEEP IS OUTSIDE THE COLUMN THE FIRST CENSUS READ: the chart panel's numeric setting descriptors in `renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts`: TWENTY-SEVEN descriptors whose `kind` is `"number"` (method: count them in that one file, which ADR-0028 makes the single owner of chart settings), of which TWENTY-ONE carry a bound and NONE was a slider. TEN carried BOTH bounds at that reading and needed no decision — `animation.durationMs` and `appearMs` (0-5000), `startAngle`/`endAngle` (-360..360, four descriptors across families), `gradientSegments` (2-256), `categoryGapPercent` (0-100), `innerRadiusPercent`/`outerRadiusPercent` (0-100). ELEVEN carried a MINIMUM ALONE. SEVEN of them were pixel measures whose ceiling is the object's own drawn box rather than a constant — `thickness`, `lineWidth`, `markerSize`, `barWidth`, `cornerRadius` (two descriptors), `trackCornerRadius` — and THREE are bounded by something no field of their own carries: `windowSeconds` and `maxPoints` by the sample store and `total.value` by the chart's own data domain. So twenty-one of the twenty-seven carry a bound, eighteen of them a ceiling this surface can read and three a ceiling it cannot; the remaining SIX numeric descriptors are genuinely unbounded and the rule does not reach them. **THE RENDER SITES ARE NOT THREE, and this sentence is why the row was re-opened.** Measured 2026-10-15 by grepping `packages/*/src` for the literal `control: "slider"` and excluding test files: nine hits, of which SEVEN are emission sites across SIX modules — `selection-inspector/panel.ts` (two), `selection-inspector/per-kind-column.ts`, `selection-inspector/bounds-from-drawn-box.ts`, `selection-inspector/appearance.ts`, `selection-inspector/glass.ts` and `chart-manager/panel.ts` — and TWO are the union's own type declaration (`selection-inspector/view.ts`, `chart-manager/chart-fields.tsx`). The "three" was an enumeration of what one grep printed on one date, and the "four" before it the same mistake a revision earlier; neither was a count of the owners. NOT COVERED, and so not claimed: the artboard panel, the palette and theme panes and the settings modal have no numeric `control` site at all (a grep over all five packages returns only the emission sites counted above), but whether they carry a bounded number through some other control shape was not checked. OUTCOME, 2026-10-15 (Task 14.1, re-measured in its fix round): the rule is applied to every bounded number the selection inspector and the chart manager offer, and the bound is read from its owner rather than chosen at the field. The inspector's four typed-only fields are sliders now — the panel border and the shadow's blur take the panel's own drawn edge, the corner radius half of it (`drawnEdge` and `radiusBound`, which are `vg-478`, moved out of `panel.ts` into `selection-inspector/bounds-from-drawn-box.ts` in the same fix round that crossed AGENTS.md's 800-line stop), and rotation is -360..360 in `per-kind-column.ts`. `panel-shadow-offset` is the one that stays typed-only, and `panel.ts` says why: Fabric's `offsetY` is unbounded, so there is no ceiling for the rule to reach. In the chart manager the ten descriptors that already carried both bounds hand those over, `padAngle` gained `max: 360` as the unit's own ceiling (making eleven both-bound), and the seven pixel measures declare the *source* of their ceiling (`bound: "drawnBox"` / `"halfDrawnBox"` in `renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts`) so `chart-manager/panel.ts` reads it off the chart's own drawn box at projection time; a chart whose box cannot be read keeps a typed number rather than a guessed ceiling. **THE CHART MANAGER'S OWN HAND-BUILT SERIES ROW WAS MISSED BY THE FIRST PASS**, which is the failure `vg-490` records — a check of a capability *nearby* is not a check of the finding: `chart-manager/chart-fields.tsx` rendered a series' `Precision` through `ControlNumber min 0 max 6` with no track, inside the surface the census claimed to have swept. It is a `ControlSlider` over the schema's own 0–6 whole steps now, and every `ControlNumber` in that file carrying both a `min` and a `max` was swept **by form rather than by the one site a review named**: ONE was found and converted, and `Scale` and `Offset` carry no bound at all, so they stay typed. THREE FIELDS GET NO SLIDER and the ruling says so rather than leaving them to look unfinished: `windowSeconds` and `maxPoints` are bounded by the sample store and `total.value` by the chart's own data domain, so a track would offer a range that neither honours. THE `NOT COVERED` CLAUSE ABOVE IS CHECKED NOW, and the first reading of it was wrong in the same direction: the artboard, palette and theme panes do carry numeric controls through `ControlNumber` rather than through the `control` union, and THREE bounded typed-only controls sit outside the two surfaces swept here rather than one — the artboard size pair (both halves `min: 1 max: 16384` in `panes/document/artboard-fields.tsx` and `new-document-chooser.tsx`), the chart series' `Precision` above (converted in this task, and inside the chart manager rather than outside it), and a gradient stop's offset at `min: 0 max: 1` in `panes/tokens/paint-list.tsx` (`data-yunari-palette-stop-offset`), which is filed as `vg-493` rather than swept here. THE ARTBOARD PAIR STAYS TYPED: 16384 is `MAX_ARTBOARD_DIMENSION` (`renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts`), the largest artboard a package may hold — a *validity ceiling* the document format enforces, not a range anyone drags — which is a different thing from `precision`'s 0–6 or this offset's 0–1, and `vg-493` carries that reason so it is not re-litigated.
check: Every bounded number the selection inspector and the chart manager offer carries a slider with a typed well beside it — where **bounded means it carries a `max` this surface reads**, so the three descriptors whose ceiling lives in the sample store or in the chart's own data (`windowSeconds`, `maxPoints`, `total.value`) are outside the universal rather than exceptions to it — and each bound is read from the field's owner: read by `selection-inspector/panel.dom.test.ts`'s `carries the track-and-well pair on every bounded panel number` (border, corner radius and shadow blur are ranges with a `-well`, the unbounded offset is a text box), `index.dom.test.ts`'s `refuses a fractional rotation rather than storing it` (rotation is a range bounded -360..360 with a typed well), `chart-manager/panel.dom.test.ts`'s `gives every bounded number a slider, with its bound read from its owner` (the drawn box hands the ceiling over and a radius takes half of it) and `leaves the three a track cannot honour typed, and says why`, and `chart-manager/chart-fields.dom.test.tsx`'s `carries a precision as a bounded whole number, and refuses a fraction in its well` (the hand-built series row a fix round converted — it was typed-only with `min 0 max 6`, so this check was false as written until that case existed). The rendered readings are on BOTH surfaces: `tests/e2e/inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s `gives every bounded number in the column the pair, and leaves the unbounded one typed` for the selection column, and the same file's `gives every bounded number in the chart manager the pair, read rendered` for the chart manager, which censuses every `data-yunari-chart-setting` and `data-yunari-binding-field` control by form. Landed by `51d48065` (the inspector: corner radius, panel border, shadow blur, rotation) and `8598fde2` (the chart settings, including the three the ruling leaves typed). The bounded field the check was false for and the rendered census of the other surface both landed in `dc0fa28d`.

title: The corner radius accepts any value and stores it, while the render saturates at half the smaller dimension, so past that the field shows a radius nothing draws
detail: FOUND BY THE USER testing on 2026-10-15: "For corner radius. I found that even though it accepts any values, past a certain value it no longer has any visible effects." CAUSE ESTABLISHED AT THE SOURCE, and the user's reading is right. The field writes `rx` through `selection-inspector/panel.ts`'s `panel-radius`, which carries no bounds, and Fabric renders the property CLAMPED: `fabric/src/shapes/Rect.ts:93-94` computes `Math.min(this.rx, w / 2)` and `Math.min(this.ry, h / 2)` at draw time, so the stored value keeps rising while the drawn corner stops moving. THE BOUND IS DERIVED RATHER THAN CONSTANT — half the SMALLER dimension of the object as it is drawn — which is why the descriptor declares none and why a slider cannot simply be given a number. THE DECISION THE FIX NEEDS, and therefore why this is a row rather than a patch: either the write clamps to what the render can show (so the field cannot hold a value nothing draws), or the control is bounded by the object's own half-dimension and re-bounds when the object is resized, or both. The first is one owner and settles it; the second needs the field to read the object's drawn size, which is the same live-rebounded control the min/max sweep in vg-469 would need for this field. IT IS vg-109's SHAPE IN ANOTHER FIELD — a control that believes what it was told rather than what is drawn — so the two should be read together, and vg-469's census names this field's upper bound as the one that is not a constant. OUTCOME, 2026-10-15 (Task 14.1): both halves the row named as the decision landed. The write clamps to what the render can show — the `panel-radius` branch of `selection-inspector/panel.ts`'s `writePanelField` takes `radiusBound(drawnEdge(object))` and stores `min(max(value, 0), ceiling)` on both axes — and the control is bounded by the object's own half-dimension, so it re-bounds when the object is resized: `max` is half the smaller *drawn* edge (`width * scaleX`, `height * scaleY`), read at projection time and never written as a constant. A box that cannot be read clamps to the floor alone rather than to a guessed ceiling. The chart settings' four radius descriptors carry the same bound through `bound: "halfDrawnBox"`.
check: The corner radius is bounded by half the panel's smaller drawn dimension, and the render can always show what the field holds: read by `selection-inspector/panel.dom.test.ts`'s `bounds the corner radius by half the box Fabric draws it in`, a jsdom reading which asserts the track's `max` is `100` for a 360x200 rect, that a draft of 240 is refused with `at most 100` and writes nothing, and that a `writePanelField` call bypassing the control lands `rx` and `ry` on `100` — so the field no longer shows a radius nothing draws. Landed by `51d48065` (the inspector) and `8598fde2` (the chart settings' four radius descriptors, bounded by `bound: "halfDrawnBox"`).

title: The mockup was never replaced where a surface was deliberately rebuilt differently, so the checked reference still draws a design the product does not ship
detail:
FOUND BY THE USER on 2026-10-10, looking at the captures Task 6 had just re-taken: the gap between them and docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html is still large. WHICH GAP IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the new set includes -editorial (flat cream) and shell-palette-light captures, while the mockup is drawn on graphite (#0b0e12 per Task 6's D9), so comparing a light capture to it shows the palette rather than drift, and that has to be ruled out first by naming the files compared. THE USER THEN NAMED THE GAP, on 2026-10-10: "The panels on both sides, rail, top menu bar are all on their separate islands with rounded corners. That's completely different from the mockup. The graphite color scheme is different from the mockup's, too." Both are shell-level - plan 2's chrome and 0035's palette - not plan 6's glyphs or copy. The bible's own §3 makes panels `--radius-lg` (8px) and reserves `--radius-xl` (10px) plus backdrop blur for floating clusters OVER THE CANVAS (dock, view controls, identity chip), while the shipped stylesheet carries four literal `border-radius: 12px`, a value the closed scale (4/6/8/10) does not contain. A read-only measurement of both halves - per region, per palette role - is running as .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-08-settings-and-appearance/mockup-vs-shell-measurement.md, and this row's detail gets the measured values when it lands. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED is the structural cause. docs/design/mockups/README.md's "Keeping them current" section ends: "If a surface is rebuilt differently on purpose, capture the new state and replace the mockup file - the reference is always the current target, never a historical one", and its opening line is "These are the target." Neither parity gate did that. Plan 2's Task 10 adjudicated 22 shell differences and plan 5's Task 6 eleven settings differences, ten of them deliberate (horizontal tab strip where the mockup draws a vertical sidebar; 2-column radio choice rows with one ground+accent chip where the mockup draws a 3x2 grid of two-bar cards; no printed description under the heading; a Close the mockup omits; a Keyboard tab header and Reset placement the mockup predates; the modal painting the palette's glass), and every one was recorded in a commit while the drawing stayed as it was - so the rule the README states was applied as "say why" rather than "replace the file". CONSEQUENCE: the repo's own reference is now a historical target for two surfaces, which the README calls worse than no mockup because it is believed; the shell half carries the same shape in vg-217, vg-219 and vg-230. NOT FIXED HERE: replacing the mockup is design work over the adjudicated lists, it needs a home (plan 6's closing parity capture, or design-md-replaces-the-bible which decides the mockups' standing beside DESIGN.md), and the alternative - pulling the product back to the drawing - would reopen plans 2 and 5 and needs the user's call. What would settle it: name the files compared, then replace the settings section and the shell features the two lists adjudicated, or rule the drawing the target again and schedule the product work. UPDATE 2026-10-10, THE USER'S RULING: the mockup is NOT replaced ("Do not replace the mockup."), so the product-vs-drawing fork this row left open is closed in favour of the product, and what survives here is this row's process half alone — nothing signals that a mockup and the product have drifted, and docs/design/mockups/README.md's "replace the mockup file" rule was applied as "say why" for two surfaces across two plans (plan 2's 22 shell differences, plan 5's eleven settings differences, ten called deliberate). ADJACENT ROW, DIFFERENT DEFECT: vg-292 is the missing comparison itself — no gate anywhere compares a built surface to the mockup, so §13's parity capture could not fail; this row is the stale file, that one is the absent instrument, and the instrument is the cause.

RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D4's ruling on this row: it DISSOLVES INTO vg-292's instrument row -- one row, one plan, owned by Phase 10 (W9). The stale-file record stops being an item of its own.

title: The settings modal's Close button is `--shell-text` on `--yunari-control-bg` where the drawing draws `--muted` on `--panel2`, and no plan-8 task owns it
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 1 (2026-10-11, census row #19, filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `9a6667ac`). MEASURED: the re-adjudication of the closed plan's region #19 - the drawing at `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html` draws the modal's Close control in `--muted` on `--panel2`, and the product renders it in `--shell-text` on `--yunari-control-bg`. The census classifies it `fix` - no predating rule requires the product's treatment - but no task in plan 8's ten touches the control, so it is filed here rather than folded into a task it does not belong to. WHY IT IS NOT IN PLAN 8: the plan's tasks were written from the measurement's own region list, and region #19 moved when the drawing did - the measurement's row read `undefined`, because the superseded `editor-shell.html` drew no Close control at all, and the current set does. So the row is new evidence the plan could not have scheduled, and adding a task for it now would put an unscheduled edit in a plan whose phases are already dispatched. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §4 colour-role correction on the Close control's rule in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css`, with plan 8 Task 1's settings row (or a fifth row) reading `--muted` against `--panel2`, and the §13 capture in Task 10 showing it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the product's treatment is deliberate - the control is a `ControlButton` and `--yunari-control-bg` may be the control set's own resting fill rather than a second declaration of the same value. If it is the control set's, the fix is the control's owner and the blast radius is every surface using it, which is why this is a row and not a one-line change. SECOND INSTANCE - PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11): the Keyboard panel's return-to-default actions render the same fill against the same drawn treatment. The drawing draws `border:1px solid var(--edge);border-radius:6px;background:var(--panel2);color:var(--muted)` on every one of them (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:50`, `:61`, `:70`, `:79`, `:92`, `:101`, `:110`, `:119`, `:128`) while `.editor-shell-keyboard-action` renders `background: var(--yunari-control-bg)` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1586-1594`), so the class is the Close button plus these - and the text colour is NOT part of this instance, because the product's `--shell-muted` is the drawing's `var(--muted)` renamed. Task 7 reported it rather than fixing it, because the fill belongs to the control set's owner and the blast radius is every surface using it, which is what this row already says. The correction belongs to that one owner, not to three edits. PLAN 8 TASK 10 RE-CONFIRMED THIS ROW'S FIRST INSTANCE AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (2026-10-11, commit b78ee264): the Close renders --shell-text on --yunari-control-bg, left-aligned, padding 6px 12px, margin-top 18px (`editor-shell.css:1397-1416`) where `current/settings.html` draws --muted on --panel2, right-aligned, padding 4px 12px, margin-top 16px - and no section names this control's fill or text colour, so it is a fix with no predating licence. Its 18px is also one of the four vg-325 values Task 9's ceiling counts by name, and the left alignment is visible in the committed capture beside the drawing. TASK 2.4b, 2026-10-12: the reading is taken on the built preview at base 7f88dff3, in force palette light. The settings modal's Close renders color rgb(16, 33, 25) (--shell-text) on background rgb(245, 241, 232) (--yunari-control-bg), margin-top 16px, padding 6px 12px; the Keyboard tab's return-to-default actions, 21 of them, render rgb(79, 102, 89) (--shell-muted) on the same fill. The drawing's roles resolve to --shell-muted #4f6659 on --panel-2 #f8fffbdf, so the fill is the divergence and the text colour is not, exactly as this row says. Two citations on this line corrected, and one number: .editor-shell-dialog > button is at editor-shell.css:1502, not :1397-1416; .editor-shell-keyboard-action is at :1694, not :1586-1594; and its margin-top is 16px today, not the 18px this line records — the drawing's own value, so that half of the divergence is already gone. STAYS OPEN, and the one-token fix is deliberately NOT taken: --yunari-control-bg is declared on five rules across six palettes, and design-language.spec.ts:2045-2050 names it as the separation editorial carries in place of its panel rung, so repainting it is a design decision about the control set rather than a fixer's edit. RECORD CORRECTED AND THE OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED, 2026-10-13, measured on the tree at ec1e39e7; no product file changed. (1) THE LAST LINE OF TASK 2.4b IS FALSE OF THIS ROW'S FIRST INSTANCE. 'the fill is the divergence and the text colour is not' holds for the Keyboard instance and not for the Close: the same sentence measures the Close's label at rgb(16, 33, 25) (`--shell-text`) where the drawing draws `--muted`, which resolves to the product's `--shell-muted` #4f6659, and this row's own title says the same. So the Close carries three divergent properties, not one - the fill, the colour, and a padding the rule states as `6px 12px` (`editor-shell.css:1589`) against the drawing's 4px 12px - and a fixer reading that line alone would repaint the fill and leave two. (2) 'NOT ESTABLISHED' IS NOW ESTABLISHED, AND ON THE SIDE THE ROW WARNED ABOUT. `--yunari-control-bg` IS the control set's own resting fill rather than a second declaration of `--panel-2`: seven palette declarations (`editor-shell.css:106`, `:153`, `:204`, `:275`, `:325`, `:355`, `:385`) and five consuming rule-blocks, every one of them in that single file - the panel's asset buttons (`:1317`), the layer rename (`:1332`), the inspector's action block (`:1353`), the dialog's button (`:1587`) and the keyboard action (`:1782`). It is not one of section 4's roles, and its value differs from the named role's in the palette the drawing actually compares: light declares control-bg #f5f1e8 where its `--panel-2` is #f8fffbdf. So the divergence is systemic across the control set rather than a Close-button slip. (3) THE CLOSE PATH THIS ROW STATES ('a section 4 colour-role correction') IS NOT AVAILABLE AS WRITTEN, because DESIGN.md gives a labelled button no fill to correct to. Section 4's role table names `--panel-2` as 'A panel, and a control inside it'; every filled control in section 5's vocabulary is `--panel-2` (Well, Segmented, Choice row); and section 5's list, whose own first line is 'The vocabulary is closed', holds no labelled button - so a button is not a control in the language's own words. The only text about buttons anywhere in DESIGN.md is about the primary one: `button` occurs at `:110` ('the primary button', in the accent rationing), `:150` ('650-700 only for the brand mark and a primary button') and `:203` ('`Publish` is the only filled, accent-coloured button in the editor'), and none of the three defines a secondary button's shape. `:203`'s strict reading - no other button is filled - would make both the drawing's fill and the product's wrong, so the two sides of this difference are not a colour-role disagreement at all. The gap is filed as `vg-441`. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT, REVISED: a decision in DESIGN.md on the secondary button's shape before any edit to the five rule-blocks - section 5 gaining the control, or `:203`'s 'only filled' standing with every labelled button becoming unfilled - with the Close's colour and padding following that decision. NEAR ROWS: `vg-441` (the vocabulary gap that makes this row undecidable), `vg-322` (item 16's other difference, blocked on the parked `vg-330`), `vg-436` (the same width-vs-rule trap in the drawings' own pair). RULED 2026-10-14: NAME THE ROLE. DESIGN.md §4's role table gains the control fill the settings modal's Close uses, so the fill is named by the language rather than licensed by a parity-table entry, and §5's closed vocabulary stops having a hole where labelled buttons are. The product does not change, and the `--yunari-control-bg` citation stops being the one place the fill's legitimacy is written down.

title: The dialog's shared `h3` and read-only `dl` rules resolve no bible role: a group heading is `--text-xs` where §2 gives the eyebrow `--text-2xs`, the row pads 3px where §3's steps have no 3, and §5 rule 2's 74px label column is drawn by neither side
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 8 TASK 4'S REVIEW (2026-10-11, findings F1 and F4, `task-4-review.md`) and NOT carried by its commit - `6ca510ce` has no `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer, so it is materialised from the review instead, which is why the provenance names a finding number rather than a message. THE THREE FACTS, each measured at the line it rests on. ONE, the group heading: `.editor-shell-dialog h3` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1353-1357`) is `font-size: 11px` with `letter-spacing: 0.12em`, while §2 (`docs/design/design-language.md:47`) gives the eyebrow role `--text-2xs` 10px and `:55-57` fixes an eyebrow at `--text-2xs`, `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`, muted, 'always labels a region, never a control' - 11px is `--text-xs`, whose role at `:48` is 'Panel rows, hints, status bar'. Task 4's drawing is right and the product is wrong: `current/settings-keyboard.html:54` draws `font:600 10px/1.2 ...;letter-spacing:.11em`. TWO, the read-only row's inset: `.editor-shell-dialog dl > div` (`editor-shell.css:1368`) is `padding: 3px 0`, and §3's steps (`design-language.md:69`) are `4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32` - there is no 3. The drawing takes 4px (`current/settings-about.html:50`). THREE, §5 rule 2's grid: the rule (`:163-165`) says read-only rows 'share the grid with controls so a section does not jump between shapes' and that 'the grid is a 74px label column and one value cell', while the product's rule is `justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px` with a content-sized label and the drawing copied that shape - so the column is implemented by neither side. WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN EDIT: all three live on two shared element rules, and those rules are rendered by three surfaces across two dialogs - `settings-keyboard.tsx:153-154`, `settings.tsx:146` and `:214`, `shortcut-reference.tsx:39-40` - so a per-surface patch would fix the settings modal and leave the `?` sheet's group headings wrong, which is the defect Task 3 already fixed once at its owner. WHY NO ROW READS ANY OF IT TODAY: the parity table's About and Keyboard rows read the panels' own declared properties and pass, and plan 8 Task 8's widened gate reads the DRAWINGS' literals, not the product's - so the three facts are invisible to every gate in the repo. THE 74px HALF IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION rather than a value: whether §5 rule 2 binds a dialog's read-only `dl`, or whether the shared grid is the control rows' alone, decides whether the About panel's rows must take a column the Appearance panel also uses. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a §2 role on the `h3` rule, a §3 step on the `dl` row's inset, a ruling on the grid question, and a parity row that reads each - with the §13 capture in Task 10 showing the result. RELATED, NOT THE SAME: `vg-317` is the dialog body's UNDECLARED 13px base, `vg-295` (verified) was the class one level up - the dialog's lead - and `vg-302` (verified) is the same 74px column on CONTROL rows, which plan 7 Task 8 landed as `ControlRow`'s `column`/`boxed`/`headed` shapes; this row is the READ-ONLY row's half, which that one did not cover. SECOND MEASUREMENT - PLAN 8 TASK 7 (2026-10-11): the Keyboard panel's group heading is this same shared rule, and the divergence is two properties with one cause. The drawing declares `font:600 10px/1.2 system-ui;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase` (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:54`) and `.editor-shell-dialog h3` renders `font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css:1367-1372`), which is section 2's eyebrow rule (`design-language.md:55-57` - `--text-2xs` at 10px, weight `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`) read one step and one thousandth off. CORRECTED BY TASK 7'S REVIEW (2026-10-11): the first version of this sentence gave the wrong reason - that sharing puts it out of reach, 'the same reasoning that scoped the chord chip'. Those are opposite moves. Scoping the chip fixed the panel WITHOUT touching the sheet, and a `.editor-shell-keyboard h3` scope would fix this panel's eyebrows without touching the sheet either, so sharing is not what puts the value out of reach. The reason is OWNERSHIP: a per-surface patch would fix the settings modal and leave the `?` sheet's group headings off section 2, splitting one concept across two owners, so the fix belongs at the shared rule's owner, which is where this row already puts it. The divergence is live and correctly deferred either way; what was wrong was the reason, because a later reader could have reused it to defer something genuinely in scope. The Keyboard panel alone is off section 2 on twenty eyebrows until the shared rule moves. This is evidence for the row, not a second row. A THIRD INSTANCE, MEASURED BY PLAN 8 TASK 10 AND FILED AS ITS TRAILER IN b78ee264 (2026-10-11): the Appearance drawing's own heading is `font:600 12px/1` sentence case (`current/settings.html:42`) where the Keyboard drawing draws its group headings at `font:600 10px/1.2;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase` (`current/settings-keyboard.html:54` and four siblings), and the product renders both through the shared `.editor-shell-dialog h3` at 11px / .12em uppercase - so the DRAWING side does not hold the treatment section 2 reserves for a section eyebrow either, and the two sides are wrong in opposite directions. The eyebrow rule is `design-language.md:54` (a first pass cited `:56`, which is the middle of the sentence). Task 4 and Task 7 reported the product side identically. READING 2026-10-12 (built from 3451e55e (clean tree), `desktop-chromium` project, editor preview 4174, the portalled `.editor-shell-dialog`): all three facts measure on the built bundle, and the sheet the row predicted they reach is the third surface. ONE - the shared `h3`: the Appearance group heading ("Shell palette") computes to font-size 11px, letter-spacing 1.32px (0.12em), uppercase, weight 400, against §2's eyebrow (--text-2xs, 10px, .11em, weight 600).
