The `?` sheet takes the same two shared rules in the places that were read: all five of its group headings ("File", "Edit", "Canvas", "Publish", "Help") compute to 11px / 1.32px, and of the 20 `dl > div` rows it holds, the one read takes `padding: 3px 0px`. So a per-surface patch leaves the sheet wrong, which is the row's ownership argument measured at those two rules. CITATIONS REFRESHED WITHOUT REWRITING THEM, 2026-10-13. Every `docs/design/design-language.md` line above was measured against the bible, which has since been replaced -- the file no longer exists and its `§N` markers now live in `DESIGN.md` (`AGENTS.md` holds `§N` stable). The current equivalents, verified 2026-10-13: `§2`'s eyebrow role at `DESIGN.md:145`, `§3`'s steps at `:177`, and `§5` rule 2's read-only rows and its 74px grid at `:423` and `:425`. **The historical numbers are left as written rather than repointed**, because a citation records where a rule stood when it was read, and editing it onto a path that did not exist then would assert a reading nobody took -- the same ruling this drain applied to the dated snapshots under `docs/architecture/`. **FACT TWO IS FIXED, 2026-10-13.** `.editor-shell-dialog dl > div`'s `padding: 3px 0` became `4px 0` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css`, and its now-dead entry was removed from `CEILINGS` in `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` in the same change -- the instrument reddens on an exemption that matches nothing, so the value and its licence move together. The drawing already took 4 (`docs/design/mockups/current/settings-about.html:50`) and `§3` has no 3, so this is a substitution rather than a design pass; the parity row that reads this element (`tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:1376`) asserts its `gap`, not its padding, so nothing pinned the old value. Measured after: `npm run design:check` exits **0**, `counted: 0`, `dead: 0`. **FACTS ONE AND THREE REMAIN OPEN, each on a design decision rather than a value.** The group heading's shared `h3` is off `§2` in one direction while the Appearance drawing is off it in the other -- 10px uppercase against 12px sentence case -- so no single shared rule can satisfy both; and `§5` rule 2's 74px column is implemented by neither side. Both were measured on the built bundle in this row's 2026-10-12 reading, and neither is a fixer's edit. FACT ONE'S OTHER SIDE, MEASURED 2026-10-13: the row rests on `settings-keyboard.html` drawing the group heading at `font:600 10px/1.2` with `letter-spacing:.11em` (five of them) and calls the product wrong. **The other settings sheet draws a different heading, so the conflict is between the drawings and not between one drawing and the product.** `settings.html:42` draws the panel's own group heading as `
Shell palette
` -- 12px, sentence case, no tracking, no uppercase -- over the same palette grid this row's sheet would head at 10px. The seven `font-size:11px` declarations in the same file are the palette cards' captions and the system-follow row (`:50`, `:57`, `:64`, `:71`, `:78`, `:85`, `:90`), not headings, so 12px is the sheet's only heading size. **So the choice is a drawing's, not a fixer's**, which is what keeps this fact open: whichever sheet wins decides whether the product's `11px` moves to `--text-2xs` 10px (the keyboard sheet and section 2's eyebrow) or to `--text-sm` 12px sentence case (the settings sheet, which would also drop the uppercase and the tracking the product currently has at `letter-spacing: 0.12em`). Both are single-rule edits and they are different edits. **Also recorded because it narrows the fact-3 question beside it**: no drawing implements section 5 rule 2's 74px label column, which that fact already says, and this measurement adds that the two sheets agree on the read-only row's shape (`padding:4px 0`, `justify-content:space-between;gap:16px`) while disagreeing on the heading above it -- so the grid question and the heading question are independent and neither is settled by the other. WHAT THE NORM SAYS ABOUT FACT ONE, MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND WHY THE QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN TWO DRAWINGS. DESIGN.md section 2 reserves uppercase rather than describing it - 'Uppercase is reserved for **section eyebrows** - Content, Position, Layer, Paint, Spends, and the group headings in the Add pane' - and adds 'Nothing else is uppercase: a chord is printed as the platform prints it, and a menu row is sentence case'. Section 7.3 is the only other place the role is granted: a pane's body, where 'Sections use the section 2 eyebrow'. Every surface named is a shell surface, and no normative source gives a dialog's group heading the eyebrow role. The product renders `.editor-shell-dialog h3` uppercase at 11px with `letter-spacing: 0.12em` and weight 400, which is neither the eyebrow section 2 defines (10px, 600, .11em) nor sentence case - so it resolves no section 2 role whichever way this fact is read. THE CHAIN, STATED SO IT CAN BE ATTACKED AT ONE LINK: if section 2's list is the reservation it says it is, a dialog heading may not be uppercase, `current/settings.html:42`'s 12px / 600 sentence case is the drawn treatment that survives, and `current/settings-keyboard.html:54`'s uppercase heading is the stale side - the same shape as `vg-440`, a drawing losing to the written rule. The fix is then one rule at `.editor-shell-dialog h3`'s owner: `font-size: var(--text-sm)`, weight `600`, tracking and `text-transform` dropped, reaching the settings modal and the `?` sheet together. WHAT SETTLES IT: one sentence confirming that reservation, or a section 2 or section 7 clause granting a dialog's group heading the eyebrow role - in which case the product's 11px / .12em / 400 becomes 10px / 600 / .11em and the keyboard sheet is the right one. Both are one rule; they are different rules, which is why this is a ruling and not a fixer's edit. FACT THREE'S SENTENCE, FOUND 2026-10-13, AND THE READING IT SUPPORTS. Section 5 rule 2 does not stop at the 74px column; it ends with an escape: 'A row a surface's own drawing shapes differently - a switch row whose label fills the row inside a panel box, a control spanning the row under its own heading - is not a field row and keeps the shape it is drawn with.' Both settings sheets draw the read-only row as `justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px`, which this row's own 2026-10-13 measurement confirms, so if that clause reaches this row then it is not a field row, the 74px column does not bind it, the product's copy of the drawing is right, and fact three is not a defect at all - it is a rule whose own escape clause covers the case. THE COUNTER-READING, STATED SO IT IS NOT HIDDEN: the clause's two examples are shapes a drawing invents, a switch row inside a panel box and a control spanning the row under its own heading, where this is a label-and-value row that a drawing aligns differently, and rule 2's grid is plausibly exactly what a read-only row is for. Which one is meant is a sentence from the same owner fact one waits on, and the two facts are independent: confirming the escape clause does not decide the heading, and confirming section 2's reservation does not decide the grid. RULED 2026-10-14, THE ROW'S THIRD FACT: THE RULE GOVERNS. §5 rule 2's 74px label column is what a read-only row is for, so the two sheets' 16px gap is a mismatch rather than a rule whose escape clause covers its own case, and the product is pulled to the rule — the gap becomes the column. The escape clause keeps its two examples and its shape: a switch row inside a panel box and a control spanning the row under its own heading are shapes a drawing invents, and a label-and-value row is not one of them. The row's other two facts are untouched and stay as its own text states them: the heading's case is decided by §2's reservation, and whether rule 2's grid is drawn by both sides is what this ruling settles. RULED 2026-10-14: **ALL THREE FACTS ARE SETTLED, and each by a source rather than by preference.** Fact two needed no ruling — `padding: 3px 0` was not one of §3's steps, the drawing already took 4, and nothing pinned the old value, so it was a substitution and landed at `69e6e7f1`. **Fact one: the reservation governs.** §2 does not describe uppercase, it *reserves* it for the shell surfaces it names, and §7.3 grants it once more to a pane's body; a dialog's group heading is neither, so the product's uppercase / 11px / 0.12em / 400 `h3` resolved no §2 role under either reading — the settings sheet's sentence case survives and the keyboard sheet's heading is the stale side. **Fact three: the rule governs.** §5 rule 2's grid is a 74px label column and one value cell, and its escape clause reaches a row a *surface's drawing* shapes differently; a read-only label-and-value row is not one of those shapes, so the product is pulled to the rule and the gap becomes the column. Both landed at `9827f0f7`.

title: DESIGN.md closes section 5's control vocabulary with no labelled button in it, while sections 2, 4 and 7.1 name 'the primary button' and three product owners render labelled buttons, so a control the editor uses in three places has no shape in the language
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13, reading DESIGN.md against the tree while answering `vg-316`, and it is that row's cause rather than its content. **MEASURED.** Section 5 opens its vocabulary table with 'The vocabulary is closed. A control is one of these, or it is not a control.' (`DESIGN.md:403`) and lists nine: Well, Well with chevron, Well with unit, Slider + well, Swatch well, Toggle, Segmented, Icon button, Choice row. No entry is a labelled button. Every filled entry in that list is `--panel-2`-filled (Well, Segmented, Choice row), and the only action entry, Icon button, is 'glyph only' with no resting border (rule 6). **THE WORD `button` OCCURS IN DESIGN.md THREE TIMES AND ALWAYS AS THE PRIMARY ONE.** `:110` in section 4's rationing ('the selected rail slot, the focused control, the selected row, the primary button'); `:150` in section 2's weights ('650-700 only for the brand mark and a primary button'); `:203` in section 7.1 ('Right: the publish chord, then the primary button. `Publish` is the only filled, accent-coloured button in the editor.'). No line in the file states a secondary or labelled button's fill, border, radius, padding or text colour. **THE PRODUCT RENDERS LABELLED BUTTONS IN THREE OWNERS.** `ACTION_BUTTON`, which three dialogs' `.yunari-dialog-actions` wrap; `.editor-shell-dialog > button` (`editor-shell.css:1587`), which reaches the settings modal's Close and the `?` sheet's; and `.editor-shell-keyboard-action` (`:1782`), 21 of them on the keyboard tab. Every button those owners render therefore carries a shape the design language does not define, and `vg-316`'s difference is the visible consequence: the acceptance instrument and the product resolved the gap differently, and neither resolution can be called wrong by a cited rule. **WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-SENTENCE EDIT.** `:203`'s 'the only filled, accent-coloured button in the editor' reads two ways - co-ordinately (no other button is both filled and accent-coloured, which permits the product's control-bg fill) or restrictively (no other button is filled, which forbids it and forbids the drawing's `--panel-2` fill too). The two readings disagree about every labelled button in the editor, and section 5's 'closed' claim is only true under the second. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT.** A ruling on which reading holds, then either a section 5 entry for the secondary button stating its fill, border, radius, padding and text colour, or the correction of every filled labelled button in the product and in the drawings to the unfilled treatment. **OWNER.** DESIGN.md is the redesign's target document, so this is the design language's owner. NEAR ROWS: `vg-316` (the difference this gap makes undecidable), `vg-440` (the drawings' own stale half), `vg-402` (the frames nothing re-shoots).

Landed at `dedf2d77`: the vocabulary table gained the Labelled button row after Icon button, its fill is the control role section 4 now names, and its resting shape is read from the two owners that render one — `.editor-shell-dialog > button` and `ACTION_BUTTON`. The two owners disagree in three properties; that disagreement is filed rather than reconciled, which is the ruling's own scope. `npm run design:check` exits 0 at `8c4c79b9`.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong. RULED 2026-10-14: BROWSER STORAGE, AND THE BLOCK IS LIFTED. The draft holds authored theme JSON rather than asset bytes, so the asset-ownership question does not move it — whether the host owns asset bytes is a question about assets, and a draft of the authored document is not one of them. The rest of the row's ruling stands unchanged: write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page, recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost, and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need.
check: The draft, its writes and the recovery prompt, at the three commits that landed them. `draft-store.ts` holds the `yunari.editor.draft` slot, writes a dirty document on a ~30 s timer and again on `pagehide`, and clears it when the document becomes clean; `draft-recovery-prompt.tsx` offers restore or discard, discard drawn last, naming the theme and the time it was written; and `editor-main.ts` offers it at boot, before anything opens. `draft-store.test.ts` pins the store's read, write and clear, the timer's write, the dirty gate, the transition rule and the recovery answers. The browser reading at `87d5b30d` walked the real path in Chromium: a draft recovered, a draft the build refused surviving the fallback mount, and an edit undone to clean clearing the draft. `npm run gate` exits 0 (256 files, 3422 tests).

title: Importing a file silently does one of two different things, and only the file type decides which
detail: FOUND BY AN AGENT READING THE CODE, NOT BY THE USER, and corrected on 2026-10-07: this row was first filed attributing it to the user testing report, and that attribution was wrong — the user imported JPEG images only and their report is vg-156. This row stands on its own reading. asset-manager/index.ts:21-31 defines four asset kinds — image (png/jpg/jpeg/webp), svg, video (mp4/webm), font (woff2/woff/ttf/otf) — and isPlaceable at asset-manager/panel.ts:232-236 is the two-element allowlist image or svg. add() at panel.ts:114-183 imports, tests isPlaceable, and only then places via manager.placeImage at :211. So importing a PNG is declared and placed, dropping a new object on the canvas, while importing an MP4 or a font is declared only: the canvas is untouched, no layer appears, and nothing in the pane distinguishes the two outcomes. Whether that is a defect at all is arguable, because a font is not supposed to be a layer, and the honest part of the finding is only that the two outcomes are indistinguishable to the author. It shares a fix site with vg-154 but is not the user report and should be judged on its own or withdrawn. RULED 2026-10-14: MAKE IT SAY WHICH. The two outcomes stay different — a font or a video cannot be placed on a canvas, so declaring it is right — but the pane distinguishes them: an import that declares only says so, and the canvas is visibly untouched rather than the difference being invisible in what the pane shows. The row closes when the pane reports what each import did, which is a rendering of the existing distinction rather than a change to which types are placeable. PATH CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (§8.11). Two of the paths above moved when the Add pane absorbed the file section: `c8dc0b1a` deleted `asset-manager/panel.ts` and its test, and `isPlaceable` with the import-then-place step now sit in `panes/add/file-section.tsx`, while `manager.placeImage` is `AssetManager.placeImage` in `asset-manager/index.ts`. The line numbers are dropped rather than re-pointed, for the reason recorded on `vg-301`. What the row measured is unchanged: the allowlist is still `image` or `svg`, now spelled as `isPlaceable`'s narrowed return of `PlacedAssetReference`, and `asset-manager/index.ts`'s `TYPES` still holds the four kinds, so that path needed no correction. The row's own `check` already named the moved files by their current paths, which is why this drift survived the gate: the checker validates `artefacts` against git and never tests whether a `check`'s path exists.
check: The Add pane's one message now reports which of the two outcomes an importing took. `file-section.tsx`'s `importFile` sets `assetPlaced` when `isPlaceable(asset)` placed the file, and the kind's own string when it did not, through an exhaustive switch on `asset.kind` with no `default`, so a fifth kind is a type error rather than a silent fall through. `file-section.dom.test.tsx` asserts the video case's alert text and that `placeImage` was not called, and the image case's alert text and that it was. Which kinds are placeable did not change, which is the ruling's own scope. Landed at `453b9553`.

title: The hover label waits 600 ms, which the author reads as the app being slow
detail: PART OF THE USER'S 2026-10-13 SLUGGISHNESS REPORT — "icons that supposed to appear on hover takes half a second or so to appear" — AND MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: it is a constant, not a stall. `editor-shell/controls/tooltip.ts` declares `HOVER_DELAY_MS = 600`, and the comment beside it gives the reason ("a delay is what stops a pointer crossing the dock from flashing every label"). THE EDITOR AT REST IS OTHERWISE CLEAN, which is what makes this the whole explanation: on the built bundle, 2,783 animation frames with exactly one over 40 ms, and four long tasks totalling 374 ms, every one of them during load. Nothing is making the label late; the label is scheduled that late. THE QUESTION IS THE VALUE AND NOT THE MECHANISM: 600 ms is longer than the settling delay of the platform tooltips this shell imitates, and it is applied to icon-only controls whose label is the only name they carry — the case where the delay costs the most and buys the least, because there is no other word on screen to read instead. Whether a shorter delay reintroduces the flashing the comment is about is a measurement, not an opinion: the dock is a row of adjacent controls, so the crossing it protects against is short and its cost is a per-control hover timer. OWNER: the tooltip's own constant, and the design language if section 7 ever fixes a value for it. SEVERITY: low, and it is felt latency rather than a defect — reversing it is one number. RULED 2026-10-14: SHORTEN IT, AND LET THE MEASUREMENT SET THE NUMBER rather than choosing one. The dock is a row of adjacent controls, so the crossing the delay protects against is short and its cost is a per-control hover timer; the row's own question — whether a shorter delay reintroduces the flashing the current comment is about — is a measurement, so the row closes on a measured delay and an assertion that pins it, not on a number picked here. MEASURED 2026-10-15, IN TWO INDEPENDENT HARNESSES: the dock's 296px row of ten 26px controls was crossed at 0.39s, 0.83s, 1.23s and 1.62s, and the maximum dwell on any one control was 195.2ms at the slowest of those against 120.4ms at the fastest. A pointer arriving to read comes to rest in about 110ms, and the shortest deliberate hold driven was 400ms — at which the old 600ms showed no label at all. The scoped re-review re-took the reading and got 148.5ms and 139.4ms at the same traversal times, a step-granularity difference in the safe direction, and its own boundary drag at a 244.4ms dwell opened five labels — so the zero is a measurement and not a harness that cannot open one. HOVER_DELAY_MS is 220ms: above the floor both harnesses measured, clear of the 6.4ms run-to-run spread that 200ms would sit inside, and far below the 400ms ceiling. Below roughly 150px/s the suppression fails, because a 311ms dwell on a 26px control is indistinguishable from intent to read, so the constant's comment names the traversal range it holds for rather than a bare maximum.
check: The hover label's wait is measured rather than chosen: `HOVER_DELAY_MS` is 220 ms, above the 195.2 ms the dock's slowest traversal measured and well below the 400 ms a deliberate hover holds, where the old 600 ms showed no label at all. Two independent browser readings drove the slow crossings first and found no label opening on any of them, while a settled hover showed one 262.6 ms after entry and each harness also opened labels on a boundary drag — so the zero is a measurement rather than a harness that cannot open one. `tooltip.dom.test.ts` pins 220 as literals (219 then 1), so a moved constant fails it in both directions. Landed at `19c79c3a`, `d820fb4a` and `5b05b9f3`.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: RULING STANDS: a slight per-shape difference is acceptable rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. CHARACTERISED, NOT FIXED, and the lead I gave the investigator was wrong. I offered "the Circle region measured 127,449 px against the Rect 156,009 for the same box" as proof the region was shape-dependent. It is not: that sweep gave every shape the same AUTHORING box, and a Circle has no 240x160. Both numbers reconstruct exactly at the sweep pad — 437x357 = 156,009 and 357x357 = 127,449, predicted ratio 0.8165 against 0.81691 measured. At one 260x260 box all five shapes take a byte-identical 362x362 region (131,044 px). PARTIAL COVERAGE REFUTED: no collapse at the rim, and the bin touching the boundary is the largest bin in three of four measurements. MATERIAL PARITY IS BIT-IDENTICAL: mean luma 94.75/94.75 over stripes and 93.41/93.41 over a photograph, distinct colours 40/40 and 10/10, and the frost boxes are pixel-identical at thresholds 2, 1.5 and 1. WHAT DIFFERS IS FOOTPRINT: a Circle covers 78.54% of its box, 21.5% less frosted area — which reads LIGHTER, not stronger, so it is the wrong direction to explain the report. STILL OPEN, and the leading hypothesis is not the renderer: a Circle authored size is a RADIUS and a Rect authored size is a WIDTH, so the same number gives a disc twice the area. Checked and not yet confirmed in the scene where it was seen. glass.ts is byte-identical to the base sha; nothing was simulated away, per the ruling. THE AUTHORS PATH TO THIS COMPARISON IS REACHABLE AFTER ALL, and I said otherwise earlier and was wrong twice about it. First: I claimed the Glass blur control does not exist on a chart. It does not exist on a chart because a chart cannot be frosted — the control appears once there is a radius to tune, and I compared an object that was refused against one that already had frost on. Second: I then said the report could not have come from the editor because the line charts control cannot be changed. True, and beside the point: the report is about a CIRCLE and a RECT, and both are perfectly authorable. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY SHAPE, which is also the ruling ADR-0015 predicts: Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon all offer an ENABLED Frosted glass control; Polyline and Line are aria-disabled, correctly, having no closed area to frost. And the two shapes the report names get the SAME DEFAULT: a fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both become yunariGlass at blurRadius 16 the moment frost is switched on, with the blur control appearing alongside it. So the situation the report describes — a Circle and a Rect at the same value — is exactly what the product produces by default, and the row stands on its own merits again. What remains is what the earlier characterisation established and this does not change: over the area they share the frost is bit-identical, and what differs is footprint, a Circle covering 78.54 percent of its box. If a Circle reads stronger, the leading hypothesis is still the authors own — a Circle size is a RADIUS where a Rectangle size is a WIDTH — and it is still unconfirmed in the scene where it was seen. RULED 2026-10-14: MEASURE FIRST. Drive the real scene, read the frost over a Circle and a Rect at the same value, and let the number answer whether an area-equalisation is wanted — the row is not decided on the hypothesis (a Circle's size is a RADIUS where a Rect's is a WIDTH, so a Circle covers 78.54 percent of its box; over the area they share the frost is bit-identical). The effect is unconfirmed in the scene where it was seen, which is why the measurement is the ruling rather than a lead-in to one. MEASURED 2026-10-15 IN THE RUNNING EDITOR, IN TWO INDEPENDENT HARNESSES: the product's default pair — Rectangle 360x200 and Ellipse rx = ry = 180 as the Add pane makes them, no position and no size edit, Frosted glass on and Glass blur 24 on each — gives the Rect 12,650 frosted px against the Circle's 18,311, a ratio of 1.4475 (scene units 72,000 against 101,787.6 = 1.4137). So in the report's own case the circle is the LARGER object and the author's 'stronger' was MORE OF IT. The material parity is a proof by construction rather than a measurement: composite() in scene-fabric/src/glass.ts blurs the same source at the same radius and clips, so over an interior point the clip is a mask that is 'on' for both — confirmed as max |rect - circle| = 0 over all 4,480 disc pixels, not merely four equal means. The first round's same-box experiment was rejected because parity there was forced AND its extent sign was the opposite of the report's; the second round's sensitivity control was corrected because it varies the AMOUNT of glass rather than the treatment, and the disc mean responds to blur 8 against blur 24 by only 0.18 luma. ANSWER: no area-equalisation is wanted; editor/src/selection-inspector/glass.ts is untouched. The rendered side-by-side reading is method-dependent at the box rim by 462 px (13,228 against 12,766), cause not established, filed as vg-516.
check: Measured in the running editor rather than argued. The product's own default pair — a Rectangle 360x200 and an Ellipse rx = ry = 180 as the Add pane makes them, no position or size edit, the same Glass blur 24 on each — gives the Circle 18,311 frosted px against the Rect's 12,650, a ratio of 1.4475, so in the report's own case the circle is the LARGER object and the frost the author read as a stronger treatment was more of it. The parity is a proof by construction from composite() in scene-fabric/src/glass.ts, where the frost is a function of source, blur radius and tint — all three identical for both shapes — so a shape can only change how much frost there is, confirmed as max |rect - circle| = 0 over all 4,480 disc pixels rather than equal means alone. An independent scoped re-review reproduced every default-pair number to full precision. Answer: no area-equalisation; editor/src/selection-inspector/glass.ts is untouched. Landed at `cc1ea2d0` and `679b7110`.

title: A rejection arriving after the scene mounted calls showLoadFailure, which replaces the whole document and discards a display that was already drawn
detail: FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 8 TASK 1.3 at 66ee3414. THE STRUCTURE, read rather than guessed: `main.ts:104` is a `catch` around all of `await startHostedTheme(...)`, and that function mounts the scene at `main.ts:301` via `mountFabricScene({ host, ... })` and then keeps running the refresh cadence and the transport wiring. So a rejection raised anywhere in the display lifecycle after that mount reaches `showLoadFailure`, which now calls `document.body.replaceChildren(...)`. NOT A REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY 1.3, and this is the part worth reading twice: the previous form was `host.replaceChildren(view)` with `host` the artboard host, and the mounted canvas lives INSIDE that host, so the canvas was discarded either way. What 1.3 changed is the blast radius, not the loss -- the chrome bands now go with it. THE OPEN QUESTION is therefore older than plan 8: whether a failure arriving after a display is already drawn should replace the screen at all, or should leave the working display alone and say something smaller beside it, given that a theme whose font failed to load after mount is arguably still a theme worth showing. THE PLAN'S OWN PREMISE WAS FALSE and is corrected in place: it asserted that this runs before any scene is mounted so there is no canvas to lose, which is true of `main.ts:89` (reached when `requested === null`, before anything) and false of `main.ts:104`. The landed comment states the behaviour without claiming an intent for it. NOT REPRODUCED: the call structure is established, but no test raises a post-mount rejection, so which of `loadFontAssets` (`:316`), `reviveThemeEnvelope` (`:324`) or the direct `refresh()` (`:359`) can actually reject is unmeasured -- the reading shows the path exists, not that anything walks it. Filed rather than fixed because the answer is a design decision about what a wall display should do when it breaks late, and because the behaviour predates plan 8, which merely widened it. RULED 2026-10-14: REPLACE IT. The failure document replaces the scene as it does today — a display that says it is broken beats one showing stale art — so the behaviour is intended rather than a defect, and the landed comment's correction stands: the intent is recorded here instead of being inferred from the call structure. What keeps the row open is its own measurement debt and nothing else: no test raises a post-mount rejection, so which of `loadFontAssets`, `reviveThemeEnvelope` or the direct `refresh()` can actually reject is still unmeasured, and the row closes when a case pins the replace-on-late-rejection path. MEASURED 2026-10-15, AND THE DEBT IS DISCHARGED: of the three calls startHostedTheme makes after mountFabricScene, exactly ONE can reject. loadFontAssets CANNOT — font-assets.ts routes every failure shape (no FontFace API, missing bytes, missing metadata, a face that will not load) to options.onError and carries on, which main.ts's own comment records as deliberate. refresh CANNOT — it is (): void and synchronous, so there is no promise to reject. reviveThemeEnvelope CAN, and is the only one: it is awaited after the mount, and persist.ts opens with assertFabricThemeEnvelopeCompatible(envelope) BEFORE its first await, so an incompatible envelope throws inside an async function and the catch around the display's whole lifetime turns it into showLoadFailure. AND THE PATH IS WALKABLE RATHER THAN MERELY PRESENT, which is what the row's own concession asked for: fabric-envelope-validate.ts pins only the SHAPE of fabricVersion and never compares it to the running runtime, so an envelope the loader serves, validates and accepts is still refused at the mount. The case is packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts, main.ts's first test: it serves fabricVersion 0.0.1, mocks NO module (only window.fetch and EventSource, so assertFabricThemeEnvelopeCompatible is the real one refusing a real envelope), and asserts REPLACEMENT rather than presence — the artboard host disconnected and both chrome bands gone — which is the distinction the ruling drew, since a case asserting only that the failure view exists would pass for the notice-beside-the-display shape the ruling rejected. Shown load-bearing by three deliberate breaks, all restored byte-identically with cmp: hoisting the refusal above the mount fails the post-mount assertion, dropping showLoadFailure from the catch fails the wait, and APPENDING the view instead of replacing the body fails host.isConnected — with the parentElement assertion passing under that last break, which is why the host and the bands are what carry the claim.
check: Pinned by a case that drives the real main.ts through a post-mount rejection. A theme envelope the loader accepts — fabric-envelope-validate.ts pins only the shape of fabricVersion and never compares it to the runtime — is refused at the mount by assertFabricThemeEnvelopeCompatible in scene-fabric/src/persist.ts, which main.ts awaits AFTER mountFabricScene, so the rejection reaches showLoadFailure with the display already drawn and the whole document is replaced. reviveThemeEnvelope is the only one of the three post-mount calls that can reject: loadFontAssets routes every failure to onError and carries on, and refresh is synchronous with no promise to reject. The case is packages/player/src/main.dom.test.ts, it mocks no module at all (only fetch and EventSource), and it asserts replacement rather than presence — the host disconnected and both chrome bands gone — which is the distinction the 2026-10-14 ruling drew. Shown load-bearing: appending the view instead of replacing the body fails host.isConnected. Landed at `e08677f3` and `eb59248b`.

title: An attended layer row whose reserved strip is wider than its own columns can spare runs the role under the state slot, which paints over it
detail: FOUND BY FIXING `vg-265` ON 2026-10-13, MEASURED ON A BUILT BUNDLE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT FIX DOES NOT REACH. `vg-265` was the slot painting its surface whether or not it held a control, so every row at rest lost the role's last glyphs to a six-pixel block that drew nothing; that half is fixed — the surface and the 6px lead-in now belong to the slot's buttons (`.yunari-layer-state:has(button)`), and `composition-panel.spec.ts`'s 'the state slot does not cover the role' reads every row at rest, role against slot, and passes. THE HALF THAT REMAINS: once the slot holds real controls the reservation is real too, and on a row where the reserved strip is wider than what the row's columns can spare, the in-flow line overflows to the right and the role ends up under the slot. MEASURED AGAIN 2026-10-15 at 1280×720 and 1600×900, desktop-chromium, the starter document, and the row's own figures do not reproduce. The four-control case is gone: `vg-462` removed the layer row's rename pen, so `composition-pane.tsx` renders at most three buttons inside `.yunari-layer-state` and `nth-child(4)` → `padding-right: 126px` is unreachable — 126px reserved on 0 rows, 96px on 8, 66px on 52. The worst attended row is not the chart row this reading named but `group-trends-card`, whose role is the group's own unit stamp (`Performance trends`, 94.9px, `flex: none`), and it left 87.2px of the role under the slot, with 29 of the starter's 60 rows painted over. WHY THE FIX IS NOT A FIX: the row's three columns are each recorded as never giving way — the mark is `flex: 0 0 28px`, the name is `flex: 1 1 auto` with a `min-width: 6ch` floor, and the role is `flex: none` with the stylesheet's own sentence 'it is never the element that gives up width: a role that clipped or ellipsised would say nothing' — so at 246px a four-control row (122px of controls on a 218px row) has no column left that may yield, and which one does is a design decision rather than a bug fix. The candidates, none of them free: lower the name's 6ch floor when the slot needs the room (the name ellipsises instead of the role being covered, and the panel's own record already measures name clipping as its cost); let the role clip in this one case (contradicting the sentence above, though a clipped role says more than a painted-over one); or move the role out of the slot's path (a layout change, since the role reads between the name and the key). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on which column yields, the same `:has` arms re-derived from it, and this file's case extended from the at-rest sweep to the attended one — the assertion is already written in the case's comment and was removed from the test because it would have asserted a defect as a pass condition. NEAR ROWS: `vg-265` (the half this came out of, closed the same day), `vg-260` (the same row width, measured from the key column's side), `vg-301`. RULED 2026-10-14: THE NAME YIELDS. The name's `6ch` floor lowers when the state slot needs the room, so a name ellipsises rather than the role being painted over. The trade is the panel's own measured cost — name clipping, which its record already prices — against a role that says nothing at all when it is covered, and the stylesheet's sentence that the role "is never the element that gives up width" stays true as written. The case extends from the at-rest sweep to the attended row, which is the assertion the case's own comment already states and the test kept out because it would have asserted a defect as a pass condition. RULED 2026-10-15: THE ROLE YIELDS LAST, AND IT CLIPS RATHER THAN BEING COVERED. The name-yields lever is necessary but not sufficient: with the name at zero, `group-trends-card`'s own columns — twisty 20 + mark 28 + role 94.9 + three 4px gaps = 154.9px — still exceed the 109px a 211px row leaves after its 6px lead-in and the 96px strip, so no column §7.3 permits can pay the residual 43.9px. §7.3 enumerates its forbidden outcomes in priority order — never drop a control, never take the mark slot below 28px, never paint over the role — and the first two are satisfiable while the third is not, so the row clips the role, which is what §7.3 already accepts for the name and the key: a role that ellipsises still says what it can, where a role under the slot says nothing at all. `DESIGN.md` §7.3 was amended by the same ruling to state the precedence order rather than the absolute, and its stale control list (`twisty, rename, eye, lock`) was corrected in the same paragraph. THE ORDERING IS THE SUBSTANCE: a plain `flex: 0 1 auto` on the role shrinks it proportionally with the name, because flexbox weights shrink by `flex-shrink × base size` and both bases are about 94.9px, so the name and the key absorb the shrink first and only the residue reaches the role. MEASURED AFTER: worst attended coverage −2.0px, rows painted over 0 of 60, and at rest all 60 rows unchanged at −2.0px, so `vg-265`'s at-rest sweep and `vg-260`'s 28px mark are both untouched; on `group-trends-card` the name box is 0px and the role 49px, clipping at the content edge 173 against the slot at 175. WHAT CLOSED IT: `composition-panel.spec.ts`'s case now hovers every row in turn and re-applies its own `overlaps()` predicate, asserting the invariant per row rather than at rest only — the assertion the case's own comment had kept out because it would have asserted a defect as a pass condition — plus an ordering assertion that reddens when the name and the key do not absorb the shrink first. **CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (`e9d5e670`, `vg-492`): the sentence reading *so at 246px a four-control row (122px of controls on a 218px row) has no column left that may yield, and which one does is a design decision rather than a bug fix* describes a shape the product no longer draws.** `vg-462` removed the layer row's rename pen at `e572c302`, so the slot holds at most three buttons and the reserve is at most 96px — this row's own 2026-10-15 reading already records that (126px on 0 rows, 96px on 8, 66px on 52), and `vg-492` deleted the fourth arm that would have matched 126px. The yield-order question the sentence states is unchanged and still this row's.
check: Pinned by a case that attends every row in the layer list and reads each role's box against the state slot's. The attended row's name yields — `.yunari-layer-name`'s `min-width: 6ch` floor drops to 0 under `:has(.yunari-layer-state button)`, so no row at rest moves — and where the name and the key have nothing left the role yields last and clips with an ellipsis rather than running under the slot, which is DESIGN.md §7.3's precedence order as the same ruling amended it. Worst attended coverage went 87.2px → 43.9px → −2.0px and rows painted over 29 → 1 → 0 of the starter's 60, with all 60 unchanged at rest. Shown load-bearing by two breaks: deleting the scoped block reddens the invariant on `group-network-card` (`overlap: 33.7`), and reverting only the name's and the key's `flex-shrink` leaves the invariant green while the ordering assertion reddens — which is what makes the yield order load-bearing on its own. Landed at `dec7e087`, `cde05033` and `f015f061`.

title: The layer list cannot select more than one row, and grouping needs a multi-selection
detail:
The row click is onClick={() => selectLayer(row.id)} and ignores the event, so a shift-click on a second row replaces the first instead of adding to it. MEASURED: shift-clicking strapline after wordmark left only strapline selected, while the same two objects shift-clicked on the canvas select both. Grouping is reachable — the context menu offers Group once the selection is eligible — but only from a canvas multi-selection, so an author working in the layer list cannot make one. Needs a decision rather than a patch: whether a shift-click toggles a row the way the canvas does, whether shift extends a range like a file list, or whether the panel stays single-select and grouping moves somewhere reachable from it. An additive select also has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which has one selectLayer(id) today.

 CROSS-LINK, deliberately NOT withdrawn: the defect is in a layer panel the redesign replaces, but the requirement behind it - that a list can select more than one row, because arrange is gated on a multi-selection - has to survive into the composition panel or arrange becomes unreachable there. §172 does not state multi-select explicitly, so closing this row would silently drop the requirement. RULED 2026-10-14: SHIFT EXTENDS A RANGE AND CTRL TOGGLES — both idioms rather than one of the three the row listed. Shift-click takes the range from the anchor to the row clicked, ctrl (cmd on a Mac) adds or removes a single row, and a plain click replaces the selection as it does today. The additive select has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which carries one `selectLayer(id)` today, and the requirement survives into the composition panel — closing this row without it would silently drop the requirement arrange is gated on.
check: Pinned by `tests/e2e/composition-panel.spec.ts`'s case, which drives a real shift-click and a real ctrl-click on the layer list's rows with Playwright's own modifiers and reads every claim back from the canvas's own active objects, so a panel that merely painted two rows cannot pass. Shift extends a range from the anchor over the panel's flat row list in render order, ctrl adds and removes one row, removing the last clears the canvas rather than only the panel, and a plain click still replaces. The row's `CROSS-LINK` — the half its own text says would be dropped silently — is discharged through the product's own predicate rather than a restatement of it: a multi-selection made in the layer list makes `canArrange` true and draws the selection inspector's arrange row, and that row is absent again for a single selection, so the assertion is the multi-selection and not a panel that always draws it. Both red proofs reproduce. Disabling the additive path reddens the range assertion with only the last-clicked row selected, which is the shape the row measured. Removing the Space branch's anchor line brings the keyboard range back eight rows instead of five while the Space select itself still passes, which is what makes that check specific to the anchor rather than to selection in general. The bridge gained a gesture-neutral `selectLayers` taking which ids and nothing about why, with `selectLayer` delegating to it in one line, so the group-resolution rule exists once and no range or toggle semantics cross the Fabric-free boundary. Landed at `26b9be94`; `npm run gate` 0 (257 files, 3423 tests) and the spec 12 passed under `desktop-chromium`.

title: The status bar renders no object or selection counts, though the bible, the spec and Task 4's own outcome all put counts on the left
detail: FOUND BY plan 2 Task 10 (the parity capture's difference list, row 22), REPORTED to the controller rather than filed because Task 10 files no row, and VERIFIED BY THE CONTROLLER against the code before filing, because it is a claim about what the product does not do. Bible section 7.6 is normative and explicit: the status bar is '26px, mono, --faint, readouts only: object and selection counts on the left, save state and the live indicator on the right.' The spec's section 3.4 repeats it ('readouts only: counts, save state, live indicator'), bible section 7's own diagram prints `status bar   counts ... saved - live`, and plan 2's Task 4 made it its first Outcome line - 'a 26px full-width strip, mono, carrying counts on the left' - and named `hosts.status` as 'the span `editor-main` writes counts and messages into'. THE PRODUCT RENDERS NO COUNT. The footer is `<footer id="status">` (shell-layout.tsx:783) holding the status host span, DiagnosticMessage, SaveState and PublishIndicator, and EVERY write into that span is a message: editor-main.ts:115, :123, :185, :245, :256, :271, :274, :277, :343, :355, :357, :391 and :400 - thirteen of them, ending at 'Fabric editor ready'. `git log --oneline -S 'objects selected' --all` returns no code commit at all, only a docs/plans commit and Task 10's own difference table. So the span has never carried a count; the capture shows the left reading as 'Fabric editor ready' and the mockup shows '52 objects   0 selected'. THE SELECTION HALF IS ALREADY COMPUTED AND UNUSED AS A READING: EditorShellSnapshot.selectedCount is real (bridge.ts:29, computed at :159 as 1 or the ActiveSelection's length), and its production consumers are the dock's arrange eligibility via memberCount (bridge.ts:179) and an effect dependency at shell-layout.tsx:407 - and neither renders it as a reading. The object count is not in the snapshot at all, so the fix is not purely presentational. A CONTROLLER ERROR IS PART OF THIS ROW, recorded because it is why the gap survived review: in Task 4's fix round I ruled that `hosts.status` was 'the counts span' - a description inherited from the brief and repeated without checking - and it is not; the comment that ruling corrected was still right for the reason it gave, but the description under it was false, and five rounds of review plus the whole-branch pass never looked at whether anything wrote counts into it. OWNER: whoever owns the status bar next (plan 2 closes with this row; the strip itself is plan 2's surface). It needs a design decision first: what the object count reads, where it comes from (the bridge exposes selection but not the scene's object total), and whether the diagnostic keeps the same span or yields to the counts. SEVERITY: medium - the bible's only stated content for the left half of the status bar is missing, and Task 4's review passed a strip whose mandated content does not exist. CORRECTED 2026-10-09 by plan 2's final whole-branch review, which found this row's consumer claim incomplete: shell-layout.tsx:407 also lists selection.selectedCount as an effect dependency. The conclusion is unchanged - nothing renders the count. RULED 2026-10-14: §7.6 WINS AND THE DRAWING IS THE STALE HALF. `current/shell.html` draws the message on the left and `docs/design/mockups/README.md` already says which way that resolves — "where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins and the file is stale: correct it in the same commit" — so a counts readout joins the message span on the left, the bridge's snapshot gains the scene's object total (selection is already there as `selectedCount`), and the drawing is corrected in the commit that adds it. The cost is named where it lands rather than discovered: `#status`'s own text is what ~20 specs assert with `toHaveText`, so each of them moves to the message child it actually owns — a second readout in the footer is not a text drift they may be edited around. The design question this row said it needed first is answered by the reading: counts are the left's resting content and a message takes the left when it has one to say, which is what "readouts only" means. CLOSED 2026-10-15, VERIFIED. The counts render on the left of the status strip and the message joins them rather than replacing them. `check`: `npx playwright test editor-rail.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1 --grep "the status bar reads the scene's counts"` -> **1 passed, exit 0**, run by the controller at `1317e07f` after `npm run build` and `npm run build:fixture`; the case is `editor-rail.spec.ts`'s "the status bar reads the scene's counts, and still carries its message", whose own step "the counts are the strip's first content, at its own left padding" asserts the position and not merely the presence. `artefacts`: `51ae5fec` (the readout, the bridge's `objectCount` and the drawing's correction) and `1317e07f` (the fix round: the five missing snapshot stubs, the drawing's off-scale `gap` corrected to `--space-6`'s 6px, and the position proof), both ancestors of `1317e07f`. THE RULING WAS APPLIED AND ONE OF ITS INSTRUCTIONS WAS WITHDRAWN: the 2026-10-14 ruling said the counts and the message swap, and the implementer reported that `editor-main.ts` writes a message into the status span at every boot and nothing clears it, so a literal swap hides the counts for the whole session and leaves this row's own defect unfixed. The controller withdrew that instruction and the join is what landed, which is the row's own word. PARITY IS NOT DISPOSED OF: the drawing's status row and the product's `.editor-shell-status` disagree about which of the two values is the gap and which is the padding — filed as its own row rather than fixed here, because which side is right is not specified and the stylesheet half is Task 12.4e's to own. MINOR 5 WAS PARKED, NOT FIXED: `objectCount` stays `number | undefined` and required, because `shell-stores.ts` does produce the `undefined` the readout renders nothing for, so narrowing the union would be a lie about a reachable state.
check: npx playwright test editor-rail.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1 --grep "the status bar reads the scene's counts" — 1 passed, exit 0

title: No pane's title bar carries the count bible section 7.3 requires, and the slot the chrome provides has no caller
detail: FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 12'S PARITY COMPARISON (2026-10-10), MEASURED ON THE BUILT BUNDLE AND NOT READ OFF THE IMAGES. `Pane` (editor-shell/pane.tsx:43) takes `count?: React.ReactNode` and renders `.editor-shell-pane-count` only when one is given; measured with Playwright over the four panes in turn, each title bar reads exactly its title (Composition, Add, Tokens, Document), `document.querySelectorAll('.editor-shell-pane-count').length` is 0 with every pane open, and the four Pane mounts (shell-layout.tsx:732-767) pass no count and no pane-level action. Bible §7.3's title bar is "glyph, title, and the count or a single pane-level action", and the mockup draws it for Add (`＋ Add  8 units`, docs/design/mockups/editor-shell.html:87, and the same row is 8 of plan 2's Task 10 difference list, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:742, which assigns it to plan 4 as "pane content" while plan 4's Out of scope says it "does not re-cut a title bar" and named it in no task). THE GAP IS BETWEEN TWO PLANS, which is why it is a row: what an Add pane would print (the mockup's 8 units is the card library's own count, not insertGroups()'s 21 objects) and what Composition, Tokens and Document would print are decisions neither plan took. RULED 2026-10-14: DERIVE PER PANE. Each pane's title bar prints the count of what that pane lists — Add's is the card library's own entry count, which is what the drawing's `8 units` counts (not `insertGroups()`'s 21 objects), and Composition, Tokens and Document each count their own list. Where a pane's count is not already exposed, the task that prints it names the source in the same commit rather than inventing one, and the drawing is extended for the three panes it does not show, since §7.3 requires the count and a drawing that omits it cannot be the instrument for it. This closes the gap-between-two-plans rather than assigning it: the count is the pane's own content, so the pane owns it.
check: The browser case `every pane's title bar carries the count of its own list, and Document carries none` in `tests/e2e/editor-rail.spec.ts` opens each of the four rail slots and reads the title bar's `.editor-shell-pane-count` against the list that pane draws — the Add pane's `[data-yunari-panel-card]` tiles, the Tokens pane's `[data-yunari-palette-token-row]` rows, and the scene's own `objectCount` for Composition, which `[data-yunari-status-objects]` prints too — asserting the Document pane carries none. Run at `8917f383`: `editor-rail.spec.ts` exits 0 with 13 passed / 13 skipped, and its dom pair (`shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` + `bridge.dom.test.ts`) exits 0 with 78 passed. The case is not vacuous: breaking the Add count to `CARD_LIBRARY.length - 1` reddens it with `Expected: "8 units" / Received: "7 units"`, and the restore is `cmp`-identical. The drawing half is `current/shell.html`'s Add pane carrying the count in the frozen original's own treatment; the three panes no drawing shows are the residue, registered as `vg-523`.

title: editor-shell.css is in no gate and no plan: the ratchet parses CSS but its list names no .css file, and 94 violations sit behind that
detail:
FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING PLAN 5 TASK 1 (2026-10-10, commit 13984ab9), CARRIED AS A `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER IN THAT COMMIT, AND MATERIALISED HERE WITH THE MEASUREMENT THE TRAILER ONLY SAMPLED. The trailer named the `.editor-shell-dialog*` rules' off-scale px; the file's exposure is larger. MEASURED at 13984ab9: `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`'s `gated` array (51 entries) names NO `.css` file (`grep -c '.css'` over it returns 0), while the guard itself parses CSS - `scripts/design-tokens.mjs:181`'s `const isCss = /.css$/.test(path)` selects a declaration-property parser for off-scale px, and eight of its self-test cases are CSS (:235-264, including "an off-scale px spacing is a violation" over `a.css`). Run with `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/editor-shell.css` as its only gated file, the guard reports 94 violations across 1 file and exits 1: 23 spacing-property values (padding 11, margin 4, margin-right 3, gap 3, right 1, margin-top 1 - 2px, 3px, 7px, 9px, 11px, 13px, 18px, 62px, 92px, 122px among them), 11 hex literals outside the `@theme` definition block (`#ffffff1f`, `#7dd3fc`, `#0009` ...), and 60 off-scale px in properties that are not spacing (the 246px rail column, 276px, 340px, 560px, 720px, 980px). THE SECOND INSTRUMENT DOES NOT CLOSE IT: `tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts:10-11` asserts that every gated element's resolved spacing is on the bible's scale, but it reads `[data-fixture-root] *` (:452), and that root is the control fixture's own `.editor-shell` (`control-fixture.tsx:60`) - so a rule reaching a fixture element is enforced from the browser and a shell-only rule is not. NEITHER REMAINING PLAN OWNS IT: `settings-and-appearance.md:529` and `iconography-and-copy.md:501` both record only the file's *hex* count as "the before-state for whatever follows the redesign", and neither adds the file to `gated`, so the conversion has no task - and whether the file should be gated at all, against a per-element browser assertion being the better instrument for a stylesheet whose values are mostly layout dimensions, is a design decision rather than a task. Not fixed in Task 1: adding the file would fail the guard over 94 pre-existing values, which is a plan's worth of work and not this task's. OWNER: whoever owns `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` and the Acceptance section's "no off-scale spacing in a surface". PLAN 7 TASK 6 MEASURED IT AND NARROWED IT (2026-10-11, artefact 45ede8e4, gate work at 43e24bc5; the task review re-measured independently and the numbers held). The title's 94 is superseded - the file holds **61** violations today: 7 hex-literal, 30 off-scale px and 24 spacing px. Task 6 arrived at 67 and fixed the six whose fix is a verifiable no-op (`--shadow-raised` for `0 12px 28px #0000003d` at `editor-shell.css:358`, three `13px` for `var(--text-md)` at `:352`, and a dead `var(--shell-accent, #7dd3fc)` fallback whose token is declared on `:root` and all five palette blocks), each checked against the declaration rather than against the built output alone. THE FILE IS NOT CLEANABLE BY SUBSTITUTION, and that is why this row is still open: 24 of the 61 are spacing values whose section 3 substitution moves pixels, which is a design pass and not a task, and three of them (`margin-right: 62px/92px/122px`, `editor-shell.css:1932/1937/1942`) cannot be expressed as any section 3 step at all. The path was added to `design-tokens.gated.json`, the gate run, and the path withdrawn in the same pass - the list's contract is the files already converted (`design-tokens.mjs:9`) and ADR-0040:12 gives the reason, that a gate which starts red and stays red is turned off. OWNER: unchanged, and now with a measurement rather than an estimate. PLAN 8 TASK 9 (2026-10-11) RE-MEASURED IT AND CAPPED THE COUNT, AND THE COUNT DID NOT FALL. Measured at HEAD: **61** violations - 6 hex-literal, 31 off-scale px, 24 spacing px - so the classes moved while the total held. The two edits that moved them: the overlay's `#0009` scrim became `var(--elev-scrim)` (one hex gone, plan 8 Task 3, `51245173`) and the modal's navigation column became `width: 150px` (one off-scale added, plan 8 Task 2, `5e8ba2b0`), and a diff of the two violation sets against `43e24bc5` shows exactly those two and nothing else. NO NO-OP REMAINED TO FIX: all 61 violation literals were compared with the 114 custom-property values this file declares and none equals one, so plan 7 Task 6's substitution rule - which closed six of the 67 it arrived at - has nothing left to convert here. THE CEILING NOW LIVES IN `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` AS `CEILINGS`, a second instrument over this one file: `max: 58` (the 61 less the three named exemptions), failing when the counted violations rise above it, so it is green at HEAD and can only fall; the comparison is strict, so a count at 58 passes and 59 fails. THE THREE INEXPRESSIBLES ARE EXEMPT BY NAME AND REASON in that constant rather than in a comment: `margin-right: 62px`, `92px` and `122px` are one class - the layer row's reserved slot for n controls, `6 + 26n + 4(n-1)`, which is section 3's own 26px row rhythm plus its 6px and 4px steps and so lands off the step table by construction (`n=1` reaches the step 32 only because its gap term is zero, so 62 is not a value a step can spell). No section 3 step can express any of the three, and correcting one would move the reserved width and let the icons cover the key again. RULED 2026-10-12: the user ruled, as D5's membership ruling covering vg-228, vg-267, vg-271, vg-274 and vg-286 together: TESTS JOIN THE GATED LIST. D9'S FOURTH VALUE IS THE ONE STILL LIVE, MEASURED 2026-10-13, AND WHAT BLOCKS IT IS AN INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN A VALUE. Plan 8's completion report (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-11-settings-parity/task-10-report.md`, the D6-D10 block) lists four values under D9 as `fix` with no predating licence: the Close's `margin-top: 18px`, the rail's `gap: 3px`, the asset buttons' `padding: 4px 7px`, and the plain-DOM control buttons' text inheriting 13px. **Three are fixed on the tree**: the Close's `margin-top` is 16px, the drawing's own value (this is `vg-316`'s row); the rail's `gap` is `4px` (`editor-shell.css:1027`), which is `vg-325`'s verified work; and the asset-button rule states `padding: 4px 8px` (`:1323`). **The fourth is live.** `.editor-shell-panel [data-yunari-asset-import]` (`:1317-1328`) and `.editor-shell-inspector [data-yunari-run-add]` (`:1353-1363`), the two boxes that `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:112` draws as one, state no `font-size` at all, so they inherit the shell root's `font: var(--text-md) / 1.4` (`:687-689`), which is 13px where section 2 gives control text `--text-sm` 12px. title: Snapping candidates are root objects only, so a card no longer snaps to anything inside a neighbouring card
detail: FOUND IN REDESIGN PLAN 2 TASK 1 REVIEW. snap-manager/index.ts:124 builds its candidate list from canvas.forEachObject, which walks roots only. That was equivalent to every object while the starter was flat; now that the cards are groups, a card snaps to other CARDS and to loose objects but never to the parts inside a neighbouring card. Nothing green covers the new granularity - the four snapping specs fail on a harness lookup before reaching this code, so the behaviour is neither proven nor disproven. DECISION, not a defect: snapping a card to another card's outline is probably more useful than to an inner text baseline, and §175 requires a ported behaviour to keep its source's practical quality rather than merely its shape, so the answer is not obvious. It may also be right to offer inner guides deliberately once selection can enter a group (redesign plan 2 Task 4), which is when an author would want to align one card's title with another's. MEASURED 2026-10-04, and the gap this row named is closed: snapping.spec.ts now resizes a part INSIDE a card and records which family of lines the edge joined, as a test annotation rather than an assertion. Result: landed 956.55 aiming at the part line 960 and the card line 700, with 0 guide rows - a resized part snaps to NOTHING, not even to a neighbouring card, while the same gesture between two loose shapes snaps (that control is green). Whether parts SHOULD align to parts is not decided here and stays the user's. RULED 2026-10-14: PARTS SNAP TO PARTS. Inner guides are offered once selection can enter a group, so a card's inner part can be aligned against a neighbouring card's — which is what the row was told to wait for. The instrument's measurement (a resized part lands at 956.55 aiming at a part line at 960 and a card line at 700, with 0 guide rows) stops being the recorded behaviour and becomes the red case the work is fixed against, with the existing loose-shape control kept beside it so the widening is proved to have widened only what it claims. REVIEWED 2026-10-15 by the independent review of `3eaf71ba`, which left the row OPEN and named what is still owed: **the row's own title — a card snapping to something inside a neighbouring card — is delivered and proved** by the new browser case, whose premise the review verified independently (every root line and the artboard's are at least 41 units from the aim against a ~10-unit acquire). **One HIGH finding stands unestablished and it is why the row did not close:** `clearSceneX` in `tests/e2e/editor-canvas.ts` builds its line set from `canvas.getObjects()` — roots only — so the widening added part lines it does not know about, and the review expects `editor.spec.ts`'s *snaps a resized object to a neighbour and shows a guide* to fail at `Math.abs(raw.right - raw.raw) < 3` and `guidePixels === 0`. **The review ran no browser, by its own brief, so this is arithmetic from authored geometry rather than a measurement — and the arithmetic does not obviously agree with that case's own comment, which names the RAM card's right edge at 1318 against VRAM's left at 1332 where the review computes a landing on 1560.** The repro is one command: `npx playwright test editor.spec.ts -g "snaps a resized object to a neighbour and shows a guide" --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1`. Two MEDIUM findings are also owed and neither is a code defect: `repeatsEnclosingBounds`'s stated property is **false on real shapes** (a declared-size group keeps its box while its child's bounding rect includes the stroke, so a single-part group's part is offered, 40 units from the group's lines) which falsifies both the task report's "identical to the old roots-only set" and `editor-canvas.ts`'s rewritten comment; and the **movement refusal's stated cause is unestablished**, because the baseline check only disagrees when the group transform is not identity and the nested fixture's cards are identity, so if that path does not refuse then a part *drag* would have snapped and the deviation's substitute gesture was avoidable.
check: Snapping candidates are the whole scene now, and the instrument that places a no-snap aim reads the same set. `collectSnapSources` in `src/web/packages/editor/src/snap-manager/index.ts` offers every root and then the parts that root holds, so a card has a candidate line inside a **neighbouring** card to snap to; the browser case `a dragged card's edge aligns to a part inside the other card` in `tests/e2e/snapping.spec.ts` asserts the landing and the guide, and the helper that chooses a no-snap aim (`clearSceneX` in `tests/e2e/editor-canvas.ts`) reads the product's own candidate set — roots plus parts, under `collectExcludedObjects`' exclusion — after the fix round found it reading roots alone and the case's own no-snap control snapping to `storage-card-value`'s centre line. Run at `7d3b3afa`: the controller re-ran `npx playwright test editor.spec.ts -g "snaps a resized object to a neighbour and shows a guide" --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` itself — exit **0**, 1 passed, and that is the case the widening broke; the round's `snapping.spec.ts` run exits 0 with 39 passed; `npm run gate` 0 (3437 tests) and `npm run typecheck` 0. Not vacuous: with the walk's descent removed the new case reddens at `landed 416 against the part edge 421`, restored `cmp`-identical. The ruling's second half is demonstrated only at unit level, and why is `vg-524`.

title: The register checker is state-blind across the two files, so an `open` row filed in the archive reads clean
detail: FOUND BY the Task 4.1 scoped re-review (2026-10-12), observation 4 of ten, and filed rather than fixed because the task's contract is an archive read **under the live file's rules** -- a per-register state allowance is a new rule, not the same one, so writing it inside that task would have been the scope creep the brief's own wording excludes. WHAT: `scripts/backlog-check.mjs`'s `STATES` accepts `open`, `in progress` and `unverified` for a row in *either* file, and `check` is never told which register it is reading, so it cannot apply a per-file rule even in principle. The two-file split is by state -- live holds what can still be worked, the archive holds `verified` and `withdrawn` and nothing else -- so an `open` row that lands in the archive is invisible to both halves: the archive read passes it, and the live-file rules that would have demanded a `check` and `artefacts` never see it. MEASURED by the review in a sandbox: an `open` row in the archive reads clean. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: Task 0.4 Step 2 and Task 4.1's own Step 5 argument both rest on the archive holding only those two states, and cross-file id disjointness is *assumed* rather than checked -- a row copied into both files, or one returned to live without being removed from the archive, has no rule against it today, and the checker that exists to catch a false close would report nothing. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: give each register its own allowed state set (live: `open`, `in progress`, `unverified`; archive: `verified`, `withdrawn`) and reject an id present in both files, each as a labelled problem in the set rather than a count. NOT URGENT, and the rule would land green: measured 2026-10-12, no id sits in both files, and the archive holds 176 `verified` and 13 `withdrawn` across 189 rows against 214 live.
check: The register checker is no longer state-blind, and both halves this row names are enforced. `checkPlacement` in `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` gives each register its own allowed states — the live file refuses a `verified` or `withdrawn` row, the `archive` refuses anything that is not one of the two — so an `open` row filed in the archive is a labelled problem rather than a clean read. `checkDisjoint` closes the second half this row names, rejecting an id present in both files. Red-proved by both halves, in the direction that happened: with an `open` row appended to the archive `node scripts/backlog-check.mjs` exits 1 naming the row and the rule, with the same id in both files it exits 1 naming the duplicate, and with either rule disabled `--self-test` exits 1 — three cases on the state half, one on the disjoint half. Each break was undone from a copy outside the repo and proved with `cmp`, not `git diff`; both restores byte-identical. The registers themselves are green: 526 items across both files, no id in both, exit 0.

title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: SPLIT, and the two halves went opposite ways. The canvas half STAYS OPEN as a decision, not a bug: the dim was declined because opacity is in Fabric stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. That reasoning still holds and nothing here overturns it. The layer half was not a decision at all but a defect, and it was worse than this row says — the row recorded that the list dims today (data-context=false), which is true only after something unrelated re-projects the tree. Fixed as vg-058. RULED 2026-10-14: THE CANVAS DIMS, AND THE DIM NEVER TOUCHES FABRIC STATE. It is a view-layer effect the renderer draws at draw time — the stage's own treatment — and never object opacity, so nothing about it serialises and the rule that only authored state is persisted stays intact. That serialisation objection is the whole of the 2026-10-04 decline, and the reading answers it rather than overruling it: the dim is a property of the view, so it belongs to the view. What it costs, named so the task is priced rather than discovered: one renderer mechanism and a DESIGN.md §7 entry for what entering a group looks like. The layer list's dim — the other half of this row, which was a defect rather than a decision — stays fixed as it is (`vg-058`).
check: Entering a group dims the canvas outside it, and the dim reaches the frame rather than the objects — read at `1436df49` by re-running the evidence, not by trusting its report. `DIM_OPACITY` in `grouping-manager/index.ts` is `0.45`, and that is the value `editor-shell.css`'s `.yunari-layer-row[data-context="false"]` dims to, so the two surfaces cannot disagree. The ruling's whole point is that nothing serialises: the alpha is written into the context Fabric hands `before:render` and never into an object, and `entered-group-state.dom.test.ts` proves it non-vacuously — the round trip is byte-identical through the product's own `serialiseScene`, and the same file asserts the dimmed object still carries `opacity: 1`, so a dim that had reached the object would fail the very case that asserts the dim. The browser case *dims the artboard outside an entered group, and leaves it on exit* is the rendered read the rule about visible behaviour requires, and it was re-run here at HEAD: exit 0, 1 passed, with the outside object's centre pixel at alpha 255 before entering, 115 inside, and 255 again after Escape, while the group's own child stays 255 throughout — so a rule that dimmed the whole canvas could not pass it. `npx vitest run packages/editor/src/grouping-manager/` exit 0 (4 files, 27 tests) and `npm run design:check` exit 0 (320 citation sources clean) were both re-run by the controller at HEAD. NOT VERIFIED, and carried rather than claimed: a `clipPath` object dimmed end to end in a browser (the cache branch is unit-covered and the e2e's own `outside` object is cached, but no browser case dims a clipped text), and the transition's cost on a large document, which is unmeasured.

title: The references panel gives a section the id "style" for a section titled "This document", so a second name says style for something that is not one
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 8.2B'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-13) WHILE CHECKING `vg-160`'s CLOSE, AND CONFIRMED AS UNNAMED BY THAT ROW. `src/web/packages/editor/src/panes/document/references.tsx:47` gives the `InspectorSection` `id="style"`, which `components/ui/inspector-section.tsx:57` renders as `data-yunari-section="style"` and `references.dom.test.tsx:67` reads. IT IS THE SAME SHAPE `vg-160` WAS FILED FOR -- a name saying style for a surface that is not the style inspector -- IN A DIFFERENT ATTRIBUTE. `vg-160` renamed the `data-yunari-panel` marker and every reader of it; the panel's `data-yunari-section` id is a separate attribute, so that fix neither saw it nor was owed it, and `vg-160`'s `check` names only the panel attribute. Neither register carries an owner. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on whether the section id is in scope for the same rename, and then the id renamed with its one reader. A rename is cheap here -- one reader -- but it is a decision rather than a substitution, because the section's identity is what a reader of the panel and a test both key on. SEVERITY: low -- a test-facing name that misleads the next person to search for the style inspector. ADDED 2026-10-15 BY TASK 14.2'S FIX ROUND, AT THE REVIEWER'S REQUEST: THE SURFACE IS GONE. The removal of both read-only sections (the user's item 17, `vg-474`) deleted `panes/document/references.tsx` outright, with `references.dom.test.tsx`, `references-fixture.ts` and `selection-inspector/style.ts`, in `aa5edf96`. The attribute this row is about -- that file's `id="style"`, rendered as `data-yunari-section="style"` -- has no producer left, so the rename the row waits on has no subject and the ruling it asks for is moot rather than made. WHICH WAY THIS ROW GOES IS THE USER'S CALL, NOT A FIX ROUND'S: the round that removed the surface appended this sentence and deliberately changed no state. `vg-474` is the row that owned the removal; this one should close as moot when that one does.

WITHDRAWN 2026-10-15 by the ruling on `vg-501`: this row's subject was deleted by Task 14.2, so it describes a surface the product no longer has.

title: backlog-check never tests that a row's detail is a string, so the one row whose detail is an array breaks every string reader in silence
detail:
FOUND WHILE verifying Phase 1's Acceptance (agent, 2026-10-16), which greps each row's `detail` for the marker format `RULED <YYYY-MM-DD>:`.

WHAT: `vg-174`'s `detail` is a **two-element array**, and it is the only row of 529 in either register whose `detail` is not a string. `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` validates a `verified` row's `check` and its `artefacts` — including rejecting a bare-string `artefacts` as "a shape the reader cannot consume" — and it never tests `detail`'s type at all, so the row passed every gate for as long as it has been that way. WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not theoretical: the failure is silent and it is *reader-dependent*. A reader doing `row.detail.match(...)` throws; a reader doing `MARKER.test(row.detail)` has the array coerced to a comma-joined string and **matches anyway**. So two probes over the same register disagree about whether `vg-174` carries a marker — which is exactly what happened here, and it took a third probe to find out why. The Phase 1 Acceptance is itself such a reader, so the instrument that decides whether a phase closes was reading a coerced value for one of its 104 rows.

ALREADY REPAIRED, in the same commit: `vg-174`'s detail is normalised to the string shape every other row uses, joining its two elements — the finding and the ruling — with a blank line, and nothing else on the line was touched. **What is filed here is the rule, not the row**: the checker should refuse a non-string `detail`, in the same spirit as its existing refusal of a bare-string `artefacts`.

NOT A MECHANICAL FIX, which is why this is a row rather than an edit: `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s watchlist, so an edit to it carries a decision note under `docs/decisions/` — the same constraint `vg-528` recorded for `scripts/design-md.mjs`. The decision is also not quite trivial: `detail` is free prose today and the register mixes `"k": "v"` and `"k":"v"` spellings, so the rule has to say what it accepts (a string, and whether an empty string is one) rather than only what it rejects. Related: `vg-529`, which files the checker's other blind spot — it never tests whether a path inside a `check` still exists.
FIXED (agent, 2026-10-16). `check()` in `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` now refuses a row whose `detail` is present and not a string, wording the refusal the way the file already words a bare-string `artefacts` — as a shape, not as an absent value — and a bare array is the case the message names.

The rule was red-proved in two halves, each restored byte-identical by `cmp`: disabling it in place makes its own self-test case fail, and planting an array `detail` on a real row reddens the CLI naming that row. Two self-test cases cover both directions, and `npm run backlog:check` reports 531 items all valid over a register where all 531 `detail` values are strings.

The decision is `docs/decisions/0046-a-rows-detail-is-a-string.md`, which also records what it does not cover: `vg-529` stays open, because whether a path inside a `check` still exists needs a decision rather than a regex.
check: `node scripts/backlog-check.mjs --self-test` exit 0 with the two new detail cases ok, and an array detail planted on a real row reddens the CLI naming that row

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
