title: Two of upstream registry titles disagree with the pairing document they point at, and one seeds the family the other names
detail:
FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FONT CATALOGUE DEDUPE, and both instances are upstream bugs, not ours - we ship a workaround for the class and this row is the durable record of it. At Fonttrio commit 8af7098ada0b90f076fbfe260244d11b05dd2403 the registry index contradicts its own pairing documents on two pairings out of 379, and in both cases the document is right. FIRST, the index is not one-to-one with its documents: it carries 380 entries for 379 distinct pairing names, because playfair-display-roboto is listed twice. Entry one is titled "Playfair Display Inter - Playfair Display + Inter + Inconsolata", entry two is titled "Playfair Display Roboto - Playfair Display + Roboto + Inconsolata", both carry the same url, and both resolve to one pairing document whose own title and cssVars name Roboto for the body role with an h1 weight of 800. So the index ships a title promising a family the record does not carry. SECOND, and independent of the duplicate: cormorant-garamond-proza-libre is titled "Cormorant Garamond Proza Libre" while its pairing document seeds Proza Libre for the heading, Cormorant Garamond for the body and JetBrains Mono for the mono - two family names run together with no separator and the mono family is absent from the title entirely. Its faces are correct, so the title is the whole defect there, where the first case is a duplicated record rather than a bad name. What made both findable is that nothing throws and the shape is valid: the catalogue is 379 unique ids of three faces each with correct weights and licences, so a count-based check passes. The test now asserts that a trio title ends with the three families it seeds, and it holds for 378 of 379 with this second case as the only exception - named in the test rather than waved through, so a third is red and a fix upstream is red too. Our workaround in docs/decisions/0024 is to treat the pairing document as the authority, keep the registry entry whose title matches it, require exactly one match and throw on none or two - so the duplicate resolves correctly today and a future contradiction stops the run instead of being guessed at. What is left for upstream is to drop the stale Inter entry or retitle it to the Roboto one the document serves, and to give cormorant-garamond-proza-libre a title that names its three families. Both are the same fix request and the same owner, which is why this is one row rather than two. RULED 2026-10-14: KEEP THE WORKAROUND. Decision 0024's rule — the pairing document is the authority, the registry entry whose title matches it is kept, exactly one match is required and none or two throws — stays the permanent answer, and upstream is not asked. The row closes recording that the request was never filed, so a later reader does not read the workaround as a stopgap waiting on a filing.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (agent, applying the ruling already on the row). The ruling is `KEEP THE WORKAROUND`: decision `0024`'s rule — the pairing document is the authority, the registry entry whose title matches it is kept, exactly one match is required and none or two throws — stays the permanent answer, and upstream is not asked. The ruling says the row closes **recording that the request was never filed, so a later reader does not read the workaround as a stopgap waiting on a filing**, which is exactly what this close does.

It asks for no change, so it needed no phase. The check was run rather than assumed: `0024` is on disk and still states the pairing rule, and no upstream issue exists for it. The ruling's own commit is `8e91e3e7`.

title: The register has no state for a finding whose subject a later change deleted, so three verified and open rows hold states that no longer describe them
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 closing Task 14.2, by running the checks its own rows name rather than trusting them (`vg-500` is the row that noticed the first two). **Task 14.2 deleted the two read-only surfaces the user's item 17 named, and three rows were riding on them:** `vg-160` and `vg-102` are archived `verified` with checks that read files and cases the removal deleted, and `vg-423` is `open` about `panes/document/references.tsx:47`'s `id="style"` — a marker on a section that no longer exists. A subject that a later change removed is neither fixed nor declined, so none of the register's states fits — `verified` claims a fix that no longer has anything to verify, and `open` claims work that has no subject. **UNTIL THE VOCABULARY HAS A STATE FOR IT, THE HONEST POSITION IS THAT ALL THREE ARE MIS-STATED**, which is why this row exists rather than three silent edits. **The options, with what each costs:** (a) add a `moot` state and close all three with the removing commit named — cheapest and truest, but it grows the register's schema, which `scripts/backlog-check.mjs` validates and which `backlog-archive.jsonl` splits on; (b) close them `withdrawn` with the removal as the reason — no schema change, but it records a decision nobody made; (c) leave them as they are with the provenance in `detail` — no false claim about *this* change, but the archived pair still greps as `verified` for a reader who does not read to the end. **THE TRIGGER IS `vg-474`'s own close**: item 17's register row, once it goes to the archive, is the natural place to rule this, because the three rows' subjects and that row's fix are the same deletion.

RULED 2026-10-15: **CLOSE THE THREE AS `withdrawn`, and add no `moot` state.** The register's vocabulary stays two-valued on the closed side, and the reason travels on each row instead — which is what keeps the close readable, since `withdrawn` on its own would read as a decision not to do work that was never done. The three are `vg-160` and `vg-102` (both archived `verified`, whose subject Task 14.2 deleted) and `vg-423` (open). title: Two DESIGN.md citations name source lines that moved, and design:md --cite passes over them because it checks the marker rather than the target

title: A DESIGN.md marker outside CITE_NUMBERS escapes every citation rule, so §7.9 is unchecked in both directions
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 12.4f implementer (agent), 2026-10-15, reported to the controller rather than fixed.

FOUND WHILE adding `DESIGN.md`'s `§7.9` for `vg-023`, and reported to the controller rather than fixed because the fix is a decision and the path is watched. WHAT: `scripts/design-md.mjs`'s `CITE_NUMBERS` stops at `"7.8"` and calls itself "the single source of truth for what a citation may resolve against". A marker outside that list is invisible to all three citation rules at once, which the code shows rather than the prose: the loop that requires every canonical number to carry a marker iterates `CITE_NUMBERS`, so `§7.9` is not required to have one; the loop that requires every marker to be claimed by a citation skips any number where `!known.has(number)`, and `§7.9` is exactly that, so it is never required to be cited either; and `UNCITED_OK` cannot record it, because that list exists to name markers the rules *would* have caught. Only the placement check still sees it, because that one walks the markers rather than the range — which is why `design:check` was red until the mapping row landed, and why the marker now passes while being uncheckable in both directions. FAILURE SHAPE: a future `§7.9` that nothing cites, or a `§7.9` marker deleted from DESIGN.md, both read green. The gap is the inverse of `vg-352`, which is about a marker being *over*-claimed by another document's numbering; this is a marker nothing can claim. NOT A MECHANICAL FIX, which is why it is a row: extending the range obliges a `§7.9` citation somewhere in `docs/`, `src/` or `scripts/` (a comment in `grouping-manager` is the natural home, beside the constant that implements the section), and `scripts/` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s watchlist — the self-test refuses a note-less edit to `scripts/anything.mjs` — so the edit carries a decision note under `docs/decisions/`. It also raises the question the migration spec owns: whether the range is edited per new §7.N or whether the subdivision should be declared as open-ended, since §7 is the only section this project keeps extending.

RULED 2026-10-15: **THE CANONICAL RANGE IS EXTENDED PER SUBDIVISION, and stays a stated list.** `"7.9"` joins `CITE_NUMBERS` and a `§7.9` citation is written in source, so the marker is required to exist *and* required to be claimed. The range does **not** become a `§7.N` predicate: the spec's declared `§7.1–§7.8` is a claim someone made, and a predicate would make it derived rather than stated. The cost is taken knowingly — each new `§7.N` obliges a `CITE_NUMBERS` edit, a citation, and a decision note under `docs/decisions/`, because `scripts/` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s watchlist.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (agent, triage batch G), executing the row's own `RULED 2026-10-15` line rather than re-deciding it: **the canonical range is extended per subdivision and stays a stated list.**

**The citation the ruling requires was already in source**, which is why the one edit closed both directions: `grouping-manager/index.ts:52` cites `§7.9` beside `DIM_OPACITY`, the constant that implements the section. `DESIGN.md:403` carries the marker. The self-test drives `cite()` with an explicit `numbers` option, so it asserts no range and needed no edit — read rather than assumed.

**Red proof, both directions, on copies restored byte-for-byte.** With the fix in place and `<!-- §7.9 -->` deleted, `node scripts/design-md.mjs --cite` exits **1** and its reason names §7.9 twice — once for the missing marker, once for the citation that resolves to nothing. With the range reverted to `§7.1–§7.8` and the marker still deleted, the same command exits **0**. The second run is the gap this row measured.

**A decision note was required and is why this was not a drive-by edit**: `scripts/` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s watchlist, so `docs/decisions/0047-the-canonical-cite-range-is-extended-per-subdivision.md` claims `scripts/design-md.mjs` before the write. Its rung 4 is recorded as **not run** rather than as finding nothing.

**The cost is taken knowingly and is written into the note**: each new `§7.N` obliges a `CITE_NUMBERS` edit, a citation and a note, which is the price of the range staying a claim rather than a derivation.
check: `"7.9"` is in `CITE_NUMBERS`, so the `<!-- §7.9 -->` marker is now required to exist **and** required to be claimed by a citation — deleting the marker makes `--cite` exit 1 and its reason names §7.9 twice, and with the range reverted to §7.1–§7.8 the same deletion exits 0

title: A File menu row's accessible name now carries its chord, so six e2e locators that match with exact: true no longer match it
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller while reading the browser suite, and ROOT-CAUSED rather than left as a flake: `composition-panel.spec.ts:931` and `:1111` fail at 30s and at 120s alike, in the shared helper `openPackageWithTiming` (`:682`), whose second line is `getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Open package", exact: true })`. **Playwright's failure snapshot shows the menu open and the row present** — `menuitem "Open package Control O" [ref=e16]` — so the element the case wants is rendered and its accessible name has simply grown the chord. **MECHANISM, read from the source rather than inferred from the symptom:** `editor-shell/shell-menu-bar.tsx:182` gives the row's `<kbd>` child `aria-label={shortcutSpokenLabel(shortcut)}`. A child with its own accessible name contributes it to the parent's computed name, so a row that prints a chord now announces as `"<label> <spoken chord>"` and an `exact: true` match against the bare label fails. The rows affected are exactly those the same file gives a fourth `item()` argument — `openPackage` and `savePackage`, i.e. the two the snapshot shows as "Open package Control O" and "Save package Control S"; `New from starter`, `Release package` and the library rows carry no chord and are unaffected. **SIX SITES IN FIVE FILES, listed so a fix does not fix two of them:** `composition-panel.spec.ts:690` and `author-journey-display.spec.ts:229` (`"Open package"`), and `author-journey-display.spec.ts:199`, `author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:926`, `editor.spec.ts:5274`, `glass-authoring.spec.ts:177` (`"Save package"`). **Three of the six were not executed while this was found** — only `composition-panel.spec.ts` was run — so whether they are red today is unmeasured and must be measured rather than assumed. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX:** the cause is named but the correct side is a decision and not a line. The product's behaviour is defensible — a screen reader hearing the chord is the point of the `aria-label` — which makes the six specs the stale side; but the `exact: true` may have been deliberate in one of them, and dropping `exact` from a menu locator widens it to substring matches, which is a different risk. **AND THE LARGER POINT THE REVIEWER'S vg-210 ALREADY PAID FOR:** this case was red at base once before (the `enterLayer` failure), was measured then, and is red again now at a different line for a different reason. A browser suite whose reds are re-attributed by hand every phase is one where a real regression cannot be told from a rotted locator, which is the gap `vg-179`'s neighbours own.
WITHDRAWN 2026-10-16 (agent, triage batch I), on measurement: **no `exact: true` remains on any `Open package`, `Save package` or `New theme` menuitem in `tests/e2e`.** `786ef12b`, "a chorded menu row is named, not labelled", touched 11 files and deleted the flag; it is an ancestor of HEAD, and `composition-panel.spec.ts` now matches `{ name: "Open package" }` with no `exact`.

The row's subject was six locators that could no longer match; there are no such locators, so the hazard is gone rather than latent.

title: The local gate omits three CI steps, so a task can close green on `npm run gate` while CI is red
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller while closing Task 12.4b (`vg-230`), from that task's own review: the review returned spec compliance FAIL on two red checks the implementer never ran, and **one of them is a CI step the local gate does not execute**. MEASURED, not inferred. `src/web/package.json`'s `gate` script is `biome check .. && npm run gates:self-test && npm run design:check && npm run test`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs, in order, `npm run gate` (`:68`), `npm run status:check` (`:71`), `npm run hooks:check` (`:77`) and `npm run typecheck` (`:86`). **So three CI steps are outside the gate: `typecheck`, `status:check` and `hooks:check`.** Reproduced at `51ae5fec`: `npm run typecheck` exits **1** with `Found 5 errors in 2 files` — a required `EditorShellSnapshot.objectCount` missing from five stub literals — while `npm run gate` at the same commit exits **0**. THE GATE'S OWN COMMENT ESTABLISHES THE PRINCIPLE AND THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF IT: it records that the unit suite joined the chain because 'a task closed with `vitest run` red (`vg-323`)', and that `design:check` joined 'for that same reason: it ran only as its own CI step, so a local `npm run gate` read green over a red live-tree verdict (`vg-435`)'. Both were fixed by adding the missing step to the chain. **`typecheck` is the same shape, unfixed, and it has now cost a fix round.** WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE COMMIT: the drain's own close rule is that every phase close names its gate command and that command's exit code, on the ground that 'gates run' is not checkable. That rule is only sound if the gate is the thing CI runs, and it is not — so every close in this plan cites a number that a red CI would not agree with. THE FIX IS ONE LINE IF THE DECISION IS TO INCLUDE IT (`npm run typecheck` in the chain), AND THE DECISION IS THE COST RATHER THAN THE CORRECTNESS: `typecheck` runs `--workspaces` and is the slowest of the three, while the gate's comment says the chain is ordered 'fastest first, so the 1.5s design check fails before the unit suite starts'. `status:check` and `hooks:check` are cheap and `hooks:check` overlaps `gates:self-test`'s `sdd-checkpoint.mjs --self-check`, so they may be deliberate omissions where `typecheck` is not — **the gate comment explains why test and design:check were added and says nothing about typecheck, which is what makes it look like an omission rather than a decision.** WHY A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX: the fix is trivial but the *contract* is not — it changes what 'the gate' means for every task in the plan, and whether a slow type-check belongs in a chain ordered for fast failure is a judgement the gate's owner should make deliberately rather than one a controller makes while closing someone else's task. NEAR ROWS: none found — `vg-323` and `vg-435` are both archived `verified` and are the two precedents this row is the third of, not duplicates of it.
NARROWED 2026-10-16 (agent, triage batch H): **the third of the three CI steps the row names is now inside the gate.** `src/web/package.json`'s `gate` chains `npm run typecheck` as of `0552af0b` (`vg-455`), so the surviving residue is two — `status:check` and `hooks:check` still run only as CI steps, and a green local gate can still precede a red CI on those two. `ci.yml`'s own comment describing the gate without `typecheck` is stale with them.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (agent, triage batch J). **The row named three CI steps the local gate did not reach; two are now in it and the third was already reached by another route**, which is a correction to the row's own count rather than only a fix.

- **`typecheck`** — in the chain since `0552af0b` (`vg-455`), because vitest transpiles without typechecking.
- **`status:check`** — in the chain as of this close. It was the one genuinely missing step.
- **`hooks:check`** — **already reached**, and this is the correction: `gates:self-test` chains `sdd-checkpoint.mjs --self-check`, which is exactly what `hooks:check` runs. The `//gate` comment had recorded that overlap all along.

**Red proof, both directions, on copies restored byte-for-byte.** With `status:check` in the chain and STATUS.md's active-plan bullet deliberately broken, `npm run gate` exits **1** and never reaches vitest. With `status:check` removed from the same chain and the same break in place, it exits **0** — which is the state the row describes, a gate green over a file its own check refuses.

**The first attempt at this proof passed while proving nothing**, and the reason is worth keeping: the break was a plain string replace of `- **Active plan:**`, and STATUS.md **documents that marker inside an HTML comment** above the bullet, so the replace hit the comment and the real bullet was untouched. A break that changes the *description* of a rule is not a break; the second attempt anchors to the line start. It is the same failure the plan's census recorded when a Global Constraints bullet naming a row moved the count by describing the problem.
check: `npm run gate` now chains `npm run status:check` beside the typecheck, so the local gate reaches every CI step it omitted — a STATUS.md the check refuses stops the gate before the unit suite starts, where the same break previously passed

title: The tooltip's delay case asserts its label through an always-true ternary, so the expression reads as a condition that is not one
detail:

CLOSED 2026-10-16 (agent, triage batch J), taking the row's own first option: **the ternary is replaced by the literal it always evaluates to.**

**The proof is not "the case now fails", because the fix changes no outcome** — `"A control".length > 0` is true on every run, so both spellings assert `"Glass blur"`. Two other things are shown instead, on copies restored byte-for-byte:

- **The replaced expression and the literal are the same value**, so the fix cannot have changed what the case asserts; the file passes at exit **0**.
- **The assertion still has teeth**: pointed at a label the case does not produce, the file reddens at exit **1**. Without that second reading, "the assertion is unchanged" and "the assertion is dead" would look identical.

The row's second option — replace it with the variable the case means to read — was not taken, because the case has no such variable: the label it waits for is the fixture's own `"Glass blur"`, so the literal is the honest spelling.

title: The settings-pane spec's section 5 counts the dialog host's consumers as six besides Settings, omits shortcut-reference.tsx and counts a test file and a CSS block among the surfaces
detail:
FOUND WHILE committing the parked-row representation (agent, 2026-10-16) — not the task being done.

WHAT: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-settings-pane-design.md` section 5 argues the modal host stays because `.editor-shell-dialog` is "consumed by six surfaces besides Settings", and enumerates them as `draft-recovery-prompt.tsx`, `new-document-chooser.tsx`, `persistence-manager/replace-document-prompt.tsx`, `theme-library-dialog.tsx`, "plus the host's own rules and `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts`". Measured at source, `components/ui/dialog.tsx` is imported by exactly six modules — those four, plus `settings.tsx` and `shortcut-reference.tsx` — so the count **besides** Settings is five. The enumeration both **omits `shortcut-reference.tsx`**, a real consumer and the `?` sheet, and **counts two non-surfaces**: a CSS block in `editor-shell.css` and a Vitest file. One sentence later the same section says "the host and the five other consumers are untouched", so the spec disagrees with itself.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not a nit: section 5's whole job is to bound the change, and its list is what an implementer reads to decide whose settings-only CSS is dead in `vg-274`'s gated file and which dialogs need a look. An enumeration that drops a consumer and pads with a test file is the instrument being wrong about its own subject.

WHAT THE FIX IS: restate section 5 on one counting basis — the six modules that import `components/ui/dialog.tsx`, five of them besides Settings, naming `shortcut-reference.tsx` — and stop counting the host's own CSS rules and a test file as surfaces. title: Sixteen of the envelope's shapes have no published counterpart, so a key added there is invisible to the schema
detail:
FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-095. The decision note settles that the code owns the key list and the published schema is a hand-written contract held to it by a test - and that arrangement only covers what the schema publishes. Of the 23 shapes KNOWN_KEYS decides, only 7 appear in the schema at all. The other 16, including transform, node, textContent and the four chart settings shapes, live inside Fabric JSON that the schema validates as an opaque jsonValue, and fabric-envelope-schema-sync.test.ts forbids publishing the node tree. So a key added to one of those sixteen is invisible to anything validating against the published schema, which is the whole reason the two registries could disagree in the first place. The sync test catches disagreement where both sides speak; it is silent where only one does. Worth deciding whether that ceiling is accepted - a partially-describing published contract is a reasonable thing to publish, provided nobody reads it as total - or whether the sixteen need some other check. Also noted alongside: serialize.ts KEY_ORDER is a THIRD hand-written list of the same key names. It decides write order rather than membership, so it is not a second owner, but it moves with every key and nothing would notice if it stopped agreeing. AND THE GATE DID NOT CATCH IT WHEN IT HAPPENED, which is worth a line of its own. This row was briefly filed as "vg-vg-1101" — an id built by string-concatenating a formatted id — and backlog-check reported 21 items, all valid, without complaint. So the id check accepts a string that is not an id. That is a small hole in the gate every row depends on, since an id is what closes, what an artefact points at and what a commit trailer names, and it is filed by hand from a script often enough that the mistake is easy to make again.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: THE PUBLISHED CONTRACT IS A CEILING, AND IT SAYS SO -- no check is added for the other 16. The contract states what it guarantees and names what it does not, which is the shape this drain has already ruled twice (vg-184 for the ownership sweep, vg-380 for the sweeps reverse direction): a claim that reads as verification while being none is the defect, and sixteen speculative checks are not the fix. COST IF WRONG: one of the 16 drifts uncaught, which is a finding about a member rather than about the contract.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (agent, applying the ruling already on the row). The ruling is `THE PUBLISHED CONTRACT IS A CEILING, AND IT SAYS SO` — no check is added for the other sixteen shapes, because a contract that states its own boundary is the fix and sixteen speculative checks are not. It asks for no change, so it needed no phase. The check was run rather than assumed: `schema/theme-document.schema.json` still assigns scene geometry and object state to Fabric in its top-level description, and `$defs.fabricScene` still names exactly what Yunari does validate — object identity, nesting bounds and JSON safety — so the ceiling is stated rather than implied. The ruling's own commit is `e5d44cfd`.

title: Shipped source cites a plan's git-ignored execution state, so the citation points at a file no clone has
detail:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING PLAN 7 (2026-10-11, as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `0c6a17c0`). MEASURED: `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts:494` introduces the `PARITY` table with "The shell's regions, as the census adjudicates them (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md`)" - a path inside `.superpowers/sdd/`, which the repo's own plan README (`docs/superpowers/plans/README.md:7`) calls "ignored execution state", and which the subagent-driven-development skill deletes when a plan's final review comes back clean. So the citation names a file no clone has, and the census it points at (the region-by-region adjudication every `PARITY` row's licence and disposition comes from) has no durable home. THE CONVENTION IS ALREADY IN USE IN TRACKED DOCS, which is why this is a question rather than a one-line fix: `.github/bug-player-chart-throw.md:123`, `docs/decisions/0003-authored-text-box-outlives-the-text.md:186` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md:605` each cite a different `.superpowers/sdd/` workspace the same way, and `docs/decisions/0003` is an accepted ADR, so the pattern predates this file. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the right answer is to keep the workspace (the plan's evidence then outlives the plan, at the cost of a git-ignored directory nothing prunes), to move a census worth keeping under `docs/evidence/` when the plan closes, or to treat the citation as provenance that a reader is expected to reconstruct from the archived plan plus the register. The third is the cheapest and is what the other three sites already rely on; the second is the only one that makes the claim checkable. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a user ruling on where a closed plan's evidence lives, since this decides whether the census a parity gate argues from is reviewable by anyone but the session that wrote it. Owned by whoever closes the next plan, not by plan 7, which is closed. RULED 2026-10-14: PROVENANCE ONLY. A citation into a plan's git-ignored execution state is provenance a reader reconstructs from the archived plan plus the register, which is what the other three sites already rely on — no closing step is added and nothing is moved under `docs/evidence/`. The cost is accepted explicitly: a citation of that kind is not checkable by a fresh clone, and the rule is that a claim needing to be checkable cites something else.

SECTION 8.7's REPLACEMENT IS NOT APPLIED, because it cannot be verified and the number is the wrong instrument. The plan orders this row's count corrected to "six tracked `.superpowers/sdd/` citations, not four"; **the row itself names four sites as a census it took by hand** — `mockup-values.ts`, `.github/bug-player-chart-throw.md`, `docs/decisions/0003`, and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-dashboard-authoring-design.md` — and each is a different workspace. The row's own question is unaffected and still open.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (agent, applying the ruling already on the row). The ruling is `PROVENANCE ONLY` — a citation into a plan's git-ignored execution state is provenance a reader reconstructs from the archived plan plus the register, so no closing step is added and nothing moves under `docs/evidence/`. It asks for no change, so it needed no phase. The check was run rather than assumed: the convention is still in use and still unreplaced — `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.ts` cites `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-shell-parity/adjudication.md` at `:1042` and the settings-parity census at `:1065`, and fifteen tracked source and doc files cite a `.superpowers/sdd/` workspace the same way. title: No check resolves a reference into the plans directory, so 55 register rows and 32 of 82 path references resolve to nothing
detail:
FOUND BY PHASE 9 TASK 9.3'S FIX ROUND (2026-10-13) AND EXPANDED BY THAT TASK'S REVIEW, WHICH RAN ITS OWN WIDER SWEEP. Task 9.3 moved six plans to `archive/`, which broke references to them outside the directory. The fix round swept markdown links from `docs/` into `docs/superpowers/plans/` -- 24 links, 23 resolving, 1 broken -- and repaired four hrefs. The review then found the sweep's grammar was the limit: it could see markdown links and not code spans, and its commit message says "every link". THE FOUR SITES, MEASURED BEFORE FILING. (1) `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md:5` links `../plans/archive/2026-09-20-packaged-fonts.md`, and no correct target exists: `9135eb47` added that plan at `.agents/plans/2026-09-20-packaged-fonts.md`, it was never migrated into `docs/superpowers/plans/`, `.agents/plans/` no longer exists, and `04dc86dd` deleted its SDD workspace as one of "the five orphan workspaces". (2) `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-settings-scope.md:3` reads `Status: in progress` while its plan sits in `plans/archive/` -- the href beside it resolves and the status contradicts it. (3) `docs/product/triage/triage-B3.md:14` cites `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-the-shell-and-the-rail.md:731-766` in a **code span**, which the sweep's grammar could not see. (4) `docs/product/triage/triage-B1.md:51` cites `plans/README.md:5-6`, stale since this task rewrote that file. WHY 3 AND 4 ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN REPOINTED: both triage batches declare their baseline -- B1 is "cut contiguously from `docs/product/backlog.jsonl` at `87cc2311`", B3 is "Written at `87cc2311`" -- so they are snapshots of where a plan stood when the batch ran, and moving a plan does not falsify a record of where it was. Repointing them would edit a measurement to say something it never measured, which is the same ruling the controller applied to the three dated snapshots under `docs/architecture/`. They are listed because they are what an unbuilt check would have to cover, not because they are wrong. TWO FURTHER INSTANCES, NEITHER FIXED. **55 of the 70 rows carrying a `plan` field name an archived plan at a path that no longer resolves** -- 41 by a full `docs/superpowers/plans/<name>.md` path and 14 by a bare filename alone, across 11 distinct plans -- and only 15 of the 70 resolve. MEASURED 2026-10-13 BY RESOLVING EVERY `plan` FIELD AGAINST `docs/superpowers/plans/` AND ITS `archive/`, AFTER THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS ROW SAID "ABOUT FIFTEEN" AND WAS WRONG BY MORE THAN THREE TIMES. So the register is not a marginal instance of this class but its largest one: almost every plan reference in `docs/product/backlog.jsonl` points at a name that has moved, and a reader following one concludes the plan was deleted. Whether those fields are meant to resolve or are historical labels is a question about the register's own semantics, so it is a ruling rather than a repoint; the measurement is what this row supplies for it. And the plans directory does have one live reader that the sweep never named: `scripts/check-status.mjs:188` resolves the active-plan slug against `docs/superpowers/plans/`, with no `archive/` fallback. It does not fire for today's active plan, whose full path resolves one line earlier at `:187` -- but it would reject a `STATUS.md` naming a plan that had been archived. THIS ROW'S OWN REVIEW MEASURED THE WHOLE CLASS RATHER THAN THIS MOVE, AND THE SCALE IS LARGER THAN THE MOVE. It enumerated every `...plans/...md` path token in tracked files with `git grep -o -E` and resolved each by hand: **82 references, 32 broken**, of which only 3 belong to this move's class (F1, and the two register files). The other 29 were already broken before this task moved anything -- `docs/decisions/0033-*.md` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-clock-and-theme-locale.md` each point at `2026-10-07-keyboard.md`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-github-issues-backlog-design.md` carries a **second** broken reference at a line the fix round did not touch even though it edited that same file at line 3; `scripts/sdd-checkpoint.mjs` holds one as a self-test fixture; and six sit inside `plans/archive/`. So roughly a third of this repository's references into the plans directory resolved to nothing before this task began, which is what makes this a missing check rather than a consequence of six moves. THE CLASS IS THE FINDING: nothing resolves references of this kind. `design:check` lints `DESIGN.md` and its citations, `backlog:check` lints the register, and `design-md --cite` fails on a `section` marker that does not exist -- but no gate resolves a link or a path reference into the plans directory, and none compares a spec's status to where its plan now sits. The fix round's sweep is exactly that instrument and it lives in a scratch file, not in `scripts/`. WHY IT MATTERS: `archive/` exists so a moved plan stays readable, and a reference that points at the right name in the wrong place makes a reader conclude the document is gone. Moving six plans in one task is what made a sweep necessary; leaving the sweep unbuilt means the next move re-breaks the same references silently, and the next reader has no way to tell a moved plan from a deleted one. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the sweep promoted into `scripts/`, widened past markdown links to path references in code spans and prose, and wired into the gate chain so every reference from `docs/` into `plans/` is resolved on every run -- plus two rulings this row does not take: what a spec's `Status:` means once its plan is archived, and whether a register `plan` field is a live pointer or a historical label. NEAR ROWS: `vg-432` (a source comment citing a `file.ts:NNN` that now lands on unrelated markup) -- the same "nothing resolves a reference" class one level down, in code rather than in docs; `vg-152` (the directory truthfulness this was found under, verified 2026-10-13). OWNER: the reference convention across `docs/` together with `scripts/`, since the fix is a check rather than an edit. SEVERITY: low -- nothing behaves wrongly and no reader is blocked; the cost is a reader concluding a document was deleted when it was only moved, and the next six-plan move re-breaking the same references silently.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 15, Task 15.3). The class is the finding, and the check is now the instrument: `scripts/check-doc-references.mjs` resolves every path token into `docs/superpowers/plans/` against `plans/` and its `archive/`, and runs in the gate as `docs:check`. **The counts are re-derived rather than restated, because they move with every commit.** Measured 2026-10-16 over 867 files: **51 references into `plans/`, 49 resolving, 2 broken** — against the 82 and 32 this row reported on 2026-10-13, so the class has been repaired in the interval. Both survivors are deliberate and carry `doc-ref-ok:` with its reason: the font-trio spec points at a plan that was never migrated out of `.agents/plans/`, and `sdd-checkpoint.mjs`'s self-test feeds the check a fixture it must refuse. **The register's `plan` field half is measured and left alone**: 59 rows carry one, all 59 name a plan that exists, and one spells it without the extension. Whether that field is a live pointer or a historical label is the ruling this row names and does not take, so the check excludes `.jsonl` and decision `0048` records why. **The proof is two-directional.** The self-test's eleven cases cover a bare name, an archive path, a code span, prose, and an escape with no reason; and breaking a reference in a live file makes the check exit 1 while the restore is byte-identical. **That proof is also what caught the check's own first bug** — `git ls-files --cached` alone cannot see a file that is still untracked, so the check reported green over the document being written; it now scans untracked-but-not-ignored files too.
check: a check now resolves every reference into the plans directory: `scripts/check-doc-references.mjs` runs in the gate as `docs:check` and refuses a reference that resolves to nothing, over 867 files

title: Nothing measures how much of the editor the design-token ratchet has not converted, so "only grows" has no target and no finish
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 8.3B'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-13), WHILE CHECKING WHY `vg-334`'s RAW LITERAL WAS NOT CAUGHT BY THE SCANNER THE ROW SAID WAS WATCHING IT. THE SCANNER IS A CONVERSION RATCHET BY DESIGN, AND THAT DESIGN IS THE FINDING: `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json` holds 71 entries, and `scripts/design-tokens.mjs:9-11` states the list is the files ALREADY CONVERTED and that it ONLY GROWS. A listed file must be clean, so a file still holding a raw literal cannot be on it -- which is exactly correct behaviour and exactly why the ratchet can never say what is left. THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: `src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/gradient-editor.tsx` sits outside it (0 grep hits; `git log -S` over the list finds no commit ever naming it) and so does its sibling `colour-picker.tsx`, which holds 17 raw hexes. IT IS NOT AN EXCLUSION BY KIND -- 14 `.dom.test.tsx` files ARE listed -- so the gap is per-file conversion progress with no denominator. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: the honest repair is not "add both files" (that is two entries against an unknown remainder) but a decision about whether the ratchet owes a measure -- a count of editor files still holding literals, or a rule that new UI files join the list when they are written. The second is the one that stops the remainder growing, and it is a policy call about where a new component's tokens come from, not a scanner edit. NEAR ROWS: `vg-334` (closed 2026-10-13 -- its `check` never claimed the gated count, so it stands; its `detail` carried the false scanner attribution and is corrected). WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a rule stating whether the gated list is a migration in progress or the permanent coverage boundary, and then either a measure of the remainder or a requirement that a new `components/ui/` file arrives with its tokens. OWNER: `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` and `scripts/design-tokens.gated.json`, with `docs/decisions/0040` (the ratchet is ours, not a biome rule) as the decision it extends. SEVERITY: low today, and it compounds -- each new component written with a literal is a file the ratchet will never see.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 15, Task 15.2). The row's two options were a measure of the remainder or a rule that a new `components/ui/` file arrives with its tokens, and it records the second as the one that stops the growth but a policy call about where a component's tokens come from. **The measure is the cheapest thing that stops the growth without taking that call**: every run reports how many product source files off the gated list still hold a literal, and refuses a run where that number grew. **The count is measured rather than assumed, and the first cut of it was wrong.** Counting every file off the list reports **81**; restricting to product source reports **19**, because a test asserting a hex is a test *about* a literal and a fixture is a document rather than a surface. A measure that mostly counts things nobody intends to convert is a count with no finish, which is the failure the row names. `components/ui/colour-picker.tsx` — the instance this row names — is one of the 19. **The ceiling is required, not optional.** An object config without `remainderCeiling` fails the run, so the measure cannot be silently omitted, and the run prints when the ceiling can be lowered so it falls with the conversion rather than staying where it was set. Measured 2026-10-16: 120 gated files clean, remainder 19, ceiling 19. **Three self-test cases cover it over a scratch tree**: the count stops at its ceiling and excludes tests and fixtures; a remainder past the ceiling fails and names the file; and a config with no ceiling fails rather than measuring nothing. Decision `0040` is extended rather than duplicated, because this row names it as the decision the work extends.
check: the ratchet now measures how much of the editor it has not converted: `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` reports the remainder off the gated list and refuses a run where it grew past `remainderCeiling`, which is 19

title: `tests/e2e/design-language.spec.ts` is 3550 lines, past the 800-line stop, and no row owns splitting it

title: The library save protocol's error is reported under the `controls` subsystem, a label that now names a module it no longer lives in
detail:
FOUND BY Task 9 candidate rank 5's review (2026-10-12) and flagged by the candidate's own report as a decision someone owes rather than something to smuggle into a refactor. Commit 248ff08f moved the save protocol out of `editor-session.ts` into `theme-library-manager/index.ts` and carried `errors.warn("controls", ...)` verbatim, so the warning's subsystem label names a module the code has left. SEVERITY: low as runtime behaviour -- the label is diagnostics, and the message still reaches the log -- but it is exactly the kind of stale name the move exists to remove, and a rename here is a user-visible string change that wants a decision rather than a refactor's side effect.

RULED 2026-10-12: RENAME the subsystem label to the module that owns the call now, in the next commit that touches that line — not as a refactor's side effect and not as a commit of its own. The label names a module the code has left, which is the kind of stale name the move existed to delete, and it is a diagnostic slug rather than designed copy: `errors.warn` labels a log line, and nothing in the design language governs a log line. Keep the message text untouched; only the slug moves. If that label is ever rendered in the diagnostics surface, the rename lands with the copy table's own review instead — as a log label it is not product copy, and that is the condition this ruling rests on rather than an assumption about the surface.
CLOSED 2026-10-16. **The ruling was already taken and only needed applying**, which is why this was a fix rather than a decision: RULED 2026-10-12, *"RENAME the subsystem label to the module that owns the call now, in the next commit that touches that line — not as a refactor's side effect and not as a commit of its own."* **What moved and what did not.** `theme-library-manager/index.ts`'s thumbnail-warning call reported under `"controls"`, the slug it carried verbatim out of `editor-session.ts` when `248ff08f` gave the library save protocol its own owner. It now reports under **`"theme-library"`**, and `EditorErrorCategory` in `error-manager/index.ts` gained that slug. **The message text is untouched**, exactly as the ruling required — *"Keep the message text untouched; only the slug moves."* **`"theme-library"` rather than `"library"` because the unprefixed word is taken**: `src/web/packages/host/src/providers/library.ts` exports `LIBRARY_PROVIDER_ID = "library"` for the host's own provider registry, which is a different concept, so the slug is prefixed rather than the incumbent renamed. `"controls"` stays in the union — eight other call sites still use it legitimately. **The red proof is the case itself, and its first attempt was invalid.** `theme-library-manager/index.test.ts`'s *"stores the picture beside the document, and a picture that fails does not fail the save"* asserts the label; reverting the slug to `"controls"` with the test left asserting `"theme-library"` makes it fail — **1 failed / 8 passed, exit 1** — and restoring gives 9 passed, exit 0, with the restore proved by `cmp`. **The first run of that proof pointed vitest at the source file rather than the test file, so both directions exited 1 for "no test files found" and the proof proved nothing**; it was redone against the test path. **This row is one of the 50 the plan's seventh census correction found named only by phases the ledger records closed** — its carrying phase had closed, so nothing re-read it. It is the sixth of those 50 to be settled and the second to be fixed rather than closed on a ruling.

title: `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx`'s publish-surface case carries a loop that removes stray `.editor-shell-positioner` nodes and removes none
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 7.3's independent review (2026-10-13), which read the guard while checking that task's own `afterEach`, and probed by that task's implementer. `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx`'s publish-surface case carries a cleanup loop over `.editor-shell-positioner` nodes left in the document: probed with the menu open and after the test's own `layout.destroy()`, it removes **zero** nodes (`+0`), while the same probe counts 3 with the menu open and 0 after the destroy. So the loop's premise -- that a positioner can outlive the test that opened it -- held for the menu cases this file used to run and does not hold here. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether the loop ever removes a node in ANY case in the file, which one probe of one case cannot establish; the row exists rather than a deletion because this repo's bias is detection before deletion and a survivor costs a ticket while a wrong deletion costs the product. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the loop was written for an ordering the file no longer has, or for a surface this file no longer mounts. NEAR ROW: vg-186, whose own probe (3 open, 0 after destroy) is the same measurement taken from the other side. OWNER: `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx`. SEVERITY: low -- a dead loop in a test implies a leak that is not there, which is exactly the reading that cost this file three stale comments.

title: `editor-shell.dom.test.ts`'s cases destroy their mounted shell on the success path only, so a failing assertion leaks the editor and the next case fails for its reason
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 6.2 (2026-10-13) as its own concern 4, and confirmed by its task review, which was the run that felt it: the reviewer's finding 3. THE MECHANISM: every case in `editor-shell.dom.test.ts` reaches `shell.destroy()` (or `reopened.destroy()`) as its last statement, with no `try/finally` and no `afterEach` anywhere in the file, so a case that throws on any assertion before that line leaves its mounted editor alive -- canvas, listeners and the `window` entry `mountEditorShell` publishes. The next case that reads that entry then fails on the previous case's leak rather than on its own subject. MEASURED, not reasoned: with Task 6.2's shared walk deliberately re-spelled root-only, the failing case `keeps a binding whose object sits two groups down` died before its `destroy()`, and the pre-existing `exposes the mounted editor on window for devtools/e2e access` case failed as well -- a fourth failure the mutation did not cause. THE GREEN PATH LEAKS NOTHING, and the controller checked rather than assumed: 15 cases mount 17 shells (one case mounts a second, `reopened`) and every one is destroyed, counted by reading the file. So the cost is confined to runs where a case fails early -- which in this repo is not rare, because the plan's own evidence rule requires every closing row to be shown red by disabling its fix first, and each of those runs is a tree where these cases fail on purpose. NOT FIXED HERE because the remedy is churn rather than a line: a `try/finally` per case across a 400-line file, or one `afterEach` plus a shared mount helper, either of which touches every case in a file two other seats were editing the same day. SEVERITY low on the green path and moderate during red-proofs, where a cascade is exactly what makes a mutation look like it broke more than it did. REPRODUCES by breaking any assertion in an early case and running the file.
CLOSED 2026-10-16. **The row's own remedy was taken in its second form: one `afterEach` plus a shared mount helper, not a `try/finally` per case.** **What was there: 16 cases reached `shell.destroy()` as their own last statement, with no `try/finally` and no `afterEach` in the file**, so any assertion failing before that line left the mounted editor alive — canvas, listeners and the `window` entry `mountEditorShell` publishes — and the next case that read that entry failed on the previous case's leak rather than on its own subject. The row measured that cascade once already: a deliberately re-spelled walk killed the failing case before its `destroy()`, and `exposes the mounted editor on window for devtools/e2e access` failed as a fourth failure the mutation did not cause. **The fix is one owner for teardown.** A module-level `live` holds the shell `mount()` returned, and `afterEach` destroys it and clears the slot. 16 mount sites go through the wrapper; the 10 destroys that were a case's last statement are gone. **The three destroys that are NOT last kept theirs and now also clear `live`**, because the `afterEach` would otherwise dispose the same Fabric canvas a second time — a correctness detail the mechanical rewrite had to carry, not a tidy-up. **Measured both directions, on the committed bytes rather than on the pre-format draft.** With a throw injected into the first case: **1 case fails with the `afterEach` present, 2 without** — the second is the cascade, and it is the row's defect reproducing. It is the same class as `vg-416`, which closed at `b23bcb67` by moving a dead per-case sweep into the file's `afterEach`.

title: The Line-endpoint geometry field could not be typed into by the browser probe, and whether the field refuses or Playwright's editability wait is the obstacle is unestablished
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 2.4b task review (2026-10-12), observation 5, and filed because the finding otherwise survives only inside an archived row. WHAT HAPPENED: driving the Line-endpoints geometry field with a non-numeric string in a browser, the implementer's Playwright `fill` did not complete, and the failure was never explained. TWO READINGS, NOT DISTINGUISHED HERE: if the field was in a refused state at that moment, `ControlNumber` renders `readOnly={refused !== undefined}` and Playwright waits for editability before it fills -- a mundane explanation and no defect at all; if the field was NOT refused, then an untypeable field is a live product defect and the row is a real one. Both readings fit the single observation, which is why this row states the observation and not a cause. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: record which actionability check failed and what the field's refusal state was at that moment; the second reading additionally needs its own repro. WHY IT IS NOT AN AMENDMENT TO `vg-376`: that row closed on a jsdom proof of the funnel contract, which is the right venue for a pure function over a `FabricObject`, and says nothing about whether a browser can drive the control that feeds it. Different surface, different owner, so it gets its own row rather than widening a closed one.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 15, Task 15.5) AS A NON-DEFECT, and the reading taken is a third one the row did not name. **The row's first reading is false.** `fill("abc")` completes in **42 ms** — no actionability check fails, so the field was not in a refused state and Playwright's editability wait was not the obstacle. Measured on a bundle built at HEAD in Chromium at 1280x720: `readOnly: false`, `disabled: false`, no `aria-disabled`, `editable: true`, and the hit target at its own centre is the element itself. **The row's second reading is false too, and this is the part worth keeping.** On blur the control refuses the draft itself — `aria-invalid="true"` with the reason element reading `not a number` — and Escape returns the field to the object's own endpoint, so unreadable text never reaches the write funnel. There is no untypeable field. **And structurally it cannot be refused**, which is why this closes as a non-defect rather than as a mystery: `refused` is set only by the chart manager (`chart-manager/panel.ts`), and the selection inspector's `panel.ts` sets none on a shape's own geometry. `control-number.tsx` is `readOnly={refused !== undefined}`, so on this surface the attribute is never true. **That holds at the original probe's base `7f88dff3` as well**, so the 2026-10-12 observation was the probe's rather than the product's. **The check is a browser case rather than a reading**, so the surface cannot silently stop being driveable: `inspector-sections.spec.ts` drives the field and asserts the refusal. **Proved red by planting `readOnly={true}` in `control-number.tsx`, rebuilding, and failing at `toBeEditable()`**; the file was restored against a byte copy with `cmp` exit 0, rebuilt, and the case passes. **Not reproduced, and stated rather than glossed: the original 30-second `fill` timeout.** That bundle is not built in the tree, so what the 2026-10-12 probe hit is explained but not re-observed. **This is one of the 44 rows the eighth census correction found named only by a phase the SDD ledger records closed.**
