title: The three scrollbar tokens are :root literals that follow no palette, so a dark shell paints a light thumb
detail:
FOUND WHILE CONSUMING THEM, in `3328ae33` (the user's item 1, `vg-458`), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. `--yunari-scrollbar-thumb`, `-thumb-hover` and `-track` are declared once on `:root` in `editor-shell/editor-shell.css` as literal colour values and are produced by no palette, so every palette that is not a light one paints the light thumb. Item 1's own words are "themed to be consistent with the shell theme", and that holds in the light palettes only — a graphite shell reads a `#c9c2b1` thumb against its own ground. NOT FIXED IN `3328ae33` because the fix is a palette-aware trio, which is a NEW PAINT VALUE, and that task's brief forbids adding one. THE DECISION IS THEREFORE A PALETTE OWNER'S, not a CSS edit: either the trio joins the palette token set so every palette declares its own, or the scrollbar is built from tokens a palette already owns (`docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the paint owner). A register row rather than an on-the-fly fix for that reason — the correct behaviour is not yet written down anywhere. **THE CASE THIS FIX WILL MEET, added 2026-10-15 from the 13.5 review:** 13.5’s new case "both shell scrollers carry the scrollbar tokens" (`shell-appearance.spec.ts`) fixes its expected value by appending a reference `div` to `document.body` and reading `--yunari-scrollbar-*` from there. That anchor resolves whatever `:root` declares, so a fix that moves the trio to `.editor-shell` (or any narrower scope) leaves the reference unresolved — and an unresolved `var()` makes the declaration invalid at computed-value time, which reds the case on its own guard ("the reference's own scrollbar-width did not resolve") rather than on the scrollers. Expect that red and update the anchor with the scope; it is not a regression in the scrollers.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.1). **Reproduced before it was fixed, on a built bundle in real Chromium**: under graphite (`--shell-text: #e8ecf3`) the thumb resolved `#c9c2b1` and the panel computed `scrollbar-color: rgb(201, 194, 177) rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, because the three tokens were declared only in the `:root` control block and no palette block declares them. **The row's second option was taken — derived, not six new per-palette values.** `--shell-text` is a role every palette already declares, so one declaration follows the palette and adds no literal. Measured after: the thumb is `color-mix(in srgb, #14120e 24%, transparent)` under editorial and `color-mix(in srgb, #e8ecf3 24%, transparent)` under graphite, and all four scrollers compute the reference pair. **The substitution is written where it is declared**, so a subtree that re-declares `--shell-*` — the palette swatch chip — resolves against the live palette rather than its own; the chip caveat is in the comment rather than left implicit. **Proved red**: restoring the literal fails *"the scrollbar thumb follows the palette in force"* with `Expected: not "#c9c2b1"`, while the sibling scroller case stays green — so the case reads the palette and not merely the presence of a value. Restore verified byte-identically with `cmp`. **This is one of the 44 rows the eighth census correction found named only by a phase the SDD ledger records closed.**
check: the scrollbar thumb follows the palette in force: `--yunari-scrollbar-thumb` is derived from `--shell-text` rather than a `:root` literal, so a dark shell paints a dark thumb — the browser case fails when the literal is restored

title: Two scrollers are portalled outside .editor-shell, so the context menu and the settings sheet keep the platform scrollbar
detail:
FOUND WHILE MEASURING WHERE THE SCROLLBAR TOKENS REACH, in `3328ae33` (the user's item 1, `vg-458`), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. The canvas context menu's popup and the settings dialog's sheet are both portalled, so the two rules the commit adds — on `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector` — never reach them and they paint the OS scrollbar. ITEM 1 AS THE USER WROTE IT IS "anywhere in the GUI", so the commit satisfies it for the pane column and the inspector and not yet for the interface as a whole. NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN A PATCH: the tokens reach these surfaces only if the rule moves to a scope a portalled node also resolves (the document root, or wherever the shell's portalled layer mounts), or if each portalled surface opts in by name. The first is one owner and a wider blast radius; the second is two edits and a list that must not go stale. Not fixed in `3328ae33` because its brief owned the two shell scrollers, and this row names the boundary it left. **THE CASE THIS FIX WILL MEET, added 2026-10-15 from the 13.5 review:** 13.5’s new case "both shell scrollers carry the scrollbar tokens" (`shell-appearance.spec.ts`) queries `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector` by class and asserts each one's computed `scrollbar-width`/`scrollbar-color`. Either remedy this row offers — widening the rule to a scope a portalled node resolves, or opting each portalled surface in by name — moves or duplicates those selectors, so the case must be widened to the portalled surfaces in the same change. As it stands it pins the two shell scrollers and says nothing about the menu and the sheet, which is exactly the boundary this row names.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.1). **Reproduced first**: both portalled classes computed `auto / auto` while `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector` computed `thin / rgb(201, 194, 177)` — a menu popup and a dialog mount outside `.editor-shell`, so a rule scoped to it never reached them. **They join by name in a scrollbar-only rule, and the layout half keeps its two selectors** — that split is deliberate rather than tidiness: the shared `overflow: auto` would turn the popup's own `overflow-y: auto` into horizontal scrolling. **Named rather than hoisted to the document root**, which would restyle every scrollable surface in the host page; the cost is a list that can go stale, and `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts` is what holds it. **The class covers more than the row's two surfaces**, and that is recorded rather than glossed: `.editor-shell-menu-popup` is shared by four menus — the canvas context menu, the display switch and two menubar menus. **Proved red in both halves**: dropping the two classes fails the unit case *".editor-shell-menu-popup takes no scrollbar-width"* and the browser case *"the menu popup is not styled thin (auto)"*, while the thumb case stays green. Restores verified byte-identically with `cmp`. **This is one of the 44 rows the eighth census correction found named only by a phase the SDD ledger records closed.**
check: the two portalled scrollers carry the shell's scrollbar: `.editor-shell-menu-popup` and `.editor-shell-dialog` are named in the rule that owns the pair, so the context menu and the settings sheet stop keeping the platform scrollbar

title: Item 1's 10px rounded thumb, its track and its hover colour are pinned only as stylesheet text, so the whole `::-webkit-scrollbar*` half can revert with every case green
detail:
FOUND BY THE REVIEW of `677ff7bf` (Phase 13.5 Steps 1–3), 2026-10-15, on that task's own new case — so this is a gap in a case landed hours earlier, not a pre-existing one. **What the case reads, and what Chromium paints from.** The case asserts `scrollbar-width` and `scrollbar-color` through the cascade on `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector`. The four rules that actually paint the scroller in Chromium are the `::-webkit-scrollbar*` family at `editor-shell.css:1127-1141` — a 10px gutter, the track, the thumb's colour and `--radius-sm`, and a hover colour. `:1120-1123` states the relationship and the statement is correct: Chrome reads the pseudo-element family and ignores the standard pair **the moment one of them matches**. So the case reads the half Chromium does not paint from, and **deleting all four webkit rules leaves it green** while the shell's thumb reverts to the platform's thin one — colour kept by the standard pair, geometry, radius and hover gone. **The one pin that exists is a text read.** `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts:385-401` reads the stylesheet's own text, which pins the declarations and not their effect. The new case's docstring declares this ceiling honestly (`it proves the scrollers are styled by the tokens, not that a thumb is painted from them`); the review's sharper point is *which* half a reader would take the case to cover. **Why a row rather than a fix in that task.** What would pin it is a rendered read of a painted thumb — geometry, a radius and a hover state — and the repo's standing rule is that screenshots are evidence rather than cross-platform goldens, so a pixel case is not obviously the answer. The alternatives each need a decision before a test edit: accept a pixel read of the scroller's edge; probe `getComputedStyle(el, '::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb')` (**a trap** — Chromium answers with the element's own style, so such a case reads green forever); or rule that the standard pair is the whole styling and delete the webkit family, which trades the 10px rounded hover thumb for the platform's thin one and so is a design change, not a simplification. **What it costs the phase:** 13.5's Step 4 pass takes one rendered reading of item 1 and `vg-458` closes on the consumption the case does prove. What must not be claimed in that close, or in any later summary of item 1, is that the thumb's geometry and hover are pinned by a case. **Near rows:** `vg-458` (item 1 itself), `vg-479` (the trio are `:root` literals that follow no palette), `vg-480` (two portalled scrollers the rule does not reach).
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.1). **The row's second option was taken — the family is deleted, not given a case — and the row was wrong on three measured counts, which is the part worth keeping.** **(1) "Can revert with every case green" is false.** Deleting the four `::-webkit-scrollbar*` rules at HEAD reddens **three** cases in `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts` — *"gives each of the three tokens a consumer"*, *"takes the pseudo-element family from the tokens as well"* and *"paints them from no literal of its own"*. The row's premise was that nothing reads them; a source-contract test does. **(2) "The shell's thumb reverts to the platform's thin one — colour kept by the standard pair, geometry, radius and hover gone" is false.** The pair was already the whole paint, so deleting the family changes **no painted pixel**. **(3) The pseudo-element read is not the trap the row says it is.** `getComputedStyle(el, "::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb").backgroundColor` answers that pseudo-element's own style and goes `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` when the rule is removed — its real ceiling is that it cannot tell painted from inert, which is a narrower thing than the row claims. **The measurement that makes the deletion right rather than merely tidy**, from isolated Chromium probes: `::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 20px }` alone gives a 20px gutter, **plus `scrollbar-width: thin` gives 10**, and `scrollbar-color` alone gives 15 — **either standard property being non-`auto` disables the family for that scroller.** So the 10px width, the radius and the hover colour were declarations no browser this repo runs would read. The stylesheet's own comment claimed the reverse and is corrected in the same commit. **One token went with them, and it is a real loss stated rather than hidden**: `--yunari-scrollbar-thumb-hover`'s only reader was the deleted hover rule, and `scrollbar-color` states a thumb and a track with no third value and no hover state — so a hover colour is what the pair cannot express and nothing else can either. **Proved red**: re-adding one webkit rule fails *"styles the scroller from the standard pair alone"*; restore verified byte-identically with `cmp`. **This is one of the 44 rows the eighth census correction found named only by a phase the SDD ledger records closed.** The row's conclusion — that the family was inert in the shipped configuration — was right; its reasoning was not, and the correction is recorded on the row because a false premise is what a later session would otherwise re-derive.
check: the `::-webkit-scrollbar*` half is deleted rather than pinned, and its own premise was false: the standard pair is the whole paint, `--yunari-scrollbar-thumb-hover` had no other reader, and a case now fails when a rule is re-added

title: ControlIconButton ignores ControlProps.describedById, so a control handed the pane's standing note loses it silently
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 13.3 while correcting ADR 0044's claims, and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`e572c302`). `ControlProps` declares the field at `components/ui/control-well.tsx:38` with the reason written beside it — *'An element outside this control that describes it — the pane's own standing note, whose id the control cannot mint'* — and four controls read it (`control-number.tsx:62`, `control-select.tsx:90`, `control-pair.tsx:45`, `control-well.tsx`). `components/ui/control-icon-button.tsx` reads `refused` at `:65` and routes it to `aria-describedby` at `:92` and to a drawn reason at `:102-104`, and **never reads `describedById` at all** — so an icon button handed a standing note is announced without it, and nothing fails, which is why it took a reader to find. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX:** the cause is named and the fix is a few lines, but *which* icon buttons are handed a note and *what* the note is are owned by the panes that draw them, so the correct behaviour is not yet specified anywhere — it needs the panes' owners looked at, not this file. `ControlProps.describedById`'s own comment names the artboard's size note as the case that motivated the field, and the artboard draws a control well rather than an icon button, so the unmet case is a surface the field was not written for. **Consequence worth separating:** ADR 0044 records its second path (`components/ui/`) as claimed and not taken because of this, so the note and the code now disagree about whether that path is in play.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.2). **Reproduced first**: `ControlIconButton` destructured no `describedById` and its `aria-describedby` was `refused`-only, and no caller passes the prop, so nothing failed — which is exactly why the row says *silently*. **The prop was made to do what it declares rather than removed.** It is `ControlProps`' contract for every control in the set, so an inert prop that is documented is worse than an absent one; the control now composes `describedBy(describedById, reason)`, so a control with both a standing note and a refusal describes both. **Proved red** by reverting the `aria-describedby` composition: the case fails with `expected [ 'yunari-control-_r_0_-reason' ] to deeply equal [ 'yunari-pane-note', … ]` — so it reads the pane's note and not merely the presence of an attribute. Restore verified byte-identically with `cmp`. **A second prop on the same control is inert for the same reason and is filed rather than fixed here** — see `vg-538`. **Homed by Task 16.2, in the phase written for the eighteen rows the orphan measurement pass of 2026-10-16 reproduced as real and still true** (Phase 16's own header in `2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md`).
check: `ControlIconButton` reads `ControlProps.describedById` and joins it to the reason, so a control handed the pane's standing note keeps it — the case fails when the join is reverted, expecting the pane's note id in `aria-describedby`

title: A palette gradient stop's offset is bounded at 0 and 1 and is typed-only, so one bounded number outside the inspector still has no slider
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1, checking the `NOT COVERED` clause of `vg-469`'s census: that row's sweep covered the selection inspector and the chart manager, and recorded that the artboard, palette, theme and settings-modal panes were never checked for a bounded number in some other control shape. They carry numeric controls through `ControlNumber` rather than through the `control` union the census read, and re-reading them on 2026-10-15 found THREE bounded typed-only controls outside those two surfaces rather than one: the artboard size pair (both halves `min: 1 max: 16384` in `panes/document/artboard-fields.tsx` and `panes/document/new-document-chooser.tsx`), a chart series' `Precision` (`chart-manager/chart-fields.tsx`, inside the chart manager, converted with the rest of that file), and this row's subject. **THE ARTBOARD PAIR STAYS TYPED and this is the reason, recorded here rather than in a report:** 16384 is `MAX_ARTBOARD_DIMENSION` (`renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts`), the largest artboard a package may hold — a *validity ceiling* the document format enforces, not a range anyone drags, and a track with sixteen thousand steps is not a control. That is a different thing from this row's offset, where 0 and 1 are the two ends of the value's own range. **THIS ROW IS THE PALETTE OFFSET ALONE:** `panes/tokens/paint-list.tsx`'s gradient stop row carries `min: 0` and `max: 1` — the stop's position along the gradient, which is a fraction by definition — and renders as a text box with no track. So a bounding range exists and `vg-007`'s rule (a bounded number clamps onto its bound and carries a native slider) is not applied to it. NOT SWEPT WITH THE INSPECTOR because it is not the inspector: this is a theme token's own editor, its commit path is `commit({ ...entry, value: { ...value, stops } })` rather than the column's edit port, and the change is a control swap in a pane Task 14.1's brief did not name. The three panes' remaining numeric controls (`angle`, `size`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) are unbounded — two of them refuse a non-positive value at the commit — so this row is the whole of what the census's unchecked clause leaves open. **KEPT FILED RATHER THAN FIXED** (ruled 2026-10-15): it is a control swap in a pane the task's brief did not name, and the row's own commit path is not the inspector's edit port.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.2). **Reproduced first**: the stop offset was a `ControlNumber` with `min: 0, max: 1`, a text box where the sibling spacing controls carry a track. **`ControlSlider` gained `step`, which the wheel handler already read back off the input**, and the pane swapped its control for a slider at `step={0.01}` — the precision the offset's own `0`–`1` bound implies. **A percentage projection was considered and rejected, and the reason is the row next door.** Showing the well `37` for a stored `0.375` would reproduce `vg-494`'s defect one level down — the thumb and the well disagreeing about what the control holds — so the fix does not introduce a second instance of the bug it sits beside. **Proved red** against HEAD's `paint-list.tsx`: *"the offset is still a text box: expected 'text' to be 'range'"*. Restore verified byte-identically with `cmp`. **Measured in the browser as well as in jsdom**: at the editor preview a gradient token's stop offset is `input[type=range]` with `min` 0, `max` 1, `step` 0.01, the accessible name `Stop 1 position`, and the typed well beside it. **One thing the change does not fix and the row never claimed**: dragging a stop past its neighbour still commits nothing, silently, exactly as the text field did. That monotonicity refusal is unchanged and is stated rather than left to be rediscovered. **Homed by Task 16.2, in the phase written for the eighteen rows the orphan measurement pass of 2026-10-16 reproduced as real and still true** (Phase 16's own header in `2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md`).
check: a palette gradient stop's offset is a slider rather than a text box: `ControlSlider` carries `step` and `paint-list.tsx` swaps the bounded `ControlNumber` for it at `step={0.01}`, so the number is no longer typed-only — the case fails on HEAD's control

title: A slider whose projected value sits outside its own range draws its thumb at the bound while its well shows the stored value, so the two halves of one control disagree
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round, in the same state its wheel finding describes, and NOT fixed by that finding's ruling. THE STATE: a panel carrying a border of 100 whose box is then typed down to a drawn edge of 40 has `max` 40 and a value of 100 — `selection-inspector/index.ts` writes `scaleX = dimension / object.width`, so a Size edit moves the bound and leaves the stored value where it was. `vg-478` fixed the radius's own version of this at the write; a border, a shadow blur and the chart's drawn-box measures can still hold a value above the ceiling their control now reads. WHAT THE RULING ALREADY SETTLED: the wheel is a no-op in that state (`control-slider.tsx`'s handler returns before it steps, so a gesture that should raise the value cannot lower it and write a history entry for an edit nobody made). WHAT IS LEFT: Base UI renders the thumb clamped to `max`, while the well — a `ControlNumber` fed the same `shown` value — reads 100. One control, two numbers, and no refusal on either half saying which is real. NEITHER HALF IS OBVIOUSLY RIGHT, which is why this is a row rather than a patch: clamping the projection would silently rewrite the author's stored 100 into 40 in the field's display (the value is out of range because another owner's measure moved, not because the author typed it), and letting the track draw out of range is not something Base UI offers. The candidates are to clamp at the write the way `vg-478` clamps the radius, to show the well's value and mark the track as out of range, or to refuse both halves with a reason until one of the two is chosen. Reachable in principle on the panel border, the shadow blur and every chart setting bounded by `bound: "drawnBox"` / "halfDrawnBox"; not reproduced in a browser by this task.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.2). **Reproduced first**, at `value=100 min=0 max=40`: the range input's `.value` read `"40"` while the well's read `"100"`, with nothing saying so. **Which half is wrong was decided rather than assumed, and the answer is neither.** The well reads the document and is right; the thumb is a projection whose range moved and is right to clamp. **The platform clamps `input[type=range]` and ARIA forbids an out-of-range `aria-valuenow`** (MDN's `slider` role), so the control cannot make the thumb show `100` — what it can do is stop the two halves disagreeing silently. **So the control states it**: a visible note, joined to both halves' `aria-describedby`, with both halves left operable. That is the reading the row's own text points at and the one the decision note records. **Proved red** against HEAD's `control-slider.tsx`: the case fails at the note (`expected null not to be null`) **while the two disagreement assertions above it pass** — so the proof shows the note is what the case reads, not that the values happen to match. Restore verified byte-identically with `cmp`. **NOT REACHED IN A BROWSER, and the row says so itself**: the default document holds groups and texts and no panel, so no drawn box can be shrunk under a stored border. The reading is jsdom, off one mounted control, and the row records the same limit. **Homed by Task 16.2, in the phase written for the eighteen rows the orphan measurement pass of 2026-10-16 reproduced as real and still true** (Phase 16's own header in `2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md`).
check: a slider whose projected value sits outside its own range states the disagreement rather than hiding it: the thumb is a projection whose range moved while the well reads the document, so a visible note joins both halves' `aria-describedby` and the case fails when the note is removed

title: The well has padded 6px horizontally while DESIGN.md §3's table assigns the 4px step to well padding, and no case asserts the well's width so nothing has ever reddened on it
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round R3, whose review read §5's new paragraph and could not follow its citation. A THREE-WAY SPLIT, all of it pre-existing and none of it this task's making: **the code pads 6** (`components/ui/control-well.tsx`'s `wellClasses` returns `px-[var(--space-6)]`, and `--space-6` is 6px at `editor-shell/editor-shell.css:465`), **both current drawings draw 6** (`docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:144` and `controls-editorial.html:145`, each `padding:4px 6px`), and **DESIGN.md §3's own table says 4** (`DESIGN.md:182`, `| 4 | Inside a control (well padding, icon button) |`; 6 is assigned to "between the rows of one section"). Code and drawings agree with each other and disagree with the normative table. WHY NOTHING REDDENS: no case asserts the well's width at all — `design-language.spec.ts` reads the well's right edge against the row and passes at either width, and `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` checks which px lengths a surface writes without comparing that list to DESIGN.md, so a padding the table does not sanction is invisible to every instrument here. WHY IT SURFACED: §5's amendment (`5f8def05`) had to cite the padding to justify 40px, and the citation pointed at §3, which fixes 4 — a reader following it computes `well − 10` and cannot reproduce the amendment at all. THE TWO REMEDIES, which are NOT equivalent: **(a) narrow the well's pad to §3's 4px.** At 36px that leaves a 26px field, so §5's 24×24 target was never violated by the 36px well — meaning no §5 amendment and no `vg-496` would have been needed at all, and this task's own outcome would be undone by the fix to its citation. Set against that: `wellClasses` is shared by EVERY well in the shell rather than the slider's alone, and §5's control vocabulary is closed, so padding one control's well to a different step makes the slider's well a different control from every other well — a drawn difference, not a code one. **(b) move §3's table** to say the well's horizontal pad is 6, as both drawings already draw it. HOW THE TRADE RUNS: (a) is the smaller edit and the only one that would erase work; (b) keeps one padding rule for every well and pulls the normative table onto what the code and two drawings already show, which AGENTS.md's "one owner per concept" favours when three sources agree and the fourth is a table cell. **THE DECISION IS OWED AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE** — it moves a §3 step's meaning for every well, which is the design-language owner's call rather than a fix round's. Read with `vg-496` (the two drawings still draw a 36px well, and the same table cell governs whether they should) and `vg-469` (item 10 is what made the well's width matter: a readout had no target rule, an input does). **Remedy (a) is not a CSS revert either**: `control-slider.tsx`'s `wellClassName` is the only writer of 40 in the scanned tree — every other 40px hit is inside a comment, and the checker strips those — and `unconsumedPx` reds an allowlist entry no file writes, so (a) is two edits (the width, and the `40` in `designLanguagePx`) while (b) is one.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.2). **The row's own ruling was taken — the table is the side that moves — and it was verified against the tree before it was acted on**, because that reverses this phase's default that a drawing loses. **The tree says the table was the odd one out, on both sides.** The code writes `px-[var(--space-6)]` (`wellClasses`), and **both current drawings draw `padding:4px 6px`** on the same well (`controls.html:144`, `controls-editorial.html:145`) — so the code and the drawings already agree on 6px horizontally and only the table said 4. **The table's single "well padding" row was ambiguous across two axes and is now split**: row 4 keeps the 4px step for an icon button and a well's **vertical** padding, and row 6 gains a well's **horizontal** padding. §5's paragraph that called §3's table "the odd one out" is corrected in the same commit, and its stale `editor-shell.css:465` line number is dropped rather than re-pointed — a line number in prose is a citation that rots. **What the code does not do, stated because the entry could be read as claiming it**: `wellClasses` sets horizontal padding and a fixed height (`WELL_HEIGHT`, 26/30/32 by density) and **no vertical padding at all**. The drawing reaches its box with `4px` vertical padding and the code reaches it with a height; the two agree on the box, and the table's new entry describes the step the drawing uses. **Proved red twice, so the case compares values rather than words**: reverting the table fails with *"§3's table names no step…"*, and setting the step to 10 fails with `expected 'flex h-[26px]…' to contain 'px-[var(--space-10)]'`. Restore verified byte-identically with `cmp`, and biome's later format pass left all three proven sources byte-identical to what the proofs ran against. **`npm run design:check` is exit 0** with `DESIGN.md` lint clean and 338 citation sources clean — run by the controller as well as the implementer, because this is the one row in the phase whose fix is a design-language edit. **Homed by Task 16.2, in the phase written for the eighteen rows the orphan measurement pass of 2026-10-16 reproduced as real and still true** (Phase 16's own header in `2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md`).

title: The layer row's fourth control arm reserves 126px for a row the product can no longer draw, and two rows state their arithmetic against it
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 13.5'S SERIAL BROWSER PASS WHILE FIXING THE FIVE STALE EXPECTATIONS IT FOUND, AND REPORTED IN THAT COMMIT'S `Discovered, not fixed:` TRAILER (`17cefbcb`). NOT BY A FAILING TEST — that is part of the finding: a dead selector changes nothing, so nothing can redden. `editor-shell.css:2339` carries the fourth arm of the attended row's reserve, `.yunari-layer-row:has(.yunari-layer-state button:nth-child(4)) { padding-right: 126px }`, and the slot it measures can hold three buttons at most: `RowAffordances` draws a visibility control and, when the row is attended or selected or locked, a lock control (`row-affordances.tsx:62-88`), and `composition-pane.tsx:666` adds at most one enter/leave control beside them. The fourth button was the rename pen, and `vg-462` (item 4) removed it — the caret's job moved onto the row itself, a double-click or F2/Enter, which the pane's own comment states at `composition-pane.tsx:663-665`. So the arm has been unreachable since `e572c302`, and the prose above it (`editor-shell.css:2320`, 'the question for one control on a row that draws four') is stale with it. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the ceiling is two or three is not the same question as whether the arm can match — 126px needs four, three needs 96px, so the arm is dead either way; and nobody has measured whether the three-control arm still leaves the role covered, which is `vg-447`'s half and not this row's. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the deletion is two lines, but `vg-447` (open) and the withdrawn `vg-260` both state their arithmetic against a row drawing all four controls ('126px reserved', `group-time-card` hovered or `group-large` selected), and `vg-447` carries a ruling still owed on which column yields — so the arm, the stale prose and those rows' arithmetic want one ruling rather than a deletion made while passing through. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: reading the arm against the ceiling the product now has, deleting it and the phrase in the comment that names four, and revising `vg-447` and `vg-260`'s four-control figures to say they were measured on a shape the product no longer produces. NEAR ROWS: `vg-447`, `vg-260`, `vg-462`.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.3). **The ceiling was re-measured rather than trusted**: `RowAffordances` draws a visibility control and, where the row is attended, selected or locked, a lock control, and `composition-pane.tsx` adds at most one entry control beside them — **three**. The fourth button the arm was written for was the rename pen, which `vg-462` removed at `e572c302`. **The arm is deleted at `editor-shell.css:2441`** (it was `:2339` when the row was filed, and the prose naming four was `:2320`, now `:2413` — both moved, as this phase's Constraints warn). Four phrases in the arms' own comment block went with it — *the four arms*, *a row that draws four*, *126 at four, so the four are one class*, and the *must not pay for four* above it — plus the entry button's *every four-control row's reservation wrong*. The comment now states why there is no fourth arm, so a later pass cannot re-add it as a tidy-up. **The proof is the count, because a dead selector moves no pixel — and that is this row's whole finding.** Every rendered reading of the layer row is identical with the arm present and with it gone, so nothing can redden for the rule itself. Two cases carry the two halves: `editor-shell.control-rules.test.ts` reads the arms out of the stylesheet and asserts one per control the row draws and none past that count, and `row-affordances.dom.test.tsx` renders the row in the one state that shows all three controls — entered, selected, hidden and locked — and asserts the slot holds exactly three. **Red proof**: the fourth arm put back leaves the stylesheet case red at `expected [ '1', '2', '3', '4' ] to deeply equal [ '1', '2', '3' ]`, exit 1; restore verified by `cmp` and `sha256sum` (`4cc8b0ca…`). Rendered corroboration on the rebuilt bundle: `composition-panel.spec.ts` 12 passed. **The row's third clause is discharged, and two of its three parts were already discharged before this task.** `vg-447` is `verified`, not open — the row's own text calls it open and that pointer is corrected here — and **its 2026-10-15 re-measurement already carries the correction verbatim**: *the four-control case is gone … 126px reserved on 0 rows, 96px on 8, 66px on 52*. `vg-260` is `withdrawn` and archived, and both rows now carry a dated clause naming the sentences that describe the retired shape. **Nothing here rewrites their arithmetic**: a withdrawn row's figures are a dated record, and the repair is a marker on the sentence rather than new numbers. **One stale pointer corrected in this close's own text**: the row called `vg-447` open where the archive holds it `verified`.

title: Every current drawing that draws the slider row's well draws it at 36px while the product and DESIGN.md §5 say 40, and the drawings README's refresh rule owns the change
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round R2, from its re-review's F1. title: A chart series with no authored precision reads 0 in its control, so dragging back to the floor writes a whole-number precision the document never had
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round R2, from its re-review's F3. THE STATE: `chart-manager/chart-fields.tsx` passes `binding.precision ?? PRECISION_FLOOR` to the series' `ControlSlider`, so a binding that carries no `precision` renders `0` on the track and in its well where the `ControlNumber` it replaced showed an empty box. `renderer-core/src/scene/plan.ts:315-327` reads an ABSENT precision as "at most one decimal" and an explicit one as that many digits, clamped 0–6 — so `0` is not the value the renderer draws with. THE SCENARIO: a line series with no authored precision draws `12.3`; the field reads `0`, and nothing in its state says the number is unauthored. An author who drags 0 → 2 → 0 to put it back writes `precision: 0` and silently switches the chart from "at most one decimal" to whole numbers — a document edit nobody meant, with a history entry for it. THE ROUTE THAT EXISTS, and why it is not enough: the well's empty draft commits `onClear` and returns the binding to absent (`control-number.tsx`'s `commit` calls it when the draft is empty and the caller supplies it), but the field then re-reads `0`, so the state the author is in is indistinguishable from the one they left. WHAT A SLIDER IS MISSING, which is why this is a row and not a patch: `ControlSlider`'s `value` is a required number and Base UI clamps it into `[min, max]`, so a track has no unauthored position — expressing one means the track drawing the renderer's fallback while the well reads empty, which is the two-halves-disagree shape `vg-494` already records, or a fourth control state. `chart-manager/panel.ts`'s `settingRows` has the same `?? bound.min` fallback for a descriptor with no family default, which round 0 accepted, so this is consistency rather than a new invention — the row is filed because the fallback has now been inherited silently twice and the hazard is not written where an author meets it.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.3). **Reproduced first**: `chart-fields.tsx` passed `binding.precision ?? PRECISION_FLOOR`, so a binding carrying no precision rendered `0` on the track and in its well where the `ControlNumber` it replaced showed an empty box, while `plan.ts` reads an absent precision as *at most one decimal*. **The decision is the row's first candidate — the track draws the renderer's fallback and the well reads empty — and it was decided rather than picked.** `ControlNumber`, which the well **is**, already owns absence (*a finite number, or nothing at all — never a zero nobody typed*) for every other optional field in this editor; a fourth control state would be a second vocabulary for one fact, three lines from the first. `0049`'s ruling puts the statement in the half that can hold it, and the well is the half that reads the document. **The track cannot hold it**: MDN's `<input type=range>` says *the value is never an empty string*, ARIA's APG makes `aria-valuenow` required for `slider` and forbids it outside the range, and Base UI 1.8.0 clamps a number with no unset presentation. `ControlSlider` gains an optional `unauthored`, and while it is set **and no gesture is in flight** the well renders `undefined` instead of the track's value. The gesture is exempted because the moving value is the control's own state while a drag is in flight (`vg-449`). **The search is in the note rather than in the commit**: `docs/decisions/0050-a-sliders-well-reads-the-document-alone.md` carries all seven rungs, and its rung 4 is a **run** rather than a reading — four ecosystem answers (Warp refuses the state, TofuPilot names an *Unset* state, `rc-range-slider` shows no value for an absent one, Material Web fills the fallback into the property). Task 16.2's `0049` recorded its rung 4 as unrun because no web search was available; this one ran. **Red proof**: removing the `unauthored` pass reddens the case at `expected '0' to be ''`, exit 1, 24 passed / 1 failed; restore verified by `cmp` and `sha256sum` (`58d48ef1…`). Green after: 102 passed over `chart-manager/` and `control.dom.test.tsx`. **The case asserts both directions**, so it is not merely the new state: the floor is still authorable on purpose, and its sibling asserts an authored precision still returns to absent through the empty draft — the route the unauthored state makes a no-op rather than a write the field then undid. **One arm is left deliberately and the reason is a different owner.** `chart-manager/panel.ts`'s `settingRows` keeps its `?? bound.min` fallback, because that fallback **is** the family's own default — what the renderer draws with — and its no-default arm is not this row. `chart-fields.tsx`'s own comment is corrected to say so. **NOT ESTABLISHED, and stated rather than implied**: whether any slider descriptor actually lacks a family default, which would make `panel.ts`'s no-default arm reachable and give its rows the same hazard. The family-default arm is the one exercised.
check: a chart series with no authored precision reads empty in the control's well while the track holds the renderer's fallback, so dragging back to the floor is tellable from an authored 0 — the case fails when the `unauthored` pass is removed

title: A construction dispatched through bridge.run reaches the session façade unwrapped, where the Add pane's private constructing() is what reports a refusal
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 13.3 while implementing `vg-460` (the pane footer's constructions), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`e572c302`). The footer now offers the constructions (`CONSTRUCTION_ACTIONS` in `object-actions.ts`), `bridge.can` exempts them from the selection gate, and `bridge.run` dispatches them — but **the rail the Add pane uses is not the rail they now take**: `panes/add/add-pane.tsx`'s own `constructing()` is what catches and reports a refused construction, and it is private to that pane. A construction that arrives through `bridge.run` is not wrapped by it, so **a refusal is silent from the footer** — in the bare case a theme with no usable token. **ALREADY TRUE, NEWLY REACHABLE:** the canvas context menu shares that route today, so this is not a defect 13.3 introduced; what 13.3 changed is that a second and more prominent surface now takes it. **WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX:** the cause is named but the remedy is a decision rather than a line — either the refusal reporting moves to the session façade (one owner, and the Add pane's private helper retires) or the facade returns an outcome each caller reports (two owners, and the footer and the menu must agree on the words). That is the shape the bug rule files rather than fixes, and `vg-422`'s subject (who owns a refusal's words) is adjacent without being the same.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.4). **Reproduced first, and the throw was traced rather than assumed**: `new-object-defaults.ts:725` → `createNewTextDefaults:520` → `insertNewText:165` → `Object.addText editor-session.ts:527` → `Object.run editor-shell/bridge.ts:704`, as `Error: New objects require a palette token.` out of the click handler. Both of the brief's line numbers held. **Candidate one of the two the row names was taken**: the refusal reporting moves to the session façade, so there is one owner rather than two callers that must agree on the words. `constructing` is now `new-object-panel.ts:227`'s exported function and the façade's `addText`, `addShape` and `addChart` delegate to it; the surfaces that reach them — the layer footer through `bridge.run`, the canvas context menu through `creationGroups` — hold a `void` and could not report a throw themselves. **What the Add pane keeps, and why it is not a double report.** `insertObject` still wraps its own tiles in `constructing`, because those tiles also reach the card and chart wiring refusals, and the Add pane calls `insertNewText`/`insertNewShape` **directly** rather than through the façade — so no path is wrapped twice. `insertCard` is deliberately not wrapped: the document reports that one at its own owner, and the row's subject is the three constructions the shell dispatches. **Red proof**: the two cases in `card-insert-surfaces.dom.test.tsx` redden on the refusal leaving the handler, before the change; green after. Break-and-restore verified with `cmp` (`exit 0`). **`bridge.ts` gained a comment and no behaviour** — the row's defect was never in that file once the façade owned the reporting, and the note `0051` claims it on that basis. Said plainly because a decision note claiming a watched path should not be read as a change to it.
check: a construction dispatched through `bridge.run` reaches the session façade wrapped in `constructing`, the one owner of a construction's refusal — removing the façade's delegation throws the refusal out of the click handler instead of reporting it

title: grouping-manager.group() removes each member with the same canvas.remove that disposes it, so a grouped chart is disposed exactly as a reparented one was
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 13.3's fix round while fixing `vg-461`'s reparent disposal (P1 of that task's review), and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`154e55ef`). The fix replaced the reparent path's root-side `canvas.remove` with a `detachFromRoot` that splices `_objects` and does not fire `object:removed`, **because `canvas.remove` synchronously triggers the scene adapter's `target.dispose()` (`scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts:62`) on an object the document still holds** — an object that still serializes, so a save that looks right reloads wrong. **The same call sits on a second path with a different owner.** `grouping-manager.group()` removes each member from the canvas by that same `canvas.remove`, so with the scene adapter installed a chart inside a grouping is disposed identically. **Measured, not inferred:** the fix round's probe returns `{grouped: true, disposed: true}`. **WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX IN THAT COMMIT:** it is the manager's own write rather than the reparent path's, so the change belongs to the manager's owner — and the manager may have a reason to want the removal event that the reparent path did not, which is a question about `group()` rather than about `moveLayer`. **The two are the same defect with two owners**, which is the bug rule's own case for filing rather than fixing on the fly. **What an owner needs is the probe, which is above**, since the symptom is invisible: the grouping is correct, the serialized scene is correct, and only the rendered backing canvas is gone. **RE-REVIEWED 2026-10-15 (`a93f010206bcb668d`): the shared cause is named, and it is the adapter's listener rather than either caller.** `scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts:61-64` subscribes `canvas.on("object:removed", ({ target }) => { target.dispose(); })`, so *any* foreign root removal disposes the target. **There is a third `canvas.remove` call site, and it is not a third defect:** `crop-manager/index.ts:84` removes a locally-constructed transient `Rect` (`:114`) that was never a document object, so that disposal is correct and the defect sites stay two — this one and `bridge.ts`'s reparent. The adapter's rule is still the one question both share: it disposes what *anyone* removes rather than what **it** removes, and that is why the crop site is named on this row at all — the fix moves the disposal obligation onto every genuine removal site, `crop-manager` included. **That fix is a design decision on a watchlisted path** — `scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts` is on `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s WATCHLIST, so it needs an ADR claiming the path — and it moves the disposal obligation onto every genuine removal site (the adapter's own `clear`, `reusable` and `removeStale`, plus the editor's `deletion-manager` and `crop-manager`), which is why it is a row rather than this task's fix round. **Interim:** 13.3's fix round 2 makes `detachFromRoot` restore the state Fabric's own removal leaves — no `_activeObject` or `_hoveredTarget` left pointing at an object that has left the root — so the reparent path corrupts nothing while this is open; `grouping-manager.group()` keeps the defect until this lands.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.4). **The row's own probe reproduced exactly, which is the whole red proof** because the symptom is invisible — the grouping is correct, the serialized scene is correct, and only the rendered backing canvas is gone. Before: `expected { grouped: true, disposed: true } to deeply equal { grouped: true, disposed: false }` in `grouping-manager/index.dom.test.ts`. **The fix is the row's re-review's shared cause, not either caller.** The adapter's `canvas.on("object:removed", ({ target }) => target.dispose())` subscription is deleted, so no removal event disposes a foreign target; **six sites now dispose what they remove** — the adapter's own `clear`, `reusable` and `removeStale`, `deletion-manager`, `crop-manager`, and `grouping-manager.ungroup`. `group()` and `bridge.ts`'s `detachFromRoot` dispose nothing, which is what the row asked for. **`crop-manager` is correct and stays**, as the row's re-review already established: it removes a locally-constructed transient that was never a document object. **`deletion-manager` gained a disposal it was missing** — a member removed from a group leaves the root without firing the event, so that leak never announced itself. **One existing case changed with the behaviour it read**: `bridge.dom.test.ts`'s parity reference now disposes explicitly, because its bare `canvas.remove` is now only the detach half. That is the parity case the row's own text relies on, and it is updated rather than deleted. **Restore verified with `cmp` (`exit 0`).** Decision note: `docs/decisions/0052-the-party-that-removes-disposes.md`, whose rung 4 is a fetch rather than a reading — see the ledger's note on this seat's search index.
check: `grouping-manager.group()` disposes nothing: the adapter subscribes no `object:removed` listener and the party that removes an object disposes it, so the probe reads grouped true and disposed false where it read disposed true before

title: An unknown chart family wears bar's mark while the row's role abstains, so the row reads Bar for a chart the document never called a bar
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 13.2b'S TASK REVIEW (its finding 2), 2026-10-15, which measured the rendering rather than reading it. **The tree is careful and the mark undoes it.** `layer-tree.ts`'s `chartMark` (`:207-216`) reports a family this build cannot name as `family: undefined`, and its own doc says why — "the row would then claim a chart is a gauge when the document says otherwise, which is the one thing a mark must never do". The mark then does exactly that, one layer up: `panes/composition/kind-mark.tsx:40-43`'s `chartFamilyGlyph` returns `CHART_FALLBACK` for an absent family *and* for one it cannot name, and `CHART_FALLBACK` is `CHART_BAR_GLYPH` (`:27`). **Nothing else on the row corrects it.** The role abstains rather than disclaiming — `ui-copy.ts:54-57` renders an unknown family as the kind word "Chart" — so the row reads `Bar` beside a mark that is a bar chart, and the document never said bar. **This is not `vg-459` again.** That was two *shapes* wearing one glyph, which is cosmetic; this claims a family the document never named, which is the failure the projection's own comment forbids. **Reachability:** `chartMark` reads `object.get("family")` as `unknown` and matches it against `CHART_FAMILIES`, so any persisted document naming a family outside that set — one written by a later build, or hand-edited — reaches it. The collision is asserted rather than hidden at `kind-mark.dom.test.tsx:211-218`, which is the assertion a fix should flip. **Why a row and not a fix:** there is no family-neutral chart mark to fall back to — `KIND_GLYPHS.chart` is *itself* `CHART_BAR_GLYPH` (`icons.ts:231`), so the generic kind mark and the unknown-family mark are one glyph, and the fix is a decision about what an unnamed chart should wear (a neutral chart glyph, or no mark at all) spanning `icons.ts` and `kind-mark.tsx`. **An owner also has the sibling arm to compare against:** `kind-mark.tsx`'s `shapeGlyph` falls back to `KIND_GLYPHS.shape`, which is honest about being unable to name the kind, so the chart arm is the one place the convention is not followed.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.4). **The red proof is the row's own measurement**: `unnamed chart and bar chart wear one mark: expected 'lucide lucide-chart-column lucide-bar…' not to be '…'` — the existing case asserted the collision rather than hiding it, and it is the assertion the fix flips. **The row said the fix spans `icons.ts` and `kind-mark.tsx`, and it does.** `chartFamilyGlyph`'s fallback becomes `KIND_GLYPHS.chart`, and `KIND_GLYPHS.chart` stops being `CHART_BAR_GLYPH` and becomes `ChartNoAxesCombined` — the one lucide glyph that draws several families at once and carries no axes, so it names no single family. Known families keep their own glyphs: `CHART_ICONS` is untouched. **Which of the row's two options was taken, and why.** The row offered *a neutral chart glyph* or *no mark at all*. The neutral glyph was taken because the kind map already has a generic-mark convention — the shape arm falls back to `KIND_GLYPHS.shape`, which is honest about being unable to name the kind — and an empty slot would make the row's mark **vanish** rather than abstain, which reads as a rendering fault. The unnamed chart joined the pairwise-distinct set, so the set now fails if any two marks collapse again. **Restore verified with `cmp` (`exit 0`).** The change moves the generic kind mark as well as the fallback, which is deliberate: they were the same constant, and the collision the row describes is exactly that they were.
check: an unknown chart family wears the kind's generic mark rather than bar's, so a chart row no longer reads Bar for a family the document never named — the case fails when the two marks are collapsed back into one

title: Item 17 removed the inspector's only route to the type-preset panel, and nothing else offers one
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 while doing Task 14.2 (the user's items 13 and 17), and it is a consequence of item 17 rather than of item 13. title: Fabric's own removal hook clears `_hoveredTarget` and `_hoveredTargets` but not `_hoveredActualTarget`, so a removed object is still reported as a hover event's `oldActualTarget`
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 13.3's fix round 2 while reproducing `Canvas._onObjectRemoved`'s cleanup for the reparent path, and reported in that commit's `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer (`c17ce13f`). The hook clears `_hoveredTarget` and `_hoveredTargets` (`fabric/src/canvas/Canvas.ts:1220`, `:1236`) and leaves `_hoveredActualTarget` pointing at the object, so the next hover event's payload can name a removed object as `oldActualTarget`. **Not this path's defect, and parity is unaffected:** `detachFromRoot` reproduces what the hook does, so the reparent path and a real `canvas.remove` leave the same `_hoveredActualTarget` — the new parity case compares the two states and passes. **Why a row rather than a fix:** the field is Fabric's and the omission is Fabric's, so an editor-side write would be a fourth private field reproduced by hand with nothing to check it against — the shape this task spent two rounds removing. **What an owner needs to decide** is whether any consumer reads `oldActualTarget` in a way a stale object can reach: measured cause is above, the consumer is unestablished. The related `hovered` accounting lives in `editor-shell/bridge.ts`'s `detachFromRoot` and its docstring.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.5). **THE UPSTREAM OMISSION IS NOT FIXED, and this row must not be read as a patch.** `SelectableCanvas.ts:356-372`'s `_onObjectRemoved` still clears `_hoveredTarget` and `_hoveredTargets` (`:367-370`) and leaves `_hoveredActualTarget` standing; that is Fabric's code, under `node_modules`, and an editor-side reproduction of a private field is the shape the task that found this spent two rounds removing. **What closed the row is the reachability half, which is the half the row said was unestablished.** **The measurement, and it is a negative claim so it is given as searches rather than as an assertion.** `oldActualTarget` has **zero** occurrences under `src/web/packages` excluding `dist`, under `src/web/tests`, and under `scripts` — so no product or test code names the event payload key. No `mouse:over`, `mouse:out` or `mouse:move` subscriber exists anywhere in `src/web`, so the synthetic in/out events that carry the key have no listener to reach. The canvas subscriptions this product installs are `selection:*`, `object:added`/`modified`/`removed` and `GROUP_CONTEXT_EVENT`. **The field itself has one reader and it is a fixture**: `editor-shell/bridge.dom.test.ts:1071` sets `canvas._hoveredActualTarget`, and `:1144-1156` lists it among the fields the reparent parity case compares — which is a test measuring Fabric's state, not a consumer a stale object could reach. That is the same fixture the earlier task built, and it is why the leak was ever noticed. **The row's own citation was wrong and the pass's correction was right**: the removal hook is `SelectableCanvas.ts`, not `Canvas.ts` (`Canvas.ts:1220` reads the field as `oldActualTarget` and `:1236` assigns it; the hook is `SelectableCanvas.ts`). Recorded because the row is a pointer someone will follow. **What an owner would do if this is ever revisited**: the omission is worth reporting upstream to Fabric rather than patched here, and this row is the evidence that it is currently harmless in this product.
check: no consumer of `oldActualTarget` exists in this product — zero occurrences under `src/web/packages` outside `dist`, `src/web/tests` and `scripts`, and no `mouse:over` or `mouse:out` listener to receive the event that carries it — so the removal hook's `_hoveredActualTarget` omission cannot reach a stale object

title: host-bleed's pixel reading paints an empty canvas when the spec runs with its own earlier cases, and passes alone, so a full-run reading cannot say whether the clip is blank
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.1's fix round, in the full browser pass its brief requires. MEASURED, three samples on the same tree (`develop` at `c242ad63`, bundle rebuilt with `npm run build` then `npm run build:fixture -w @yunari/editor`, `--workers=1`): in the whole suite the case is red with `Expected: > 1000, Received: 0` — the host player's `#artboard canvas.lower-canvas` is visible and every pixel of it is transparent; in a three-file run (`shell-appearance`, `host-bleed`, `host-player`) it is red in the same way, at 219ms; run alone (`npx playwright test tests/e2e/host-bleed.spec.ts -g "shows the same clipped quarter"`) it PASSES in 2.2s. The two cases before it in the same file passed in every sample, and they assert the notice's own sentence ("1 of 2 objects past the left edge"), so the scene is loaded and the objects exist — what fails is the pixel read alone. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and the two readings differ in the one thing that matters: either the scene renders nothing in some orders, or the pixel read races the first render and the ordering of the file's cases decides which. NOT THIS TASK'S: `packages/player` has no import path into `@yunari/editor` (its own boundary case, `packages/player/src/boundaries.test.ts`), and Task 14.1's diff touches only the editor's control set, the selection inspector and the chart manager. NOT FIXED because diagnosing it means running the file's cases in different orders, which is not what this round is for. SEVERITY: medium — the case is the only instrument that reads the player's own pixels for a deliberate bleed, so while this is open a blank display cannot be told from a race.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.5). **Reproduced first, and the red did not come back at HEAD**: the case is green alone (385 ms), in its file (3 passed), in a three-file run (39 passed) and over five repeats — **23 samples, every one green**. **The discriminator is the race, and it was found by probing the page rather than by re-running the case.** Eight loads of the same URL: the canvas element exists at 37–141 ms with **every pixel transparent**, and the ground lands at 77–170 ms — so `#artboard canvas.lower-canvas` is blank for **21–85 ms after it is visible**. The harness's own first read landed at 93–712 ms, i.e. **15–34 ms after the paint on several samples**, and a read inside that window is exactly the row's `Received: 0`. **The row's own durations agree with this**: its red run was the fast one (219 ms) against the passing one's 2.2 s, which is what a race looks like and is the detail that makes this a cause rather than a coincidence. **So the case now polls for a painted frame** (5 s, `expect.poll`) instead of reading once at canvas-visible. That is the right instrument for what the case is about — the clip, not the first frame — and a display that never paints still fails, at the timeout. **Red proof of the poll's failure path**: the threshold raised past anything the fixture paints reddens the case, exit 1, `the artboard never painted its quarter`, Received 848548; restore taken from a copy and `cmp` byte-identical. **That proof shows the poll can fail; it does not re-show the race**, which cannot be red-proven on demand — the green samples and the in-page probe are the evidence for it. **NOT RE-TAKEN, and stated rather than implied**: the row's original whole-suite sample was not re-run, on cost. So what is established is that the case is green in its file, in a three-file run and over repeats — not that the whole suite is green at that case. The row's reading of its own red is superseded rather than merely re-measured: the two readings it could not choose between were *the scene renders nothing in some orders* and *the pixel read races the first render*, and the probe picks the second. **The controller re-ran the file independently**: 3 passed, exit 0.
check: host-bleed's pixel reading no longer paints an empty canvas: the case polls for a painted frame instead of reading once when the canvas element appears, and the blank window the row's red landed in is measured at 21–85 ms after that element is visible

title: The repaint loop and publishing both stop on pagehide and nothing restarts them, so an editor returned from the back/forward cache keeps neither
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.2b's implementer while fixing `vg-040`'s F1 — the draft's timer stopped on `pagehide` and was never re-armed after a back/forward cache round trip — and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `87d5b30d`. Two owners, one shape, verified at both sites. MEASURED, the repaint loop: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:426-428` registers `window.addEventListener("pagehide", () => chartRefresh.dispose(), { once: true })`, and `startChartRefresh` (`src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/chart-refresh.ts:56-64`) returns only `setRate` and `dispose` — `dispose` sets `disposed = true` and cancels the pending frame, `tick` returns early on it (`:33`), and there is no re-arm, so the loop cannot start again. The `{ once: true }` makes the second firing moot: after one round trip the listener is gone and the loop is dead. MEASURED, publishing: `editor-main.ts:432-434` stops the publisher on `pagehide` and nothing restarts it on `pageshow`. What the author sees: charts, bound text and the clock stop updating while the page is plainly still open, and the host keeps showing whatever the phone was last sent. `vg-040`'s F1 was the same shape and was fixed by binding both events in `draft-store.ts:169-180` (`bindDraftAutosave`), which is the mechanism these two need — but neither is reachable by the draft's fix, because each owns its own resource. NOT FIXED HERE because both owners sit outside `vg-040` and that row's ruling was scoped to the draft. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one page-lifetime binding that both stops and re-arms, `startChartRefresh` gaining the re-arm it lacks, and a case proving each resumes after a `pagehide`/`pageshow` pair.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.1). **The row's remedy was re-taken rather than copied, and none of the three shapes the row sketched was used.** The loop gets **`stop()`/`start()` beside `dispose()`**, because `dispose` is called by the player's own mount teardown (`player/src/main.ts:203`), so making it reversible would make the name a lie and let a stray call revive a torn-down loop; and re-creating the loop would mean `editor-main` holding the `refresh` callback and `onError` for a second construction. **The `{ once: true }` goes with it**, since it existed only because disposal was one-way — which is the clause the row itself identified as what made a second firing moot. **The state became three lifetimes rather than two** (`running`/`stopped`/`disposed`), which is the shape the row implies: the page's own lifetime is separate from the editor's, because a frozen page comes back and a disposed loop does not. **The mechanism is the one this repo already fixed this defect with.** `DraftAutosave.start`/`stop` on `4a8e339b` (`vg-040`'s F1) is the precedent, and `start()` is idempotent for the same reason that commit records — `pageshow` fires on the first load too. The publisher half is `offerOpenDocument()` on `pageshow`, and `publish.stop()` is deliberately **not** called, because the switch staying on is what makes the re-offer correct. **Red-proved in both halves.** The loop: `chart-refresh.test.ts` at the base commit, `TypeError: scheduler.stop is not a function` / `scheduler.start is not a function`. The publisher: `publish-loop.spec.ts`'s *comes back is followed again* under `own-host` — the dispatched `pagehide` took the host off the document (`/api/published` → `null`) and the dispatched `pageshow` never put it back, `Expected "e2e-publish-loop", Received null` at a 15 s poll. Restores verified with `cmp`. **NOT VERIFIED, and on the row rather than in a report**: the loop's re-arm has no browser-visible reading of its own — it is proved in the unit case, and the browser case asserts the publisher half of the same event pair. That limits the browser evidence to one of the two failures the row describes.
check: the page-lifetime pair binds `pagehide` and `pageshow` together and `startChartRefresh` carries a `stop`/`start` pair separate from its one-way `dispose`, so a page returned from the back/forward cache repaints and the host is told to follow it again — the case reddens when `start` is absent

title: A refused draft restore is announced and then immediately overwritten, so the author is never told why their work did not come back
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.2b's implementer while fixing `vg-040`'s R2, and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `87d5b30d`. MEASURED: the catch at `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:465-470` sets `status.textContent = "Could not restore the draft: …"` and then falls through to `bootTheme` at `:476`, whose opened branch mounts and overwrites the same element with `openedStatusText(...)` at `:488-489` — the implementer's own Chromium reading shows `status: "Editor ready"` after a refused Restore. So the author answers Restore, their draft does not come back, and the editor says nothing about it. The work itself is safe — that is what `87d5b30d` fixed, the draft surviving the fallback — so this is a reporting defect and not a data-loss one. NOT FIXED HERE because where the refusal should be said is a decision nothing has made yet: the boot branch owns the status line and the refusal has to survive it, which is an ordering question in `editor-main.ts`'s boot flow rather than a missing line. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on where a refused restore reports, and the refusal surviving the boot that follows it. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.1). **The ruling the row said nothing had made is now made, and it does not use the status line.** The refusal is held in `editor-main.ts` and emitted from the **mount that follows it**, through `shell.editor.errorManager.warn("draft", …)`, after `layout.setBridge(...)` — because the diagnostic line is a subscription on that canvas, so the mount is also the first moment a shell exists to report through. **Why the status element was rejected rather than reordered.** It is last-writer-wins by design and the boot writes it last, so any ordering fix is undone by the next writer; and it carries what **is open** rather than what failed. The diagnostic line is held until the first committed edit, which is exactly as long as the refusal is true. **The precedent is this repo's own accepted decision `0051`** — *a toast would be a second message surface for a refusal that already has one* — so this adds no surface. **The message names the fate as well as the reason**, which is where `vg-512`'s ruling landed: `Could not restore the draft "": . Editing this document will replace it.` An author who is told only that the restore failed, and not that the document now in front of them is about to take the slot, has been told half of it. **Red-proved**: `editor-draft-restore.spec.ts` at the base commit — the prompt, the Restore click and the fallback mount all passed, and `.editor-shell-diagnostic` resolved to `

` with `Received string: ""`, so red is exactly the missing report and not a mount that failed earlier. Green after, 1 passed, exit 0, re-run independently by the controller. **`error-manager/index.ts` gained a `draft` category**, which is the vocabulary half: an unsaved document the browser kept and a boot that could not read it is not any of the six categories that existed.
check: a refused draft restore is reported through the shell's diagnostic line, which nothing in the boot writes, so the report survives the boot that follows it — the case reddens with the diagnostic element resolving to an empty string

title: The draft slot holds one document, so a refused restore's draft survives only until the author edits the document that replaced it
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by the scoped re-review of Task 12.2b's R2, and carried as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in R3. MEASURED by reading the two branches: after a refused restore, `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-main.ts:465` catches, `bootTheme` at `:476` mounts a clean fallback document B, and the unrenderable draft D is still in the single slot with the autosave's `dirty` false — so R2's transition rule leaves D alone. But the **write** branch, `draft-store.ts:146`, is not gated on the transition: the author's first edit of B takes the next tick and overwrites D, and an edit followed by an undo before that tick clears it at `:147`. Either way D is gone within 30 s of the author touching B, with no save and no discard. The behaviour is deliberate and is not itself the defect — one slot is `vg-040`'s own decision 1, and the alternative, leaving D in place, would leave the document the author is actually editing undrafted, which is strictly worse. What was wrong was the claim: `editor-main.ts:466-468` says "the draft stays where a build that can read it will find it" and R2's docblock at `draft-store.ts:126-131` says clearing "would delete the only copy of the author's work", and both hold only until that first edit. R3 corrects the two comments; the ceiling is filed here rather than left in a comment, because a comment that overstates is how the next reader is misled. NOT FIXED because changing it is a decision nothing has made: a second slot, a pinned draft, or refusing to draft the fallback document until the author saves it are each a different product. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on what the single slot owes a draft the build cannot render, and the store changed to match it.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.1), **and the honest reading is that the store did not change.** The row's WHAT-WOULD-CLOSE-IT asked for *a ruling on what the single slot owes a draft the build cannot render, and the store changed to match it*. **The ruling is that the slot owes the announcement, not a different slot — so the store needed no change and the announcement is what changed.** That is stated here rather than glossed, because a `verified` row whose subject is a store behaviour should not be read as a store edit. **None of the row's three candidates was taken, and each is rejected on the row's own ground.** A second slot reverses `vg-040`'s decision 1 to preserve a copy this build cannot open. A pinned draft and *refuse to draft the fallback until the author saves it* both leave the document the author **is** editing undrafted — which the row itself calls strictly worse — and the third additionally trades usable work for unusable work. **What the slot owes is the announcement, and it now exists**: `vg-511`'s message names the draft, the reason, and the fact that editing the document replaces it. So the ceiling is announced at the moment it matters rather than discovered 30 s later. **The ruling is recorded where the store owns it** — `draft-store.ts`'s `startDraftAutosave` docblock, replacing the paragraph `vg-512`'s R3 had to correct — and the ordering is pinned by a case in `draft-store.test.ts`: the slot is untouched through the fallback's clean ticks, and the first written edit takes it. **NO RED PROOF, AND NONE IS CLAIMED.** The change is a ruling plus a characterisation case that passes at HEAD by design, so there is nothing to disable. **The row's title remains true** — the draft does survive only until that first edit — and what was wrong was never the behaviour: the row says so itself (*the behaviour is deliberate and is not itself the defect*). What is discharged is the ceiling being unstated. **A later reader who disagrees with this state has the lever the row names**: if the single slot should instead preserve the copy, that is a product decision this close rejects rather than one it never saw.
check: the draft slot's ceiling is stated where the store owns it and announced to the author before their first edit of the fallback replaces the draft — the ordering is pinned by a case, and no store behaviour changed because the ruling is that the slot owes the announcement

title: The glass blur radius follows scaleX and ignores scaleY, so a panel stretched horizontally blurs more than one stretched vertically at the same authored value
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.3b's implementer, carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `cc1ea2d0`, and its cause verified by the controller against the source before it was allowed to become a row. MEASURED: `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/glass.ts:376` reads `const blurRadius = treatment.blurRadius * Math.hypot(own[0], own[1]);`, where `own = deviceMatrix(object, canvas)` and `deviceMatrix` (`:543`) returns Fabric's `[a, b, c, d, e, f]`. So `own[0]`/`own[1]` are the matrix's `a` and `b`, and at angle 0 `a = scaleX * viewportScale * retina` while `b = 0` — `hypot` therefore yields `|scaleX * viewportScale * retina|`, which is rotation-independent and in which `scaleY` does not appear at all. The inspector's own Size fields are what write `scaleX`/`scaleY` (`index.ts`'s `width`/`height` arms scale a shape rather than resizing it), so the asymmetry is reachable from the product's UI. NOT FIXED HERE because whether a non-uniformly scaled panel SHOULD blur isotropically is a design decision, not a defect with a specified correct behaviour: a single scalar radius must be chosen for a non-uniform scale, and `hypot(a, b)` (the transformed unit-x length) is one convention among several. A COMMIT BODY CANNOT BE AMENDED, so the pointer is corrected here: the trailer and the report both said bare "`glass.ts`" while THREE tracked files bear that name (`editor/src/selection-inspector/glass.ts`, `renderer-core/src/theme/glass.ts`, `scene-fabric/src/glass.ts`), and this row's subject is the last of the three. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the intended behaviour for a non-uniform scale chosen and either the radius made isotropic (a `hypot` over both axes' transformed lengths) or the current convention stated as deliberate in a comment and a test.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.2). **The row's analysis was taken as given and the decision it said was missing is the work.** `blurRadius` was `treatment.blurRadius * Math.hypot(own[0], own[1])` — the matrix's x row alone, which is `scaleX` — and is now `treatment.blurRadius * Math.sqrt(Math.abs(own[0] * own[3] - own[1] * own[2]))`, **the determinant's root**, recorded in `docs/decisions/0053-a-non-uniform-scale-blurs-by-area.md` before the first write to the watchlisted file. **Why the equal-area scale and not the row's other candidates.** A filter takes one length and the draw is at identity, so the two scales have to become one number; the determinant's root is the only rotation-independent choice that is **unchanged whenever the scale is uniform**, which is what keeps every uniformly scaled panel — the overwhelming majority — painting exactly as it did. The smaller scale would under-blur a stretched panel and the larger would over-blur it, and neither has a reason beyond taste; this one has the invariance. **Red-proved twice.** The unit cases at the base commit read `blur(96px)` for 4×1 and `blur(24px)` for 1×4 where 48 is required — three cases red. The browser reading is the one that matters for a visual property: `glass-stretch-parity.spec.ts` read **2.375 against 9.164** with the fix off and **6.000 against 6.075** with it on, at the same 170 media precondition. Both files restored byte-identically (`cmp`). **A limit worth stating**: 6.000 against 6.075 is not equality, because the two panels' own rasterisation differs by a fraction at the same blur — the case asserts the pair is close rather than identical, and says so.
check: the glass blur radius is the equal-area scale rather than `scaleX` alone — the determinant's root, so a 4×1 and a 1×4 panel blur alike at one authored value; the browser parity case reads 6.000 against 6.075 where it read 2.375 against 9.164 with the fix disabled

title: The frost-extent instrument is method-dependent at the box rim, so two harnesses read the same frost 3.6 percent apart
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.3b's implementer during fix round R2's re-take, and it is a defect in the evidence instrument rather than in the product. MEASURED: the same frosted Rectangle in the same side-by-side scene reads 13,228 px under the whole-scene cross-page pair (one capture with the rect frosted and the circle bare, against one with the circle frosted and the rect bare) and 12,766 px under the per-shape pair (each shape differenced against an untreated capture of itself) — a 3.6 percent difference in a quantity both harnesses agree on in the interior, so the committed ratio for that scene is 1.3831 under one method and 1.4332 under the other. The circle reads 18,296 px under both. WHERE THEY DIFFER, located rather than described: exactly the rect box's outer rim, 462 px, at rows 236-239 and 319-320 (about 31 px per row) and columns 52-54 and 201-203 (about 30 px per column), with onlyCrossPage 462 and onlyPerShapePair 0. WHAT WAS RULED OUT: a between-page shift of the scene, because the far baseline over the photograph at (215,300)-(305,380) reads 0 under both pairs and all four corners of the rect box read 0 under both. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, in those words, on the row and in the committed probe — the two methods differ only in which untreated capture is the baseline, so the leading hypothesis is a difference in the threshold's noise floor at a soft rim, and it has not been tested. NOT FIXED HERE because the cause is not established and establishing it is an investigation rather than an edit. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the 462 rim pixels explained (a threshold effect, a baseline-capture difference, or something else), the instrument made method-independent or the method named as part of the reading, and the probe carrying one number per scene rather than two. The consequence if left: a future task measuring a frost extent by a different method will read a few percent away and chase a phantom regression.
