CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.2). **The row's two harnesses no longer exist, so the 3.6 percent was re-taken from baselines rebuilt in-tree — and they agree exactly.** Both the bare page (the per-shape pair's baseline) and the circle-frosted page (the cross-page pair's baseline) read **11,631 px, 0 px differing**, over one frosted capture with the region read from the rect's own box rather than from the frost. **THE ROW'S 462 px IS NOT REPRODUCED, AND THE HONEST STATEMENT IS THAT IT IS AN INFERENCE RATHER THAN A MEASUREMENT.** The two harnesses that produced it are gone, so what is recorded in the probe is the same class of effect at a different capture scale, marked as inference. **A later reader who needs the original number needs the original harnesses, which no commit holds.** **The cause found is a real one and it is the cache, not the frost.** Attaching the treatment calls `uncacheChain`, so a frosted page's rectangle paints **uncached** where a bare page's paints through its cache, and the two rasterise the edge a fraction apart: lifting the treatment on the same page moves 11,631 → 11,620, **53 px, every one on the frost's own outline**, and a bare page with only `objectCaching` turned off lands on the same 11,620 with 0 px between them. So the rim is a threshold effect at a soft edge — **not the frost and not the baseline page**. **The instrument's limit is now written down where the number is**: the outermost 2–4 px of a thresholded frost box is not a measurement of the frost. The probe carries one number per scene (rect 13,228, circle 18,296) with the rim resolution in place of the two-method split, and the frame measure moved to `tests/e2e/frame-diff.ts` so one instrument serves both questions. **Red proof**: with the cache control removed the bare page returns to 11,631 and the *cache held equal* assertion fails at 53 px differing, exit 1. Spec restored, `cmp` identical, re-run 3 passed.
check: the frost-extent instrument reads the same from either baseline — both rebuilt in-tree baselines read 11,631 px with 0 px differing — and the rim's threshold effect is recorded as the instrument's limit rather than as a second method

title: host-player's reconnect case finds no connection strip to assert, in the ordered suite and alone on the real host
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller's serial browser pass at Phase 14's close (`npx playwright test --workers=1` over a bundle built in the runbook's order: 301 passed / 4 failed / 226 skipped, exit 1). **Three of the four reds are rows the register already owns** — `vg-431` (`glass-lifecycle.spec.ts:25`, named verbatim), `vg-258` (the display cluster's phone assertions) and `vg-212` (publish-loop's ordered-suite red) — and **this one is named by no row, which is what makes it the pass's finding rather than an expected red.** `[desktop-host] tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts:1280`, "a display fed by the real host › reconnects after the stream fails, and the reading resumes", fails at `:1307` on `await expect(page.locator("#yunari-connection")).toHaveText(/reconnect|connect/i)` with **"Error: element(s) not found" inside a 5000 ms timeout** — the strip never appears, so the case never reaches its text assertion. **Reproduced in isolation** (`--project=desktop-host -g "reconnects after the stream fails" --workers=1`: 1 failed, exit 1), so this is not the ordered suite's load. **Not this wave's change:** neither `tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` nor `packages/player/src/chrome.ts`, which owns the strip at `:180`, was touched by Phase 13 or Phase 14 — the newest commit on either is from an earlier wave. **CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and two candidates are open rather than one:** the strip is conditional (the same `chrome.ts` calls `removeStrip` for it, and a dozen cases in this same spec assert `toHaveCount(0)`), so either a failed stream no longer drives the player into the state that draws it, or the real host never fails the stream on this machine. **The environment is a live candidate, not a dismissed one** — `vg-143` records this same spec file's units case timing out on the real host in isolation too. NOT FIXED HERE: the cause is not established and the fix needs the host's own behaviour read rather than a locator moved, so it is filed rather than guessed at.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.2). **The row's premise is refuted, and refuting it was the work.** The row says the case *finds no connection strip to assert*; what the case actually did was **never refuse the stream**. `page.route("**/ws")` is globbed against the whole URL and the stream's is `…/ws?keys=…&session=…`, so the route matched nothing, nothing was aborted, and the case caught the ordinary *Connecting to the host — 1 sensors requested* strip at about 250 ms — which is why the ordered-suite red and the isolation red looked identical and why no row named it. **So this was a defect in the case rather than in the player**, and the red was the case's own: the assertion was reached and satisfied by the wrong state, and the failure the pass saw was the route's absence rather than the product's. Fixed with a URL predicate on `SAMPLE_STREAM_PATH` — `url.pathname.endsWith(SAMPLE_STREAM_PATH)` — and the assertion now reads the real reconnecting copy. **Red proof is the difference between the two routes on the same tree**: the `**/ws` glob gives the strip at 0 ms and count 0 from 250 ms to 15 s with the route still aborting, and the predicate gives *Lost the host. Values shown are the last received, not current.* from 250 ms on. Green after: 1 passed, 7.6 s, re-run independently by the controller at 4.7 s. **The row's own three neighbours are not this row and stay red**: `vg-431`, `vg-258` and `vg-212`. **`vg-431` was re-measured at the base commit by the previous task and fails identically there.** **What this row teaches, recorded because the register has this shape more than once**: a red that reproduces *both* in the ordered suite and alone is normally read as evidence of a product defect, and here it was evidence of a test whose own setup never ran. The isolation re-run the row's own text leans on could not tell the two apart.
check: host-player's reconnect case's route refuses the stream, so the strip it asserts is the reconnecting one rather than the ordinary connecting one — the case fails when the route predicate is reverted to the `**/ws` glob that never matched

title: A package saved while a group is entered stores a dimmed thumbnail
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 12.4f implementer (agent), 2026-10-15, carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `1436df49`.

WHAT: `captureCanvas` renders the live canvas, and `vg-023` makes the live canvas a dimmed one while a group is entered — so a theme package saved from inside a group stores a thumbnail with everything outside the entered group at `0.45`. WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX AND WAS NOT TAKEN: whether a capture should lift a view state at all is a decision the register does not have yet, and the two defensible answers differ for reasons rather than taste — a thumbnail that lifts the dim shows the document as it would be shared, while one that keeps it shows what the author actually saw. It is the same class as the row above it: a view state reaching an artifact that outlives the session. NOT YET MEASURED: whether the thumbnail is regenerated on exit rather than only on save, which decides whether this is visible at all in the common path; the implementer established that the capture reads the live canvas, not that a stored thumbnail ever differs from a post-exit one. SETTLED BY: a ruling on whether capture is a read of the document or a read of the screen.

RULED 2026-10-15: **A CAPTURE READS THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE SCREEN.** A capture lifts a view state, so a thumbnail shows the document as it would be shared and the dim never reaches a saved artifact. This settles the question the row defers, and it is the same principle the row above it rests on: a view state must not reach something that outlives the session.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.2). **The row's 2026-10-15 ruling was implemented, not re-taken**: *a capture reads the document, not the screen* — a capture lifts a view state, so a thumbnail shows the document as it would be shared and the dim never reaches a saved artifact. **The mechanism is one the capture path owns rather than a second renderer.** `grouping-manager` gains `suspendDim()`, returning a release; `captureCanvas` and `captureThumbnail` take it as an argument and hold it **across `toCanvasElement` alone**, so the live canvas keeps its dim and only the captured pixels are undimmed. Two callers pass it — `editor-main.ts:376` and `editor-document.ts:249` — which is why it is an argument rather than a module the capture imports. **Red-proved on both halves.** The unit case read `['shot']` where `['lift','shot','restore']` is required, and the browser case read the outside object at alpha **115** in the capture where the document's paint is **255**, with the live canvas correctly 115 in both runs — so the proof shows the capture is what changed and not the screen. Green after: 1 passed. **The row's own unmeasured clause was settled first**: *whether the thumbnail is regenerated on exit rather than only on save*. It is the save that captures, so the defect is reachable in the common path rather than only in a corner, which is what made the fix worth taking rather than filing.
check: a capture reads the document rather than the entered-group dim: the capture holds the dim suspended across the render alone, so a package saved from inside a group stores an undimmed thumbnail while the live canvas keeps the dim

title: backlog-check validates every row and never the set, so a register row that vanished passes the gate that owns it
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 while closing Task 14.2, by breaking it: an append script of the controller's own used `lastIndexOf` to find the final line's start and cut the register's last row (`vg-500`) instead of appending after it. **`node scripts/backlog-check.mjs` reported `500 items across both registers, all valid` BEFORE the edit and `500 items across both registers, all valid` AFTER it** — the deletion and the addition cancelled in the only number the gate prints, and every remaining row still parsed, so the run was green with a filed finding gone. The same blindness is total for a plain deletion: removing `vg-500` alone reports `499 items ... all valid` and exits 0. **THE GATE CHECKS MEMBERSHIP, NOT CONTINUITY** — it validates each row's shape, its `§` escapes, its state and (for `verified`) its `check` and `artefacts`, and it has no notion of the set as it was. **NOT FIXED HERE, because the fix needs a decision rather than a patch:** an id-gap rule is the obvious candidate and would NOT have caught this one (the deleted id was replaced by the next id, so the sequence stayed unbroken), which leaves comparing against a previous revision — reading the register out of `git`, so the gate depends on history — or recording a count and a high-water mark inside the file itself, which makes the register carry state about itself. **A reader who trusts the gate's one number should know what it does not say.** Related: `vg-455` is the plan's named unowned gate hole, and this is a second one in the same script.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.4, steps 1-3). **The decision the row said was missing is taken, and it is taken against the two candidates the row itself sketched.** Decision `0054`. **The rule**: the id set of **both** registers is compared against `HEAD` and an id that existed there and exists in neither now is refused. **Both registers, not the live file alone**, because every legitimate close *moves* an id from live to archive — a rule reading one file would fire on the register's normal operation. The invariant is that the register never loses a row, and the two files are one register split by state. **The id-gap rule is declined on the row's own ground.** The row already established that a gap rule would not have caught this incident — the deleted id was replaced by the next id, so the sequence stayed unbroken — and implementing a rule that does not catch the incident it was filed for is worse than none, because it reads as coverage. **The per-row hash chain is declined on rung 4, and the finding is that it would not have worked either.** The ecosystem documents this exactly: `tamperlog` (*"it misses the attack that actually matters: truncation … The fix is not a better hash"*), `arcaeon-ledger` (*"Lop off the most recent rows and what remains verifies clean"*), `dan8433-user/ledger` (*"The chain can't catch truncation alone"*) and `matrym-hashchain` (a dropped tail is caught *"with an anchor … the chain alone can't see truncation"*). **The project this checker's own header cites as its model, beads, has left the format entirely** — its README now calls the JSONL *"an export for viewers and interchange, not the source of truth or a backup"*. All of them are defending against an adversary who can edit the file; ours was a `lastIndexOf` off-by-one, and **the anchor already exists and is already a dependency: git**. **The limit is stated rather than implied**: the comparison is against `HEAD`, so it catches a loss in the window between the edit and the commit — which is the window the incident happened in, and the window the workflow runs the check in. Once a loss is committed, `HEAD` becomes the loss. Closing that would mean reading every revision that ever touched the registers, a `git show` per commit in a gate that runs on every commit. **Red-proved three ways, each restored byte-identically by `cmp`.** Rule 9 neutered turns the self-test case red; **and the incident itself is replayed**: one live row cut, another appended, the count identical at 543 with every surviving row valid — **green at `HEAD`'s checker (exit 0) and red at this one (exit 1), naming `vg-348`**. That last proof needed a `maxBuffer`: the archive passed `execFileSync`'s 1 MiB default on 2026-10-16 and threw `ENOBUFS`, which the summary line would have reported as `continuity NOT checked` rather than as a failure — the read's ceiling is now named with the size that broke it. **A run that could not compare does not print an unqualified green**: the summary line reads `valid by shape, continuity NOT checked (<reason>)`, which is `dan8433-user/ledger`'s three-valued verdict borrowed — a run that skipped rows never mints a green.
check: the checker compares the register's id set against HEAD and a row that vanished is refused by name — the incident replayed (one row cut, one appended, the count unchanged at 543) reads green at HEAD's checker and red at this one, naming vg-348

title: An open register row can carry a check, and the checker validates checks only on verified rows, so a stale check survives invisibly
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by the controller while preparing Task 12.3b's close, as a near-miss: `vg-037` was `open` and already carried a `check` — the 2026-10-14 characterisation's ("Measured across every shape in the running editor … A fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both take blurRadius 16 on the same click") — which checks a capability NEARBY the row's claim and says nothing about a Circle's frost reading stronger than a Rect's. The close script's guard `if (/"check"\s*:/.test(line)) throw` would have rejected the close as written. MEASURED, not inferred: of 199 live rows, all `open`, 2 carry a `check` (`vg-037`, `vg-348`) and 0 carry `artefacts`; of 299 archived `verified` rows, 0 fail the word-overlap test. BOTH live instances PASS that test comfortably — `vg-037` shares 5 words with its own title (line, glass, control, circle, rect) and `vg-348` shares 8 — so the mechanical test cannot tell a stale check from a current one. THE CAUSE IS NAMED: `scripts/backlog-check.mjs:121` gates the `check` and `artefacts` rules on `item.state === "verified"`, so a check on an open row is unvalidated by construction; nothing rejects it and nothing checks it. NOT FIXED HERE because the correct behaviour is NOT already specified — the contract says what a `verified` row must carry and is silent on whether an `open` row may carry a check — so this needs a design decision: reject a check on an open row and strip it on reopen, or tolerate it as inert and make every close REPLACE the value rather than append it. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one of those two behaviours chosen, the checker enforcing it, and a case proving an open row with a check is rejected (or that a reopen clears it). The consequence if left: a reopened row closed again without its check replaced records a nearby capability as its evidence, which is the failure AGENTS.md records as having already cost two false 'landed' reports.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.4, steps 1-3). **The first of the row's two candidate behaviours was taken, on an axis the checker already owned.** Decision `0055`. **The rule**: `check` and `artefacts` are refused on a row whose state is not closed. **Closed means `verified` or `withdrawn`, which is the same pair `checkPlacement` already computes** — so this is one rule on an axis the checker already uses, not a second notion of done. The other candidate, tolerating the field as inert with every close replacing it, was declined because nothing would enforce the replacement either, and a rule the checker knows and does not test is the convention the row was filed about. **The measurement that decided the axis, taken before writing the rule**: of 543 rows, 154 are `open` and **1** carries a `check`; 366 are `verified` and all carry both; **23 are `withdrawn` and 7 carry a `check` with 3 carrying an `artefacts`**. So a rule written on `verified` rather than on **closed** would have failed ten existing rows — and deleting a withdrawn row's check would be destroying the register's memory of what was examined before the subject turned out to be gone, to satisfy a rule about closes. **The live instance was read in full and is the shape the rule exists to refuse**: `vg-348`'s `check` read `"NOT YET RUN - the case to add: …"` — a to-do written into the field that means *here is what proved this*. Its content is already in the row's own `detail` (the same measurement, the same case, the ruling), so stripping the field loses nothing. **The row's own example, `vg-037`, has since closed and moved to the archive as `verified`**, so the live violation was exactly one row, not the two the row measured. **A pre-existing self-test case carried the old premise and was propagated rather than left red**: *an open item needs no check* passed `check: undefined` while keeping `artefacts: ["HEAD"]` from the shared fixture, which rule 10 makes the same claim in another field. It now drops both, and says why. **Red-proved**: with the rule deleted, three self-test cases go red — a check on an open row, an artefacts on an open row, and a check on an in-progress row — while *a check on a withdrawn row passes* is the case that keeps the axis honest, since a rule written on `verified` would fail it. Restored byte-identically by `cmp`; self-test 40 cases exit 0.
check: the checker refuses a check or an artefacts on an open register row, and the self-test case fails when the rule is disabled — the axis is closed rather than verified, so a withdrawn row keeps its check as the record of what was examined

title: No spec asserts the player's update loop reaches the canvas now the case that did was deleted with display-fabric.spec.ts
detail:
FOUND BY Phase 0 of the backlog drain (2026-10-12), filing the residual spec section 3.2 states for vg-196 rather than reading the coverage out of a row whose subject was deleted. WHAT CLOSED, AND WHY THAT LEAVES A HOLE: vg-196's subject was `display-fabric.spec.ts`'s case `keeps repainting as samples arrive`, held by that row's own words to be a STANDING RED -- a 30 s timeout landing before its assertion, reproduced at `af499716` -- so the coverage the file believed it had for the update loop was absent rather than passing. Commit `ad94e5ed` deleted the spec and with it the red; it did not repair the loop, and whether the loop is still covered was never answered. WHAT IS VERIFIED AT HEAD (2026-10-12): `openCanvasPlayer`, the shared helper that case awaited, has zero occurrences repo-wide; `page.clock` survives only as the shared `tests/e2e/clock.ts` helper `installFixedClock`, whose call sites are `tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts`'s two determinism captures (`:4435`, `:4518`) and `clock.ts`'s own `openPaused`, an exported helper with no callers anywhere (measured 2026-10-12), so no player spec installs a clock; and no surviving spec reads the artboard canvas twice with a sample between the reads -- `tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` proves samples arrive (its `batchCount` reading and the disappearance of `#yunari-connection`) and that the artboard canvas is visible, neither of which is a repaint. The case in `src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/scene/mount.dom.test.ts` that does drive `handle.update` asserts DOM span identity, which is the DOM renderer, not the Fabric canvas the player mounts. WHY IT MATTERS: the deleted case's own comment recorded its failure verified by sabotage -- the update call cut, and it goes red -- and it was the only thing in the suite that would notice the update loop ceasing to reach the canvas. OWNER: the refresh path that reaches the canvas is `src/web/packages/player/src/main.ts` (`refresh()`, which drives `hydrateCharts` and `refreshBoundText` and then calls `handle.canvas.requestRenderAll()`, scheduled by `startChartRefresh(refresh, 30, ...)`), whose binding helpers come from the scene-fabric package — `refreshBoundText` in `fabric-text.ts` and `startChartRefresh` in `chart-refresh.ts`, with `hydrateCharts` local to the player — while `src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts` is the mount path (`createSceneAdapter`), not the refresh; a replacement case belongs in `src/web/tests/e2e/host-player.spec.ts` beside its live-sample test. WHAT SETTLES IT: one browser case that reads the artboard canvas, drives at least one sample, and requires the pixels to differ between the two reads. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the coverage is wanted at all -- the close is legitimate without it, and this row exists so the hole is tracked rather than reconstructed from a row whose subject is gone.
TWO SUPPORTING MEASUREMENTS CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (agent, triage batch H), while reproducing the headline claim. **The headline holds** — no spec drives a sample and requires the artboard pixels to differ, and the surviving player case requires two paused frames to be byte-identical. But two of the row's supporting facts are now false: `openPaused` (`tests/e2e/clock.ts:124`) **does** have a caller at `host-player.spec.ts:923`, so "no player spec installs a clock" no longer describes HEAD; and `installFixedClock`'s sites are now `editor.spec.ts:5188` and `:5271`, not `:4435` and `:4518`. The new caller still asserts frame equality rather than repaint, which is why the coverage gap stands.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.3). **The case was written rather than the row closed on *coverage not wanted***, which the row left open as a legitimate alternative — so the first of its two options was taken, and the second is recorded as declined rather than as unconsidered. **The case**: `host-player.spec.ts:802` *a live sample repaints the artboard* (desktop-host). It screenshots `#artboard canvas.lower-canvas`, waits for a consumed batch, polls for the clock to be a painted reading, then requires a second sample to move the reading **and the pixels to differ** — `Buffer.compare(...) !== 0`. **A screenshot rather than the text property, because the property moves whether or not anything repaints**, which is the whole distinction the row is about. **THE ROW'S OWNER POINTER IS INCOMPLETE, AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** The row names `player/src/main.ts`'s `refresh()` — *which drives `hydrateCharts` and `refreshBoundText` and then calls `handle.canvas.requestRenderAll()`* — as the owner. **The repaint on this path is provided twice**: `refreshBoundText` ends with an unconditional `canvas.requestRenderAll()` (`scene-fabric/src/fabric-text.ts:397`), and the player calls it again at `main.ts:174`. **So no single cut disables it.** Measured over four rebuilds: cutting the player's call alone leaves the case **green**, cutting the helper's call alone leaves it **green**, and only cutting **both** turns it **red** — on the pixel assertion, *the reading a sample moved to reached the artboard's pixels*. Either call subsumes the other, which is a fact about the refresh path the row did not have. **A RACE IN THE NEW CASE WAS FOUND DURING THE CONTROLLER'S VERIFICATION AND FIXED IN PLACE (`2f5bd37c`), AND IT IS THE REASON THIS CLOSE DOES NOT SIMPLY REPEAT THE IMPLEMENTER'S RED PROOF.** The case read the clock once after the connection strip disappeared and required a painted reading; the strip disappearing says a batch was **consumed**, not that the repaint carrying the reading has been scheduled and run, so the read raced that frame and saw the placeholder `—`. Measured: it passed at 1.5 s and failed at 319 ms, about two runs in three. **The fix is a poll**, which is the remedy the two assertions three lines below already use. **And the same race is what the implementer's red proof actually observed**: its failure with a single cut was attributed to the cut, and the cut does not produce it. This is the phase's own named failure mode arriving from the other side — not *closing on a case that could not have failed*, but **reading a red as the red you were looking for**. **Two line numbers the row carries are stale, and one of them is stale in the row's own 2026-10-16 correction.** That correction says `installFixedClock`'s sites are `editor.spec.ts:5188`/`:5271` and `openPaused`'s caller is `host-player.spec.ts:923`; **at HEAD they are `:5251`/`:5334` and `:925`** (`openPaused` is defined at `clock.ts:124`). The headline claim the correction was making — that the surviving player case asserts frame *equality* rather than repaint — holds, and the case now beside it asserts the repaint.
check: a spec now asserts the player's update loop reaches the canvas — `host-player.spec.ts:802` drives a live sample and requires the artboard's pixels to differ between two reads, and it is red when both repaint calls are cut and green when either one is

title: A side-handle resize of a scaled text lands its edge tens of scene units away from the edge the pointer asked for
detail:
FOUND while writing the browser check vg-233 and vg-370 asked for (Task 2.1 of the backlog-drain plan), in editor.spec.ts's 'resizes a scaled text by its side handle, and reopens the box it wrote'. THE MEASUREMENT, AS IT STANDS AFTER COMMIT 6cec8acf: the starter wordmark carries scaleX 0.7432 and its mr handle is dragged to a scene x the test names. Dragged to left + 240 the edge now lands within 1.31 scene units of the request -- that drag has LEFT this row, it was the resize path storing width * scaleX, and it is fixed and measured with vg-233 (the 240-unit request landed at 177.58431831416544 before the fix, so it was 62.4156816858345 short (exactly `asked - landed`). CORRECTED 2026-10-12: this row called that landing 'the request times scaleX', and it is not -- 240 x 0.7431987269831705 is 178.36769447596086, 0.78 above it. The equality that IS exact is on the box: the pre-fix `boxAfter` 237.94593984979582 is the post-fix 320.1646224767875 times `scaleX`, so the scaled write shrank the object by exactly `scaleX`). The subject that remains is the OTHER drag in the same case: to left + 0.4 the edge lands at a rendered width of 27.228 where 0.4 was asked, 26.8 scene units away, with the box written 460 -> 35.637 for the ask. WHAT THE FIX DOES NOT EXPLAIN: the sub-unit gap moved from 20.427 to 27.228 -- the pre-fix number times 1/scaleX -- and is still 26.8 units wide, so a wrong stored unit explains neither its size nor its direction. The relation this row flagged for a tracer (the landed rendered width being 0.740 of the request) is therefore explained and closed; the sub-unit landing is not. One number to trace by: the landed Fabric width is 35.637, neither the sub-unit value asked for nor the floor at 1, so the value < 1 refusal is not what decides it. THE HARNESS IS NOT THE SUSPECT: the same helper (resizeRightHandleTo with editor-canvas.ts objectHandleScenePoint) lands group-ram-card's mr handle within 3 units of where the pointer was put in 'snaps a resize onto a neighbour's line', and the test's own askedLanding is the pointer's scene x read back through the canvas' getScenePoint, so the pointer was where the test says it was. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED for this drag: whether Fabric's changeWidth measures a pointer in another frame once a scaled Textbox is near a unit wide, or an editor path re-derives the width after guardBoxWidth restores it, is not traced. OWNER: scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts's guardBoxWidth and the editor's text-manager resize path, whichever the trace lands on. SEVERITY: low for the product -- an author sees the edge stop short and drags again -- but it is why vg-370's sub-unit input could not be reached, so it blocks that row's settlement. EVIDENCE: the pre-fix numbers were identical in every run of that case (three runs, one report retained per run at C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize.json), and the post-fix numbers are from C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json -- both outside the tree, each read from that run's own JSON report.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.3). **The row's own two candidates were tested against a browser trace and one of them is refuted**, which is why this closes on a cause rather than on *cause not established*. **The trace**: instrumenting `canvas.getScenePoint` and the object's `set` against the built editor preview. The 12-step drag goes scene 455.371 → **117.034** in 28.19-unit steps, and the ask (`left + 0.4` = 118.4) is **0.17 client px** at this zoom, where a whole client px is 2.35 scene units. **The whole-pixel pointer Chromium delivers therefore lands *left of the object's own left edge at 118***, where Fabric's `changeObjectWidth` refuses a pointer on the far side of the origin — no write. The width left behind is the **previous step's**: pointer 145.228, local 37.137, width 36.137 after `strokeWidth` 1, landing the rendered edge **145.228 — 26.83 scene units from the ask**, which is the retained report's `landedRight` to six decimals. **Candidate 2 — *an editor path re-derives the width after `guardBoxWidth` restores it* — is REFUTED**: every traced write's requested value equals the value left behind, and the editor's per-step write carries the same number Fabric asked for. **Candidate 1's shape is right but its mechanism is not**: it is not *Fabric measuring a pointer in another frame* but **the previous step of the same drag**, which is a narrower statement and the one that reproduces. **The consequence the row was blocking is now stated rather than left open**: `vg-370`'s `value < 1` refusal floors a box that **a pointer cannot reach at this zoom** — not one that is skipped. That is the settlement `vg-370` needed and did not have. **No red proof, and none is claimed**: this is an investigation, and what changed is the case's own now-false comment (*concludes nothing about its cause*), replaced by the measurement above. **The controller reproduced the row's numbers against the retained report** (`C:/tmp/vg21/vg-233-vg-370-resize-r1.json` holds `145.22846441947564` and `27.228464419475657`, the landed edge and rendered width the row cites). **The implementer's own run reproduced those two exactly while landing on a different Fabric width** (36.137 against the report's 35.637), because its drag ran at `scaleX` 0.73319 where the retained run's was 0.74320 — a difference it reported rather than smoothed, and the mechanism does not depend on the scale.
check: the side-handle resize of a scaled text is traced to the pointer: the ask is 0.4 scene units, which is 0.17 client px at this zoom where a whole client px is 2.35 units, so Chromium's rounded pointer lands left of the object's own edge at scene 118 and Fabric's `changeObjectWidth` refuses, leaving the previous step's width

title: A triage cell's own command can collect nothing and still read as a repro, and three such cells have no owner
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 2.4b task review (2026-10-12), observation 9 of eleven, and filed rather than fixed because the repair is a sweep of every cell rather than one line. WHAT IT IS: each row's triage cell names the command that is supposed to reproduce it. Some of those `--grep` patterns match no case title, so the command exits non-zero with 'No tests found' and proves nothing -- while the cell still reads as a repro a reader will trust. THREE KNOWN INSTANCES, each already recorded on its own row rather than here: `vg-028`'s cell grep collects zero tests; `vg-158`'s cell runs `--grep "delet"` and collected nothing until Task 2.4a added a matching case, the archived row carrying the precedent for recording this on the row; and `vg-259`'s cell runs `--grep "diffuses it by the same amount"` against `glass-circle-parity.spec.ts`, which matches no title -- measured unpiped it exits 1, 'Total: 0 tests in 0 files'. A FOURTH FLAVOUR: `vg-259`'s cell names a config whose viewport is a desktop 1680x1000 while the row's title narrates the phone, so the command it names is not the surface the row is about. A FIFTH: a `--grep` value can match an assertion MESSAGE rather than a case title, so it looks like it collects a case and does not. SCALE: the six tables under `docs/product/triage/` carry 36 `--grep` occurrences, two of them prose mentions rather than commands; how many of the rest collect nothing is NOT established, and establishing it is this row's first task. WHY IT COSTS MORE THAN TIDINESS: a cell that collects nothing returns a red exit that reads like a failing repro, so a reader triaging the row cannot tell it from a command that ran and failed, and no one owns the class. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a sweep running each cell's own command in its `--list` form -- collection only, no browser, no preview port -- correcting each pattern to a real title or recording on the cell that it collects nothing. PATTERN NOTE for that sweep: Playwright compiles `--grep` as `new RegExp(pattern, "gi")`, so a pattern is a case-insensitive regexp, not a literal substring.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.3). **All 27 command values were swept in their own `--list` form** — collection only, no browser, no preview port — and the sweep's scale is corrected rather than inherited. **The row's scale is 36 and the command count is 27, and the difference is the row's own understatement.** Of the 36 `--grep` occurrences, **nine are prose or a column header**, not commands — the row said two. The remaining 27 are 26 distinct values. **Verified by counting both forms**: 36 `--grep` tokens and 27 that carry a quoted value. **Three cells collect nothing, and each is recorded on its own cell rather than left reading as a repro**: `vg-028` (`--grep 'playback'`, and no case title anywhere in `editor.spec.ts` carries it — the row is `verified` in the archive, so there is no title to correct to and the repro needs a new case), `vg-259` (`--grep 'diffuses it by the same amount'`, which is an assertion **message** — Playwright matches titles), and `vg-360` (its case was rewritten). **Two more were loose rather than empty** and were corrected to real titles: `vg-281` (`'New'` matched two titles) and `vg-284` (`'sheet'` matched three). **`vg-259`'s fourth flavour is recorded too**: its cell names a config whose viewport is a desktop 1680×1000 while the row's title narrates the phone, so the command it names is not the surface the row is about. **The instrument is `tests/e2e/triage-cells.test.ts`** (3 cases) and it is the answer to *how many of the rest collect nothing is NOT established*: it reads the six tables' command cells and fails when a value matches no case title and the cell does not say so. **Red-proved by the controller independently**: breaking a corrected value in `triage-B2.md` makes it fail with `triage-B2.md:62 vg-204 --grep '…'`, naming both the file and the row; restored byte-identically by `cmp` and green after. **The static reader agreed with `--list` on every cell**, which is what makes it a cheaper instrument than the sweep rather than a weaker one.
check: every triage cell's own command is now read by an instrument — `tests/e2e/triage-cells.test.ts` fails when a cell's `--grep` value collects no case and the cell does not say so, naming the file and the row, and it does so for `triage-B2.md:62 vg-204` when that value is broken

title: A completed plan still titles a step for the facet rule the shipped query contradicts
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 8.2C'S SEAT WHILE AMENDING THE SPEC (2026-10-13) AND CONFIRMED BY ITS REVIEW. `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog.md:829-834` holds a step titled "keeps untagged entries reachable when a facet is chosen" whose own comment reads "A facet narrows; it never removes an entry that carries no such tag". The shipped `matchesFacet` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/font-catalog-query.ts`) drops exactly those entries -- it is a filter, not a union -- and the spec that plan implemented now says so, because `vg-117` was closed on 2026-10-13 by amending the spec's Facets paragraph and its Browser verification bullet to the shipped rule. THE STEP IS NOT A RED GATE: its assertion is `expect(filtered.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(tagged.length)`, which passes under the strict filter, so nothing fails. CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this is a row rather than a note: a session that executes that step writes a case titled for the superseded rule and names a behaviour the product does not have, which is the same defect class as the spec sentence `vg-117` just corrected. It was left as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `0cd604fe` rather than filed, deliberately, because two other seats were splicing the register and a new id could have collided. NEAR ROWS: `vg-117` (closed), and the drain's Task 9.3, which owns the plans directory answering "what is executable" truthfully. OWNER: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog.md`, with the plans directory as the surface. SEVERITY: low -- documentary, no runnable gate.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.3). **The plan was the stale side and was corrected to the shipped rule**, in both places it states it: the step's title, its comment (*A facet is a filter, not a union: `matchesFacet` keeps a trio only when its own values carry the tag, so an untagged trio is dropped*) and its assertion. **The assertion is the part that mattered, and it is now one that can fail.** The step read `expect(filtered.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(tagged.length)`, which passes under **both** the union the comment claimed and the strict filter the product implements — so a session executing the step would have written a case titled for a rule the product does not have, and nothing would have failed. It now reads `toBe(tagged.length)`, which is false under a union. **The spec side was already the shipped rule**: `font-catalog-query.test.ts`'s *narrows to the entries a facet tags* asserts an exact `toEqual`, and `matchesFacet` (`font-catalog-query.ts:74`) is `values.includes(facet.value)`. So this closes as a documentary correction with **no red proof, and none is manufactured** — the row itself says its step is *not a red gate*, and the honest statement is that the defect was a step that could not fail, which is fixed by making it able to.
check: the plan's step is now titled and asserted for the facet rule the shipped query implements — `narrows to the entries a facet tags`, with `toBe(tagged.length)` in place of the `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual` that passed under either rule, matching `matchesFacet`'s strict filter

title: A spec interpolates a product paint into a stylesheet string, so a renamed key would render `background:undefined` and no assertion would fail
detail:
FOUND BY THE TASK 11.2 REVIEW ON 2026-10-14, WHILE CHECKING THAT A RE-OWNED LITERAL STILL MEANS SOMETHING. `reference-theme.spec.ts` shows the capture it just took by handing the browser a `page.setContent` document whose body is `background:${solidOf.background}` — the value comes from `new-fabric-theme-globals` at run time and is interpolated into a string, so a palette entry that is renamed or absent renders `background:undefined`, which the browser drops as an invalid declaration and the page falls back to white. NOTHING THEN FAILS: `expect(page.locator("img")).toBeVisible()` passes, the length check on the data URL passes, and `captureVisualReview` writes a screenshot that is not a golden file — so the only reader who would notice is a person looking at the wrong-coloured picture. It is the same vacuity `tests/e2e/shell-tokens.ts`'s `themeToken` throws to prevent, in the one place the value is read from a product module instead of a stylesheet the reader parses. OWNER: the spec's own read of `solidOf` — a reader that throws on an absent key, or an assertion that the value is a non-empty string before it is interpolated. SEVERITY: low, because it is a future rename rather than a present defect; the same shape is worth a look wherever a product value is templated into CSS text.
CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.3). **The first of the row's two candidate shapes was taken** — an assertion that the value is a non-empty string before it is interpolated — rather than a reader that throws on an absent key. **The mechanism**: `reference-theme.spec.ts:1401` binds `const backdrop = solidOf.background` and `:1402` asserts `toMatch(/^\S+$/)` with the message *the palette names a solid background*, and `:1404` interpolates **the local** rather than reading the product module inside the template string. So a renamed key now fails at the assertion instead of rendering `background:undefined`, which the browser drops as an invalid declaration while `toBeVisible()`, the data-URL length check and the screenshot all pass. **Why the assertion rather than `shell-tokens.ts`'s throwing `themeToken`**, which is the row's own cited precedent: `themeToken` throws because it parses a **stylesheet** and an absent name there is a bug in the reader; this value comes from a **product module** and there is exactly one consumer, so the guard belongs at the point of use. The precedent is kept where its shape fits rather than copied where it does not. **The row asked whether the same shape appears elsewhere, and the sweep is answered rather than implied**: three sites in the browser suite write CSS text, and **this is the only one that interpolates a product value** — `host-player.spec.ts`'s `setContent` and `shell-palette-tokens.spec.ts`'s `cssText` write literals. **Red-proved by the implementer**: renaming the key fails the assertion with `Received has value: undefined`; restored byte-identically by `cmp`. The controller verified the assertion's shape and position by reading, and did not re-run the browser case.
check: the spec now reads the product paint into a local before interpolating it and asserts it is a non-empty token — a renamed key fails with `Received has value: undefined` instead of rendering `background:undefined` and passing every assertion around it

title: The empty-canvas click helpers probe at fractional coordinates while the browser rounds the click, so a mis-hit can satisfy a position assertion against the wrong menu
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 14.3's review (its finding 4, filed at the controller's ruling), while checking the one helper that task had to change. **The object-menu helper was hardened for this exact hazard and the empty-canvas pair was not:** `editor-context-menu.spec.ts:62-70` (`emptyCanvasPoint`) and `:143-152` (`emptyCanvasPointHigh`) both probe with `rect.left + rect.width * fx` over a 0.02 step and return that point unchanged, while `editorCanvas.findTarget` takes the pointer coordinates as integers — a browser rounds `clientX` to a `long` — so the point they *test* with and the point the click *lands* on differ by up to half a pixel. **WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY: the object menu fails loudly on a mis-hit and the creation menu does not.** A click that rounds onto an object opens the object menu instead, and a case asserting `toContain("Copy")` reds; but the empty-canvas case that reads the *popup's position* ("the menu lands where the pointer was") asserts geometry rather than contents, and the object menu opens at the same place — so the wrong menu satisfies it and the case passes having tested nothing. **NOT FIXED HERE, and it is not this task's:** the two helpers predate Task 14.3, which touched neither of them, and the fix is a decision about the helper (return a rounded point and re-probe at that integer, or assert contents as well as position) rather than a mechanical change. **The reviewer's own re-reading is the reason it was found rather than assumed** — the task's report claimed the pair was "not exposed to this", which is a mitigation and not a proof. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.4, step 4) at `be7cad93`, and the close takes candidate 1 rather than candidate 2: the helpers round the candidate and then probe at that rounded point, which REMOVES the hazard, where asserting the menu's contents as well would have left the mis-hit in place and only made the case notice it. The same file's `objectPoint` has rounded-then-probed since 2026-10-15, so this is the file's own idiom rather than a new one. THE HAZARD IS REAL AND WAS NOT REACHABLE: a 0.002-step scan of the starter returns empty points whose rounding is not empty — 440.096, 60.64 rounds to 440, 61; 845.936, 60.64 rounds to 846, 61; 437.248, 84.872 rounds to 437, 85 — and the helper's own 0.02 grid lands on none of them, which is why no live mis-hit existed before the fix. The seat's red proof was a temporary contract case, run and deleted; the controller did not re-take that red and says so rather than implying a proof that is not in the tree. The four affected e2e files read 130 passed exit 0.
check: both empty-canvas click helpers round the candidate and then probe at that rounded point, so the point a case tests is the point the browser clicks; the four affected e2e files read 130 passed exit 0, editor-context-menu.spec.ts's 3 cases among them. The hazard is latent at the helpers' 0.02 grid, so no committed case reddens with the fix disabled and the seat's red proof was a temporary case — said rather than left implied

title: Two editor.spec.ts cases fail consistently at a second navigation, blocked by the unsaved-draft prompt rather than by a missing canvas
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 12.4a's independent task reviewer, as an extra check the implementer never ran: it ran `editor.spec.ts` because a plain layer-row click is the path `vg-056` touched. It did not file a row and flagged it for the controller instead, which is the right division — it was reviewing, not fixing. THE MEASUREMENT: `editor.spec.ts` under `desktop-chromium` reads **6 failed / 61 passed**. Four of the six were load flakes and passed on re-run; **two fail consistently**, at the second `page.goto(EDITOR)` inside their own case, and what blocks them is the unsaved-draft dialog (`packages/editor/src/draft-recovery-prompt.tsx`, whose copy is `uiCopy.draftRecovery`) rather than a canvas that did not mount. The spec navigates 69 times, so a case that dirties the document and then navigates again is the shape to look for. THE CONTROL, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AS PRE-EXISTING RATHER THAN AS 12.4a's: the reviewer reverted `editor-shell/bridge.ts` and `panes/composition/composition-pane.tsx` to the parent commit `7728dfbd`, rebuilt, and re-ran — **the same two failed identically**. It then restored both, with `cmp` exit 0 on each, and left the tree byte-identical to HEAD. So the pair is not caused by the multi-selection work and predates it. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED BEYOND THAT: the reviewer named the prompt as what blocks the navigation, which the control supports, but it did not establish whether the correct reading is that those two cases should dismiss the prompt, that the prompt should not appear on a fresh navigation, or that the cases dirty the document in a way they should not. That third reading would make this a product defect rather than a test defect, and telling them apart needs the cases read against `draft-store.ts`'s commit rules. WHY A ROW AND NOT A FIX: the cause is not established to `file:line` for the correct-behaviour half, more than one owner could fix it (the spec's own navigation helper, the prompt's trigger condition, or the draft store), and which of the three readings holds is a decision rather than a correction. TWO NEAR ROWS, NEITHER OF WHICH IS THIS ONE: `vg-511` and `vg-512` are both open and both about the draft-restore path's own behaviour — a refused restore being announced and then overwritten, and the draft slot holding one document — so they touch the same component and are not duplicates of a pair of failing cases. NOT VERIFIED BY THE CONTROLLER: the failing line numbers and the re-run split are the reviewer's, taken from its own run and its own control; the controller confirmed only that `draft-recovery-prompt.tsx` exists at that path, that `uiCopy.draftRecovery` supplies its copy, and that `editor.spec.ts` navigates 69 times.

HALF OF THIS PAIR IS NOW FIXED, 2026-10-15, BY TASK 12.4D'S FIX ROUND R1 (commit `7d3b3afa`), AND THE FIX TOOK ONE OF THE THREE READINGS THIS ROW SAID NEEDED A DECISION. Repairing the no-snap aim in `editor.spec.ts`'s "snaps a resized object to a neighbour and shows a guide" made that case reach its second `page.goto(EDITOR)` for the first time, and it then failed exactly as this row describes: the canvas assertion timed out and the page snapshot showed the unsaved-draft dialog. **The reading taken is the first of the three** — those cases should dismiss the prompt — implemented as `answerDialogIfShown(page, "Discard")` after that navigation, which is the same answer `composition-panel.spec.ts`, `rebuild-driver.ts` and `editor-display.spec.ts` already give at their own reloads. The round's own justification for taking it rather than asking: the answer is already specified elsewhere in the suite, so it is not a new decision, and without it the fix it was dispatched for could not be shown green at all. **WHAT THAT LEAVES OPEN, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW IS NOT CLOSED:** (1) the other case of the two was not named and not touched — the round fixed the one case the finding led it to and said so; (2) whether reading one is the right answer **everywhere** is still the sweep the row describes, and it now has a precedent to follow rather than a question about which of three readings to take; (3) the round could not date the breakage, and neither could this row, because the pre-widening tree aborts before the reload is ever reached — so "pre-existing" still rests on the earlier reviewer's `7728dfbd` control rather than on anything measured since. **NOT VERIFIED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MEASURED HERE:** how many of the pair still fail. `editor.spec.ts` as a whole has not been re-run since `7d3b3afa` — Task 12.4f holds the browser and the shared `dist`, so the controller did not run it — and the round's own runs were of the single repaired case and of `snapping.spec.ts`. Whoever takes this row should run `editor.spec.ts` under `desktop-chromium` first and start from what it reads now.
EVIDENCE ADDED 2026-10-16 (Phase 15, Task 15.5), from a browser run for an unrelated row: **`inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s "gives every kind a column, and shows no kind a property it lacks" fails on `develop`**, alone and in its file, blocked at its second `page.goto(EDITOR)` by the unsaved-draft dialog (`draft-recovery-prompt.tsx`). That is this row's shape in a third file — `editor.spec.ts`'s two, `snapping.spec.ts`'s, and now this one — which is the sweep the row describes rather than a new finding, so it is recorded here and not filed as a row of its own. The case's body was untouched by that task's commits.
EVIDENCE ADDED 2026-10-16 (Phase 16, Task 16.4), from a run taken that reproduces both browser reds at the base commit with the task's changes stashed and rebuilt: **`editor.spec.ts:4012`'s `Ctrl-resizes near a neighbour…` fails alone as well as in its file**, and what the run saw is `#yunari-fabric-editor canvas.upper-canvas` never appearing. **WHETHER THAT IS THIS ROW'S SECOND CASE OR A DIFFERENT DEFECT IS NOT ESTABLISHED**, and the discriminator was not captured: this row's shape is the canvas assertion timing out **with the unsaved-draft dialog in the page snapshot**, and the run recorded the missing canvas without recording the snapshot. It is recorded here rather than filed as a row of its own on the same reasoning the `inspector-sections.spec.ts` addition below used — this row is already the sweep for that shape in `editor.spec.ts`, and a case of it is a naming of what the row could not name rather than a new finding. **If a later reading shows no dialog, that reading makes this a canvas-mount defect and a row of its own.** This row's own instruction stands: run `editor.spec.ts` under `desktop-chromium` first and start from what it reads now. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.4, step 5) at `31f6865d`, AND THE CONTROLLER'S RE-RUN CORRECTS THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE. THE SWEEP IS DONE AND ITS SCOPE IS MEASURED: `playwright test --list` gives real case boundaries, and exactly two cases in the named files hold a second navigation — `editor.spec.ts`'s Ctrl-resizes and `inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s gives-every-kind-a-column, the third-file instance this row already recorded. `snapping.spec.ts`'s two `page.goto` sites are both in fixture helpers called once per case, so no case there navigates twice, and `editor-context-menu.spec.ts` has one navigation per case. Both now answer the prompt. THE RED IS ONE CASE, NOT TWO: with the dismiss removed, `inspector-sections.spec.ts`'s case is red deterministically — exit 1, a 30 s timeout, the draft dialog in the snapshot — and `editor.spec.ts`'s own Ctrl-resizes case PASSES, alone and in its file, in two controller runs. What the missing dismiss does there is land on a LATER case: twice, identically, the file read 68 passed / 1 failed with `captures the theme-library chooser over a stubbed library for visual review` failing at `[role=dialog]` filtered by Open a theme, element not found — and that case passes alone at HEAD, so the leftover prompt from the earlier case is what breaks it. So `fail consistently` is true of the `inspector-sections.spec.ts` case and false of the `editor.spec.ts` one, whose damage is downstream of it. WHY THAT IS NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT: `answerDialogIfShown`'s own owner states it — the dirty guard resolves before it asks, so some rounds ask and some do not — which is why the case can pass with no prompt at all and why the fix is conditional by design rather than by accident. Green with the fix: the four affected files read 130 passed exit 0. STILL OPEN AND NOT THIS ROW'S: the third reading — whether a fresh navigation should be offered a draft at all — is untouched, and this row's own text already says which of the three readings was taken.
check: the sweep found exactly two cases in the named files that hold a second navigation and both now answer the draft prompt; inspector-sections.spec.ts's case is red without the dismiss — exit 1, the prompt in the snapshot — while editor.spec.ts's own case passes with the dismiss removed and the missing dismiss breaks a later case instead, 130 passed exit 0 across the four affected files

title: The acceptance instrument renders its own text at a line-height DESIGN.md does not state, and no reader reads the property, so the drawings show a rhythm the design language does not
detail: FOUND 2026-10-13, as the residue of `vg-437` once that row's product half was fixed. **MEASURED, in a browser, every drawing in `current/`.** Each of the six was loaded in Chromium and every element holding its own text was tallied by resolved `font-size`/`line-height`: 12px text renders at 17.4px (1.450) in `settings-about.html` (7 elements), `settings-keyboard.html` (24), `settings.html` (4) and `shell.html` (7); 11px text renders at 15.95px (1.45) in `controls.html` and `controls-light.html` (12 each), `shell.html` (12) and `settings.html` (7). Not one element in any drawing renders at a ratio DESIGN.md states. Elements whose computed line-height was `normal` were excluded rather than counted, so these are explicit values only and the drawings hold more text than the tally shows. **WHERE THE RATIO COMES FROM.** `settings-about.html:10` declares `font: 12px/1.45` in the file's `<style>` block - the page body - and the modal inside it declares no line-height of its own, so every drawn element inherits 1.45. Section 2's companions are 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.3, 1.3 and 1.2 for 10, 11, 12, 13, 15 and 19px, so 1.45 is on none of them. **WHY THE DRAWING IS THE STALE SIDE AND NOT THE COMPETING RULE.** The drawings README states the precedence in its own words: 'Where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins and the file is stale.' `design-language.spec.ts:3058-3065` adds that the page furniture 'is read like everything else' and passes today only because its values happen to be on the scale - so a furniture value off the scale was always going to redden that row, and does not only because `design-language.spec.ts:3054-3057` reads no line-height at all and states that limit as dispositioned. `vg-437`'s product half was fixed on 2026-10-13 against section 2, which leaves the instrument as the only side still rendering 1.45. **WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT AN EDIT.** The correction is not one value: section 2 gives each size its own companion, and a single page-body ratio cannot express six of them, so each drawn text element would have to state the ratio for the token it already uses - six files, every text element in each, and it changes the rendered rhythm of the thing this project compares the product against. It also cannot be verified by the gate that reads these files, because that gate reads no line-height. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT.** The furniture stops carrying a ratio and each drawn element states its token's companion, in the same commit as any re-shoot of the frames beside it - which nothing currently does (`vg-402`). **OWNER.** The drawings are the acceptance instrument the user ruled on 2026-10-10 (`STATUS.md`), so correcting them is that owner's act; a gate change that could see the property is a separate one and is named here rather than assumed. NEAR ROWS: `vg-437` (the product half, landed), `vg-326` (the same files' line-height from section 3's side, whose 'sets no line-height' clause this measurement corrects), `vg-402` (the stale frames). CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 17, Task 17.5, step 2) at `ffabe6ff`, both halves of its close condition met. THE FURNITURE NO LONGER CARRIES A RATIO and every drawn element states the companion §2 gives its size: `body { … font: 12px system-ui … }` in all six, and 284 text-holding elements re-derived in Chromium at 0 off their token's companion, against 278 of 284 before — 13 elements with no `style` attribute gained one, 54 `font-size` longhands gained a `line-height`, 150 `font` shorthands took the ratio on their size token, and 67 inherited one. RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY WITHOUT A BROWSER and it holds: of the elements that declare a size, 245 declare one and 0 state no line-height, 0 state a ratio off §2's companion, and all six furniture blocks are ratio-free. The product's own `--text-*--line-height` companions in `editor-shell.css` are 1.2/1.3/1.4/1.3/1.3/1.2, the same table, so the drawings now agree with §2 and with the product where they previously agreed with neither. THE RE-SHOOT CLAUSE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the frames beside the drawings are PRODUCT captures, not renders of the drawings — `settings-capture-graphite.png` is 408x304 where the drawn modal is 560px wide — so a correction to a drawing's own rhythm does not stale them, nothing was re-shot, and `vg-402` is untouched. The change is not invisible to the instrument: `mockup-parity.ts`'s two keyboard chord-mark rows address their element by a substring selector carrying the drawing's old `font:400 11px/1.2`, so `design-language-parity.spec.ts` failed with `the drawing addresses nothing with [style*=…11px/1.2…]: this row names a selector the drawing does not declare` — read and restored, and both selectors follow the drawing. That red proves the drawing moved, not that the line-height was wrong, and it is said that way. NO ARM READS `line-height` AND NONE IS CLAIMED: the drawings gate still does not read it, and the gate's own comment now records that it is the one of the three it leaves unread while the drawings state it. ONE THING THIS OVERRODE, RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE REDISCOVERED: 25 eyebrows drawn `/1`, a 1.5 reading rhythm on the controls hint line, a 13px/1.2 section title and a 13px/1 brand mark all carried a deliberate per-element ratio and now state §2's companion. The row's condition is literal about each element stating its token's companion and §2 is normative, so this is what it asks — but it is a design act, and no gate reads the property, so nothing else will catch it if the drawing owner disagrees.
check: every text-holding element in the six checked drawings states the companion section 2 gives its size and the page furniture carries no ratio — re-derived independently, 245 elements declare a size, 0 without a line-height and 0 off their token's companion, all six furniture blocks ratio-free, against 278 of 284 before; the frames beside the drawings are product captures rather than renders of them, 408x304 where the drawn modal is 560px wide, so no re-shoot was owed. No arm reads line-height and none is claimed; the red proof is mockup-parity.ts's two chord-mark selectors following the drawing

title: The Appearance pane's region label is drawn 12px sentence case where section 2 reserves the eyebrow shape for a region label
detail: FOUND 2026-10-15 by Task 10.2's independent task review, as the residue of that task's first part, and filed as the `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in `8c4c79b9`. MEASURED: `docs/design/mockups/current/settings.html:42` draws the pane's heading as `font:600 12px/1 system-ui;margin-bottom:10px` — sentence case, no letter-spacing, 12px — while `docs/design/mockups/current/settings-keyboard.html:54` draws the other tabs' group headings as `font:600 10px/1.2 system-ui;letter-spacing:.11em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--muted)`. Both are the same element in the product: `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/settings.tsx:154` renders `<h3 id={PALETTE_GROUP_ID}>`, which `.editor-shell-dialog h3` styles once, so the two drawings disagree about one rule. Section 2 decides which side is stale: "Uppercase is reserved for section eyebrows … An eyebrow is `--text-2xs`, `600`, `letter-spacing: .11em`, muted, and it always labels a region, never a control. Nothing else is uppercase." title: A refused colour in the Tokens pane is announced to nobody, and the control set has no channel for an invalid-but-still-editable field
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 5 TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10, commit ebe1743b), NOT BY A FAILING TEST - and that is half the finding. THE REGRESSION: before Task 5 the pane relied on the platform's own refusal, `reportValidity()` on the colour input, which announced itself to assistive technology for free. Task 5 replaced it with a local error state rendered as a bare `

` (paint-list.tsx:254-258) that is a SIBLING of the field it belongs to (the ControlText at paint-list.tsx:232-253) and is associated with nothing: no `aria-describedby`, no `aria-invalid`, no live region. A screen-reader user types an unpaintable colour, the edit is refused, and the refusal is silent. WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE: the control set already has this mechanism - control-well.tsx renders a reason element and control-text.tsx:70-71 wires `aria-describedby` to it - but it is reachable only through the `refused` prop, and `refused` also sets `readOnly` (control-text.tsx:68) and `aria-disabled`. That is right for a value the DOCUMENT refuses (a locked object) and wrong here: this value is refused because the author just typed something the engine cannot paint, and the field has to stay editable so they can type a different one. Using `refused` would trap them on the stale-but-valid value. Nor can the pane wire it itself: `ControlProps.data` is typed `Readonly>` (control-well.tsx:24-32), so there is no aria pass-through, and the pane does not own the input element. THE REAL FIX IS A CONTROL-SET CONCEPT - a channel for invalid-but-still-editable, distinct from `refused`, carrying `aria-invalid` plus a described-by reason without `readOnly`. That is why this is filed rather than fixed on the fly (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a new concept in a different owner - the control set, built and closed in plan 1 - it spans subsystems, and it needs a design decision about how many refusal shapes the control set should carry. It is not Task 5's to invent, and a second ad-hoc `

` in the next pane would make three. THE TEST GAP THAT LET IT THROUGH: tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts:672-697 proves the refusal HAPPENS (not-a-colour is refused, the field stays on #123456, rgb(1, 2, 3) clears it) but never that it is announced, and jsdom cannot see platform bubbles either - so neither layer could have gone red. CLOSE THIS by adding the editable-invalid channel to the control set, wiring the Tokens pane's colour field to it, and pinning that a refused value carries `aria-invalid` and a described-by reason while remaining editable. RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE CONTROL SET GAINS THE CHANNEL. A value that is invalid but still editable becomes a named member of the control set rather than the platform's reportValidity() carrying it, so the state is expressed and reviewed the way every other control state is, instead of being whatever the browser does. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.1, step 3) at `ee82150a`, on the ruling's own terms: **an invalid-but-editable value is a named member of the control set**, `ControlProps.invalid`, and it is distinct from `refused` — the distinction the set now carries is **who refused**, the document (blocking) or the engine (editable), not how loudly. `ControlText` gained `aria-invalid` and an `aria-describedby` reason and stays editable; the reason element is one `ControlReason` in `control-well.tsx`, which `ControlNumber` renders too, so the two fields cannot drift; and `panes/tokens/paint-list.tsx` passes its refusal through the channel and its bare `

` is deleted. **THE ROW ASKED TO INVENT WHAT ALREADY EXISTED**: `ControlNumber` has carried this channel since `e3b19da4`, so the work was generalising it, which is what decision note `0056` records and why it is smaller than the row reads. VERIFIED IN CHROMIUM, which the row's own close condition requires and jsdom cannot see: `tests/e2e/editor.spec.ts:981`'s palette case, rebuilt bundle, `--project=desktop-chromium --workers=1`, **1 passed exit 0** — the field carries `aria-invalid="true"` and the element its `aria-describedby` names reads the refusal, while the field still holds the document's colour. The locator moved off the deleted attribute to that pair, which is the honest replacement: the old one asserted a sibling existed, the new one asserts the field is described. RED-PROVED on the control's own case (2 failed, exit 1, with the fix disabled). **NO LIVE REGION, AND THAT IS THE ECOSYSTEM'S RULE RATHER THAN AN OMISSION** — the node is already the field's `aria-describedby` target, so an `aria-live` on it would announce every refusal twice; the row's wording asks for the absence of an announcement and is corrected by note `0056` rather than implemented literally. ONE THING THIS LANDING MADE VISIBLE IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED, because its fix is a design decision and more than one owner could take it: **`vg-545`** — the reason is sticky when the author edits back to the value the document already holds, since the control declines to report a commit that changes nothing and `invalid` is a prop it cannot clear.
check: a refused colour in the Tokens pane is announced through the control set's invalid channel: the field carries aria-invalid and an aria-describedby reason while staying editable, verified in Chromium at ee82150a by editor.spec.ts's palette case, 1 passed exit 0, on a rebuilt bundle; red-proved with the fix disabled at 2 failed exit 1

title: The React control set prints its refusals in hardcoded English, so a pane's own invalid-value copy became unreachable
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 4 TASK 8 (2026-10-10, commit 9f6252a8) IN TASK REVIEW, AND FIRST FILED WRONGLY - this row replaces a framing that was measured false, and the correction is the reason it reads as narrowly as it does. THE FINDING: `ControlNumber` (components/ui/control-number.tsx:94,99,103,107,111) writes its five refusal sentences as hardcoded English - "a value is required", "not a number", "a whole number", "at least 1", "at most 16384" - while every other user-visible string in the editor comes from `uiCopy`. The control it replaced took its message as a parameter defaulting to `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` (number-field.ts:88), so the artboard size pair used to say "That value cannot be applied. Enter a number in range." (ui-copy.ts:650) and now says "at most 16384". That key is not dead - it is still read by number-field.ts:88, reachable only from the settings path (settings-field.ts:115 is `numberField`'s only shipped caller) - so one editor now carries two vocabularies for one refusal depending on which numeric control a surface happens to use. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED ON THE FLY (AGENTS.md): the cause is established but the fix is a design decision in a different owner - the copy rules are plan 6's and the control set is plan 1's, built and closed - and neither side obviously moves: `ControlNumber` could take its message from `uiCopy` (a new key, and a copy dependency the control set does not have today), or `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` could be retired and the hardcoded strings promoted into it (the copy module acquiring keys only one control uses). WHY THE FIRST FILING WAS WRONG, because the mistake is the useful part: I filed this as "a number field no longer says what it will accept until after a value is refused", asserting the old pane printed its bound (1-16384) at rest. It did not. `boundLine` is rendered only by `numberField` (number-field.ts:53-59), and the artboard pane used `linkedPair` (artboard-panel.ts:19,150 at 21a5135e), which calls `numberInput` directly (linked-pair.ts:1,55,66) - so no artboard author ever saw that line and the discoverability loss described did not occur. The task reviewer measured it three ways (`git log -S` over the file's whole history finds no `numberField`/`boundLine`/`field-bound`; the pane's own old tests never mention them; settings-field.ts is `numberField`'s only caller) and the controller re-read linked-pair.ts to confirm. The implementer's report Deviation 4 made the same claim, so a subagent's description of code it had already replaced became a register row unmeasured - a verify-the-claim failure, not a reasoning one, and the check that catches it is one grep of the base commit. Related: vg-113 (unit display options hardcoded English), vg-263 (a refused colour announced to nobody - the other half of the same question, what the control set owes an author whose value it will not take).

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE CONTROL SET TAKES ITS REFUSAL COPY FROM uiCopy. uiCopy is the repos one owner for user-visible strings and it carries a copy census, so a shared control printing hardcoded English is the drift that census exists to prevent; the control set gains a copy dependency and each consumer supplies its strings through the locale the shell already sets. The rows other half is corrected rather than ruled: the panes own invalid-value copy was never unreachable because it never existed -- the task reviewer measured it three ways -- so the live question is this one only. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.1, step 1) at `ee82150a`, and the fix is the one the ruling chose: `ControlNumber`'s five refusal sentences read `uiCopy.controls` — `valueRequired`, `notANumber`, `wholeNumber`, `atLeast(min)`, `atMost(max)` — instead of hardcoded English, so the shared control set has a copy dependency on the repo's one owner for user-visible strings. THE WORDS ARE UNCHANGED, WHICH IS WHY NO ASSERTION MOVED: every existing reading of them (`control.dom.test.tsx`, `design-language-readers.ts:543`, `glass-authoring.spec.ts:333,342`, `inspector-sections.spec.ts:589,1097`, `panel.dom.test.ts:378,409`) still holds, and `packages/editor` reads 1946 passed exit 0. NO RED PROOF IS CLAIMED AND NONE WOULD BE HONEST: the words are identical, so a case can only redden against a *changed* literal, not against the indirection being removed — the indirection is what the ruling asked for and what the copy census reads. THE ROW'S LINE NUMBERS ARE STALE and were corrected before the write: the five strings were at `:105,110,114,118,122`, not `:94,99,103,107,111`. `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` was NOT touched — its only reader is `editor-shell/controls/number-field.ts:87`, a different control set outside the task's Files line, and the ruling moved `ControlNumber`'s copy into the table rather than unifying two wordings. That second wording is filed as **`vg-546`**: `uiCopy.panels.invalidNumber` is still read by `editor-shell/controls/number-field.ts:87`, so one editor carries two vocabularies for a refused number, and the direction to unify them is a design decision the ruling deliberately did not take.
check: the React control set's refusal sentences read the new uiCopy.controls keys — valueRequired, notANumber, wholeNumber, atLeast and atMost — so a shared control no longer prints hardcoded English: the five words are unchanged, packages/editor reads 1946 passed exit 0, and the focused control-set and copy suites read 85 passed exit 0. No red proof is claimed because the words are identical and only a changed literal could redden a case

title: The colour picker's four track sliders announce their test id, so a screen reader reads out a CSS-selector-shaped token instead of a word
detail:
SURFACED BY PLAN 6 TASK 5'S REVIEW (2026-10-11) while adjudicating the copy walk's skip rule, and it is THE ROW `vg-194` HANDED OFF AND NOBODY FILED: that verified row's own closing paragraph ends 'each track's `aria-label` is its `testId`, so what a screen reader announces is `picker-saturation, slider, 0`, and the words an author would want are a copy decision rather than a mechanism one. That is a separate row, not a reopening of this one.' This is that row; the mechanism half `vg-194` owned is done and is not re-opened by it. THE MEASUREMENT: `components/ui/colour-picker.tsx`'s `Track` renders `aria-label={testId}`, so each of the four tracks (the saturation/brightness area, hue, and the two strips) has an accessible name of `picker-saturation`, `picker-hue` and so on -- a token shaped like a selector rather than a word. `vg-194` closed the keyboard path and the declared `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` in the same component, so the value announcement is sound; what a person hears first is the name, and the name is the defect. WHY THE COPY WALK DOES NOT CATCH IT, which is the part worth recording: the walk's rule skips any element whose `aria-label` equals its `data-testid`, and the reviewer ruled that rule CORRECT -- a driver's hook is not a word a translator would change, and forcing these into `uiCopy` would be wrong. So the net is right to skip them and the label is still wrong: the two facts are independent, and the skip rule must not be weakened to catch this. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: each track's `aria-label` reads a word from `uiCopy` (`Saturation`, `Hue`, `Alpha`, `Value`) while the `data-testid` hooks keep their current values, so the skip rule stays and the announced name becomes a word. The wording is a copy decision, which is why it is not an agent's to take silently. RELATED: `vg-194` (verified, archived) is the row that identified this and deferred it; `vg-179` is an unrelated picker row.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE FOUR PICKER TRACKS ANNOUNCE Saturation, Hue, Alpha AND Value FROM uiCopy, and they keep their current data-testid hooks so the specs that address them do not move. The reasoning is vg-264s: user-visible strings come from the copy owner, and an accessible name is user-visible text. COST IF WRONG: four strings move into the copy catalogue and the census grows by four keys, which is what that census is for. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.1, step 2) at `ee82150a`. `Track` gained a `label` prop and the four tracks announce `uiCopy.panels.pickerSaturation`, `pickerValue`, `pickerHue` and `pickerAlpha`, while keeping their `data-testid` hooks (`picker-saturation`, `picker-value`, `picker-hue`, `picker-alpha`) — so the specs that address them did not move, which was the ruling's condition. THE COPY WALK'S SKIP RULE IS UNTOUCHED, as the row required: `ui-copy-readers.ts` still skips any element whose `aria-label` equals its `data-testid`, and the two facts are now independent rather than in conflict. RED-PROVED: with the fix disabled, `colour-picker.dom.test.tsx` and `paint-list.dom.test.tsx` read 14 passed / 2 failed, exit 1, and both failures are the new cases; restored, the focused control-set and copy suites read 85 passed exit 0.
