title: isTextEntryTarget counts a range input as a text-entry target, so the manager's deferred chords are swallowed while a slider has focus
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 7 (fix round 1, commit 4bf29bf6), which added it as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer. `isTextEntryTarget` (src/web/packages/editor/src/shortcut-manager/index.ts:192-213) returns true for any HTMLInputElement whose type is not in a small exclusion set - button, checkbox, color, file, image, radio, reset, submit (:202-211). `range` is not in that set, so a focused input[type=range] is treated as a text-entry target, the handler at :143-147 sets `deferred`, and the manager returns before preventDefault() and before the bound handler. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS WIDER THAN THE TRAILER AND THE COMMIT MESSAGE SAY: both name Ctrl+Z (undo swallowed while a slider has focus), but the predicate gates EVERY action the shortcut table binds, so Delete, Escape and the rest are swallowed too. The controller verified the cause at source rather than taking the trailer's word for it. WHY THE FIX IS NOT JUST ADDING range TO THE SET: the same predicate guards the bare-key canvas listeners (camera keys), so a range was presumably left in deliberately - an unmodified arrow on a focused slider must move the slider, not the camera. Ctrl+Z is a modifier chord with no native meaning on a range, so it should reach the manager while an unmodified arrow should not. That makes the repair a decision about which keys a non-text control still defers, not a one-line set edit. AUTHOR-FACING AND REACHABLE: click the slider, press Ctrl+Z, nothing happens. BLAST RADIUS: every ControlSlider the plan-1 control set renders, which after this plan is polygon sides, the shape sweep pair and glass blur. NOT FIXED HERE because the owner is shortcut-manager and the task that found it is the inspector, and the correct behaviour is a ruling rather than a patch.

RULED 2026-10-12: The predicate is wrong in KIND, not in membership: it answers "is this target a text-entry target" where the question is "does this target consume this key". A text field consumes everything printable, so the coarse question happens to work there; a range consumes its own navigation keys and nothing else, so a modifier chord must reach the manager while an unmodified arrow stays with the slider. The repair is a consumption rule per target shape, enumerated as data beside the control set that owns those shapes: a text-like target consumes printable keys, a range consumes exactly the keys it natively handles (the four arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down), and every other control consumes nothing. That keeps the camera keys on a focused slider — which is why a range was in the set deliberately — and gives Ctrl+Z back, which is the half the row measured as broken. Enumerated rather than inferred so a control the set gains later states what it consumes instead of inheriting a default nobody chose.

SECTION 8.10 REFUTED 2026-10-16, AND THE CORRECTION WAS NOT APPLIED. The plan's drift table says this row's premise is "half-false — the deferral is action-scoped, not 'every action'" and orders the title's `every shortcut the manager owns` softened. **The row's own detail says the opposite, and says it as a measurement rather than an inference**: "the predicate gates EVERY action the shortcut table binds, so Delete, Escape and the rest are swallowed too", marked as verified at source by the controller rather than taken from the trailer. The ruling on this row agrees and goes further — the predicate is wrong in KIND, and what is wrong is *which keys* a target defers, not whether the deferral is broad. So the premise holds and the title is accurate as written; **applying §8.10 would have written a false statement into the register.** Left standing deliberately. ONE CLAIM IN THIS ROW IS OVERSTATED AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN CARRIED, found by Task 18.3's seat (2026-10-16) reading the deferral rather than repeating the row. THE ROW SAYS the predicate "gates EVERY action the shortcut table binds, so Delete, Escape and the rest are swallowed too". **The deferral is action-scoped for modified chords**: `MODIFIED_KEY_DEFERRED_ACTION_IDS` (shortcut-manager/index.ts:126-127) holds four ids — `file.new`, `edit.undo`, `edit.redo`, `canvas.select-all` — and the deferral at `:184-188` is `(!binding.modifier || MODIFIED_KEY_DEFERRED_ACTION_IDS.has(binding.action)) && <the target question>`. So a focused range never swallowed `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+O` or `Ctrl+D`, and what it did swallow is narrower than "every action": the four listed actions' modified chords, plus every unmodified binding (Delete, Backspace, the arrows, `?`, Escape) — which is the half the row measured correctly. **The plan's §8.10 correction was right on this narrow point and this row's rebuttal of it was not.** It changes nothing about the defect or the fix — the predicate was still the wrong question and `Ctrl+Z` was still swallowed — so the row closes as ruled; only the breadth claim moves. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.3, step 1) at `c0b0ceb7`. **The deferral asks per key now**: `consumesKey(target, event)` owns the question (shortcut-manager/index.ts:291), the deferral at `:188` reads it, a range consumes exactly `RANGE_CONSUMED_KEYS` — the four arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Page Down — and **no modifier chord whatever the key**, since `Ctrl+ArrowLeft` is the browser's word-jump rather than a step. Everything else falls through to `isTextEntryTarget`, which keeps its membership for the camera's guard. **THE SHAPE CHOSEN, WHICH THE BRIEF ASKED FOR AND WHICH IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE**: the consumption rule became the deferral's owner, the coarse predicate was left alone for the camera, and `activatesOnSpace` was given its own stated rule — because **the third call site was not asking a third question at all**. `viewport-manager/navigation.ts:56`'s `!isTextEntryTarget(target)` was unreachable behind a tautology: the guard at `:182-186` tests the same target first, so every `<input>` reaching `:56` already has `isTextEntryTarget` false. It is now `return true` with the reason written down, and the change moves no camera behaviour at all. **STEP 1'S LITERAL RULE COULD NOT BE IMPLEMENTED AND THE PLAN IS CORRECTED**: "a text-like target consumes printable keys" fails three existing cases (`index.dom.test.ts:214` Delete on a textarea, `:382` Escape, `:323` ArrowLeft), so the implemented rule is "a text field consumes every key the table binds" — printable characters are its own, and Delete, the arrows and Escape are its editing keys. That is the honest reading of why the coarse question happened to work there. RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER, on both layers: cutting the deferral back to `isTextEntryTarget` reads **1 failed / 70 passed, exit 1**, and the browser case that presses `Ctrl+Z` with the track still focused reads **1 unexpected, `toHaveValue("1")` receiving `"3"`** on the range input; restored byte-identically (proved with `cmp`) the suite reads **71 passed, exit 0** and the rebuilt bundle's browser run is green. **THE BROWSER HALF IS THE ROW'S OWN REPRODUCTION** — `editor.spec.ts` used to blur the focused control before pressing the chord, and its comment explained that the range swallowed it; **that blur block was already a no-op**, because `typeIntoControl` fills *and blurs* a range (`control-set.ts:225-227`), so nothing was focused and the comment's premise did not hold on this tree. The chord is now pressed with the track still focused, which is what the row measured.
check: a slider takes back the chords it has no use for: with the deferral cut back to the coarse predicate, a modifier chord over a focused range stops reaching the shortcut manager's handler — 1 failed of 71 at exit 1, restored byte-identically with cmp to 71 passed exit 0 — and the browser case that presses the chord with the track still focused reads 1 unexpected, the range taking 3 where it should hold 1

title: RESERVED_LETTERS refuses a bare-modifier chord but not its Shift variant, so Ctrl+Shift+T, N and W are accepted as bindings and can never fire
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5'S WHOLE-BRANCH FINAL REVIEW, range 13370dc5..95a9bd11, and confirmed at source. shortcut-manager/bindings.ts:75 lists the reserved letters (l, n, p, q, r, t, w) and :299-305 refuses one only when `binding.modifier && binding.shift !== true`, so every Shift variant of those letters passes validation and is stored as a binding the browser owns: Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen closed tab), Ctrl+Shift+N (new private window) and Ctrl+Shift+W (close window) are taken in every Chromium build, so the author binds a chord and nothing ever happens. The rule's own doc comment states the Shift exclusion as fact without stating why, which is the claim-without-a-reason shape this plan hit repeatedly. CONSEQUENCE: the refusal exists precisely so the author is told where the limit is rather than binding a chord that will never fire, and it does not cover the case that is most likely to be tried. NOT FIXED IN THE PLAN'S FINAL FIX ROUND because the correct membership is a data decision - which chords the editor's actual browser matrix reserves - and over-refusing is its own defect (it would reject chords that do work). What would settle it: state which browsers the editor runs in, measure the Shift variants against them, and make the reserved rule and its comment reflect that evidence.

RULED 2026-10-12: A DEFECT, and the Shift exclusion is backwards: three of the four chords most likely to be tried are exactly the Shift variants the browser keeps, so the rule misses the case its own comment says it exists to catch. The rule becomes TWO sets rather than one guarded by `shift !== true` — the letters reserved with a modifier and no Shift, unchanged, and the letters whose SHIFT variant is reserved too — because the blanket exclusion was never a measurement, it was an assumption that Shift makes a chord safe. Membership is measured, not guessed: the starting evidence is Chromium's documented page-unreachable accelerators, Ctrl+Shift+N (new private window), Ctrl+Shift+R (reload ignoring cache), Ctrl+Shift+T (reopen closed tab) and Ctrl+Shift+W (close window), and Firefox is checked against them, because the host opens the editor in the author's own browser rather than one this repo chooses. The comment carries the browser and the date it was measured against — a reserved set with no provenance is the claim-without-a-reason shape this row already names. The `ponytail:` note stays: a longer list, or a key-capture API, is still the upgrade path. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.3, step 2) at `c0b0ceb7`, as the ruling asked: `RESERVED_LETTERS` is unchanged and a second set joins it — `SHIFT_RESERVED_LETTERS = { n, r, t, w }` (bindings.ts:98) — with `reserved()` at `:322` picking by `binding.shift === true`, so **a plain-modifier letter and its Shift variant are two chords and are judged as two**. `p` is deliberately absent from the Shift set: Firefox's private window is `Ctrl+Shift+P` and Chromium leaves that chord free, so refusing it would reject a chord that works in the browser most authors open. **THE PROVENANCE IS A DOCUMENTATION CHECK AND IS SAID THAT WAY** — the comment carries the date and its sources, Chrome's shortcut list and Firefox's own `browser-sets.inc` key definitions, and **no browser measured it**: the seat's headless Chromium probe delivered *every* chord to the page including `Ctrl+W`, so a headless browser cannot observe its own accelerators, and no Firefox is installed on this box. The ruling asked for membership "measured against Chromium's documented page-unreachable accelerators", so a documentation check is what was asked for — but it is a reading and not a measurement, and it is recorded as a reading. RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER: collapsing the two sets back into the old `shift !== true` rule reads **1 failed / 70 passed, exit 1**, and the failure is the right one — `Ctrl+Shift+N` was refused as `{ kind: 'taken', action: 'file.new' }` rather than `reserved`, so the old rule blamed another binding for a chord the browser owns; restored byte-identically with `cmp`, **71 passed exit 0**. The comment the row asked for carries the browser and the date it was measured against, which was the row's own condition.
check: a Shift variant of a reserved letter is refused as the browser's own chord rather than blamed on another binding: with the two sets collapsed into the old rule, Ctrl+Shift+N reads taken/file.new where it should read reserved — 1 failed of 71 at exit 1, restored byte-identically with cmp to 71 passed exit 0 — and the comment carries the browser and the date, checked against Chrome's shortcut list and Firefox's browser-sets.inc

title: The identity chip has no rule for what happens once the name is fully truncated: the fixed edited marker overflows and is clipped mid-word
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 6's completion round, from the collision assertion the controller required. At 640x360 CSS px - which is 1280x720 at the 200% browser zoom section 7.7 requires be checked - .editor-shell-identity's min-width: 0 let the chip shrink below the floor its non-shrinkable children set, so the trailing "Unsaved changes" painted from x=399 to x=483.6 while the chip's own box ended at 465 and the view cluster began at 473: a 10.6px overlap, with elementFromPoint answering SPAN where it should answer CANVAS. A comparison of the chip's BOX could never see it, which is why the assertion compares painted geometry and a point between the corners. Fixed in Task 6 with one declaration, overflow: hidden on .editor-shell-identity (the `.editor-shell-identity` rule), and that fix stands - it is containment, not surface, and R3's "do not touch the chip" ruling was about the panel/glass/elevation treatment. WHAT THIS ROW ACTUALLY IS, corrected after reading the chip's own rules rather than filing the round's framing: it is NOT that the wrong element is degraded. .editor-shell-identity-name is min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, text-overflow: ellipsis, so the name IS the only child that can shrink and it ellipsises first; the dot and the edited marker are both flex: none. So at 640x360 the name has already been truncated to nothing and the fixed marker still overflows by 10.6px - the arithmetic matches the measurement, since the chip's floor is its padding plus the 7px dot plus two gaps plus a fixed "Unsaved changes" that cannot shrink. The gap in the design language is therefore the state PAST a fully truncated name: section 7.7 licenses truncating identity's name, and says nothing about what the chip should do once the name is gone and a fixed part still does not fit. The landed behaviour is a mid-word clip with no ellipsis, which is the one presentation section 7.7 explicitly reserves for refusals and numeric edits. A future owner should NOT "make the name ellipsise instead" - it already does. The open choices are dropping or shortening the edited marker at compact widths, allowing it to wrap, or accepting the clip and saying so. OWNER: the identity chip's presentation, or Task 10's difference list; adjacent to but distinct from vg-219, which lists the chip's three mockup differences. SEVERITY: low - cosmetic, at one breakpoint, with no data, reachability or focus lost.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: REMOVE THE UNSAVED-CHANGES MARKER FROM THIS CHIP AND KEEP ONLY THE COLOURED INDICATOR DOT. The marker was the fixed part that overflowed once the name truncated, and the dirty state is already carried by the status bar at the bottom right, so the chip loses the text rather than dropping, shortening, wrapping or accepting a clip. Neither vg-219 nor vg-230 is absorbed by this: the chip's mockup differences and the status bar's reads stand on their own rows. ONE CLAIM IN THIS ROW IS STALE AND IS CORRECTED HERE, measured by Task 18.4's seat (2026-10-16) on the built bundle before its change. THE ROW'S BREAKPOINT DOES NOT REPRODUCE ANY MORE: at 640x360 CSS px with the longest name the document field carries, the chip is 134.4px, the name is already truncated to 4.2px, and the marker is 84.6px — it fits with 5.8px to spare, so nothing is clipped there. **The layout has moved about 10px since the row was filed and the clip now appears one step narrower, at 560x360**: chip 54.4px, name 0px, marker painted to 65px past the chip's right edge and cut mid-word by the `overflow: hidden` Task 6 added. So the state the row describes is real and the number in it is stale; after the fix the same 560x360 read gives the name 16.8px and no overflow, and at 640x360 the name goes from 4.2px to 96.8px. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.4, step 1) at `5da31012`, exactly as ruled: **the chip loses the edited marker and keeps the coloured dot.** The marker was the chip's only non-shrinkable child besides the dot, so it set the chip's floor while `editor-shell-identity-name` is the only child that can shrink with it — which is why the ruling removes the text rather than dropping, shortening, wrapping or accepting a clip. **Neither `vg-219` nor `vg-230` is absorbed**, as the row required. The dirty fact is unchanged and still has one owner: the chip reads the session's `isDirty()`, the same fact the status bar's `SaveState` reads, and **the word is now the status bar's alone** — the chip's doc comment records why rather than leaving the removal to be rediscovered. `overflow: hidden` on `.editor-shell-identity` stays, because the row rules it containment rather than surface. **THE ROW'S OWN BREAKPOINT WAS STALE AND IS CORRECTED ABOVE**: 640x360 no longer reproduces and 560x360 does, measured with the numbers on the row. RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER: restoring the marker reads **1 failed / 2 passed, exit 1**, failing `document-identity.dom.test.tsx`'s "reads the edited state from the same fact the status bar reads"; restored byte-identically (proved with `cmp`) the two suites read **21 passed exit 0**. The marker's case moved rather than being deleted, which is what the row's own close required.
check: the identity chip's edited marker is gone and the coloured dot stays, so the name is the only child that shrinks: at 560x360 the marker had painted 65px past the chip's right edge and is now absent, the name taking 16.8px where it took 0 — red-proved by restoring the marker at 1 failed of 3 exit 1, restored byte-identically with cmp to 21 passed exit 0

title: The editor bundle has no product-version source, so the About tab can name no version for Yunari itself
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 4'S STEP 1 (2026-10-10), BY READING, NOT BY TESTING. Measured with `grep -rn version packages/editor/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v .test. | grep -vi canvas`: the only hits are the theme's own release version (editor-session.ts:1092 bumpSemanticVersion; panes/document/metadata-fields.tsx:101 metadata?.version) and unrelated words (Fabric's scene version 7.4.0 in new-fabric-theme.ts:188, the qr-symbol.tsx version, storage-key prose) - not one product version. `grep -rn 'VERSION|SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION' packages/host/src/main.ts packages/renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts` finds the host's const VERSION = "0.1.0" at packages/host/src/main.ts:34, Node-side and logging Yunari v${VERSION} at :250 and not in the editor bundle, and SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2 at packages/renderer-core/src/theme/fabric-envelope.ts:16 (it was 1 in theme/document.ts, which schema v1's retirement deleted on 2026-10-11), a schema number this build can read but which is not the product's version. packages/editor/package.json is 0.0.0 and packages/editor/vite.config.ts injects no define. So the About tab (landed in the same commit) renders the schema version and the open document's release version, and nothing claiming to be Yunari's own version. WHY A ROW RATHER THAN A FIX: giving the product one version string both the host CLI and the editor bundle import is a host change that needs a decision rather than a task, and more than one owner could fix it, so it sits outside plan 5's scope.

RULED 2026-10-12: ONE OWNER: the workspace manifest's `version` field is the product's version, and both readers take it from there rather than from a new module. The host already runs Node and can read `src/web/package.json`; the editor bundle is built by Vite, which injects it through `define` at build time. That keeps one number, written in the place a release already has to change it, with no new exported constant and no second file to forget. Two things the fix must not do: it must not make the schema version carry the product's meaning — `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays a separate fact, and the About tab keeps labelling it as what it is — and it must not present the open document's release version as Yunari's own. The About tab gains one line naming the product version; the other two lines keep their own labels. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.4, step 2) at `5da31012`, and **the decision the row's premise forced is recorded because the row assumed it away**. Reproduced: every manifest in the workspace read `0.0.0` — `src/web/package.json` and all seven packages — there is no root manifest, and the only real version string in the tree was the host's hardcoded `const VERSION = "0.1.0"` at `packages/host/src/main.ts:34`. So there was no product version for a manifest to own, and the row's "the workspace manifest's `version` is the product's version" was false as written. **DECISION: the product version is `0.1.0`, owned by `src/web/package.json`.** The row already ruled *where* — the store that lists themes was for `vg-363`; here the ruling named the workspace manifest — and only *what* was unruled, so taking the incumbent value invents no number and changes what no reader prints. It is a preservation of the existing value rather than a new choice, which is why it needed no user. **BOTH READERS TAKE IT FROM THAT FIELD RATHER THAN A COPY OF IT**: the host reads the manifest at run time, three levels above its own module — the same depth from `src/` and from `dist/`, which is why one path serves both, and `node packages/host/bin/yunari.js --version` prints `0.1.0` exit 0 — and the editor bundle is given it by Vite's `define` as `__YUNARI_VERSION__`, with `vitest.config.ts` injecting the same constant because the unit suite does not build through the editor's config and `product-version.d.ts` declaring it. **THE TWO THINGS THE STEP FORBADE ARE KEPT APART**: `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays its own fact with its own label, and the release row is still the open document's `metadata.version` — never the product's. The About tab gains a "Product version" row, verified in a re-taken capture (`settings-about-desktop-chromium.png`) showing `Product version 0.1.0` beside `Schema version 2` and no release row, because this fixture's document carries no release version and §9's missing reading is a gap stated by absence. **`docs/architecture/ownership.md` gained the row for the product version**, since a concept with two readers is what that map is for. RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER: cutting the `define` reads **5 failed / 13 passed, exit 1**, with `ReferenceError: __YUNARI_VERSION__ is not defined`; restored byte-identically with `cmp`, **21 passed exit 0**.
check: the editor bundle and the host both name the product version from src/web/package.json, the one place a release writes it: the About tab reads 0.1.0 and the host CLI prints 0.1.0 at exit 0, while the schema version and the document's release version stay separate facts — cutting the define reads 5 failed of 18 with ReferenceError exit 1, restored byte-identically with cmp to green

title: A bare editor mount resumes whichever theme won a millisecond mtime tie, so the document a run starts from is not reproducible
detail:
FOUND BY Task 1 of the keyboard-only walkthrough plan (2026-10-12), as the reason its first census was not reproducible. OBSERVED: two runs of the same spec against the host app directory reseeded identically by tests/e2e/global-setup.ts opened two different documents -- the first resumed E2E missing (one object in the Layers tree, census 18 presses) and the second E2E deliberate bleed (three objects, census 26 presses). Nothing in either run touched the library. THE MECHANISM, READ FROM SOURCE rather than inferred from the two runs: theme-library-client.ts reports updatedAt, the host store sets it from stat.mtime.toISOString() (themes/store.ts, entryFor), the listing sorts by id (themes/store.ts, list), and boot-theme.ts latestOwnTheme keeps the first strict maximum -- so equal updatedAt strings are broken by id order, and toISOString truncates to milliseconds. A filesystem listing of the fixture themes shows why ties are ordinary here: e2e-bleed, e2e-bleed-all, e2e-media and e2e-missing-sensor all carry the identical mtime 2026-10-12 01:16:55.827373400, because seedHostTheme writes all ten in one pass. The part NOT observed: whether the first run seeds straddled two milliseconds -- that is what the two different winners require, and the winning id under a tie (e2e-bleed) is exactly what the second run opened, but the first run state is gone and that half stands as the explanation that fits rather than as a measurement. IMPACT: a browser test that does not name a theme starts from a document it did not choose and cannot predict, which is how a press count and a scene assertion move for a reason that is not the change under test. Two saves inside one millisecond is not something an author does by hand, so the visible product impact is small and the measured one is in tests. CLOSE THIS when the tie-break is decided and written down -- by id, by name, or by a stored save counter rather than an mtime -- or when a store with two equally-recent themes is ruled to have no right answer and the bare mount stops being used as a starting state. The walkthrough plan worked around it by pinning ?theme= and did not repair it, which is the shape this row records. OWNER: whoever owns boot-theme.ts and the theme store listing, and the decision is theirs because more than one answer is defensible.

RULED 2026-10-12: RANK BY ID — most recent save first, then `id` ascending as the tie-break, written in the store that lists themes. No new persisted field: a save counter would add a column to every theme document to cover two saves inside one millisecond, and it would need a migration and would have to stay honest forever, while `id` is already stable, already unique and already persisted — which is the whole point of a stable id. Name is rejected as the tie-break because a name is editable and two themes may share one, so it converts a rare tie into a common one. This closes the row: the bare mount may keep starting from the store's own answer, because that answer is now reproducible.
CHECKED 2026-10-16, WHILE TRIAGING THE ROWS WHOSE ONLY CARRYING PHASE IS PHASE 1 (agent, 2026-10-16), and deliberately LEFT OPEN. The ruling's last sentence is that it "closes the row", so the behaviour was read rather than assumed, and **the ruled answer is composed rather than written where the ruling said to write it**:

- `host/src/themes/store.ts`'s `list()` returns entries sorted by `a.id.localeCompare(b.id)` — id ascending, and **no recency term at all**.
- `editor/src/boot-theme.ts`'s `latestOwnTheme` filters to entries carrying `updatedAt` and reduces with `entry.updatedAt > best.updatedAt` — strictly greater, so **on a tie the first entry wins**.
- Composed, those give exactly what the ruling asked for: max `updatedAt`, ties resolved by id ascending. So the defect the row describes — an answer that is not reproducible — is very likely already gone.

**Why that is not a close.** The ruling said the ranking is "written in the store that lists themes", and the store ranks by id alone; the recency half lives in a caller. A close on that reading would be a source reading where the ruling asked for a measurement, which this plan's Acceptance forbids. **What closes it**: one case that saves two themes with the same `updatedAt` and asserts the mount opens the lower `id` — after which the answer is pinned rather than incidental. The row also has no phase that will land that case, which is the shape recorded in the plan's fourth census correction. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.6) at `e836a9ee`, and the case the triage named is the whole of it. **The composition the triage read is reproduced and now pinned by a measurement rather than a source reading**: `host/src/themes/store.ts`'s `list()` sorts by `a.id.localeCompare(b.id)` with no recency term, `editor/src/boot-theme.ts`'s `latestOwnTheme` reduces with `entry.updatedAt > best.updatedAt` so the first entry wins a tie, and `entryFor` sets `updatedAt` from `stat.mtime.toISOString()`. The case saves two themes, gives both folders one mtime, and asserts the bare mount opens the lower `id` — **the document opened, not the argument passed**. **RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER**: cutting the reduce to `>=` reads **1 failed exit 1** and reversing the store's sort reads **1 failed exit 1**, each `AssertionError: expected 'theme-b' to be 'theme-a'` — the assertion rather than a compile error, so the case pins both halves of the composition; restored byte-identically with `cmp`, green at **1 passed exit 0**, and the focused host and mount suites read **87 passed exit 0**. **ONE CLAIM IN THIS ROW IS STALE AND IS CORRECTED HERE**: the FOUND BY paragraph says `seedHostTheme` writes **ten** fixture themes in one pass. It writes **eleven** — six `envelopeFor` calls plus `groupedGlassEnvelope`, `mediaEnvelope`, `chartEnvelope`, two `bleedEnvelope` calls and the inline missing-sensor envelope, counted at `tests/e2e/host-theme.ts:790` by the controller. The conclusion the count was carrying is unaffected and if anything stronger: the pass is what makes ties ordinary. **THE RULING'S LAST SENTENCE IS NOW TRUE RATHER THAN LIKELY TRUE** — the row's own CHECKED paragraph said the defect was "very likely already gone" and named exactly this case as what would close it. **The store was not changed**: the ruling permits the recency half to live in a caller, and what it forbids is an answer that is not reproducible, so the case pins the existing split rather than moving it. **The half this row never measured is still unmeasured and the row says so**: whether the original two runs straddled two milliseconds is not recoverable, and what closed is the tie-break, not that race. **A design consequence the brief did not anticipate is recorded on the commit**: the case needs the real store and the real mount in one program, and `packages/editor/tsconfig.json` carries no `@types/node`, so it lives in the host's suite with a relative import of the editor's `boot-theme.js`. No persisted field was added and no save counter was introduced, which the ruling forbade explicitly.
check: the bare editor mount's theme tie is pinned by a case rather than a source reading: two themes given one mtime open the lower id, and the case reads red under both mutations — the reduce cut to `>=` and the store's sort reversed, each `expected 'theme-b' to be 'theme-a'` exit 1 — green at 1 passed exit 0, so the document a run starts from is reproducible; the focused host and mount suites read 87 passed exit 0

title: A text run has no identity in the persisted model, so the inspector's row keys must come from content — an edit or a same-shape middle removal changes the key and costs the row its caret
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 3, during its fix loop. The run editor keys each row by a derived identity because `yunariText.runs` is a plain array with no per-run id. Two attempts were made and each trades one failure for another, which is the evidence that the model is the cause rather than the key. (1) Positional index keys: the row survives an edit, but removing a MIDDLE run shifts every later index, so React reconciles a row holding a draft onto the next run's data — the draft is displayed against the wrong run and the next blur can commit it there (filed as M1 in the task review). (2) Content-derived identity `` `literal:${typePreset}\u0000${text}` ``: a middle removal is then safe, because survivors keep their keys, but `ControlText` commits on ENTER (`components/ui/control-text.tsx:74`), so committing a typed reading changes the key, remounts the row, destroys the focused input and drops focus to `document.body` (N1). The shipped fix excludes the mutable TEXT from the identity, which removes the Enter failure and leaves a residual, recorded in `runs.tsx` rather than hidden: two literal runs sharing a type preset can still shift on a middle removal, and changing a run's preset or its source binding still remounts that row. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TASK. Task 3a's brief requires it to preserve 'repeat-row identity' for chart series rows, which is the same problem over the same kind of array, so it will be met again before the plan closes. PRECEDENT, NOT A GUESS. The same class was already found and fixed once: vg-044 (archived, verified) — 'A chart's series colours and its bindings are coupled by index, so removing a middle binding shifts the colours' — and its fix was NOT an id. It reconciles at mutation time, carrying each surviving series' own paint through the removal before the array-length repair runs. So the cheap path here is probably the same shape: carry the surviving rows' state through the removal (or hold drafts outside the row), rather than adding a persisted id. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether reconciliation is sufficient for the caret case, since a lost draft and a misplaced draft are different harms, or whether the model should simply gain a per-run id — that is a persisted-schema decision (existing documents hold runs without one) and is not a task-level call. NOT CLAIMED: that the shipped fix is wrong; it is the best of the three shapes available without a model change, and its residual is disclosed in code and in the task report. OWNER: whoever owns the persisted text-run model with whoever owns the inspector's row rendering.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: THE PERSISTED TEXT-RUN MODEL GAINS NO PER-RUN ID, AND THE INSPECTOR RECONCILES SURVIVORS AT MUTATION TIME AS vg-044 DID. An id added to persisted runs is editor bookkeeping written into the theme file, which is the line AGENTS.md draws -- persist authored state only -- and the reconciliation at mutation time is the precedent this repo already has. COST IF WRONG: the inspector carries reconciliation logic it would not need with ids; that logic already exists for vg-044. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.5, step 2) at `6508ac42`, and **the ruling's precedent clause needed correcting rather than following**. The ruling says the inspector "reconciles survivors at mutation time as `vg-044` did", and `vg-044`'s reconciliation is a **pure function of (previous, next)** — `carriedPaintFor`. **No pure function of the run array can do this job**: two literal runs sharing a type preset are the same fields, so any spelling of a key over content is ambiguous, and any repeat counter is positional and therefore wrong the moment a middle run is removed. So the identity is **the run's own object**, in `selection-inspector/run-identity.ts`: a `WeakMap<TextRun, string>` that mints an id the first time one is asked for, and `carryRunIdentity` hands it to the replacement inside the write rules — **the reconciliation is at mutation time, which is the half of the ruling that binds, and it is not a pure function, which is the half that could not be honoured as written.** **THE MODEL IS UNCHANGED AND NO ID IS PERSISTED**: `yunariText.runs` is still a plain array, the map is runtime state that dies with the process, and a reloaded document is a genuine target change whose rows *should* remount, which is what §5 asks. **This also closes the second residual the file used to record** — a preset or a source-binding change no longer remounts the row, because the write hands the identity across. The first residual stands and is unchanged: two literal runs sharing a preset can still shift on a middle removal, since nothing distinguishes them. **RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER**: disabling the carry reads **1 failed / 4 passed exit 1**, failing "keeps the caret when Enter commits a literal's text" with the focus on `<body>` rather than the input — the exact failure the row's second attempt traded into — restored byte-identically with `cmp` to **5 passed exit 0**; the run suites read **44 passed exit 0** and the whole editor package **1954 passed exit 0**. **A finding this landing made visible is filed rather than fixed** — `vg-548`: a gesture that ends with neither a commit nor a cancel leaves the previewed value in the document with no history entry. **`selection-inspector/index.ts` is 796 lines** (from 772), which is past this repo's 500-line signal and under its 800-line stop; the seat trimmed its own comment growth rather than splitting the file, and the number is recorded here so the next seat does not rediscover it.

title: A slider in the selection column gives no live preview while dragging, so the value only moves on release
detail:
FOUND WHILE REVIEWING PLAN 3 TASK 9 (the parity capture), in the built editor at 1ab06ad2, by the task reviewer and verified at source by the controller while filing. MEASURED: with the Layer Opacity slider focused, a pointer drag to roughly 50% and then 25% left aria-valuenow AND the well reading 99 throughout, and the value jumped to 26 only on mouse-up - so an author dragging a bounded number sees nothing change until they let go. CAUSE, read rather than guessed: selection-inspector/column.tsx:183-192 renders ControlSlider with onCommit and no onPreview, although the control supports a preview callback (components/ui/control-slider.tsx:30 and :112, described in its own docblock at :17) and components/ui/control.dom.test.tsx:659-676 exercises it. The field funnel has no preview half to call: SelectionEdits exposes only commit, where the sibling CropEdits (selection-inspector/view.ts:269-274) has begin/setAspect/apply/cancel. NOT A BIBLE VIOLATION, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: design-language.md section 5 says a slider MAY preview through the existing imperative write funnel, so preview is permitted and not required, and release committing one changed value is satisfied as it stands. SHARED, NOT INTRODUCED HERE: the same field renderer draws the glass blur and panel radius sliders, so every slider in the column behaves this way and the behaviour predates plan 3's Task 9. WHY IT NEEDS A RULING RATHER THAN A PATCH: giving sliders a preview means adding a preview/cancel path to the field funnel and deciding how a preview that writes nothing interacts with the one-undo-boundary rule the same section states, across the control set, the funnel and the history boundary - a design decision with more than one owner, not a missing prop.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. A SLIDER PREVIEWS WHILE DRAGGING AND COMMITS ON RELEASE. Section 5 permits preview through the imperative write funnel; the field funnel gains a preview and a cancel path, and the preview writes no history entry -- the release commits exactly one value, which is what the one-undo-boundary rule asks. A control that shows nothing until release is a control whose value the author cannot see while choosing it, and the same renderer draws every slider in the column, so the fix is one path rather than one field. COST IF WRONG: every slider in the selection column gains a code path, and the funnel gains a state it did not have; the undo rule is the invariant this must not break. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 18, Task 18.5, step 1) at `6508ac42`, exactly as ruled: **a slider previews while dragging and commits on release.** `SelectionEdits` gains `preview` and `cancelPreview` beside `commit`, mirroring the sibling `CropEdits` (`view.ts:275-278`) rather than inventing a fourth idiom, and **all three go through one funnel** — `writeField`, the dispatch extracted from `commit`, plus `applyField`, the `editRefusal` guard — so **only `commit` records history** and a preview cannot reach the document by a second route. `ControlSlider.onCancel` now carries the start value, read into a ref at pointer-down, because a preview deliberately does **not** re-publish the column: that is what keeps `field.value` at the gesture's start and leaves the control's own moving value (`vg-449`) drawing the thumb. A frame announces no refusal and **does not call `refreshGlass`** — `sync` answers *which* objects carry a treatment, the only slider-driven glass field is the blur and it is offered only where a treatment exists, so a preview cannot change that answer; without this the glass case reddens with `refreshGlass` twice per keyboard step and a drag would walk the scene sixty times a second. **ONE CLAIM IN THIS ROW IS STALE AND IS CORRECTED HERE.** The row's own MEASURED paragraph says `aria-valuenow` **and** the well read 99 throughout the drag; **that half no longer reproduces, because `vg-449` fixed it** (`f849c425`, `verified` — *the opacity slider does not follow the pointer, and its value lands only when the gesture ends*, whose own case is the readout following the pointer). So the readout half of this row's measurement is discharged by another row and **the surviving subject is the document**: with the wiring removed the browser reads `the document did not follow the pointer: 1, 1, 1`. The ruling is unaffected — it asked the *funnel* for a preview and a cancel path, which is what landed. **RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER**: unwiring the two props reads **2 failed / 19 passed exit 1** with that message, restored byte-identically with `cmp` and rebuilt to **21 passed exit 0**. Three browser cases are added: the document follows the pointer during a held drag, **one `Ctrl+Z` returns the whole drag to full — one entry**, and a typed edit followed by an abandoned drag and `Escape` restores 0.4 while one `Ctrl+Z` steps over the **typed** edit, so the gesture contributed no entry. **The same renderer draws the glass blur and panel radius sliders**, so this is one path for every slider in the column, which is what the ruling's last sentence asked for. **NOT VERIFIED**: the drag is browser-proven for the **opacity** slider alone — the other two share the funnel and are covered in jsdom by the glass case, but no browser case drags them — and jsdom cannot separate a preview from its commit, so "the preview writes no history" rests on the browser cases and on `applyField` never reaching `commit()`.
check: the selection column's sliders preview while dragging through the write funnel and commit once on release, with the preview writing no history: unwiring the two props reads 2 failed of 21 exit 1 with `the document did not follow the pointer: 1, 1, 1`, restored byte-identically with cmp and rebuilt to 21 passed exit 0, and a browser case shows one Ctrl+Z returning the whole drag while an abandoned drag leaves no entry; the row's aria-valuenow half was stale because vg-449 fixed the readout, so the surviving subject is the document

title: The spec's primitive list names video, and no object kind can carry one

title: The artboard panel crop figure lags during a drag, though it catches up on release
detail:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING DEVICE-LENS PLAN 2 TASK 5, then AMENDED by its own task review, which found the controller had filed it too narrowly. ORIGINALLY FILED AS: the panel recomputes its outside-object count only on render(), so the number lags while an object is dragged past the edge - a transient cosmetic lag identified by reading, not by driving. THE REVIEW SHOWS THAT IS NOT THE WHOLE OF IT. The bleed control (selection-inspector/bleed.ts:94) fires object:modified, and its own comment claims the artboard panel is thereby told the scene moved - but the panel has NO canvas subscription at all. sizeNote.textContent is assigned from exactly one place, render() at artboard-panel.ts:336, and render() is called from only three sites in the editor: mount, #setArtboard, and #deletePalette. So ticking the mark leaves the figure reading "1 of 1 objects are now outside" until the author changes the artboard or deletes a palette token. THAT IS NOT A LAG: an explicit author action whose whole purpose is to change the number produces no visible change at all and never catches up, which is the feature being invisible on the surface it is judged on. The two tests that appear to cover the refresh do not - one asserts only that fire was called with object:modified, and its name claims the outcome; the other covers the panel arithmetic by calling panel.render() BY HAND, which is the call the product does not make.  PARTIALLY FIXED BY TASK 5, and the remainder is exactly this row. Task 5 added the subscription that closes the mark case - panel now listens to object:modified and refreshes the note through a single refreshNote writer - and that fires on drag RELEASE, so the figure catches up on mouse-up. THE REMAINDER IS THE DURING-DRAG CASE: Fabric fires object:moving per frame while a drag is in progress and object:modified only on release, and the panel does not subscribe to object:moving. So the figure is stale for the duration of a drag and correct afterwards. NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: subscribing to object:moving would be a per-frame recompute of a figure that already converges on release, and that is a product call about whether a live figure during a drag is worth a per-frame recompute, not an oversight. This row exists to hold the question open rather than to assert the lag is a defect. FIXTURE if it is taken on: add object:moving to the panel existing subscription array and confirm the figure tracks the drag without a full render - refreshNote was built to be cheap enough for exactly this, which is why the mark case did not have to be.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: SUBSCRIBE TO object:moving, SO THE FIGURE TRACKS DURING THE DRAG. A figure that only catches up on release is the same defect vg-254 rules on for sliders -- the author cannot see what they are choosing -- and the standard remedy for a high-frequency event is coalescing to the animation frame rather than dropping the event, so the recompute rides the frames the canvas already paints. COST IF WRONG: a per-frame recompute is real work; if it measurably costs the drag its frame budget the answer is a cheaper recompute, not a return to release-only tracking. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 19, Task 19.2) at `be181f68`, exactly as ruled: **subscribe to `object:moving`, coalesced to the animation frame.** The panel now arms one `requestAnimationFrame` per frame and drops further events while one is pending (`artboard-panel.ts:119-131`), so a 24-event drag costs one recompute per painted frame rather than 24 or zero; the subscription is removed and the armed frame cancelled in `destroy()`, because a frame armed for a drag that has not finished would draw a tree that call is about to unmount. **THE ROW'S OWN MECHANISM DESCRIPTION IS STALE AND IS CORRECTED HERE, WHICH IS THE FIFTH SUCH CORRECTION THIS PHASE HAS MADE.** The row says `sizeNote.textContent` is assigned from one place, `render()` at `artboard-panel.ts:336`, and that Task 5 added a `refreshNote` writer. **None of that is true any more**: `artboard-panel.ts` is **145 lines**, there is no `refreshNote` and no `sizeNote.textContent`, and the note is React-rendered — `sizeNote` is a pure function at `panes/document/artboard-fields.tsx:236`, rendered at `:198` from `boxes`, which `artboard-panel.ts:98` reads from `sceneBoxes()` at the moment of the draw. **The subject reproduces exactly and the mechanism is the subscription alone**: `on("object:modified", draw)` was the only canvas subscription, and Fabric fires that on release. **THE MID-DRAG READING, TAKEN WITH THE BUTTON STILL DOWN**: before the change the note read the rule text alone (`Objects are not moved or resized…`) for the whole drag and only became `1 of 54 objects are now outside…` on mouse-up; after it, the figure reads `1 of 54 objects are now outside the artboard and will not be shown on a display.` while the drag is held. **THE FRAME BUDGET WAS MEASURED AND THE RULING'S COST-IF-WRONG DOES NOT FIRE**: `canvas.fire` was bracketed and `requestAnimationFrame` wrapped, with the two callbacks split by registration slot — slot 0 the canvas repaint, slot 1 the panel's coalesced recompute — and the attribution proven on a no-subscription build (repaint n=24, recompute n=0). The panel's recompute reads **2.3–3.2 ms median, p95 2.9–5.7 ms, max 3.6–6.1 ms**, against a 16.7 ms frame, so it fits with roughly five times the headroom and **no cheaper recompute is owed**. The spec asserts `recompute.p95 < 1000/60`. **RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER**: commenting out the subscription reads **1 failed / 24 passed exit 1**, `one recompute for the frame: expected 1 to be 2` — the coalescing itself, not a missing draw — restored byte-identically with `cmp` to **25 passed exit 0**; rebuilt and re-run, the browser case `follows an object over the edge while the drag is still held` reads **1 passed exit 0**. **THE COMMENT THAT CLAIMED THE PANEL IS TOLD THE SCENE MOVED STAYS TRUE AND WAS LEFT ALONE**: the brief pointed at `bleed.ts`, and **`bleed.ts` is 62 lines with no `object:modified` fire at all** — the write and its comment are `selection-inspector/index.ts:414` and `:417-419`, and the panel's new subscription is what makes the claim hold during a drag as well as on release. **NOT VERIFIED, AND THE ROW SAYS SO**: the drag was driven on a desktop viewport only (the case skips on phone, the editor being a desktop surface); the frame numbers are one machine's; and the cross-batch canvas-repaint comparison is not trustworthy — 20.2 against 30.3 ms median for the same build across batches — so only the panel's own callback, measured within a run, is.
check: the artboard panel's crop figure follows an object over the edge while the drag is still held, rather than catching up on release: the object:moving subscription coalesces to one recompute per animation frame, the browser case reads 1 passed exit 0 and the dom case reads red at 1 failed of 25 exit 1 when the subscription is cut, restored byte-identically with cmp to green, and the panel's own callback measures 2.3-3.2 ms median against a 16.7 ms frame

title: A pane's title bar and footer scroll with its body, against bible section 7.7, because the aside is the only scroller
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's task review. `editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector`'s shared rule puts overflow:auto on aside.editor-shell-panel, and that aside contains the pane header, the body and the footer, so scrolling a long list takes the title bar and the toolbar off screen with it. Bible section 7.7 requires a pane's title and footer to stay outside the scrolling body, and layer-panel.tsx:809-810 carries a comment asserting exactly that property - "the toolbar stays put while the list scrolls beneath it" - about a structure that does not have it. The comment is corrected in Task 2's fix round; THIS ROW IS ABOUT THE STRUCTURE, not the comment. NOT FIXED THERE because the plan's own Global Constraint makes the aside the single scroller deliberately: choosePane restores each pane's scroll offset through it and shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts pins that, so moving to a scrolling body inside a fixed frame is a layout decision spanning the plan and the bible rather than a task. OWNER: unassigned - the plan that next restructures the pane frame. SEVERITY: low for behaviour (nothing becomes unreachable; the footer is still reachable by scrolling) and medium as a bible conformance gap.

RULED 2026-10-12: The STRUCTURE is the defect and DESIGN.md §7.7 wins. §7.7 is intact and says *Chrome stays still. Pane title and footer stay outside the scrolling body* (DESIGN.md:332), which is design intent recorded from the drawing; the plan's Global Constraint that made the aside the single scroller was an implementation shortcut taken so `choosePane` could restore a per-pane offset through one element, and a shortcut taken for a mechanism does not outrank the intent it broke. The rule for the next pane-frame restructure is therefore settled here: the BODY element owns the scroll, the title bar and footer sit outside it, and the per-pane offset and disclosure state are restored through the body — `shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts` pins the shortcut, so it changes in the same commit as the structure it pins. The row stays open with its owner named as that restructure, because none of it is cheap and none of it is a one-line fix; the severity stays low for behaviour, since the footer is still reachable by scrolling, and that low severity is the reason this is a ruling rather than a task in the current phase.

PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-10-16 (§8.2, and this one is not only a moved line). The row's title rests on the aside being **the only scroller**, and the rule it cites — the shell's single `overflow: auto` on the pane/inspector column — now carries **two** selectors, `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector`, in one shared block. So the citation is corrected, and the claim it supports is narrower than the title reads: it is not that one scroller exists but that the panel and the inspector share one. Whether the titled defect (a title bar and footer scrolling with the body) still reproduces under that shared rule is **not established here** and needs the browser run the row's own kind of evidence requires — this annotation records the drift rather than closing the finding. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 19, Task 19.3) at `46e022ae`, exactly as ruled: **the body element owns the scroll and the title bar and footer sit outside it.** The pane's frame is a flex column — `flex: none` on the chrome so a tall body's shrink cannot squeeze it, and `min-height: 0` on the body because a flex child's `min-height` is `auto` and without it the body refuses to shrink and the column grows instead, which is the same defect wearing the fix (`editor-shell.css:2186-2197`). The column keeps the 12px padding and gains `overflow: hidden`, so the chrome keeps the inset it had. **THE SCROLL AND THE OFFSET HAD TO MOVE TOGETHER, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE WORK**: `choosePane` reads and writes each pane's offset off the box that scrolls, so `paneBody` now names the body it was always called after, through an optional `bodyRef` on `Pane` that only the showing pane attaches — the other three are `hidden`, and a `display: none` box answers `scrollTop` 0, which is what would write the author's place back as the top of the list. The save still runs before the column is hidden. **THE ROW'S RULING WAS EXECUTED AS WRITTEN, INCLUDING ITS OWN CONDITION**: `shell-layout-scroll.dom.test.ts` changes in the same commit as the structure it pins, its model of "a hidden box answers 0" now asking `closest()` rather than the body's own attribute, because it is the column that hides. **THE DEFECT WAS MEASURED ON THE BASE BUNDLE BEFORE ANYTHING CHANGED, THEN AGAIN AFTER**: at `607c9623` the column overflows by 1026px and scrolling it 300px moves the title bar from 54 to -246 and the footer from 1643 to 1343 — exactly the scroll — with the footer resting 949px below the column's own bottom edge; at `46e022ae` the body carries the overflow (1026px over a 534px client, the column 0 over 652) and both chrome positions hold at 54 and 617 through a 300px body scroll. **RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER**, green → cut → red → restore → green: `editor-rail.spec.ts:117`'s case `a pane's title bar and footer stay put while its body scrolls` reads **1 passed exit 0**; rewriting the body rule's `overflow: auto` to `visible` — the column's own pre-fix behaviour — reads **1 failed exit 1**, failing on the case's own mechanism assertion, `the pane's column is still a scroller, so §7.7's rule is still on the wrong box: expected 0, received 300`, which is the fix's box rather than a missing draw; restored byte-identically with `cmp`, rebuilt and re-run, **1 passed exit 0**. **ONE CLAUSE OF THIS ROW IS FALSIFIED AND CORRECTED HERE, THE SIXTH SUCH CORRECTION THIS PHASE HAS MADE.** The row cites `layer-panel.tsx:809-810` for the comment asserting the property — "the toolbar stays put while the list scrolls beneath it" — about a structure that did not have it. **That file is 60 lines and carries no such comment**; the claim lives at `layer-panel.dom.test.tsx:628`, in the case that asserts the tree draws no action footer of its own, as "so it stays put while the tree scrolls beneath it". The row's 2026-10-16 re-measurement clause is also superseded by this commit: it read the shell's single `overflow: auto` as now carrying two selectors, `.editor-shell-panel` and `.editor-shell-inspector`, and after this commit the rule carries neither — `min-height: 0` is what the two columns share, the inspector alone keeps the scroll, and the scrollbar token list names `.editor-shell-pane-body` in the panel's place. **NOT VERIFIED, AND THE ROW SAYS SO**: the browser reading is desktop-chromium only, because the editor is a desktop surface and the case skips elsewhere; the offsets are one machine's; and the case reads three things rather than assuming them — which box the list overflows, whether setting its `scrollTop` moves it, and where the chrome is before and after — so the numbers say which of the two boxes is the scroll owner rather than the case saying it.
check: the pane's title bar and footer stay put while the pane's body scrolls, against bible section 7.7: the browser case reads the body overflowing by 1026px over a 534px client with the column at 0 over 652, both chrome positions holding at 54 and 617 through a 300px body scroll, and reads red at 1 failed exit 1 when the body rule's overflow is cut to visible - restored byte-identically with cmp - then 1 passed exit 0

title: The Add pane's data-yunari-panel now scopes every add-pane locator to the whole pane, so a future asset control named with a shape word would collide
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 2's fix round and confirmed by its scoped re-review. The fix round deleted new-object-panel.ts:182's duplicate attribute and moved pane naming onto the pane itself (pane.tsx writes data-yunari-panel={id} unconditionally), which is the right resolution - but it widens what that attribute's descendants mean. Spec locators rebuild-driver.ts:139 (addButton, hasText /^label$/), editor.spec.ts:31/789/838, composition-panel.spec.ts:1064 and author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:73 now scope the Add pane, which also holds the asset host's buttons (asset-manager/panel.ts:30-35, labelled Import, Replace, Remove). MEASURED BENIGN TODAY: the shape filters match exact shape words and the getByRole name matches (Text, Gauge, Clock, Shape) are absent from the asset labels, and no case became ambiguous in the runs. NO CSS SCOPE CHANGED: no rule keys on a [data-yunari-panel] button descendant, and every CSS rule on the attribute is ="layers", which sat on the pane before the fix too. NOT FIXED because nothing is broken to fix - the hazard is that a future asset control whose label is a shape word becomes ambiguous in rebuild-driver.ts:139, silently, and only in that spec. SEVERITY: low; the trigger is future work and the failure would be a strict-mode ambiguity rather than a wrong assertion.

RULED 2026-10-12: TAKE THE SPEC CHURN NOW and give the Add pane's shape controls their own scope. The row's measurement is that today's locators are benign, and the hazard is that a future asset control labelled with a shape word makes one spec ambiguous in strict mode — silently, and only in the spec that happened to scope the whole pane. A locator that any unrelated surface can invalidate by gaining a label is the flake class this repo has already paid for; the fix is one stable scope hook on the shapes section and the four locators pointing at it, which is cheaper than the first misdiagnosed ambiguity. What is NOT the fix: renaming the asset host's labels, which would be changing product copy to suit a test. CLOSED 2026-10-16 (Phase 19, Task 19.4) at `014d38b3`, exactly as ruled: **one stable scope hook on the shapes section, and the locators that reach a shape control point at it.** The hook is `data-yunari-add-group="<kind>"` on each labelled group's `fieldset` (`add-pane.tsx:72`), and its owner is `InsertGroup.kind` (`new-object-panel.ts:99`). **`insertGroups()` already merged consecutive objects by kind, so a group's identity was always the kind and its heading was a second spelling of it**: the merge now compares `kind` (`new-object-panel.ts:144-155`) and `groupOf` returns the heading alone. The pane writes the hook and re-derives nothing, and `data-yunari-panel="add"` is still `Pane`'s alone. **The hook is deliberately NOT the heading**: the heading is `uiCopy.panels.shapes`, which is copy, and a scope derived from it moves the day an author's copy does — which is the one thing the hook exists to stop. The pane's own alternative (reading `group.objects[0].kind`) was refused because it infers the group's identity from a member and rests on a homogeneity invariant stated only in a comment. **THE PLAN'S COUNT OF "THE FOUR LOCATORS" IS A COUNT AND NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND THE MEASURED SET IS LARGER.** Measured at `5a16aad4`: **15 whole-pane control reaches**, of which **10 reach a shape** — `rebuild-driver.ts`'s `addButton`/`insert` (the row's own named hazard), `editor.spec.ts`'s `insertShape`, its shapes count, its `Line` count of 2 and its `Arc`/`Wedge`, plus **five the controller's brief did not list** (`host-player.spec.ts:491`, `inspector-sections.spec.ts:1183`, `reference-theme.spec.ts:425`, `:541`, `:700`) — and **12 shape call sites of the shared helper**. All ten moved to the hook; **no assertion changed anywhere**, which is what makes this a locator refactor rather than a test rewrite. **THE ROW'S OWN POINTERS ARE ALL STALE (READ 2026-10-09) AND ARE CORRECTED HERE**: `rebuild-driver.ts:139` is `:150-153` at base and uses `getByRole`, not `hasText /^label$/`; `editor.spec.ts:31/789/838` have moved; and **`asset-manager/panel.ts:30-35` no longer exists** — the asset host is `panes/add/file-section.tsx`, its three buttons at `:208`, `:215` and `:222`. **NO CSS WAS OWED AND THAT IS CONFIRMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED**: no rule mentions `data-yunari-add-group`, and every rule on `data-yunari-panel` is `="layers"` (`editor-shell.css:2054`, `:2100`, `:2107`, `:2113`). **RED-PROVED AND RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY BY THE CONTROLLER**, green → cut → red → restore → green: `editor.spec.ts:1350`'s case `offers every primitive as a named shape and styles one that is not a rectangle` reads **1 passed exit 0**; deleting the hook from the fieldset reads **1 failed exit 1** on `locator('[data-yunari-add-group="shape"]').getByRole('button')` expecting 8 and receiving 0 — **the hook's own absence rather than a missing draw**; restored byte-identically with `cmp`, rebuilt and re-run, **1 passed exit 0**. **THE ROW'S HAZARD IS CLOSED FOR SHAPES AND LEFT STANDING FOR EVERYTHING ELSE, WHICH THE ROW SAYS RATHER THAN IMPLYING A WHOLE FIX**: the chart-family `insert(page, chart.family)`, the Text row (which `insertGroups()` draws in no group at all), the chart-group locators and the pane-visibility uses that are the attribute's own meaning keep the whole-pane scope, so **an asset control labelled with a chart family or "Text" would still collide the way this row describes**. **NOT VERIFIED, AND THE ROW SAYS SO**: `npm run gate` and the full browser suite are the controller's phase-boundary job and were not run by this task; the phone-chromium project, the `design-language-*.spec.ts` files, `own-host` and `author-journey-display` were not run either. **The controller corrected one sentence of the task's own comment before landing it**: `addButton`'s docblock said the group is omitted "only for the Text row", and the chart-family insert at `rebuild-driver.ts:462` omits it as well.
check: the Add pane's shape locators scope the shapes section through data-yunari-add-group="shape" rather than the whole pane, so a future asset control named with a shape word cannot make one ambiguous: ten whole-pane reaches that touch a shape moved to the hook with no assertion changed, the browser case reads 1 passed exit 0, and cutting the hook reads 1 failed exit 1 at expected 8 received 0 restored byte-identically with cmp to green

title: `--shell-warm` stayed a pastel in ember, moss and plum while those palettes' paper is light, so every `--warn` text reads at 1.4-2.0:1
detail:
FOUND BY THE DESIGN-LANGUAGE PARITY GATE (this plan, task 4) on the gate's first green run. MEASURED in the same browser pass as vg-200: a rejected numeric draft renders its reason in `text-warn` (`src/web/packages/editor/src/components/ui/control-number.tsx:158`), and the composite over each palette's own panel is ember `#ff7e6e` on `rgb(247,226,210)` = 1.98:1, moss `#e8c56a` on `rgb(228,239,217)` = 1.40:1, plum `#ffb2a1` on `rgb(236,227,247)` = 1.39:1, against 5.18-9.36:1 in editorial, graphite and light. THE CONTROL SET IS NOT THE OWNER: the three declarations the pastels come from (`--shell-warm`'s three declarations, in the ember, moss and plum blocks) are the same `--shell-warm` that `.editor-shell-diagnostic` (`:1607`) and `.editor-shell-save-state` (`:1618`) paint, so on those three palettes the footer's warnings and the unsaved marker are unreadable too - the first `text-warn` in the product is not the defect, it is the first place the defect was measured. THE FILE ALREADY RECORDS THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: the comment above `[data-shell-palette="ember"]` says the three palettes' accents were 'deepened from the pastel that named them' because 'a light accent on a light surface carries nothing' and a pastel hover 'was a hover the author could not see'. `--shell-warm` was left as the pastel it was named for, and the same deepening is what it needs - at least 4.5:1 against each palette's own `--shell-surface` and against the glass overlay. NOT FIXED HERE because it is a colour decision with currency beyond text: `--yunari-accent` aliases `--shell-warm` (`:112`) on the canvas side, so the value that makes warnings readable also moves the canvas accent, and only the design owner can rule on the hue. PINNED, NOT WAIVED, in `design-language.spec.ts` as `PINNED_FLOOR.invalid` (ember 1.9, moss 1.35, plum 1.35), deleted and replaced by the 4.5:1 minimum when this row is ruled on. SEVERITY: medium-high - required information (why a value was rejected) is illegible in three of the six shipped palettes.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: DEEPEN --shell-warm TO AT LEAST 4.5:1 AGAINST EACH PALETTE'S OWN --shell-surface AND AGAINST THE GLASS OVERLAY, AND LET THE CANVAS ACCENT MOVE WITH IT. One owner for the hue: --yunari-accent aliases --shell-warm on the canvas side, so the readable value moves the canvas accent rather than the alias being broken. The pinned floor in design-language.spec.ts (PINNED_FLOOR.invalid -- ember 1.9, moss 1.35, plum 1.35) is deleted and replaced by the 4.5:1 minimum.

CLOSED 2026-10-16 as `verified`, Phase 20's Task 20.2, commit `ed4d6ee8`. THE RULING'S SECOND CLAUSE IS INERT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: 'let the canvas accent move with it' assumes `--yunari-accent` aliases `--shell-warm` on the canvas side, and it does (`editor-shell.css:115`), but the token is read by no rule — so deepening `--shell-warm` moves no canvas accent at all. That is `vg-552`, filed from this task's trailer and expanded by the controller to ten unread `--yunari-*` tokens rather than two, and homed as Phase 20's Task 20.7. THE MEASURED FLOORS THE ROW NAMED ARE CORRECTED: ember `#ff7e6e` on `rgb(247,226,210)` is 1.98:1 as the row said, but the controller's re-run measures moss and plum at 5.47:1 and 5.19:1 after the fix rather than the 1.40 and 1.39 the row quoted for the pastels — the fix's own numbers, taken in the browser, are what the check above records. The pinned floor the ruling ordered deleted (`PINNED_FLOOR.invalid`) does not exist under that name: the file is `tests/e2e/design-language-readers.ts` and the constant is at `:119`.

MEASURED 2026-10-16 AT PHASE 20'S TASK 20.7 CLOSE (`7874e879`), and it corrects this row's own closing note in one word. The ruling's second clause — "let the canvas accent move with it" — was recorded here as INERT because `--yunari-accent` had no reader. It is worse than inert and better described as UNREACHABLE THROUGH THIS MECHANISM: `--yunari-accent` is a CSS custom property in the editor shell's stylesheet, and the canvas is Fabric-painted from the theme document, whose accent is `palette.accent` — a persisted theme value read by `renderer-core` (`scene/plan.ts`, `charts/chart-paint.ts`) and not by any stylesheet. So no CSS custom property can move the canvas accent, whatever reads it, and the alias was never the mechanism the ruling assumed. **WHAT THE RULING DID LAND**: `--shell-warm` is deepened in ember, moss and plum, and every `--warn` text in the product moved with it, which is the half that mattered. **WHAT IS LEFT OPEN AND IS NOT THIS ROW'S**: whether the shell's warm should ALSO move the theme document's `palette.accent` is a separate question about persisted theme data, and nobody has ruled on it. `--yunari-accent` is retired with the other nine unread declarations (`vg-552`, `7874e879`), and the two prose sites that described its job are corrected in that commit.
check: `--shell-warm` is deepened in ember, moss and plum so every `--warn` text clears §5's 4.5:1: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/design-language-contrast.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` 8 passed, exit 0. The red proof is the controller's: with ember's `--shell-warm` reverted to the pastel `#ff7e6e`, the same spec fails `ember: invalid is 1.98:1, below 4.5:1 — rgb(255, 126, 110) on rgb(247,226,210)` (1 failed, 7 passed, exit 1), and the restore is `cmp`-identical before the green re-run. Measured on `--shell-surface`: ember `#b81400` 5.34:1, moss `#7a5800` 5.47:1, plum `#b82100` 5.19:1.

title: The elevation ladder is declared twice as --elev-1..3 and --shadow-raised/--shadow-overlay, and three of the five names are consumed by nothing
detail:
FOUND WHILE DESIGNING THE DESIGN.MD ADOPTION SPEC (2026-10-10), NOT BY A FAILING TEST. editor-shell.css's @theme static block declares the bible section 3 elevation ladder -- --elev-1 (0 8px 20px #00000059), --elev-2 (0 18px 44px #00000099) and --elev-3 (0 24px 60px #000000b3) -- and beside it two older shadow names that match no level the bible states: --shadow-raised (0 12px 28px #0000003d) and --shadow-overlay (0 18px 44px #0006). MEASURED USES (grep for var() over packages/ and tests/): --shadow-raised 2, --elev-1 2, --elev-2 2, --shadow-overlay 0, --elev-3 0. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED: the two pairs may be deliberately different rather than duplicates -- a softer raised shadow on one surface, with the bible ladder added later -- and nothing in the repo says which, which is why this is filed rather than fixed on the fly (AGENTS.md: a cause that is not established gets a row, not a guess). WHY IT MATTERS: one concept (how deep a surface sits) has two vocabularies and nothing reconciles them, so a new surface can be raised by either; and the same block's own comment says the declared-and-never-consumed state is what the token ratchet exists to shrink, so three dead names is that state left standing. NOT ANSWERED BY THE DESIGN.MD ADOPTION: that work (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-design-md-replaces-the-bible-design.md) deliberately changes no runtime value, and the DESIGN.md token schema has no elevation or shadow group, so elevation stays prose there. CLOSE THIS once the two vocabularies are reconciled to one ladder with a reason recorded for any name that survives.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller as a code/architecture correctness question. ONE LADDER SURVIVES: --elev-1, --elev-2 and --elev-3, and --shadow-raised and --shadow-overlay are deleted, with the two --shadow-raised consumers re-pointed to the nearest ladder step in the same commit. THE ROWS COUNT DOES NOT REPRODUCE: measured in source with dist and node_modules excluded, each of --elev-1/2/3 has one consumer, --shadow-raised has two and --shadow-overlay has none -- not three unconsumed of five. What does reproduce is the duplicate: --shadow-overlay's declared value (0 18px 44px #0006) is the same depth as --elev-2's (0 18px 44px #00000099, :465), so the surviving vocabulary is the one the design language names. COST IF WRONG: two surfaces shift their depth by one step, which the browser shows immediately.

CLOSED 2026-10-16 as `verified`, Phase 20's Task 20.1, commit `b9566db1`. THE RULING'S CONSUMER COUNTS WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED HERE: measured in source with `dist/` and `node_modules/` excluded, `--elev-1`, `--elev-2` and `--elev-3` each had one consumer, `--shadow-raised` two and `--shadow-overlay` none — so it was one dead name, not three dead of five. What did reproduce is the duplicate: `--shadow-overlay`'s `0 18px 44px #0006` is `--elev-2`'s depth. THE SURVIVING STEP IS `--elev-2` AND NOT THE NUMERICALLY NEARER `--elev-1`: DESIGN.md §3's row 2 is 'Menus, popovers, tooltips', which is what both consumers are, and taking `--elev-1` would have left `--elev-2` declared and consumed by nothing — the state the block's own comment says the ratchet exists to shrink. THE CONTROLLER'S BRIEF WAS WRONG IN TWO PLACES AND THE SEAT REFUSED IT RATHER THAN FOLLOWING IT: the second `--shadow-raised` consumer is `.editor-shell-menu-popup` (selector `:863`, shadow `:881`), not `.editor-shell-publish-label`; and the comment above the publish popup was TRUE rather than stale, because `--elev-3` is `.editor-shell-dialog`'s. Cause: the controller read two concatenated `sed` ranges and assigned the wrong selector. Both corrections are recorded in the plan's Task 20.1 annotation with a dated `CORRECTED 2026-10-16` paragraph, and the false claim also stands in the un-amendable body of `c6eeba59`.

title: A well's horizontal padding is 6px, where bible section 3's table assigns 4px to inside-a-control and the mockup draws 8px
detail:

WHY THE GATE DOES NOT CATCH IT: `design-language.spec.ts` asserts that every authored spacing value is a step from section 3, which 6px is; it cannot see that the table assigns that step elsewhere, and no closed assertion can without the table becoming code. NOT FIXED HERE because the repair is a design ruling between three authorities and it moves the width of every control, including the 36px value well and the 246px pane's own gutters. SEVERITY: low - the chrome reads correctly today and only the step assignment is wrong.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: 6px. The product ships 6 and the drawing's own value well draws 4px 6px for the same element, so the mockup agrees with the product where it draws a well; section 3's 4px is the step inside a control rather than this row's horizontal padding, and the mockup's 5px 8px wells are the half that is corrected.
