title: The drawings invent the treatment of two controls no original draws - the segmented control and the in-button chord - so a surface the product has is given a gold target that no normative source states
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 9'S TASK REVIEW (2026-10-10), reviewing commit 5773f652 against the user's ruling that the original mockup style is the gold target while the content is corrected to the product. THE GAP: `docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html` and `shell.html` draw two surfaces that no original draws and that the bible's closed control vocabulary does not name - the segmented control (Left/Centre/Right, Top/Middle/Bottom; the product's `control-segmented.tsx`) and the chord drawn INSIDE the publish trigger (the product renders `<kbd class="editor-shell-primary-key">` as a child of the trigger at `publish-control.tsx:145`, where the original drew a standalone chip). The drawings are right that the surfaces exist - that is content, and the user's ruling puts content on the product's side - but their **treatment** is invented by extending the well idiom, and treatment is the half the user ruled is gold. CONSEQUENCE: the in-button chip's border is `#06131a59` in the drawing, about 35%, where the product composes `color-mix(currentColor 45%, transparent)` - a numeric drift between the drawing and the product that no `PARITY` row asserts, because no row reads either drawing today. Under spec section 13 as amended a deliberate difference must name a normative source that requires it, and there is none for a treatment nobody has ruled on. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the drawn treatment is what the original's author would have drawn, or the implementer's reasonable extension - the review found no original that draws either control, so the question cannot be answered from the drawings. FLAGGED AS MINOR BY THE REVIEW, and filed rather than fixed because the fix is a ruling on the treatment, not an edit. OWNED BY NO PLAN: plan 7 Task 8 makes the two control drawings read by a test (its Step 1 adds the PARITY rows), which is what would catch the drift once the treatment is settled. What would settle it: a ruling naming the treatment for a control the originals do not draw - most cheaply, the product's own composed value adopted as the drawing's, since the drawing is otherwise a copy of the product's treatment for every surface that has an original.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE PRODUCT'S COMPOSED VALUES STAND AS THE DRAWINGS' VALUES. The segmented control and the in-button chord keep the composed paint -- the chip border as color-mix(currentColor 45%) -- and the drawings are corrected where they differ, rather than a drawn value being ruled for them.

CITATION CORRECTED 2026-10-16 (§8.2). The rule this row measures is `border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 45%, transparent)` in `editor-shell.css`, which still exists, so this is a moved line rather than a changed value: the row's number pointed at `color: var(--muted)` in an unrelated block. The line number is dropped rather than re-pointed — the sentence already quotes the value, and a fresh number re-arms the same rot. PATH CHECKED 2026-10-16 (§8.11), no drift. All three paths this row cites resolve once the extension is read in full — `components/ui/control-segmented.tsx`, the publish trigger's own control, and `editor-shell/editor-shell.css` — so the §8.2 correction above is the whole of what this row owed and the §8.11 half is discharged rather than deferred.

CLOSED 2026-10-16 as `verified` on its CHORD HALF ONLY, Phase 20's Task 20.4, commit `5ea10439`. THE RULING NAMES TWO CONTROLS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM DIFFERS BY A VALUE. The in-button chord is a one-declaration drift and it is corrected: the drawing carried the literal `#06131a59` (alpha 0x59 = 34.9%) where the product composes `color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 45%, transparent)`, and the drawing now carries the same expression, so the two cannot drift again. THE SEGMENTED CONTROL'S HALF IS SPLIT OUT AS `vg-554`, NOT SILENTLY DROPPED, and the reason is that the ruling's premise for it does not reproduce: the ruling says *"the chip border as color-mix(currentColor 45%)"*, and the segmented chip draws NO BORDER AT ALL — only the container does, and its `--well-edge` equals `--shell-edge` `#242b34` under graphite, so the named difference does not exist. Measured on the built fixture with the palette settled, the two treatments differ in six declarations and not one: the product's `ToggleGroup` container is `bg-panel-2` filled at `padding:4px`, `gap:4px` and `rounded-md` while both drawings draw a transparent container with `border:1px solid var(--well-edge)` and no padding or gap; and the product's pressed chip is `var(--stage)` at `border-radius:4px` and `padding:4px 8px` while the drawings draw edge-to-edge chips with no radius, hairline dividers and a `var(--well)` fill. Correcting those is a redraw of the control rather than a value correction, which is the decision `vg-554` carries.

title: Ten of the fifteen `--yunari-*` declarations in the shell's control block are read by no rule, so the block's own comment describes jobs those tokens do not have
detail:
FOUND BY THE SEAT IMPLEMENTING PHASE 20'S TASK 20.2 (`vg-201`), which filed it as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer naming TWO tokens — `--yunari-accent` and `--yunari-accent-dim`. THE CONTROLLER EXPANDED IT BY MEASUREMENT, and the count is ten of fifteen, not two. THE MEASUREMENT, per token by name, `grep -rn "var(--yunari-<t>)" src/web --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.css`, with `dist/` and `node_modules/` excluded: `--yunari-canvas-bg` 1 reader, `--yunari-control-bg` 5, `--yunari-subdued` 1, `--yunari-scrollbar-thumb` 3, `--yunari-scrollbar-track` 3 — and **zero** for `--yunari-text`, `--yunari-panel-bg`, `--yunari-panel-border`, `--yunari-control-border`, `--yunari-input-bg`, `--yunari-muted`, `--yunari-selection-bg`, `--yunari-accent`, `--yunari-accent-dim` and `--yunari-guide`. THE NEGATIVE IS SEARCHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is what a read-by-nothing claim needs: the block sits on a plain `:root` and NOT inside `@theme` (the file's two `@theme` blocks are at :489 and :555), so Tailwind generates no utility from these names; a repo-wide sweep finds no `setProperty` for a theme token outside `node_modules`; no template constructs a `--yunari-…` name (every backticked mention is prose in `editor-shell.css` or a test comment); and a sweep for `yunari-` NOT preceded by `--` over `src/web` returns only DOM element ids (`yunari-chart-binding-*`, `yunari-pane-note`), which are unrelated to the token names. WHY IT MATTERS, and the reason it is not merely tidy-up: the block's own comment at `editor-shell.css:91-99` describes LIVE jobs for tokens nothing reads — `--yunari-input-bg` is 'a text field's own white', `--yunari-subdued` and `--yunari-selection-bg` 'sit between the shell's muted and its surface', and `--yunari-accent` is 'the control layer's highlight', brown rather than ink. A declaration whose comment describes a job it does not have is the same defect `vg-312` closed for `--shell-flat`: a knob that lies, where changing it moves nothing and fails nothing. AND ONE RULING DEPENDS ON IT: `vg-201`'s ruling says 'let the canvas accent move with it', justified by `--yunari-accent` aliasing `--shell-warm` 'on the canvas side' — but with no reader, deepening `--shell-warm` moves no canvas accent at all, so that half of the ruling is inert today. NOT FIXED ON THE FLY because the disposition is a vocabulary decision and not a patch: each of the ten is either retired the way `--shell-flat` was, or wired to the surface its comment names, and which is right turns on whether the reference's control layer is still a destination the shell is migrating to — the question `vg-426` says nothing measures. A token kept because a comment describes it is not a decision; the reason has to be a rule that reads it. Homed as Phase 20's Task 20.7, the phase whose subject is the token vocabulary.

CLOSED 2026-10-16 as `verified`, Phase 20's Task 20.7, commit `7874e879`. ALL TEN ARE RETIRED AND NONE IS WIRED, because the seat checked each named surface against the product and none exists: the five plain aliases (`text`, `panel-bg`, `panel-border`, `control-border`, `muted`) duplicate `--shell-*` roles every surface already reads directly; `--yunari-input-bg`'s "text field's own white" has no white surface, because the field is `bg-transparent` inside `ControlWell`, which is `bg-panel-2` inside `border-edge` (`control-well.tsx:91`, `control-text.tsx:101`); `--yunari-selection-bg` has no reader because the selected layer row paints `color-mix(in srgb, var(--shell-text) 14%, transparent)` (`editor-shell.css:2220`); and `--yunari-guide` has no reader because guides are Fabric's `GUIDE_COLOR` in `snap-manager/constants.ts:2`. THE FOOTPRINT WAS ONE DECLARATION EACH, unlike `vg-312`'s eight: every one was declared once, in the `:root` block, with no test mention and no `--yunari-*` name in any mockup, and two prose sites that described the retired jobs are corrected in the same commit (`editor-shell.css`'s ember comment and `design-language-readers.ts`'s `PINNED_FLOOR` note). **THE ROW'S TWO REFINEMENTS WERE RE-MEASURED BY THE CONTROLLER AND BOTH HOLD**: there are three `setProperty(` calls in `src/web` and none takes a `--yunari-*` key — `composition-pane.tsx:538` and `:542` set `--layer-dropline-top` and `--layer-dropline-left`, and `cursor-indicator.ts:105` iterates `CURSOR_INDICATOR_STYLES`, whose keys are plain CSS properties — and the sweep for `yunari-` not preceded by `--` returns DOM hooks and not token names, though it also walks `src/web/.agent-scratch/`, which is gitignored scratch and inflates any `src/web` walk. **THE ROW'S OWN CLAIM ABOUT `vg-201` IS CORRECTED IN ONE WORD**: see that row's dated note — the ruling's second clause is not merely inert, it is unreachable through a CSS custom property at all, and the canvas's accent is a persisted theme value rather than a stylesheet one.
check: The ten `--yunari-*` declarations are retired and the control block's own comment now describes only the five that stay, so no token's comment describes a job it does not have. Re-run of the row's own command, per token by name, reads `--yunari-canvas-bg` 1, `--yunari-control-bg` 5, `--yunari-subdued` 1, `--yunari-scrollbar-thumb` 3 and `--yunari-scrollbar-track` 3, and zero for the ten, which are declared nowhere. `npx vitest run packages/editor` 150 files / 1962 passed exit 0; `npm run design:check` exit 0.

title: Nothing guards the `@theme static` block's absences, so a retired shadow name can be declared again with every gate green
detail:
FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER WHILE RUNNING `vg-261`'S RED PROOF, and it is the reason that proof could not be run: there is no guard to cut. `vg-261`'s fix deleted `--shadow-raised` and `--shadow-overlay` from the `@theme static` block and re-pointed their two consumers, and AGENTS.md asks that a new regression test fail when the fix is disabled before it is trusted — for this fix, nothing fails. MEASURED, one site at a time: the `@theme` value pin at `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts:339` is `expect(Object.fromEntries(values)).toMatchObject({ … })`, which is non-exhaustive, so an ADDED name is never a failure and only a changed PINNED value is; the list at `:296-310` is a forbidden list — `expect(onRoot).not.toContain(token)` — over the type scale, and its purpose is that `:root` beats `@layer theme`, not that the vocabulary is closed; `scripts/design-tokens.mjs` checks literals in gated files and the tier-2 allowlist's consumption, not the token set, and its only `--shadow-raised` is a fixture string inside its own self-test at `:501` (`tests/scripts/design-md.test.ts:99` is a fixture too); and `tests/e2e/shell-palette-tokens.spec.ts`'s `themeToken()` samples tokens by name and throws on an absent one, which catches a REMOVAL and never an addition. So the surviving guard is one-directional: it notices a token that went away and not one that came back, which is the direction a duplicate vocabulary re-enters by. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE NAME: the same shape governs every retirement Phase 20 makes — `vg-312`'s `--shell-flat` has a guard only because the `NOT_A_COLOUR` exclusion set is a length assertion, which is incidental rather than designed — so the phase is deleting vocabulary with no general instrument that says the vocabulary stayed deleted. NOT FIXED ON THE FLY because the guard's SHAPE is a decision and not a patch: an exhaustive assertion over the whole `@theme static` block would redden on every legitimate addition, since the block also carries the `--color-*` aliases and the type scale, so the open question is the granularity — a closed set per family, a per-retirement absence assertion, or a comment the reviewer reads. Homed as a clause of Phase 20's Task 20.7, the task whose subject is what the token vocabulary keeps and what asserts it.

CLOSED 2026-10-16 as `verified`, Phase 20's Task 20.7, commit `150ad617`. THE GRANULARITY CHOSEN IS A PER-RETIREMENT LIST, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic: an exhaustive assertion over `@theme static` would redden on every legitimate addition because that block also carries the type scale and the `--color-*` aliases, and one over the `:root` control block would redden because it carries the §4 roles — so a closed set over either is a maintenance tax that a reviewer would learn to edit rather than read. `RETIRED_TOKENS` is instead the vocabulary this phase closed, and **a name joins it when it is retired**, which is the one moment the fact is known. Comments are blanked before the match rather than removed, so a prose mention is not read as a declaration and a failure message keeps its line number. **THE CONTROLLER RE-RAN THE RED PROOF ON ONE NAME PER RETIREMENT COMMIT** rather than trusting the seat's sweep of all thirteen: `--shadow-raised` (20.1), `--shell-flat` (20.3) and `--yunari-accent` (20.7) each read exit 1 with the case's own message, and each restore is `cmp`-identical. **This is the guard `vg-261`'s close found missing**, and it is the first assertion in the file that fails on an ADDITION rather than a removal.
check: `RETIRED_TOKENS` in `editor-shell.tokens.test.ts` names all thirteen names this phase retired — `--shadow-raised` and `--shadow-overlay` (20.1), `--shell-flat` (20.3) and the ten `--yunari-*` (20.7) — and one case asserts none is declared again and none is read again, so a retired shadow name can no longer be declared again with every gate green. Red proof re-run by the controller, one name per retirement commit: baseline green 14/14 exit 0, and re-declaring `--shadow-raised`, `--shell-flat` or `--yunari-accent` inside `@theme static` each reads exit 1 on `<name> is declared again, so a name this phase retired is back`, with every restore `cmp`-identical.

title: The segmented control's drawn treatment differs from the product's in six declarations, and the header's publish trigger appears in no registered capture
detail:
FOUND BY THE SEAT IMPLEMENTING PHASE 20'S TASK 20.4 (`vg-301`), which stopped rather than redrawing a control the ruling described as one declaration away, and filed it as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `5ea10439`. MEASURED ON THE BUILT FIXTURE, palette settled: the product's `ToggleGroup` container (`components/ui/control-segmented.tsx:78`) is `bg-panel-2` filled — graphite `#171c23`, editorial `#fffdf7` — with `padding:4px`, `gap:4px` and `rounded-md`, and its pressed chip is `var(--stage)` — graphite `#0b0e12`, editorial `#f5f1e8` — at `border-radius:4px` and `padding:4px 8px`; while BOTH drawings (`docs/design/mockups/current/controls.html:48-77` and `current/controls-editorial.html:48-78`) draw a TRANSPARENT container with `border:1px solid var(--well-edge)` and no padding or gap, edge-to-edge chips with no radius and hairline dividers, and a pressed chip filled `var(--well)`. Six declarations differ, not the one the ruling names. THE RULING'S NAMED DIFFERENCE DOES NOT EXIST FOR THIS CONTROL: `vg-301`'s ruling says *"the chip border as color-mix(currentColor 45%)"*, but the segmented chip draws no border at all — only the container does, and its `--well-edge` equals `--shell-edge` `#242b34` under graphite — and `color-mix` over `currentColor` is one site in the whole product, `.editor-shell-primary-key`'s, which is the chord `vg-301` closed on. WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT AN EDIT: the ruling's operative sentence is *"the drawings are corrected where they differ"*, and read literally that covers this — but the difference is a redraw of the control's whole drawn treatment rather than a value correction, and one numeric difference is entangled with a second, since under editorial `--well` is already `#f5f1e8` and equals `--stage` while that drawing's `--bg`/`--panel2` are swapped against the product's editorial palette, so correcting the pressed fill alone is not available without a correction nobody ruled. THE SECOND CLAUSE, from the same task: NO REGISTERED CAPTURE SHOWS THE CORRECTED ELEMENT AT ALL. `shell-capture-add.png`, `shell-capture-graphite.png` and `shell-capture-glyphs.png` are taken on the editor preview, where `PublishControl` returns `null` because no host answers `/api/hosting`, so the header in all three draws no publish trigger and no chord — the seat read both PNGs and did not rebuild them, because the corrected value is not in them and a rebuild is clock-dependent churn. Homed as Phase 20's Task 20.8, added for it: the phase whose subject is the design tokens and the drawings they came from. MEASUREMENT TRAP WORTH KEEPING: `.editor-shell button` carries a 140 ms `background-color` transition, so a palette probe read without settling returns an INTERPOLATED colour — the seat's first reads gave `rgb(11,14,18)` and then `rgb(155,154,150)` for the same chip, both mid-fade, and 400 ms of settling fixed it.

CLOSED 2026-10-17 as `verified`, Phase 20's Task 20.8, commit `e4785eaa`. **THE ROW'S OWN COUNT IS CORRECTED HERE: the drawn treatment differed in EIGHT declarations, not six.** The six the row named are the container's fill, padding and gap and the chip's radius, padding and pressed fill; the seat found two more and settled both deliberately rather than silently. The first is the **middle chips' `border-left`/`border-right` hairlines**, which the product does not draw at all, and they are removed. title: `current/controls-editorial.html`'s palette table is inverted against the product's editorial palette, so every fill in that drawing lands on the wrong role
detail: FOUND BY THE SEAT IMPLEMENTING PHASE 20'S TASK 20.8 (`vg-554`), which hit it while correcting the segmented control and filed it as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `e4785eaa` rather than extending the redraw. MEASURED, and the two fill roles are demonstrably swapped: that drawing's table at `controls-editorial.html:19` declares `--bg:#fffdf7` and `--panel2:#f5f1e8`, where the product's editorial palette has `--shell-backdrop: #f5f1e8` and `--shell-surface-strong: #fffdf7`, and `mockup-values.ts`'s `SHELL_ROLES` maps `--bg` to `--shell-backdrop` (`:187`) and `--panel2` to `--shell-surface-strong` (`:190`). So the two fill declarations Task 20.8 landed render that ground's paper and cream inverted relative to the product's editorial, and the seat measured it in the browser: the container renders `rgb(245,241,232)` and the pressed chip `rgb(255,253,247)`. WHAT SETTLES THAT IT IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A HAND-DRAWN GROUND: `docs/design/mockups/README.md:25` describes this file as *"the same column on the editorial ground — the same file with the token table swapped, so a hard-coded colour cannot hide in it"*, so its table is meant to BE the editorial palette's values in the roles it names, and a swap defeats the file's whole purpose. THE DIVERGENCE IS WIDER THAN THOSE TWO and the rest needs the same ruling rather than a second guess: `--edge:#e4ddcb` against the product's editorial `--shell-edge: #14120e`, and `--accent:#0d7a6a` against `--shell-accent: #14120e`, both measured here, with `--well-edge:#b8af9d` having no product counterpart to compare against at all. WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: correcting the table is a palette-wide correction nobody ruled, and this phase's named failure mode is *"correcting a drawing to a value nobody ruled"* — the seat measured the divergence, named which values differ, and stopped, which is the right half of that trade. Homed as Phase 20's Task 20.9, added for it and for `vg-556`. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 20.9, and the two fills are corrected to the palette the file claims to draw: `--bg:#f5f1e8` and `--panel2:#fffdf7` at `controls-editorial.html:19`. THE LICENCE IS STRONGER THAN THE ONE THE ROW NAMED, and it was found while reading the product rather than the README: the editorial palette block aliases DESIGN.md §4's whole vocabulary per palette, so it declares the drawing's own token names — `--bg: var(--shell-backdrop)`, `--panel-2: var(--shell-surface-strong)`, `--edge: var(--shell-edge)`, `--accent: var(--shell-accent)`. The twin's table is therefore not merely 'meant to be' the editorial values; the product states the mapping outright, and two of the twin's declarations contradicted it. `README.md:46-49` is what makes that a correction rather than a style — where the current set and DESIGN.md disagree, DESIGN.md wins and the file is stale. THE SEAT READ `README.md:25` DIFFERENTLY AND SAID SO, which is why this close does not rest on it: the sentence says the two files differ only in the table, which does not by itself establish that the table must be role-exact. `vg-436`'s ruling was read against this row before the correction was accepted, because that ruling says the drawing's token table stays editorial and nothing is redrawn; it is not contravened, because its rejected option (a) was a redraw against `light`'s mint and its rationale was that a redraw 'would change what the parity instrument checks for that row in exchange for fixing a name'. This correction moves the table toward the editorial reading `vg-436` chose, and changes no instrument row. WHAT THIS CLOSE DOES NOT COVER: `--edge`, `--edge2`, `--faint` and `--accent` still contradict the same alias block, filed as `vg-558`, and `--well`, `--well-edge`, `--kind`, `--value`, `--knob` and `--knob-edge` name no §4 role at all and are left.

The wider divergence in the same table is `vg-558`.

title: The reuse gate is satisfied forever by any older note claiming the same directory
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 3, TASK 1. scripts/reuse-gate.mjs answers "has any note in docs/decisions/ ever claimed this path", not "is this change argued for". 0005-chart-glow-is-skipped-pending-an-artboard-unit.md claims src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/ and 0022/0023 claim src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/theme/, so a first write to either returns EXIT=0 before any note about that change exists - measured with printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts"}}' | node scripts/reuse-gate.mjs. The README calls the check deliberately blunt and presence-only, so that a weak note must be caught in review; this is a different property: the gate is a one-shot latch per directory, so it guards the first change to a boundary and nothing after it. Whether a per-change claim, a staleness rule, or nothing at all is wanted is a design decision, not a fix.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: A NOTE MUST CLAIM THE FILE, NOT THE DIRECTORY. A path claim matches the file being written rather than a directory prefix, so 0005's claim on charts/ stops licensing every later change in it and the gate answers the question it appears to answer. The blunt, presence-only reading stays; what changes is the unit a claim is made in. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.1, and the ruling is applied as it reads: `covers()` is now `claimed.some((c) => rel === c)` — a claim names the file being written and only that file. The trailing-slash branch and the file-as-directory arm were **deleted rather than narrowed**, and both were measured before the deletion rather than assumed: the trailing-slash branch's `rel.startsWith(base)` has no separator, so a claim on `charts/` would also have covered a sibling named `chartsomething`, and **no such sibling exists**, so it was real in code and unreachable in fact; the non-slash arm's `startsWith(base + "/")` was **dead**, checked pairwise over all 63 claims, none of which is a prefix-directory of another. **The blunt, presence-only reading stays**, as the ruling requires. The registry is re-pointed in the same commit: 14 notes carried 15 directory claims and now carry 80 distinct file claims and no directory claim at all, each list read from the note and the commit that landed it. `docs/decisions/0059` is landed before the first write to `scripts/`. **The brief's expected probe value was wrong and the seat said so**: it predicted `charts/settings-fields.ts` would return EXIT=2, and it returns EXIT=0 correctly, because `0028` is the note whose decision IS the descriptor table in that file and it claims it after the re-point — the fix's effect is visible on `charts/grid.ts` instead. **Two live-registry self-test cases were added**, which is `vg-425`'s other half: the old cases asserted against a synthetic `claimed` array, so no case could see the real registry.
check: The gate refuses a write to a watchlisted path no note claims, and allows one a note does: `printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/grid.ts"}}' | node scripts/reuse-gate.mjs` returns EXIT=2 where it returned EXIT=0 before the fix, and the same probe for `charts/settings-fields.ts` returns EXIT=0 because `0028` claims that file after the re-point; `node scripts/reuse-gate.mjs --self-test` is 12 cases, exit 0, and reverting `covers()` reddens 'refuses a file under a directory claim' at exit 1.

title: The reuse gate cannot refuse a new file in most of its watchlisted directories, because a note claiming the directory covers everything beneath it
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER (2026-10-13) WHILE CHECKING WHETHER TWO LIVE SEATS WERE BLOCKED BY THE GATE -- they were not, and finding out why surfaced this. `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`'s `covers()` treats a `Paths:` claim ending in `/` as covering every path beneath it, so a note that claims a DIRECTORY permits a first write to ANY file in it, including files that did not exist when the note was written and that the note never discusses. THE MEASUREMENT, taken by piping a synthetic path for every watchlist entry through the gate itself (`{tool_input:{file_path}}` on stdin; the probe lives at `C:\tmp\yunari-drain\gate-audit.mjs`): **16 of the 20 watchlist entries allow a brand-new file.** The four that can still refuse are anchored file entries or the bare `scripts/` -- `scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts`, `scene-fabric/src/object-asset.ts`, `renderer-core/src/data/protocol.ts`, `scripts/`. Every directory entry is open, and the notes claiming them are about other decisions: `renderer-core/src/theme/` is claimed by 0022, 0023, 0028 and 0041; `editor/src/components/ui/` by 0033, 0036, 0037 and 0038; `renderer-core/src/charts/` by 0028; and `host/src/providers/` -- a directory whose whole purpose is that each provider's acquisition is its own mechanism -- is opened by a note naming one provider. WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: the gate's `--self-test` still passes and its refusal path still works, because it asserts against a SYNTHETIC `claimed` array (`reuse-gate.mjs:161-171`), so no self-test case can see the real registry. And whether a directory claim is MEANT to cover a new file is a decision, not an obvious correction -- the honest case for today's behaviour is that four notes collectively own the theme package. `docs/decisions/0025` decided a different question (how deep a bare entry matches) and does not settle this. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a rule stating whether a directory claim reaches files the note never discusses, then either a per-file claim convention or a gate that asks for a note naming the file. OWNER: `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`, with `docs/decisions/README.md`. SEVERITY: low at the surface and high in kind -- nothing breaks, and the boundary the watchlist names is unguarded for a new file in most of it, which is the gate's own stated failure ("a gate that cannot see a boundary is worse than no gate"). CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.1, which is the convention this row's park was waiting on. **The park is lifted rather than left standing**, because its own condition is met: the convention it waited for is the one that landed, and a closed row has nothing left to defer. **The park's own text is the evidence that it was the right park**: it named two things it waited on — a per-file claim convention, and a self-test that can see the live registry — and both landed together. The park also recorded that the count it reports — 16 of 20 watchlist entries allowing a brand-new file — **could not be re-derived, because the probe that took it lived outside the tree and is gone**. It was re-derived here rather than inherited: one plausible new file under each of the five directory entries (`renderer-core/src/theme/`, `renderer-core/src/charts/`, `host/src/providers/`, `editor/src/components/ui/`, `scripts/`) is piped through the gate, and **all five now return EXIT=2** where `covers()`'s trailing-slash branch allowed all five. **The park's second half is discharged too**: the row's own reason for not being a one-line fix was that the self-test asserted against a synthetic `claimed` array so no case could see the real registry, and Task 21.1 added two cases that read it — one allowing a chart file a note names and one refusing a file no note names, both with paths found rather than pinned. **`vg-535` is not discharged by this**: it measures the hook not blocking at all, which is a different defect and stays open.
check: A brand-new file under every directory entry in the reuse gate's watchlist is now refused: piping `{tool_input:{file_path}}` for one new file beneath each of the five directory entries returns EXIT=2 five times out of five, where `covers()`'s trailing-slash branch allowed all five before. The gate's own `--self-test` is 12 cases exit 0, and two of them read the live registry rather than a synthetic array.

title: The §1–§10 marker range is a shared namespace, so rule 3 accepts a bare §N from another document's numbering as a claim on a DESIGN.md marker
detail:
FOUND BY the Task 2 review (2026-10-11, reviewed commit 127ff808), finding 1, filed rather than fixed. WHAT: scripts/design-md.mjs's citation rule 3 asserts that every `<!-- §N -->` marker in DESIGN.md is claimed by at least one citation, but its claim test is a bare text match over `docs/`, `src/` and `scripts/` with no notion of which document is speaking, and §1–§10 is a shared namespace. docs/product/requirements.md marks its own requirements `## §N — title` and carries a bare §7 (requirements.md:20, the Product and scope heading); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-editor-design-language-design.md numbers itself §1–§13. So an in-range §N from another document satisfies rule 3 for a DESIGN.md marker that nothing has actually cited. FAILURE SHAPE: if DESIGN.md's §7 marker's genuine citations were later removed, requirements.md's own §7 heading would keep rule 3 silent — the check would pass while the marker went unclaimed. DORMANT TODAY: §7 carries 178 genuine DESIGN.md claims and it is the only overlap (requirements' other markers are §31 and above); the review's independent census found each of the 18 markers carries 6–198 real claims, so no marker is currently satisfied only by a foreign §N. WHY NOT FIXED HERE: a correct fix needs a decision the plan does not make — whether a citation must come from a document that is *about* the design language, and if so which documents those are; inventing that policy inside a fix round would either over-exclude real claims or set a rule the plan owns, and the fix round was scoped to findings 2 and 3. THE SPEC'S D3 IS THE SOURCE: it claims every other §N in the range belongs to the redesign spec, which is false because requirements.md also uses §7. OWNER: whoever next touches the citation rule — the design-md-replaces-the-bible prose and code sweep (Tasks 4–5), or a follow-up to scripts/design-md.mjs. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on which documents' §N may claim a DESIGN.md marker, then encode that set as a source filter in the check. ALSO A SWEEP GUARD: Tasks 4 and 5 must not re-point a requirements.md §N as if it were a bible citation.

RULED 2026-10-12: A DECISION THE CHECK ENCODES: the citation namespace is DECLARED BY SOURCE, not inferred from the number. `scripts/design-md.mjs --cite` accepts any `§N` in the canonical range from any document, so `requirements.md`'s own §7 — which numbers that document's requirements — reads as a claim on `DESIGN.md`'s §7. The fix is a SOURCE SET: the check takes the list of documents whose `§N` are design-language citations (the redesign spec and the specs that build on it), declared where the canonical range is declared; `requirements.md` is NOT in it, because a document about the product's requirements is not a document about the design language and its numbers belong to itself. Two consequences stated so they are not rediscovered: `DESIGN.md` is the target and never a source, and the sweep's guard stands — Tasks 4 and 5 must not re-point a `requirements.md` §N as though it were a bible citation. Over-exclusion is the risk the row names, and the set bounds it: a document joins by being ABOUT the design language, which is a property a reviewer can check, unlike a number. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.2, decision note `0060`. The ruling's shape is what landed: the namespace is **declared by source, not inferred from the number**, and the set lives beside `CITE_NUMBERS` where the ruling says it belongs. `CITE_SOURCES` is six prefixes — `src/`, `scripts/`, `docs/decisions/`, `docs/design/`, `docs/superpowers/`, `docs/product/triage/` — and `isCitationSource` is the set's one rule, applied to the path each citation was read from. **The near-misses are the evidence the set was argued rather than guessed**: `requirements.md` (the ruling's own exclusion, which numbers its requirements `## §N — title`), `tester-runbook.md` (its own `## 0.`–`## 6.`), `docs/product/probes/README.md` (cites the runbook's §0), `docs/architecture/` (both censuses number their own `## 1.`–`## 4.`, and the README cites requirements §97), `docs/evidence/` (no in-range `§N` at all), the two `.jsonl` registers (already out by `CITE_EXTENSIONS`), `DESIGN.md` (target, never source) and `CITE_EXCLUDE`'s two files. **THE REPRODUCTION THE BRIEF ASKED FOR IS IMPOSSIBLE ON THE REAL TREE AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN EXCUSE**: §7 carries 179 claims, so removing all but `requirements.md`'s is not a tree edit. What replaced it: 193 tracked files carry an in-range `§N` and nine documents number their own sections and carry one, yet **0 of the 18 markers is claimed only by one area** — which is why every candidate set passes today and the set has to be argued rather than measured. The delta is recorded: §7 179→178, the one dropped being `requirements.md:20`'s own heading, and the only other markers to lose a claim (§1, §2, §3, §4, §6) lost an architecture census's or the runbook's numbering. **No marker lost all its claims.** The red proof was re-run by the controller rather than taken from the seat: disabling `isCitationSource` reddens exactly those three cases at exit 1, and the file was restored byte-identical before the green re-run. **A second consumer the brief did not know about** — `src/web/tests/e2e/mockup-values.test.ts` calls `checkCitations`, so the `{ path, text }` shape reached it and the gate caught it. The residual limit is `vg-560`.
check: The check takes a declared source set and no longer accepts a bare `§N` from a document that numbers itself: `scripts/design-md.mjs` declares `CITE_SOURCES` beside `CITE_NUMBERS` and `isCitationSource` filters every citation by the path it came from, so `requirements.md`'s own `## §7` heading is not a claim on `DESIGN.md`'s marker. `node scripts/design-md.mjs --cite` exit 0 (337 sources clean) and `node scripts/design-md.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (44 cases), three of which fail at exit 1 when `isCitationSource` is disabled: `a requirements.md §7 passes as its own number, and claims nothing`, the runbook's own §2 and §3, and an architecture census's own §3.

title: Nothing detects a committed capture that a later plan invalidates, so the shell-palette and keyboard-reference images sat two plans stale
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5 TASK 6 (commit b602dd13), by reading the images it was about to re-capture rather than by any test. The seven files committed until then under docs/evidence/screenshots/ (shell-palette-* x6 and keyboard-reference) were pictures of the PRE-PLAN-2 shell: no rail, a `Layers | Insert | Assets | Document` pane bar, a palette chip in the header, `Save package`. Plan 2 rebuilt all of that, and nothing noticed, because a capture is only ever refreshed by the action that owns it running again — and every registry in docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md and docs/design/mockups/README.md names an action and a file, never a surface version or a plan that produced it. Re-captured here against rebuilt bundles. CONSEQUENCE: visual evidence in the repo can contradict the product for an arbitrary number of plans while every gate stays green, which is the opposite of what spec §13 asks a capture to be. NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is a detection mechanism (a marker recording the commit or shell generation each image was taken against, checked by a gate, or an ownership link from a surface to its captures), which is design work no active plan owns. What would settle it: decide who owns a capture's freshness and express it as a check rather than as a habit.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence. THE REGISTRY OWNS A CAPTURES FRESHNESS, AND THE CHECK IS A RECORDED SHA AGAINST THE SURFACE IT DEPICTS. Each registered capture records the commit it was taken at and the surface paths it shows; a script reports a capture whose surface paths have commits after that sha, so a stale image is a finding rather than a habit. Today both READMEs name an action and a file and nothing about the product generation, which is why the shell-palette and keyboard-reference images could contradict the product for two plans with every gate green. COST IF WRONG: a new scanner and a manifest to maintain, and a capture whose surface paths are wrong is reported stale for the wrong reason -- which is visible and fixable, unlike the present silence. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.3, decision note `0061`. The ruling's shape is what landed: **the registry owns a capture's freshness, and the check is a recorded sha against the surface it depicts**. **The manifest is the copy table itself**, extended with two columns — `Taken at` (the commit that last wrote the action's own file) and `Surfaces` (backticked repo-relative paths) — rather than a `registry.json` beside it, because a second file would be the same eleven captures twice and adding a capture would mean editing two files, which is the drift the instrument exists to catch. The table does not re-list actions: those are Playwright titles in the spec files, which the capture workflow's `grep` input names, so a manifest repeating them would be a third list. **Bytes are never compared, and that is the recorded measurement rather than taste**: two runs of `captures the settings modal's three tabs` on one bundle produce different bytes at identical dimensions, so a byte-diff scanner reports that capture stale on every run. **THE FIRST LIVE RUN IS THE FINDING AND IT WAS REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: 11 registered captures, 11 stale, 0 broken, exit 1.** Every one is moved by `editor-shell.css` (17 commits since the recorded sha, newest `7874e879`, Task 20.7's token retirement) and by `editor-shell/` and `components/ui/` — so **Phase 20's own token and elevation work is the cause**, and the eleven are left alone because re-shooting is the action owner's job and needs built bundles, one worker and `YUNARI_CAPTURE=1`. **The self-test is chained into `gates:self-test`** rather than left as a script nobody runs, which is the pattern Task 21.7 states; the live run is a command rather than a gate step, because gating on it would hold every commit red until the eleven are re-shot. **The red proof was re-run by the controller rather than taken from the seat**: with `commitsAfter` disabled the self-test reddens the named case at exit 1 and the live run goes silent at `0 stale`, exit 0 — which is the defect itself — and the file was restored byte-identical before the green re-run. **Two gaps are filed rather than left in the note alone**: `vg-561` (the same README claims the two copies are the same bytes and nothing checks it) and `vg-562` (the three shell captures' surface sets omit the package that paints the stage they show).
check: A committed capture that a later commit invalidates is now reported rather than noticed by hand: `node scripts/capture-freshness.mjs` reads the registry's `Taken at` and `Surfaces` columns and runs `git log <sha>..HEAD -- <path>` per surface, exiting 1 on a finding — measured on the live tree it reports 11 registered captures, 11 stale, 0 broken. `node scripts/capture-freshness.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (5 cases), chained into `npm run gates:self-test`, and one case fails at exit 1 when `commitsAfter` is disabled: `reports a stale capture`.

title: The sweep has no instrument for the reverse direction: a class production source writes that no stylesheet defines
detail:
FOUND BY Task 2's independent review (2026-10-12), which recorded it as the opposite direction from that task's own question and deliberately did not chase it; VERIFIED by the controller before filing, with one repo-wide search. `settings-field.ts:248` writes `note.className = "yunari-field-hint"`, and the string `yunari-field-hint` occurs exactly ONCE in the entire checkout -- that write. No rule in `editor-shell.css` or `host/public/yunari-page.css` defines it. NOT ESTABLISHED that this instance is a defect, and it probably is not: six lines below, the same statement sets an inline `cssText` that hides the element (`position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;clip-path:inset(50%)`), so it is a screen-reader-only description node and a missing rule costs nothing visible. **The row is the GAP, not the instance**: Task 2's report reads CSS-to-source (which selectors the product still reaches) and Task 1's scanner reads modules and exports nothing imports, so a class that production writes and no stylesheet defines falls outside every instrument this sweep built -- and this example is harmless only by accident of the inline style beside it. SEVERITY: low for behaviour, moderate as a completeness finding about the sweep's own coverage. What settles it: a decision on whether the reverse direction is in scope at all. If it is, the cheap form is extending the selector instrument to read `className`/`classList` writes alongside `class=` literals, which is also the shape that would make the `PRODUCT` column independent of whether a name happens to appear in prose.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: THE REVERSE DIRECTION IS IN SCOPE, AND THE SELECTOR INSTRUMENT WIDENS. It reads className and classList writes alongside class= literals, so a class production writes that no stylesheet defines becomes visible and the PRODUCT column stops depending on whether a name happens to appear in prose. The one measured instance is harmless by accident, which is why the gap is closed before an instance arrives that is not. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.4, decision note `0062`. The ruling's shape is what landed: **the reverse direction is in scope, and the selector instrument widens to class writes**. **THE PLAN'S `Files:` LINE FOR THIS TASK NAMED A THING THAT DOES NOT EXIST** — *"Modify: the sweep script's selector instrument"* — because `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs` contains **0** occurrences of `selector`, `className`, `classList` or `class=`, and nothing under `scripts/` or in `src/web/package.json` read or wrote `docs/architecture/dead-selectors.md`. **The instrument was a one-off `node -e` command pasted into that document**, on its own stated argument that a command has *"no script to keep in step with the file it reads"*. The document keeps its reasoning and loses its command, so there is one executable copy. **THE `--self-test` IS CHAINED INTO `gates:self-test` AND THE LIVE RUN IS A COMMAND**, because it exits 1 at HEAD and gating on it would hold every commit red — the same distinction Task 21.3 drew. **THIS ROW'S OWN MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG AND THE SEAT MEASURED IT RATHER THAN INHERITING IT**: the detail says `yunari-field-hint` *"occurs exactly ONCE in the entire checkout"*, which is true of the **string** and not of the **direction** — the reverse reading reports **eleven** classes, the other ten never having been counted. title: The sweep's `redundant-export` tier counts a declaration-shaped occurrence as a use, so a symbol kept alive by its own object key or its own re-export reads as live
detail:
FOUND BY Task 4's independent review of the dead-code sweep (2026-10-12), verifying a claim the sweep's implementer raised and deliberately did not file. MECHANISM: the tier's liveness test is an occurrence of the symbol's name outside quoted strings in its own declaring file, and `panel:` inside an object literal satisfies it while being a KEY rather than a read. OBSERVED at the sweep's base commit `5854bed5`: the row for `panel` in `packages/editor/src/new-fabric-theme-globals.ts` read "the symbol is LIVE: its own declaring file uses it (2 occurrence(s) of the name outside quoted strings, the declaration that names it excluded)", and both occurrences are property keys -- `starterPalette.panel` (now `:84`, `panel: { name: "Panel", value: { kind: "solid", color: "#081523d9" } }`) and the second map's `panel: "#081523d9"` (now `:163`). Neither is a reference and the const had no reader, so the sweep deleted it in `93bb2c5f`; what flagged it was `noUnusedVariables` once the `export` keyword came off, so TYPECHECK IS THE BACKSTOP for this class rather than the tier. CONSEQUENCE, and it is the safe direction: every symbol whose name happens to appear as an object key in its own declaring file is withheld from the removal list, so this tier can only over-retain; the cost is survivors, never breakage, and the plan's bias prefers a survivor to a bad delete. It is nonetheless a precision defect in the instrument that produced the removal list, and it hid one deletion behind a verdict that read as evidence. FIX DIRECTION NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the tier should stop counting property keys, or whether the tier is meant as a pre-filter whose survivors typecheck re-tests -- deciding that is the work. Owner: `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`. VERIFIED by the review report at `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep/task-4-review.md`. SECOND INSTANCE, found 2026-10-12 by Task 5's independent review of the same sweep (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-12-the-dead-code-sweep/task-5-review.md`, attack 6) and carried by that task as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer in commit `c9ed9dcc`. The same self-use test is satisfied by a RE-EXPORT STATEMENT: `packages/player/src/artboard-crop.ts` re-exported `countable` and `EDGE_TOLERANCE`, and the tier read those re-export lines as in-file uses, which withheld both rows from the removal list. Verified in `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`: the tier asks `usesIn(selfUse.get(file), name)`, and `declaredExports` reads `export { x };` as declared exports, so a re-export is counted as a use of the name it re-exports. Task 5 removed the dead re-export anyway, on the grounds that the re-export line is the thing that needed removing rather than evidence that the symbol was live. CORRECTION TO THE TRAILER, for whoever picks this up: the trailer quotes the scanner as printing "(2 occurrence(s))" where it prints 1, because `usesDeclaration` subtracts the import specifier. AND THE TWO INSTANCES SHARE ONE FIX, which is why this is an amendment rather than a second row: the self-use test counts an occurrence that DECLARES the name (an object key, a re-export) as though it READ it, so the fix direction is stated once -- either the test excludes declaration-shaped occurrences, or the tier is treated as a pre-filter whose survivors typecheck re-tests. Owner: `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs`.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: A DECLARATION IS NOT A USE. The self-use test excludes declaration-shaped occurrences, so an object key or a re-export stops counting as a read of the name it declares and the redundant-export tier reports a symbol kept alive only by its own declaration. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.5, decision note `0063`. The ruling's shape is what landed: **a declaration is not a use**. `readsOutsideDeclaration` excludes exactly three shapes, each one that structurally cannot be a read of the binding: the declaration site (the name after `function|class|const|let|var|interface|type|enum|namespace`), a specifier in an import or export list (which is the re-export instance, and `declaredExports` already read `export { x }` as a declared export), and an object key (which needs `{`, `,` or a line start before and a `:` after — **the colon is the whole guard**, because without it `case name:` and `cond ? name : x` are swallowed). **The cost of a false positive is stated on the note and it is the unsafe direction**: the two export tiers take opposite remedies, so an exclusion firing on a read moves a live symbol from *"only the `export` keyword is unnecessary"* onto the removal list. Every rule is one that structurally cannot match a read, which is the test applied rather than a likelihood judgement. Recorded as limits and not excluded: `obj.name` (a property, not a binding, and not *declaration*-shaped, so the ruling does not reach it) and `const { panel } = obj` (over-retains, which is the safe direction). **THE ROW'S OWN TEXT CARRIES TWO FALSE CLAIMS AND THEY ARE CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT FOR THE NEXT READER.** (1) **Its *"CORRECTION TO THE TRAILER"* is itself wrong.** It asserts the trailer quotes the scanner as printing `"(2 occurrence(s))"` *"where it prints 1, because `usesDeclaration` subtracts the import specifier"* — but `usesDeclaration` **never existed in this repo** (`git log --all -S usesDeclaration -- scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs` is empty), and the pre-fix `usesOutsideDeclaration` was `Math.max(0, usesIn(text, name) - 1)`, so for `new-fabric-theme-globals.ts`'s `panel` — 3 occurrences at `93bb2c5f^` (`:24` the declaration, `:86` and `:165` two object keys) — it printed **2**. **The trailer's quote was right and the correction that overrode it was wrong.** (2) **Its *"typecheck is the backstop"* names the wrong owner.** No tsconfig in the repo enables `noUnusedLocals` or `noUnusedParameters`, so `npm run typecheck` would have flagged nothing; the rule that actually fired on `panel` is **Biome's `noUnusedVariables`** (`biome.json:14`, `error`, reached through `gate`'s `biome check ..`), and its sibling **`noUnusedImports`** (`biome.json:15`) covers the re-export class the same way, because removing a re-export leaves the import with no reader. So the backstop holds for **both** classes and its owner is Biome, not `tsc` — with the caveat the seat recorded: it fires only *after* the wrong remedy is applied, one commit later than this report. **STEP 2'S ANSWER IS THE EMPTY SET AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED**: the two instances the row names are already gone (`panel` deleted at `93bb2c5f`, the re-export at `c9ed9dcc`), and a base-to-HEAD diff of the sweep's own `--json` report shows the four tier counts identical (6/99/11/5), **0 rows added, 0 rows removed and 0 evidence numbers changed** — 105 evidence *sentences* were reworded, which is the fix's own text and not a finding. The classifier was proved against the two historical file contents instead: `panel` at `93bb2c5f^` goes 3 occurrences → **0 reads**, and `countable` and `EDGE_TOLERANCE` at `c9ed9dcc^` each go 2 → **0**, so each would now be reported `dead-export` where it was `redundant-export`. **The sweep's self-test went from 22 cases to 25**; the two cases the brief flagged as a trap were handled rather than weakened — `a redundant row reports uses, not occurrences` passes unchanged, and `every redundant row's number is its use count` became `...its read count` with `claimed === readsOutsideDeclaration(...)` instead of `usesIn(...) - 1`, which is the assertion that was wrong because it counted a declaration-shaped occurrence as a use. **The red proof was re-run by the controller, and the seat's stated recipe does not reproduce**: a copy of the script outside the repo cannot find the tree, because the sweep resolves its root from its own directory — the copy reddens 14 of 25 cases for the wrong reason. Patched **in place** the result reproduces exactly: **22 of 25 pass, exit 1**, the three failures being the three new fixtures. The file was restored byte-identical and the green re-run is exit 0. **One finding is filed rather than left in the commit**: `vg-564` (four documents cite line numbers into `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs` that had already drifted, and this is the fourth instance of a shape three archived rows each fixed once).
check: The `redundant-export` tier no longer counts a declaration-shaped occurrence as a use: `readsOutsideDeclaration` excludes the declaration site, an import or export specifier, and an object key, so a symbol kept alive only by its own object key or its own re-export reads as dead. Measured at HEAD the sweep's four tiers are unchanged in count — dead-export 6, redundant-export 99, test-only-consumer 11, unreachable-branch 5, identical to the base — so no symbol moved tier. `node scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (25 of 25 cases, from 22), and three of them fail at exit 1 when the pre-fix body is restored: `an object key is not a read`, `a re-export of an imported name is not a read`, `a value beside a key is still a read`.

title: The sweep's `barrel-only-export` tier is unreachable, so 133 candidate exports were never reported and the report's zero reads as a measurement
detail:
FOUND BY the final whole-branch review of the dead-code sweep (2026-10-12), a read-only seat, as one of its two load-bearing findings; REPRODUCED by the controller against the real classification loop before this row was written, because the seat's own evidence sat in an ignored directory a clone does not carry.  THE MECHANISM, and it is structural rather than a property of this tree. `scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs:705` is `if (prodConsumers.length > 0) continue;`, and it runs before the `barrel-only-export` branch at `:708`. A file's own package barrel reaches it by a re-export edge the scanner does follow, and the barrel is not a test file, so `prodConsumers` is non-empty for exactly the shape `:708` exists to report. Its condition can therefore only be evaluated when it is already false: the tier cannot fire for any input.  THE PLAN REQUIRES THAT SHAPE, in those words. Step 2 of Task 1: "`barrel-only-export` - a name whose only importer is its own package's `index.ts`." So the requirement is unimplemented, not merely unexercised, and the difference matters to whoever acts on this row: an unexercised kind may fire tomorrow, this one cannot fire at all. The ledger parked it at line 838 as "remains unexercised", which understates it by exactly that gap.  MEASURED, by a copy of the scanner with one filter corrected to exclude the file's own barrel from `prodConsumers`, run over the same tree at `93fa9a5a`: 240 candidates, of which `barrel-only-export` is 133, and the other kinds come out at exactly their HEAD counts (dead-export 8, redundant-export 83, test-only-consumer 7, unreachable-branch 9, and `no-importer-file` at 0, so it has no rows). The 133 are therefore pure additions and the existing 107 do not reclassify. By package: editor 1, fake-source 2, host 21, renderer-core 91, scene-fabric 18.  TWO DEFENSIBLE DEFINITIONS, and the disagreement is part of the defect rather than noise around it. The plan's literal wording - the only importer is the barrel, tests included - yields 76: those of the 133 whose evidence names no test importer. The code's own intent at `:708` - no production consumer other than the barrel, with test consumers disclosed in the row - yields all 133. Both measured: 76 rows have an empty test-importer list and 57 name test importers. Which one the tier means is a decision, and that is why this is filed rather than fixed on the spot, even though the filter itself is one condition.  NOT PROVEN DEAD, and nothing may be deleted on this row alone. A candidate is not a verdict. renderer-core's 91 (49 strict, 42 test-consumed) is consistent with a private library barrel wider than its consumers, but no row was adjudicated and the string-resolved vocabulary this repo resolves at runtime is invisible to the graph.  WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE THE SWEEP'S REMOVALS BEING SOUND. Nothing the sweep removed had been reported by the missing tier, so the removals stand. What does not stand is the picture: `docs/architecture/dead-code-candidates.md` reports this kind as 0 in its by-kind table and again in its delta table, which reads as a measurement that there are none, and its own disclosure said the kind "has never fired in this tree" - inviting the same conclusion instead of naming the incapability. The sweep's after-picture, 312 candidates to 107, is a floor rather than a measurement of what remains, and the report now says so.  REMEDY, and it is deliberately not taken inside the sweep: correct the filter, decide the tier's definition, re-run, and adjudicate the newly visible rows as a sweep of its own. Reopening a phase three reviews had closed, to make the candidate count larger rather than more correct, was the wrong trade at that plan's close.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: the barrel-only-export tier means NO PRODUCTION CONSUMER OTHER THAN THE BARREL, WITH TEST CONSUMERS DISCLOSED -- 133 candidates, not the plan's literal sole-importer shape's 76. A test importing a barrel export is disclosed in the report and does not hide the export from the tier, because a survivor costs a ticket and a deleted live symbol costs the product, so the bias stays on detection. The filter is corrected, the sweep is re-run, and the newly visible rows are adjudicated as a sweep of its own. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.6, decision note `0064`. The ruling's shape is what landed: **the tier means no production consumer other than the barrel, with test consumers disclosed** — 133 candidates as ruled, not the plan's literal sole-importer shape's 76, and the count is **132** at HEAD because the tree moved. **THE FIX IS ONE CONDITION**: `consumers.filter((file_) => !isTestFile(file_))` became `... && file_ !== barrel`, and the branch's now-vacuous `prodConsumers.length === 0 &&` clause was dropped with it, leaving `if (consumers.includes(barrel))`. The kind's header description and the row's evidence sentence were corrected with it (`no file` → `no production file`). **THE MEASUREMENT THE PHASE'S ACCEPTANCE ASKS FOR**: the command is `node scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs --json <path>`, and at `89c9a035` it reports 253 rows against the base's 121 — `barrel-only-export` **0 → 132**, with the other four kinds **identical at 11 / 6 / 99 / 5**, so **0 rows were added outside the tier and 0 removed**. By package the 132 are editor 1, fake-source 2, host 21, renderer-core 90, scene-fabric 18. **STEP 2'S ADJUDICATION IS GROUPED AND ITS WARRANT IS STATED**: every row is a name its package's `src/index.ts` re-exports and no production file imports, directly or through that barrel, so the grouping is by package barrel — 132 rows across 38 files and 5 packages. Over every production `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.mjs` outside each row's declaring file and barrel: a word-boundary name search found **8 collisions, all dismissed on inspection** (`ArtboardSize` and `Point`, each declared per package; `Interpolation`, a label string; `PieTotal`; `MEASUREMENT_SYSTEMS`, comments; and `bottom`/`right`/`countable`, common words plus the sweep's own fixture), and a quoted-string and kebab-case search found **none** of the string-resolved shapes the sweep's header lists. Per row: **85 live in their own file and test-consumed, 26 live in their own file with no consumer, 20 declared and read by nothing but a test (named in §3.4), and 1 with no reader at all** — `host/src/server.ts`'s `HostingPeer`. **NOTHING WAS DELETED**, which the row's own text demands: *"NOT PROVEN DEAD, and nothing may be deleted on this row alone. A candidate is not a verdict."* The invisibility limit is stated in §3.4 rather than implied — the graph is textual, and the searches cover the shapes it misses without being a proof of death. **THE TWO COMMENTS THAT RECORDED THE UNREACHABILITY WERE REWRITTEN AND `vg-386` IS NAMED IN NEITHER**: the docblock near the self-test and the comment above *"a barrel's re-export is followed as a route (an import is not)"* both asserted the branch *"is unreachable by construction"* and cited this row by name, and nothing would have reddened to say so, because that case exercises `barrelRoutes` rather than the tier. A file that still claims its own branch is unreachable is a worse artefact than the bug. A new case pins the fix — `barrel-only-export fires` — as a **count rather than a pinned file**, so Task 21.8 can still move the kind-fires checks. **THE REPORT IS HAND-AUTHORED AND WAS CORRECTED IN PLACE**, which was itself a false premise in this task's brief: nothing under `scripts/` or in `src/web/package.json` generates `docs/architecture/dead-code-candidates.md`, so the correction is an edit to a dated snapshot rather than to a generator. §1.1's by-kind row and total, §1.3's delta row and prose, and §3.4 were rewritten, and §4's `ROOT`-pinned recipe was removed. **A SECOND BRIEF PREMISE WAS FALSE AND THE SEAT MEASURED IT**: the brief said the report's disclosure *"said the kind has never fired in this tree"* — that phrase is **absent at HEAD** (`grep` returns 0; `git log -S` shows it entering at `149ecc88`/`6b3f1a1f` and leaving before HEAD), so what was actually stale was the present-tense *"the tier cannot fire"* claim, which is what the fix falsified and what was corrected. **A THIRD**: the brief carried the row's 133 and its 76/57 test-consumed split as current; at HEAD the count is **132** and the split is **105/27**. **The red proof was re-run by the controller rather than taken from the seat**: with the filter reverted in place, `--self-test` is **25 of 26, exit 1**, failing exactly `barrel-only-export fires (the production-consumer gate looks past the file's own barrel)`; the file was restored byte-identical and the green re-run is exit 0 (26 of 26). **Two documents were deliberately left alone and the reasoning is recorded rather than the omission**: `docs/product/triage/triage-B6.md` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain-design.md` still say *"today it reports zero"*, and both are dated records of this row's state at the sha they describe rather than current-truth documents — the same distinction the architecture snapshots rest on. `docs/architecture/dead-code-candidates.md` §3.2/§3.3 still cite line numbers into the sweep; those are `vg-564`'s.
check: The `barrel-only-export` tier is no longer unreachable, so the candidate exports it never reported are reported: the production-consumer gate now reads `!isTestFile(file_) && file_ !== barrel`, so a file's own package barrel no longer counts as a production consumer of the shape that branch exists to report. Measured with `node scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs --json <path>` at `89c9a035`, the sweep reports **253** rows where it reported 121 — `barrel-only-export` 0 → **132**, and the other four kinds identical (test-only-consumer 11, dead-export 6, redundant-export 99, unreachable-branch 5), so the 132 are pure additions and no existing row reclassified. `node scripts/dead-code-sweep.mjs --self-test` exit 0 (26 cases), and `barrel-only-export fires` fails at exit 1 when the filter is reverted.

title: `AGENTS.md`'s 800-line stop has no instrument: 47 tracked `src/web` files are past it, 33 named by no row, and the one-row-per-file policy that named the other 14 is a register that grows with the codebase
detail: MEASURED 2026-10-16 AT `5ad08048`, FOUND WHILE HOMING `vg-415` AND `vg-420` IN TASK 15.6 AND NOT PART OF IT. Method: `git ls-files src/web` restricted to `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.mjs`/`.css`, excluding `dist` and `node_modules`, counted by lines; a file counts as named when a register row's own TITLE carries its basename, because a row that mentions a file in its `detail` is not a row about that file. **47 files are over the 800-line stop and 33 of them are named by no row at all.** The 14 that are named: `editor.spec.ts` (5631), `editor-shell.css` (2788), `reference-theme.spec.ts` (2638), `mockup-values.ts` (1785), `themes/store.test.ts` (1662), `host/src/server.ts` (1608), `composition-panel.spec.ts` (1537), `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` (1373), `ui-copy.test.ts` (1056), `ui-copy.ts` (908), `runs.dom.test.ts` (818) — and `layer-panel.tsx`, `editor-session.ts` and `shell-layout.tsx`, whose rows (`vg-209`, `vg-374`, `vg-276`) are `verified` while the file the row named has since been overtaken by its own test. **THE ONE-ROW-PER-FILE POLICY HAS ALREADY FAILED TWICE OVER, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN THE COUNT.** `vg-209` closed on `layer-panel.tsx` at 838 lines; `layer-panel.dom.test.tsx` is now **1968** with no row. `vg-374` closed on `editor-session.ts`; `editor-session.dom.test.ts` is now **1707** with no row. `vg-394` and `vg-395` closed at Task 15.4 on the two files that task happened to know about, and the same class was found two rows short the same day (`vg-415`, `vg-420`). A policy that files one row per breaching file needs a filing per file per growth, and nothing reads the whole set — so the register's own size is the instrument, and it does not converge. **THE CUT IS NOT THE ONE `vg-426` JUST TOOK.** That row's token ratchet counts product source and excludes tests and fixtures, because a test asserting a hex is a test *about* a literal. This stop applies to test files too — `vg-415`, `vg-420`, `vg-394` and `vg-395` are all test files, and four of the six largest entries here are e2e specs. So a measure needs the other cut: **authored versus generated**, since `font-trios.generated.ts` is 28284 lines of generated data and `editor-shell.css` is a stylesheet the ratchet already parses. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the shape `vg-426` landed, not a row per file.** A check that reports the over-stop set with a ceiling that falls as files are split, so the number is visible and cannot grow silently. `AGENTS.md` states 500 as a signal and 800 as a stop; nothing in the repo computes either. **This row does not ask for 33 splits** — it asks for the measure that makes the next split a decision rather than a discovery. OWNER: `scripts/` (a new check, chained into `gates:self-test` the way the other eleven are). SEVERITY: low per file, and it compounds — this is the shape `vg-337`, `vg-394`, `vg-395`, `vg-415` and `vg-420` were each filed as, one at a time. CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.7, decision note `0065`. The instrument is `scripts/oversize-files.mjs` with `scripts/oversize-files.ceiling.json` (45 paths), chained into `gates:self-test` as its **14th** step. **THE CEILING IS A SET RATCHET THAT FAILS ON AN ADDITION ONLY** — a path over the stop that the ceiling does not name exits 1, while a ceiling entry no longer over the stop is **reported and never required to be removed**. That is what makes it not the brief's *"edit on every split"*: a breach that is split clears the failure with **no edit at all**, because the path was never in the ceiling, so the ceiling does not grow with the codebase. Rejected and recorded: a **count ratchet** (splitting one file and growing another keeps it flat, so the next breach is a discovery — this row's own failure) and **report-only** (nothing makes anyone run it). **RE-MEASURED AT HEAD, AND THE DISAGREEMENTS WITH THE CONTROLLER'S CROSS-CHECK ARE RECONCILED RATHER THAN PICKED.** The row's 47 over the stop and 33 unnamed were taken at `5ad08048`; at `5742a071` the reading is **667 tracked files, 46 over the stop before the cut, 1 generated, 45 authored over it, 109 past the 500 signal**, and **9 named by a row title against 37 named by none**. Two differences were found and both are fault lines in the row's own method: **the named/unnamed split is 9/37, not the controller's 10/36**, because `shell-layout.dom.test.tsx` is named by no title while `vg-276`'s title carries `shell-layout.tsx`, so a stem reading counts it — **the row is internally inconsistent on that one file**, its prose list of 14 counting it named while its own stated method does not; title: scripts/reuse-gate.mjs's watchlist names a path that no longer exists, so one of its entries can never fire

title: The dead-code sweep's self-test pins a live source file as its test-only-consumer case, so a task that legitimately mounts that file reddens the gate
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER AT THE PHASE 19 CLOSE (2026-10-16), running `npm run gate` at `014d38b3` — the first full gate since Phase 18 closed, because every task between ran only its focused suites. `gates:self-test` read **21/22 passed**, `failed: ['test-only-consumer lands on font-picker.tsx']`, and `npm run gate` exited 1. **THE CAUSE IS ESTABLISHED AND IT IS THIS DRAIN'S OWN WORK**: Task 19.1 (`055c7ecc`) mounted `FontPicker` from `selection-inspector/font-face-field.tsx`, which is exactly what `vg-268` and `vg-283` ruled and both closed on, so `font-picker.tsx` stopped being a test-only consumer and the sweep correctly stopped reporting it. **The sweep is right and the pin is stale** — the check was asserting the bug two rows existed to end. **THIS IS THE SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A ROW RATHER THAN A NOTE**: Phase 5's Acceptance records the first — `BootThemeOutcome` was exported from `boot-theme.ts`, the sweep's *negative* fixture, with no production importer, so `the negative case is absent from every kind` went red at `a50870b5` and was fixed at the consumer in `b1383446`; the gate then stayed red for the whole of Phase 6 because no close named the command and its exit code. **FIXED ON THE FLY AT THIS CLOSE, and the fix is the smaller half**: the check now pins `src/web/packages/editor/src/ui-copy-readers.ts` — a production-named file with no production importer, consumed by two test files, whose test-only status is permanent rather than incidental, because a test reader is supposed to have no production importer — under decision note `0058`, which carries the search. **WHAT REMAINS IS THE DESIGN QUESTION, NOT THE RED.** The self-test deliberately runs against the real tree: `the walk found the tree` counts > 400 files and `the walk found the test suite` counts > 200 test files, so **every file it names is one the product is free to change for good reasons**, and the field's answer is a fixture the tool owns — `repowise` runs its analyzer against `tests/fixtures/ts_sample` and asserts a planted dead interface and a planted orphan module; `pruneguard` keeps `fixtures/parity/<family>/<name>/` with an `expected.json` naming findings by path and symbol; `locrin` calls `fixture("dead_export", "flag")`; `astro-cli` verifies its gate by planting a deliberately-unreachable function and reading the gate fail. **Adopting that means keeping both**, and that is the work: a synthetic tree for the kind-fires checks, and the real tree for the invariants, because `no test file is ever a candidate`, `no package barrel is a no-importer-file` and `no ambient .d.ts is a candidate` are claims about *this* tree and would be vacuous against a synthetic one. The three other file-pinning checks (`settings-field.ts`, `card-library.ts`, `boot-theme.ts`) have the same fragility and move with it. **The searches are `0058`'s rungs 1-6 and are not repeated here.** NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a fixture tree would keep the self-test's cost acceptable, since the sweep walks the real tree today and a second walk is unmeasured. OWNER: Phase 21, Task 21.8 — the phase whose subject is the repo's own instruments. **CLOSED 2026-10-17 BY TASK 21.8, decision note `0067`.** The design question this row left open is answered: **the kind-fires checks run against a fixture tree the tool owns, and both real-tree walks stay.** The fixture is five files written to `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "dead-code-sweep-fixture-"))` and analysed **by running the sweep again over that root** (`--root <tmp> --json <tmp>`), not by a second in-process classifier — **the child is the same program over a different root, so there is nothing to drift from**, which is the honesty question the brief asked and the row's own searches did not answer. Its contents: `live.ts` (production-imported, the negative case), `reader.ts` + `reader.test.ts` (test-only), and `field.ts`/`card.ts` (a mutual import gives each a production importer while the symbol stays unimported) — exactly **3 candidate rows, 0 strays, `live.ts` absent**. **THE ROW'S `NOT ESTABLISHED` IS NOW MEASURED**: the child run costs **66–73 ms** against the real tree's **406–433 ms**, so `--self-test` runs **458–538 ms** and the second walk is **~16%**. **FIVE CHECKS MOVED, NOT THE FOUR THIS ROW AND THE PLAN NAME**: the four bindings were read by five checks, because `card-library.ts` was pinned both by `at("redundant-export", …)` and by `a redundant row reports uses, not occurrences` — an undercount in the plan's Step 4, corrected in place. **A sixth live-path pin was deliberately left alone**: `a barrel's re-export is followed as a route` names `charts/settings-fields.ts` inline, and it asserts a route mechanism rather than a kind firing, which neither this row nor Step 4 names. **BOTH REAL-TREE WALKS RETAINED, AND BOTH ARE THRESHOLDS RATHER THAN EXACT COUNTS** — `the walk found the tree` is `all.length > 400` (measured 668) and `the walk found the test suite` is test files `> 200` (measured 340) — so a split does not break them, which was the brief's question and is what makes keeping them cheap. `no test file is ever a candidate`, `no package barrel is a no-importer-file` and `no ambient .d.ts is a candidate` stay on the real tree, because against a synthetic one they would be vacuous. **THE RED PROOF IS BOTH WAYS AND WAS RE-RUN BY THE CONTROLLER**, each patched in place and restored byte-identical under `cmp`: **removing the fixture's expected finding** (the `instantiateCard();` call) exits **1**, failing `redundant-export fires on the fixture (its own file calls the symbol)` and `a redundant row reports uses, not occurrences`; **dropping the classify loop's test-file guard** exits **1** on `no test file is ever a candidate (discovery is an edge)`. **THE REAL-TREE CANDIDATE REPORT IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE BASE**, verified by the controller with a `git worktree` at `07dd4676` and `cmp` — which is the guard that the split changed no real-tree behaviour, **and it is also what proves a false positive the seat introduced and fixed is gone**: the sweep scans its own `scripts/`, so the fixture's import strings were first read as four unresolved imports, fixed with an `importFrom` helper. **`0067` extends `0058` rather than repeating it**: it relies on **rung 4** (the field pins a fixture the tool owns) and **rung 5** (the self-test is deliberately on the real tree, so keep both), and it **moves rung 6's fix**, since `ui-copy-readers.ts` was a third pin on a live file rather than an answer. **`--self-test` went 26/26 to 27/27.** **One row is filed from this task** (`vg-566`, the sweep's own false unresolved-import entry). **Doc rot in `docs/architecture/dead-code-candidates.md`, which cites two `dead-code-sweep.mjs` line ranges already stale at the base, is `vg-564`'s class and gets no row.**
