title: The json reporter writes to one shared test-results/summary.json unless the run also passes --reporter=json, and a plan that names only the env var never notices
detail:
FOUND WHILE EXECUTING PLAN 4 TASK 3, trying to keep this session's report out of the shared test-results/summary.json. THE ROW'S FIRST VERSION OVERSTATED IT AND IS CORRECTED HERE, because the controller reproduced both sides rather than accepting one. Measured, first run (the agent's): PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_NAME=<temp>/probe.json npx playwright test composition-panel --workers=1, with NO --reporter flag - the probe file was never created and test-results/summary.json carried that run. Measured, second run (the controller's, same spec, same machine): the same env var with --reporter=json on the command line - the probe file WAS created, and test-results/summary.json was not written at all. CAUSE, named to the line: src/web/playwright.config.ts:60-65 configures the json reporter as ["json", { outputFile: "test-results/summary.json" }]. A CLI --reporter replaces that list, so the CLI json reporter runs with no outputFile and the environment variable applies; without the flag the config's reporter runs, its own outputFile wins, and the variable has nothing to apply to. So the variable is not inert - it is inert WITHOUT THE FLAG, which is the condition every instruction this repo writes omits. WHAT IT COSTS: test-results/summary.json is one unqualified path, plans 3 and 4 both tell agents to route the JSON through the environment variable and neither says to pass --reporter=json, and on a machine where two sessions run the same suite an agent that obeys without the flag reads a file it did not write and reports another run's numbers as its own. STILL OPEN because the hazard is real once the flag is dropped, and the two candidate fixes are a decision: name --reporter=json in the instruction - cheap, keeps the collision for anyone who forgets - or drop outputFile from the config, which makes the variable apply unconditionally but moves where every session's report lands. The controller has corrected the instruction in plan 4's briefs and in its own session memory; the config is untouched.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: DROP outputFile FROM THE CONFIG. The environment variable then applies unconditionally, so an instruction naming only the variable cannot be obeyed wrongly, and the shared one-path collision ends rather than being documented in every instruction. Every session's report lands where the variable says.
check: playwright.config.ts json reporter no longer sets outputFile; env var applies unconditionally

title: No tsconfig includes tests/e2e, so a type error in any browser spec is checked by nothing
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT ON 2026-10-08 while running plan 8 Task 2.3's gates on a new spec file (`src/web/tests/e2e/host-chrome.spec.ts`, commit 1e52b8da), and it is repo-wide rather than this task's. THE MEASUREMENT, read from the configuration rather than assumed: `cd src/web && npm run typecheck` runs `npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present`, and `package.json`'s workspaces are `packages/renderer-core`, `packages/theme-package`, `packages/scene-fabric`, `packages/player`, `packages/editor`, `packages/fake-source` and `packages/host` -- `tests/` is not among them, so no workspace tsc program can see it. There is no `src/web/tsconfig.json` and no `tests/tsconfig.json` (`ls tsconfig*.json tests/tsconfig*.json` finds only `tsconfig.base.json`). Of the seven package tsconfigs, `renderer-core` includes `src/**/*.ts` and `theme-package` includes `src/**/*.ts`; the other five carry no `include` at all and fall back to TypeScript's default, which is `**/*` relative to the config's own directory -- so every one of them is scoped inside its own package. The one config that mentions tests, `packages/editor/tsconfig.json`, mentions them in a comment about `src/core`'s architecture tests and includes only `src/**/*.ts` and `src/**/*.tsx`. WHAT STILL RUNS: `./node_modules/.bin/biome lint tests/...` checks syntax and style but is not a type checker, and Playwright transpiles specs with esbuild, which strips types without checking them -- so a spec that reads a property which does not exist on a fixture, or passes the wrong shape to a helper, fails only at runtime and only in the branch that reads it. NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT BLOCKING: this is the state every existing browser spec has always been in, and it cost nothing in this task because the new file's helpers are copies of a spec that runs. It is filed because the absence is invisible -- a green `npm run typecheck` reads as coverage of the whole workspace, and it is not -- and because the fix is a decision rather than a one-liner: adding `tests/` to a program pulls `@playwright/test` and both DOM and Node libs into one project, which is the conflict the editor's tsconfig already documents for `@types/node`. NOW LOAD-BEARING (2026-10-09, plan 3's close): plan 3 rewrote three tests/e2e/ specs (author-journey-rebuild, inspector-sections and editor-canvas) and added four parity captures, and none of that is typechecked by any tsconfig - which the close's own reviews kept re-learning, since the standing trap 'tests/e2e/ belongs to no tsconfig' had to be stated in briefs to stop a mis-typed locator passing review. The risk is no longer theoretical.

RULED 2026-10-12: YES — `tests/e2e/` joins a tsconfig program, as its OWN project rather than by folding into the editor's. The absence is invisible and now load-bearing: plan 3 rewrote three specs and added four parity captures with no typechecker anywhere, and briefs had to carry a standing warning so a mis-typed locator would not pass review — an error class that only review catches is the state `npm run typecheck` exists to prevent. Its own `tsconfig.e2e.json` rather than a shared program, because the DOM/Node lib conflict is exactly what TypeScript solves by separating projects: the e2e project needs Playwright's types and the DOM, and pulling those into the editor's program would trade one missing check for a weaker one. Wire it into the typecheck script in the same commit, or the project exists and nothing runs it.
check: `tsconfig.e2e.json` is its own TypeScript program over all 80 `tests/e2e/**/*.ts` inputs (80/80 listed by `--listFilesOnly`, none of them in the editor's program) and the root `typecheck` runs it: `npm run typecheck` exit 0, and a deliberate type error in a browser spec made the same command exit 1 naming that spec, then a byte-identical restore and exit 0 again. Independent review reproduced both, the coverage count and the strict-flag audit.

title: A stamp on a nested group is unchecked, because the walk skips every group
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW, over 5230778c..194f9e5a. Plan 5s Review Focus 1 says a stamp that leaked onto a child is pinned in Task 5 and Task 6. The Task 5 half pins only the non-group children: card-library.test.ts:186 is `if (object["type"] === "Group") continue;`, which skips every group at every depth, so a nested group carrying a stamp is asserted nowhere in the tree. The Task 6 half cannot cover it either: layer-tree.test.ts:836-837 filters `row.kind === "group" && row.depth > 0` and expects length 0, but the starter has no nested group at all, so that assertion is structurally empty and could only fail if a card legitimately gained one. WHAT IS REALLY PINNED, and was proved by the reviews own break: a stamp on a non-group part, the panel and every part inside a card, does fail when removed. The gap is the nested-group half of RF1 and nothing else. NOT FIXED IN PLAN 5 because the honest fix is not another assertion of the same shape: with no nested group in the starter, any such assertion is unfalsifiable, so closing this means deciding to walk the projection against a constructed document that does have one, which is a test-design decision rather than a correction.

RULED 2026-10-12: YES — walk the projection against a CONSTRUCTED document that contains a nested group, and keep the starter out of it. The assertion this row names is structurally empty: `layer-tree.test.ts:836-837` filters `row.kind === "group" && row.depth > 0` and expects length 0, which can only fail if the starter gains a nested group by accident, so it asserts nothing about the stamp rule it sits beside. AGENTS.md's own verification rule decides it — a regression test must fail when its fix is disabled before it is trusted — and an unfalsifiable assertion cannot. Constructed rather than authored into the starter, because the starter is product content and its shape is not a test's to choose. The two halves the review's break proved stay exactly as they are.
check: `layer-tree.test.ts` walks a CONSTRUCTED card and pins the nested group's own stamp: the case `reads a nested group's own stamp, and lends it to nothing beneath` exits 1 alone (1 failed of 50) when the stamp walk in `groupRole` is disabled and 0 restored byte-for-byte, and the structurally empty depth filter it replaced is gone.

title: The pin that the builders words agree with the library is a tautology
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 5S WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW. Plan 5s Task 5 Constraints say the task adds a pin that the unit word in the builders and the unit word in CARD_LIBRARY agree, naming the failure mode a unit label re-spelled in the builder instead of read from uiCopy.cardLibrary. The test cannot detect that: CARD_LIBRARY is built from uiCopy.cardLibrary (card-library.ts:105-138, `label: uiCopy.cardLibrary.time` and so on) and the builders pass the same uiCopy.cardLibrary references (new-fabric-theme-cards.ts:99-101, :386, :401). Both sides resolve one object, so the comparison holds for any value that object ever takes and a re-spelled literal in a builder would have to be introduced on the library side too to go unnoticed, which is not the failure mode. What the test does pin is real and was proved by a break: the stamp present at all, and its widgetId. The precedent the plan cited is no stronger: new-object-defaults.test.ts:626 reads uiCopy.shapeKinds on both sides as well. The cross-path agreement that IS sound is the one Task 6 added, layer-tree.test.ts:820-834, which compares a revived document against CARD_LIBRARY. NOT FIXED HERE because closing it means asserting on the builders source rather than on a value, which is a shape assertion and a decision about how much source-reading this suite wants, not a correction to a wrong test.

RULED 2026-10-12: REMOVE the tautology and do NOT replace it with a source-shape assertion. `uiCopy.cardLibrary` compared against `new-fabric-theme-cards.ts:99-101` resolves one object on both sides, so the comparison holds for every value that object could ever take: it cannot fail for the reason it claims to check, which makes it evidence of nothing — the same defect as vg-167. Source-reading is rejected as the replacement: this suite's business is behaviour, and an assertion over a builder's spelling pins the text of a file rather than what the product does. title: The layer footer's add-element buttons were never requested; the always-visible ask was about the layer actions, not new constructions
detail: RAISED BY THE USER on 2026-10-17 after testing the editor: the layer panel's bottom toolbar carries the Add pane's construction buttons (text plus one per primitive), and the user says they asked only for the toolbar to always show, never for those buttons. WHERE THEY CAME FROM, established: `vg-460` (archive, `verified`) recorded the user's item 3 of 2026-10-14 — "layer bottom toolbar should always be visible, not just when a layer is selected" — and its row left open which actions are unconditionally available. Commit `e572c302` answered that by adding `CONSTRUCTION_ACTIONS` (`object-actions.ts`, text plus `SHAPE_KINDS`) to `LayerActions` (`editor-shell/layer-panel.tsx`), so the footer is never empty; the dock comparison and `pane.dom.test.tsx` were updated to expect them. The user now rejects that interpretation. **RULED 2026-10-17 by the user, asked directly: the footer keeps the layer's own commands and shows them GREYED while nothing is selected — not the constructions, and not an empty row.** So `CONSTRUCTION_ACTIONS` leaves the footer, and the no-selection state draws the registry's object commands disabled rather than absent; whether ineligible commands also grey while a selection exists is not ruled, and the registry's own documented rule is that an action the selection cannot run is absent rather than greyed, so the minimal reading is: grey in the no-selection state only, existing eligibility rules unchanged once something is selected. TWO CONSEQUENCES TO SETTLE WITH THE CHANGE: `vg-484` (archive, `verified`) is about a construction dispatched through `bridge.run` reaching the session façade unwrapped, and the footer was that path's caller, so the bridge's construction exemption may become dead code rather than a live defect; and `vg-460`'s check pins the footer's set against the Add pane's tiles, so it must be rewritten to the new rule rather than left contradicting it. OWNER: `src/web/packages/editor/src/object-actions.ts` (`CONSTRUCTION_ACTIONS`), `src/web/packages/editor/src/editor-shell/layer-panel.tsx` (`LayerActions`), and the tests that pin the footer's set (`layer-panel.dom.test.tsx`, `pane.dom.test.tsx`, `tests/e2e/snapping.spec.ts`). CLOSED 2026-10-18 by Task 25.1, and the closure found a second defect in the same surface: the first pass shipped a footer where every button carried `disabled` and eleven of twelve greyed, but the disabled Delete painted `--hot` — pixel-identical to its enabled state — because `editor-shell.css`'s `[data-yunari-destructive]` rule was UNLAYERED and outranked the `text-faint` class `ControlIconButton` computes for a blocked control, which sits in `@layer utilities`. Every case the first pass shipped asserted the `disabled` attribute and never a colour, so nothing could see it; an independent review measured the built editor's computed colours and caught it. The rule is now `[data-yunari-destructive]:not([disabled]):not([aria-disabled="true"])`, so the mark paints only where the control can run, and `editor-shell.css`'s comment no longer claims the old invariant ("no surface passes `disabled` for a destructive action") that this footer broke. `hasSelection` is exported from `object-actions.ts` rather than re-spelled in the footer. THE FOOTER'S NO-DOCUMENT STATE IS NOT COVERED BY THE RULING: with no bridge it draws the same twelve disabled commands, where the canvas dock renders nothing visible; ruled by the controller to stand, because never-empty is what `vg-460` asked for. UNVERIFIED: the browser case asserts one colour across the idle footer rather than `--faint` specifically, so a cascade fault painting the whole row one wrong shared colour would pass it; and the `:not([aria-disabled="true"])` half has no case, because no surface passes `refused` for a destructive action today.

title: The player's warning banner should overlay the artboard and clear itself after three seconds
detail: REQUESTED BY THE USER on 2026-10-17 while testing the player: the warning banner should be an overlay rather than resizing the artboard, and should disappear after 3 seconds. CURRENT SOURCE STATE AT 1524a6a7, read rather than assumed: `showAvailabilityNotice` already passes `overlay: true` (`src/web/packages/player/src/chrome.ts`), which makes the amber strip `position:fixed` so raising or clearing it cannot re-fit the scene; that overlay landed in `476d8db7` (2026-10-14, vg-028). `showCropNotice` is the top strip that still sits in the flow band and therefore shrinks the artboard, but it is deliberately persistent and describes a composition gap, not a warning. NO player strip auto-dismisses: the availability strip is rebuilt on every refresh and removed only when readings return, and the connection strip clears only when the source goes live. So the reported resize either ran a bundle built before 476d8db7 or names the crop strip; reproduce on a rebuilt bundle before changing which strip is meant. THE DURABLE DELTA is a three-second dismissal for the availability warning. Whether the crop notice should also clear is unresolved and applying it there would contradict the §97 requirement that a cropped object stay legible as a different gap from an unreadable sensor. OWNER: `src/web/packages/player/src/chrome.ts` (`putStrip`, `showAvailabilityNotice`), `src/web/packages/player/src/main.ts` (refresh cadence), `src/web/packages/player/src/availability-notice.ts`. This is runtime chrome state and must never be persisted. **CONFIRMED BY THE USER 2026-10-18: the strip does not resize the artboard.** So the resize half of this report is not a live defect — the bundle it was seen on was almost certainly built before `476d8db7` — and the task makes no placement change. The artboard's box not moving is the invariant the dismissal must preserve rather than a fault to repair, and what remains of this row is the three-second clear alone. CLOSED 2026-10-18 by Task 25.2. The notice now owns a three-state lifetime — `idle | up | dismissed` with one timer — because `main.ts` calls `refresh()` through `startChartRefresh(refresh, 30)`, thirty times a second, so a timer armed per call would never fire and a strip rebuilt per call would flicker. Raised once, cleared at 3000 ms, and while `up` or `dismissed` the frame-rate calls return before either the DOM write or the timer; the re-arm path needs `idle`, which needs the condition to have cleared. THE CONSEQUENCE, recorded rather than left to be found: a display that loads while a sensor is already failing shows the warning for three seconds and then nothing, for as long as the outage lasts, and nothing else names the cause — the bound text renders `—` and the charts draw a bare track, which is §97's never-fabricate half without the why. Two narrower consequences of the same state: a second sensor failing while the first gap persists changes the strip's text but raises nothing, and only a page reload tells a reader again. Ruled by the user 2026-10-17, so these are the ruled behaviour's price rather than defects. A LATENT COUPLING was found and recorded on `vg-540` instead of here: a timer pending at `pagehide` is never cleared and the notice's state survives teardown, inert today because the callback holds no mount reference and nothing re-arms the mount, but load-bearing the moment `vg-540` is ruled to re-arm it.
check: The player's warning banner clears itself three seconds after it is raised and does not come back while the condition persists: `chrome.dom.test.ts`'s cases `clears itself three seconds after it is raised` and `does not re-raise it while the condition persists` drive the lifetime under fake timers, and `host-chrome.spec.ts`'s case `a notice that arrives after the fit clears itself without moving the composition` reads the built bundle's artboard geometry while the banner is up and again after it clears, asserting both boxes equal and no strips left. The overlay was already built (`476d8db7`); the invariant the browser case pins is that clearing the banner does not move the composition, and Task 25.2's review proved it is genuinely pinned rather than merely asserted by removing `overlay: true`, which failed the case with `[844, 344.40625]` against `[844, 390]`. The user confirmed on 2026-10-18 that the strip does not resize the artboard, so no placement change was owed. Landed by `79882c0c`.

title: Phone player needs a tap-revealed semi-translucent fullscreen control in its top-right corner
detail: Requested by the user on 2026-10-17 while testing phone publishing: add a semi-translucent control to the top-right of the phone player, visible only on tap, allowing fullscreen entry. BOUNDED DESIGN PRESENTED, APPROVAL PENDING: initially hidden, tap reveals, enter/exit fullscreen toggle, auto-hide after three seconds except keyboard focus, safe-area inset, overlay without shifting authored composition. Capability-detect native Fullscreen API and explain unsupported capability rather than exposing a dead control; MDN compatibility data currently says arbitrary-element requestFullscreen is unavailable on iPhone Safari, while Android browsers support it. Three-second duration, exit toggle and unsupported treatment are proposals, not user rulings. No implementation, browser proof or physical-phone compatibility claim. Player chrome owns transient controls; preserve renderer/editor separation and never persist this runtime state. Request remains undecided until user approves bounded behavior. CLOSED 2026-10-18 by Task 25.3, with the settings question it arrived beside (`vg-576`). The control is one of three in a tap-revealed bar, and the bar is `position: fixed` so it never takes room from the composition — the invariant `vg-028` and Task 25.2 both paid for. WHERE THE CLIENT HAS NO FULLSCREEN, the control explains itself and names the home-screen path instead of doing nothing; iPhone Safari has no arbitrary-element fullscreen, so that is its honest route until Task 25.6's standalone mode exists. MEASURED, not asserted: Chromium at a 412x839 viewport on `http://127.0.0.1:4175` reported `requestFullscreen: true` and `secureContext: true`, and the same API was present on the LAN origin `http://192.168.2.56:<port>` where the context was NOT secure — Chromium does not secure-context-gate `requestFullscreen`, unlike the wake lock. NOT VERIFIED: no physical phone, and no iPhone Safari — the refusal path was forced by deleting `Element.prototype.requestFullscreen` rather than observed on a device that lacks it.
check: The phone player draws a tap-revealed, semi-translucent control in its top-right corner that toggles fullscreen where the client has it: `display-controls.dom.test.ts`'s case `enters and leaves on one control where the client has it` drives the toggle, and `host-player.spec.ts`'s cases read the built bundle at a 412x839 viewport — the bar appears on a tap, hides itself after three seconds, and the composition's column holds only the two declared chrome bands and the artboard, with the artboard filling exactly what they leave, asserted absolutely rather than against an earlier reading of the same page. Where the client has no arbitrary-element fullscreen the control explains itself and names the home-screen path rather than doing nothing. Landed by af1fa064, with the assertion hardened by 703c9e5e after an independent review showed the first version passed with the control in flow.

title: The player is asked for display-client settings — keep-awake above all — and whether a browser can carry them at all is unanswered
detail: ASKED BY THE USER on 2026-10-17, alongside the phone-player reports: whether the player can have a settings panel for display-client specifics, naming keep-awake (overriding the device's screen-off setting) as the example, and asking whether a standard browser can do it or a native player app is required. THE ONE CAPABILITY WITH A BROWSER ANSWER is the Screen Wake Lock API (`navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')`): secure context only, the lock is released automatically when the page is hidden, and re-acquiring on `visibilitychange` is the caller's own job — so a wake lock is a re-acquiring loop rather than a switch, and the device's own screen-off gesture ends it regardless. UNVERIFIED FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT: the exact client support matrix; no web tool answered here and MDN's compatibility tables do not scrape, so any support claim must be feature-detected at runtime and reported as detected rather than assumed. WHAT IS NOT A BROWSER'S TO GIVE, and the reason this needs a spec rather than a task: fullscreen of arbitrary elements on iPhone Safari (see `vg-568`), any control of the OS screen-off timer beyond the wake lock, orientation locking on every client, and a kiosk mode that survives the browser being backgrounded. WHAT IT OWES: a spec that decides first what a display client may configure — per client rather than per theme, which is `vg-574`'s map — then which of those a browser can honour, then the honest unsupported path for the rest, before any native shell is considered. **RULED 2026-10-17 by the user, in the same message that ordered the PWA: no settings modal for now.** The controls they named — keep-awake, a brightness control and a fullscreen button — are player chrome, and the installable PWA in `vg-577` is what carries them, so no spec and no modal are owed yet; the per-display settings map (`vg-574`) stays the owner of what a display client is configured with, and this row stays open until those three controls exist. BRIGHTNESS IS NOT THE BACKLIGHT: a browser cannot set a device's panel brightness, so the only control it can offer is a dimming overlay over the rendered display — a real dark-room feature, and not the device's own slider. NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED beyond those three controls. CLOSED 2026-10-18 by Task 25.3, as the ruling it asked for rather than as a settings panel: the user answered the question by removing it — "If we can have the screen wakelock, a brightness slider and fullscreen button then we don't need a setting modal, for now" — so the three controls live in the player's chrome and no modal exists. THE TWO LIMITS IT MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED: at `http://192.168.2.56:<port>` the client reported `secureContext: false` and `wakeLock: "undefined"`, so keep-awake cannot hold a lock on the origin a phone actually uses today (`vg-580`, Task 25.8); and headless Chromium REFUSED the lock with `NotAllowedError` even on a secure origin, so the refusal path is reachable on https too and not only over plain http. The dimmer is an overlay over the rendered picture and is labelled as that, because a browser cannot set a device's panel brightness. NOT VERIFIED: no physical phone, and the re-acquisition across a hide and a show used a synthetic release event and an overridden `document.visibilityState` rather than a real backgrounded tab.
check: No settings modal was built, which is the ruling the user gave on 2026-10-18: keep-awake, a dimmer and fullscreen are player chrome instead, and the keep-awake control re-acquires a Screen Wake Lock across a hide and a show while reporting the lock it holds rather than the one it asked for — `host-player.spec.ts` reads the built bundle on the client it ran on and asserts all three states: pressed with a lock held, not pressed with the refusal sentence after the client's own `NotAllowedError`, and pressed again once re-acquired. The dimmer is named as an overlay over the picture rather than the screen's own brightness, and nothing about any of the three is persisted. The browser it ran on is Chromium at a 412x839 viewport on `http://127.0.0.1:4175`; no physical phone and no iPhone Safari were involved. Landed by af1fa064, with the wake-lock refusal corrected by 703c9e5e after an independent review.

title: Live line charts dropped points early at the left edge, because the chart asked the source for no history before its own axis minimum
detail: REPORTED BY THE USER on 2026-10-17 while watching the phone player against a live source: the lines appeared to correct themselves for about half a second at the right edge, and points disappeared about half a second too early at the left edge. THE USER'S REPORT WAS ONE OBSERVATION AND TWO DEFECTS, established by Task 25.4's per-frame probe rather than by reading: the left edge was the window this row closes on, and the right edge is the overscan gutter, now its own row `vg-582` with its own owner. THE ROW'S ORIGINAL READING IS REFUTED and is kept here as refuted rather than dropped: it claimed `createLiveSource` overwrites every sample's `presentationTimestamp` with the browser's arrival time, so every sample in one batch shares a timestamp and the axis's slide against the data's quantisation explained both symptoms. Measured, the host sends ONE sample per key per batch, so a batch cannot place several points of one series on one x, and the repeated timestamps the probe did see sit at the OLDEST end of the series in a narrow band around the frame the window first fills — a connect-time burst of several batches inside one millisecond, not one batch sharing a stamp. The reading was plausible and wrong, which is why the task was required to measure before fixing. WHAT THE LEFT EDGE ACTUALLY WAS: the chart asked the source for exactly the axis window, so the sample before `xAxis.min` that `toSeriesPoints` needs to start the line was never requested and never existed; the series therefore began INSIDE the plot, at a position that moved with the host's cadence. NOT ESTABLISHED: the host's cadence on the user's own phone, and the residual 16-19.5 % of steady frames that still hold no sample at or below the axis minimum, which is the host's cadence rather than the window — measured p50 1005-1026 ms and max 1869-3243 ms against the 1 000 ms `DEFAULT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_MS` declares. OWNER: `renderer-core/src/charts/line.ts`. CLOSED 2026-10-18 by Task 25.4, on a measurement rather than on the reading above. WHAT THE READINGS SHOWED, from the per-frame probe `tests/e2e/live-chart-edge.spec.ts` on the built player bundle at 412x839 against the real host: the left-edge symptom is real, and it is the window rather than the timestamp. Before the fix, 364 of 504 steady-state frames (72.2 %) held NO sample at or below `xAxis.min`, so the line began inside the plot, at a mean of +199 ms past the axis start and up to 990 ms. After it, the same reading is 16.0 % and 19.5 % on two runs and 8.3 % on a third, with the mean at -367 / -320 / -424 ms — inverted, which is the fix working: the series now starts at or before the axis minimum and is clipped there, which is what `toSeriesPoints`' predecessor rule intends. THE CAUSE: `buildChartPlan` asked the source for exactly `windowSeconds + delay`, and that request's cutoff IS `xAxis.min`, so the one sample strictly below the window start that `toSeriesPoints` keeps had never been requested and did not exist. `lineHistorySeconds` now returns `windowSeconds + 2 × delay`, and both callers ask it (`plan.ts` and `editor/src/chart-manager/index.ts`, where the wider window is behaviourally a no-op because the newest sample cannot move). THE RESIDUAL, named and not closed: 16-19.5 % of steady frames still begin inside the plot, and it is the host's cadence rather than the window — inter-batch gaps measured p50 1 006-1 021 ms and up to 3 243 ms against the 1 000 ms `LIVE_SOURCE_CHART_PLAYBACK_DELAY_MS` stands in for, so more than half of the gaps already outrun the figure the fix asks for. Two delays is the most the line can ask for while no source declares a cadence. THE OTHER HALF OF THE USER'S ONE REPORT is `vg-582`, a different owner. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by review `acee041d802f41397`, which reproduced the measurement to the digit, the red proof (`4 failed | 48 passed`, all three cadences failing at frame 0) and the restore by `fc /b` plus SHA-256, and established that this repo has no git hooks for the seat's `--no-verify` first attempt to have skipped. NOT VERIFIED: no physical phone and no iPhone Safari, so the user's own device is not among the clients this ran on, and the host's cadence on that device is unknown. THE PLAN'S FILE LIST WAS WRONG, and the measurement is what corrected it: it named `renderer-core/src/data/live-source.ts` and `player/src/main.ts`, and neither was touched, because the defect was in the window the chart asks for rather than in the timestamp the source writes.
check: The live line chart asks the source for the history its own left edge is drawn from, so the series begins at or before `xAxis.min` instead of inside the plot: `lineHistorySeconds` returns `windowSeconds + 2 × delay` and both callers ask it rather than spelling the window out again — `plan.test.ts`'s `requests the delayed line viewport's left-edge predecessor` drives `SampleStore` at 700, 950 and 1018 ms cadences and asserts the first drawn point's timestamp is at or below `xAxis.min` on every frame of each cadence, and it exits 1 with all three failing at frame 0 when the helper is disabled (`4 failed | 48 passed`), which is the reading the fix is for. Gap preservation and the playback delay are intact, shown by pre-existing cases (`line.test.ts`'s gap rule and `plan.test.ts`'s delayed line viewport, with `renderOverscanRightMs` 1000 and `xAxis.max` at now). Measured on the built bundle at a 412x839 viewport against the real host, frames holding no sample at or below the axis minimum fell from 72.2 % (364 of 504) to 16.0 / 19.5 / 8.3 %, the mean moving from +199 ms inside the plot to -367 / -320 / -424 ms. Landed by 0fcafba6, with the probe made opt-in by 6d2b24dd.

title: The crop notice and the bleed toggle are to be gone: a display says nothing about a cropped object and no object is marked as deliberately bleeding
detail: RULED 2026-10-18 by the user, asked directly to settle the scope: "BOTH, EVERYWHERE". The player raises no crop notice at all, and the bleed toggle leaves the selection inspector, so nothing is marked and every overhang counts as cropped. PROVENANCE, and the reason this row exists at all: the user said they had ruled this before, and the controller could not find that ruling anywhere — both register files, `docs/superpowers/specs/`, `DESIGN.md`, `docs/decisions/` including `0027-a-deliberate-bleed-is-marked-not-warned-about.md`, and `git log --all` were searched and none of them recorded it. So it lived in a session and not on disk, which is the failure the register's own trailer rule exists to prevent; it is recorded here rather than reconstructed. WHAT IT SUPERSEDES: decision 0027 in full, since the mark it created is what goes; the player's half of the composition-gap-versus-sensor-gap distinction (`chrome.ts`'s `showCropNotice` comment cites §97 for it, and `§97`'s own text in `docs/product/requirements.md` is about not fabricating readings, so the distinction is a derived reading rather than §97's words); and `vg-191`, the open row asking for a fixture that raises a data gap and a composition gap together, whose subject one half disappears from. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, ruled by the controller and open to the user: the ARTBOARD PANEL's crop figure (`artboard-panel.ts`, `artboard-fields.tsx`'s size note, `vg-142`'s surface) stays. It is the editor's count of what the frame loses, on the one surface where the figure is actionable, and the user named a notice and a toggle rather than the author's own measurement; what does change there is that nothing is excluded from the count any more. BLAST RADIUS, read from source: `renderer-core/src/theme/bleed.ts` (`YUNARI_BLEEDS_PROPERTY`, `objectBleeds`, `isBleedMark`) and the envelope validator that pins the mark (`fabric-envelope-validate.ts`'s `objectBleeds`); `scene-fabric/src/artboard-crop.ts`'s `SceneBox.bleeds` and the `bleeds` term in `countable`; `editor/src/selection-inspector/bleed.ts` and the Position row that renders it; `player/src/artboard-crop.ts`'s `cropNoticeText` and `chrome.ts`'s `showCropNotice` with its `yunari-crop` strip and the CSS that paints it. THE ONE DECISION THE TASK MUST SETTLE WITH EVIDENCE, not by preference: `yunariBleeds` is PERSISTED authored state — a Fabric custom property on the object, written because the document persists Fabric JSON — and the envelope validator refuses unknown keys, so removing the property from what is allowed could make a theme saved with the mark refuse to load. The task establishes whether any theme in this repo or on this box carries it before choosing between refusing the key and dropping it on read, and records what it found; a refusal that strands a saved theme is data loss and is not the same decision as deleting an unreachable branch. **RULED 2026-10-18, and the editor's count is confirmed with it: "showing the count in the editor is fine, since it's actionable for the author. We can remove the yunariBleeds key from the schema and all existing themes."** The evidence that makes that safe rather than a preference, gathered before the ruling: `git grep` over tracked files finds the key in the published schema (`schema/theme-document.schema.json:156`), in `renderer-core`'s source, in decision 0027 and in the tests — and in NO theme file. The only two theme files that carry it (`src/web/.e2e-host-app/themes/e2e-bleed/theme.json` and `e2e-bleed-all/theme.json`) are gitignored and written by the specs that exercise the notice, and a search of the author's own app folder (`~/.yunari/themes/`, four themes) found none. So there is no authored work to strand, and the migration is a schema and source deletion rather than a rewrite of anyone's document. `fabric-envelope-schema-sync.test.ts` is the case that keeps the published schema and `validate.ts`'s hand-maintained keys in step, so it is what will catch the two drifting apart. CONSEQUENCE, recorded rather than left to be discovered: with the mark gone the count cannot exclude a deliberate bleed, so an author who wants an object to run off the edge has no way to say so and the count reports it as a fault for as long as it stands. That is the price of the mark going, and the user ruled the count stays anyway because it is actionable. CLOSED 2026-10-18 by Task 25.7, on the user's ruling and on a reading rather than on the absence of a symbol. WHAT WENT: the mark (`YUNARI_BLEEDS_PROPERTY`, `objectBleeds`, `isBleedMark`) and the envelope validator's pin on it; `SceneBox.bleeds` and the `bleeds` term in `countable`; the inspector's bleed field, its write path and the Position row that rendered it; the player's `cropNoticeText`, `showCropNotice` and the `yunari-crop` strip with the rules that painted it. Decision 0027 is superseded by 0069. WHAT THE PERSISTED KEY COST, AND THE ANSWER: nothing. It left the published schema with no migration, and an independent review drove a real document carrying it through the host's own `/api/themes/:id` route — 200, with an envelope JSON-identical to the source and the key CARRIED rather than dropped. The reason is that the published schema has no runtime consumer: the decider is `envelope-keys.ts` (ADR-0023), and `fabricObject` is deliberately in neither of its lists because the schema publishes that shape with `additionalProperties: {jsonValue}` rather than `false`. The editor's next save drops the key, which is the intended outcome rather than a loss. THE COUNT, AS RULED: the artboard panel keeps its figure and now excludes nothing — `countable` is `visible && width > 0 && height > 0`, and the group case moved from `counted: 2` to `counted: 3` because the group no longer carries a mark for the count to skip. THE CONSEQUENCE THE RULING ACCEPTED: an author who wants an object to run off the edge on purpose has no way to say so, so the count reports it as a fault for as long as it stands. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS PROJECT'S OWN PAPERWORK, found while doing it: the plan's Step 3 named `renderer-core/src/theme/validate.ts`, which does not exist because ADR-0041 retired schema v1 by deletion — the hand-maintained key list is `envelope-keys.ts` for the closed bags, with the published schema and `fabric-envelope-validate.ts` covering the object shape; and `[data-yunari-crop]` named two different things, the player's notice strip (removed) and the editor's image-crop button (kept). AN ACCEPTANCE GAP THE REVIEW CAUGHT AND THE TASK THEN CLOSED: deleting `player/src/artboard-crop.test.ts` wholesale had taken the only coverage of `EDGE_TOLERANCE` and of `outsideEdges`' edge naming, both of which survive as live functions; three cases were re-pointed onto them, with the tolerance arms stated absolutely rather than derived from the constant, because an arm derived from `EDGE_TOLERANCE` passes at `EDGE_TOLERANCE = 0` — proved red both ways, at 0 and at 2.

Read per frame on the built player: 0 of 3255 frames carry a `yunari-crop` strip after the removal, against 3249 of roughly 3250 before it. The artboard panel's own crop count stays and now excludes nothing, which the group case shows by moving from `counted: 2` to `counted: 3`. The persisted `yunariBleeds` key left the published schema with no migration and no theme is stranded: a document carrying it loads through the host's own route with a JSON-identical envelope, and `fabric-envelope-validate.test.ts` pins that an unknown key on a scene object is carried rather than refused. The edge tolerance and the edge naming keep their cases, re-pointed onto the surviving functions. Landed by 4f664dea, with the re-pointed cases in 4ad9e767.

title: The line chart still slides left on the phone player, and a chrome strip taking room is the only measured mechanism that can move it
detail: REPORTED BY THE USER on 2026-10-17 while watching the phone player against a live source: the chart still occasionally slides to the left, the same complaint archived `vg-028` recorded. THE ROW'S OWN CANDIDATE IS REFUTED, AND THE OBSERVATION IS NOT. Task 25.5 measured a viewport height change driven under the page on the built player (`tests/e2e/host-viewport-refit.spec.ts`, opt-in behind `YUNARI_VIEWPORT_PROBE`), and a height change cannot move a width-limited composition horizontally: at 390x844 portrait the fit's scale stays 0.609375 and `offsetX` stays 0 for every drive, every object's `sx` span is exactly 0 across 3249 frames, and the composition returns to the baseline transform and the same object rects within 15-18 ms. At 844x390 landscape, where the artboard is height-limited, it contracts symmetrically about its centre instead — scale 1.002778 to 0.836111 and `offsetX` 101.1111 to 154.4444 for a 60 px bar — which is a two-sided contraction, not the one-way slide this row describes. So the viewport is not a mechanism for it. WHAT REMAINS, AND IS MEASURED: a chrome strip still takes room from the artboard by design, because `vg-028`'s ruling kept permanent chrome in flow and made only the transient notices overlay, and the crop strip is permanent. In Task 25.5's own recording the crop strip arriving at mount moved `stray-quarter` +30.61 px right and `bleeding-quarter` -8.05 px left — the same 16-30 px mechanism `vg-028` measured — and the reading excluded it only because its baseline was captured after the strip had settled, with the strip never driven to arrive or leave. `player/src/chrome.ts`'s `showCropNotice` runs once at mount, and Task 25.7 removes the strip. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the crop strip is what the user saw, since it arrives at mount and stays, so a recurring slide needs something that makes one come and go and no run has driven that; and whether a phone's own URL bar resolves `height:100%` against the small or the large viewport, which the implementer says a desktop Chromium cannot answer — so the case this row is about is unmeasured on the device it was reported from. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: Task 25.7's removal of the crop strip, with a reading showing the composition does not move where a strip would have taken room — or the user's own ruling to withdraw it, which is theirs to give and not an agent's to assume. CLOSED 2026-10-18, and the closing event is the one this row was corrected to wait on. Task 25.7 removed the crop notice, which was the last strip taking room from the artboard — `vg-028`'s ruling had already made the transient notices overlay, and the crop strip was the permanent one it kept in flow on purpose. THE CLOSING READING, per frame on the built player against the real host, using Task 25.5's probe: after the removal the composition holds ONE transform, ONE painted height and ONE `sy` per object across 539 portrait and 538 landscape mounted frames, and that window includes the mount frames where a strip used to arrive. Before the removal the same probe on the same composition read TWO values of each — portrait `tr.oy` 312.3125 and 289.3125 with every object's `sy` moving 394.46875 to 371.46875, exactly 23 px — and carried a `yunari-crop` strip in 3249 of roughly 3250 frames, against 0 of 3255 after. The transport notice is still present and still moves nothing, which is the control that a room-taking strip is what this reading is about. THE OTHER HALF IS REFUTED AND STAYS REFUTED: the viewport cannot do this — a height change cannot move a width-limited composition horizontally at all, and on a height-limited one it contracts symmetrically about the centre rather than sliding one way. NOT VERIFIED, and it is the same gap this row has always had: no physical phone was involved, and whether Chrome Android resolves `height:100%` against the small or the large viewport is not something a desktop Chromium answers. What is closed is the mechanism, not the device.
check: The line chart no longer slides on the phone player, because the only strip that could still move it is gone: the crop notice was the last chrome strip taking room from the artboard, and removing it leaves the composition holding one transform, one painted height and one `sy` per object across 539 portrait and 538 landscape mounted frames, read per frame on the built player against the real host by Task 25.5's probe (`tests/e2e/host-viewport-refit.spec.ts`, opt-in behind `YUNARI_VIEWPORT_PROBE`) — against two values of each and a `yunari-crop` strip in 3249 of roughly 3250 frames before. No frame of the new run carries that strip, and the transport notice is still present and still moves nothing. The viewport was separately refuted as the mechanism: a height change cannot move a width-limited composition horizontally at all. Landed by 4f664dea, on the instrument from 38ca1afb.

title: The host serves plain http, so a phone on the LAN is not a secure context: no wake lock, no service worker, no install prompt
detail: FOUND BY THE CONTROLLER on 2026-10-18 while briefing Task 25.3, and it is the thing that decides whether two of the user's rulings can exist at all. EVIDENCE, read rather than assumed: neither `host/src/hosting.ts` nor `host/src/server.ts` mentions https, TLS, a certificate or `createSecureServer` — the host is `http.createServer` on a LAN port. WHAT THAT COSTS, because both APIs the user asked for are gated on a secure context: `navigator.wakeLock` (the keep-awake control in `vg-576`) and `navigator.serviceWorker` (the PWA in `vg-577`, and with it the install prompt, since a browser will not offer installation without a service worker). A display opened at `http://<lan-ip>:<port>` gets neither, so the keep-awake control cannot hold a lock and the player cannot install — not because of a bug in either, but because the origin is not secure. THE TRAP THIS ROW EXISTS TO PREVENT: `localhost` IS a secure context, so a controller or a seat testing on the host machine itself sees `navigator.wakeLock` present and a service worker register cleanly, and concludes the feature works, while the phone the feature is for has neither. Any proof for `vg-576` or `vg-577` must run against the origin a display actually uses, and say which origin it used. THE OPTIONS, none of them free and none of them chosen here: a self-signed certificate, which works but earns a browser warning per device and per browser profile until it is trusted by hand; a local CA (the mkcert shape) installed once on each display, which removes the warning at the cost of a setup step per device; or accept plain http and rule both features absent on a phone, which is the honest reading of the current host. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the host's own pairing or display flow already assumes an origin, whether a certificate could be generated and trusted from the host without the user touching each device, and what each display browser actually does with a self-signed certificate. OWNER: `host/src/hosting.ts`, `host/src/server.ts`, the host's startup and its settings surface, with `player/src/chrome.ts` on the receiving end of whatever is decided.
check: The host no longer serves plain http alone: it serves a secure context on the same port, from a local CA it mints itself, and the two APIs gated on one are now reachable on a phone. Read on the built host over a real TLS socket at the LAN address, never loopback (`tests/e2e/host-secure-origin.spec.ts`, project `own-host`, headed, --workers=1): origin `https://192.168.2.56:4233`, client Chromium 153.0.8010.12, `isSecureContext` true, `navigator.wakeLock.request("screen")` granted with `sentinel.type` `screen`, and `navigator.serviceWorker.register` returning a registration with scope `https://192.168.2.56:4233/assets/` — the wake lock and the service worker the row named, both read at the origin a display uses rather than at `localhost`, which is the trap the row existed to remove. The arrangement is `docs/decisions/0070`: one root kept at `<settingsDir>/tls/ca.key`, mode 0600 and outside the tree, with a leaf re-issued in memory at every start covering every non-internal interface address plus `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and `os.hostname()`, so a DHCP change costs a restart and not a re-install. Plain http is KEPT on the same port, the first byte deciding the owner, because the pairing link that points at it belongs to the per-display-themes spec — so this row's own state is narrowed rather than fully removed: nothing advertises the secure origin except the host's console, and `vg-587` carries that handoff. Two cases fail when the change is disabled: with the chain cut to the leaf alone, `page.goto` reports `net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`; and with the port's mid-response guard reverted, `closeIdleConnections()` destroys a TLS response in flight. NOT VERIFIED, and it is the same gap the row opened with: no phone was available, so every statement about iOS and Android is documentation, and the reading was taken with the root allowlisted by `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list` rather than installed in an OS trust store — what is proven is that the origin admits both APIs once the chain validates, not that a given phone's trust store accepts the root. Landed by 0c4d6b1d, with the guard, the minimal serial and the printed root URL in f0122f4e.

title: The player is to be an installable PWA, which is also what answers iPhone's missing fullscreen
detail: REQUESTED BY THE USER on 2026-10-17, after the phone-player reports: "Make the player a pwa webapp", given alongside their ruling that keep-awake, brightness and fullscreen as chrome controls replace the settings modal for now (`vg-576`). WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND INSTALLABILITY: an installed display running in standalone mode draws without the browser's own chrome, which is the closest thing to fullscreen an iPhone has — Safari there never implemented `Element.requestFullscreen()` (see `vg-568`) — so this is the honest path for that client rather than a dead control. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED FROM SOURCE, read rather than assumed: the player is served at the host's ROOT, not under a mount prefix — `host/src/server.ts` calls `serveStatic` with `bundles.player` and passes `url.pathname === "/"` as the html fallback, so `/manifest.webmanifest` and a root-scoped service worker both resolve; the bundle's static root is `packages/player/public/`, which Vite copies into the build, and `packages/player/index.html` already carries `viewport-fit=cover`, a `color-scheme` meta and its own favicon link. WHAT BLOCKS IT TODAY: `host/src/serve/static-path.ts`'s `CONTENT_TYPES` allowlist has no `.webmanifest` entry, so the manifest would be served as `application/octet-stream` and every browser would refuse it; that file is a REUSE-GATE MECHANISM BOUNDARY in `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs`, so a decision note at `docs/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md` claiming that path must exist before the first write, and `.json` is already mapped if the manifest is served under that extension instead. WHAT THE SERVICE WORKER MUST NOT DO: cache the live data. The player's whole subject is live telemetry and the host owns scheduling, buffering and fallback, so the shell (document, scripts, styles, icons) is cacheable and `/api/**` including the event stream is not — an offline display showing yesterday's numbers as though they were live is the fabrication the project forbids. NOT ESTABLISHED: how the user installs it (home screen, kiosk browser, or a vendor's own install flow), whether an offline shell is wanted at all rather than a plain no-network page, and any client's real behaviour — none of this was run in a browser. OWNER: `packages/player/public/` (manifest and icons), `packages/player/index.html`, a service worker under the player's static root, and `host/src/serve/static-path.ts`'s content-type allowlist.
check: The player is an installable PWA, and it is what answers a client with no fullscreen API: the manifest is served with a content type a browser accepts, `display: standalone` is what draws without browser chrome, and a root-scoped service worker registers and controls the document. Read on the integrated tree at the LAN address, never loopback (`tests/e2e/host-pwa.spec.ts`, project `own-host`, headed, --workers=1, port 4235): origin `https://192.168.2.56:4235`, client Chromium 153.0.8010.12, `isSecureContext` true, `content-type: application/manifest+json`, `display: standalone`, `start_url` and `scope` `/`, `registration.scope` `https://192.168.2.56:4235/`, `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` `https://192.168.2.56:4235/sw.js`, with `Page.getAppManifest.errors` and `Page.getInstallabilityErrors` both empty. Offline, read the same way: the document comes from the cache, the player's own failure page is shown, `/api/**` is refused, and the cache holds exactly the manifest, the favicon, the two content-hashed bundle assets and the document — no entry under `/api/`, because a display showing cached numbers as though they were live is the fabrication the project forbids. A case fails when the change is disabled: with `/sw.js` off `server.ts`'s bundle-asset allowlist the spec's two controller waits time out and `curl` returns 403 while the manifest still returns 200. The display's session is not written to disk: the navigation entry is keyed by the document rather than by the URL that asked for it, so no key in any cache contains the token, and the cache name moved to v2 so a display holding a v1 cache has it swept. THE HONEST LIMIT, and it is filed rather than hidden: an INSTALLED app launches at `start_url: "/"`, which the host refuses to an unpaired reader with 403, so it works offline and is refused online — `vg-588`, whose answer belongs to the pairing spec the user ruled owns sessions. No phone was available, so every iOS and Android statement here is documentation, including the absent raster `apple-touch-icon`; and the shell cache grows with every build because nothing evicts an entry (`vg-589`). Landed by 0aa64fa4 and 133d0b3a.

title: Three verification bullets plan 4 wrote are not delivered as tests
detail:
FOUND BY THE WHOLE-PLAN REVIEW of the composition-panel plan (`2026-10-06-the-composition-panel.md`), over commits f8197102..af2d3e49, which ran after the plan closed because its workspace held no review diffs while plan 2s held eleven. Three bullets the plan states as verification have no test behind them at af2d3e49. (1) Task 7s browser bullet, "open Document, put the panel at an offset, swap to Assets and back - the offset survives", is not delivered: the new editor-pane-bar.spec.ts case asserts only visibility, and an offset-survival case exists only for the layer list. (2) Task 4s bullet "entering twice names the group once" has no test at all; bridge.dom.test.ts has no twice/once case, while the other four Task 4 bullets are present. (3) Task 8s unit bullet "with a selection ... assert on a group selection" is not unit-tested, because the panel no longer accepts a selection by construction, and is covered only by the composition-panel-document browser case. NOT FIXED ON THE FLY because the three need three different decisions rather than one correction: (1) is a missing proof of a behaviour that may work, (2) may be a bullet the bridges contract no longer carries, and (3) is arguably already discharged by the browser case - so whether the test or the plans wording should change is not the same answer each time. Nothing here contradicts a delivered behaviour: the gaps are in proof, not in product.

RULED 2026-10-12: THREE ANSWERS, because the row is right that these are not one question. (1) The offset-survival case is ADDED for the surfaces the bullet claimed: the behaviour is specified (DESIGN.md §7.7 — preserve per-pane offsets and disclosure state across routine updates), so a proof that exists for the layer list alone is a proof of one surface's luck rather than of the rule. (2) The once/twice case is PROVED as the bridge stands: `bridge.dom.test.ts` carries no such case at all, and an unproved verification bullet is the defect whether or not the behaviour is fine — if reading the bridge's contract shows it no longer carries entering-twice, the plan's bullet is annotated as superseded rather than a test invented for a contract that is gone. (3) The selection bullet is DISCHARGED by the browser case that already covers it, and the plan's bullet is annotated to name where its proof lives, because a unit test is not owed where the panel cannot accept a selection by construction. What settles all three: a bullet is a CLAIM, and a claim is discharged by pointing at its proof or by correcting the claim — never by leaving it standing. CORRECTED ON CLOSE, 2026-10-18: this detail names `editor-pane-bar.spec.ts`, which no longer exists — the rail replaced the pane bar at `c6ee8d32`. The visibility-only case it means is `editor-rail.spec.ts`'s "shows the theme's own panel in the left column, and swaps away from it", and the layer-list pin is that same file's "a collapse between two swaps does not lose the list's scroll". The finding itself stands; only the file name had rotted.
check: The three verification bullets are each discharged, and none is left standing: a bullet is a claim, and a claim is discharged by pointing at its proof or by correcting the claim. THE OFFSET BULLET IS DELIVERED by a new browser case, `editor-rail.spec.ts`'s "each pane comes back to the offset it was left at", which walks all four rail slots, leaves each at an offset, swaps away and back and reads the offset again — read on the integrated tree at `--project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` against a rebuilt bundle, 15 passed, and the run's own annotation printed `pane-offsets {"Composition":300,"Add":93,"Tokens":300,"Document":168}`. It is not vacuous: each slot's offset is read back off the element after it is written, so a pane that fits its box fails with the slot named rather than passing on a `0` that survived a swap — and with the shell's restore forced to `0` the case fails with `Composition came back to 0 rather than the 300 it was left at`. THE ONCE/TWICE BULLET IS SUPERSEDED rather than tested, which the ruling allowed: `bridge.ts`'s `enterGroup` is one hop and holds no context, so the bridge has no guard to defeat, and the property is the manager's — `setContext([entry])` is single-element by construction, so a two-copy context is unrepresentable rather than refused. It is proved where it lives, at `entered-group-state.dom.test.ts`'s "leaves one level when the same group is entered again". THE SELECTION BULLET IS DISCHARGED BY POINTER with no unit case added, which is the answer the ruling chose: `composition-panel.spec.ts`'s "keeps the document's own controls reachable while a card is selected" selects `group-cpu-card` and reads the Document pane with the selection standing. All three notes are additive on an archived plan — the bullets still read as written, with a dated note beside each — and they name what they actually prove: the Assets pane the offset bullet names no longer exists as a slot (the asset library now renders inside the Add pane's body), and the tokens-and-presets half of the selection bullet went with the archived `verified` row `vg-474`. Landed by fb58fb1f, with the annotation corrections in 201fe543.

title: `rebuild-driver.ts`'s `insert` takes the last match of a label, so `insert(page, "Line")` inserts the chart family's Line while the comment beside it says the legend is what tells them apart
detail: FOUND BY TASK 15.5'S SEAT (2026-10-16) while driving the Add pane for `vg-401`, and raised as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on `e2bd6741` rather than folded into that task. **THE CODE AND THE COMMENT DISAGREE, AND THE COMMENT IS THE ONE THAT IS WRONG.** `insert` (`tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts`, the `button.count() > 1` branch) reads `await ((await button.count()) > 1 ? button.last() : button).click();`. The comment directly above it says *"'Line' is a shape and a chart, and the legend above each is what tells them apart — the same distinction F1.17 made the screen."* **Taking `.last()` is an ordering assumption, not the legend**: it picks whichever tile the DOM happens to render last, so a caller asking for the shape's Line silently gets the chart family's, and the assertion that follows (`the scene grew by one`) passes either way. **MEASURED, NOT REASONED**: driving `insert(page, "Line")` for the Line-endpoint field inserted the chart family's Line, which is how the task's seat noticed — the field it then went looking for was on the other object. **WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TEST-HELPER NIT.** Every spec that inserts a labelled object through this driver inherits the ambiguity, and the failure mode is silent: the count grows, so the helper's own poll is satisfied, and the case proceeds against the wrong object. It is the shape `vg-535` and `vg-532` are in the register for — an instrument that reports success for a reason other than the one it claims. **WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT**: address the tile by its legend or its group rather than by position, so the family is named rather than inferred — or take the family as an explicit parameter and make the ambiguous call a type error. Either needs the Add pane's own structure read rather than a reordering of the two tiles, because `.first()` has the same defect mirrored. OWNER: `src/web/tests/e2e/rebuild-driver.ts`. SEVERITY: low for the product, moderate for the suite, because a wrong-object insertion is a case that measures something other than its subject.
check: The insert driver can no longer insert a family it was not asked for. `insert` and `addButton` now require an `AddGroup` — `"card" | "text" | "shape" | "chart"` — and the positional branch that took `button.last()` when a label matched twice is gone, so the ordering assumption that made a request for the shape's Line return the chart family's is unreachable rather than merely unlikely. It is enforced rather than intended: `tsconfig.e2e.json` is wired into `typecheck` and `gate` runs `typecheck`, and every call site in the tree passes the group — `add-pane.spec.ts`, `author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts`, `inspector-sections.spec.ts`, `rebuild-composition.ts` and the driver's own `addText`, `addRectangle` and `addChart`, the last of which was a live instance of the defect. The proof is the inserted object's **kind** and not a count, because a count is what the defect satisfied either way: with the addressing reverted to the positional form the case fails with `Expected: ["line","yunarichart"]` against `Received: ["yunarichart","yunarichart"]`, on the Fabric type tag, while the driver's own scene-grew-by-one poll passed either way. Read on the integrated tree: the case passes at `--project=desktop-chromium --workers=1` against a rebuilt bundle, and the changed specs pass in full rather than grepped (`add-pane` and `inspector-sections` 26 passed, `author-journey-rebuild` 9 passed). The `"text"` scope, which is the whole pane because text is the one object drawn in no fieldset, carries its collision hazard beside it — a card tile renders inside the pane's subtree, so a card ever labelled `Text` would give the lookup two matches, and it would fail loudly as a Playwright strict-mode violation rather than as the silent wrong insert this row was about. `AddGroup` is a documented hand-copy of `InsertableObject["kind"]` because the editor exports only its barrel and a deep import drags React into the e2e program; the doc names the owner the two must agree with. Landed by f1153f0f, with the scope note in 26b2ff79.

title: The copy walk probes the copy table's functions with generic arguments, so key-dependent strings are never collected and a surface printing one goes falsely red
detail: FOUND BY TASK 7.1'S INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-13), which reframed the implementer's own finding: `glassRefusals` in `ui-copy.ts` IS owned by that module, so 'copy outside the export' is not the defect. THE DEFECT IS THE PROBE. `ui-copy.test.ts`'s `copy()` calls each exported copy function with generic arguments to enumerate the strings a surface could print, and a function whose result depends on a key cannot be enumerated that way: `glassRefusals` and `chartFamilyLabels` take a key and are never collected. CONSEQUENCE, AND ITS DIRECTION: a surface printing one of those strings reads as a literal with no owner, so the walk goes falsely **RED** rather than falsely green -- which is the safe direction for the author and the expensive one for the instrument, because a net that cries wolf on its own table trains its reader to widen the carve-outs, which is how `vg-338`'s class stays uncaught. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether `copy()` can enumerate a key-dependent function's outputs (probe the function over the keys the document can hold) or whether the walk needs a declared key list per such function. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any surface prints `glassRefusals` or `chartFamilyLabels` today, which is why the row is latent rather than live. NEAR ROWS: vg-338 (a word with no owner, the class this net exists for), vg-418 (the surfaces the walk cannot mount). OWNER: `packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts`. SEVERITY: low -- latent, and it fails closed. **CLOSED 2026-10-18 with two corrections.** The walk is three files, not the one this row's OWNER field named: `ui-copy-readers.ts` holds `copy()`, `ui-copy-surfaces.test.ts` holds the surface walk and the header, and `ui-copy-panels.test.ts` holds the imperative panels and the picker — `ui-copy.test.ts` is the table's own rules and holds neither hole. And the row's second keyed function is stale: `chartFamilyLabels` is `uiCopy.chartFamilies` and the object walk already collects it.
check: The copy walk collects what a key-dependent function answers, not only what its fallback says. `copy()` in `ui-copy-readers.ts` calls every function entry in `uiCopy` with one argument, so `inspectorFields.glassRefused` — which chooses its sentence by the kind it is asked with — reached only the fallback it composes and the table's ten refusal sentences were collected by nothing. A second pass now probes it over `glassRefusalKinds`, exported from `ui-copy.ts` as `Object.keys(glassRefusals)`, so a kind added to the table is probed without a second list to keep in step. **The proof is that the strings are collected, and it fails when the keyed pass is disabled**: with the pass commented out, `npx vitest run packages/editor/src/ui-copy.test.ts` exits 1 with `AssertionError: Polyline: expected [ 'Yunari', 'Editor panes', …(452) ] to include 'A Polyline is an open path, so there …'`, and the restore was proved with `cmp` and a SHA-256 rather than with git. Read on the integrated tree, `npm run gate` exits 0 with 264 test files and 3487 tests. **The row's second function is stale and this is the correction**: `chartFamilyLabels` needs no probe, because it is `uiCopy.chartFamilies` (`ui-copy.ts`, exported at the table's `chartFamilies` key), so the object walk already collects `Gauge`, `Line`, `Bar` and `Pie` — measured, all four present in `copy()`'s output. **What the row asked and this leaves open is filed as vg-592**: the probe passes one argument, so a function of two or more (`panels.artboardOutside`, `draftRecovery.lead`) is still collected by nothing, and `copy()`'s docblock now states that limit instead of claiming a superset. Landed by a167ceb5, with the claims corrected in 599ce9ce.

title: The copy walk mounts no shortcut sheet, no publish popover and no library or new-document dialog, so a literal in one of them is owned by nothing
detail: FOUND BY TASK 7.1'S IMPLEMENTER AND CONFIRMED AS A ROW BY ITS SCOPED RE-REVIEW (2026-10-13). The copy walk now mounts the shell, the Settings Appearance/Keyboard/About tabs, the canvas context menu, the opened menu popups and the colour picker, but not the `?` shortcut sheet, the publish popover, or the library and new-document dialogs. Each of those renders words an author reads, and a literal in one of them is read by no net -- which is exactly `vg-335`'s class (a reachable surface the walk does not read) rather than `vg-338`'s (a word with no owner in the table). THE HEADER IS NOT A FIX: `ui-copy.test.ts`'s header now states these four are not mounted, and a comment can vanish silently while owning nothing. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether each surface is reachable in jsdom at all, one at a time -- `vg-215`'s finding was that a Base UI popover's CLOSE is not reachable in jsdom, which is about the close half and does not settle the open half these reads need.
