title: A whole-suite browser run against a `dist` built by `npm run build` alone has no `control-fixture.html`, so the fixture-mounting `design-language-*.spec.ts` specs fail as a missing page and read as a product regression
detail:
MEASURED 2026-10-13, on the acceptance section's 'Are the fifteen met verdicts still supported' review. **The trap, measured rather than argued**: `npm run build -w @yunari/editor` (exit 0) leaves `packages/editor/dist` holding `assets/`, `favicon.svg` and `index.html`; `npm run build:fixture -w @yunari/editor` (exit 0) then adds `control-fixture.html`. The cause is deliberate and documented in `packages/editor/vite.config.fixture.ts`, whose docblock says the fixture is a second invocation rather than a second `rollupOptions.input` so the production build 'emits exactly the bundle graph it emitted before the fixture existed' and does not ship test scaffolding. So the page's existence depends on which build was run last, and a plain `npm run build` **deletes** it (`emptyOutDir` is true there, false in the fixture config). **What it costs.** Playwright's webServer previews `packages/editor` on 4174 and `openFixture` navigates to `http://127.0.0.1:4174/control-fixture.html`, so with the page absent that case fails on a 404 and looks identical to a design-language violation. **It has already produced a false classification in a durable record.** The phase-8 close annotation in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:915` triages the 18 whole-suite reds at `3a368c6a` and lists `design-language.spec.ts:437` among the three that are 'pre-existing, failing identically at base', with its cause correctly stated as 'its fixture page is not a vite input and so is absent from every built dist'. **The cause is right and the classification is wrong**: it failed identically at base only because neither run ran the recipe the repository documents, and at HEAD `aa16a2c5`, with `npm run build` then `npm run build:fixture`, the case **passes** (desktop-chromium, 15.4 s) in a whole-suite run. It is not pre-existing and it is not a product defect. **The recipe is documented and unowned.** Five places state it by hand - `docs/evidence/screenshots/README.md:8`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-12-the-backlog-drain.md:510`, `docs/product/triage/triage-B6.md:11` and `triage-B5.md:120`, and the archived `plans/archive/2026-10-12-the-backlog-reproduction-pass.md:24` ('Build before browser runs') - and the archived `2026-10-11-settings-parity.md:29` records the exact hazard ('`npm run build -w @yunari/editor` empties `dist` and deletes `control-fixture.html`, so `npm run build:fixture` must follow it'). No script enforces it: `test:e2e` is bare `playwright test`, and nothing in `playwright.config.ts` builds or asserts the page. **The decision it needs, which is why it is filed rather than fixed on the fly**: whether `npm run test:e2e` builds the fixture itself, or a `globalSetup` asserts the page exists and refuses with this cause, or the precondition stays documented and a run that skips it is simply wrong. Three owners could take it - the e2e config, the build scripts, or the docs - and each has a different cost: auto-building puts the fixture in every browser run including CI's, while asserting keeps the two builds separate and turns a 404 into a named refusal. **Scope, measured so the row is not read as bigger than it is**: this is the only case in either whole-suite sample that fails on a missing built page. `control-fixture.html` is reached by this case alone; the other fixture-opening specs (`glass-authoring`, `snapping`) build their own pages into the root preview and are unaffected. **Sampled beside it, at the same commits**: two whole-suite runs, `3a368c6a` (273 passed / 18 failed / 214 skipped) and `aa16a2c5` (273 / 18 / 214), whose red **memberships differ by nine of eighteen** - so a whole-suite red count is a load artefact rather than a defect list, and the five acceptance-relevant reds sampled from the second run (`shell-appearance.spec.ts:478`, `editor.spec.ts:1025`, `editor.spec.ts:2103`, `snapping.spec.ts:598` and `:702`) all pass alone and serial at that same commit.
**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-10-16.** This row's title and detail name `design-language.spec.ts:437`, and Phase 15's Task 15.4 split that file by surface into seven spec files over one reader module — so the line number names nothing and the file no longer exists. **The defect is unchanged**: `control-fixture.html` is still reached by the specs that mount the fixture, and a `dist` built by `npm run build` alone still omits it. The earlier line number is left standing in the detail above as the record of what was read on 2026-10-13, which is a dated measurement rather than a live pointer. **CLOSED 2026-10-18, with this row's own premise corrected.** The detail above says the specs fail on a **404**; measured, they do not — `vite preview` defaults to `appType: 'spa'` and answers `/control-fixture.html` with **200 serving `index.html`**, so the failure was a missing mount rather than a missing route, and a status check would have been a guard that cannot fail. The defect is otherwise as written, and the `discovered, not fixed` half of it is filed as vg-595: the shared 4174 preview reuses an existing server, so a browser proof can be served by another worktree's `dist` — which is how the controller's first red-proof attempt read green.
check: The fixture-mounting specs no longer read a missing page as a product regression. `openFixture` in `tests/e2e/design-language-readers.ts` is the single opener all three of them share (`design-language-contrast`, `-controls` and `-layout`, through `prepareControls`), and it now checks the served page for the fixture's own `#control-fixture` mount — static markup in `control-fixture.html` that `index.html`'s `#app` is not — and throws a message naming the cause and the recipe instead of failing at the `[data-fixture-root]` assert. **The check keys on the marker rather than the status because the status cannot fail, and that is this row's own premise corrected**: with no `control-fixture.html` on disk, `npx vite preview packages/editor` (default `appType: 'spa'`) answers that route with **200** and `text/html` serving `index.html` — measured, `has #control-fixture: false`, `has #app: true` — so a `response.ok()` guard would have been green in exactly the case it was written for. **The proof is the failure the reader now sees**, reproduced on the integrated tree against a `dist` built by `npm run build` alone: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/design-language-controls.spec.ts --project=desktop-chromium --workers=1 --grep "the control set renders in the design language"` exits 1 with `http://127.0.0.1:4174/control-fixture.html served no control fixture: the built editor has no `control-fixture.html`, so the preview fell back to `index.html`. Build it with `npm run build:fixture -w @yunari/editor` after `npm run build -w @yunari/editor` — the production build empties `dist` and deletes the fixture page.` thrown at `openFixture` via `prepareControls`; after `npm run build:fixture -w @yunari/editor` the same command exits 0 with 1 passed. **The production build is untouched** — the change is one test-only file — so `npm run build` still deletes the fixture page, which is the deliberate design `vite.config.fixture.ts` documents rather than the defect. Scoped to the three specs that reach the fixture rather than to the process-wide `global-setup.ts`, which would refuse every spec including those that never open the fixture. `npm run gate` exit 0. Landed by a796d77e.

title: lanAddress() returns the first non-internal IPv4 with no preference for a physical adapter, so the header can name an address no phone can reach
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 1.3, which was told to file it and instead left a Discovered, not fixed trailer, because its dispatch forbade writing the register. src/web/packages/host/src/cli/net.ts:90-100 iterates os.networkInterfaces() and returns the first non-internal IPv4. A laptop that also carries a Hyper-V virtual switch, a WSL adapter, a Docker bridge or a VPN routinely enumerates one of those first, so GET /api/hosting hands the editor header an address no phone on the Wi-Fi can reach, and the QR encodes it. Nothing on this machine shows the mistake -- the header renders a plausible dotted quad and the failure appears only on the phone that cannot connect. That address is the header's entire payload, so this is a correctness defect and not a cosmetic one. Not fixed there: the fix needs a decision that task did not own -- which interface wins, how to rank them, and what to do when three are plausible -- and it belongs to lanAddress()'s owner rather than to the route that reads it. Reproduction: run the host on a machine with any virtual adapter present and compare the address printed after Phones on this Wi-Fi with the physical adapter's own.

RULED 2026-10-12: THE DEFAULT-ROUTE INTERFACE WINS, and the ranking is data beside `lanAddress()`'s owner (`host/src/cli/net.ts:90-100`, which today returns the first non-internal IPv4 and therefore whatever the OS enumerates first). The rule, in order: drop loopback, link-local and internal candidates; drop interfaces whose name matches a virtual-adapter pattern (Hyper-V and `vEthernet`, WSL, Docker and `br-`, VirtualBox, VMware, and the tunnel adapters a VPN installs), because those are exactly the ones a phone cannot reach; among what remains prefer the interface carrying the default IPv4 route, since that is the address the phone's own traffic leaves by. When two candidates survive and neither carries the route, the host keeps its choice DETERMINISTIC (lowest interface index) and logs the alternatives rather than silently guessing — the failure this row describes is invisible on the machine that makes it, so the alternatives being on the record is what makes a wrong pick findable without a phone. The pattern list is data, owned beside the function, so a new virtual adapter is a one-line addition rather than a new heuristic. **CLOSED 2026-10-18.** Three things the fix did not settle are filed rather than absorbed: `vg-596` (the fallback `systeminformation` returns cannot be told from a real route read, so the tie-break warning is suppressed on a machine whose route query fails), `vg-597` (the route read is an `execSync` `netstat -r`, measured at 126-149 ms of blocked event loop plus a child process, on every `GET /api/hosting`) and `vg-598` (four e2e specs carry their own copy of the old first-non-internal rule). The two contradictions this created in the queued per-display-themes spec and plan are annotated in `0689aee4`.
check: `lanAddress()` no longer returns the first non-internal IPv4, so the header and the QR cannot name an address no phone on the Wi-Fi can reach. `rankLanAddresses` implements the row's ruling as a pure, injectable function: drop loopback, link-local and internal; drop virtual adapters by name through `VIRTUAL_ADAPTER_PATTERNS`, which is data beside the function; prefer the interface carrying the default IPv4 route; otherwise take the first the OS enumerated and name the alternatives. **The route is read through `systeminformation`, already a shipped host dependency and already in both notices** — Node exposes no routing table and no interface index, so "lowest index" is read as "first enumerated", which the review confirmed is forced rather than chosen. **The proof is a fixture rather than the machine**: `rankLanAddresses` takes a `LanSource`, and `readLanSource` is the only reader of the real OS, so the cases carry a virtual switch and a link-local pseudo-adapter ahead of a physical NIC, a default route that is not the first candidate, a tie-break that names its alternatives, and a single-physical-adapter no-regression case. Reproduced on the integrated tree with the ranking swapped back to the old first-non-internal loop: `npx vitest run packages/host/src/cli/net.test.ts` exits 1 with 5 failed and 9 passed of 14, naming the virtual-switch, tie-break, default-route, only-virtual and console-warning cases, and the restore is proved by `cmp` and a SHA-256 rather than by git. `npm run gate` exit 0 — 265 test files, 3501 tests. **Two corrections are recorded rather than amended**: `7dc4332e`'s body says "the two that still pass" of the nine cases, and four passed — two of them the pattern cases, which never touch the ranking — and the review refuted the docblock's claim that a failed query yields `undefined`, because `systeminformation` falls back to a name of its own; the docblock now states that measured mechanism and the tie-break suppression it causes is filed as vg-596. Landed by 3628257d, with the totality fix and four measured pattern entries in ba553f98.

title: A GET that arrives while a LAN move is in flight waits for a move that is waiting for it, and the host never listens again
detail:
FOUND BY PLAN 6'S TASK 3.4, which reasoned it, could not reproduce it, and left it unfiled because its cause was not established; filed here because the consequence is a permanently dead host rather than a slow answer. The mechanism, read from the code rather than observed: server.ts:770 has the GET await binding?.idle(); cli/hosting.ts:86 has the move await server.close(), which does not complete until every existing connection ends. A GET whose handler is parked on idle() is one of those connections and will not end until it answers, so the move never finishes, bind(next) never runs, and the server never listens again -- every editor and every display on that host is dead until the process is restarted. It is NOT a slow editor re-read, which is how it was first described. That is the whole reason it is worth a row. Reachability is narrow and the narrowness is the honest part: `finish` -> setLan -> server.close() runs in one synchronous run with no await between them, so no connection can be ACCEPTED in that window, and closeIdleConnections() has already taken the idle keep-alive sockets. What remains is a request already sitting on an accepted connection when close() is called -- a second editor tab, a display reconnecting, anything issued concurrently with the PUT rather than after it. Ordinary single-client use cannot reach it, which is why no reproduction was found. The fix is a design decision between two hazards, and they are not symmetric: the move could destroy connections instead of waiting on them -- closeAllConnections() is now safe precisely BECAUSE the answer is already flushed, which is what Task 3.4's Step 5 accidentally proved when putting it back did not break anything -- at the cost of an empty reply to whichever request was unlucky, which the editor's bounded re-read already tolerates; or the GET could bound its wait and answer from state(), at the cost of answering before the move settles. The first is the smaller change and the failure it trades for is bounded; somebody should still choose rather than inherit.

RULED 2026-10-12: THE MOVE MUST NOT WAIT ON A REQUEST: destroy the remaining connections rather than letting `server.close` wait for them. As written, `move()` calls `closeIdleConnections()` and then `server.close(cb)` (`host/src/cli/hosting.ts:85-86`), and close waits for ACTIVE connections — so a GET arriving during the move blocks the callback, the move blocks the GET, and the host never listens again. That is a deadlock reachable by any second client, not a race, and a deadlock is not a hazard to be weighed against an empty reply. The trade is the one `vg-173` already measured and the editor already tolerates: whichever request was unlucky gets an empty reply, and its bounded re-read recovers. The other branch is rejected on the repo own rule rather than on taste — answering from `state()` before the move settles would have the host assert something it knows to be stale, which is the fabrication this product forbids everywhere else. **CLOSED 2026-10-18.** Two things this leaves are filed rather than absorbed: `vg-599` (`closeIdleConnections()` and the per-connection `answering` bookkeeping have no production caller left, so decision 0070's connection-pruning paragraph justifies a capability nothing invokes) and `vg-600` (whether a display's SSE stream still ends gracefully after a move, since `SseConnection.close()` is `response.end()` and the move destroys that socket just after). The row's mechanism is confirmed rather than corrected — the review built the parked-on-`idle()` arrangement the seat had argued was unreachable.
check: A LAN move can no longer wait on a request, so the host always listens again. `move()` in `cli/hosting.ts` called `closeIdleConnections()` and then `await server.close(cb)`, and `close()` waits for connections that are still answering — so a request in flight held the callback, the move held the request, and the host was dead until the process restarted. It now calls `closeAllConnections()`, which is the ruling of 2026-10-12 taken literally: destroy the remaining connections rather than let `close` wait for them, spending the trade `vg-173` measured and the editor already tolerates. **The case reproduces the row's own mechanism rather than a weaker one**, and the reviewer built that version after refuting the seat's argument that it was not constructible: a socket whose request the host is still reading is spared by `closeIdleConnections()` because it is mid-request, so it survives the move and goes idle-and-alive once its promised body arrives, and a **second** request on that same socket runs its handler after `setLan` has assigned `moving` — parking on `idle()` for a move parked on that connection. **The proof is that arrangement failing when the fix is disabled**, reproduced by the controller on the integrated tree: `npx vitest run packages/host/src/server.test.ts -t "does not leave a request parked"` exits 1 with `AssertionError: expected { ended: false, controlAnswered: true } to match object { ended: true }` — the socket still alive and still dispatching (`/api/health` answers beside it) while `/api/hosting` never does — and the restore is proved by `cmp` and a SHA-256 rather than by git. `npm run gate` exit 0 — 265 test files, 3502 tests. **Three corrections came out of the review and are recorded rather than amended**: the seat's reachability argument was wrong (refuted by a working construction), the stale `server.ts` PUT-handler comment was free to correct because nine existing decision notes already claim that path (the gate exits 0 on it; the seat had reasoned from the watchlist entry instead of probing `covers()`), and `expect(answered.status).toBe(200)` is not the discriminating assertion — it passes with the fix absent too, because the move starts on `response.once("finish")` and those bytes are already with the OS. Landed by b142f2ef, with the case and the comment in 73c3b87a.

title: The theme document schema gives metadata.name no minLength, so an empty name validates
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 5's task review and CONFIRMED by the controller against the schema. schema/theme-document.schema.json defines the theme's name as $defs/metadata/properties/name = {type: string, maxLength: 200} - there is NO minLength, so an imported or hand-edited envelope carrying metadata.name: "" is schema-valid. That reaches the identity chip as an empty name: editor-main.ts:294 reads metadata?.name ?? envelope.id, and ?? falls back only on null/undefined, so "" passes through and DocumentIdentity (which hides only on undefined) renders a nameless frame - the bible section 9 failure its own comment promises cannot happen. The code side was fixed in Task 5's fix round by switching to ||; THIS row is the schema side, filed rather than fixed because adding minLength: 1 would start rejecting documents that validate today, which is a compatibility decision rather than a bug fix. Evidence it is an oversight rather than a decision: the sibling $defs/fontAssetReference/properties/license/name and the palette and typePreset group names all carry minLength: 1, and the theme's own top-level name is the one that does not. OWNER: unassigned - whoever owns document validation; the decision is whether a nameless theme is legal at all. SEVERITY: low once the read site is defensive - no data is lost, and the worst case is a chip showing an id instead of a name.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the controller, as a code/architecture correctness question under the users standing licence: name GAINS minLength 1, AND THE LOADER NAMES WHAT IT FINDS UNNAMED. A theme with an empty name cannot be presented in the library, so the schema refuses it -- but a stored document that validates today is not allowed to become unloadable, so the migration supplies a name at load (from the file or a generated label) and the schema holds for anything written from now on. COST IF WRONG: a theme saved without a name gains one the author did not choose, which is visible and renameable, where the alternative is a document that cannot be opened at all. **CLOSED 2026-10-18.** What the sequence leaves is filed rather than absorbed: `vg-601` (the runtime has no twin of either bound — it repairs an empty name rather than refusing it, and stores one over 200 characters). Three comments that asserted the schema permits an empty name were corrected in the same sequence, and the migration case's comment with them: `entryFor`'s `??` does not fall back on `""`, so the library line read empty before this, which the commit had claimed otherwise.
check: The published schema now gives `metadata.name` a `minLength`, so an empty name is refused instead of validating: `$defs/metadata/properties/name` in `schema/theme-document.schema.json` reads `{type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 200}`, and `fabric-envelope-schema-sync.test.ts` pins both bounds, because `envelope-keys-disagreement.test.ts` compares key sets alone and would not notice either one moving. The refusal is the published half only — no JSON-schema engine runs in this repo (no `ajv`, and the only in-repo readers of the schema are test files) — and the loader is the half that keeps a stored document loading: `namedEnvelope` in `envelope-semantics.ts` supplies the document's own `id`, applied by `validateFabricThemeEnvelope`, which is where a document becomes an envelope whatever brought the bytes. **The migration case is the row's own claim** — a real `theme.json` on disk carrying `name: ""` — and it fails when the naming is disabled, reproduced by the controller on the integrated tree: exit 1 with `AssertionError: expected '' to be 'nameless'`, restore proved by `cmp` and a SHA-256 rather than by git. The independent review then found the first version threw on `name: null` (`null.length`), which is the same failure the migration exists to prevent — and `ThemeStore.list`'s catch turned one such document into an empty library — so the guard reads the name as a string; that case reddens the same way, `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')`. `npm run gate` exit 0 — 265 test files, 3506 tests. Landed by b1804b30, with the null-name fix in 2adf1247.

title: The editor's pairing control mints nothing, because it reads the session answer the host no longer sends
detail:
FOUND WHILE DOING TASK 1.2 OF THE PER-DISPLAY-THEMES PLAN (2026-10-18), in the commit that deleted the expiring session store. `mintSession` in `packages/editor/src/hosting-client.ts` POSTs `/api/pairing/sessions` and accepts only `{ session: { token, expiresAt } }`, answering `undefined` when `expiresAt` is not a string. The host now answers `{ display, token }` (the pairing block in `packages/host/src/server.ts`), because ruling 12 removes the TTL and with it `expiresAt` — so the control had no code to draw. **THE FIX ROUND RULED THE MINT OUT ENTIRELY** (`cd6d6d6a`, R9): `HostingStore` no longer calls `mintSession` on either path, because a mint per read persists a junk display holding a never-expiring credential, and the surface now shows the host's address — a fact from `/api/hosting` that needs no credential — with no QR and no expiry. What is left here is the function itself: `mintSession` still cannot parse the answer the host sends, and Task 1.4 owns it and the exchange that replaces the flow. **THIS IS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE PLAN'S OWN SEQUENCING AND MAY ALREADY BE OWNED BY IT**: Task 1.3 reshapes the pairing routes (`POST ?displayId`, `GET { displays }`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/displays/:id`) and the editor has to follow it either way; this row exists because no task in that plan names `packages/editor/src/hosting-client.ts`, so the update may have no owner. **WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT**: a task that reads the display answer in `mintSession` and `HostingAnswer`, or a ruling that the editor's pairing control is withdrawn until the one-time-code exchange exists (spec section 'Pairing a display that has no camera'). **NOT ESTABLISHED**: whether the plan's route-shape phase carries an editor task its file list does not show, and what the surface should show in place of an expiry now that a pairing does not expire. **THE SHAPE OF THE FIX**: `HostingAnswer.session` becomes the minted display and its token, and the expiry line in `publish-control.tsx` goes with it. NEAR ROWS: vg-587 (the pairing surfaces' ownership split). OWNER: `packages/editor/src/hosting-client.ts` with `packages/editor/src/editor-shell/publish-control.tsx`. SEVERITY: medium — a visible control stops working on a path the plan is mid-way through changing.

CLOSED 2026-10-18 by f864d4e4, Task 1.4 of the per-display-themes plan, which is the task the controller's ruling R7 assigned this row to. The row's own two candidates for settling it both landed: the one-time-code exchange exists, and the function that could not parse the answer is deleted rather than repaired. The shape the row predicted is not the shape that shipped — `HostingAnswer.session` did not become the minted display; the field is gone, because the card shows a code the host mints and not a credential the editor holds.
check: `mintSession` is gone, so the editor's pairing control no longer reads a session answer. title: The re-find ladder always builds an http origin, so from an https page every probe is mixed content and it can never match
detail: FOUND BY TASK 4.6 OF PLAN 2026-10-18-PER-DISPLAY-THEMES, and carried in that commit as a Discovered, not fixed trailer with no register row until now. originFor and refindTarget hard-code the scheme (src/web/packages/player/src/host-refind.ts:98-119), so every probe the ladder makes is http://<address>:<port>. The commit body justifies that with the host answering both on one port, which is true at the network level (server.ts:940-950) and irrelevant to the browser: a page served over https probing an http origin is mixed content, which browsers block, so refindHost would answer undefined on every attempt and a display would be stranded at an address that moved. CAUSE ESTABLISHED by reading the two builders and the browser rule. NOT REACHABLE TODAY: nothing in the repo emits an https display URL. pair.html navigates to a relative /?session=, and hosting-client.ts displayUrl and publish-control.tsx phone address both print http:// (vg-587); vg-580 verified the LAN origin is plain http and not a secure context. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the fix is a decision, not a line. The scheme must come from somewhere -- the page it runs on, or the pairing -- and it also decides what refindTarget NAVIGATES to, which is the certificate the display must then trust; 0070 means the host now mints its own local CA, so the secure origin is real and unadvertised, and the two changes belong together. Owner: src/web/packages/player/src/host-refind.ts for the builders, with the scheme decision shared with vg-587, which owns advertising the secure origin. A regression test would serve a display over https, move the host, and assert the ladder still matches.
check: The ladder no longer builds an http origin for an https page. Verified after 8ddb1fc2: src/web/packages/player/src/main-https.dom.test.ts runs the player at an https URL and asserts every absolute URL the ladder asks for is https, including both named rungs and the sweep (probes.length > 2), and it reddens alone when main.ts hard-codes "http"; host-refind.test.ts carries the scheme through all three rungs and keeps the http display working.

title: Glass loses its backdrop for one frame every few seconds on a phone, because a looping background video drops below HAVE_CURRENT_DATA at its loop seam
detail: REPORTED BY THE USER on 2026-10-20, from a real phone player, with a screen recording (3.53 s, 2340x1080, C:\tmp\9remote-uploads\1792502498947_Screen_Recording_20261020_202035_Chrome.mp4). Their observations, in the order they gave them, and the last one is the one that names the defect: it happens ONLY with a video background (a static background ran for tens of minutes with nothing), it happens every few seconds, and - correcting their own first description - it is not that panels disappear: **all the glass material becomes way more transparent for one frame, then returns to normal.** Their fourth observation, given on 2026-10-20 after the mechanism was filed, is the one that DISCRIMINATES: **the video itself appeared normal when it happened.** Their fifth, the same day, and it is the one that closes the mechanism rather than narrowing it: **at the frame the glass became less opaque there is a video frame behind the panels, not a background colour** - and they could not tell whether the video also froze, which is itself informative, since a one-frame hold at a loop seam is invisible where a stall is not. THE MECHANISM, established by reading and matching every one of those observations. (1) The glass renderer's scratch surface is CLEARED at the start of every render - `surfaceFor` ends with `context.clearRect(0, 0, region.width, region.height)` (`scene-fabric/src/glass.ts`). (2) The backdrop is painted into that now-empty scratch immediately after: `media.paint(scratchContext, region, {...})` (`glass.ts:413-421`), and `media` is the background-media layer's own `backdrop()`. (3) The panel's own content is then composited over it (`glass.ts:422-432`). So the glass material IS the backdrop plus a tint: when the backdrop paint draws nothing, the panel composites over TRANSPARENCY, which reads as glass that has lost its body - more transparent, not missing. That is the reported symptom exactly, and it is why the first description (panels vanishing) was the wrong reading of the same frame. (4) The backdrop paint fails when the video has no current frame: `paint` begins `const source = intrinsic(mounted); if (source === undefined) return false;` and `intrinsic` refuses a video with `if (element.readyState < 2) return undefined;` (`scene-fabric/src/background-media.ts`). `readyState < 2` is below HAVE_CURRENT_DATA, which is precisely the state a looping video passes through at its loop seam, because `mounted.loop = true` (`background-media.ts:131`) makes the element re-seek to zero. (5) WHY IT IS PERIODIC AND WHY IT IS THE VIDEO'S OWN PERIOD: the video's decoded frames are what drive the repaints - `followFrames` is a `requestVideoFrameCallback` loop (`background-media.ts:262-283`) whose callback is `() => { if (glass.liveSurfaces() > 0) canvas.requestRenderAll(); }` (`scene-fabric/src/scene.ts:142-144`) - so the seam window is hit by a repaint, and the period is the background video's duration. (6) WHY ALL GLASS AT ONCE: every glass panel samples the same one backdrop in the same render. (7) WHY ONLY A VIDEO: a still image's `intrinsic` refuses only before its bytes land (`!element.complete || naturalWidth === 0`), once, so a static background never re-enters that state; `background-media.ts`'s own `notifyOnDecode` comment already describes the one-shot version of this for images and nothing handles the video's recurring one. WHAT THE VIDEO'S OWN NORMAL APPEARANCE RULES OUT, which is why that observation is worth more than the symptom it accompanies: it excludes every cause on the MEDIA side. A stall or a rebuffer would have frozen the video, a decode failure would have blanked it, and `update()` tearing the element down would have removed it from the page (`background-media.ts:93` `layer.replaceChildren()`, then `:121-137`), and the user saw none of those - so the media was presenting correctly throughout and the loss is entirely in the SAMPLER. That leaves the one asymmetry the code shows: the browser composites the video from the frame it last presented, while the canvas sampler re-checks `readyState` (`background-media.ts:312`) and refuses. The video keeps looking right because the compositor is holding a frame; `drawImage` is gated on a different question - does the element report data at the current position - and at a loop wrap that answer is briefly no. WHAT THE FIFTH OBSERVATION SETTLES, by reading the composite rather than reasoning about it. `composite` (`glass.ts:347`) builds each panel's backdrop in a scratch surface in TWO steps: `media.paint(scratchContext, ...)` first (`:413-421`), then the CANVAS'S OWN PIXELS drawn in over it (`scratchContext.drawImage(target, region.left, region.top, ...)`, `:422-432`); that scratch is then drawn back over the panel's area with `blur(...) saturate(...)` (`:474-484`). So when the media paint draws nothing, the scratch holds only the canvas's own pixels in that region - and the canvas there is TRANSPARENT, because the video is a DOM sibling BELOW the canvas (`background-media.ts:60` prepends the layer) rather than an object on it. The panel's area therefore keeps the canvas's transparency, and the panel's own semi-transparent fill is drawn over it: the reader sees the RAW VIDEO through the tint, where they normally see BLUR(VIDEO) through the tint. That is exactly "a video frame behind them, not background color", and it is why the panel reads as less opaque rather than absent - the tint is unchanged and only its backdrop lost the diffusion. It also closes the two remaining alternatives in one observation: a whole-canvas loss would have taken the panel's own content with it, and a background colour would have meant the canvas was painting something there; the reader saw neither. STILL NOT MEASURED, and it is a browser-level claim rather than a code-level one: that a looping video's `readyState` really does dip below 2 at the wrap. No phone is in this loop. The cheap on-device proof needs no rebuild - listen for `seeking`/`seeked`/`waiting`/`stalled`/`emptied`/`suspend` on the video element and log `readyState` with `currentTime`; if one of those with `readyState < 2` lands on the same beat as the fade, the mechanism is measured rather than inferred. WHY IT IS A ROW AND NOT AN ON-THE-FLY FIX: the cause is now named, but the correct behaviour is not specified anywhere - what SHOULD glass show when its backdrop has no frame? The candidates are to skip the whole glass render for that frame so the panel keeps its previous appearance (cheapest, and invisible), to keep the last successfully painted backdrop rather than clearing it, or to treat a video that has already presented a frame as usable and draw its last frame. **The evidence now favours the second**: the media is genuinely being shown to the reader and only the sampler lost it, so keeping the last good backdrop restores exactly what was there. It also disqualifies the third on its own terms - if `readyState` is below 2 there is no current frame for `drawImage` either, so the eligibility check may be honest and the defect is the `clearRect` that already ran (`glass.ts:523`, ahead of the paint at `:413-421`), which means the fix has to reorder the clear against the paint rather than loosen the check. Each is a different answer to a product question, both `glass.ts` and `background-media.ts` are on the reuse gate's watchlist so a decision note is owed before the first write, and the regression test is not obvious because it needs a video that stalls. Filed as issue 49 as well. OWNER: `scene-fabric`'s glass renderer together with its background-media layer.
check: `npx vitest run packages/scene-fabric/src/glass-lifecycle.dom.test.ts` exit 0, the case named "keeps the last backdrop across a frame the media cannot paint" passing — and it is the ONE case that fails (exit 1, `expected [ 255, 255, 255, 129 ] to deeply equal [ 255, 127, 255, 255 ]`) when `backdropFor`'s `return unmoved ? element : undefined;` is disabled to `return undefined;`. The check names the backdrop the title names. Stronger, and outside the repo: the browser A/B in decision 0079's rung 6b, where the same disable reads alpha 130 (the tint over transparency) at every loop wrap against alpha 255 with the fix.

title: An opaque artboard paint covers the DOM media layer, so a theme with both a video background and a solid board shows no video and nothing reports it
detail: FOUND 2026-10-20 while building the browser A/B for decision 0079 (the glass backdrop fix), and it is why the first run of that harness was void. WHERE: `createApplyArtboard` (`src/web/packages/scene-fabric/src/adapter.ts:272-290`) sets `canvas.backgroundColor = fabricArtboardPaint(plan.artboard.background, ...) ?? ""` whenever the resolved paint changed, and it reads nothing about `plan.artboard.backgroundMedia` — nor could it, because `planArtboard` (`renderer-core/src/scene/plan.ts:172`) resolves the paint from the theme and `ScenePlan` never carries the media. `mountBackgroundMedia` prepends its layer to the host (`background-media.ts:60`) and `scene.ts:98` appends the canvas after it, so the canvas paints ON TOP of the media: an opaque artboard paint covers the video completely. MEASURED, not inferred: a harness page mounting a real 3.533 s video behind a glass panel, with `plan.artboard.background` `#101318`, read `getImageData(4,4)` as `[16,19,24,255]` — the board's own fill, opaque — and the panel's colour did not move by a single channel across 1208 frames (`maxFrameDelta` 0), because no video pixel ever reached the glass. With `background: "transparent"` the same page reads `[0,0,0,0]` outside the panel and the video reaches it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this is a defect or intended precedence — a board's own paint winning over the media behind it is a defensible rule, and `vg-639` already records that two packages disagree about what a board with media behind it even is. What is not defensible either way is that it is silent: nothing reports it, and the e2e `videoEnvelope` (`tests/e2e/host-theme.ts:401`) declares exactly this combination (`background: palette.bar`, an opaque `#101318`) while no test decodes its video, so the fixture ships the trap and cannot see it. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a ruling on precedence, then either a validation issue when both are declared or a paint the media suppresses. WHY FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: the correct behaviour is a product decision, more than one owner could implement it (the adapter, the plan builder, or theme validation), and it is not the task that found it. REPORTED BY the controller, from the harness's own first run. RESOLVED 2026-10-21: the user ruled on the precedence this row could not settle — the media layer belongs above the board's colour, and the colour is the letterbox a `fit: "theme"` layer leaves — so decision 0080 took the paint off the canvas entirely, left it on the host behind the media layer, and moved it into the glass backdrop, which now composes the board's paint under its media. The editor's plate was the same defect in the other surface and is dropped once the board declares media. The second half of the title is answered rather than fixed: with the combination ruled correct, there is nothing left to report. PROVED IN THE BROWSER, one script both arms, on the 0079 harness with the board opaque at `#101318`: the fixed build reads the panel at alpha 255 across 1211 frames with `maxFrameDelta` 123 and the canvas at `[0,0,0,0]`; the pre-fix build reads 0 across 1209 with the canvas at `[16,19,24,255]`.
check: ran the browser A/B on the 0079 harness with an opaque #101318 board behind a real looping video: the panel reads alpha 255 across 1211 frames with maxFrameDelta 123, where the pre-fix build read 0 across 1209 — the video reaches the glass, so no paint covers the media layer any more

title: A chart's scalar settings are validated on neither path, so a v2 envelope carrying min above max, windowSeconds 0, or innerRadiusPercent above outerRadiusPercent is accepted
detail:
FOUND BY the review of ad94e5ed (finding 5), which asked the retirement report to stop justifying the deleted chart-content cases as coverage the Fabric half performs. It does not: fabric-envelope-validate.ts chartPaintReferences (line 513, called at line 96) reads a chart's settings for PAINT fields only - gauge track/progress, line stroke/area/palette, bar fill/track, pie remainderFill/palette - and its isRecord guard means a chart whose settings is not an object skips even those. WHAT WAS SEARCHED, so the negative can be judged rather than trusted: grep -rn for windowSeconds, maxPoints, innerRadiusPercent, outerRadiusPercent, min, max and total across src/web/packages/*/src and src/web/tests (excluding *.test.ts), plus schema/theme-document.schema.json. The only hits that touch these scalars are charts/settings-fields.ts (authoring bounds for the inspector, which ADR-0028 explicitly says must not become document validation), charts/line.ts and charts/pie.ts (render, where pie clamps via clampPercent and never refuses), data/store.ts and fake-source (Math.max(0, windowSeconds) floors the window rather than refusing it), and editor/src/preview-source.ts. schema/theme-document.schema.json carries no settings property at all, because a v2 scene is opaque Fabric JSON, so no JSON-Schema bound exists either. MEASURED, not inferred: calling validateFabricThemeEnvelope on a conforming envelope whose chart object carries gauge {min: 10, max: 1}, line {windowSeconds: 0}, line {maxPoints: -5}, pie {innerRadiusPercent: 80, outerRadiusPercent: 20}, pie {total: {kind: fixed, value: null}}, or settings: ["windowSeconds"] returns ok: true for all six. PRE-EXISTING, NOT CREATED BY THE RETIREMENT: the deleted v1 validator did own these (validate.ts validateSettingsRange required gauge/bar max > min, line windowSeconds and maxPoints above 0, pie outer above inner and a finite fixed total), but the v2 path never reached it - fabric-envelope-validate.ts called validateThemeDocument with a synthetic {schemaVersion: 1, nodes: []} document, so no node-level case ever ran against an envelope. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether a scalar chart bound is meant to be enforced at the envelope boundary (refuse) or recovered at render (clamp, as pie already does); if recovery is the intent, this closes as intended behaviour with the clamping owners named.

RULED 2026-10-12: REFUSE AT THE ENVELOPE BOUNDARY, and the range comes from the descriptor table rather than a second table written into the validator. `charts/settings-fields.ts` already owns each scalar setting and already carries its own `min` (windowSeconds 1, maxPoints 2, lineWidth and markerSize 0), so the validator READS that owner instead of re-deciding it — which is what the deleted v1 validator did, and deleting it removed the refusal without moving the ownership anywhere. The relational cases are the same rule one step out: Y `min` above `max`, and `innerRadiusPercent` at or above `outerRadiusPercent`, are a PAIR the family's own descriptor owns, so they are refused where the pair is complete rather than by a range on either half. `settings: ["windowSeconds"]` is the third shape of the same rule — the allowed key set is the descriptor table's own reading, not a list the validator keeps. The pie's render-time clamp STAYS, as defence for the in-memory path that never passes through the envelope, but it stops being the only thing between an impossible document and a drawing. A document whose saved numbers disagree with what is drawn is the authored-versus-derived split this repo forbids, and a clamp at render is exactly that disagreement made invisible.
check: `npx vitest run packages/renderer-core/src/theme/fabric-envelope-validate.test.ts` from `src/web/` — the case `refuses a chart scalar the descriptor table bounds` refuses `windowSeconds: 0` as `out-of-range` at `/scene/objects/0/settings/windowSeconds` and `maxPoints: -5`, and `refuses a crossed pair the family's own descriptors own` refuses a gauge `min` above its `max` and `innerRadiusPercent` above `outerRadiusPercent`; the refusal was shown to be load-bearing, with the whole chart check disabled the same file reads 5 failed / 39 passed.

title: The chart descriptor table's own header still says the validator must not read it, which Task 23.4 made false
detail: FOUND 2026-10-21 by Task 23.4 of the backlog-drain plan (Phase 23), in the commit that landed the refusal: `charts/settings-fields.ts` carries a header section headed `## Why the validator does not read this table` (`:65`), whose paragraph (`:66-74`) states that driving validation from the table's `min`/`max` `is decided against (ADR-0028)` because authoring bounds and validation invariants are different questions, and that consuming them `would start refusing documents that validate today`. That is now the opposite of what the code does: `renderer-core/src/theme/fabric-envelope-validate.ts` reads `CHART_SETTINGS_FIELDS` and `CHART_PAINT_FIELDS` directly (its `chartScalars`), and the register row `vg-348`'s ruling of 2026-10-12 explicitly chose that reading over a second table in the validator. So one of the two records of this decision is stale and they now contradict each other: the row and decision note 0082 say the validator reads the table, the table's own header says it must not. HOW IT WAS CLOSED, AND WHY THE FIRST CLAUSE HERE WAS WRONG: it was filed on the assumption that `charts/settings-fields.ts` was read-only for this task, because the brief names it as what you READ, never write. The task review ruled the other way — a defect introduced *by* the task is fixed *in* it, not filed beside it — so the header was rewritten in place in `5bf21b78`, the same commit this row closes `verified` on. The finding's substance stands unchanged: the two records contradicted each other, the header was the one that was false, and decision 0082 is now the corrected record. HOW IT WAS SETTLED: that header section was rewritten to say what the table's bounds are now used for at the envelope boundary (a floor, never a `bound`-derived ceiling) and which half of the old argument survives — the `bound` fields (`drawnBox`, `halfDrawnBox`) still have no ceiling the envelope can name, which is the part of the original reasoning the implementation kept.
check: `grep -c "Why the validator does not read this table" src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/charts/settings-fields.ts` returns 0 and exit 1, and `grep -n "The validator reads this table"` returns `:65`, so the chart descriptor table's header no longer claims the validator must not read it; the same file's live-sounding `validateSettingsRange is now an exhaustive` claim also returns 0. The replacement section states that the table's `min`/`max` are the document's bounds and that `bound` is not one. Landed in 5bf21b78, whose write the reuse gate allowed on note 0082's `Paths:` claim.

title: HostingStore never polls, so an out-of-band host change leaves the editor's live indicator stale until a reload
detail:
FOUND BY plan 2 Task 3's task review as a caveat, then MEASURED by the controller against the source. HostingStore (packages/editor/src/editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:201-282) reads the host once in its constructor (:207-209) and re-emits only from its own actions - toggle() emits on the success path (:273-280) and on the refusal path (:261-270), and read() is public. So the review's phrasing 'read() runs only in the constructor' overstates it: the store does follow its own writes. What is genuinely missing is any poll or host-pushed update, so a change made outside the editor - the host CLI's own setLan (packages/host/src/cli/hosting.ts:29), or a host restart - is not observed until the page is reloaded or the control is pressed in-editor, and the live indicator renders a stale claim meanwhile. OWNER: Task 4's status bar owns the live indicator (its brief names PublishIndicator reading this store), so the fix belongs there if it is judged worth making; the alternative is to accept that the editor is the only in-session writer and close this as by-design. NOT FIXED in Task 3 because polling policy is the indicator's concern, not the header control's. SEVERITY: low - needs an external writer against the same host while the editor is open to be reachable at all.

RULED 2026-10-12: NO POLL — the host pushes, or the editor is the session's only writer. An editor polling the host for out-of-band changes is a timer the host owns, per this repo's own boundary (providers acquire; the host owns scheduling), and it would race the editor's own writes for no benefit the author can see. The channel already exists: the editor holds a live connection to the host, and the host is the only process that can observe its own `setLan` or a restart. So the ruling is a direction, not a feature: when the stale indicator is judged worth fixing, the host announces the change on that connection and the store re-reads; the editor never polls. Until then the row's own alternative stands — the editor is the only in-session writer by design — and that must be stated wherever the indicator's contract is written, so the staleness reads as a boundary rather than as a bug.

title: scene-fabric/src/persist.ts lists "locked" in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES with no row owning that decision
detail:
FOUND BY the manager census (2026-10-12), carried as a `Discovered, not fixed:` trailer on commit a2fe5a89 and materialised here as its own row. scene-fabric/src/persist.ts:81 lists "locked" in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES, so whether an object's lock state persists is decided in the persist list. That is a decision about the persisted scene with no row and no map entry, and the rule that only authored state persists makes it a question rather than an oversight: a lock is authored state if the user set it deliberately and derived state if it merely mirrors a transform flag. Whether the two can disagree after a restore is not established here.

RULED 2026-10-12: `locked` IS AUTHORED STATE and persists — and the decision is already made and stated in code, which is why the missing thing is the RECORD and not the behaviour. `object-lock-manager/index.ts:92-94` says it in as many words: undo rebuilds the scene, so a revived locked object is a new instance back at Fabric's defaults, `locked` is the persisted state, and the transform flags are re-derived from it rather than persisted alongside it; `onHistoryLoaded` is the re-derivation. A lock is the author's deliberate refusal of a transform, and dropping it on save would silently re-enable editing on whichever machine reloads the file. The ownership-map entry and this row's closure belong to the ownership map's filing pass, which is the pass that exists for exactly this shape. `selectable` and `evented` beside it in the same list are NOT covered by this ruling and are not the same case: the lock writes `hasControls` and the `lock*` flags and never those two, so nothing in the lock path makes them authored — whether some other writer does is a separate question this row does not answer, and it is named in the map entry rather than answered by it.

title: The docs map sent architecture decisions to `adr/` while the live decision register is `decisions/`: the map is fixed, and whether `docs/adr/` is merged into `decisions/`, kept as a second class of record, or removed is still open
detail:
FOUND BY THE ROOT while adding a row to docs/README.md for the new design language, so this is a doc-map defect spotted in passing rather than the task being done. MEASURED: docs/README.md's table has the row 'Why major architecture choices were made | adr/'. Two directories exist and they are not the same register: docs/adr/ holds 0002-0010 plus its own README, and docs/decisions/ holds 0019-0039 plus its own README. AGENTS.md's *Reuse before build* section names the live one plainly - 'Land a note at docs/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md' - and scripts/reuse-gate.mjs enforces writes against that directory, so the gate and the map disagree about where a decision note goes. The numbering is contiguous when the two are read together (0002-0010, then 0019-0039) and there is a gap at 0011-0018, which is consistent with decisions/ having replaced adr/ at 0019 rather than with two registers running in parallel. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether adr/ is deliberately kept for a different class of decision - nothing in either README says it is, and both READMEs describe the same thing, one file per decision where the way something is built was not obvious. That is the same text in both places, which is what a superseded directory looks like when it was copied and then diverged. The cost is that the canonical map - the file AGENTS.md points a fresh session at for durable project truth - sends a reader to a register that stopped receiving rows at 0010. The fix is a judgement rather than a lookup, which is why this is a row and not a drive-by edit: either the map points at decisions/, or adr/ is the live one and decisions/ is the mistake, or the two are merged and the gap at 0011-0018 is explained. Nothing here changes either directory. AMENDED 2026-10-12 by the dead-code sweep's Task 6 (`f7900f5c`) and retitled by Task 7 to what survives. THE MAP HALF IS DONE: `docs/README.md`'s row now reads "`decisions/` - the live register, and the one `scripts/reuse-gate.mjs` enforces; the earlier set stopped at 0010 in `adr/`", so the disagreement this row's old title stated - the map sending readers to a register that stopped receiving rows at 0010 - no longer holds, and the map is no longer one of the three candidates. WHAT SURVIVES is the half the row raised and Task 6 explicitly did not settle: whether `docs/adr/` (0002-0010, last commit `36f141b1`, 2026-09-25) should be merged into `decisions/`, kept as a deliberate second class of record, or removed. The two directories' numbers still collide (both hold a `0004`), the gap at 0011-0018 is still unexplained, and nothing rules between the three. Retitled rather than closed for that reason, exactly as `vg-266` was.

RULED 2026-10-12: KEEP `docs/adr/` as a CLOSED series and make its citations explicit — do not merge, do not remove, do not renumber. Merging is not available at a price anyone should pay: the two series collide across 0001-0010 (both hold 0001-0005, and both hold a 0004 on a different decision), so a merge renumbers one of them and breaks every citation to the other, and this repo's citation discipline is what makes that cost real rather than theoretical. Removing is rejected because 0002-0010 still bind the architecture — `0002-fabric-is-the-single-renderer` is the decision the whole product is built on, and `0010` is the dispatch-record rule `AGENTS.md` cites by number — and deleting a decision that still governs is not housekeeping. What the row needs is legibility, which is cheap: a header in `docs/adr/README.md` saying the series closed at 0010 on 2026-09-25 and its numbers are its own, a citation convention that always writes the directory (`adr/0004` against `decisions/0004`), and one line in `docs/decisions/README.md` accounting for the 0011-0018 gap so the next reader does not go looking for it.

AMENDED 2026-10-21 by the backlog drain's Task 23.8 (`b5e77a1e`): the 0011-0018 gap this row and its RULED paragraph state is FALSE. Measured from the directory: `docs/decisions/` holds 80 files numbered 0001-0083, and the absent numbers are **0006, 0034 and 0042**; 0011 through 0018 all exist. The claim was an artefact of the 2026-10-08 measurement quoted above, which described the range by its high end (0019-0039) rather than as a range, and the inference drawn from it — that `decisions/` replaced `adr/` at 0019 — is wrong for the same reason, since both series run from 0001, which is the collision and not a handoff. `docs/decisions/README.md` now states the three real gaps; the quoted RULED paragraph above is left verbatim.

title: the ownership sweep cannot see an exported id vocabulary spelled as a type union or a dot-separated id, though ownership.md claims it finds every one
detail:
FOUND BY TASK 2.2 OF PLAN 7 while adjudicating a hit the plan told it to expect and the sweep never produced. Verified here at the source, not taken from the report. THE CONTRACT IT BREAKS: `docs/architecture/ownership.md:22-23` says the sweep "finds every module exporting an id vocabulary and reports any other module re-spelling two or more of those ids" -- unqualified. `shortcut-manager/index.ts:2-21` exports exactly that: `ProductShortcutId`, a nineteen-member id vocabulary, with `PRODUCT_SHORTCUTS` the table that binds it. Task 2.2 put eight of those ids into `object-actions.ts`, and `npm run ownership:sweep` exits 0 naming neither module. BOTH HALVES OF THE MECHANISM MISS IT, and they miss for different reasons. `discriminatorsIn` (`scripts/ownership-sweep.mjs:84`) matches `"([a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+)"` -- the `(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+` group requires **at least one hyphen**, so `"edit.duplicate"` is never a candidate at all. `exportedVocabularies` (`:91-101`) parses two shapes only: `const NAME = [ ... ]` with three or more quoted ids, and `Readonly<Record<string, ...>>` records. `ProductShortcutId` is a `type` union, so it is never seen as anyone vocabulary. A vocabulary that is a union *and* dotted is invisible twice over. THE SWEEP IS NOT BROKEN, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS PRECISE: the same run finds two genuine collisions -- `packages/host/src/settings/devices.ts` against `main.ts` and against `server.ts`, sharing `system-disk` and `data-disk`. So the mechanism works; it is blind to one shape, not failing generally. WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED: `ownership.md:122-123` records a blindness, and it is a *different* one -- the seven object-creation sites "each inline a string literal" and so export no vocabulary at all. That is a module with no vocabulary. This is a module with a vocabulary the sweep cannot read, and the doc gives no sign of knowing that shape exists. WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: it is a verification gate, so widening it is a decision about precision against recall, not a bug fix. Dropping the hyphen requirement would make every dotted string in the tree a candidate discriminator and flood the report -- and `ownership.md:48` already carries the hard-won lesson that a gate flagging most of the tree gets ignored, which is why the count floor exists. Accepting type unions means writing a third parser for a syntax the sweep currently reads as data. Neither has an obvious regression test. Consequence for the plan that found it: Task 2.2s constraint told the executor the sweep would report this change and required it to adjudicate the hit as a consumer. There was no hit. The plan asserted a gate watched something the gate cannot see, which is worse than the gate being absent -- it reads as verification and is not.

RULED 2026-10-12: RULED 2026-10-12 by the user: DO NOT WIDEN -- CORRECT THE CLAIM. The defect is the claim rather than the coverage: ownership.md says the sweep finds every exported id vocabulary when it cannot see a type union or a dotted id, and that reads as verification while being none. The doc states the boundary instead, because a gate widened to flag most of the tree is ignored, which ownership.md:48 already records as the hard-won lesson.
check: `grep -n "one shape of vocabulary" docs/architecture/ownership.md` from the repo root, exit 0 with one match (`:23`): the claim now says what the sweep reads, where it promised it "finds every module exporting an id vocabulary", so a doc still carrying that promise cannot contain the phrase. The shape it cannot see is an exported vocabulary spelled as a `type` union or with dot-separated ids — `npm run ownership:sweep` exits 0 over 189 lines and names neither `shortcut-manager` nor `object-actions`.

detail: FOUND BY TASK 5.3 (2026-10-13), by its task reviewer: vg-110's fix covers a theme that fails validation and leaves the row's third clause open for a theme that is refused for size instead. Not established here: whether any real document reaches 32 MiB, and whether the write path's own refusal (`ThemeAssetLimitError` at `:751`, for assets rather than `theme.json`) already tells the user at save time. title: A second colour parser lives in `renderer-core` with a different contract, so the ownership map's single 'shared colour parsing' row names only the editor's half
detail:
FOUND 2026-10-13 while self-reviewing `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-colour-and-gradient-rebuild-design.md`, which had written the unification the wrong way round. **The duplication, measured.** `export function parseHex(input: string): Rgba | undefined` sits at `editor/src/components/ui/colour-maths.ts` beside `parseColour`, `toHex`, `rgbaToHsva` and `hsvaToRgba`, and **`export function parseHex(color: string): [number, number, number] | undefined` sits again at `renderer-core/src/charts/fill.ts`** — same name, same job, different return type. The editor's module is imported by exactly three files (`colour-picker.tsx`, `gradient-editor.tsx`, `colour-picker.test.ts`), so neither is shared with the other. **Why the map's row does not cover it.** `docs/architecture/ownership.md` names the editor's file as the owner of 'shared colour parsing — hex, rgba and hsva conversion, and the refusal that returns `undefined` for a value that is not a colour', which is the row `vg-246`'s close added. That row is scoped to the Editor section, so `renderer-core`'s copy appears in no row at all — the same failure mode `vg-246` reported, one layer down and still true after its close. **`vg-246` is not a duplicate of this and did not measure it.** Its own detail ends with **NOT ESTABLISHED: 'whether colour-maths.ts is the right owner (it is a components/ui helper, which may be why it was never promoted) or whether other colour parsing exists that the survey did not find'** — and it closed `verified` against `dd308143` on the narrower check, that the map promotes the de-facto owner and drops the Known-ownership-gaps bullet. The map row is real; the second implementation is the half its own text left open, now measured. **The direction that cannot be built, which is what the spec had to correct.** The obvious unification — the editor's module owns it and `fill.ts` consumes it — is an upward import: `renderer-core` imports nothing from `editor` (measured), and the editor bundles `renderer-core` from source through a Vite alias, so that direction is a cycle. Any single-owner resolution therefore moves the primitive **down** into `renderer-core` and leaves the editor's richer conversions consuming it, or scopes the claim to the editor and records `fill.ts`'s tuple parser as a deliberately separate contract for chart fill strings. **Owner and cost.** Whoever owns the map decides, and the spec's decision currently takes the first: primitive down, `colour-maths.ts` keeps `Hsva`/`rgbaToHsva`/`hsvaToRgba`/`toHex` and consumes it, `fill.ts` retires its copy, and the ownership row moves with the primitive. The cost if that is wrong is a package-boundary move of one small pure module plus a row rewrite; the cost of leaving it is a third parser the next colour surface will write.

PARK LIFTED 2026-10-24 (the row was PARKED on 2026-10-16): the decision the row asks for is already taken in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-colour-and-gradient-rebuild-design.md`, which states the direction that can be built (the primitive moves down into `renderer-core` and `fill.ts` retires its copy) and the one that cannot (an upward import is a cycle); measured 2026-10-16, both `parseHex` definitions are still in place, so the work is real and unscheduled. It waits transitively on that spec's review, the same shape as `vg-322`'s park on `vg-330`: the row's decision lives in a document the user has not read yet, so the work cannot enter a phase before it. Parked rather than closed because the finding is real and the register's policy is that a real-but-low-value finding is parked rather than forgotten, and parked rather than left plain because the triage's job is to say what each row waits on.
check: `src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/color.test.ts`'s parseColor and formatColor cases prove the one parser the rebuild moved into renderer-core, with the editor consuming parseColor and formatColor by name.

title: The Runs inspector stacks every run; numeric tabs would show one run's properties at a time
detail: The user asked on 2026-10-24, while the text-elements plan was executing, for the Runs section to become numeric tabs — 1, 2, 3, … plus a + — where selecting a tab reveals only that run's properties below, instead of today's stacked editor. ADDED TO THE TEXT-ELEMENTS PLAN as Task 2.3 on 2026-10-24 at the user's direction; it was queued when raised because that plan owned the worktree. WHAT EXISTS TODAY: selection-inspector/runs.tsx renders every run through RunRow under RunEditor, with the shared Align, vertical-align and Overflow controls above and an Add run button below; each row carries its own Remove run N action and rows are keyed by the ids run-identity.ts derives. WHAT IT WOULD TAKE: transient selected-run state (never persisted, like selection), an accessible-name scheme for the tabs (Run 1 …), a visible selected state, overflow behaviour when there are more runs than fit the strip, + wired to the same edits.addRun() and a decision whether it also selects the new run, keeping Remove run N reachable from the selected panel, and updates to the inspector census and accessible-name tests plus the walkthrough e2e. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a spec deciding tab-strip overflow, whether + selects the new run, and whether tab order is run order. RENUMBERED at the main merge: filed as vg-710 on the text branch while the colour-picker branch had taken the same id; this is the same finding.

title: Game metadata from a store network is not used, so a store-agnostic name and cover need a privacy and matching ruling
detail: FOUND 2026-10-24 by the user, asking whether game info could come from IGDB or from Steam's CDN/SteamDB regardless of purchase store. Evidence gathered the same day. IGDB: requires a Twitch Developer app (client ID and secret, Confidential type), OAuth client_credentials, tokens lasting about 60 days, 4 requests/second, 500 rows per request; free for non-commercial use under the Twitch Developer Services Agreement, commercial needs a partnership, and the secret cannot ship in a distributed app, so each install would need its own credentials (BYOK) or a commercial arrangement. Its images are CDN URLs (images.igdb.com); store ids can be matched through /v4/external_games before falling back to a name search. SteamDB: has no API at all (its FAQ says one may come later) and explicitly forbids scraping and auto-refreshing, with bans for doing so, so there is no key to obtain. Steam itself: the public store endpoint store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails is keyless and returns name and header/capsule images, while api.steampowered.com Web API methods require a user key and carry a 100k/day limit and the Steam Web API terms; its CDN image URLs (cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/<appid>/...) are public. THE OBSTACLE IS NOT ACCESS, IT IS THE CONTRACT: the spec refuses a Steam CDN request because it would leak library membership, so every remote lookup needs a spec amendment plus an explicit opt-in and a statement of what is sent; and for a game bought elsewhere there is no shared id, so a Steam appid must be recovered by name matching against the public app list, which can attach the wrong cover. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a ruling on whether remote metadata is opt-in per host with its own credential (IGDB) or a keyless Steam store lookup with a cached name-to-appid table, plus the rule that remote images are fetched once, cached locally, and served through the existing gated artwork route so no display ever sees a third-party URL.
check: ran the game-metadata e2e against a fixture store: the canonical name and cover painted, a cached reload served both from cache with no store request, and a stopped store fell back to the authored image

title: The player has no descriptor catalogue, so a custom source unit never converts on a display
detail: FOUND 2026-10-24 by the fix pass that closed the final whole-branch review of the sensor-platform plan. That pass made the descriptor which supplied a dynamic key drive unit conversion, and the editor now threads its sensor catalogue through PlanInputs.descriptors into the plan and the repaint. The player never fetches /api/sensors and has no catalogue of its own, so a custom key carrying unit °C and unitKind temperature renders °C on a real display even when the binding asks for °F; only the editor preview converts. The wire-to-descriptor mapping lives in packages/editor/src/sensor-catalogue.ts, which the player cannot import, so the player needs one shared owner for that mapping rather than a second copy. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: move the mapping to a player-safe shared module, have the player load descriptors from the host on connect and pass them into plan and repaint, and add a browser test that binds a custom temperature key with a °F binding and reads °F on the player surface. This is the residual of the final review's descriptor finding, not a new defect.
check: ran the custom-source e2e: the player fetches /api/sensors, converts a custom °C source to the theme's °F binding, and a real display paints 212°F

title: Every foreground process reads as a running game, so a browser or the desktop sets game.running true
detail: FOUND 2026-10-24 while preparing Task 6.3 of the sensor-platform plan. The plan's presence rule (from the spec's non-Steam fallback) says a non-Steam foreground process reports its executable name in game.app and game.running true with no game.name. Locally there is no way to tell a game from any other foreground window, so a terminal, Explorer or a browser all read as a game while focused; a widget bound to game.running says a game is running almost always, and game.app churns with whatever window the user clicks. The rule was followed rather than silently changed, because the spec names the non-Steam fallback explicitly. WHAT IT NEEDS: a ruling on what counts as a game — Steam-app match only (honest, loses non-Steam games), a fullscreen/borderless foreground check, or a user-authored allow-list — then the provider's presence test and the vocabulary note follow it. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the ruling plus a regression test that a browser-focused desktop reports no running game.
check: ran the game classifier and provider unit tests: game-classifier.test.ts rejects a fullscreen browser, and the provider test reports a fullscreen browser as not running while still naming its process, while a catalogue match reports true

title: The live SMTC helper tests fail because GetSessions() returns a COM object with no Count, so an empty session list emits no line
detail: FOUND 2026-10-25 at the Phase 1 gate of the game-identity plan. `npm run gate` exits 1 on packages/host/src/providers/media/smtc-helper.windows.test.ts: 2 of 10 tests fail with `no line within 20000 ms` and 0 artwork lines. It reproduces with the file run alone, so it is not suite load. Probe: the helper script emits its audio line every poll, but `$manager.GetSessions()` returns `System.__ComObject` whose `.Count` reads empty, so `if ($sessions.Count -eq 0)` is false and the loop emits neither `none` nor a session line. NOT FIXED HERE because it is outside Task 1.5 (the catalogue split) and the owner is the media helper. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a projection that yields the WinRT session list as a PowerShell collection so the empty case emits `none` and a non-empty case emits its session lines, plus a proof that the empty manager answers a line.
check: ran smtc-helper.windows.test.ts live with a playing Chromium media session: the helper emits a session line and its artwork line, and exactly {"kind":"none"} once the session stops; GetSessions() is projected into a PowerShell array so an empty session list now answers a line

title: The Linux trash fallthrough never advances, because the runner drops the exit code, so trash-put is never tried when gio is missing
detail: FOUND BY the fonts-and-assets plan's Task 18 re-review (2026-10-26), as an out-of-scope observation in a file that task already owned. `themes/trash.ts`'s `run` rejected with a plain `Error`, discarding `error.code`, while `moveToTrash` advanced to the next route only when that code was `ENOENT` — so on a Linux machine without `gio` the `trash-put` route was never tried and every theme delete failed. The re-reviewer measured the wrapper directly: a missing command produced `code= undefined msg= spawn definitely-not-a-command-xyz ENOENT`. Pre-existing at `fc4d5260`, not introduced by Task 18. Fixed on the fly in `4637b557` because Task 18's own claim about the fallthrough depended on it: the rejection now carries the code and `cause`, and `runTrashRoutes` takes an injected runner so a fake missing command drives the fallthrough in `trash.test.ts`. Owner: `packages/host/src/themes/trash.ts`. The commit trailer says 'Discovered, not fixed', which is inaccurate — the fix is in the same commit, and this row is filed as verified rather than open.
check: the Linux trash fallthrough advances on a missing command: `runTrashRoutes` given an injected runner that rejects `ENOENT` once and resolves on the second route completes, and the case passes in `packages/host/src/themes/trash.test.ts` (host suite 120 files / 1939 tests, exit 0)

title: Dropped sample batches make the editor receive one batch per two host intervals, so the 2 s playback delay is only one received cadence and the line holds and steps on most gaps
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING THE OWNER'S 2026-10-27 RIGHT-EDGE REPORT, and measured rather than inferred. The host emits a batch every 1000 ms (measured directly against /ws: 21 batches over 20 s, gaps 997-1019 ms), but the editor page received chart samples at p50 1992 ms (34 samples over 61.9 s), because SseConnection.offer keeps only the newest pending frame (KeepLatestSlot) while the response stream is backed up, so every other batch is dropped before delivery. LIVE_SOURCE_CHART_PLAYBACK_DELAY_MS is 2000 ms, two configured host cadences and therefore only ONE received cadence when batches drop; 16 of 33 received gaps in the probe exceeded 2000 ms. With the painted-history fix in this branch's line.ts, those gaps now render as the intended flat hold and a step instead of being reshaped one batch later, so more than half of the stretches are staircase. NOT ESTABLISHED: how much of the drop rate is the headless probe's software rendering versus a real editor or phone; the phone player's earlier reading had a ~1 s received cadence with gaps up to 3.2 s. THE DECISION OWED: whether the host should queue samples for history, declare its achieved cadence so the display can size the delay, or the display should accept a longer fixed delay; each trades latency for smoothness. OWNER: the host transport's keep-latest policy against the display's delay, src/web/packages/host/src/transport/keep-latest.ts and src/web/packages/renderer-core/src/data/live-source.ts. RESOLVED 2026-10-27 by e6f0e754 (0124): the host transport now queues sample frames in a bounded FIFO (FrameQueue, 120) and SseConnection drains it on drain instead of replacing the pending frame, so a slow connection loses no measurement until the queue is full; the playback delay this row proposed to size was deleted rather than tuned, because the line is now placed by its data clock. MEASURED in the 1 fps browser probe: 41 batches over 80 s and 40 axis steps, each step at a batch, with no blank right edge. NOT ESTABLISHED still: whether a real editor or phone drops frames for a reason other than the old keep-latest slot; the probe read one host on this machine.
check: the SSE transport keeps every queued sample batch instead of the newest one: hold the response unwritable, offer three frames, drain, and SseConnection writes first/second/third in order with droppedCount 0, while the bounded queue drops only the oldest past 120 (packages/host/src/transport/sse.test.ts and frame-queue.test.ts). The playback delay the row sized against a dropped cadence no longer exists — chartPlaybackDelayMs, chartPlaybackDelayFor and LIVE_SOURCE_CHART_PLAYBACK_DELAY_MS are deleted, and the line is placed by its newest reading — so no delay can be mis-sized by a 2 s received cadence.

title: A panel still is JPEG-compressed before being sent as raw pixels
detail: Found by the user looking at the TURZX 5" panel (2026-10-29): the image reads as over-denoised, especially text. panel-raster.ts captures every still as JPEG quality 85 (Page.captureScreenshot, format jpeg, scale 1 at 800x480), and the TURZX adapter then decodes it to raw BGRA for the wire. The JPEG is a pure lossy intermediate: the panel never receives a JPEG, so the compression buys nothing and costs sharpness. Capture stills as PNG (lossless) and keep JPEG only for the USB families that stream JPEG to the device. Decode is unchanged (panel-image handles PNG). Verified on the branch: the TURZX adapter declares stillFormat "png", the rasteriser captures in the format the device states, and the overlay path is PNG by construction. The panel was sent stills in this form on hardware; the sharpness itself is the user's observation.
check: turzx-panel.test.ts asks for a lossless still because it is decoded, not streamed; panel-raster.test.ts asserts PNG with no quality for an overlay; a panel sent raw pixels is no longer JPEG-compressed between capture and the wire.
